review_text: “Free bad attitude at Allerton!” We got stuck with the Allerton on Priceline. My wife and I visit Chicago often and have stayed in more than 10 different hotels there. My experience with using Priceline is that most hotels will tend to give you the less than desirable rooms, so I called the day before my stay to book a King non-smoking room. I was told that they couldn't promise me that, but that they were not very busy and that it shouldn't be a problem. Check in is at 3:00, we got there at 5:15 and was told there were no clean rooms available unless I wanted a smoking room with a full size bed. I told them either a King or Queen would be fine but it's got to be non-smoking. The reservation clerk quickly pointed out that because I was a Priceline customer they could pretty much give me what they wanted to, but if I would come back in an hour they would have something ready. Great.... I come back in an hour and it's still another 20 minutes until they can get me a room. Finally, at 6:30 we got a non-smoking Queen. This place is old and the rooms are tiny. Although I did have a great view of the Magnificent Mile, the room was very worn with torn shades, water damage to the ceiling and cobwebs in the corners. For the money, the only thing this place has going for it is the location. I now know what it feels like to be in a cocoon.

“Not Worth The Money.” First off let me say the Hotel is in a woderful spot in the city.There is a subway entrance right out side the door.China town is 3 or 4 blocks south.There isnt much after dark around the Hotel so plan ahead.There is a deli 2 blocks away and a Starbucks that closes early for a starbucks. -----The Hotel charges $150 a day for incidentals.Plan ahead. I didnt and was shocked when told I had to pay that. I also had all the junk removed from my room so that I couldnt be charged for it.. -----If you use the phone even for local calls you will be charged $1.50.You can talk all you want I guess but you still get charged the intial $1.50.. -----When I stayed weekend of April 22. The Hotel is only Half open.Floor 27th is the highest that availble....Pool not done. Spa not open. SoHI not open. ----- If you goto the Trump site there isnt a picture of the rooms.You would think they would be able to take up to date photos and put them on the site.Theres a reason there isnt actual photos on the Site. -----Also if you want to use the internet its $14.95 a day.For unsecured wired/wireless connection. This is 2010 everyone uses the internet these days. ----- I feel I was nickled and dimed. It seems as though if you stay here you are helping train the staff. I know that currently it is availble for a discounted rate. There is a reason.. I had a Supuerior Room. It is small.Had I brought my wife we wouldnt have had any room in the closet for clothes.There were like 6 hangers. I was disapointed and was up graded to a Deluxe. Which ment it was a little bit bigger but still small. In both rooms the Bathroom was the only bright spot. It had a large deep tub next to the window.The shower was a nice.You have 2 choices. There is a wand where the water shoots out and a non adjustable rain head over head.I have stayed in NYC.The room was small. Its only a 5-star hotel if you care about the Taschen books and bench thats worth $1500. I dont care about any of that. You dont go to NYC to pend all day in the Room. +++ The maid service was beyond belif.They come by 2 times a day.They folded my clothes. ++++ Door men were outstanding as well.Always nice,polite and friendly. ++++ The view while looking out the window was nice.I could see Empire State building ,the Brooklin bridge,Another bridge and central park..I will say if you had a room at the top there isnt a better view in the city from a hotel. ++++ The bed was really soft.I slept well on it. In closing I dont feel right now its a 5-star hotel.It will be in the future.There is no way I would pay the prices that the hotel will ask for in the future.I didnt want to pay the $300 a night even if it was fully open. The rooms are to small. I guess I can say I stayed there when the Celebity Apprentice Final shows. For the price go stay else where..

“All Is Not Well At The Wellington” I was fortunate to get a VERY good price through Priceline. However this was not a 3 star hotel. The first room I was offered smelled like urine. They graciously offered me another upgrade and it did not smell. However one could not regulate the heat,and it was very hot. So I regulated this by sleeping with the window open all night and this was in December. All the guests were complaining about the heat. Although "clean" the toilet fixtures were covered with rust and paneling was coming off the doors. The room doors are very heavy and whenever your neighbor leaves their room the door slams shut unless they happen to be very attentive and kind. There was also renovating going on early i the morning. The staff was kind. I guess they have much to make up for.

“Old hotel. Room was in need of renovation. Bathroom disgusting.” As a Diamond Member chose to stay here instead of the JW Marriott by the convention center. The front desk staff were very pleasant. The lobby and restaurant area was nice. The room was my only complaint. I was in 602. The furniture was old and "dinged", the bathtub was 1960s with old loose caulking, handles falling off and mold growing all over the door jams. If you like old world stuff, this might be the place for you. Reminded me of the old Drake in Chicago. I would have to pass this up on my next visit.

“Could this be a worse dump?” Noisy, dirty and they managed to lose our laundry. So my favorite jeans are now history, along with my wife's. The front desk didn't even care. Bring your ear plugs. The curtains are filthy. The bed covers have burn holes, it just disgusting. Don't even consider it.

“An unpleasant place to stay” I spent the weekend at this hotel, that had just changed ownership to Sheraton, four months before. After a few problems I decided to take notes: The room doors slam at early hours of the morning. There just a hole on the bathroom door frame rather than a striker plate. This means that the door only somewhat closes and rattles. The surface of the bathroom ceiling all bubbled and discolored. There were three thermostats in the room, two identical on the wall. We had no idea which to use. The closet door does not slide open without a great effort. Auxiliary entrance doors gave the hours when the doors were to be locked, but they were locked too early. They were supposed to be unlocked at 6am and we could not use them and 9am and so had to walk around the building. Even major doors do not have power openers making it hard to get luggage out. The shower has smooth and a little slippery floor, but there are no handholds for support. The elevators were a study in themselves. --They skipped floors. -- Closing doors could be stopped with and arm but would not open to release arm. --They seemed to be badly programmed, and there were long queues formed. -- It was not uncommon to have 7-minute waits for the elevator and then have two cars arrive seconds apart.

“Worst experience in NY” The hotel I normally stay at in NYC was booked. I booked the Hotel Mela as a package through US Airways. What an awful experience. The rooms were tiny--I listened to couple after couple beg to be put in a larger room only to be told it would be another $100 plus per night. There is no concierge and really no bell person. The front desk staff was very unhelpful even doing simple things like getting us a cab. It took 45 minutes just to get ice to the room. There is no way to get help with tickets or dinner reservations. We ended up using the services at the Marriott and the Broadway Millenium across the street. A large part of the space minus the bed in the room is taken up with a basket full of items they want you to buy and a charge bar. There is no drawer space and a tiny closet. Service seemed to worse for those who booked a package--probably figured we had already paid and there was nothing we could do. You can do a lot better in NYC.

“Not such a great value, location misleading” The location of this hotel according to Expedia and Google Maps is within 3-4 blocks of the Arizona Center. This is NOT the case. It's actually about 15 long Phoenix blocks from AZ center. But that is not the main reason I'm giving the hotel a poor rating. The hotel is not really maintained well. The electrical outlets were grimy and somewhat scary. My colleague complained to me about hearing the person upstairs taking a pee. The continental breakfast should be skipped altogether. The front desk clerk recommended a cafe with only sandwiches for dinner when we asked for a proper restaurant. On the bright side, the bed was clean and the wi-fi worked ok. The pillows were way too hard. We paid $99/night using Expedia, but there are likely cheaper hotels for the same quality and same distance from downtown.

“Not up to par” Our stay at the BH Plaza was adequate at best. The location was great for us, as we were attending a wedding around the corner, and our room was spacious (an end suite way back by the waterfall). The lobby staff, though, was unhelpful and at times downright rude, and the last day, I noticed that some of my jewelry had gone missing. I asked when we checked out, and the concierge said that the only person that had gone into our room was housecleaning. She said I had to ask them, but no housekeeping staff could be found. I called back 3 times that week and each time was given the brush-off. No help searching for the jewelry or inquiring about it. For the price of our stay, we should have gotten better service.

“Seen Better Days” This was a Priceline stay, and it was rated 3*, This property has seen better days, like 25 years ago. It was nice once, I'm sure. Now, it's very dated with parts of old features still around. It was very close to the SeaTac airport. They don't have their own shuttle, you use one of the parking lot buses. There are four, I believe; A,B,C, and D. That's confusing, only one works. My room was large, but it had an irregular shape. Things all worked, but the bathroom was outmoded. The employees were OK, no one stood out. For a 3* property it did not make it. This Red Lion is 2.5* at best.

“Love the DoubleTree chain, but not this location” There was a convention at the DT this weekend. The guests were extremely rude running up and down the halls all night. The pool hours were posted as 8am to 11pm, which is WAY too late if you have a room facing the pool. Guests were in the pool before 6am making noise! I called down to the front desk and was told the pool opened at 6am! The property itself is very old. The rooms have not been updated in quiet a while (albeit they have nice flat screen tv). The interior doors are ugly brown with cheap wood veneer paneling that is chipping and peeling. Guests are allowed to smoke on the verandas but the smoke just blows right back into the rooms and the hallways. The hallways reeked of marijuana this morning when we went down for breakfast. I complained to the front desk and I did receive compensation; however, that DID NOT help the lack of sleep! i will not stay at this location again. I am a Hilton-diamond

“Wouldn't go back” We had such a negative experience at the Radission Austin that by the end of the weekend we started to ignore further problems. Advertisements for this hotel promise a "Sleep Number" bed and a view of the lake or the city. After checking in we learned that the Sleep Number beds are only available on a limited number of floors (less than half) in the hotel. Because the hotel was full with weekend events, no switch would be possible. Additionally, our room looked out on a dirty rooftop with a piecemeal view of the lake - between parked cars in the adjacent parking structure. So we kept the drapes pulled for most of the weekend. Despite leaving the room for several hours during the day on Saturday, our room was never cleaned during our stay - so Sunday morning we were still looking at wine glasses from Friday night. The front desk promised to bring some amenities right away that we'd forgotten and called about - 45 minutes later, we had to come up with another solution or risk missing the event we were in town for. Overall, for the price that we paid and the service we expected from a hotel chain of the class that the Radisson likes to advertise, we were severely disappointed and would reconsider booking at another hotel chain in other cities, much less in Austin again. It might have a good location, but so do several other hotels.

“questionable business practices” I booked this motel through the Motel 6 website - where it stated "credit card required to guarantee for late arrival" or something similar. So I trusted this motel with my credit card information, and I trusted the website. I left a note that I would be arriving late and even stated "after 10PM". My flight was late, and I arrived after midnight. The clerk was rude and nasty and had sold my room to someone else for a higher rate. She barked "you were supposed to be here at 10 o-clock, and I've charged your credit card". She growled there was nothing she could do for me, and I would have to come back and speak with the manager in the morning. First of all, I can understand that the credit card is required in case I don't show up, so they don't lose money, but this motel is running a scam and making twice the money off the room - by re-selling rooms at higher rates to drop-ins, and refusing to refund money to those who reserved and showed up. Second, why would I want to waste my time speaking with a manager who authorizes his staff to conduct those types of business practices. I'm travelling, I don't have time to waste running around over $60. Also - she gave me a printout of the charges, but they don't actually supply any phone numbers or names to that particular hotel, so you can't call them anyway unless you go to a lot of trouble. The invoice did state the motel was "independently owned" - so I don't think this is standard practice for Motel 6, but beware of this motel. In the end, I called the Motel 6 company complaints line, and eventually got my credit card refunded - and the company was very helpful and did not question this as it is obviously dishonest. Although I was able to get my money back, I think it is important to know the potential problems you may face with this hotel. In summary - this motel tried to rip me off, were not helpful and have the most unprofessional staff I have encountered.

“This hotel certainly does not add any pleasure to your trip” I stayed for three nights. Positives: - OK location with Subway three blocks away and nice Indian restaurants in the neighborhood. - Free Wireless - Price OK Negatives: - Skip the breakfast, loveless buffet - Small room - Reception desk service OK but again: lacking the extra bit of effort. - No nice lobby to wait - No doorman for taxi service - Incredibly slow elevator

“lots of improvements, but poorly managed” I have stayed here off and on over 10 years and they have complied with Holiday Inns' directives to upgrade the property to minimal levels with new carpets and TV's and such. They have some helpful people at the front desk, but when there is a problem the managers don't follow up. My last visit was a repeat of a recurring problem with TV cable not working and it stayed out for most channels for the three nights i was there. Every morning i asked if it would be fixed and if not, i was going to check into a different hotel and they said it would be fixed that day and it was not. Never heard a word from the managers and no reply to my request for an adjustment in the cost of a very expensive room.

“Bad Bad Bad” Room was ok as was the price, but the hotel is REALLY noisy. On our second night the entire 2nd floor was booked for a birthday party and the music floated up the elevator shaft. I thought the music was from across the hall and it was actually 8 floors down. I complained 4 times and the front desk said they couldn't do anything about it because catering had booked the party and they didn't have authority to shut it down (HUH????). I couldn't leave or switch rooms because my 2 kids were fast asleep in an adjoining room. Better me on no sleep than them. The next morning I recieved a 75% refund which appealed to the cheap side of me. I felt sorry for the others who had reserved (and paid from on-line sites)- they couldn't get a refund from the hotel. I would NEVER stay again - a VERY unsafe location - would book something in Galleria.

“Awful- old rooms, highway noise, nothing around” Awful- old roooms with old carpet and lots of highway noise in basically all rooms. Everything old and front desk tried to act like nice property and what could you possibly complain about. Well-alot! I was there for business but would stay somewhere else and drive to meeting the next time!

“bargain basement lodging” I spent one night here in November. The check-in host was dressed as a maintenance man (which I assume he was), the toilet seat would not stay up (not an issue for women) because the fixture was installed too close to a ledge/lip that could not be moved, and I found a hair in my sink first thing! Things got better, however. The room was comfortable, it was relatively modern, and the towels and soap/shampoo were there, although sparse. (nothing but soap and shampoo) There was plenty of free parking (not available in center city). I did not try the continental breakfast since I had a breakfast meeting elsewhere, but several men were seated in the eating area and appeared satisfied. I hope I can afford a better place, next time, but this place will do if necessary.

“This hotel is epitome of a stereotype airport hotel” This hotel showed a listing of 3.5 stars on Hotwire.com, but the dirty, discusting room should result in a 2 star rating. It was really a dirty room with hair in the bathroom, soiled carpet not worthy of nice slippers (lol) let alone bare feet. There are other hotels in the area, some I have reviewed, that will give you a better room. I would pick the Marriott, Hilton, Westin or a couple other ones before this place. The best part was the airport shuttle that got me off property in the morning.

“over the top!” I stayed for 2 nights. The one good thing is that the staff is genuinely nice, esp. given the total chaos, noise, long lines, etc. The rooms are fairly big for NYC, but generic. The bad: the elevators are extremely sloooowww! I waited 8 minutes at one point for an elevator to go two floors. Apparently, they are installing new ones, but in the meantime, it's a real problem. The hotel itself was not for me: too big, too many people, too loud, too chaotic. A constant din in the hallways! Many, many tourists, and you have to wait for everything. Good if you like feeling in the center of everthing, esp. if you like being right in Times Square. Otherwise, I'd go elsewhere, esp. for the $$.

“Don't waste your money on this hotel!” I find it hard to believe that anyone would give this hotel a good review. Hyatt should remove their name from this hotel because I will no longer stay in any Hyatt after this experience. When you walk into the hotel "lobby" you feel more like you are walking into an extremely busy shopping mall. People are packed in there like sardines. We got the impression that this was more of a hangout for locals rather than a hotel for guests only. The check-in desk is hard to find as it is no where near the hotel entry. Instead, it is located upstairs where even more people are hanging out. The check-in clerk was very friendly and helpful. Unfortunately, we had trouble hearing her due to the noise of the crowd. Our room was borderline clean and the walls were paper thin. We could hear the conversations of the people in the room next door. We were given a room designed for the handicapped which would have been fine except for the fact that the door wouldn't shut when you went in and out. Instead, it stayed open for about 30 seconds and there was no way to force it shut. This was a big security concern for us since at one point we had someone pounding on our door and yelling "let me in". Of course we didn't open the door and the person finally realized they had the wrong floor but it did cause us to be very concerned for our safety. The fact that we couldn't shut the door if needed added to our concerns. I will say that I booked our room online but called to confirm and the person I spoke to was extremely helpful. Unfortunately, good customer service cannot overcome the magnitude of the other issues.

“A multitude of better options nearby. Okay if you pay half of the going rate.” We were staying at this hotel for one night when we had a late arriving flight and an early appointment nearby. We booked this on Travelocity’s “Top Secret”, which by the way I will NEVER use again, poor customer service and inflated ratings compared to Hotwire and Priceline. I am a frequent traveler, and rarely use opaque, but for a quick crash stay like this it seemed appropriate. Their front desk at least over the phone leaves a lot to be desired, when we called to request a King Non Smoking room ahead of time they were not very helpful and one person even said “you are in a special type of room which is just double beds, I will not be able to make a notation” – what a joke, as the place was nearly empty! On the phone the front desk staff was disinterested and bordered on rude. After several calls back I finally gave up and had to call the Priority Club Platinum desk to get the request notated. (I am Platinum with Priority Club) I absolutely know requests cannot be promised, especially on these opaque reservations, but at least say “we will try”! To their credit, In the end though, they did have us in a king nonsmoking room in the good part of the hotel when we arrived so all was good. My wife called and seemed to get a pleasant response but nothing to encouraging. Also, Travelocity called this a non-smoking property which is an out and out false statement. I had to argue with them on the phone for 30 minutes and they finally got the hotel to guarantee a non-smoking room. Also there is NO way I would call this a 3.5 star…maybe a 2.5. The night audit clerk who checked us in was friendly and accommodating, as was the clerk in the AM who checked us out. We arrived around midnight Tuesday evening and departed at 7:30 am on Wednesday morning...so as you can tell this was a short visit. Check in went fast and there was no mention of Travelocity other than the fact that the room was fully prepaid. The hotel lobby appears to be pretty well kept and is inviting but you can tell that this is a very old hotel with a fresh coat of decorating. The hotel is right on the freeway but we did not experience any excessive traffic noise. There is a restaurant off the lobby of the hotel, and they have a decent looking outdoor pool. As a cautionary note, they seem to have an older “motel style” section as well as the main tower. Our room was a nice King room, but nothing impressive. The room faced the freeway, but noise was not really a problem. The room had a nice sized work desk and TV. The closet and bathroom is space tiny. Though the hotel has been remodeled, but it was like putting a fresh coat of paint over the messed up walls and such….nothing impressive. And to think, they put us in the “good rooms”! Though there is nothing they can do about the tiny bathroom space, they sure could have remodeled better. Towels were fluffy and comfortable. The climate control system worked well, and the blower can be set to on for white noise while still using the air conditioning, though it did groan and squeak a bit. The bed and pillows were comfortable. The room has a medium sized Flat Panel HDTV and a reasonable selection of channels. The rooms are quiet and dark at night. I am unsure of their business center, but wifi was free. We did not check out their fitness center. We did not try the restaurant or bar, as we ate off site. The inside relatively clean but the outdated walls and fixtures make it feel old. If you can get this hotel for about half of the going rate and only need one night….I would say it’s fine, but I would not be happy staying here longer. For their regular prices I would never choose to stay here. They really need a god polish to live up to the other Crowne Plazas I have stayed at elsewhere in the world. Also, they really need to improve their customer service on the phone line. As a local resident I would not recommend this hotel to any friends or business associates coming in. Nothing horrible, but nothing to write home about either. There are a multitude better options nearby, but given the rate we paid we were...okay, not happy but okay.

“Nauseating Smell and Weirdly Furnished” We checked in today, so I admit this review is premature. However, first impressions are important so I will post this now and amend as necessary. First, the good news. We had paid for the upgrade to a “fireplace suite”, and our requests for a high floor and upgraded kitchen were met. Sadly, our view was of a dirty roof and the refinery. Our upgraded kitchen was a bar sink, a microwave, and a mini-fridge. No plates or utensils, although I am sure the folks at the Residence Inn I can see out my window have some they might share. The weird thing- the kitchen has a nice wooden floor big enough to dance in but has no table of any kind. The overhead chandelier suggests there once was a table, but not now. There is a formica-covered coffee table in between two odd chairs, but no couch or loveseat as featured in other TA pictures. The chairs are very odd with arms as high as your armpits, (and we are very tall people) and exceedingly uncomfortable with saggy cushions. Bedroom is tiny, but fine. Bathroom is also fine, nothing fancy but adequate. The walk-in closet is nice, but having enough drawers to accommodate clothes for our 4-night stay would have been better. We will live out of our suitcases this trip. The “complementary cocktail hour” is in a really nice basement location. The furniture is the only amenity. Coors and Bud on tap, and the guy fills up a pitcher so that is half foam, dumps half the pitcher, and then pours you a glass of really, really warm beer into a really, really warm glass. Ugh. No snacks of any kind, but there is a guy making the rounds hawking overpriced appetizers. Really? Not even popcorn or pretzels? Makes the Embassy Suites down the road seem more like the Ritz (we have stayed at both those hotels, so the comparison is not just random). HOWEVER, the real problem is the pervasive, foul odor that permeates the hotel. From the moment you walk in it overwhelms you. It smells like a combination of dirty diaper, bratwurst, cumin, and damp mustiness. The worst part is that the windows are caulked shut, so you are stuck with this foul air. The smell is, frankly, nauseating. This single reason is why we won’t return. We could live with the other odd things, but have never encountered a hotel that actually smelled bad enough to take away your appetite.

“Never again THIS Howard Johnson” I thought I might be in trouble when I saw the uniformed security guard in the office that afternoon. I had wanted a downtown, not terribly expensive, "decent", place to stay near the wonderful mass transit system in Chicago. I send very little time in the room so to me decent meant clean, bed, TV, safe. Had bed, had TV, never felt safe, wasn't clean. Walking in room with socks I would STICK to the floor. Safe? Aside from THEM feeling they needed a guard 24/7, the window in the room was opaque, could not look out, did not open. NEVER, NEVER AGAIN. Oh, yes, the location was great, between the Brown and Red lines (two-three blocks in either direction) and not far from the bus line (51? 53?) I could take to my daughter's.

“Not as bad as you`d think - but almost!” We stayed here for 5 nights in September, and having read previous TA reviews was not expecting much. However it was my girlfriends first visit to NYC, so we weren`t planning on spending alot of time in the room. Firstly, the check-in and out queues are as bad as previously suggested. And to store luggage in the lobby before a late flight home was a painful experience. Unlike every other hotel I`ve stayed in I had to PAY for the privilage($4 / bag), queue up AGAIN at check-in to get a luggage tag, then locate the lugage room via an elevator and a creepy walk down in the bowels of the hotel. Also there are no restrooms in the lobby. The staff were generally typical New York, direct and too the point, which is fine, but at least a please and thankyou would have been nice once in a while. The rooms were actually OK. I`d requested a `renovated` room, only to be told they had no such thing - honest at least! However the room was very clean, the TV worked fine, and the bathroom was acceptable for this price. Also, I found the hotel corridors to be perfectly well lit and not at all creep as previous reviewers have suggested. The only negatives to the rooms were the maid service. Towels got less and less each day, bed not properly made and attempting to walk in the room at 8am despite the `Do not disturb` sign! Overall, the location and price means that its a bit of a bargain really. It has a motel feel to it, and its clear the staff do not care. This maybe due to the fact the place is looking likely to be knocked down shortly for redevelopment.. Personally I would pay another $60 a night and stay at the Doubletree Met or Novotel uptown.

“Hated it!” Stayed for 4 nights in an interior facing king. Upon arrival the doormen were totally overwhelmed and we had to drag our bags from the kerb to the front desk right ourselves right past the bell desk where again no one offered assistance. Long line to check so I did the kiosk check in which worked out OK. Then dragged the bags to the lift ourselves. Once we got to our floor our room was on the exact parallel corner and this is a big hotel. I sent my other half to the room about half way there as the carpeted hallways are tough to drag small wheeled luggage on and I had to take a break. One we got to the room it was fine. No safe so had to lock laptop in my suitcase. Did not matter what temp you set the thermostat at the room temp stayed the same. Bed was comfortable. Room on the small side. Wireless did not reliably work 2 of the 4 days I was there. Room would be made up late in the afternoon. There were lines for everything. Check in, line, Concierge, line. Buffet, line. Lifts, line. Escalators, line. Taxi, line. Starbucks, line, Check out, line. These lines could be very long. Concierge was overwhelmed and I did not know if they had confirmed my return transfer or not until the night before and I gave the request to them 2 days prior. The restaurant was marginal and overpriced. Service was sketchy. The bellmen share the same lifts with the guests and I saw one literally pin a female guest to the elevator wall with the cart. They were quick to retrieve my bags at check out but there was confusion about getting the bags in the car to get to the airport. Preserved/plastic plants on the interior ledges are an odd colour and stand out. I did go have drinks and dinner at the Park Hyatt and there is a world of difference between the Park and the Grand so if you have a chance stay at the Park. The rooms are amazing as well. The Grand is simply a glorified people warehouse for conventioneers and should be avoided unless that is what you are here to do or to burn points.

“Horrible Place...” Our flight was delayed and we missed the last flight to our destination and needed a hotel room close to the airport. This one had an easter sale, but i sincerely advise you all , it is not worth to stay here. The location is not safe, there is a stripclub across it and all sorts of duboius lookiing bars around the area. The hotel itself is not safe, the doors to outside do not lock soundly , needs maintenance, and anyone can come in at night. The room is FILTHY..the toilet seat has all sorts of CRUD and SOIL on it. The lounge chair smells of urine and we dare not even walk barefoot on the carpet. One sleepless night, on the stinky bed and pillows. One lesson learned , never again trust these deals , otherwise airport would have been a better option. Same sleepless night but a cleaner bathroom.

“Wyndham in Name ONLY” Won this hotel on Priceline, but was a little leery seeing the reviews on here. My fears started to be realized when I called on Friday, July 1 (check-in day) to confirm my reservation and the phone wasn't answered (12 rings each time) the first two times that I called. Arrived and had a 5 minute wait to check in even though neither of the two people in front of me were checking in, the staff member seemed to have trouble answering the questions and the other woman at the desk was too busy talking to another employee to help me. I finally got to check in and was given a key to a room that was already occupied! Back down to the front desk where I told the clerk that the room was occupied, and she said NOTHING for about 20 seconds, before I finally got "I'm sorry for that". Got to the new room and it was OK, but had problems. The room had a faintly smoky smell, and the closet had a strange, musty smell, so much that I didn't use it. The free internet is wired and very slow. Carpets are ancient and the room as a whole is in need of renovations. I left the room at 10:45 AM Saturday morning, got back to the room around 1:30 AM Sunday morning to find that it hadn't been cleaned. When I called the desk to inform them, the clerk said "Well you probably had the DND sign out when she went by, and she didn't come back. We do have 400 rooms." I tried to get some sleep at this point, but the people from the horror convention started roaming the halls with no regard to noise level. I again had to call the front desk 3 times before getting an answer. Eventually, the noise did stop. As the title of my review states, this property is a Wyndham in name only. A more accurate description would be Motel 6. Do not stay here unless you like disappointment.

“Cheap, 2 star Sheraton” Not up to Sheraton standards. I asked what this hotel was before it became a Sheraton and was told it was a Days Inn. The lobby is nice, but the rooms are total 2 star and definitely not worth the $90 / nt we paid. And the bar closes by 10:00 PM.

“Very Polite Staff But Noisy Hotel And No Late Check Out” The staff does try had and the hotel is in a very good location. However I would not stay here again. I was kept awake until 4am by the guests next door. The were not being loud or rowdy. It is just that they were awake talking in normal voices and moving around. Due to what must be very very thin walls in between rooms I could hear every word and even put in earplugs and could still hear them. I could also hear everything going on in the hallway. Due to the lack of sleep I asked for a late check out of only one hour which was denied. It was the day of New Years Eve but they had rooms left in every category on their web site. The room was tiny even for NYC but it would have been acceptable if not for the noise.

“Strange location, grumpy staff, bad food...” First off, they have created a sort of "hotel ghetto" near the Denver Airport that is neither attractive, nor particularly convenient. I booked at the Holiday Inn, which is directly in front of the more down-market Holiday Inn Express, because of its promimity to the airport. I had a bad experience booking, having reserved a room on either end of my business trip. When I had to cancel the stay at the head of my trip, they mistakenly cancelled the stay at the end of my trip as well. Luckily I happened to notice it when I went to check my reservation online, but when I asked to have the reservation reinstated, it was done so at a higher rate. The woman who "greeted" me at check-in was clearly having a bad day. She was the most grim check-in staffer I think I've ever encountered. But she notified me that I was upgraded to a superior room because I'm a gold level member of their club. The room/suite was quite large but not very well designed. There was a very dark sitting area immediately inside the door with a wet-bar area and empty mini-fridge. The bathroom was OK, and the separate bedroom had a reasonably comfortable king bed, but it was immediately next to the air-con/heating wall unit. Luckily I'm not a light sleeper, but I heard someone complaining on the shuttle to the airport about the noisy equipment next to the bed--so apparently my room wasn't the only one with that configuration. I had dinner at the hotel's sports-bar restaurant, since there is really no other choice unless you have a car--and it was a mistake. Mediocre service; it seemed that most of the beers on the menu were no longer available; after striking out on three brands, the waitress finally handed me her hand-written list of what was actually available. I ordered the ribs for dinner, which were tough and clearly had been microwaved. They were messy to eat, so I went to wash my hands in the restroom, and when I came back, my table had been cleared--including my half-drunken beer. When I checked out the next morning, I asked for the next shuttle to the airport, which is not immediately nearby. I was told that I should have made a reservation the night before, since most were now booked up. It would have been nice is Ms. Grumpy had told me that at check-in, since she knew I didn't have a car. So I had to wait in the lobby for about 45 minutes, and the shuttle was still overbooked, with one elderly passenger having to sit on the step-stool they use to load the van. I got a good night's sleep, but the rest of the experience was less than satisfying.

“Time travel to the 70s in the heart of Boston” The Midtown is a budget-traveler and bus tour standby because of its "cheap-for-Boston" rates and proximity to major tourist sites. The hotel itself is really nothing special and you feel as though you have stepped 30 years into the past when you walk in. It can get a little loud and feels a little outdated but overall it is a decent place to stay and a true bargain for downtown Boston.

“Frustrating and overpriced” I needed an airport hotel to stay overnight so I would be pre-positioned for an early flight one night when an ice storm was pending. I chose the Hilton for it's location (right across the street) and quality (I could get some work done). I booked through the Hilton website, where I am a silver member. This hotel, while clean and well-appointed, is far below the standards set for the chain for service and amenities. It is a sprawling horizontal building, rambling over a hillside with very poor markings. We drove around it several times trying to find the entrance. The checking was slow: they were understaffed and lingered over the many questions of confused travelers while the lines grew longer. The room that I was given turned out to be literally a quarter mile away: across the lobby, around the restaurants, down one long hall, through the convention area, down another hall (at this point a hotel employee pointed me onward as I studied a map), around the fitness center, up some stairs, an elevator, another long hall...amazing! The room was huge but spartan. Internet access was extra !! well over $10 for the night. There are lots of outside lights from signs and traffic, parking lots and streets. Bathroom was as-expected, good hot water and pressure. The morning was the same in reverse, a long trek to checkout, endless lines that didn't move because of chronic under-staffing, and no breakfast snack or coffee offered. The shuttle bus was confusing: but was on time. I'm sorry, this experience was rough, and well below Hilton standards.

“Wasted Potential” The Argent is potential wasted. Rates are usually good but everything else is downhill. Having stayed here 4 times I must say the hotel has issues. If it is full forget getting breakfast, it took us over 1 hour in the restaurant. Rooms can be very nice but once I found rotting food under the bed, once I found dirt everywhere and once my room was triangular/tiny and most uncomfortable. The Front desk staff are useless and expect issues checking in and there is no hope they will solve problems. On the brighter side common areas are lovely, some rooms are great and the bar is nice.

“You have a choice - choose an alternative” If you know and like Westin - you won't like this. Austin has many better properties. Question the validity of the other reviews on the site? Corners have been cut to create a small contemporary version that removes the concierge lounge on the SPG floors, free internet for SPG members and any decent parking. Service delivered by anyone over 17 with authority doesn't exist. Room service failed, the single phone in the room didn't work and a wireless connection took all night . While it's adjacent to the Domain Center... you have to drive over and park again. They've cut every corner, then overcharge for the basics. Shame on this limited partnership owner.

“The heating system bites” The Magnolia is a nice hotel in an older building that's been well-renovated. My suite was spacious, nicely decorated, and had all the necessary amenities. The hotel also has a complimentary domestic beer/wine hour and free cookies in the evening. A free pool table was also a nice touch. The employees were all extremely friendly. I thought I would be giving this hotel a four-star rating, but both nights I had to get up several times to adjust the thermostat. It is a primitive system that fails to maintain a constant temperature. Sometimes I would wake up in sauna-like heat. Other times it wouldn't come back on soon enough and I woke feeling like I was outside in the freezing cold. The second night was even worse when the heater went on the fritz at 2:30am. It began blowing in cold air which was even worse than it not working at all. I ended up turning it off and putting on more clothing before getting back into bed. So, despite the hotel's many good qualities, I would recommend staying elsewhere until they revamp their climate controls!

“Rodeway San Antonio” I visited this hotel as part of an extensive trip around the US, extensive and budget! The hotel looks like one of the motels in a crime thriller blockbuster where they go to interrogate the witness or sleep en route to dumping the body. I can’t say I felt particularly safe there but that may be the motel connotations apparently obvious with this chain… not so obvious to foreign travellers. Anyway a chair pushed up against the door and the aircon on full to block the highway noise and we slept well enough. The city is lovely especially around the riverwalk but a little like Birmingham as an English comparison, its defiantly worth attending the art gatherings at the Star brewery if possible, and free web access can be obtained from the local library. The hotel claimed to have a restaurant but it appears to be privately owned slightly offsite, The lovely Latino ladies of Lulu’s were great fun with the early morning coffee’s, although the memories of chicken fried steak will always haunt me. We tried to use the coin op washer only to get pretty much totally messed about by the hotel staff, I don’t think they had much appreciation for the cleanliness of travellers as reflected in the dodgy bed sheets… thank heavens for the two singles they mistakenly gave us, we could double up on the least offensive looking one.

“Could do better” Our room was VERY small, and had a strange odor, like baby powder. Bathroom was also tiny and smelled like burnt wiring. The floors were filthy! Rooms are definetly not big enough for more than two people. The location is convenient to Medieval Times and the downtown area. The clerk however, did not even know where Medieval Times was. It was right around the corner, but couldn't be seen from the hotel. How could he not know where it was? Breakfast was basic continental. I don't know if the restaurant is still open, it appeared to be closed.

“More Issues Than People Magazine” First, the good news. The hotel is a great historic building. JFK stayed here the last night he was alive and is honored by a cardboard cut out and cool photos scattered throughout the hotel. I had a small issue with my booking that couldn't be resolved by at least three people I spoke with. They like to settle small issue by just saying "no" or saying the issue is fixed, then not doing a thing about it. To be fair, after I contacted the hotel manager, I was refunded the full price of my room, but this could have been taken care of with one phone call. I didn't want a free room, I wanted a great stay at a great hotel. On of the issues with this hotel is the relatively young staff. Historic hotels usually have older, experienced people working there. I did not see this here. As an example, at check in, the young lady said, "You are going to love your room! It looks out on all the city lights and it is just beautiful!" Then she said, "Uh, that is not your room, your room has a view of... actually, it doesn't have a view". Thanks a lot! Nice to know in our price catagory great rooms are available, but we didn't get one. The other issues are noise and security. The escalators up to the rooms are placed so that it is possible for someone to walk in and not be seen by the front desk. I don't know how the group of 8-10 very drunk people got past the front desk and into our hallway at 2:30 AM. The were partying loudly in the room next door until we called security. Seriously, they sounded like a parade coming into their room. After they FINALLY left, the couple that stayed started loudly fighting over the TV chanel selection. We called security again. We finally got to sleep at around 4:30 in the morning. The least thing a nice hotel should do is provide you with a peaceful, safe night's sleep. It is sad to see the decline of such a grand old hotel. I hope the Hilton Corporation puts a better management team in here so it can truly live up to it's potential. I wish I would have stayed at one of the much cheaper hotels in the area.

“Overpriced and Not Very Nice!” Although most big city hotels are expensive, this hotel is way overpriced for what you get. $300/night? Please. The only way you can justify paying that is if you are a corporate dink traveling on the company time. There were quit a few of them in the hotel, including one self-important dink who talked on his cell-phone at the check-in desk, holding up the line. I bet there wasn't even anyone else on the other end! Two of the four elevators were broken during our three night stay, which made it take forever to get up to our room. The room was mediocre at best. Strictly average in size and decor and it didn't even include a fridge or safe. However, you can bet it included the minibar stocked with overpriced items. At least the beds were comfortable. The rooms weren't especially quiet. If there were people in the hall or kids running up and down, you could hear them as if they were in your room. You could easily hear it when people next door or upstairs took showers. To make matters worse, the service was slow, from checking (a huge line) to getting basic stuff like toilet paper delievered to the room (three calls). Finally, the icing on the cake was the 6:00am wake-up call I didn't order, but got! Overall, if you do a bit of searching, you can find both a nicer and a cheaper place. Also, don't expect anything to be complementary with your room. One reviewer said that you had to pay to use the work-out room. I don't know if that is the case, since I didn't use it. Also, I read the fine-print on the hotel key-card holder and apparently, if you don't walk the USA Today back down to the front desk they deliver to your room each morning, they bill your account for an extra $0.75! Give me a break!

“Lousy service” I stayed for 3 nights and had to change the room 3 times, first it was noise coming from the room above me, second it was clogged toilet which they could not fix in 2 hrs, that too in morning hrs.. you could understand, third time it was the shower not working...The hotel itself is great, its a boutique hotel, curtains, linens are different in a better way. All the three rooms were designed with Orange theme...location is good, although it says right in middle of Gaslamp quarter but I would say its good 10 minutes walk...and given San Diego Downtown is not the safest one, I wouldnot recommend walking. There are few restaurent near hotel but they are not the best. Parking is valet only and $32 per night. I dont agree that the hotel matches 4 star quality, service is horrible for the price you pay.. Indigo hotels are nice but this one certainly doesnt live upto all the hypes

“Great Location in NYC ,is it worth the price?” To be fair, the Priceline bid rate of $270 during Christmas week is a great price in midtown Manhattan. The Grand Hyatt has a super location at 42nd and Park aves, and is adjacent to Grand Central Station. For check in which we chose to use the kiosk which was perfect,swift and convenient. From the time we handed the car keys to the valet, to entering our room on floor 16, it only took about 8 minutes. The lobby is impressive,clean and busy with people moving in and out , so this is a great place for people watching. The staff was helpful and smiled even with a full house! Room- This is the major downfall of this hotel. It has nothing to do with the size of the living space or the bath. It is all to do with the cleanliness, which I have to give a 2 on a scale of 1-10. Moldy shower tiles, bath floors which look as if they have not seen a clean mop in years, dust and "stuff" all over fixtures,window sills and with no exaggeration, years of dust under end tables and by heat fixtures. This would lower my rating to a category 3 at the very best. We ate out, and I suggest using Open Table, a internet reservation site which can aid you in finding a great restaurant, not only by category,but also by neighborhood. I found this site about 3 years ago and it is priceless in most cities. You can find restaurants on very short notice and eliminate the waiting game. Reviews are linked to this site,as well,so you should be able to find the right food at whatever price range that you choose. We did eat breakfast at the hotel, which has only one restaurant open in the am and encountered a long line. After about a 30 minute wait, we ate the buffet (at $30 per) which did have a decent amount of choices at typical NYC rates. HINT: Go downstairs into Grand Central Station which has a huge dining,floor with many,many dining choices. Real restaurants, as well as fast food in a historic setting. There are loads of stores underground,as well,so do not miss this detour! Overall, if you are looking for a great location and can live with questionable cleaning of guest rooms, make sure you get a great deal. If not, try to stay at the Intercontinental or Waldorf which are within a couple blocks! This hotel has so much going for it, but the cleaning issue is scary!

“Very Bizarre place” This place is surreal! Our room was very nicely decorated,,,and that is the only good thing I can say positively about the place. Lobby was way too dark and they need to rethink the art they have there...I love art, but it has it place and suggestive nudes do not belong in a hotel lobby IMO. The staff was VERY indifferant and downright unfriendly! I think the owners should have waited til the place was revamped because now it has received so many bad reviews, it will be hard to overcome! Case in point, they ran out of creamer and sweet and low at the coffee area.....I asked if they had anymore and they said their coffee man had not been in lately, I said there was a Safeway 3 blocks away, and they just looked at me, as if to say so what. Hotwire really flubbed this one...they even gave ne a 231$ refund, because the amenities they had listed did not exist..

“She's going downhill” I've been staying at the Omni in downtown Indy for several years. My wife and I stayed one night for a quick weekend getaway in Feb 2011. Our disappointment started at arrival when we learned our reservation was not correct. They had us down for a double bed room when my reservation and profie clearly stated it was supposed to be a king bed. When I brought this to the attention of the front desk they indicated that no king room was currently availble and that the only one that woudl be available was just below the floors being renovated. There was never a note on the website about this hotel being under construction and repairs. The front desk finally said they could upgrade us for a $50 fee but quickly changed their position when I calmly suggested that was not acceptable. To their credit, even though this room was not yet ready either, they did take our bags upstairs so we could go about our day. When we finally made it to our room we were pleased about the size fo the suite. With that said, the room itself was very tired. The televisions were very old (no plasma or LCD's), the carpet was torn in the some locations, and the bathroom was very small and just odd. The room was clean and large but that's about it. The air/ heat sysetm was also very loud and did not seem to do a very good job keeping the room at a constant temp. The room in general was load with some of the construction during the late afternoon. The location of this hotel is great. The staff was very nice acroos the board. We were disappointed to see that the hotel condition has slipped since our last visit. We will likley look elsewhere when we book our next visit to Indy.

“Bad Review before the Stay” This may be a first for me. I am writing a review for this Five Star Hotel because I did not stay there. I made a reservation in May for an August 3 night visit for $288 per night. The room came with a $200 resort credit. I asked for an email confimation when I made the reservation. I did not get it and called back July 28th and asked for it again. Did not come after an hour. Called back again and was told it might take an hour. I asked them to fax it to me. The fax (because of dark background on the print out) was unreadable. I called back again and finally got an email confirmation on my fourth request. The email did not contain the $200 resort credit and included a $25 per day resort fee for such "extras" as "fitness center access, daily newspaper, wireless internet and twice daily housekkeeping service" - things which I would expect as a part of the $288 they were already charging per night to stay in a luxury hotel. The only thing listed on their extras that I would care about was a daily newspaper - and I am certainly not paying $25 a day for delivery. I cancelled the reservation and went to a better hotel, with no resort charges, for less money.

“2 star hotel” The area surrounding the hotel is very sketchy. There, as previously pointed out, is a strip club next door. I almost overlooked this fact due to the fact it is around the block from an in-n-out burger, though! Parking in the hotel appeared horrible. How some of those cars managed to park in those spaces is beyond me. The likelihood of your getting damaged or vandalized given the hotel's surroundings is high, in my opinion. Thankfully, I didn't have a car, thinking I could rely on the shuttle to get me to and from the airport...nope! My flight landed after midnight and their "airport" shuttle ends at 11pm...hmm...After forking over 20 bucks for a cab ride, I arrived at the hotel. Check-in was quick and friendly, and as I was recognized as an HHonors Gold member and received a free soda and could pick offerings from the snack basket. I did receive an upgrade to a 2-king bedroom on the top floor, which was appreciated. The bed was a typical Hampton Inn bed, as was the shower. The bed skirts on the bed base were noticeably filthy, though...yuck! The room had lots of plugs, which was appreciated. The shuttle did get me reliably back to the airport in the morning, though as pointed out here previously, only runs once-an-hour...thank God I didn't miss it! Overall, I would likely avoid a stay at this hotel in the near future, as there are better options nearby.

“avoid if you need anything like internet or even someone at the desk” Rooms are fine. Convenient to companies in the area. Neaby Hilton, Marriott, etc. Horrible internet....slow would be a huge complement. And, if you try to call the front desk for assistance, you never get an answer--no one ever even picks up the phone. Don't know what one would do if there were a serious emergency. Maybe you pay for what you get but I'd avod this hotel

“Staff Saved The Day - Don't Bring A Child!” Please note - the overall rating I have given for the property reflects the stupidity of the Motel 6 website - not the actual quality of the hotel, room or staff. It's cheap, cheerful and good value for money if there's one or two of you - just don't bring a kid! The dumb Motel 6 website allows you to cheerfully book a child in a motel that doesn't have room for them! At no stage were we warned that the property could not accommodate children in any way, shape or form. Staff didn't even have a rollaway bed for emergencies. We were told that it 'happens a lot'. Morons. Whilst I'm grateful that the member of staff helped us move the next night to the other Motel 6 across town (after asking her to call and move us), it was still a totally unnecessary stressful situation to be placed in. This should not have happened. This is basic for a hotel website. It cost us time, money, inconvenience with moving luggage and worry. We were lucky as they had one room left. Had we left it until the morning to book, I think we would have been stuffed. Three of us crammed into a bed for the night, because we were too tired to care after a long drive. On the positive side, the room was very clean, fast (chargeable) Wifi, large range of TV channels but a little cramped. Our room was on the top floor which was away from the noise. Parking is right next door (free with a permit) and you can get a great takeaway pizza from the restaurant behind the motel and water/milk from the nearby petrol station. Buyer beware if you have small ones with you and use the Motel 6 website to book.

“Horrible - Gave my prepaid room away!” Arrived late to checkin for prepaid Priceline.com reservation and the night manager tells me he thinks the other front desk person just sold my room to the person standing next to me at the counter. I'm upset but stay calm and wait for them to book me a room at another hotel. Something didn't feel right so I asked if they absolutely had no rooms available and was told they had nothing to offer. I didn't feel any sense of apology or responsibility from either person. The clerk that had supposedly just sold my room didn't apologize once and the night manager gave me a half hearted apology and actually said "blame the teacher" whatever that meant. I left to go to the hotel they put me in and realized it was a run down motel and I was livid. I went back and let them know I wasn't going to be put in a motel and wanted to be put up in a comparable hotel and was then told that they called every hotel in Austin and they were all booked and that was all that was available. As I'm standing there I notice a guy checking in. When I confronted them about the fact that they had told me no rooms were available I was told that his room was pre-blocked. So a PREPAID room isn't pre-blocked?? Also - if there are no rooms available in the city you GIVE AWAY someones PREPAID room!! Why wasn't I given warning and an explanation as to why I was being put up in place that had the appearance of a 1/2 star motel? That would have done wonders and I would of least understood why they were putting me in that motel. At this point I didn't know what to believe. I was able to confirm that the city was in a sell-out situation but again that perplexes me even more as to why my room was given away and someone else arriving later was saved. The way the night manager handled it was extremely poor and I felt like he didn't show any real concern, care, or responsibility for the situation. Horrible customer service and ruined my night before a big proposal the next day.

“Like trains?” The Fairfield Inn NW on the Mo-Pac is well located for this author's purposes; convenient to 183 via Braker Street and restaurants. Do not miss Sushi Sake if you like sushi, see that review. The staff is friendly and well-trained, and they recognize Marriott Elite members on return visits. The morning breakfast staff is quite good, although breakfast is really not adequate and not up to Marriott's standards. Trains. The rooms are nicer than most FairField Inn rooms, well-appointed and maintained. This author has never had any issues with facilities or rooms at this Fairfield Inn. Trains. Breakfast eggs. The eggs are powdered, the sausage and bacon are unrecognizable. Forget it and go out to eat. There are plenty of good places close, though, so no worries. Trains. This hotel would be much better without the train set in the backyard. The train set is very realistic and runs all night long on the east side so try and get a room on the west side - though the author has never been successful.

“No, thank you.” I stayed here for a night. Wow, really not nice. Small room. Felt dirty. Stained. Grungy. Towels were like sand paper. I think a 13 inch television. I would never recommend this hotel.

“Oh, My. Pictures are certainly deceiving...” I feel for the Blake Hotel. Really, I do. It's an older property, and they've really TRIED, but... well? You can't make a silk purse out a sow's ear. Sorry! So, the hotel is as pictured on the website--however, it reminds me of a line from the 90's movie Clueless--It's a full-on Monet. From far away, it's okay, but up close, it's a big-ole mess. They created a very cool aesthetic, but up close, all you see is cheap materials and shoddy workmanship. OK, so it doesn't look all that good. Well, it doesn't look all that CLEAN either, so that certainly didn't help the appeal. Some of the people we were travelling with were perturbed by the bedroom decor, which consists of a very large, floor-to-ceiling-(nearly)wall-to-wall mirror across from a bed with a very large leather headboard. He found it fetishy in a creepy way. Naive me, I just thought they were trying to make a small room look bigger. The bed was sleepable. There were no bugs, thank GOD. The bathroom was a bit pitiful, but I could take a shower. Breakfast was included in our room rate but was really poor. Not worth it, folks, I don't care how hungry you are. So all of this was reason enough to never stay here again, but then we get to the location. It is on the outskirts of Uptown, just along the freeway. Y'all, it ain't safe over there. And the parking is beyond sketchy. I would never, ever, EVER recommend this to a woman travelling alone. I'm not entirely sure I would recommend it to a MAN travelling alone. The parking situation is just so, so bad. They desperately need to fence it in, light it, ding-dang, provide a VALET for crying out loud (though I don't want the poor valets to get mugged either...). So, my recommendation? Avoid. Yes, it's cheap, but it ain't even worth that. There are other inexpensive places to stay that are safer.

“Irksome, not fatal flaws” We have stayed here before and found it to be an excellent combination of location, value, and amenities. This time we are not so sure. Kudos though to the woman who called us (Sylvia, Stella...sorry I didn't write the name down) ahead of time to welcome us. That was superb customer service, and she is a great asset to this hotel. However, even her excellent customer service doesn't make up for other failings. 1. Valet parking was +50$ (with taxes) which, even for the city, seems ludicrous. We never even took our car out. 2. There is only one comfortable chair to sit on. The desk chair is excellent for computer work, but for cocktails and visiting doesn't do the job. 3. Charging for the Internet is ludicrous. If we had stayed a few blocks away at the Courtyard by Marriott it would have been free. In this era, charging for the Internet is like having to put quarters in the box to make the TV play or the bed shake. 4. Thank God that the windows open, because this hotel is like an oven inside. Even in the dead of winter (and yes, SF does get cold in winter) we could not have survived without having the windows open full tilt. Open windows also helped with the pervasive smell of mold (which is still better than cigarette smoke of course, so Thank You Marriott for blazing that trail.) 5. No ice machines. In the US. Really? When we travel abroad we expect that, but not here in the US. The "butler" service does gladly bring you your allocation of 12 ice cubes of course. Fortunately, there are several Walgreens nearby, and you can buy a 3-pack of ice for less than 3$. And there is no tip required. 5. The bathroom has nice stone work which is going to deteriorate quickly because they don't clean the mold out of the grout. I mentioned this last year when we stayed, we had a different room this year, and the problem was the same. A little Tilex would go a long way. 6. The towels and bath rugs were frayed. Like mine at home actually. But I wouldn't charge someone $200 a night to use mine.:) 7. Check in was S-L-O-W and we arrived about 7:00 pm,, well after the onslaught. And there was only one person ahead of us. And she was checking out. Check-out (once again) could not be accomplished through the TV. Why bother to pretend to offer technology that clearly never works? Overall, there are so many other choices in this area that next time we will want to try something else. Probably we will select one of the "Orchards" properties.

“Disappointing” The online photos gave me hope, but the amenities are sorely lacking here. The walls are paper thin, many rooms face a noisy highway, the Internet was as slow as dial-up, and the parking garage has such narrow ramps and turns that I could barely get a large sedan out of it.

“Defnitely a rip off!” Overall, this hotel is over rated and nothing but hype! The quality and service definitely do not measure up to its "reputation". My partner and I arrive at the hotel after a 18-hour long flight at 8am. Despite our request through email for an early check-in, we were told to come back at 3pm. In their own words, "it's only a request". Can you imagine that we had to comb the streets of new york looking like zombies?? The receptionist was not helpful at all. The hotel was not well kept. The carpets (along the corridor and room) and the place just look OLD! When we finally got the room, it was not the colour theme that we had requested for (if they can't get this right, why bother to ask us in the first place when we did our booking?). But that was the last thing on our mind since we were both dead tired. The first impression of the room was BAD! Carpet is dirty (I wonder how often do they vacuum clean the carpet!). Necessities such as the bedroom slippers are also missing. The toilet door is faulty. The sheets are not even neatly pressed. The gym is pathetic! The treadmill's really old and they have limited equipments. It's okay if you just want a quick cardio exercise and get out of the tiny room or gym . Don't bother about the in-house breakfast! It's US$15 for a continental breakfast... way too pricey. Thank goodness, we didn't pay for the over-priced meal. My recommendation is try the deli around the area. Starbucks, Food Empire and McDonald's are just round the corner. I wonder how on earth does the hotel justify its rates?? There are better hotels in that area. The only consolation is that the hotel is located in a prime area and is near to the subway. The asian doorman is really helpful and friendly (the rest of the staff does not even know what does good service entail). Frankly, the review would have been better if the room rates were at 3-star prices (or even 2-star). Unfortunately, it's not the case. Having stayed at better hotels around the world, the Time DOES NOT offer good value for money. We will defnitely not return to this hotel. A hip hotel? Definitely far from it!

“This is not good hotel” I had the smallest room imaginable in this hotel. I’ve been traveling forbusiness over 15 years and I have never seen a room so small and this was with an upgrade ad Marriott Gold member. The exercise room was a joke the concierge lounge food was a cold Pizza and some crackers, the hotel was unwelcoming as possible, I cannot recommend staying at this Hotel

“Maybe for leisure, but definitely not for business” I had a very important interview in SF and was going to be getting in late in the evening and had to be out very early in the morning. I did not want to pay tons of money considering all I needed was a bed to sleep in. I saw the pics, it looked reasonable. No bed bugs, clean rooms, some blankets, good enough right? Well, almost. The Good: Honestly, the location cannot be beat! literally, you could not get closer to everything you could possibly want. The hotel looks small and old and lives up to those standards. My room was barely big enough for me and definitely would have been cramped with anyone else. There was literally about 18 inches of space to walk around the bed to the bathroom. The door barely swung open because the bed was right there. Of course they have a flat screen, nothing else would fit in here. The room was very clean though and extremely warm, thanks to the old radiator, which brought back fond memories of my late grandmother's very old house back East. The sheets were fresh, bathroom was very clean, etc. The Bad: Others have commented on the noise. I assumed that they have probably never stayed in a highly urban area before. Being from NY, I figured, I had seen (heard) it all. Well, it was about 11:30 when I checked in and there were screaming children singing songs and jumping on their beds. They must have been adjacent to my room because it sounded like they were in my closet. I had to be up at 6:00 am, but decided to step out for a bite and hoped they would be asleep when I got back. Sure enough, they were asleep, but then the clubs must have started letting out and there seemed to be parades of loud drunk folks in the halls getting phone calls and banging on each others' doors. Not entirely the hotel's fault, but it speaks to the quality of the rooms and the clientele. In the morning, I was getting ready to go and called down to the front desk to request a taxi to my interview that accepts credit cards. I had told them that I would need this when I checked in. I informed the lady at the desk several times over the phone that I needed to leave in 20 minutes, at 7:20, in 20 minutes so that I would not be late. For some reason, she called me 10 minutes later and told me to come down quickly before the cab left. I reiterated the time that I needed the cab and she told me in broken English "It is difficult because sometimes the cab shows up early and they will not wait." I asked her to request another for the time that I had indicated. When I got downstairs and asked if my cab was ready she said no and told me that she had not called. She informed me that I could walk down the street and find one, which seemed to be my only choice. The first few did not accept credit cards, and finally, I lucked out and caught one that did. I was not late, luckily, but no thanks to the incompetent employees. Also, breakfast was not ready yet, but that did not really bother me because I probably would not have eaten it anyway. Summary: This place is definitely no-frills, which I expected. Had I been alone and here to party, this would have been great, but I would never stay here with my wife or when in town on business. In those cases, I would definitely stay at one of the nicer places nearby because you just cannot compare to a comfortable sleep before an important 9-hour day. If you are in town and get a really good price (i.e., less than $70) and want to be near the action, book it. But think of it more as a high-end hostel than a mid-range hotel.

“Essentially a Nightclub with Rooms to Rent” The ZaZa has a lot to recommend it. However, the ineptitude of the staff and the tendency to be overwhelmed by the parties they allow to take over the entire first floor make this a hard hotel to recommend. The staff is mostly cheerful, and ready to help, but you'll find they have to do a lot to correct housekeeping and other service errors that shouldn't occur in the first place. Our first night, we had to have the sheets replaced, because the existing ones were damp. Second night, the entire first floor was full of a party with extremely loud music. OK, but it was a private party that completely precluded us from having dinner or even a drink with friends (and, we had to stand in line even to enter the lobby to get to the elevators). That night, the airconditioning was non functional. The staff cheerfully fixed it. The bedside lamps were similarly non functional. That couldn't be fixed. The wired internet was non functional and couldn't be fixed. The wireless was adequate. The room service hamburger was quite good, timely delivered and reasonably priced. In general, the rooms are an odd combination of luxe and cheap. Perhaps just what happens when you retrofit an old building. Some rooms are decorated in a very fun, if ridiculous manner. Some are very large, multi room affairs. But, If you are expecting to be able to shave or put on makeup in the bathroom, or read a book or do some work, you'll find the lightling quite inadequate. I've seen six rooms. None of them has an adequate work space for a business traveler. The windows are not double glazed, so even on the 11th floor you will hear a lot of traffic and other street noise. I would beware of the valet parking. They lost our car the first day, and when it was finally located, I noted that someone had driven 25 miles since I handed it over (I have a habit of noting milage when I give the car to a valet). The next day, the car hadn't had any adventures over night, but, someone had cleaned our my change drawer and explored the storage spaces rather roughly. Despite promises to make it right, we've never recieved the promised claim form, and the hotel carefully explains that they have no responsibility for the valet service, which has been outsourced to another firm. Overall, the ZaZa has potential. Good location, fun atmosphere and nice rooms. But I don't think being a hotel is first on their business plan. Even the front desk folks show a notable lack of enthusiasm for guests, while going out of their way to greet folks entering to attend functions. I think they just want to run a nightclub, and provide rooms for revelers who decide to stay over.

“blood on the sheets” When I checked in, all seemed in order. When we pulled down the sheets of the bed that night we found blood on the sheets. The people at the desk offered to change our room but the kids were already in their bed. (we looked carefully at theirs too, no problem there.) So I had the housekeeping staff come up to change the bedding. This took nearly an hour. No call from a manager. In the morning as I checked out the staff did not have any idea about what transpired. They offered to take the parking charges off of the bill. No manager came out to discuss this and I received no call from anyone. Not happy, no not at all.

“Was OK, But Nothing Great” My wife and I stayed at the Eastgate Towers May 8-12, 2007. The room was very outdated. The furniture was extremely old. The easy chair's arms were worn away from years of use. The two dressers were from the 70's and were also worn and nicked up. Looked like garage sale material for a college dorm. The bed was comfortable but the blanket was full of cigarette burn holes. The carpet was old and worn away from foot traffic. Even the alarm clock was a decade old and didn't operate properly! The kitchenette was not used so I can't comment. The absolute worst part of the room was the bathroom. There was mold on the caulking all around the tub. The floor was old and worn away and the walls had old peeling wallpaper. You didnt want to walk in there barefoot! As for convenience, the subway is about a ten minute walk that I wouldn't want to make in the winter. Cabs pass by quite regularly and the bell hop was nice and helpful. The cleaning maids need to be retrained as they left gargabe next to the bed from the last guest and it remained throughout my stay (grape stems). Overall, I read alot of great reviews on TripAdvisor-thats why I stayed here. I must have got a bad room or the rest of you are liars!

“Overpriced & Impersonal” We stayed at the Westin the night before our cruise to Bermuda. Beause it was my 12 year old son's birthday, we wanted to stay near Times Square. We normally stay at Affina hotels, because of the fine service and great value, but to save time and cab fare, elected to stay at the Westin this one night. The hotel is very modern, but also impersonal. The public areas felt very crowded and the service was very institutional. Our room was small and overlooked the side of a building. The cost of the room was about the same as we later paid for a 1 bedroom with full kitchen on the 33rd floor of the Affina Dumont. When I booked the room, I visualized that we would have a view of all of the crowds and activity of Times Square from our room and this would be exciting for my son's birthday. Once we got there, we realized that it is NEAR (as in a couple blocks) rather than in the heart of Times Square. There is a Ben & Jerry's across the street and a few other restaurants here and there, but you mostly need to walk a few blocks to get into the heart of the Times Square action. The rooms were fine and the bed was fairly comfortable. The A/C was cranked very cold when we came in, so it took about 30 minutes before we felt comfortable in the room. I would not stay here again. If we were to do it over again, I would spring for the $5-7 each way cab fare and stay at the Affiina Dumont or Benjamin instead.

“sure agree with previous review re service” upon checkin, front desk couldnt find my reservation by my name until I presented my confirmation number (and only then it took a second front desk staffer to do so). When a fire alarm went off throughout hotel, guests who went to front desk were told they should evacuate "if alarm going off on their floor" (it was going off on all floors). I left a "please make up room sign on my door when left early in am, and upon arriving late at night found a note under door saying, "we respected your wishes not to disturb you," and did not make up room. room and "sleep quality" ratings low because of very thin walls, through which one could easily hear neighboring room.

“Needs remodeling, once it has the new logo I might go back” We've stayed at this hotel two summers in a row for the same event. I had my 2009 review removed because our stay this year was that much worse. So this place needs serious remodeling. Our room was just old. Old bedding, dirty lampshades, rusty tub, stained counter top, etc, etc. (I'll attach photos) The front desk staff was nice. Slow, but nice. After getting into our room we turned on the tv.
