Problem was the tv kept looping back to the menu. I tried pressing the menu button on the remote thinking maybe it was stuck or something, no luck. Our friend staying in another room actually had the same problem when he checked in. The maintenance guy was really nice. He finally figured out (literally after 30mins) that the problem had something to do with the video game controller. He unplugged it and we were good to go. I guess it wasn't a huge deal, but the menu screen blares and we couldn't watch anything at all on our tv. The beds were comfy so we slept well. We didn't have any issues with springs in the bed poking us. That is once the kids that were running the halls stopped. Our room last year was your basic, fine Holiday Inn room. It was an atrium room so I expected it to be noisy. But, this year not only was our room and furnishing in shoddy shape, but even at the end of the hall on the first floor it was still loud. This place might be great for bringing your kid and all of his/her friends for a party and some unsupervised running through the halls, but that seems to be all it's good for. I won't be back until this place is remodeled. Location wise, I like it. It's close to Costco, chain restaurants, I-465. This place just needs help!

“Terrible service and terrible amenities” We booked this hotel for a family trip to Jacksonville, Florida and were very unhappy with our choice. The hotel is right off the exit but hard to find due to no signage and is located around multiple other "run down" and closed hotels. At check-in the clerks were very rude and unhelpful. They took a long time to deal with customers and were not apologetic. Once in the room, basic amenities such as dish washing detergent, etc. which are common to Residence Inn were not provided. Breakfast was total chaos with poorly stocked breakfast area, lots of mess all over with food all over the serving area, and unfriendly service. We stayed 2 nights and confidently will never return again. A bad experience that I would never recommend to anyone. Stay away!

“If mildew is your thing...” ... You'll love this place! Extremely friendly front desk staff, who even knew about nearby a hidden running trail. Wonderful lush garden courtyard. Excellent restaurant. Convenient to the San Jose Airport. BUT The rooms haven't been updated since the Nixon administration. No elevators, so had to haul luggage up to the second floor. Even though the suicide risk jumping from that height is low, the sliding door was blocked to prohibit access to the balcony. My room had a stale odor that makes you wonder when the last time any fresh air had entered. You've got to wonder who thought sticking a TV high up in the wall would give a decent viewing angle. At least my room faced the courtyard on this visit. Last time I stayed here (not my choice!) my room overlooked the street and light-rail system. No problem with that unless you want to sleep in after the trains start running at 5:30am (or if you are a really heavy sleeper) - DING DING DING DING intrudes loudly as the trains cross the street. If you're bargain shopping, the Garden Hotel might fit the bill. Just don't expect too much.

“Hotel is tired and beat up. Front Desk personnel not very competent” I have stayed at this hotel for a tournament the past three years. What was a relatively nice hotel, is now a VERY tired and not clean property. Furniture in rooms are stained and beat up as are carpets. Bathroom is okay, but areas where floor meets wall in rooms are dusty and dirty. Complimentary breakfast is above average. Free internet in room is good. Great location, but loud, live music from the West End Restaurants bothered some of the people in our group. Also had incident where another guest was given a key to my room. They evidently took it back to front desk and then were sent back up to my room with a hotel employee who used a master key to walk in my room. Didn't realize it until that happened that the security bar that I thought I had latched on my door was broken! Hotel front desk apologized when I complained and did replace the security latch by the time I came back the next night.

“Depressing and Outdated: Needs a Remodeling!” I am surprised this chain lends its name to this hotel: the front lobby is dark and impersonal, it's overly seaweed monochromatic theme is dull to the eyes and the hallways have cracked/chipped crown molding. The positives: check in was easy and they let patiently waited for me to retrieve my bags before I self-parked (I was told valet is $40 a day!). The work-out facility is pretty decent with several cardio machines, weight machines, exercise balls, medicine balls and free weights. The equipment was excellent, but this Westin missed out again because the room was big and impersonal with harsh lighting. Personally, I love natural lighting in gyms, it's more motivating. Like I said before, the rooms themselves were pretty drab; they tried to have a calm, inviting tone to the room but it comes across as tired and outdated. I had a huge room that dwarfed a small double bed; seriously, no queen-size available? The carpet had a large stain in the middle of my room and the seating area consisted of two tiny, uncomfortable chairs. The disproportionate relative size of the room and furniture didn't make me feel at home at all.

“Called ahead in route, no room when we arrived” Called while travelling to check on availability for a family of 5, and were told no problem, we could choose our floor. Got there a couple hours later and they said they had given out the last room that holds 5. Obviously they misinformed us on the phone, or we would have had one reserved for us. They did not try to set us up anywhere even though we went right next store to the Fairfield and they worked hard to set us up as there rooms are made for 4, not familes of 5 like ours. So we saved over $ 100 and stayed right next store where they have superior service. The best part, was they tried to have us park in the parking garage before we were even checked in, so if we had not got a room next store I guess we would have been out the parking fee too.

“Historical - yes; Luxury - no” We stayed two nights over the 4th of July holiday weekend at this hotel. One of the shortcomings of this property was obvious when we pulled up to the curb to check in – the valet parking situation is lousy for this grade of hotel. The interior driveway is closed and since the crew was not prepared for the rush of Friday arrivals, we had to wait in a line amongst the street traffic for our turn. There was no one to help us with our bags but once inside, check-in was professional and prompt. However, in spite of my SPG status and because I had negotiated their lowest rate, we were assigned a NS King on the somewhat shabby lowest level. The room was very small and even thought the hotel has been updated recently, it already appears dated and worn. The bathroom had limited counter space and has a modern bowl sink which seems out of place in this historic setting. We had to run the AC unit on the noisy high setting to get the room moderately cool. I understand that this hotel is used for high profile special event dinners and receptions, but I am at a loss as to why. One of my main complaints about this property is that the hotel lobby environment is not conducive to hanging out and the receception/concierge desks are back in the corners so there is no interaction with the desk staff as the guests enter and leave the hotel. On a positive note, housekeeping was thorough and offered a nice turn down service. As far as location, the hotel is conveniently located on the edge of the Gaslamp District, but it is surrounded by dilapidated and abandoned buildings. Every one that we came into contact with was pleasant and helpful, but there are too many negatives to ignore. Considering all aspects of my disappointment with this hotel, next time I visit San Diego, I would choose the Omni, Marriott or Hilton by the Convention Center or even stay at one of the beach communities like La Jolla.

“Do Not Stay Here” What a disappointment. I was in NYC to attend a conference in the area. I do not normally stay in this part of the city and when I tried to book at the Club Quarters - Wall Street it was sold out. Seeing how close CQ WTC was to CQ WS, I booked there instead. What a mistake!! Like many others on this site the first room I was offered was only a pull out sofa bed. When I called to complain I was told that was what I booked. I was swtiched for a higher nightly charge to a different room. This room was bigger (1803), but was simply not clean. There was a large stain on the carpet by the bed on the floor. Near the desk there were food crumbs on the carpet which remained there all three nights. Oh and to boot, construction was 24/7 on the WTC site. The hotel should be letting people know this when they book. I totally understand that the construction is necessary, but people should be aware of what they are getting into. In fact, when I called the front desk to ask about it on the first night I was told it would stop at 11:00 pm. It simply did not. Stay somewhere else - at all costs.

“My room was 15 foot long by ten feet wide” ... And it cost $350 a night! Am I mad to have expected more? Oh and it stank of stale smoke. Oh, and in this 24 hour city, room service stops at midnight. Useless if your plane into town was delayer.

“Don't stay here!” I've stayed at a number of LaQuinta properties over the years and, for the most part, have been satisfied. This particular property is the worst. Other than a friendly staff, I would give it an absolute zero. The room was dirty and I mean dirty. The blanket on the bed had not been cleaned in a long time and, if you did wash it, it would probably fall apart. The room next to me had a coule who put a dog in the closet that barked for nearly an hour before I finally had that tended to. There was a group of "ladies" in a taxi about six doors down earlier in the evening who were obviously looking for "someone". They were shouting some name outside and the music was blaring. I finally called security on that one. NEVER again will I stay at this nasty place. The cost was still $100 per night....had it been $50, I might have deserved thsi type of setting.

“Check with them after Construction” Did I just stay at the same hotel as recent posts? This hotel is a complete mess. When reservations were made we were hesitant because of the 3 star class rating however it had 4 stars from past guests, so we gave it a try. What a mistake. Let me say first of all the staff is OUTSTANDING and went over and above to make everyone happy. NONE of this is directed to them!!!! I wish I could give them a 5 alone. Bellmen, Front Desk, Maintenence, Housekeeping were all professional and pleasant. With that said, we were not aware until check - in that the water system was going to be upgraded and the water would be shut down from 10pm-6am on Sept.20 We arrived at 8pm and took showers and went to dinner. We arrived back at 11:30 with no water. We brused our teeth, washed faces and used the restroom with bottled water. (People should not be booked in this hotel during this time) No shower the next morning (Yuck) as our meetings were in Wheeling at 7am and we had no water. Can you imagine this? When water did come back on, brown gunk came through and then dirt and sediment the rest of the trip. The front desk area is a temporary location and so cramped we had to step aside to let each other pass. The restaurant is closed however there are many great restaurants nearby. The desk does have complimentary chips, cookies and bottled water. The elevators are all padded and used by construction workers and guests. Doors open on certain floors to show completely gutted fllors under construction. Be sure to keep shades down because work is being done outside hotel also and workers were on ropes outside. We were in 1207. I dont know If we had a new room or not. Some of it looked new and things like a rusted lamp no table, desk, or any surface used to do work or put a laptop on was available. The bathroom is tiny, but has a great mirror. I just dont think they should be open but Ive said that. Great things are: The location, bath products, bath mirror, and STAFF. I am going back to my hotel at 108 E.Superior, and I wish that I could take this staff with me, they could use them all there. I always say that, "You can have the best product in the world, but if you cant back it up efficiently and effectively you dont have a darn thing." In this case I was wrong. The staff couldnt make up for conditions of the construction.

“Hmmmm...probably not again....” I stayed here for 3 nights on business. The Marriott Marquis was charging about $400 a night the week I went (I think it was spring break) and this hotel was about $100 less, so my company encouraged me to stay here. Now, I like the Marriott chain, overall. I play the "point game" when I travel on business so while there might be better choices nearby, I chose here for "other" reasons. The good: 1) Nice bedding and clean room. 2) Friendly and professional staff. 2) Decent wait times for an elevator (which can be a problem in other large hotels in NYC). 3)Quick room-service The not-so-good: 1) Immediate location is not that interesting (and yes, I know this is Manhattan, but I was here on business and stayed reasonably close to the hotel after working a long day). It was too far of a walk for me to see any noteworthy "sites" such as Times Square, Central Park, etc. 2) Building seemed dated and in need of an immediate refurb. 3) Price could probably get something nicer if you aren't playing the Marriott Point game. 4) Rooms were small for the price paid. 5) No view even though I was on a higher floor (unless you like staring at an office building across the street). 6) Overall "old" feeling to atmosphere (and I don't mean the people, just the "tiredness" of everything associated with the property). Will you have a great time if you stay here? Of course. It's NYC and that should overshadow every nuiance I've cited (it just won't be greater because you stayed here).

“Quirky inn” I was booked by someone else into the Tabard Inn for a meeting in DC (due to the inn's proximity to the meeting site). The inn is "quirky," to say the least. I love historic places, but this one needs work. My room (#43) was not particularly clean, the mattress on the bed was hard as a rock, the bathroom was inconvenient (no place to set things down), and the hot water came and went during showers. Noise from the patio, which is part of the restaurant, was a problem until 11 p.m. With some sprucing up--and a thorough cleaning--the inn would be charming. Its location is great, and I loved both the bar and the restaurant, which are popular with local DC residents. I will make a point of eating at the restaurant during future trips to DC but probably won't stay at the inn again--unless I know it has undergone some rehabilitation.

“Nice staff, but horrible hotel” My husband and I travel for work and pleasure about once a month. This is by far the worst hotel we have stayed in. I almost feel badly saying that, as the staff was extremely friendly and nice. We had to wait fifteen minutes for parking, the room was dirty from age and wear, the room lights were dim. The carpet needs to be replaced in room 552. Both my husband and I experienced allergy problems due to the musty carpet smell. There were some mud stains on the duvet. When I used the face cloths they left a cottony film on my face. The bathroom tiles and grout need replacing. The alarm clock didn't work. Someone was vacuming at about 9:30PM. On the plus side, the staff was very friendly and personable. The bed was very comfortable. And the hotel was in close proximity to the Florida Theatre, where we were seeing a concert.

“Hello, does anyone work here?” Everything at this hotel seems slow and staff are nonexistent. Checkin was slow despite an empty lobby, room service doesn't answer, room is ok but ac is a noisy unit like the kind found in motels. This is my second stay and last was the same.

“Not impressed” If you want to get drunk and party, this hotel is great. Otherwise, skip it. Maybe if I had been drunk I wouldn't have noticed the stained walls (really needed a new paint job), the broken faucet in the bathroom, the hardware store special shower head in a tub that was too tiny even for me (just over 5 ft), and the not quite what they were going for decor. And never ever get room service. The BBQ sauce was awful, and my hamburger patties looked like they just took them from the packet and placed them on the bun. Rarer than rare. They had room service late, which was fine because they put us in a room with the ice maker right outside the door (not in an alcove, but right outside) so we were up all night anyway. When we checked in they required an additional hold of $100 for the room bar or whatever. Not thrilled, but didn't mind too much - until days later they still had not removed the charge from the card even though we didn't use anything. After much discussion with the accounting department the charge was finally removed. My only complements were, the bed was decently comfortable, the view was nice, it was conveniently located, and the room service and accounting people were nice. I chose to stay here because the reviews seemed ok and I've always loved the building. I won't be repeating that mistake.

“not the best experience” Below average: I would not stay at this hotel again. The front desk staff were not pleasant at all. The attitudes of the two receptionists (one on check-in, a different one on check-out) were abominable. When I first walked in the door, there was an argument going on between the front desk and a patron. It was noon. I tried to check in; the woman would not even bother calling housekeeping to see if they had anything open. She told me to return at 2. I returned at 2:30. The woman then said that she knew they had rooms because there had been a lot of check-outs. But housekeeping hadn't entered them in the computer yet. Would she call at that point? No. She said that I would have to wait. I sat down right in front of her. 10 minutes later, some people walked in and checked in with a second person that came out from the back office. I then walked up to her and asked, "Are you checking in people?" She responded, "Please wait." I said, "I have been waiting for two hours." She then said "name" and proceeded with check-in. This woman should not be in this position. The check-out staffer was equally ornery and wore dirty and stained clothing. Additionally, housekeeping was subpar. They made the beds; that's about it. They took towels and bathmat; they didn't replace them. They didn't replenish the coffee. They left dirty cups about, etc. The breakfast was ok, but it was uncomfortably crowded.

“Nice Hotel, Horrible Location” Was here for a conference recently. The problem with this hotel is the location. Market Center is really not the center of anything. The hotel itself is nice, but there's no point in staying here as there's nothing around. The hotel offers a free shuttle service to the downtown area which helps, but otherwise it's about a 10-15$ cab ride. There are only two restaurants in the area - Denny's and Buck's Prime (which is actually a good spot for BBQ but they close early - around 8pm) and the Hawaii Spa which is dodgy to say the least. The hotel rooms are nice - standard fare. Didn't use the hotel restaurant or bar so cannot comment on that. The conference room was better than average but they had a cricket infestation which seemed to be a recurring problem. The pool area looked nice but I did not use it. If you are coming to this hotel, I'd reccommend renting a car.

“One of the worst hotels in this area” I have stayed in a lot of Houston hotels, and this place is more expensive than several nicer Galleria area hotels, and does not even offer a free breakfast. The service in the overpriced "cafe" was awful and the food mediocre. Room was old and worn with carpet stains, mismatched furniture and smelled musty. I know Houston is humid but it just smelled bad my whole stay....almost like their carpets were mildewy. Beds, linens and pillows were really old and the bed was one of the most uncomfortable I have ever slept on in a hotel. This was very disappointing for a courtyard....by far the worst I have ever stayed in. I have stayed in several Fairfields that are nicer. I will not stay here again unless my company insists on it!

“Unusually Bad W Hotel” I usually enjoy my stays at the W brand; but not this one. As a top-tier frequent guest at Starwood properties I go all the way back to the first W properties in NYC. The W San Diego is easily the worst of the many in which I have stayed. Things started off badly when I arrived and no one was at the valet station (there is no self parking.) I hate paying 35 a night to be inconvenienced. It got worse at the front desk where I had to fight for an upgrade; I had to take a low floor/handicapped room to get a larger room. I booked the room last minute myself but my platinum reservation agent let me know that the hotel had plenty of rooms in all categories for my stay that night so an upgrade should be no problem. The desk clerk falsely claimed that nothing else was available. Warning to SPG members this hotel will not treat you well. I unpacked and started to take a shower. I quickly noticed that the handicapped shower floor was not angled properly causing the water to start to flood into the bathroom. What a pain. I knew this was not good and called the front desk for a room change. I found out that the hotel had been aware of the problem for years and usually asked to guests to make a 'towel dam" on the floor to control the water. This place is a mess. In order to get a non-flooding room I had to take a downgrade to a standard no water view room. Gee thanks. The decor is odd for a W property. The rooms are white laminate (chipped and painted over) with a chalkboard with no chalk or erasers. Probably too many guests were writing This Place Sucks on the blackboard. I have a feeling W rightly abandoned this decor as I have not seen it elsewhere. The pool, pool area, and the fitness room are microscopic. As if that were not bad enough the entire pool area was taken over for a business meeting. It was really bizarre to be sweating on a machine while a business conference is in session inches away. I cant imagine trying to swim with the tablecloths nearly dipping in the water of the tiny pool. It is so wrong for any hotel to usurp the fitness area and pool area for private parties. The location is off putting as welI. It is next to the high-rise jail and is surrounded by the usual bail bond places and their customers. It seems most of the rooms have crappy views. My first room was of a parking lot and bus transit area. The second room view was not much better. The hotel seemed deserted and had none of the usual W vibe. The restaurants were both empty at breakfast and dinner. I did not try them. This hotel is the worst in the W chain and by far the worst of all the Starwood options in San Diego area. Avoid it, as you can find much better nearby.

“Common Areas Need Improvement” The hotel was a bit worn around the edges. The lobby and hallways were not the cleanest and the parking garage smelled badly. Granted, parking garages never smell great but this one really smelled bad. The common areas looked like they could use a good vacuuming and the carpet needed a thorough cleaning. The room was ok and the location of the hotel is well within walking distance of the inner harbor. However, I probably would not stay there again.

“Night Club with Rooms” This is a W hotel that has had a Luxury Collection nameplate added so they could charge higher rates.The rooms are W decor which would not be bad if that is what is represented. In this case you think you are getting a better class of room for $600/nt but it is a grand lobby with basic rooms. They cater to a night life croud which means music blares until 1:30 in the morning and you are asked to take the staircase and not the elevator because of a style show and bar scene. The maid service is iffy at best with calls to the front desk to get it done. I would say this is the worst SPG experience I have ever had .

“Out of Date - Appeared Dirty -” Warning - I'm about to pan this place. I know people don't like it when people give bad reviews. If you read my review you will probably think "well that guy is picky or a snob" or "this guy is an idiot that has never travelled because look at all the positive reviews". Just so you know where I am coming from and can better judge whether or not you believe my bad review. I'm a 30 year old professional and have done a lot of travelling - some for business and a lot for fun. I'm from Toronto. I've travelled extensively in the United States. I know that this place is a 3 star hotel and not a 5 star hotel. I understand that in a major North American city that $180 is not a lot to spend for a nights stay in a downtown location. All I expect from a 3 star hotel is: clean and current decor in the lobby and rooms but nothing flashy, basic amenities like internet and a desk to do some work on, and reasonable staff that are polite and moderately helpful. If this place had all of these things I would have given it a 5 rating or said it was excellent. I was on my honeymoon and I would not come back to this hotel. My main complaint is the rooms. I'd rather just spend an extra $75 or $100 a night to stay somewhere decent. If I had known what this hotel was really like I would have gladly dropped the extra cash somewhere else. I paid about $180 bucks for a Thursday night stay - too expensive for what it was. - Cons - The pictures on the website are misleading because they don't show you the grungy bathrooms, noisy window unit air-conditioners, or stained carpets. The room also had a musty smell which I might expect in Mexico or South America but not in the United States. I was pretty disgusted with our first room and asked to be moved. The next room was still grungy but slightly better. Honestly, this place needs to change the carpets in the rooms. It could use a complete overhaul, however, it definitely needs new carpets. I know that the rooms are probably just as clean or dirty as any other hotel but when the carpets are beat up and stained it just makes you feel like you need to wear shoes in the room at all times. Both the rooms had a dirty $30 a night motel feel about them. - Pros - Good location to do all the tacky Hollywood stuff (visit Mann's theatre, the walk of fame, etc.). Friendly and helpful staff during the day time. The night time staff llooked like they were into goth, demons and depression. Maybe I'm getting old but I'm not into hotel staff having lip rings and blue hair (I don't know if they were friendly or helpful because I didn't bother talking to them). The pool was open 24 hours (but looked pretty nasty and was more of kids urinal than a pool). Free WiFi for your laptop. Nice soaps, creams, and stuff. Pretty comfortable bed and bedding. Free snacks and DVDs that are available in the lobby. - How is this #2 on TripAdvisor???? - Because of this hotel and it's #2 rating in Los Angeles, I don't know whether I will ever trust TripAdvisor ratings again. Are travellers so enamoured by friendly staff and free candy bars that they overlook the rooms being disgusting and in drastic need of renovation. The only thing magical about this place is that it somehow got a #2 rating on TripAdvisor. Don't stay here if you want to spend anytime at all in your room or at the hotel. This place is NOT romantic. It might be okay for famillies with kids because you can get rooms with kitchenettes to save on dining costs. We just had a room without the kitchen. Overall my 2 rating is generous.

“Just an average hotel” Clean hotel.Boring decor.The restaurant is in the lobby in a strange way.It looks like a hotel from the 60's (newly decorated) but just the lobby,the rest is old (80's). The hotel needs to be redocorated.Free internet. The bathroom ceiling look a bit dirty. Otherwise its like any Marriott.But its a hotel that you can stay but expect nothing wow.Its very plain.

“Disappointed” The hotel is located near by Union Square and Market Street, which was fine. Unfortunately our room was very worn down, and the carpets were disgusting! Internet access costs 5 $ for 5 minutes. There is valet parking for approximately 30 $ pr. day. For breakfast go to Cafe Mason at Mason Street a few minutes walk away.

“Worse and worse” We stayed here for the 7th time in about as many years and this hotel keeps getting worse. The rooms seem to get dirtier each time we visit. There's a Penn 5000 check in counter that's just never open, so you have to stand in line for an hour, just to check in. Front desk was rude, claimed I didn't have a Penn 5000 room when it clearly stated it on my Expedia reservation, so I guess they don't want you to reserve through another site. The bathroom in the room was disgusting; stain everywhere, so bad my wife cleaned it herself right after check in. I can honestly say: enough is enough, this was the last time we stayed at hotel Pennsylvania.

“Great Location, But Watch Your Credit Card Statement” My wife and I stayed at the Westin Times Square for 3 nights in late August. The Good: - Location, location, location. Hotel is at 43rd and 8th which is less than a block away from the center of Times Square on 7th Ave. There's also a convenient rear entrance into the hotel on 42nd street through the movie theatre lobby. - Very comfortable beds. Slept very well. - No bed bugs found in room 4207. We checked very thoroughly pulling up mattresses, etc. - Room was clean and well maintained. Had all the amenities we would want. 32" flat screen TV, coffee and tea, free USA Today, nice soaps and lotions, plenty of desk space, free refrigerator upon request (we didn't request one). We had a view on the 42nd floor overlooking the Hudson. Nice view from up there and we rarely heard any street noise. - Concierge really knew her stuff. She was extremely helpful and friendly to all she encountered when I was there. She knew midtown well and was able to make reservations and offer discounts at local restaurants, etc. The Not So Good: - First and foremost, the minibar charges were a problem. We were charged about $8 after the first day for something in the minibar, but we hadn't taken anything. We opened it to see if anything was missing, but couldn't tell. We did notice, however, that there were half full bottles of soda in there. We called the front desk to have the charge removed and report the half full bottles. They removed the charge from our folio. Then the day after we checked out, they charged my credit card $53.90. I called to inquire about this charge and they said it was for the minibar again. The person in accounting submitted a credit back to my card which showed up about a week later. I can see a mistake happening the first time, but the large 2nd charge goes beyond being a mistake. This is the reason I would not recommend this hotel. Wonder how much money they make from people who don't check their credit card statements thoroughly. Based on their reaction, it seems this happens frequently. - The front desk was efficient, but the gentleman who checked us in seemed put off that there was a customer in front of him. I inquired about upgrade availability since I'm an SPG Gold Member. I was told we could get a room on a higher floor (that everyone gets when occupancy is low). When I asked about an atrium room, he said there were some available, but it would be an extra $50/night. Okay, so much for having status at this hotel. I don't know if it was just him or hotel policy not to provide upgrades to their members with status. This wasn't a good first impression. - The bathroom didn't have much counter space, but it was enough for the items we brought. Not a big deal here. Overall, I would not recommend this hotel only because they cannot seem to control the minibar charges. Either that or they use the minibar as a way to steal from their customers. I would hope it's not the latter. Otherwise, I liked the hotel for the comfort and location.

“Good value, but loud and dirty” Huge rooms with kitchens (table and chairs, full fridge, microwave, dishwasher, etc.), living area (couch, coffee table, flat screen TV), and good size bed. Do not expect that lush Marriott bedding, it is pretty threadbare on top of a hard mattress. Unfortunately, there is a train that runs right by the hotel that is extremely loud. Also, the rooms and common areas were a bit dirty and the smells in the hallways got pretty bad at times - guessing because of cooking. Good internet connection. Free breakfast every morning, and dinner Monday through Wednesday, movie nights Saturday and Sunday. Self-laundry was great and reasonably priced - bring quarters - $1 each to wash and dry. Great location for visiting the Mall and museums. Dismal for anything else - there are really no good restaurants or bars within walking distance. Cab rides to better areas are pretty reasonable. Walk south on 4th Street a few blocks to get to a new Safeway.

“Definately not my idea of a 5 star motel” I stayed here because of the price and reviews but was highly disappointed. First of all, when I checked in, the lady at the front desk asked if it was my first time to stay at this motel and I said yes, which it was. She put me in a room at the end of the 2nd floor hall next door to the mechanical room, not to mention the 8 air conditioning compressor units that were outside both the living room and bedroom windows. I did not sleep well that night. Other problems; no ice in the freezer and no ice machines on the property, the flat screen TV in the bedroom did not work, the light next to the bed (on the side that I normally sleep on) did not work, the sliding glass closet doors would not slide open without falling off their track, no tissue (but the box was there), the hallway and elevator carpet was filthy and not vacuumed, and no USA Today paper delivered to my room despite the advertisement that one would be delivered every morning. And about the "hot breakfast" ...it was horrible. I ended up driving downtown to find some decent food. I will not be back, even if the price is right.

“Lombardy quaint for some, annoying for others” Unless you find hand-operated small elevators and traditional (but dark) decor quaint, do not stay here unless you get a deal of $100 or less per night. The location and the price are the hotel's biggest advantages, and rooms do have a small alcove-type kitchen. The negatives: small, old bathrooms with tubs that don't drain, limited TV choices, elevators that only fit a couple of people if they have luggage, no one to help with cabs after business hours, limited and spotty room service (esp for breakfast) and dark, low-ceiling hallways and bar. I would be willing to pay more for modern conveniences and a slightly less desirable location.

“Velvet Rope Must Go!” What would be a good option if you have reason to be in Hollywood, is somewhat soured by their weird, obnoxious velvet rope convention. At most fine hotels the doorman welcomes you with a smile, yet when you enter the W you submit yourself to their judgment. (on the list? do you belong?) If security is an issue, why not place someone at the elevator? They were clearly encouraging non-hotel guests to mingle in their bars. At other times it was empty. But the ropers were ever present. When we had friends meet us for a drink at the hotel, they had trouble getting in. We were paying guests, they were our guests, what’s the deal? No, I’m not old and hopelessly out of touch (well, not terribly old, I did live through NYC club life in the 1990s and velvet ropes were a cliché even then.) If it’s supposed to make the guests feel important, then they are appealing to a very insecure crowd that likes that sort of thing. I’d stay elsewhere. The rooms were quite fun, though.

“Not good” My daughter myself and family stayed here in Oct 2007 it is an older motel, the rooms were very small and we had to drag our luggage up the stairs, restaurant. was good as was the pool, we were not overly impressed by the front desk service. But we were only there for 4 days so we coped.

“Not a safe hotel” This hotel is in desperate need of a refurbish. Looks as if they recently did major renovations to the lobby area and did absolutely nothing to the rooms. At check in we noticed a few unsavory characters hanging around, loitering, whether they were guest of the hotel or not, I don’t really know. Parking at this hotel can be very dangerous. The parking garage is not well lit and signs warn of not being responsible for personal damages to vehicles. If you are a singe lady and traveling alone, please do not stay here, I live in Houston and can tell you this would not be a good idea. Despite the advertised location,its quite a distance to the Galleria. The rooms seemed dirty and the bed had a sink hole in the middle. The noise from the freeway in front of the hotel will not let you sleep even if you are lucky enough climb out of the sink hole in the bed. This hotel reminds me of those flea bag hotels in Vegas for 25.00 a night...Oh yes, at this hotel you will see first hand Houston’s culture, Pimps, prostitutes, drug pushers and strung out users, and if you’re lucky your car will be there in the morning.

“Dreadful customer service.” Very disappointing hotel. The staff - and I dealt with quite a few - were unfriendly, unhelpful and just plain rude. The hotel is nothing special and certainly not somewhere I'd look to stay again. Food at breakfast was depressingly bad. I don't really have any positives for this hotel other than the fact that it appears to be in a decent part of Philadelphia and it has free wifi.

“Hotel staff apparently stole my iPhone and Kindle from my hotel bedroom” This hotel seemed fine, but I left my belongings in the room before going to dinner, and it transpired that when I returned to my hotel room, my iPad and Kindle had been stolen. I realized they had vanished the following morning, was very distressed, and complained. Later that day, after vigorous pursuit by my office, the hotel retrieved my items. They didn't so much as apologize, and were so inefficient in returning them to me that I nearly missed my plane. The fact that my belongings weren't safe in my locked room, plus the fact that management were unperturbed and not apologetic about causing me extreme stress and inconvenience, means I'd advise anyone to avoid this hotel at all costs.

“Absolutely Pathetic Service” Okay - there was a blackout for 7 hours which was not the hotel's fault but what transpired during the blackout makes me really angry when I think about it. Not once did the hotel try to contact guests over a telephone system that was still working. There were fire trucks outside and alarms going off and nothing - 10 floors on the hotel maybe they could find ten employees with flashlights to go through the floors making some kind of announcement. People who's windows were not facing the right way had complete darkness. People who were entering the hotel during the blackout were given necklaces that you get an amusement park that glows and told to walk to their rooms ! I could go on but enough - you get the message - the hotel did not care one bit for its guests and even pushed people out early the next day offering a paltry free coffee.

“Shared air ducts bewtwen rooms makes for uncomfortable stay” Shared air ducts made for a horrible experience. We had to move rooms 3 times. The air ducts are shared between rooms at least the corner suites. We could hear normal toned conversations from the next room coming from the air duct opening. It was like our neighbors were in the room with us. The only peace we got was moving rooms when no one was next door. According to a staff memeber it used to a UCLA dorm before it was a hotel. On the bright side the rooms were big and well appointed. The property and common area were great. Westwood area had a lot to offer. The staff could not have been nicer in spite of the ongoing noise problems. The noise issue really ruined our stay. I would not return or recommend. In respect to Chill the outdoor ice skating rink over the pool. It is not ice. It is a modular plastic floor that simulates ice. It is not big enough to really skate on. It is the size of a small pool that it was covering.

“Thanksgiving Stay” We stayed 5 nights over Thanksgiving. The big plus is the location. Despite another poster's comments, there is actually a subway station exactly 1 block from the hotel (the F train, 40th St. & Bryant Park station, which is at the corner of 40th a & Avenue of the Americas). Elevators were not great, but not that bad either, except during prime breakfast time. Even then, I think 3 or 4 minutes was the max we waited. The breakfast wasn't worth waiting for anyway. We did eat cereal and bagels, coffee and juice, but the one morning I wanted hot food, all of the food was "out". I'm sure they came out with more, but they should plan better, as the line then gets very long. Three doors down from the hotel is The Croissant Shop which has fabulous house-baked croissants, so mostly we ate there. Service/staff was excellent and friendly with one exception (still friendly, just not excellent). We asked for an additional comforter (for the sofabed, so the springs wouldn't be felt) and an additional thin sofa-bed blanket. The guy at the front desk just could not get it through his head that I wanted a comforter and a blanket, not a blanket and a flat sheet. So, nothing showed up. Next day, I asked again and got exactly what we asked for. The room, when the sofabed is closed, is nice-sized. We ended up not using the kitchen, except for soda. The regular bed is very comfortable. They recently added WiFi. Worked well in one part of the room, not in another. The bathroom is tiny, for one person at a time only. But our biggest problem with the room wasn't the size of the bathroom, it was the fact that the shower was truly pathetic. At first, we had no pressure and only lukewarm water. We told them to call us if they couldn't fix it, and we'd return to change rooms. They called us and told us it was fixed. Ha! (Not). We called again. This time the engineer came right away and fixed the heat issue by tightening a value, but that didn't help the "pressure" issue. The stream of water from the rainshower head was as light as a summer mist, and from the hand-shower so narrow that I could circle my thumbs and forefingers around the water. Awful. I have no idea if other rooms are better, or if this is what they consider "normal", but they will get a letter of complaint from me. I didn't pay $400 a night for the worst hotel shower I've ever had. Lastly, on our last night, the clock radio alarm didn't go off and the wakeup call we asked for never came. I realize these are all small issues (well, except the shower), but all in all, next time we want a hotel in this same category, we'll stay at the Courtyard Midtown East next time (stayed there before and liked it better).

“Consistently poor service and disorganized staff” We stay here very frequently because my sister lives nearby. I've waited to write a review because every time we stay we expect it to improve. Finally we've given up staying here and just drive a little farther to get to her place because we pretty much can't stand it any more. Some things that have happened when we have stayed there: 1. No towels in the room. Call to get some and it takes 6 hours and 5 phone calls to get towels. 2. Call in advance (like a week) to say we want a king and a roll away. Get there to find they have lost the reservation, there is no room for us at all. Show them the reservation with the request for king and rollaway. Be told there are no roll aways and no rooms with doubles because there is a high school convention in town. So there is nowhere for my son to sleep. Can they make up a bed for him? No. Where will he sleep? Not their problem. Have to drive my son to my sister's house at 9 pm (he was 5) to get an air mattress. Argue with the hotel to have them bring us sheets. 3. Have the valet lose the car in the lot for an hour. 4. Have them double charge us on multiple occasions. 5. Get bills from them weeks later for charges that are not ours. 6. Get valet parking comped (see #2) only to have them double charge it later. 7. Be accused of trying to scam the hotel because they are incompetent and the manager has given us coupons for free parking for our next stay and then something bad happens. 8. Find used cosmetics in "clean" bathroom 9. Find someone's underwear in "clean" room I think this pretty much sums up why we don't stay here any more. We've written to management and they even gave us a weekend in an executive suite, but honestly? The service still is terrible and the location is not so amazing that it's worth staying there when you can stay elsewhere and have great service.
“not for me” Again its simply a business hotel you check in and out little soul really

“It sucks, Super 8 is nicer” This place SUCKS.....joke is on you if you stay here. Only reason we did is because we hosted a customer seminar here the next morning. However, if you like staying in your great-great-great-great grandmothers old time shack you would enjoy it. Please see my blog at http://talesfromtheroad-mwalno.blogspot.com/ We arrived late (around 9 pm) and the valet guys were pretty good. I don't know if you can self park the car anywhere close. Valet asked my name and spoke into his headset, but after I walked the ten feet to the front desk the clerk had no clue who I was or what I was doing there (basically no clue at all). She couldn't tell me where our event would be (I like to check out the room the night before) or if anything had arrived for us (we shipped some things). I headed up to the room and it reeked of fresh paint. I was going to call down, but decided I would stop on my way to the fitness center. The itself was AWFUL - could have really used a good cleaning and some new wall paper.....it just looked old and beat-up. Don't ever get suckered into staying in room 827. Headed down to front desk and asked if the room was just painted, answer was "I don't think so", and instead of asking if they put me in a new room that was it. Service = Horrible. The "newly remodeled" fitness center was weak -- very, very small, limited free weights, tread mills/ellipticals, and old weight machines. It would be a disaster if they had a house full of people who wanted to work out. Might be a nice spot if you were over 100 years old! Headed back up to the room and was unimpressed with the shower and bathroom. I would say it was on par with a Super 8. Although breakfast was included in our package, I headed down early to our event. I will say the food for that was great, service was top notch and the coffee cake was so unbelievably good...I also liked the free shoe shine. No way would I ever stay at this location or any Ritz for that matter. Total - $231.80 (room was 208 for the Schwab rate - including $18 breakfast)

“Noisy, old and tired” Easily the noisiest hotel I have encountered in decades. The hotel is deceiving as it has a beautiful entrance and lobby that looks brand new. However, this facade hides an old worn out hotel poorly constructed where noise abounds. They did have location as we were attending a wedding at the Karl Strauss Brewery just across the street.

“Pretty Mediocre” Pretty mediocre. My phone didn't work when I arrived and they couldn't replace it. I called the front desk from my cellphone because they wouldn't answer the Service Express button or couldn't reach the Operator from my second phone. Wakeup call came 45 minutes late. Despite a sign stating there were certain amenities in the room, they weren't there (ie: Panna water). Clean comfortable room but that's it. Not a great advertisement for Westin.

“Not worth the location, the price, your time” Bottom line....rooms were dirty, staff not knowledgable, hotel over priced, never again. The food in latitude 41 was fine. When I pointed out the mold and mildew in bathroom, housekeeping supervisor told me that is what one expects in Columbus. My previous stay at the Hampton Inn, just around the corner had no mold or mildew. My niece stayed in a different room, she found a pack of cigarettes and dirty socks. This is not expected in an expensive hotel. The wall paper in bathroom was dirty and peeling. Everything was just a bit dirty and the service was a bit off. The staff in the rest of the hotel was a beat or two off as well. There was something amiss with the hotel's management.

“OK but room for improvement” Stayed 2 nights in a king bedded room for business. Excellent: Décor Good: Staff. Bed. Desk lighting. OK: Location. Close to the mall but close to eyesores. Internet. Elevators. So So: Housekeeping is not consistent. Lighting by door is poor. Clogged sink drain was fixed but the maintenance staff left the clog blob of hair, etc. in the toilet. I guess it was to let me know they were there and they had fixed it. Room had view of the transient hotels across the street which was at times more entertaining than what was on TV. Lots of street noise (people, cars, trucks, etc.). Shame on the big paint drops on the floor in the bathroom and sloppy paint job in the hallways (paint on the elevator lights, etc.) that make you wonder if they were rushed finishing up. Bad: Trucks would idle outside my window until the wee hours of the morning so if you are a light sleeper bring ear plugs. FYI: The coffeemaker is hidden in the credenza in the entry way. This hotel has very good bones and will improve with age. When the neighbourhood catches up with it it will be a big plus.

“There are better places to stay in New York” There are better places to stay in New York than this Hilton. Like other reviewers I had to queue to book in - for about 30 mins and there was a very long line behind me. The room was very average (not as nice as the Millenium Hilton rooms) although the bed was comfy. The bathroom was small - the length of the bath, the TV had patchy reception, room service was decidely average (as was the food), the bar area felt like being in a mall food court, the lifts were slow and the whole hotel felt shabby. As I was here on business I was surprised that the internet connection had a cost associated with it. The concierge always had a queue and it was also long wait on taxi's. I stay elsewhere now.

“I will think twice about staying here again...” I have always been a fan of the Fairfax Embassy Row hotel in DC. I have stayed here several times and have suggested several people to stay here as well. My latest visit to the Fairfax proved to be extremely disappointing. I am a Starwood elite member, but NO elite member benefits at this property. My room was no larger than 180 square feet and had no desk/workspace, and the layout was awful (the television is placed perpendicular to the bed) so impossible to watch if sharing the bed with someone, and only possible to watch by lying on your side. Also, my room had a horrible view of the back loading dock. This hotel is part of Starwood's Luxury Collection, again, does not give elite member benefits like bottled water, breakfast, etc. What I did get is a room full of dust and a shower full of mildew (please see the gross pictures). I asked to speak to the manager to show him/her my room and I was told they would come right up, but they never did. I love the location, but this property has no customer service. I have quite a few reservations at this hotel in the next few months that I am seriously considering canceling

“Wasn't very keen on this hotel at all.” I've stayed at 5 different hotels in New York City in my various visits there. This hotel ranks as my least favourite of the lot and it had the biggest star rating (4.5*). Right from the time I arrived I felt less than welcome. The room was not ready when we arrived, even though it was after 3pm. When we finally did check in, the last occupant's used old shampoo bottles and soap had not been removed upon our arrival. Yuck! The room itself was nothing spectacular, in fact, the bathroom was in rough shape, very dated and not particularly clean. The charges for room service and courtesy bar items were completely outrageous. I would not stay here again.

“Not worth the money” Stayed here for five days in September. It was our first visit to New York (usually do California) so I decided to pay more than I usually would and treat my partner and I to a high end property. The only thing this hotel really has going for it is it's location and it's architecture. I was very disappointed with the room. It was too stark and modern for my liking. The bathroom was worse. It looked like something out of a prison! Give me marble opulence any day over an aluminium wash basin. The "Heavenly" bed drowned me (I'm 5'4"). The duvet and covers were far too heavy. Before I wrote this I read a few other reviews and was surprised to find that not having your room tidied had happened to other people too. This is the only hotel I've ever stayed in where the room was not tidied upon my arrival back after a long day out. Considering the price they are charging you really don't get much. If you are loaded - go ahead spend your money- if you are on a regular budget I really don't recommend this property as the treat you are hoping it will be.

“Going downhill - lots of better DC options” I've stayed at this property numerous times over the last few years, but my recent trip in the last few days will be my last. I'm not sure if it is the harsh economic times in the US or just the hotel is being a victim of its own success and the owners are being greedy. Check in was warm and welcoming. But there was a sting in the tail. I was told that the internet, which in the past had been complimentary was now chargeable. I don't seem to recall seeing that in the booking parts on the website. And being in the highest tier of the loyalty program and having booked an Executive Room didn't make any difference. I was also told that the Executive lounge was open, which it hadn't been on my previous visits and I had been given vouchers for drinks and breakfast. So you can imagine my surprise to find that the lounge wasn't in fact serving breakfast or drinks. Very disappointing - what is the point in booking an Executive Room if you don't get the perks? I eventually was given some breakfast vouchers but no apology for not being given them in the first place. Speaking of perks, again being an elite member of Priority Club program, didn't result in a room upgrade. It was a nice enough room on the top floor overlooking the park (maybe that counts as an upgrade being on the top floor?) If you like sunny rooms then high up on this side will give you plenty of that. I know that room upgrades are subject to availability, but Hilton does a much better job in telling you if you have been upgraded and if you haven't offering you something in return, But more of that later. The hotel restaurant and staff, were, however, excellent. The Chef, George Lopez, came out and talked with my guests and explained the food which was a real nice touch. They also had a great deal on with a free (excellent) bottle of house wine with two main courses. Can't rate all of that highly enough. The rest of the staff around the hotel were very friendly too. One thing that will impact you if you staff here, and rather confirms my view of margin maximisation on the management's behalf, are the lifts/elevators. Expect to wait an eternity for them even when the place isn't busy (it was my perception that it wasn't busy during my stay.) And expect to be packed in when it is busy. There were only two working out of four and this was similar to my last visit in September. Can't see why it would take so long to fix them - granted an old building but refurbished a few years ago. I've brought considerable business to this hotel over the last couple of years. Not just my own stays but numerous other colleagues who have stayed there and eaten in the restaurant and spent money in the bar. The staff there are all excellent. However, there are better value hotels in DC, where you'll get complimentary internet and faster lifts/elevators. I know I'll be voting with my feet and my wallet. It isn't that I can't afford the internet cost but I feel I was mislead on so many fronts and that the hotel failed to deliver its side of the deal. Hilton here I come.......

“Look elsewhere” Stayed here for one night on business. The lobby is absolutely beautiful so it's a big letdown when you get to your room. Small, crowded, dark, not too clean and very dated. All for $200 plus per night - no thanks. I can also say quite honestly that the person checking us in was definitely the rudest person I've ever experienced at a hotel check-in. Quite a surprise for a Hilton. There's lots of hotel in Chicago - I'd suggest you stay elsewhere.

“Worst Residence Inn Experience Ever” We stayed at this Residence Inn on a trip to the Rose Bowl. First, its not in Beverly Hills it is on a very noisy corner of Pico and Beverly Blvd. There is a Vons market across the street but for everything else you have to drive. From start to finish this was a sad story of poor facilities and horrible service. Check in was fairly easy however I had requested an upper floor away from the stairwell and I got a lower floor right next to the stairwell. The major problems started when we walked in the room (very small and poorly maintained). We found that the cloths rack in the closet was broken and the plug in the bathroom was broken--both things that were very visible to housekeeping. Called down and had someone come up and fix. The next day we had trouble with the safe and happened to notice that a low battery signal was flashing (thanks heavens we noticed then and not when we were leaving at 5:00 a.m. and needed our Rose parade and Rose bowl tickets). Had someone come up and change the battery but again this is a basic maintenance issue. Housekeeping was horrible. Towels were not stocked, coffee pot not emptied, bathroom sink not cleaned, crumbs still on the kitchen counter top. Second night I specifically asked to have more towels delivered the next day as my cousin was joining us. Not only did we not get extra towels but we got fewer towels than the first day. And then there was the parking.--$22 a day for secure parking. Problem was that they kept the gate open all weekend so there was nothing secure about the parking. So people who checked in on Saturday just drove in the parking lot and weren't charged while those of us who checked in on Thursday and Friday paid for the entire stay. Of greater concern were the 40+ car arson fires, some less than a mile from our location yet the hotel didn't keep its garage secure. When I asked, every time I was assured that the gate was being fixed. Breakfast was not restocked. If you didn't get down before 8:30 there was not much left. And I always love the fact that Marriott wants you to reuse towels and sheets to protect the environment, but they use enough Styrofoam to fill a landfill. Just a poor hotel all the way around.

“Don't Travel Alone to this Hotel” ...the staff was very funky toward me and a hat of mine came up missing. The desk staff pick and choose who they are courteous to. When I told the cleaning woman that I didn't need my room cleaned because I would be changing (they gave me a smoking/handicapped room because I checked in early a.m.) she rolled her eyes at me and smacked her lips...if I were her mother, I'd have smacked her on the spot. No movies, no room service, no tub in my room, no map, no hotel directory. On a positive note, good location in relation to landmarks. Thank god because you don't want to spend alot of time in your room. Spend the extra $20 or so and get a better hotel.

“Horrible service at check in and beyond” Check in took 1 hr too get a totally unacceptable room. Requested move and of course more $$$ but worst was the promised noon room was ready at 5pm and took 11/2 hrs to get luggage delivered. Should have stayed at the Palace

“Wouldn't stay here again.” I stayed at this hotel for one night in April of 2006. From outside, the hotel looked ok. Lobby was nothing special as this was a budget hotel but we were really disappointed on the way to the room and when we got to the room. Hallway smelled pretty bad and elevator had some dark gray wood panel interior which almost make you feel depressed just looking at it. Room was pretty small, furniture was super old, wall paper was peeling, and etc. Even the mattress were even. I booked this hotel through hotwire.com and it said that this hotel has a 3 star rating. There is no way this hotel deserves 3 star rating...maybe 2 star rating, if that. Only thing nice about this hotel was the location. There are lots of restaurants and shops in the area and it's pretty close to sea world and san diego zoo area. Overall, I did not like the hotel at all and would never stay here again.

“Waste of time - awful place” The Standard looks like it was decorated at kmart -- all plastic and not really clean. It was noisy, really odd and missing essentials that business travelers need. The hotel staff in general portray an attitude that they are better than their guests. Wake up call was 20 minutes late without an apology. The ironing board was a desk top (hard to iron the suit), the bathroom was just hard to deal with (no kleenex, not sparkling clean tile, no place to put your toothbrush). The bedroom was decorated in inexpensive grey carpet and walls were blemished. The all around step to the bed (without box spring and low to the ground) was easy to trip on (as I did at least twice). I quickly checked out after one night and moved to a more suitable hotel for business travelers.

“Cheap for downtown, but BRING EARPLUGS!” Right next to railroad tracks with freight trains going by and blasting their horn at least once per hour. This definitely kept me awake despite wearing earplugs. On the bright side, the breakfast was good and this is walking distance to some good bars and restaurants in the gaslamp as well as the SS Midway and other ships in the harbor.

“Urgh! Stay away!” The only good thing about this hotel is the location, right opposite Madison Square Gardens. The room was dirty, smelly and noisy. The staff were very unfriendly. I would not recommend anyone to stay in this hotel.

“Poor Service and Old Hotel” I stayed at this hotel for an event happening at the convention center. I have Gold Status with SPG and expected the pleasant room I'm accustomed to when I stay at a Sheraton. While checking in, I was told there was "Nooo way" I was getting a King bed... And that "I was lucky I had a room with the Cheerleading Competition here" (I did have a reservation?). The room was old, and the bathroom was in need to maintained; the bathtub paint (yes, paint?) was peeling and the mirror was dirty. I called down and was told there were no other rooms available. I asked where the rest of my group was going to be placed when they checked in later in the day- in lieu of answering; I was told that maintenance would be sent to address my concerns. I went to lunch. When I returned my mirror had been wiped down and the paint seemed to be scrapped off of the tub. Later in the evening (9pm) the cheerleaders where practicing in the hall. With the extra large gaps under the door, it was very loud... Around 11pm, I called down to ask the front desk, and was told they would send someone up. At 11:30, I called again. At 11:45 I called again and was told that maintenance had come up and reported no one was in the hallway. I held my phone up and asked if they could hear the yelling (they could), and they said that the adults should be keeping the kids quiet. The adults were in the hallway with the kids... I called SPG customer service and they called the hotel... Finally, the kids were moved to the lobby. Restaurant also closed at 11pm- far too early for a business hotel though it's better to leave the hotel, food wasn't great.

“Nice, but high incidental charges mar experience” High quality hotel, but all the very high incidental charges for parking ($27), wireless ($10), bottled water ($7), and even insta-charges if you move any item in the mini-bar ruin the overall experience. The hotel bar charged the room for drinks even though we thought we put them on a credit card. Mattress was mediocre for such a high-end hotel. TV remote was only intermittently functional. Front desk was unreasonable on room upgrade requests, even when the hotel is empty. Clearly they treat Hotwire customers as second-class citizens. They gave us a view of the parking garage even though the hotel was empty. On the plus side, the foyer is great for meetings, the Roaring Fork restaurant is top notch, and the bar deck with a view of the capitol has great ambiance.

“Incredibly Disappointed” My partner, for years, wanted to stay at this iconic hotel. Check-in was chaotic with only one representative working. She, however, was courteous. Our room was not ready, as it was early, so we left bags with the bell desk. When we returned a few hours later the room was ready, so we asked for the baggage to be delivered. It was a king room. Even for New York, it was very small. There was a small desk against the wall, the bed and the flatscreen. No other space. The bathroom had a small toilet, sink and small corner shower. The bath products are Bath & Body Works - not high-end. 30 minutes later, the bags had not been delivered due to bell staffing shortage. Later that night, the heater was making a loud banging noise. Maintenance could not fix it, but offered a space heater for the 17 degree (-8 celsius) night. The night manager acted as if we bothered him and offered us a room with twin beds. Considering the steep price, nasty attitude of the night manager and poor service, we booked a room down the street and left.

“Not so sweet suite” Hotel operated for 3 days without hot water and did not offer any information about the situation at any point. It continued to accept new guests knowing the problems and made no attempt to reaccomodate. The hotel in general is at the poor end of Fairfield properties. Avoid at all cost as there are many other hotels within walking distance.

“nice furnishings, good food and cloth shower curtains that STINK!” Nice big room with fancy furniture, including a sleep comfort bed, BUT, for heaven' sake, if you are going to use cloth shower curtains; take them down and wash them occasionally. They stink of mildew and urine when they get wet; enough to make you gag! Good breakfast that costs extra and parking costs extra as well.

“Won't stay here again” The hotel is fairly clean and tired. The staff was just as tired and unhelpful. My key didn't work on the Hhonors lounge section. The room was small - I think it was the smallest bathroom I've had in a long time. Given I stay in about 70+ hotels a year, this was nothing special and I won't come back.

“Broken thermostats in all rooms and poor house keeping!” I have stayed at the Washington Hilton a few times before The time I thought I just had a room where the a/c doesn't kick in so they gave me a new room but the other room had the same problem! Every time I have stayed here the thermostat goes up and then goes down giving you sweats and for a second you're cool throughout the night it tends to be very uncomfortable! I thought maybe it's just me.. maybe I don't know how to work it so I called for help and waited for an hour (probably bc the elevator is close to a half a mile from the room!) he came in, fiddled with it, and left not a changing a thing! It is most uncomfortable when the temperature in your room is blowing out heat when it is 81 degrees outside and all you want to do is come into a cool room. I didn't receive room service the first day so I also gave that the benefit of the doubt thinking that I may have left too late out of the room but the next day I didn't receive room service either so I called it in and they said they ll take care of it but when I came back to the room the room looked like just the bed was made and sloppy at that! The used coffee bag was still in the coffee machine and no toiletries were replaced in the bathroom and the towels were still wet and on the floor! the garbage was still on the table! This is not my idea of staying at a "Hilton" hotel! What happened to comfort and luxury? I'm really surprised that the company is not on top of this and I just warn you that you will deal with this if you stay here! Its definitely annoying! What an awful experience!

“Unimpressed” After reading some of the other reviews I have to wonder if we were staying at the same hotel. I have heard very positive things about this hotel both from associates and this website and am quite confused as my experience was nothing special. The hotel has a very small lobby that is dark in tone and not altogether welcoming. I didn't encounter any service issues, just felt as though the property itself did not compare to other 4 star hotels in the area. The bedroom was a decent size and looked to be recently re-decorated, but the bathroom was just awful. Despite reading on their website, and even in a brochure sitting in my room, that all bathrooms had a soaking tub and separate enclosed shower mine did not. It had a small tub with a shower head on the wall. The tub looked to be old and had been covered with some sort of vinyl covering that crinkled when you stepped on it. The black and white tile on the floors and walls reminded me more of a dorm bathroom than a 4 star hotel. Having stayed in many of the 4 star hotels downtown, I would say this is one of the worst. The "fitness center" is just an old hotel room that they have placed 4 or 5 cardio machines into with no other changes to decor. It was one of the worst I have seen. The location itself is good and there are a lot of opportunities for food close by, but the same would be true at the Sofitel or The Drake. Overall I would not go back.

“Would not stay again” Stayed here for two nights, some good and bad things. Firstly we got the worst room location you could get, ground floor facing carpark, thems the breaks I suppose. Rooms are nice but lacking a little touch that you would expect at a Sheraton. location is okay, good walk to little Italy but it would be more convenient in gaslamp quarter. then there's the bugs, 2 cockroaches in 2 days in the bathroom, not a highlight.

“Go elsewhere” Got this hotel on hot-wire $43 per night. All I can say is believe all previous reviews and stay elsewhere. We arrived late 10.30pm, got to our room in need of a coffee. Coffee maker did not have the carafe so we forgot that idea and decided on a shower instead. Beware of shower floor, it was very very slippery. Had to hold onto bar in shower to avoid falling. Lighting in room was very poor. Room outdated. Breakfast was poor. Fruit in bowl needed to be thrown out. Coffee - the worst I have ever had at any hotel. Had quick look at pool....would not consider swimming in it. It seriously needed a clean. Slime on bottom of pool. Service was just ok. Don't waste your money Here.

“Cramped and uncomfortable” Making a special effort to login and provide this review because this place sucks. Dropped off outside the hotel by my cab, noted the hotel bar/restaurant "The Daily Grill" as looking decent (which it was - good menu, great happy hour and good selection of beer and booze - three points that were let down by the slow, surly bartenders) and was happy enough with the check-in process - they warned me that my street front room might be a little noisy at night, but if I wanted to wait, I could get a quieter room facing the courtyard. I took the street front room as I needed to get unpacked and to a meeting. The moment I stepped out of the elevator on the 6th floor, things started to go downhill. The hallways are shabby and poorly lit in parts and opening the door to my room, the gloomy interior didn't help. The room was really too small to accommodate the two queen beds and in unpacking, I discovered the only drawers available for my clothes were in the night table and required the removal of the Gideon's bible, yellow pages and a guide book to fit anything into them. The bathroom is tiny and shower was the worst I've seen in a hotel boasting the Handlery's rating. Tiled walls with a corner entrance covered by a thin curtain which failed to get down as far as the lip of the shower tray, thus resulting a damp bathroom floor. Fortunately, the water pressure was so feeble that the bathroom was not at risk of flooding. The warning of street noise was fair, but really didn't affect my sleep. The complete failure of the door to prevent noise from the hallway coming through had already ensured that I woke up when the guests in the room next door discovered their keycard wasn't working. Fortunately, this only bothered me on the first night and I was so exhausted on the second night, that I slept through. Only to discover that the mattress was so uncomfortable I could barely straighten my neck the following morning - I would rate the 45 minutes of sleep I got on my redeye from San Francisco Detroit as superior to any sleep I managed at the Handlery. The A/C was also completely inadequate - it took 2 days of the AC set to 66 before the room became tolerable. Avoid this place - Park 55 and the Westin are both in the immediate area and far superior. I'm also a fan of the Palomar a few blocks further out. If you're looking for budget, there appeared to be a hostel around the corner that is probably an improvement on the Handlery. For anyone wondering why this still gets a second star - I'm trying to save 1 star ratings for anything with a cockroach.

“Decent hotel for the money but be forewarned......” I suspect a lot of people are drawn to this hotel for the same reason I was, the low cost and the location. If thats your goal, then its a deal. For me, though, the negatives, as expressed by other reviewers, outweigh the positives. I too had a left-side room on a Friday night, and the partying at the apartment house next door was in full swing. The parking is a challenge as the lot is tiny and when it fills up, you trudge down to the Chevron station a block away, leaving your car out in the open in a tough area. On the positive side, the place was clean and the beds comfortable. Keep in mind this hotel is like a lot of LA properties that are over 50 years old, so the bathrooms are dated, but you get used to that if you stay around this area enough. In fact, one of th appealing things is the art-deco architecture of this place and others in LA. The rooms have both wired and wireless web access, and, like the parking, is free. Both of these can add up to a lot of money at the chain properties in this town. Front desk is accurate but robotic and not speedy. I still can't find the appeal of Hollywood itself as a reason to stay nearby. The crowd on this Friday night was young and tough and not for kids. While I didn't feel unsafe, its still adult oriented. It dawned on my that most of the other guests were European and didn't know of the option to stay elsewhere and drive to Hollywood and visit, but not stay overnight. The Boulevard may have been glamorous a long time ago but its not now even after being "reinvented" by urban renewal. The Hollwyood-Highland rail station is here too with all that brings to the neighborhood:) The breakfast is coffee, juice and small selection of pastries and not enough to rely on other than get you out the door. Orchid is officially a dead-end street off of busy Franklin, but you can sneak through the alleyway behing the Kodak theater and get out. A better option the next trip will be the Orchid Suites , which has secured basement parking and appears to be more modern, and is 2 doors down. It has the same price point as this place. In summary, OK place to stay if you are determined to be in downtown Hollywood but be prepared for the negatives and ask for a right-side room.

“Process after Process after Process” I stayed here for one night. I love starwood, and I like the location of this hotel, the beds are comfortable, and the staff are helpful. However under the veneer of a newly finished room is decay. The room had glue marks along the ceiling. The wifi is from the stone age, and outsourced customer service in the Philippines that took 30 mins to sort out because I wouldn't allow them to follow me on line to use their service ( they wanted me to enable cookies) and while they were able to sort that out.. and still charge me $16.03, It left me wondering why they couldn't just do that from the beginning. A call to management cleared that up and gave me the internet free from my bill (process)... but whats one day of free internet? Had I been staying here for a week I doubt they would have been so accommodating. At the end of the call the Philippina told me I could call back and enjoy her 30 mins of script reading again if I had any issues ... YEAH!!! nothing like customer service with cue cards (process). There is no bottled water in the rooms .. in a horrible dry climate, and if you're like me and have seen the exposes on what goes on with the drinking glasses in the rooms,,, it leaves you with the flavored water in the mini bar (yuck) or tap to hand .. wait did I just go on a pioneer adventure for 185.00 a night plus 16.03, plus valet? (process) The elevators are run down, the lobby is huge and dated (process).. and it took 40 mins to get my bag from the bellman because of some a process where I as the guest take a number to the check in on the 2nd floor, hand it to the desk person, after a the normal check in process of 10 mins, who then sends them a confirmation a floor below where I arrived to let them know what room Im in blah blah blah .. smoke signals would have been faster (process) the issue is that after you deal with Denver Airport and its HUGE processes, then the laborious rental process and adventure one really could do without more huge process at your hotel... Stay at the four seasons up the street. an even better location ... beautiful rooms, free internet.. and low on the process .... by the time I was spit out the other end of the factory .. I needed a vacation from this hotel ..

“Looking for NY 4S Style Hotel? Go to the Mandarin!” We love going to 4S in general, its a great brand. But this Boston one should simply not carry the 4S brand. As regular 4S travellers, we expect 4S quality and this hotel does not deliver the 4S experience and quality we expect and for which we pay for. Compared to New York and Istanbul for example, the hotel suffers from very old and low quality hotel building. Shower curtains is what we get at Hampton Inn on the highway, not at 4S. The breakfast area is packed with outsiders and the food quality is also not 4S caliber. It deserves to be redone 100%. Bangkok 4S is old and suffers a bit of the same drawbacks. But the service is so exceptional you almost forget the building issues. One positive note: the concierge "David" is top notch and the staff outside are very friendly and helpful.
