But nevertheless I would not return until its been renovated and I would tell anyone looking for the NY 4S style experience to simply book at the Mandarin which we also tried and loved.

“Terrible hotel, only thing decent is the Dome Bar...” My boyfriend and I stayed at the Camino Real over the Thanksgiving weekend. I grew up in the area and so I figured I would pick this place having been there for nice formal events. Well, I guess I'm thinking back 10 years too long because this place has gone down hill. That probably happened when the Westin company left... The rooms are very run down..furniture is beaten up...the beds are uncomfortable, the bathroom, also not great...and the place just felt filthy. You're better off staying at a nice hotel near the airport..or stay in a budget hotel in the area that is newer and cleaner. This place needs a BIG makeover. Oh..and don't even think about using the pool...it's really small and you won't want to sit at it..trust me. The Dome Bar is there..it's nice but not worth it.

“Disappointing” This was my second visit to Cambria Suites. The hotel is very beautiful and the rooms are excellent, but the customer service at the front desk was horrible. The person literally ignored me for 5 minutes when I came to check in. I wrote up a card and even sent an email to Mr Rump. Not even a "received your email" response. The gas station down the street has better service. I am very disappointed.

“Soulless, busy hotel, just about accceptable - in 1979” Here for a conference, work paying the bill. Yet another soulless, frayed large American city-centre hotel. Rooms comfortable enough but all the usual problems, namely long queues at front desk, charming but often clueless staff, and an annoying, sprawling layout which means that if you forget something in your room popping back to get it is a major chore. The gym, a miserable affair, is so far from the rooms it might as well be in another state, and one lunchtime it took half an hour to get a table for food (even though there were plenty of free ones available). That said, the location is pretty good, Stetson's Restaurant is actually pretty good and room rates are quite reasonable. But no one here is trying really hard.

“Free Concert (all night long)” I spent one night at the Omni last weekend after a full day of traveling and didn't rest very well at all. First, the hotel cancelled my reservation. I was traveling with a large group and although they confirmed my room with the trip coordinator, somehow my name was "erased" from the hotel's nightly manifest. After being told that I'd have to get a room at another nearby hotel (apart from the rest of the 100 people in my group), a manager finally "found" an available room. Even after being accommodated, I got no rest. The hotel is located in a prime downtown area and it seems ( as experienced by other reviewers) to be right next to a nightly open-air concert. I mean, I was on the 10th floor and I could clearly hear the bass beats and words of every song sung until about 11:30 PM when I finally just turned the TV up to drown out the sound and fell asleep. Ultimately, my rest was anything but restful at the Omni.

“BAD for Tourists - No where near downtown sites, just those built for locals” "Southie" as it is known, was a solidly working class ethnic enclave for generations of Irish immigrants. The triple decker (often occupied by generations of the same family) is king here, except for some prime oceanfront homes owned primarily by noted local politicians, "king makers" and those who became "lace curtain" Irish somewhere down the road. This tradition has been invaded by outside yuppies during the past twenty years, but the resulting skyrocketing housing prices also brought some upgraded places for foodies and a bit of sorely needed decorum. If you rent a car, you will note the cross streets are alphabetical, the bars such as Amrein's (sp?) are more home-away-from-homes to the crowded urbanism, and the corner diners have some of the great breakfast offering around. Even if you are not "from here" - a question I was guardedly asked upon many occasions - you can still appreciate the interesting, clannish character that it this unique place offers. South Boston has some great attractions, most notably Castle Island, which is a peaceful peninsula which is perfect for walks along the ocean without any audible disturbance from the packed surrounding urban areas. When the Tall Ships come into town this is a prime viewing venue, as some of the ships remain in full sail until just before this marker. Castle Island remains an oasis for generations of Bostonians and newbies alike. If you take a short taxi ride to this place, you will be treated to cheap, great burgers and shakes at the iconic Sullivan's at the entrance to the island. And there are some traditional bathhouses and sweaty gyms along the way, which pepper the long, slim beaches. Unfortunately, none of these studies are vaguely approachable from the Ramada Inn Boston. I felt so very sorry for the legions of foreign and American tourists who may have used this Ramada as home base for the only long weekend they may have had in their lives to drink in the history and culture of my beloved Boston. At the ample and free breakfast Ramada provides, I met a family from Miami who had saved to show the children what the history books scan: the cemeteries where Mother Goose and the Hancock family have graves, the myth of Bunker Hill (the battle was actually fought on Breed's Hill which is a short distance away), the fabulous interior of the gold-domed Mass State House, which looks down on the acreage of the Boston Common (foundation of the modern day rallies) as well as the Public Gardens with private spaces and the Swan Boats which are great for those who want a full spectrumof the gardens without the walk, the street side lounge at the Taj (former Ritz) along the way for some respite. Then the Italian North End for pasta the various fisherman's feasts throughout the street on weekends (to celebrate the catch of the year and give thanks to the Creator), peering in the new money area of the Back Bay along Commonwealth Ave, which was modeled after the Champs-Elysee in Pris and the old money Yankee area Beacon Hill. Freedom Trail Walk, Duck Tours...ya see what I am sayin'? Were this Ramada located next door to the Red Line, or at at-will shuttle to the Red Line, this review would be different. Boston has the country's oldest but quite efficient and functional public transportation system, and it is a shame to be at the mercy of a shuttle to get to it. Like Massachusetts taxes (high but the services more than make up for it) one gets what one pays for in some respects. The property itself was not well thought out in design. To protect from the winter winds, airless vacuums were created that offer no air flow during this unseasonably warm summer. One faces the desert navigating through these tunnels to get to the rooms. The rooms are OK, though I was not excited to take a shower much less a relaxing bath. If you paid more than $99 nightly, go to priceline and start bidding for a property closer to town or at least more accessible to the transit system.

“Lipstick on a Pig” This place is a dump and the title says it all. The carpets are disgusting, the bathrooms haven't been remodeled - they basically replaced outdated tile with outdated tile and cut corners left and right to make the place look presentable. The staff made no effort to be friendly or make us feel comfortable. I had to stay at the New Yorker because my company got a block of rooms at a good price - shocker. If you have a choice, don't stay here. If you are unfortunate enough to book a room here, keep everything off the floor and furniture. I stored everything I could on hangars in the closet. It's definitely one of the most disgusting hotels I stayed at in NY in this price range.

“Avoid the "taxi" service” I stayed at the Mela for one night - Saturday, March 27th. The hotel is fine and even though I've never stayed here, the rooms seem to have been updated recently. Current stylish furnishings in a decent sized room for Midtown NY standards. The bed was great. One big complaint... upon check-out the bellman asked if I needed a taxi and I said yes. He told me he had "taxis" standing by outside. I saw a black town car pulling up and asked the front desk if these cars cost the same as taxis and was told they do. When I asked outside what the fare was I was told $40 flat. When I scoffed the bellman offered me the car for $35 and said that the average fare from Midtown to LaGuardia is $40. This is completely false!!! I take cabs from midtown all the time and they NEVER cost more than $30 WITH the toll and the hotel staff knows this. I hate that they take advantage of unknowing tourists with this scam. Don't take their town car service.

“Never saw the inside” As a Diamond frequent stay member of the Hilton Honors program I had read reasonably positive reviews here on Trip Advisor and booked a three night reservation at this property. In July I called the HH Diamond desk reservation line and asked that the reservation be amended to one night from three as my family member had returned to the hospital with their battle against cancer and I would be returning home earlier. Before allowing the changes to be made to my reservation I asked the agent to make sure that the rate would not change and they assured me it would not. After hanging up the rate had tripled when I looked back at the reservation online. Though the weekend rate for Friday I was requesting could have originally been booked at the same rate for one night or each of the three nights as originally booked. In calling back to the 800 Hilton/Doubletree reservations line I was to told to call the hotel myself as Hilton Reservations couldn’t get anyone to fix their error........ I spoke first with the hotels front office manger first for assistance who said you will have to pay the new rate in our system as we don’t honor our companies booking errors. The General Manager of the hotel also said we will not honor the rate you originally booked with us at our website. Reason given. The hotel is doing better business now since you originally booked the reservation. We are here to make as much as we can on our rooms. However we could rebook the room for 50 dollars off the rack rate for the Friday night. you intend to stay......... Never in decades of travel have I come across such silly behavior with a brand I support all over the domestic US. And booking mistakes have certainly happend before over the years. Needled to say I cancelled and had a fine stay elsewhere. This post is just to make others aware of the less then cooperative business behavior of the hotel and in no way represents the experience inside the hotel itself during a stay. My experience tells me when a hotels management and business culture is this inflexible before the stay I would not want to be a guest inside the hotel and need their cooperation during my stay.It is interesting to note that this same hotel who refused to honor my previously booked and confirmed reservation through the Hilton website had been dumping rooms on Priceline for 50 dollars a night on those same nights.My suggestion is management get a refresher course in a good hotel business school...........

“Party Central...for MTV Rap Videos!” If you have no interest to actually sleeping at night since music will be pumping through the walls due to the clientele this hotel attracts, then this would be the place for you! Objectively - the hotel is nicely renovated, rooms are nice, etc. No complaints at all. Service is on par and consistent with other Westin hotels in major cities so no issues here either (reading between the lines is that Westin service is good, not stellar but not poor either). However, one thing unfortunately that this hotel cannot control is the pockets of clientele it attracts...which is extremely low class unfortunately. Not what I expected given the price point but just picture Jersey Shore / rap video shoot as if this is a party hotel in Vegas.

“Poor hotel for business travelers” The staff was quite nice but this is a not a great hotel for business travelers. It's really just about the rooms. There are only a few power outlets in the room in hard to access places. There is no wireless internet. There isn't actually a desk either - its just a square table pushed against the wall.

“No thank you” Depressing depressing depressing. Lots of parking lots, lots of highway noise. Rooms on the first floor, in particular, felt a bit unsafe. Don't know if the hotel has ever had any problems, but it didn't feel that secure. It's just a Day's Inn, not a five star place, I know, but it was an uncomfortable feeling being there.

“Avoid any rooms under the restaurant if you want sleep” Recently got back from a week long trip to san diego. We stayed in one of the bigger suites of the porto vista hotel with a colleague of mine. We were visiting for Comic Con so the location was a good hike from the convention center but the variety of restaurants in Little Italy made up for it I think. The room itself was spacious, it featured a separate living room with a full size pull out and also a large balcony. The layout of the room is kind of weird, the bathroom door when open blocks the door to the bedroom, so it was kind of awkward. Also for the size of the bathroom they could have added an extra door to it so it could be accessed from the living room without having to go through the bedroom for privacy. The bathroom had separate tub and standing shower which was a nice touch on the other hand. The room felt dated and a bit dirty, the TV in the bedroom is one of those old boxy TV's, and the sliding doors that lead to the balcony looked like they hadn't gotten a dose of windex in ages and the sliding screen was beat up. Then there's the noise. The room sits below the hotel's restaurant above it. They must have hardwood floors up there or something, because whatever the case, when any chairs or furniture moves, you definitely hear it throughout the room. This was particularly annoying considering the hotel's breakfast begins very early in the morning and what I imagine is the staff setting the restaurant up so you wake up to rumbles of furniture moving. This was the major complaint. For $260 a night, I feel like you definitely deserve better. Upon check-out, I noticed I was being charged for valet parking every night even though I don't own a car. They did fix it promptly, but I'd definitely recommend checking your invoice before you head-off.

“Great Location, A Little Overpriced” My wife and I stayed at the Red Lion for an extended Labor Day getaway. The hotel was in a great location downtown. The room size was fine and generally clean but the bathroom could use updating and an good cleaning. If you can find this hotel for an extremely well discounted rate it was fine but I felt the discounted rate we rec'd from the hotel's web site was a higher price than I would ever pay again for a similar property. Have fun in Seattle, it's a great place to visit.

“ok hotel - clean, location bit of walk to anything” the rooms here were ok - clean for the most part. i was there for 3 nights and my room was not made up the first night, but was the other two. this area there arent many restaurants and it is bit of a walk or taxi to get to some. seems this area closes down a bit early. overall the rooms are a little small, had to request an iron to be brought up to the room, other than that relatively inexpensive and not bad option to get to my office.

“So disgusting and dirtly, I left early” I stayed here on business and the room was so disgusting that I, and one other person attending the same meeting as I (we were in separate rooms and had similar experiences), checked out early, and moved to another hotel in the Inner Harbor area. The bathroom was filthy. There was no toilet paper in the holder. I later found the roll placed on the back of the tank. Yeah, maids, you may live like this at home, but please, I don't. The tub was had a ring of dirt around it. The carpet was disgusting and coated with dirt and looked like they just brought the vacuum in for a visit but didn't actually turn it on. I guess they' re saving energy. The worst part was the smell. I had a non-smoking room that smelled like a Vegas casino, embedded with alcohol and cigarettes. The bedspread likely hadn't been cleaned in, well, forever. The walls outside every room had room service trays, some that stayed for days. Can you say ants? cockroaches? mice? I hardly slept at night with the smell and dust. I couldn't leave soon enough and I will never be back. Needless to say, I do not recommend the Sheraton Inner Harbor to anyone.

“Noise from new restaurant” Choose this as thought it was away from the noise of Times Square. However, a new restaurant around the corner, 157 Lafayette apparently opened up. It is more of a club with a live DJ playing loud music through the night. Complained but management couldnt do anything. Make sure you dont get a room facing the back or you will need ear plugs to sleep. Otherwise it is a nice small room.

“Very underwhelming.” After reading the website descriptions, I expected a much better experience here. The lobby was beautifully appointed, and parking was fairly easy, but once we hit our floor I was confronted with a horrible stale smoke odor intermittently dotted with an off-putting commercial bathroom air freshener scent. Our room did not offer relief, unfortunately. I'm sure we broke protocol by opening our window for some relief. I just got a grody feeling. The visible dust bunnies in the lobby and our misshapen lamp didn't help. Their website clearly stated both HBO and Showtime were offered, but only HBO is available. Maybe this isn't a big deal for some, but I specifically chose this place for the multiple movie channels. (That's a sell for me.) Hopefully, someone will give the Riverwalk Plaza some TLC and a good airing out!

“Never Again!” I booked this room via Priceline for $48 a night. When I tried to check in early, I was told to wait until later. When I returned, the front desk said that there were no more NS rooms. I had confirmed my reservation for a NS king the night before as well as two hours earlier. I demanded that she call the Residence Inn which shares the building with the Courtyard and ask if they had any NS rooms. They did but they would not honor the Priceline reservation. I then asked to talk to the manager. Suddenly, the clerk found a NS room with two double beds in the computer. The common areas and the room smelled of body odor, like a locker room. The renovated historic building formerly housed an oil company. The rooms were odd shaped. One side of the building is the Courtyyard by Marriott and the other side is the Residence Inn. An unlocked door separates the two hotels on each floor. They both share the same pool, fitness room, and laundry room. The Residence Inn side get the traffic noise, The Courtyard side gets the street car noise.

“Yuk.” I stayed here because my organization has a contract with them. Unfortunately. I was in a room on the first floor (which always makes me uneasy) and I couldn't open the shades because the room faced right onto the restaurant rooftop patio. Also, I had to go through several fire doors to get from the elevator to the hallway (my other choice was up a flight of stairs, but that's hard with two suitcases). The room has recently been remodeled and unfortunately, they just really didn't get it right...it was awful...it was all shiny and "retro" with a indoor outdoor type carpet, and a divider for a wall (it must have been a meeting room in a previous life). The TV was sort of hanging in the middle of the room, and tacky furniture and lamps reminded me of rent by the hour place--it was just missing the mirror on the ceiling. There was no hairdryer (they must have forgotten to install it) and within an hour of arrival, I saw a large cockroach walking across the floor. The maintenance guy was nice (the one who killed the roach) but the rest of the staff seemed rather bothered by my asking for a hairdryer and for a copy of my bill (which the company paid for--in fact, i couldn't get a copy). Overall, I will not stay here again.

“Not worth it!” We spent more than we usually would ($600/night) to experience the plaza. It was definitely not worth it. The service was average. They forgot our turn down service and were defensive when we brought it to their attention. Because the plaza is well known, the lobby is always full of tourists. Our room was small and dark. The bathroom was very large and almost made up for the tiny room. Other than the bathroom, this hotel was not as nice as many we have stayed at in Manhattan for half the price.

“Nicely furnished, poorly managed. Stay elsewhere” First, this review is for the Washington Hilton. Some reviewers of this hotel appear to be talking about the Capitol Hilton. Don't stay here, but if you do, make sure you're clear to cab drivers. (Locals call it the Hinckley Hilton, a reference to its grim historical role.) The place looks great and has some nice amenities. Rooms are clean and feel new - paint carts were all over the place when we visited, so seems like they're committed to keeping them that way. Sparkling, large fitness center and a nice pool (though don't expect the lifeguards to let you stay in it to the posted closing time - they shut it down nearly ten minutes early, apparently eager to get home). The nice interior is the only thing keeping this from getting a "Terrible" TA rating. The problem is service, and I don't mean the people providing it. Everyone, literally everyone we met was excessively nice and seemed dedicated and experienced. But the people managing them don't seem to have it together and/or they haven't hired enough staff. I could offer a number of examples. Expect long waits for someone to pick up the guest services line. At least twice it took more than a dozen rings for someone to even answer, and neither was at an odd time. I asked around later and the hotel wasn't even full that day, so just imagine what it would be like if there's a big convention or something. At another point, there was a major mechanical problem in our room that required maintenance to fix it, which caused severe inconvenience. At other hotels, for much more minor issues I've been offered a room upgrade, bottle of wine, something to make up for the hassle. The maintenance guys were super nice and took care of the problem the same day, but management didn't even send an apology note. I'm told the interior was recently renovated. But until there's better management of the nice people working there (and maybe more of them hired), this is a no go unless you're forced to or find a truly unbelievable deal.

“Mediocre at best--this hotel left me felling cold” I'll list the pros and cons of this hotel in downtown Denver. We choose it because of the location to the famous 16th St. Mall. The location is good, the room large with many amenities. It should have been a pleasant experience. The valet was nice, the check in fine, and then things began to go downhill. Not with the hotel itself, but with the staff. I'll explain... We ordered dinner from room service—a few minutes later we were called back and told that the items we ordered were no longer available, that the menu had been changed. Although the new menus were not in the rooms. Why not? OK, we'll order something else—no problem. Could we get some vegetables to go with the main course? No we don't have any. What? No veggies? Strange. So we ordered a salad. When the meal arrived there was the entree, the salad, a salt shaker and silverware. No pepper, water, bread, butter—nothing. All for the grand total of $60.00. Not good! The bathroom while a decent size had very poor water pressure. The bed was very uncomfortable, it's a select comfort type—I personally hated it. The room was clean, and had not the other problems occurred I might stay here again, however, when my husband went down to the lobby to make a business call—well, he was treated quite rudely. It seems he inquired about coffee and was rudely told that it wasn't out yet. My husband is very easy going, had he been told nicely this would not have been a problem. It seems that common hotel courtesy has gone the way of the airlines. Too bad, there are a wide variety of hotels in Denver—we'll have our pick and it won't be this one!

“Scans drivers license and credit card into their computer” This hotel scans your drivers license and credit card into their computer. They say it for my benefit so another person can't walk in and pretend they are me. I don't believe that and I don't want to be in their system. It is more dangerous for me because their computers can be used by dishonest employees or hacked and I don't know the safeguards. I asked for the cards to be deleted from the computer after I left but the clerk said they can't be deleted. I'll call my credit card company tomorrow and the North Carolina Chamber of Commerce. The hotel clerk said all Best Westerns scan drivers licenses and credit cards. My room was paid ahead and was nonrefundable. I guess I will cancel my credit card after I get home. I want to inquire at the NC Chamber of Commerce and the NC Board of Corporations to see if this policy is legal.

“Legendary hotel but...” I've stayed at this hotel numerous times for business. This is a strange hotel because of the wide variety of people who "hang out" at this place. This is definitely not a very clean or modern hotel. The premises are kind of run down. The rooms are dirty, the furniture is cheap, the TVs are old, the bathrooms could use a facelift, but at least the beds are comfy. This hotel is more suited for people who just want to hang out by the pool and drink. After all the negatives about this place, it is still a legendary place to stay and hang out, and that somehow makes up for everything else.

“Most horrible hotel experience EVER - STAY AWAY” I really used to like the charm of this inn (even though the outside is very 70s outdated and rooms are odd), but the grounds are lovely and quiant. I have stayed many times, but the last time, was the worst hotel experience i have ever had anywhere. no one (except f/b manager) in the staff cared about our needs or our group at all - the general manager himself was literally screaming at me and threatened my entire livlihood. there were ants in the rooms, broken airconditioners, etc etc They made soo many mistakes on our bills, reservations and even served fish tacos that stunk BAD... they have very serious problems with their neighbors and noise issues - so PLANNERS BEWARE... This is a property that doesn't care to make their customers happy. the resort is in the back of a neighborhood, not anywhere near the beach or downtown san diego.. so there is nothing to do there either. there are sooo many lovely properties in the area- i will never ever go back to this one again.

“Quaint Downstairs bedrooms terrible” We were booked into this hotel for 7 nights, downstairs is really quite nice there is complementary sherry and biscuits available in the afternoon. Most of the furniture looks to be antique and it’s all very quaint. The problem is that the furniture in the room we were in was also of a similar vintage and should have been replaced a long time ago as basically it’s all worn out. We had breakfast included in our room rate and it was very poor quality, the breakfast muffins were mouldy and there were slug or snail tracks over the carpet in the dining area. The staff in the hotel reception were helpful and friendly, but the bedrooms really let this hotel down

“Outdated and Disappointing” I expected a glamorous room and I walked into a disappointment. Housekeeping and Management must not be concerned with attention to detail at this hotel. If you like staying somewhere that the air in the rooms doesn't go down past 74, the closet is 24" wide, all old/dirty brass fixtures, beds that are a little bigger than a twin, showerheads that barely put out water, then this is your hotel. I might be spoiled by staying in Marriott's, but I stay in hotels 1/3 of the year and was severly disappionted. No free breakfasts or a room change will get me to stay here again.

“Sadly disappointed” I read some of the reports on trip advisor and the only thing I can guess is that I got one of the rooms that had not been updated. The carpet is dated and stained, the room had an old musky smell and the bathrooms were dated with old tile and showers. The beds were comfy but that was the only small concession, as the front desk was understaffed and it was hard to get questions answered. I had planned to stay here a week from now and already changed my reservation. Too many other places to stay that are close to the airport to settle for this one.

“Nice lobby - dump of a room” The carpet was old when it was installed back in the 20's. The bed was so old that the mattress sank at least six inches from the edge to the middle. Water was $6.50 a bottle. If I could only use one word to describe this location - it would be "dump". Take lots of ones - everyone wanta a tip. $26.00 to park your car.

“Dirty, dirty little secret motel” I stayed here because of a Suicide Girls pictorial I saw that was shot here. Is that a good reason? whatever. The fact is when In stayed here there were rocker chocks giggling all night in the room next to mine which made it worth while. The room was small, scented of inhabitance past, dark, old and stained which in some weird aspects is a turn on. A pool of tiny measure is in the court yard but I would even think of swimming in it. I guess I would say this place is perfect for a secret rendez vous for nobody would ever look for you here.

“Terrible Value for the Money” The Taj Boston reminds me of staying with your 90-year old great aunt, who use to be a very fashionable lady 30 years ago, but hasn't updated anything since then. Most hotels were sold out for my trip to Boston, so I reluctantly ended up here at a rate of $450/night. The hotel has so much potential if it's owner was actually willing to invest a little money in her, but sadly, this place is old and tired. Location: Excellent. Probably the best of any hotel in Boston. Rooms: Terrible. Nothing updated in years (I doubt Taj has spent a dime on this property since they bought it from Ritz several years ago). Wallpaper is fraying, marble vanities in bathroom are cracked, plenty of noise from the streets coming through the old window, an ancient thermostat on the wall that's older than me, etc, etc, etc. I found the bed particularly amusing: it's the highest bed I've ever seen. I'm 5'9", so not exactly short, but I felt like I had to jump to get on this bed. I can only imagine the difficulty had by all the little old ladies who stay here (as evidenced by crowds in the lobby). Service: Not very good. I had difficulty with connecting to wifi, and nobody in the hotel had any clue what to do or with whom I should speak. I called the front desk for a wake-up call, but nobody answered, so I had to go to the front desk to get it. I went out with friends at night and didn't return to the hotel until about 2am - the front door was locked, and nobody answered the after-hours door bell, which I wrang for about 10 min. Finally, a janitor saw me and let me in. My wake-up call came 10 min early (not a big deal, but seriously?!!). On check out, I asked that my receipt be emailed to me (which virtually every hotel I stay at has no difficulty doing). The clerk took my email address and said he'd email it to me, but didn't get it until after I called the hotel several days later.

“Hated it!” I was looking at reviews of hotels in Chicago and somehow followed a link to a review of the Belvedere in NY. As I read the review I recognized the lobby and rooms from the pictures on line. My mom and I stayed there back in 05 for one night while we were in town to see Mamma Mia. We absolutely HATED the hotel. The location was good, steps away from the Times Square area and an easy walk to the theatre... so if location is of prime concern to you, the Belvedere will do. However... the rooms were ridiculously small and dark, the beds were hard and uncomfortable, the view from the window was the back of the neighbouring buildings. We honestly hated the place, but it served the purpose for our one night in NY. We did travel to NY again in 07 and stayed at the Afffinia - a much better stay, slightly different location (see my review on Affinia). My one caveat is that maybe the Belvedere has upgraded their rooms since 05, but beware...!

“Nice old hotel. Staff at front desk not very friendly. Garland hotel much better place to stay.” Staff not friendly. Long wait for check-in. Would rather be at the Garland Hotel Where they are much more considerate And friendly. Very long wait till check-in. Arrived a little early, about 10:00am After driving all night. Customer service is poor.

“Mold, holes in walls, a Wyndham reservation, paid, that was not honored and an indifferent clerk should be enough for you to ju” Check in was denied even with acknowledged reservation in the system. Clerk said "sorry someone already in your room". Sorry doesn't get it. She expected me to leave with my prepaid nonrefundable Wyndham reservation unfulfilled. I had to demand she call her boss who after discussion miraculously found a room, non smoking. But with two beds and no?t the king I reserved and pad for in advance. The general conditions of the room were not noticed at midnight but the next morning. The aesthetic state of repair is poor. Patches in walls unpainted. Much fuzzy mold in the bath shower. Electric wall switch plates filthy. Foreign dried spots on walls. Dirty and splattered floor and carpet especially in corners. But the place was full in spite if this so why should the ownership change anything? They don't want or need your business. Especially mine.

“Never again” Simply No Good! The cons really outweigh the pros. I should have heeded people's warnings on the net. That same old man was really rude to us. He sounded like he was yelling at me at one point. For whatever reason, the second keycard they gave us was not working and when we went down to the front desk to ask about it, the old man gave us an attitude. Very unprofessional! The room was big enough but old and dingy looking. The bed sheets and blankets had cigarette burns and odd stains. The hardwood floor was nice, at least. Oh, and I did not see any bugs. Location is perfect if you plan on going to Burbank (not too far via the highway) or lots of places in east LA area, like Chinatown (you're right in it!), Lil Tokyo, Downtown, Hollywood, etc. However if you want to go to the west LA area or the beaches, you'll be on the road for a while. And another cool thing is we were right near the festivals and events. We heard and saw bike marathon right outside our window one night, and a few mornings later, we could hear drumming from a Chinese festival happening a few blocks away. Parking is challenging and very squishy. There isn't enough parking spaces, so they squeeze you via parallel-style. Price was $70 or something around there. Should have been lower. It is a motel. There is no security. Some creepy man followed my friend and I to our room! Luckily we locked it quickly but he was knocking a minute after we closed the door. Then 2 minutes later, he was knocking again! Luckily he went away. Put simply, we could have been raped. That was our last night staying there, but I definitely would have found somewhere else to stay after that night!

“Do not stay here if you want to sleep at night” My wife and I are on a 7 week holiday around the southern states and needed affordable accommodation in locations that allowed us to get around without a car. The M Star has very attractive and comfortable rooms ( granite showers etc) and was located near bus stops ( 40 mins to downtown), a mall and restaurants- but that is where the positives stopped. Throughout the 5 nights we stayed there we were often woken up at various hours of the night/morning by very loud ‘beeping’ noises. After the first night we asked management about this and they told us it was our smoke alarm, even though we told them it was coming from outside. The motel has a lot of ‘rules’ posted in its lobby and one was ‘no room changes after check in.’ To this day we don’t know exactly what the sounds were but our guess is some type of alarm in the motel, guests car alarms or a buzzer from the Shell service station located next door- the noises were worse on weekend nights. We were also frustrated with the management checking in other guests at 4am in the rooms next to us when the motel was over half empty. The wi-fi was poor, our dinner tray did not get cleaned in the 5 days, the breakfast was minimal and only ran until 9am and there were ants in our bathroom- we put up with these things as we are budget travelers, and had paid upfront through a hotel website. The management informed us that they have only been operating the motel for 4 months, and taxi drivers told us that it used to be an Econo Lodge. So all previous reviews are for the old Econo Lodge. Basically, if you want uninterrupted sleep dont stay here.

“Great location, but smelly and overpriced.” On the last night of a family trip centered around seeing Mount Rushmore, we wanted to be in the heart of Denver. On the positive side, the Oxford is ideally situated one block from the 16th street Mall (a very nice fifteen-block promenade). It has some wonderful restaurants nearby (Gumbos was a treasure) and is perfectly located for access to the river trail, the performing arts center, and the various sports complexes. On the negative side, there is the snootiness of select members of the staff, a wretched cover-up smell of the room (aimed at hiding tobacco remnants), and a general lack of customer service. When we first arrived, the curbside parking for the hotel valet had five cars occupying the entire section. After circling for roughly twenty minutes, the same five cars were there, including a van for a vendor in their lobby promoting their service. We eventually found metered parking. Upon entering the double doors to the lobby with our bags, we literally bumped into two employees on their way out the doors who rather than offer to assist, instead barreled right past us, not even noticing we were there. Perhaps they were on their lunch break, but the basic courtesy of yielding right of way to people schlepping bags or at least holding a door open as a nice gesture would have been appropriate, not as an employee, but a basic rule of etiquette. While waiting for our turn to check in, two people popped behind the counter to collect documents from a printer. Neither took even a second to look up and at least acknowledge that they were not a desk clerk and that the one desk employee would be with us soon. This set the tone for nearly the entire stay (sans the valet at checkout, who was wonderful). What perhaps is most vexing is that while we waited to check in, we were asked if we needed a house pet by a vendor in the lobby. While we are animal lovers, it felt a bit pressured to be hustled a dog or a cat while on vacation and checking into a hotel. Once in our room, we got a telemarketing call from their spa pushing us to make an appointment. This was after we already mentioned to the clerk at check in that we weren’t interested in the spa service. If they would put half the effort they put into selling you more services while on site into making the stained plastic bathtub and ugly caulking a bit nicer, the rooms would be magnificent. The room itself is very well appointed, except for the bathroom. The psychotic temperature of the shower water is to be expected in an old building, but be prepared for a hot-to-icy-back-to-hot ride in the shower. The only issue we have with the hotel itself is that we reserved a non-smoking room that they deemed to be tobacco-free after unloading enough “air-freshener” to kill any and all insects that may have been living in the room. The fact that only one of three windows opened (the other two were painted shut) didn't allow the fragrance to vent as it should have. All-in-all, it was a very below-average experience. We did have a great experience at the other two Denver area hotels we selected during this trip, but they aren't as ideally situated as the Oxford. Be advised, this is NOT a place to stay with kids. They don’t promise to be, so it’s no fault on their part. If you wish to stay here with kids, plan many off-site activities (which there are several within walking distance).

“Disappointing” Stayed three nights here at the end of June. I was expecting far more, given the numerous positive reviews on this site. My main complaint concerns cleanliness: the sheets and blankets had several stains, and the carpet had lots of pet hair, as if nobody had vacuumed. The halls reeked of cooking food (and not in a good way). Management was friendly, and the internet worked very well. But unless you're staying for an extended period of time (when, presumably, you would be bringing your own toiletries) it's a bit annoying to come for a short trip and have to supply your own bath products and have no housekeeping (especially when the room could have used cleaning).

“Classic old hotel, dated, with few public bathrooms and poor ADA access” I spent 4 days here at a work conference. The hotel is a "Grand Old Dame" hotel in Chicago and still boasts having the largest number of rooms. Rooms are small. Room bathrooms are updated. There are many conference rooms, but all have poor ADA access. The conference rooms are up and down stairs and escalators. I was shocked that there were absolutely no bathrooms near the ballrooms. One had to go down 3 flights of stairs or to another tower. The hotel states it has done lots of renovations to modernize the 1927 facility. They have NOT invested in bathrooms, however, near the conference rooms or ballrooms. The hotel's restaurants aare not good. But, just a few blocks away there are good restaurants. The hotel is located on South Michigan Ave. It's a bus or taxi ride away to the "Miracle Mile." If your budget is limited, than the tiny rooms and challenges of this old hotel may be worth it. Otherwise, I'd recommend something newer, with improved facilities, and nearer the primary end of Michigan Ave.

“AC unit extremely LOUD. Barely slept all night” Stayed here on 8/23 and the AC wall unit is EXTREMELY loud. The thermostat is also several degrees off. I never could get the temp right. The AC wall unit woke me up 3-4 times, making a loud "clunk" when it turned on and then the fan running was so loud it was hard to get back to sleep. The rooms in this hotel are smallish and the decor is drab and simple. Breakfast is good - I'll give them that. Otherwise there are much better options in the HHonors portfolio in the JAX area than having to deal with Motel 6 style Air conditioning issues.

“Blame it on the third party” I booked an Oceanfront Two Room Suite through a third party, confirmed my reservation with central Hyatt reservations and twice with the Guest Services personnel at the hotel. At check in they had me wait 10 minutes due to my reservation being a different night in their computer. They blamed the third party for the mix up and the option they gave me for a different room was not comparable. (made me feel like I was an idiot for booking through a third party as well and the manager wanted to get back to me in 10 minutes when I called because she was too busy working the phones-at a 420 bed fully commited hotel) We ended up with two rooms (standard) and after complaining about the service; free breakfast. If this is a four star property I would like to say that the service was not. Third party buyers BEWARE.

“Horrid” I did not even stay here due to the poor customer service and the lack of assistance. I arrived to the hotel, which is one of the older motor court style hotels, which is fine. I parked and walked into the office and waited .. waited and waited. After about 10 minutes of no help, I opened the door again to make the chime go off, still nothing. It was past the cancel time at this point. I called the hotel directly from my phone and someone finally showed up. At this point I did not want the hotel to retain my business, I asked and told them I would be canceling my reservation with no penalty. The associate at the front desk had to "call the manager". This was "approved". There are better hotels about .2 miles away (SpringHill Suites).

“over-rated, over-priced” On a recent trip to Memphis to visit relatives, I stayed at this Comfort suites becuase my usual hotel (Drury Inn Sycamore View) was booked because of Memphis in May's last weekend. This hotel was double what I usually pay at the Drury, with supposedly the same amenities. After a long drive, I was too tired to check out after seeing the condition of the rooms. When I tried to find other accommodations in the morning, I couldn't so we had to stay anyway. I went to a local walmart and bought cleaning supplies myself and scoured the room myself just so that it would be clean enough to actually stay in. I also made sure that my family kept their socks on at all times because the carpet was absolutely filthy. The only good things I can say about this hotel is that the rooms were huge and spacious with two tvs so that the kids could watch thier shows and we could watch the news, the night desk clerk was accommodating and professional, and the breakfast was extensive and edible. If you don't mind cleaning your own room, don't mind ants all over the beds and nightstand, don't mind overlooking mysterious stains that look like dried blood on the floors and, yes, even on the walls, and you don't mind paying $120 a night for these things, then this is the hotel for you. Personally, it's not the hotel for me.

“NOT a 4 star hotel” Terrible hotel. I've stayed at other Westin's and they have been wonderful. I still can't believe the Westin chain would put their name on this hotel. It felt like kids were running the hotel and they all seemed completely overwhelmed. 1. The bed was lumpy and hard 2. There was no noise control 3. Our room key had to be reprogrammed after every entry 4. The staff didn't know where anything was 5. We wanted a cab and they told us to go get one. They called one after WE suggested they get one for us. 6. The air conditioning was completely out of wack. The heat would go on if the thermostat hit 68 degrees 7. Carpet was dirty 8. Someone spilled some kind of beverage in the elevator and it was there waiting for someone to slip on for over an hour I'm hoping they were remodeling because the overall feel was very generic and had no style. We will never stay there again and I'm very hesitant to ever stay at another Westin.

“Hyatt, you can do better!” I wanted to like this hotel. I usually like Hyatts. I couldn't find much to like here. Pros: - Fabulous location - Decent-sized room by Manhattan standards Cons: - Condition of room and common areas. Many things are just too worn or sloppy. For example, cracked tiles and peeling paint in the bathroom. An HVAC unit that looks like it could have flown on an Apollo mission. A clock radio that refused to display the correct time. Thin walls. I could go on... - Indifferent service. P.S. If you bring a car, the hotel will charge you $50/day to park it. Welcome to New York!

“Not bad, not great, good location” We were originally going to stay here for 3 nights after a cruise. Arrived before noon and were given an accessible room with 2 beds as requested. All the accessible rooms connect and of course there were loud people in the room next to us..as well as all around us. As a Platinum Marriott member I got nothing...no upgrade, nada! And come to find out I should have gotten discount coupons for the restaurant. The rooms are pretty basic courtyard rooms...on the ugly side without much atmosphere. I have stayed in better Courtyards! Most of the stadd was nice if a little clueless. One supervisor was rather short with many guests....somewhat unprofessional in his demeanor. The hotel is located near a CVS, Whole Foods and lots of restaurants. The mexican place around the corner was very good but hte burger place next door was lousy. It's about a 20 minute walk over to the fun stuff in Inner Harbor. There is plenty to occupy people in the Harbor East area though. All in all, I will most likely not return. We moved to the Renaissance where I am at least in the middle of things, in a nice room with a view. I will review this property after checkout. Parking at the CY is 22 dollars a day-we did not have a car to park though luckily. I used a reward from Marriott to pay for the room and as I changed my reservation, the desk clerk had to call the hotline to find out how to handle my certificate. (She originally said that there was no one at Marriott Rewards on a Saturday to help which I knew was not the case.) The hotel isn't that bad and can be a good value. The location is fine, but we were disappointed in the overall experience and will not stay there again. The rooms need updating. They do have a flat screen TV and decent selection of channels though! Didn't eat breakfast in the hotel so I am not sure if it is any good.

“Would have been four stars if the room didn't need work” Was here for a convention for one night before switching to the Omni (which was closer to the convention center). The lobby is beautiful and the staff wonderful. My room however had a couple issues that showed lack of concern by the hotel (cleaning staff and/or maintenance). First the rubber seal under my room door was half off, causing it to drag whenever the door was opened or closed (and made closing the door harder). Second the access panel under my sink was open and would not close (did find a bottle of water in there however :) ). Each and every day the cleaning staff go in and out of that room - how could they not notice this and report it? That said, if the room had been in good working condition, this would certainly be a four star hotel.

“Location-A; Room-C” Stayed here with business colleagues. I came late, they came earlier, reported the dinner was excellent. My room, as others have reported, was quite small, with a great deal of street noise. The TV was laughably tiny, and I was nearly scalded by a overly hot shower. The location is great for exploring Boston, but Boston is so small, with good transportation, that you really can stay anywhere. (I used to live there) My room rate included a full breakfast, which was quite good. Overall, while I liked the food and the location, and would eat at the Bistro, I doubt I'd go out of my way to stay there again.

“Great location and lobby. Room below expectations” Disappointing room by Marriott standards but being just a five minute walk from the Sears tower and a few minutes walk from subway this is perfect for the tourist and would have have been a 5 but for the room. The smart lobby is huge and includes a large bar, Starbucks and at the weekend I was there the place had quite a buzz. My room on the 40? something floor was perfectly adequate but below expectations for both decor and linen but being such a big hotel one could assume this varies throughout and I maybe I got unlucky or maybe it was the small window that gave the room a gloomy feel, however, the aircon was quiet and efficient. I stayed here maybe 3 years previous and did not recollect having same impression about the room.

“Wonderful staff. Wish the bed was more comfortable.” Front desk staff was super nice. Parking and wifi were free. Hotel is small and cozy. Only complaint is that the bed was in need of a new mattress.

“For a Westin, it's tired and desperately needs an update” I think another review said it best but it appears that they recently updated this hotel and put all the money into the lobby. The lobby is great but once you're in the rooms, I could have sworn I was staying at a Sheraton by the airport. I'll start with the positives. Check-in was easy and friendly and they informed me that I would get free internet because of my Starwood membership. The rooms are very large for a hotel in any big city and the bathroom was also just as big. The fitness center is one of the best hotel fitness centers I've been to. There are multiple machines of all kinds (treadmill, elliptical, bikes) and they have a nice size weight room. The equipment was well kept and all high tech. I also like that they give you a complimentary bottle of water each day. Location is great for tourists. It's across the street from the Hancock Tower and on the Magnificient Mile. Walking distance to lots of attractions and shopping. Now for the negatives: the room itself was very average for a Westin. Everything in the room was old except for the TV. Some of the money used to make the lobby fabulous should have been used to at least update the furniture and the carpet in these rooms. Yes the bed is a Heavenly Bed but this was anything but heavenly. The way the beds are made, it is clear that the pillows are super old as they were yelllowed and stained (the pillowcases don't cover the pillows so you can see it!). My duvet was stained and it was obviously that they don't change those during each guest stay. Yuck! Check-out was a nightmare because there was only one person at front desk and her time was dominated by someone who had an issue that couldn't be resolved immediately. Took 10-12 minutes for them to send a second person out and by then there was a line of at least 8 people. Unfortunately this hotel doesn't give you a copy of your hotel bill under your door the night before you check-out so you can't leave without speaking to someone. I've stayed in a number of Westins in different countries and by far, this one did not live up to the chain's standards.

“They try hard” Stayed in room 1723 for two nights while on a business trip to Boston. The Hyatt was the only hotel in the central part of downtown with a decent rate for the nights I wanted. I found the hotel to be very quiet and comfortable, with a staff that tries hard to ensure you have a pleasant stay. I did have some issues about the neighborhood, however. I was out walking after an early dinner (it was still light out) and was approached by a man in front of the nearby abandoned Paramount Theater who asked for money in a very aggressive way. The sidewalks around the Hyatt were littered with trash both days I was there and even the cab driver said "this is not the best part of Boston". But the Ritz Carlton is only three blocks away, so it seems the area is on the upswing. I recommend this hotel but be careful in the area at night.

“Phenomenal Location but quite Pricey” Situated in the Back Bay area of Beantown, the Sheraton Boston offers two towers of lodging. Upon arrival, a front desk attendant warmly greeted me and obliged my request to be on a high floor. Not only was I placed on a high floor (28th), I was also rewarded with a room on the Starwood Preferred Guest Level in the south tower (Smiling helps when requesting a room upgrade). My room was very spacious (double beds) and had a partial view of Charles River. If you want an unobstructed view of the river, request a room in the north tower. The closet was big, as was the bathroom. I did notice a botched patchwork job in the bathroom, which alarmed me, since the room was quite pricey. Despite the dated décor and inadequate soundproofing, the hotel is conveniently located. I was in town for a conference at the Hynes Convention Center and the weather was horrible. To my surprise, the hotel is connected to a mall and the convention center. Be warned, this is not a sexy hotel but a business hotel with a lot of people walking around with conference badges. I did enjoy the free Wi-Fi in the lobby, as did a host of other travelers who didn’t want to pay the premium to surf the web in their rooms. I did take advantage of the gym, which is located on the 5th floor and divided into two rooms by an indoor pool. The equipment looked new and there was plenty of it to accommodate a large crowd of exercise-addicted travelers. Overall, my two-night stay was pleasant and I would recommend this hotel to people who don’t mind spending a lot of money for location.

“Simple, effective, and did the job - but nothing special” Good location, good enough hotel, clean, and did the job. Sort of similar to one of those hotels you'd stay on I-95 but a bit cleaner and larger. The front desk staff at night were useless and the restaurant was incredibly expensive. Otherwise, cheap and effective hotel.

“A privately owned Super 8” Nothing special about this hotel. It looks like a Super 8 that was privately purchased. It was clean and a place to sleep but nothing else. The toiletries were very cheap (I don't expect much from a hotel, but these were worse than most) and there was no blow dryer in the room. There was also a large gouge out of the toilet seat which looked tacky, cheap and unclean. The air conditioner/heater did not have a thermostat, only an on/off, so it was very hard to control the temperature in the room. It also smelled slightly musty. The area itself has a few restaurants and bars within a few blocks, but overall, not an area in Seattle I would consider visiting again...my boyfriend and I frequent Seattle so we stayed here to check out the Georgetown area. It is a pretty run down area, but we did walk to a nice pizza place that was about 3 blocks away and also encountered a couple of ok bars.

“Small And Sufficient” This little hotel is perfectly situated for anyone wanting to hit the shops in Soho and explore the surrounding villages of downtown New York. We easily walked to West Village, East Village, Noho, Nolita and the Meatpacking District from here. We felt absolutely safe walking through the streets at night. Subway station is located within 100 metres of the hotel as well. The rooms were smaller than expected here. We had a queen bed with a sufficient room for our bags. The room has a large TV, small dresser and small wardrobe with in-room safe. The safe was suitable to store our valuables and laptop. They also provide an umbrella in the room. The bathroom was quite small. It was only fit for 1 adult in there at a time. Not much room to store your own amenities. The amenities provided seem more like what you would find in a motel than a hotel. However, the bathroom did look new, modern and very clean. The heating unit was quite noisy, as it would make loud noises as it switched on and off, as well as when it was heating up the room. Our room had a nice view of the wall next door. The free wifi throughout the hotel made it convenient for us, as we had free wifi in the room. The hotel had a small breakfast room, tiny bar, small lobby and reception area, which got really crowded in the mornings. There is also an internet station with 2 PCs for those that don't have their own with them. The staff were very helpful and professional, always on the ball with everything and greeted with a smile. All in all, this hotel does the basics well and would recommend to those who want something in the Soho area without paying a fortune for it.

“great location, impersonal, huge older tower block type hotel” Checking in reminded us of being in as busy airport. A very helpful check in staff allocated us an upgrade but totally ignored our request for a quiet location-she even showeed us a schematic of the noisy rooms and she had allocated us one. So back down and changed rooms which was achived very quickly biut now no upgrade but still got a good view and now a quiet location. Breakfast was outstanding even by Hilton standards and very friendly and efficient staff. Location is very good-close by the cable car stops-close by Chinatown and the major retailers are close by as well. Car parking very expensive so we ended our rental early and walked and took taxis and saved a bundle Would we go back?-yes for the breakfast -probably the best hotel breakfast we ever had-yes for location but probably a NO for the sheer size and feeling of impersonal servcice that comes with being so big

“Small, but nice” I stayed at the Crowne Plaza Chicago-Allerton on Friday night. It was a great location to all the clubs and bars. We walked about nine blocks to get to Sound-bar, Y, RiNo, Spyclub, etc. FINDING YOUR WAY AROUND: My friend and I took the subway from O'Hare to the Chicago (Red line) stop and walked about 3 blocks to Michigan Ave. Once on Michigan we began out search for the Crowne Plaza to learn that it is NOT on Michigan Ave technically--the enterance is on Huron. The Nine West shoe store shares the same building and its front is on the Mag Mile. When we entered the Hotel, we learned that check-in is on the THIRD floor using the elevator on the right. If you wanted to go to your room, you had to get on another set of elevators on the third floor. To go to Taps or the lounge, you got on the elevator on the first floor to your left. THE ROOM: Very small. We checked in at 5PM and that's the only avalable room they had. My friend saw it and had a fit, but I didn't care because we didn't spend so much time in it. It had a standard bed (full), a small desk, and a TV on a TV stand. The linens and towels were white and clean. The bathroom was quite nice with marble-ish floors and a see through glass shower. On, the floors are very slippery! The room was very clean and stocked with the following: -Shampoo, conditioner, soap, lotion, and shoe polish -Hair dryer and make-up mirror -On the bed was a linen spray and earplugs -Iron, extra blanket and pillow in the closet STAFF: Helpful, if not a bit sarcastic. They at least knew how to get around the city. You can also leave your luggage there after check-out to walk around the city.

“Nothing bad, nothing exceptional” Want to start off by saying I love Seattle. This is one of my favorite places to visit and I always look forward to returning. Hotel Max was provided by the travel desk at work so not sure about cost versus value. The building is old and they have attempted to freshen it up and give it an edge. The room was sizable but not very functional. No real closet, big wardrobe near the door. Bathroom as very small in comparison to the rest of the room. The honor bar is one you can actually put your own items into without being charged so that's a bonus. Sheets and towels are a little to be desired but a comfortable nights sleep. Air conditioner is right next to the bed and noisy but if you run it at full blast before bed you should be able to make it through the night. Overall, not a bad stay but I prefer the larger full service hotels nearby.

“nice stay, nice rooms” Stayed here in May 2006 over Memorial Day weekend at 119.00 per night for the room. The check in went smoothly and the room was good sized and nicely appointed. I stayed at the Quality Suites in April 2006 and it is next door sharing the parking lot and a few amenities(swimming pool and weight room). The good thing about this hotel is that all the amenities are at the Quality Suites and so all of the noise is at that hotel. I would recommend staying at the Holiday Inn because it is much quieter and the rooms are nicer, even though it is a little more expensive than the Quality Suites. Would stay here again. Only complaint is because they share the parking lot, it can get really crowded and hard to find parking..Other than that, the breakfast is good and the workers are friendly.

“Average even during hurricane!” The hotel is in a reasonably good location for Mid town. The rooms have recently been renovated to a modern spec which is nice, it's not a case of painting over the old layers, the rooms have been fully stripped and refurbished. The room was fairly small but I presume this is common in Manhattan. The room rates were good by comparison to the competition. We had 2 double beds but they were small double beds. There is a busy lobby and bar as you enter but I didn't think there was any real character to the hotel. Overall they held up well during the storm which is to their credit. All things considered I would recommend it for the right price.

“Good Value” This hotel is a very good value if you want to be close to downtown without paying downtown prices. The rooms are pretty standard, but the deluxe room is quite large. The bathrooms are standard. The pool is very nice - large and deep. The lifeguard is a bit overzealous. He will keep you safe, but your kids fun factor may be diminished a bit. The restaurant is a very good value for breakfast. Overall I would recommend the place.

“another good kimpton experience” if a city i am travelling to has a kimpton hotel, i will usually stay there. i think that they provide a very consistent level of service for a reasonable price. my opinon was reaffirmed with a two night stay at 70 park avenue. i was travelling with my family and we had two rooms. one with a queen and one with two queens. for NYC rooms they had a decent amount of space, including a desk and big flat screen tv. the staff was very friendly and helpful with suggestions. 70 park ave is in a nice location to reach much of manhattan easily. unless you are willing to shell out $500+ per night, i think 70 park ave is a great choice in manhattan.

“Get what you pay for...would stay again for the right price” Great location. 4 minute walk to Faneuil Hall area. You aren't going to find many hotels that are 2 blocks from Faneuil Hall and under $100. I paid $90 per night for labor day weekend. I got what I paid for...but all of the travel website should reconsider the 3 star rating. Very outdated hotel...a bit of a dirty atmosphere(probably because of the style it is decorated in)...not unbearable. The front desk clerks were not very friendly. The rooms were a lot better than I expected for the price. They had a queen bed, a table with 2 chairs, a fridge, microwave, and sink. The bathroom was small but did the job. The linens were pretty gross. They definitely should bring some new towels into the rotation. They also only prepare the room for 1 person...this is probably because club quarters hotels are made for business travelers, who are typically alone. A call to the front desk will get you some extra towels. I would definitely stay again for $100 or under. I am shocked that this hotel usually goes for $160 per night(over priced) but all of the other hotels in the same area were quite a bit more. So if its a cheap room that you need...definitely do priceline.com and search the downtown/charlestown area...you might get lucky.

“Adequate Interstate stop” Called to get a room here at 8 PM as an unscheduled stop on our way through the area. Price was $81 with AAA discount plus taxes. Clean, quiet room. Typical continental breakfast with waffle maker. Free internet worked well. Worked well as brief overnight stop.

“Not a three star hotel” I have stayed here several times. This hotel is clean with good service. However it is a older hotel with small rooms and a noisy airconditioner and heater that is inadequate to set a temperature you feel comfortable with. It cuts off and on and blows onto the bed area. I could not stream video on my computer in my room. There was no charge for the internet but the signal is weak. There is a charge for any breakfast . There ia a business room with printers and computers. There is a gym room with machines.

“Great location, but uncaring staff and cramped rooms” The hotel is located in Midtown Manhattan on 44th Street between 5th and 6th Avenues. It is only about two blocks from the small, but beautiful Bryant Park. The taxi ride from JFK is a flat $45 plus $5 toll and tip. It is a relatively small hotel sharing a narrow street with the Sofitel and another hotels as well as a diner and a few restaurants, including the Triomphe which is the hotel's restaurant and where room service comes from. I cannot comment on the food because I did not eat any of it. However, the Triomphe was rated high by Zagat (average of about 23 or so). The Internet worked intermittently, but no different from anywhere else in the USA. The staff were uncaring and barely helpful. Also, when the doorman opened the door for us I overheard him saying to another staff member, "You know Jose only made $20 in tips?" That is just not classy. At night, there was no staff at the desk or no doorman, so security is a bit of a concern. There was a video camera installed in the elevator, but I think people can use the staircase from the first floor. The guy who was there at night was not very friendly or even really tried to be helpful. The concierge was only seen a few times during the day. The deluxe room was very nice with an old New York feel to it. However, it was a bit cramped New York-style, too. When you go use the toilet and leave the door open, for example, you have to pee sideways because the door blocks your way. Also, the shower/bathtub is an older type in which you need to pull all the way to get proper water pressure and then push a metal stick to have the water come out of the showerhead. The bathroom amenities were alright though. Our rooms faced the courtyard which had a noisy airconditioning system or some kind of machine that hummed loudly all day. The lobby is like a mix between a classic New York pub and someone's living room (there is a den with computer). The price of the hotel jumped up to double when we tried to add extra nights. So I think we got a very good deal. The manager was helpful and negotiated a lower rate for us which was nice of her. SUMMARY: This is a four star hotel in quality of the rooms, but I think the service could be much better. It was really lacking when we were there and so I want to give this hotel three and a half stars overall. I would stay somewhere else before choosing the Iroquois Hotel again.

“Ok, not fantastic, but ok” Location of the hotel is great. It doesn't quite give the ' feel ' of a hotel, very mis-matched. The room had a slight tired feel, as did the bathroom. The bed was comfortable, as were the pillows. The bathroom functional, albeit small. The hotel has only one restaurant, which is also where breakfast is served. Staff, both in the restaurant and reception were friendly and fast.

“Used To Be Better” I know that this hotel is simply for those going in and out of LAX airport. However, two things stand out and not in a good way. The Executive Lounge's offerings have been going steadily downhill and this last visit, breakfast was bare bones. Yes, there is fruit, cereal and some breads. But everything is spread out on the counter to look as if there is an abundance of items. The rooms have comfortable beds but when are the t.v.'s going to come into the 21st century? Service at check in is prompt and cordial.

“Great location but uncomfortable rooms” We stayed here for one night last week. The hotel is in a great location - 10 mins walk to Pike Place Mkt and lots of shops, close to Space Needle and other attractions. The close proximity to everything downtown is the ONLY reason I would ever stay here again. Parking is $28 per night. If you rent a car, try to rent one from National or Alamo so you can return it here and avoid the horrendous parking fee. Our room on the 25th floor looked updated. We did have a partial water view. We decided on two double beds instead of one king bed because our daughter was staying with us for a few hours until her red-eye later that night. We're used to sleeping in queen beds at home so a double was tiny and uncomfortable. The bed was also very firm and the pillows were very mushy. The A/C by the window was loud but turning it off made the room stuffy. We did not get a good night's sleep in this room. Bathroom was clean but tiny, particularly the toilet/shower area. There were more than enough towels and everything felt fresh and clean. We noticed we were at the end of the hall next to the icemaker so we worried about the noise but surprisingly, we didn't hear anything. The elevators seemed efficient. We never had to wait more than a couple minutes. In this hotel, if you want to go up from the lobby, you have to insert your room key into a slot in the elevator or it won't go! I understand why this is done but it got a little annoying at times. Front desk was efficient and friendly and we were checked in very quickly. The concierge was also very helpful when I asked for suggestions and directions to a location. I also used the business center computers to print out a boarding pass. The lobby area was also nice with big comfortable couches and chairs. The fireplace was going when I sat down there to use their free wi-fi. We also had a late dinner at the lobby bar lounge. The burgers are great and the atmosphere is relaxed and unrushed. My husband feels this is the worst Hilton he's ever stayed in because the room was so uncomfortable for him to sleep in but he's spent a lot of nights in quite a few of them and had better sleep. I would still recommend this place only for the great location but I'm not sure I'd stay here again. With all the great hotels in downtown Seattle, I'm sure we could find one with more comfortable rooms.

“Pretty guy with ugly teeth . . .” The structure the Courtyard is located in is magnificent. It was the City Hall Annex. So, imagine a majestic structure constructed n 1926 restored to its former glory. There is no question this hotel is gorgeous, it is absolutely centrally located to everything fun ther is in Philly and it is very reasonably priced. Hence, the "pretty guy . . ." metaphor. But, this place has problems. Before launching on the negative, let's stick to the good: the rooms are new and nicely decorated. The lobby is pretty and there is a very tidy little gym and pool area with everything an exercise fanatic might like to see: three ellipticals, 5 treadmills, free weights, weight machines and even some weighted medicine balls. The problems: I am really concerned about security. The back door near the Johnson library leads directly to the elevator. Although the elevator requires a key to access each floor the door into that side of the building is unstaffed and desolate. The only staff I saw was at the front desk, otherwise the buiilding had that unmanned feel. For example, trash sat near the soda vending machine on the 11th floor for a full 24 hours. The gym was not properly cleaned up: towels and empty bottles were about. The room itself was somewhat petite, but even worse, really stuffy. It was either freezing in the room or airless. The bathroom did not have an exhaust which made things worse. Now the towels: rough and thin. The pillows: hands down the worst pillows I have ever encountered. Sleeping on a folding towel would have had more loft. The bed was comfortable, however, and it was certainly clean. There was not much natural light in the room because the black out shade was too wide for the opening and it obstructed half the window. One thing which was really puzzling was why the door beween the bathroom and vanity area swings inwards. The way it is now is not only stupid but dangerous. On the one side is the toilet; on the other the hairdryer. So, if someone has finished showering and wants to walk into the vanity area there is a good chance someone drying their hair is going to get whacked on the head. Now, the breakfast buffet: $16.95. I mean, really, this is just a Courtyard in Philly- way over priced. Had it been priced at $10.95 the place would have been packed. Do away with the omelette guy or charge an additional fee for an omelette. Would I recommend this place? Oddly, yes. It's just that this place can be so much better than it is.

“OK if you need a large room with a kitchen” For some unkown reason south jacksonville can be a difficult place to find a hotel at the last minute M-W, always has been. So when I travel there we stay on occassion at the Residence Inn Jacksonville Baymeadows. It is an older Residence Inn and appears to be getting ready for a major renovation. Altough old the property is well maintained and amoung the other hotels nearby it is handsdown the cleanist and nicest, even the nearby Embassy Suites is the worst Embassy Suites I have every stayed at. I hope that after the pending renovations this hotel is top notch, but I do agree the breakfast is not great.

“Good, But?” This property is a really nice one. My only problem is in having to pay $13 a night for WI-Fi. Once upon a time maybe, but Wi-FI has become rather common and is free in most cases. This is a premium priced property and yet they are going to "nickel-dime" you over WI-Fi? At the price of $13 a day it is an outlandish charge. One can stay in much cheaper properties and get the WIFI for free. Walk next door to the Barnes and Noble book store and use their WI-FI for free, but why should one have to do that when staying in a premium price property? Cheap, cheap, cheap.

“Great Location Almost Compensates For Problems.” We booked the Hilton as we were attending a conference, but I filed the review under leisure rather than buisness because of all the fun we had in NYC too... but I think I can probably speak to both. Chose this Hilton as that is where our conference was, and the conference rate of above 300 a night was still better than anything else we could find in the area. That being said, it was definitely too much money for this quality of hotel. It is advertised as a 3 and 1/2 star hotel, and I see how that could be true. The lobby is large and open, looks pretty nice at first impression. We got a room on the 28th floor, which was nice. But it had two double beds, and I requested a king-- though I didn't ask to change because I was happy with the high floor. At first the room seemed okay though dated, at least the TV was a flat screen and the beds looked well made. Well, the beds were very comfortable, I slept great, and no signs of bed bugs. Everything else seemed not very good at all. Nice TV, but the remote was broken. The bathroom was small but typical for NY, but the mildew on the shower curtain was gross. Nice big towels in good shape, and they had decent soap/shampoo/conditioner/lotion. The room was not well cleaned on further inspection, either. There was an empty water bottle under the nightstand, for example, with dust that looked like it hadn't been touched in a long time. I know that in NYC things tend to be pricier-- but somethings here at the Hilton were ridiculous. The bellman charged you to hold your bags, $3.50 per bag per day not including tip. I have never had to pay for this service before--- the line to pick up and drop off was huge, and seemed to run efficiently enough. Internet at the hotel is 20 bucks a day, which seems excessive too. Luckly our 3G service seemed to be just fine in the room. The location was excellent, close to the E station, so easy to take public transit from JFK. But I think that for the $ we would have been better off at a boutique hotel or another option nearby.

“Good stay” My husband and I stayed here for two nights as part of our trip. We got a great rate on quikbook for $229 plus tax per night.
