Our impressions of the hotel was that it was extremely clean and our room was very large, especially by NY standards. The bed was large and extremely comfortable. Nice bathroom with good size shower. Water pressure was great. The location is brilliant, being so close to Central Station makes it very easy to get to anywhere. The only thing that we were disappointed with is that we didn't find the staff very friendly. Although the girl at check-out was pleasant, only once did a staff member greet us on entering the hotel the remainder of the time. I think part of the reason that we would pick a Fitzpatrick hotel is to have those personal touches which were lacking for us so I don't think we would stay here again.

“A hotel for shoppers.....” The location of this hotel can't be beat if you want to spend your time shopping in NYC. Macy's is a block away and there is tons of other shopping near and in Times Square (about 7 blocks away). It looks like this is a newer hotel and actually shares a wall with the Hampton Inn next door. Staff was pleasant at check-in and I was given my welcome amenity as an HHonors member (I think the asst. manager checked me in). However, I never received a copy of the USA Today newspaper outside my door while almost everyone else on my floor did. (???) A small item I know but it makes me wonder what benefits do you really get as a hotel club member (I never received the high floor, foam pillows request that I had put in so I didn't get to experience the view of the Empire State Building that others have talked about). Rooms are NY sized-----tiny, but clean, new and comfortable. There is a decent sized refrigerator and microwave in the room as well as an in-room safe. Hallways are tiny and there are only about 7 or 8 rooms on a floor so if you ask for a room away from the elevator, that's nearly impossible (only the bigger sized corner rooms might qualify but you may have to pay more). I didn't dine at the restaurant downstairs but it looked decent (there are tons of places around the corner, if it's too busy). Like others have said the ESB is almost right next door and so is Koreatown (which is basically the next couple of streets down) if you want something different. The Subway is basically right outside the hotel so it's convenient if you don't have a car (which I never do). All in all, a good choice for a clean comfortable hotel.

“Good Holiday Inn” This Holiday in is very clean. It is in new condition. The location is out of the way, but it was good for what I needed. Rooms are nice and clean. Liked the bathroom, but would have liked a tub instead of just a shower. Although I did like the subway tiles in the shower. I just have a few issues. The people are really nice at this hotel. However, they are not familiar enough with the surrounds of the hotel to be able to tell folks how to get to the hotel if you get lost. They also can't tell you how to get anywhere without using google maps. If I say, "I don't want to travel the highway", they are lost. Another issue I had is when I asked for a drink in the bar and requested lime in my soda, the young lady used her bare hand to put the lime in the soda. Now these are the same hands that are punching numbers into the register taking order and touching the same register that others have touched as well. That is gross. Either take the orders or handle the food/drinks, but don't do both. So that meant is I had the germs from the register from which other peoples hands were on. Again, I say gross. Finally, what is the need of having a room service line if everytime you call you get a voicemail. I called twice and twice I received a voicemail for them to call me back. Then when I did get to place my order for what I wanted, they forgot part of my order. I didn't even call them back to correct. The food they sent was pretty good. Grits were horrid, potatoes were cooked in too much grease, but the other stuff was OK. Would I stay here again...maybe, but I would eat and drink somewhere else.

“3 Star quality at a 4 star price” I stayed here for 3 nights on business for a conference at the dallas convention center. I'm a pretty seasoned business and leisure traveler and I can't say I would stay at this hotel again if I was in downtown dallas. It's not that I didn't have an enjoyable experience, it's just that the hotel did not meet my expectations for what a 4-star hotel should have been. Let me start - the hotel isn't conveniently located near any restaurants and it's a long walk to anything nearby. The room was comfortable but I was surprised by the lack of quality/clean sheets - I would prefer my bed sheets be a bit more white and you could tell the sheets were heavily used and reused. The room needs to be modernized as well - they were still using an old Television (and small screensize as well). Internet was a pain - their interface to pay (economy plan $9.95 for 24 hours) isn't exactly the best and the economy plan is slow as heck. I had to wait on hold for an hour with tech support to get it to work. Some good things though, the service was very friendly and they had a decent gym with updated equipment. The room was also very quiet and I slept comfortably (the pillows were very nice). I would only recommend this hotel if traveling for business - there are better options out there if you're traveling for leisure.

“Three nights was too long” Room was noisy and had seats outside so we had to listen to some drunken argument at 2am. Expensive and the room I booked was not available upon arrival, so we had to switch after the first night.

“Outrageous prices!” I stayed here last week and the cost of one night would have bought me a carribean cruise. Simply outrageous that this property would charge this amount. The food was also overpriced and it was not a high quality. Basic expensive pub grub. I recommend using hotwire when staying at Logan. You'll save a fortune for the same type of rooms.

“Feels dated - service was very low” I checked in with my family for a mid-week visit to the Children's Museum. A bell staff to help with luggage was non-existent and when we got to our room, the decor and amenities (outside the new TV's) was very dated. This Embassy is connected to a mall, which made dinner very easy for our family. The breakfast was of lower quality than other Embassy Suites, so we went to Panera (connected to hotel). I'm a Hilton Honors Diamond and will try other Indy Hilton properties before staying here again.

“Great staff, funky rooms, clean, huge flat screen TV, free breakfast” The hotel has a rather funky layout and the rooms do as well. Room had a sectional sofa and huge flat panel tv. The air conditioner was very cooling and loud, but that worked well for me as background noise for sleeping, Everyone working there did whatever they could to helo and be supportive,

“Beautiful views, holes in the sheets.” I enjoyed my stay at the Standard but would never pay full price. They had a deal on Jetsetter so I decided to buy it as a birthday treat. Beautiful view, stylish room, friendly service, great bath tub, and robes. However, I was surprised to find multiple holes in the sheets. Also, room keys dont appear to work to go to the roof bar. There was a line outside to get in so we didn't even get to check it out. There are better options in New York, at much lower prices. (the next night we stayed in the Yotel which was fantastic!)

“Basic functional” An average place for under $100. Older hotel with basic room perhaps a couple notches up from a Motel 6. Looked like they may have regular or long-term construction workers staying there. Major new construction of large buildings a block over. The complimentary breakfast was basic with toast, juice, fruit, & coffee. All functional for a quick one-night stay over to catch a meeting the next day,

“Decent Price but Needs Updating” Stayed at the ES Dallas Market Center this past week - the second time I've been there. I agree with the other reviewers - the hotel is definitely outdated. Not dirty or messy, but terribly outdated. The staff were friendly and helpful (front desk, gift shop, and meal area). There is a fitness center behind the pool area - has the standard treadmills, cycles, and nautilus machines. Didn't try the pool or hot tub, but like the rest of the hotel, they look pretty outdated. I didn't try the restaurant, but the breakfast area has the standard ES fare - it was good, and the staff were friendly. They had a check-in/out kiosk at the front desk - if you used it for either, you should get 500 HHonors points each time. Great idea - haven't gotten the points yet though. The kiosk was useful if there was a line waiting to check in, but it would have been faster to check in at the front desk than using the kiosk. Check out was pretty quick. The hotel is very convenient to downtown and Love Field, but there really isn't anything terribly close by except a Whataburger two buildings over. If you have a car and can drive everywhere, the location isn't too bad. If you need to get on the Tollway North - go up to Mockingbird and then over - otherwise you have to circle through downtown - yuck. All that said, it boils down to a lesson in economics - depending on the price, I'd stay here again. A rate in this area for under $100 is a pretty good deal, plus throw in the free breakfast and manager's reception - not too bad. Anything much over that, and I'd probably stay somewhere else.

“ok, but not GREAT” We have stayed at this resort about 3 times since we live down the street. Each time we keep thinking it will be better. The good is 1) the rooms. they are spacious and comfy and have big bathtubs and the beds are to die for. 2) the bartender and the bar. Very friendly and chatty bartender who knew how to make a drink and make an alone lady not feel so alone. 3) lots of great movies to choose from and room service is FAST! Here is the bad: 1) upon checking, 5000 employees must have greeted me which was ok. My husband had to run to the store and had dropped me off with the inention of being right back. The front desk would not let me checkin b/c my husband and i have different last names on our separate credit cards. Iwas pissed and tired and a spa massage planned within the hour. All i could do sit at the bar and wait for hubby to get back. So progressive women who didnt keep their husband's last night, beware 2) the spa sucks. It is very small and doesnt even compare to the spas i am used to. It the "ladies louge area" where women sit around and read mags in the towels eithrt pre or post massage to relax. I didnt find it relaxing to chear women chew and crunch and talk to their friends in whispers as even we could not hear. Checkout at the spa was awful. There was a new girl they were training and she just doesnt seem to get it. There was some language barriers as well. 3) The spa massage, i got a 50 min deep tissue was again ok. I ended up having a male therapist and a young one at that. He started late and ended early. So there is the good and bad.
“Not disappointed, but not impressed either...” Room is comfortable but small. Parking is expensive, $45 per night for valet parking. Typical American breakfast buffet, no much variety.

“Ok priced, decent hotel in central location. Rubbish WiFi, noisy aircon.” Stayed here for 5 nights in August with my girlfriend. The hotel was clean, comfortable and spacious. Staff were polite and helpful, though not terribly friendly compared to other places i've stayed. It's in a good central location for site seeing, but the area lacks the buzz and character of other parts of Manhattan being in the commercial district which can feel a little quiet after hours. My only real complaints were the wifi that was so slow that it was useless to all intents and purposes. Even when i went down to the lobby it was rubbish. Effectively, we had no internet for our stay. Also the aircon unit in the room was so noisy that we ended up turning it off at night even though it was august and extremely hot. Those things aside we enjoyed our stay here and it's definitely a perfectly good option for $220 a night.

“Fine Stay in Wardman Park” Just got back from a four night business/pleasure stay at the Marriott Wardman Park. This is a huge hotel - about 1,300 rooms, that is a few miles northwest of the mall/DC attractions. We stayed in the historic part of the hotel which as others have mentioned, is a good walk from the lobby. Our room was clean but rather small and a bit dated. In fact I noticed a hotel brochure with pictures of their other rooms and they were much more modern than ours. A refridgerator was a nice touch but it was in an awkward spot on the floor (no table or cabinet). The coffee maker was sorta randomly placed on top. The vanity space in the bathroom is pretty much non-exsistant so it was really hard to place your toiletries. The desk chair looked like it came from my grandmother's basement and the desk itself had tons of scratches, etc. There was a really nice flat-screen TV and the bed was super comfy. Oh and oddly enough, two of the wall hangings were the exact same picture. A minor "issue" but perhaps gives you a sense of their concern for detail. All of the public areas were very clean and well-appointed. The gym was one of the nicest and roomiest I have seen in a long time. It was obviously closed for the season but they had a huge outdoor pool that I'm sure is very inviting come summertime. Service was polite and friendly. Valet guys were particularily helpful. Overall it was a fine stay. The hotel is a 2 minute walk from the Metro's Red Line and a little commerical area with a CVS, McDonalds and a handful of ethnic restaurants. I stayed here for business and didn't really have a choice. If I were coming to DC as a tourist, and got a good deal on the Marriott Wardman, I would consider staying there again. Otherwise I would try to find a hotel a bit more toward downtown.

“Great Value in Old Town” This property is as advertised! Reasonable and located within walking distance to Old Town, the staff is welcoming and helpful. Dogs (any size) are welcome guests as well. The breakfast was good (no eggs however), the prices more than fair. Parking garage is located underneath the hotel and the pool was full of happy kids on vacation. Good for families, especially with dogs, wanting a central location at a great value. I would not recommend the property for couples or business travel as this property was built for location and value rather than to impress or be romantic.

“Very average” Good for a solo business traveller that gets a deal via priceline. Otherwise, if you are paying full price, you'll probably be disappointed. My room was small and had a strong chlorine smell. The doormen are creepy, not made for the job. My room was right next to elevator, but thankfully I didn't hear them; even when the very loud in-room A/C was off.

“Good value, close to airport, long wait for shuttle” Good location close to the airport. The wait for the shuttle from the terminal to the hotel look longer. But the rooms are OK for an overnight stay. value for money.

“Disappointed With the Hilton Palacio del Rio” I spent a night at the Hilton Palacio del Rio while I was in San Antonio on business. Overall, I was disappointed with my stay. First the good: the hotel is in a very good location, on the Riverwalk, right next to La Vallita, the centuries-old section of town that is now filled with arts and crafts shops, while the Alamo is only a couple of blocks away. Each room has a refrigerator, a patio and a nice granite sink. Finally, the staff was friendly and competent. Unfortunately, the bad list is much longer: (1) parking is expensive--$15 to self-park at a garage two blocks away, or $29 for valet parking; (2) the entire hotel is in serious need of a major renovation. The hotel was built in 1968, and feels rather dreary due to the low ceilings, dim lighting and cramped lobby; (3) the bed was OK, with lots of pillows and a nice comforter, but not up to "heavenly bed" standards; (4) the TV was a standard 27" tube with a modest 26 channels and limited news selection (no Fox or MSNBC); (5) half the rooms have no view (except of concrete buildings and San Antonio traffic). If you want a view, pay extra; (6) The rooms seemed very tired and the furniture somewhat cheap. Except for the new sink and the new Hilton radio, it does not appear as though much money has been spent on the room. At regular rates of $200+, I consider this hotel a very poor value. If you want a very nice hotel on the Riverwalk, I would stick with the Westin. For a good value, look elsewhere.

“No big complaints but no charm” I prefer boutique hotels and San Francisco has a lot of them. However, I was not paying for the room at the Grand Hyatt so did not get to choose. I have no complaints about the room, it was clean, comfortable and had the expected amenities. The view towards the Coit Tower was fabulous. The view from the bar at the top was also great. Too bad the fitness room, also near the top, has no windows at all. The location is great but there are tons of choices in the same area. There were a few problems, the outside door which was supposed to open to let in fresh air got stuck after only opening a crack and room service was somewhat slow. The biggest disappointment was the lack of knowledge of the front desk staff. We asked for a good wine shop and were directed to a corner store with no good wines, only cheap ones. We found a huge wine specialty store on the other side of Union Square by wandering around ourselves. I would have expected better knowledge, especially since San Francisco hosts so many wine loving tourists. If I was going to pay for a room, I would look for a boutique at a cheaper rate.

“Vastly improved” I have stayed at the Days Broadway previously and was compelled to write reviews describing an awful hotel. A client booked me into a New York hotel for 3 nights and I was horrified to discover they had chosen the Days Hotel Broadway. Anyway, circumstances conspired such that I could not change the reservation and I checked in with trepidation. I have to say the improvement is vast. The room was on the 14th floor and it was clean, the sheets were pristine, the bed was comfortable and the air conditioning/heating worked. My only problems were a lack of hot water and the truely awful elevators. It is hard to conceive how they can be so slow. I will have no hesitation about staying there in future.

“Nice Hotel with "Modern Problems"” This Intercontinental is less than a year old, and is what you'd expect in a new, five-star hotel in a major city. It does have a range of "modern hotel problems", however. I was upgraded to a nice, high-floor corner room due to my Ambassador Club status. Hotel was pretty empty, despite a major convention at Moscone Center (a block away). Rooms are tastefully appointed, clean and comfortable. A/C system is particularly good, very quiet. However, when I first checked in, I was warned that a "maintenance issue" would require the hotel electricity to be turned off for an hour that afternoon. Fair enough. But during the late night hours, while I was working (phone and internet), the power again went out along with all communications - AND THE ELEVATORS. No warning at all. This pattern of electrical service continued for the next day as well. Apparently still-unresolved construction issues. The phones go down because of a too-small UPS system specified. My other "modern hotel" pet peeve is the showers. Part of luxury hotel life is a good, powerful hot shower. Instead this hotel has barely enough water pressure to get wet. If this is due to some kind of "green initiative", I object. If this is just due to bad water-saving shower heads, it should be fixed. Midline management was dismissive of the concerns I raised. I was able to finally raise the hotel manager with a call to IC head office about the electrical/communication issues. Management shouldn't be hiding from the customers. One other note for potential visitors - much of SFO including the area adjacent to this hotel has become extremely street unsafe, even during the daytime. Factor in cab fares if you're planning on doing sightseeing.

“Good Experience” The bellmen were friendly and helpful, but it is odd to have a taxi drop you off to the entrance to the hotel, then be surprised by having to take an elevator to the 6th floor lobby. The lobby was small, although hotel front desk staff were efficient. Elevators (only 2) were slow. Hotel room itself was pleasant. Large TVs in both rooms, functional kitchen with refrigerator and dishwasher too. The daily breakfast was good, but ran out of fruit and there were few healthy choices. Coffee and tea were never hot, only lukewarm. Plenty of tables to choose to eat, but beware if the hotel is full then so is the breakfast room. Small pool on top floor and a small exercise room. Location is probably the best part of this hotel. A few blocks north of the river and a few blocks west of Michigan's Miracle Mile. Huge number and type of restaurants within a few blocks. Overall, a good experience, but not "very good".

“Close to airport - noisy” The hotel itself was fine, clean and the only drawback we could find was that it was noisy with visitors from the airport arriving at all hours of the night. If you are looking for a quick sleep in a clean room - this is good for that but not good for couple weekends out or nice trip out of town.

“Park Avenue Ordinary” The rooms are clean and quiet. The plasma TV's are nice. But other than that the hotel experience was very ordinary. The hallways are narrow and dark, the lobby is small and need of an upgrade. The complimentary (?) 15 minutes of internet access is a joke, either make it free or don't offer it. Our room had a nice view of the air conditioning equipment. If you can get a good rate (around $200 per night) I would say it is a good value, but if not don't bother.

“OK. Which was Better than Expected” I stayed at this motel (at this insistence of a friend) during Indy 500 race weekend. Although my expectations were low, I was pleasantly surprised at this motel. Don't get me wrong, it's definitely not the Ritz Carlton or even a Holiday Inn for that matter - but I thought they did a pretty good job of keeping the hotel relatively neat and the staff was very friendly. I definitely saw seedier places that were more in the "city". This motel sort of stands out by itself - near a gas/trucker station and a nearby "adult" bar. But the lack of nearby business and buildings makes the parking easy and the surrounding area less seedy - if not a little bit bland. It's close enough to make a very short trip over to the racetrack, but you are out of the craziness of staying IN Indianapolis on race weekend. My only major complaint was the price. While I typical don't mind spending a couple hundred bucks a night on a hotel...I don' t typical expect to drop over a hundred on a Super 8. I KNOW it's race weekend, but I thought that was pretty ridiculous. So, if you are REALLY on a budget, this may very well be one of the lower prices on race weekend, but I think if you spent a little bit more (and made reservation WAY IN ADVANCE) you could get a nicer hotel...but I could be wrong.

“Typical chain hotel” If you want to stay in the north part of Columbus for under $100 per night, this is a fine choice. The common areas of the hotel and of my room were very clean but offered the typical tacky decor of most middle-of-the-road chain hotels (wood-paneled elevators and yucky green carpet). However, the bed and bedding were new, nice and very comfortable. My room was spacious and had a mini-fridge (not stocked). Check in was very quick and guy at the front desk was nice enough. My biggest complaint was how loudly the room doors slammed shut when the guest don't bother to hold the door (which is most of the time). Location is convenient to interstates 270 and 71 and to route 23. Restaurants Bravo and Columbus Fish Market are walking distance across the street, and the very nice J. Gilbert's is about a block away. Also in the same suburban sprawl complex are many chain restaurants and a movie theater. I lived in Columbus for several years and traveled there for business when I didn't live there. There are many other hotels in this same area. If you can spend a little more I recommend the Sheraton Suites.

“Location was great, but the hotel was just "okay"!” I chose this hotel, because I had enough HHonors points for a free night. We usually stay at one of the Embassy Suites in downtown Chicago, but didn't have enough points for a free night there. Getting off the elevator from the parking garage, you are greeted by a pink lobby. My husband gave me the look that said he was doubting my decision. At check-in, they asked us if we wanted to stay in one room one night and then a different room the next night, since one of them was free for using my HHonors points. We said that we'd rather not have to change rooms and he said, "okay"! He gave us our cookies and our keys and sent us on our way. We were given a room on the 3rd floor, that look out at a wall. No view! My guess, is this is what is given to people who stay at enough Hilton Hotels to earn a free room. We weren't going to be in the room very much and it was a free night's stay, worth approx. $206, so we just went with it. The room was mostly clean, except for hair on the bathroom floor and on the first night, a panel fell off the cabinet on bathroom vanity. We tried to put it back on, but it wouldn't go, so we left it for the cleaning person to deal with. They didn't deal with it, so we had a cabinet door on the floor in the bathroom for our stay. The location of this hotel is great. There is a Dominick's grocery store just a block away and Emilio's Tapas restaurant is just down Ohio about a half a block. It's a wonderful place to eat! Only 2 blocks from Michigan Ave, where all the shopping is. We got a bill after the first night, that said we had been charged $206 for our night's stay. Fine. The following morning, I received a bill stating that they were going to charge us $20 for the guest room. We also had a charge for a video game, but my daughter did play a game, so that was fine. I talked to the person at the desk and I got no explanation for it, but she took it off my bill. So check you bill very closely!!!! This wasn't a bad place to stay, but there were just many things about it, that just made it not a great place to stay either. We had just come from staying at a very nice Embassy Suites in another city and this seemed like a very big step down. In large cities, I usually pick 4 star hotels, because we think they would be considered 3 star anywhere else. This hotel was definitely a 2 1/2 - 3 star. The cost of parking for the weekend, was around $80, I believe. I guess I learned, getting a free room, is never free. My husband said he'd rather pay more and stay at an Embassy Suites with breakfast included and the manager's special in the evening. Also, pink with lime green made it look like a cheesy hotel from the 60's or 70's. If they just renovated, they should of changed that. Free internet connection in the lobby only, so the lobby was always crowded.

“Enjoyed the stay for my business but not as a place for visiting Detroit” I stayed here for business and I enjoyed the stay. Convenient location for my meetings but I wouldn't stay here for visiting Detroit as it is far from everything.There are few dining options around and the neighborhood at night is not inviting. Room was ok. Complimentary breakfast in the morning is average. Staff is nice and helpful.

“Acceptable Convention Hotel Near Shopping/Dining/Transit.” This is a large, dated convention hotel facility. The rooms are a curious mixture of upper end --"Sweet Sleeper" beds, flat screen TVs, free Starbucks coffee with real half and half -- and older, beat-up furniture and a low level of bathroom amenities. Wi-fi is free in the lobby, but $10 a day for internet (non-wi-fi) in the room. Location is a big plus for this hotel. It is just off Copley Square and Newberry Street in the Back Bay, so there is plenty of dining, shopping, and people watching to be had. This is important because food and beverage prices in the hotel were prohibitive, but could be alleviated by a quick walk to much less expensive, high quality, alternatives either within the attached Prudential Center Mall, or out in the nearby neighborhoods. The Hotel is close to either the Hynes Convention Center or the Prudential stops on the Green Line (so the airport is only a $2 away on the T, if you're traveling light). Likewise, Amtrak can be accessed via Back Bay Station, which is a ten-minute walk through the connecting malls and pedestrian bridges. You only need go outside to cross Dartmouth street from the Westin to the station. For excellent, inexpensive breakfast just up the block, go to the "Pour House" on Boyleston. Really hit the spot for us and for well under half the price of the Sheraton's overpriced breakfast buffet.

“Clean, convenient, but souless” This is located right near the Navy Pier so it is in the center of action. It is efficient quiet, and clean but has little else to recommend it. There is nothing special about the place. I wouldn't choose to stay here unless I happened to get a great deal on the price. No ice machine, no free wireless, no convenient Starbucks or clone in the lobby.

“Place to be if you are small and looking for a party” Very, very eclectic hotel with low lighting, service personnel dressed in black, intriguing outdoor deck and nighttime PARTY scene. If you're looking for this (and you are a small person) then definitely stay here. It is a "scene" and "modern ambience" place. The rooms are the smallest I have EVER seen, and I travel lots. The bathrooms are impossible to move around in, the bed is low to the ground and the TV has to be flush against the wall to move around the bed. It's impossible to describe how closet like the one-bedroom is. It is also next to impossible to get an elevator at any time of day. We got a cheap rate on a "name your price" site and were staying for one night to attend the Pearl Jam concert at MSG. For one night and that purpose, it was fine.

“Great Hotel Except For Lack Of Customer Service” Our Amtrak train was delayed due to flooding and we were given a room here. Now the hotel itself was great. Clean rooms and flat screen tv's. My problem was at check in. Amtrak pays for the rooms for its guests. This hotel was telling the Amtrak passengers that they would have to post a deposit of 50 dollars. Now Amtrak does not allow any hotel to collect deposits from distressed passengers. This was not a problem for me but some passengers did not have the 50 dollars. The front desk staff were not friendly at check in. I am a Priority Club Gold member and they told me that only Platinum members get breakfast coupons. Not friendly at all.

“Great Hotel but rooms and hallways need to be refurbished” This is one of Philadelphia's older buildings and the Hyatt itself is a great hotel in a very good location. My last stay was in 2007 and it was great, unfortunately come 2011 the property and rooms especially need to be refurbished. The hotel certainly has that old world charm but that does not excuse dirty green carpet in the rooms, hallways, or bathrooms that are in dire need of refurbishment. A lot more could be done with this hotel to bring it up to date, especially in the guest rooms. The Bar and restaurant on the top floor is one of the highlights and certainly worth a visit, even if just for a quick drink. The hotel is certainly very classy and requires a bit of money to bring it back to glory. Depending on the price this hotel may or might not be a bad choice. This time when I stayed price was $109 a night so good value for the money even with the rooms needing to be redone but if price was closer to average $200 rates they normally charge, I would stay somewhere else like Westin until refurbishment is finished.

“Would not stay here again” I used my free certificate for a one night stay before an ultra long haul flight. Its one of the nearest hotels to LAX and a friend of mine dropped me to the hotel in his car. He must have parked his car for barely 30 min and was charged 14 dollars for that time!!!! Overnight valet parking for 24 hours is 32 dollars! I find this a real rip off as its much cheaper to park in Hollywood and Beverly Hills. The lobby is big and they have a separate check in for Marriott Rewards elite card holders which is manned from 3pm onwards only. Being Platinum Elite, I checked in there and was told I had been upgraded to an executive suite. I was also very happy that they accepted my request for a late check out. Being a weekend the concierge lounge was closed but this property at least gave me coupons to have breakfast in the restaurant- something quite inconsistent in other Marriotts – some offer some don’t. I proceeded to my room and here started the trek through a maze of corridors which made me realize the sheer size of this hotel. I thoroughly regretted the upgrade as the suite was in one far end of the maze of corridors. It had a small living room with a large dining table for 8 people taking half the space – making no sense at all. It had a view of the neighboring building. I would have really preferred taking a regular room facing the airport especially since it was for one night. The hotel is quite dated and so was the room. The electric outlets were very loose and finding a suitable one to charge my 220 volt appliances was not an easy task. Breakfast was nothing special – the usual hot breakfast - but the service was excellent. I returned to my room in the afternoon and the key was not working. The check in staff had forgotten to program the key for a late check out. I had to trek all the way back to front desk to get it done. At check out I was utterly shocked to see that they had charged me a dollar each time I had called a toll free 1-800 number for gaining access. In all my 20 years of stays in Marriott hotels – ranging from Residence Inn to JW Marriott Marquis properties, not a single one had ever charged this. The front desk staff however proceeded to remove it only because I was a platinum elite member. Overall there is nothing special about this property expect for the excellent staff behavior and attitude. I definitely would not be staying here during my next transit in LAX.

“Very good location for L.A. trip” Came down for a two-night stay in November, and shared a double-double room with a friend. The staff was courteous and knowledgeable; even gave us two vouchers each for free drinks at either the bar or restaurant onsite. The room was clean, the toiletries were good, and the animal-print bathrooms were a funny little touch. I had work to do in the Westwood area, but also met up with friends in BH and downtown, and the location was easy enough to get where I needed. A lot of nearby areas for dining and shopping, although not right outside your hotel. Taxis are everywhere, though, so it was easy enough to catch a quick cab somewhere.

“Old world style, nice but nothing fancy or modern.” I stayed here one night for business. The room was decent, clean. The whole hotel is very antique which is charming, but a bit over the top with the patterned rugs, walls, older furniture.
“Nice” Room was spacious and clean. Staff was very friendly and accommodating. Beds were hard, but overall nice and updated room.

“Great location but no amenities” I will start with the negative aspects. There is $10 charge per 24 hour use of internet, the in-room coffee is $1 per packet, there is no business center (however I was able to print boarding passes at the front desk), we had a really strange experience in the hotel restaurant, the service in the roof top bar is lousy- had to beg someone to wait on us. Our room was on the 4th floor at the back of the hotel which faced north. Both mornings we were there I was awakened at 5am by a really loud truck that banged dumpsters around until about 7. Believe me, this was very loud and very annoying!! There was no where to get coffee early in the morning (except to use the $1 packets in the room). Now for the positive aspects. The location of this hotel is great, the rooms are spacious and nicely decorated, the beds are very comfortable, the bathrooms are spacious, the front desk staff was friendly and helpful for the most part. I got a great rate on this hotel so I consider the experience good overall, and the only way I will stay here again will be if I get another great rate. I really don't like to stay in hotels that have no amenities! I would recommend this hotel to a friend if they were able to get a great rate, and I would warn them about all of the negatives.

“Good hotel, a little bit old fashioned” We stayed at this hotel during March for a couple of days while visiting Boston. The hotel is good, it seems that it might have been a very good business hotel like 20 years ago, but now the place looks as if we were in 1980. Good things: the rooms are quite large, they beds are comfortable, they provide complimentary coffee and tea maker and it is 1 block away from the subway. Bad things: they do not have wi-fi, they charge you if you want to use the hotel PC located in the lobby, the bed covers are a little bit dirty and ours had cigarette burns, there is only 1 elevator located in the exact opposite corner of our room and to get to the elevator from the lobby you have to climb stairs (which is complicated when you have a lot of luggage as we did) Even when we had a good time, and our stay was pleasant, I think that you might be able to find a nicier hotel for the price they charge for the room

“Needs work--newly added to Starwood group” This hotel was a disappointment. No fitness center (they have a partnership with the Westin so you can walk a bit to use their facility), no coffee makers in the rooms, no club floor, needs updating. Good location for dining and shopping but certainly needs a facelift to be a viable spot for business travelers.

“Not Bad” For what I paid I could have stayed in a midtown hotel. Nonetheless, it did its job. As far as the location, it's a bit out of the way if you want to see all of the attractions, although it's only a short walk to the park. There are plenty of places to eat nearby, but it's a good ten minute walk to the lively bars on Amsterdam Avenue. The room was a bit small compared to what we've been used to, but it was okay. The reception staff were friendly and helpful, although the cleaning staff were a bit noisy in the corridors on a morning, which might not have gone down too well with anyone nursing a hangover. Even so, I quite enjoyed my stay at this hotel and in The Upper West Side area. This might not be the ideal location for everyone. However, for anyone that wishes to escape the tourist atmosphere of the midtown area and experience a bit more of what Manhattan has to offer it does have its advantages.On the whole, not bad.

“Location and value” For New York City, Hotel 17 is a great value. But don't expect amenities like room service, complimentary breakfast, or even an ironing board or in-room coffee maker. This is a bare bones hotel meant to just sleep in and drop off your luggage. The Wifi is also very spotty, so if internet access is essential during your visit, you'd have better luck going to an internet cafe. We were given a room with a double bed and shared bathroom. My main complaint was being assigned a room in the smoking section. But the good news is the location and the relative cleanliness of the shared bathrooms. Hotel 17 is located in the East Village, very close to St. Mark's place and restaurants such as Veselka and Otafuku and bars such as Decibel. Despite its no frills approach, I would stay here again.

“Had to stay here because everything downtown was booked for SxSW” I did not realize when I booked my work trip that the SxSW music festival was taking place at the same time and EVERYTHING downtown was booked. I saw that this hotel was still relatively close to the downtown area as well as the Barton Creek Mall (where I had to be for work). My biggest challenge with the location is how difficult it was to actually get there...it is situated next to the highway but the exits are so confusing (or my Garmin device was confused) that I kept driving by the hotel on the elevated portion of the road only to have to get off at the next exit and do a loop around. I still don't know what the mistake was I was making (but I did it twice)! Without my mistakes the property is less than 10 minutes from downtown and Barton Creek. Rooms are large and clean and the refrigerator and microwave were a benefit...I love Whole Foods so I went to their flagship store and brought back some prepared food to have in the room. Check in was very friendly, the people in front of me did not have a reservation and the property was completely booked up but the person at reception gave them several options to try in the area and was very apologetic. It seemed every room I had on this trip was near a highway so I requested a room on the other side of the property to be away from the road. They were not able to accomodate me but were very apologetic about it and the room turned out to be relatively quiet. There is free WiFi throughout the hotel and a computer with printer that is complimentary. I did not take advantage of the complimentary breakfast but there were many people that seemed to be enjoying it.

“Great location” This is a big, busy hotel. It's in a very good location in New York, just a short walk from Penn Station and close to shops. My room was tiny and dark. I had to step over my suitcase and had there been two of us staying there, we'd have had to stack the suitcases up. The bathroom was also tiny with nowhere to put toiletries. I was only staying a couple of nights and didn't notice any facilities such as a gym, bar or restaurant but with so many places to eat and drink in the vicinity, that's not a problem. The staff were generally friendly and helpful. A decent enough hotel but I wouldn't want to stay more than a few days in such a small room.

“Spectacular fireworks” We actually stopped by the motel six months ago to reserve one of the top floor rooms for the 4th of July fireworks. This is one of the few establishments which will guarantee requests. Because of the holiday traffic and tremendous number of visitors in town, we had to pay the rack rate of $179 + 14% tax, and $26 a night for parking + tax. This is a bit steep but the "in your face" double fireworks easily compensated. Good walkers will appreciate the location of the motel, as the Cannery and Ghiradelli Square are within 15 minutes or less.A number of restaurants were closed on the 4th so the challenge of finding a good place to eat became even greater. Union Street has the greatest number of eateries. Good bar scene at Perry's, the watering hole popular during the 60's. We settled on the very popular Betelnut, seven blocks down Union St., an Asian restaurant which offers good value and a vibrant ambiance. There are a few problems which you may wish to note so that your own experiences won't be hindered. For example, the bathroom sign to recycle towels or room notice not to change sheets remain ignored. All four sets of towels were replaced and all sheets were changed. Then there is the parking issue. Getting into the secure garage is fine. You announce your arrival in a speaker, and the gate rises. Exiting is a different story. The gate remained down despite having checked out. After 10 minutes, someone went around to the entrance and used the arrival speaker to get the desk to respond. The rooms are bright and the beds are very comfortable. I'm sure that someday the management will do something about worn carpets and soiled chairs. Until then, this is clearly a three-circle experience, but one which we will gladly repeat.

“Clean borning hotel on the edge of downtown” My husband and I landed at this hotel through a Priceline deal. Price was about $200 and it was clean, but very boring hotel. Even the work-out area was fine, but nothing special. Rooms were large (had to pay for wi-fi). Bar had a scene during certain hours of the day but we didn't eat or drink in the hotel and lobby wasn't conducive to hanging out. The hotel was on the edge of a rough area and it was often deserted walking back at night. Wish we'd stay in a boutique hotel that added more San Fran charm to our trip.

“Rooms & facilities need some "refreshing" - continued nickel & diming” Stayed three nights on a corporate rate ($160) that included free Internet access. Pros: - Stately old hotel - some spectacular architecture & decor. - Fitness room, while dated, has lots of equipment although a few modern elliptical trainers would be a welcome change from the one circa-80's model! - Convenient location - a block from Pershing Station, many restaurants within walking distance - Large spacious business center with multiple PCs and printers Cons: - Nickel & diming hasn't changed since my last visit - Internet was included in my corporate rate, otherwise it's $10/day. Using a calling card was $1 each time - nothing obvious posted to reflect this. - My shower had two settings - hot & scalding. I asked on the second day to have someone look at it - no change on my third shower... - Elevators were far away from my room location, but no stair appeared to provide access to the lobby floor - Limited front desk staff at peak times in morning - at checkout only two (out of six?) front desk stations were manned, and the lineups could get long

“Big, Fancy, Expensive,” I've sent in 1 review on this hotel but TA hasn't put it up. I think people should know some of this stuff so i'm reposting. First, this hotel is in the middle of nowhere and close to nothing. Also, this hotel does not have in-room movies which sucks when you have kids. Most nice hotels have this feature, I was amazed that this very expensive joint had none. There is also no mini-bar in the rooms, which again was quite surprising. The staff was nice, the hotel is nice. the grounds are nice. The pool is very crowded, cabanas are 350 a day. The kids activities are pretty worthless. they're 30 bucks a pop, last 30 minutes and are pretty lame over all. although the staff did offer to loan us a monopoly game to take to our room. we passed on that very bad idea. The restaurants were poorly run and the food was terrible. the wait staff was friendly but inefficient. again the food was terrible. the main restaurant has a buffet, i would not recommend it. i would not recommend any of the food at this hotel at all. this might be a great place to golf and hang out with friends, but for families its not worth the money.

“Liked it, did not love it” If you can get it for a decent price, this is a good pick if you are looking for something in the Downtown San Diego area. It is next to the litte Italy area and relatively close to the Harbour and Gaslamp Quarter. The rooms are standard hotel rooms, were clean and seemed to be relatively well maintained. That said, housekeeping personel are using a strongly scented cleaning agent throughout the hotel to mask the hotel's "maturity". Most rooms have a balcony. My room was facing south or soutwest so I had a nice overview of the Downtown area as well as a limited view of the harbour/ocean. Internet is free at this property which is nice. A very strong positive is the hotel staff: very friendly and efficient. The hotel is within walking distance to the Little Italy trolley station if you decide to use public transit while in San Diego.

“Convenient location, but the quality of the stay felt a little cheap” I stayed here in May for a reunion and was a little disappointed. First, the benefits of the place: I was upgraded to a suite, which had a great view of the Christian Science complex. There was a small sitting area. Internet access (which I had to pay for) was fast. Room service was fast (really fast) and pleasant. But, the minuses: scratchy, polyestery sheets. Windows don't open. Chintzy towels (like the kind you get at the gym), and cheap toiletries. And the upholstery on the furniture in the sitting areas had several stains on them. I chose the hotel because I was offered a really reasonable rate, and the reunion was taking place downstairs in the ballroom. But, I had just spent the prior weekend in the Washington Hilton, which served a similar purpose (large conference hotel) and felt that the quality of the rooms were far better. Boston hotels are more expensive than other large cities. But next time, I would rather spend a little extra money for a little more luxury

“Overall decent stay” This hotel has been nicely upgraded and the room is of average size. My room felt a little damp like the ventilation was not working properly, but that is really my only negative. Parking was adequate and the business center was top notch. Excellent rate via hotwire.com

“Functional, but not spiffy!” A few months ago, I reviewed a hotel near Princeton that had this strange, sort of sterile (but not in a clean sort of way) institutional sense about it. I would have to say, this property had many of those same traits. It wasn't bad. Nor was it dirty. It just wasn't spiffy. In fact, it sort of felt like a ... University hotel! The best decision we made was to upgrade by $20 for the club level (or whatever they call it,) which meant we got a VERY nice continental breakfast for the cost of a tip. Eggs, cereal, fruit, Starbucks coffee. We left feeling very satiated, and the desk staff was certainly kind and helpful. Weird, but safe neighborhood. (Near University of Pennsylvania, with some trendy neighborhoods nearby, but you're not quite actually IN one.) Would stay again if the price were right.

“Needs updating” We stayed here years ago and nothing has changed. It needs a serious update and repaint. The whole place looks faded and rather shabby. The staff are great, helpful and cheerful, but this hotel is stuck in 1975.

“Didn't live up to the hype - nice hotel, but should be better.” My husband and I picked this hotel for a special occasion and stayed for several nights. We picked it based on good reviews on Tripadvisor. It may be that our high expectations of the hotel are the reason we felt a little disappointed, but for the price we paid (average of £290 per night during our stay) we thought the hotel and service should have been a little better. To be fair, part of our disappointment may be the poor value-for-money given the New York supplement that you implicitly pay just for the hotel being in highly desirable Manhattan. Other hotels we have stayed at in this price bracket in other cities around the world (London, LA, San Francisco, Barcelona, Rome etc.) have far surpassed Hotel Giraffe in terms of luxury, attention to detail and service. These are the things that were disappointing: Concierge couldn’t book/arrange a variety of tickets (we were told their service was mostly just theatre tickets), concierge couldn’t arrange for posting a parcel for us, the lobby is used for breakfast each morning and doesn’t have sufficient tables or toasters or crockery or staff when the hotel is busy, the housekeeping service varied each day in terms of what toiletries were left in the bathroom and slippers (only one pair, and no man-sized ones) and not getting bottled water and the iron and ironing board not being put away, room service is very limited and not of a good standard (I would avoid ordering room service from the Mexican restaurant used by the hotel), the wait time for a lift could be quite long, and no champagne was on offer during the wine-and-cheese event despite this being advertised on the hotel’s website. The things that were particularly good were: the wine-and-cheese event with live piano music most nights in the lobby was pleasant, the beds and linens were comfy, the hotel is fairly quiet despite outside traffic noise, check in and out was swift, the décor and style is good, the breakfast was good quality (though I recommend getting there early!), and the location is relatively quiet and safe and the hotel is only two short blocks from the subway. In conclusion, I think this is a nice hotel, but I think it should be better for the money.

“Fussy, not outstanding” There is no gift shop or place to pick up quick essentials nearby unless you go across the street to the Fairmont, where, you will be told after the clerk runs your credit card that you need to pay $0.10 for a bag - that is after the Fairmont gift shop clerk finishes up her conversation with another hotel staff person who is visiting. Back over at the Intercontinental, you might want to go up to the Top of the Mark for a late lunch - wrong! Even though hours are never stated in any of the in room hotel documentation, lunch is only served until 2pm. You can access the internet at two different price points, unfortunately the "basic" service is like revisiting dial-up internet from the year 2000. Rooms were nice and all that jazz, but this hotel was only so so.

“When you look up "average" in the dictionary there's a photo of this Marriott” I'm not the world's biggest Marriott fan. I admit that. Call me crazy but when I go to a city as vibrant as San Francisco I'd like my hotel to reflect a little of the local flavor. This is a dressed up Crowne Plaza and there's no mistaking that. There's a review further down with the title "Solid Marriott Experience" and I would say that's probably the best description of this hotel. Faint praise. I wouldn't book this hotel but was attending a meeting there so had no choice. The good: Location. Comfortable beds. The not-so-great: You could be in Missouri for all you'd know (all due respect to Missouri). Lackluster service and check-in Room service food neither tasty not reasonable for the quality. Jeez people - this is SF at least the bread should be fresh and delicious. Noisy - pack earplugs. Charging $12.95 for internet access when if your room is properly situated you can grab the Kimpton's free internet from across the street. There was nothing egregious about this hotel but the city is full of interesting gems. Find one.

“Great location on Mag Mile, but not five-star service” Stayed at the Intercontinental over New Year holiday. Arrived at 2.20pm. Room not ready , staff checked us in, but had to leave bags, and head out for some lunch. Not a major issue, and staff said they'd call when room was ready - no call received. Arrived back at hotel at 5pm, room was ready, and it was nice and large, in historic tower. Comfortable, but not a five-star accomodation. Everything was OK, but not the wow factor. Coffee maker in room, which was well used. One morning, there was a problem with hot water to the historic tower, and the staff offered a room in other part of the hotel for shower etc. (not great for the price of accomodation - but staff tried to assist). The hotel is right on Magnificent Mile. Ideal for all the sights. Overall, a decent stay, but nothing special for new year. If you can bag a good deal then it's a good choice. But I probably wouldnt return again - unless the price was right.

“There Are Better Options” First, the positives: the staff are friendly, well trained, and professional. The food is very good. And the location is central to all points in the District. But many rooms are postage stamp-sized. It's ridiculous to pay so much for such a small room. The shower and the sink are in the room proper, after all! The pillows and the bed were merely ok. Regardless of the cute W amenities, this is not acceptable for a top hotel. To make matters worse, my room (and I suspect many others) had only spotty cell coverage for blackberry and IPad. This was not good for the work and calls I needed to handle. The hotel scene in DC is too competitive to put up with this. I suggest finding other options if you have the choice.

“disappointing repeat(several times) visit” I will begin that I still think if you want a small one bedroom suite with living room with sofabed and need to be in theatre district, this is still your best bet, especially if you get a package with breakfast (they do continental but let you add on regular items at a small fee) and drinks. That said, I would not stay here again unless had to. Service has really declined. I was here before and after Marriott, and even my last stay- under Marriott- was better . Housekeeping is hit or mess. There is generally no doorman, and half the time you need to find a cab on your own. Room service is fine, as are drinks in the lobby. We stayed because we were seeing shows, but the "protesters" almost disrupted that Sat night. Taxis in NYC are still awful and decide if they want to take you depending on where you are going. The rickshaws are also scamming people by charging exorbitant rates. If in the area, try the Lambs Club for drinks.

“Not bad” I came to NYC for a short vacation. This hotel is almost 100 years old so I expected flaws. The lobby was very nice. The room was outdated with broken furniture and peeling wallpaper. The beds were comfortable and the bathroom was nice. Located right next to Penn Station and walking distance to Times Square and subways to other attractions.

“The best 2-1/2 star hotel” The basic architecture of the EnVision Hotel is that of a townhouse sitting on a hill; it is narrow but long, overlooking South Huntington Avenue at the front and Jamaica Freeway at the back of the structure. Two upper floors and a basement have been added since the satellite photo available online was taken, bringing the total number of floors to six (B,G,1-4). There are rooms on the four numbered floors and there are four rooms on the G floor that the front desk euphemistically calls ‘the garden level’ but that appears to consist of rooms half concealed by the hillside and that share the level with a covered parking portico and, at the rear, a small parking lot. The larger, superior rooms are located in the middle of floors 1 through 4. General pros and cons: depending upon temperament, the location of the hotel out of downtown but on the trolley and bus routes is either an advantage due to lower cost and a quick commute (15-25’) right into downtown, or a disadvantage because of the need to commute and the trolley and bus noise on Huntington Avenue. Other pros: the water was hot with good pressure. All the doors are heavy metal that close quietly and are soundproof, even the bathroom and closet doors within the rooms. Wireless internet was complimentary, easy to log onto and reasonably quick. Since there were a significant number of reviews online that complained about noise on the lower floor, we asked for an upper floor with our reservation and were given a third floor room upon arrival. Room-specific pros: With some careful and persistent internet searching, we were able to get a $109 rate for our room - about half the 'discount' rates available online. For that rate, we were given a room at the front of the hotel, overlooking S. Huntington Ave. We read the disparate reviews online before reserving and asked for an upper floor room as a condition of our stay. We were given a third floor room. The room was clean and nicely appointed with a comfortable bed, a desk, dresser, bed stand with alarm clock, refrigerator and microwave. The TV was a large flat screen with hundreds of Comcast channels. The shower was built-in, marble faced. Room-specific cons: Our front-facing room (#301) admitted the trolley noise starting at 6:15 am every day. We were up by then but a late sleeper might not tolerate it. On the last night of five, a persistent and continuous ‘cricking’, like a dripping faucet but louder, came from an outside wall. It started soon after we fell asleep but when I woke up several times during the night, it was still there. It stopped in the late morning. The marble-tiled bathroom floor was uncomfortably cold (no slippers were provided, but what do you want for 2-1/2 stars?). The HVAC consisted of your typical 2-star under-the-window unit which was typically noisy (not poorly maintained – just inherently noisy). With the extensive renovations throughout the building, it is very unfortunate that a better HVAC arrangement did not present itself. Finally, admittedly minor stuff: Only one bathrobe was provided. No big deal; the Westin that we are staying in today (q.v. review) only has one bathrobe, too, and it is not as nice as EnVision’s. The Xfinity remote control was weird. When it turned on the Comcast cable box, the LG flatscreen came on, and then went off. When pressing a trial of various buttons, the screen would power on, only to have the cable box power off. Sometimes this back-and-forth would go on for several minutes; sometimes both would stay on after only one or two tries. The fault is obviously with me for not understanding the technology; but, hey, hotel TV ought to be idiot proof. I was too embarrassed to call down to the front desk and ask how to turn the TV on. In other news, our windows each had two spring latches at the bottom and two spring latches at the top; this meant one had to have four hands in order to open a window. I never succeeded in opening a window. From the outside, the superior rooms seemed to have different windows, so perhaps this is not a problem for them. Bottom line: I would not adopt this as my Boston hotel destination but I would stay there again if it were the only way to escape the unreasonably steep hotel rates that seem to characterize this city.

“An Alright Hotel” Nice lobby, check-in was fast and easy, elevators were plentiful and fast, but the hallway to my room (917) had a rank smell to it - very displeasing. The hotel has 9 floors, room 917 was very nice and did not smell, it was clean and comfortable. Room service was fast and the food was typical hilton fare, and expensive of course. Parking close to the entrance was a bit of a problem due to the convention space they have, it was in use on every evening i was there (4 nights) - so there is a bit of a walk to the hotel entrance/elevators most evenings. All in all, it was a pleasant stay. Oh, no free in-room internet service, but the lobby did provide free wi-fi. Getting to and from downtown is a straight shot on MLK drive (under 20 minutes).

“Loud, frantic bargain-hunter's hotel; not for couples seeking relaxation” We visit San Antonio often, so thought we'd try Drury Plaza Hotel Riverwalk because of the favorable Tripadvisor reviews. It was not a pleasant experience, and we'd never stay there again. For big families looking for value, this hotel might be a good choice; the free hot breakfast can save real money. But for us, a couple with no kids, the breakfast room was mass-scale pandemonium -- the kind of thing we go on vacation to get away from. If you do stay at this hotel, do not stay in the San Fernando tower. A newer structure built over the hotel parking lot, this tower is accessible only through a convoluted procedure. You take the main building elevators, get off at 6th floor, walk a series of twisting, narrow corridors (transited by some pretty wide people) and get a second bank of elevators to your tower room. Why didn't the hotel build an elevator in this tower that at least gave street access? I felt uncomfortable knowing that if some emergency had required us to get exit in a hurry, we wouldn't have been able to. Even without an emergency, we found the 6th floor elevator exchange so jammed with breakfast crowds that we were forced to use the stairs. I suspect a city with stricter building codes would never have allowed this kind of limited egress in new construction. One thing I would highly recommend: Even if you don't stay here, walk into the beautiful lobby of the old Alamo Bank, with soaring 50-foot ceilings. It's a 1920s masterpiece.

“Basic Accommodations, Reasonable Price” The hotel is very close to the airport when exiting on 71 East. We arrived at 1:00 a.m., exhausted, and happy to find our hotel so close. We stayed in Room #304 and had a view of a mobile home park. One portion of the park had several empty, dilapidated trailers. If traveling on 71 West, there are a few restaurants and two parking areas for airport. I am unsure of the neighborhood, as there were "10 Traveler Safety Tips From McGruff" on the bed. All rooms had two sets of peep holes. The hallway lighting was unusually bright but was only lightly visible from under the doorway crack. The room had a decent sized refrigerator (approximately 3 ft. x 2 feet) with ironing board, small table and chair, and coffee maker. Furniture is inexpensive and basic – no frills – but functional. There is also a nice sized area for clothing with a metal rod. The heating/air conditioning unit is over the curtains and when the black out drapes are drawn, the drapes “balloon” out from the air blowing underneath it. However, hotel room was clean. Because the hotel is near Highway71, you can hear the traffic. Also, the sounds of aircraft taking off from the airport can be clearly heard. Lastly, the sound of running tub water can be heard from the rooms of neighboring hotel guests. Hearing these noises may be undesirable for those sensitive to sound. Internet is free, but an Ethernet cable must be obtained from the front desk with a deposit fee. The continental breakfast is available 6 a.m. to 9:30 a.m., Monday – Friday, and 6:30 a.m. to 10 a.m., Saturday – Sunday. We did not eat at the hotel but noted that the eating area is large and separated from the main lobby. There is a nice array of vending machines in the main lobby next to the reception desk for drinks and snacks. The Best Western Airport offers basic amenities at an affordable cost. For those seeking higher quality accommodations onsite at the airport, I noted a very new looking Hilton (it looks round in shape from the freeway). I believe the hotel is a good value for the price. Hotel staff is very helpful and accommodating. The hotel is sufficient for those on a budget or for a brief stay (we paid $74.00 including tax for three people under AAA Discount).

“nice concept, but expectations not met” We always hear so much hype about the Ace Hotels, so we finally stayed at THE one. For downtown Seattle the location was perfect for us ~ on the edge of center and a little off the beaten path. The size of the hotel was perfect as well - small. No fuss no muss service - meaning no bell person trying to aggressively take our bags, but the men working the front desk were kind but not intrusive. The room was small, that's no big deal in our book. We liked that we had a big window. Unfortunately it was kind of downhill from there. The bed was a full - my tall man's feet hung over the end. We had read these reviews about the rooms being so clean - they didn't seem very clean to us. Kind of grimy and in fact, the room seemed like it was time for an update, everything was worn, especially in the bathroom. But the worst part of this hotel is it is not sound proof. You can hear EVERYTHING. Every time a person moves it echoes throughout the floors and walls, every creak in the floor, every shower running, every toilet flushing, everyone blowing their nose - everything. We were lucky to hear everyone coming home late at night and felt bad knowing in a few hours we would be waking them all up when we got up at 3:30 am to go to the airport. We really wanted to like this hotel because it is very much us, but what isn't is very not us. We expected a bit more than there was in terms of quality. If the Ace took care of the noise, upgraded the interiors, and got better beds, we would be back. But I think next time we'll head somewhere else.

“Superb location, but....” Location - 5 Gardens, pool, grounds - 5 Rooms - 1 The location of this place is perfect, it is on the lagoon on one side and about 100 yards straight to Pacific beach on the other. The grounds are very tropical with lush palm trees everywhere, parrots and various ducks sharing the gardens. The pool area is very nice too. This gives it a full on 'holiday' feel. The rooms however haven't seen maintenance since they were built in what must be the 70's, if not earlier. It was quite incredible. The smell of old carpet hangs around, the bed linen had faded over the years and must be 30 years old (like when gold velvet goes smooth and very light yellow and shiny with oil stains!), there were tears in the bed sheets, the lamps didn't work, the kitchenette appliances were rusted and falling apart etc., the list goes on. It's amazing that for such a great place from the outside view, the rooms were so shabby. I'm not saying we didn't enjoy our stay, we did but I would give it serious thought about staying there again unless the rooms were modernised, even if only slightly.

“Nice, larger chain hotel, but rather outdated, and with weird computer system” We stayed here for a conference my wife was attending, so the rate was not bad, but I would not pay the regular rate. The first room we got, upon asking for a quiet room, overlooked the Hollywood Freeway, but we were given the opportunity to switch to another room, this one facing Universal Studios. The hotel is semi-eloegant, especially in the lobby areas, but overall has an outdated feel, from the decor to the older, non-flat-screen televisions. I had requested an alcove room, and was to pay $10 extra for this, but this request seems to have gotten lost (I did pay the regular conference rate). Parking was $17 for self parking. Wi Fi was not outrageously priced (about $10), but to print, you had to jump through hoops, seemingly using a third party vendor connected with the hotel, with print jobs coming out in the business center, and there was a minimum printing charge of something like $3-4 each time you printed (best to save up any printing jobs or the cost would quickly add up). I went to the business center to print, but the process was confusing there, with the representative on duty unable to reach the support technician. We asked if we could check out a little late (we were leaving the last day of the conference but not until 4, when the conference ended; we hoped to leave about 1:30). The desk clerk on duty said no, without asking what time we wanted to leave, saying that we were there with a conference if she let us stay late, everyone would want to (another representative later said okay). The hotel is within walking distance of Universal Studios and City Walk (shops and restaurants). There is a shuttle from the hotel to Universal Studios and back, but it stopped about 5 p.m. (notmuch use for dining out at City Walk). There is a shuttle between Universal Studios and the bottom of the hill (from where you just need to cross a street to access busses and subway) but did not, as far as I could see, stop at the hotel. I found it fairly easy to take a bus to NBC Studios to see a show taping. We took the subway to briefly visit Hollywood.

“Good and Bad at Hyatt Hill Country” The Hyatt Hill Country Resort is still a nice and unique place to stay... but this will likely be our last visit. The good: -The hotel's public places, especially the lobby and the grounds, are simply beautiful. Flowers everywhere. The buildings and really all resort features fit beautifully within the Hill Country setting. -Nicest resort near SeaWorld. Westin's LaCantera Resort is a nicer hotel and will likely be our next stop here, but it is closer to Fiesta Texas and is a bit more expensive. We have also stayed at the Radisson near SeaWorld and its okay but not really a resort. Its a decent hotel with a couple of pools. It is significantly less expensive than the Hyatt and may well be a better value. -Tons of kid-centered activities. Hard to beat the movies on the lawn each night, s'mores every night, the pools, the "Ramblin' River", great kid food options, Camp Hyatt, all the options for hair braiding, face painting, pony rides, (at extra cost) etc. Kudos to the staff who had puzzles and games and crayons and all sorts of other stuff set out in the grand lobby the day it rained. You really could spend a week here, never take a trip outside the resort and keep everyone very busy. -Friendly staff. Everyone... front desk, valet, pool staff, really everyone... very kind. Never spoke to a person who was rude or inappropriate. All went above and beyond. -Convenient everything... everywhere. Meaning only that you never have to leave the hotel. Its all here. Every meal option, every snack food, every toiletry, every item of clothing, everything... -Good variety of meal options: Pool side grille, buffet style meals at one restaurant (Springhouse Cafe), higher end at another (though Antler's is not near as nice, exclusive, unique as it used to be). -A couple of really nice bars. Drinks at a premium but the settings are fantastic. The less good: -Value is a relative thing. If you are stretching to pay for a room here, then everything is going to seem VERY overpriced. So, instead, I will just spell out what we paid, a few surprises, etc. And you can decide on your own the value. We arrived on a Saturday and left on a Friday. $329 for the first night, $269 for each additional... with one of the five at $269 "free". A stay 5 night and one night is free deal. It felt very expensive for what this hotel has become. Ten years ago, this was a REALLY nice place. It just doesn't quite feel worth this to us now. Our room was a double double. It was my wife and three children. They allow for three kids in a room but cannot put a roll-away bed in these rooms due to "fire code". We knew this ahead of time and our 10 year old son was fine with a sleeping bag we brought along on the floor. Camp Hyatt is more expensive than it used to be. $45 per child for a 6-10pm time slot. That $135 for one 4 hour blocks makes you think twice about making that reservation for 2 at Biga, Acenar, etc. if you want one night of your trip alone with your spouse. Springhouse Cafe buffet breakfast is $20 for adults, $10 for kids. There are slightly less expensive a la carte options. Poolside grill burgers, nachos, adult meal options are about $10 each. Kids meals about $6. Drinks extra. Sodas are $2.50 for a 20oz. Bottled water about the same. Beer is $5.50. Pina Coladas, Margaritas etc. are $8.50. The "General Store" is fantastic for less expensive eating options. Yet, granola bars are still $4. Bagels about the same. $5 for a Starbucks Mocha Tall. Breakfast tacos $3.25 each. You can get things like KrispyCreme donuts, pop-tarts, etc. if that is your kids style for food. They serve pizza, sandwiches too. Valet is $15 a night. The bad: -Its just not what it once was. Not as polished. Not as clean. -The walls either seem thinner, or our neighbors are just remarkably noisy. We could hear almost every word of conversations next door. We try to be SO tolerant... but did have to put in one call to the front desk when the family next door came in at 1130 and the two boys were screaming and wrestling, and the parents were just laughing along. -Pillows smelled musty, sweaty... like a gym. -Housekeeping seems understaffed. They could never seem to get to our room in a normal fashion so on several occasions were still at it after dinner. Neither good nor bad, but you just need to know: -I cannot FATHOM coming here as a honeymooning couple, a senior couple, really any kind of couple unless you have a slew of kids. -Again... this place is absolutely OVERRUN with kids. They are everywhere all the time. I've stayed at a lot of really nice resorts where kids fit well within the overall setting of the place. Not here. You cannot escape. Again, we are here with our 3 (ages 10, 7 and 6) ... but its tough when you find that yours are amongst the best behaved. There are kids screaming in the restaurants at all meals. There are kids screaming in rooms at all hours. There are kids running up and down the halls at nearly all hours. -Did I mention there are just a ton of kids here...? -The clientele has just changed a bit. Don't want to come off sounding elitist at all. It just feels less Nordstrom's and more JCPenny's. And don't miss the point. I may shop at Penny's sometimes too. But if I am paying Nordstrom's prices... I want Nordstrom quality. So overall, great place for kids. Not as nice as it once was. Hard to call it a value... in fact, feels pretty overpriced. Other favorites on this trip: SeaWorld still shines. FiestaTexas feels like it nickel and dimes you for everything. Loved La Fogata for dinner. Loved Acenar for lunch. Did the Rio River Boat tour for the kids sake and it was fun. Hadn't done it in years.

“good deal” If you want to visit the main atractions of DC but don't want to pay too much for a good hotel, this is a good option. It is cheaper than the others because of the location, but the hotel has a shuttle that goes to the National Mall in the morning and to the main night points in the evening. Also, even if you take a cab everyday to go wherever you want, it will still be cheaper!

“Corner king room is very misleading.” First the good news. The staff at this hotel is extraordinary-very friendly & helpful. We were greated every time we came in or stepped out of the elevator. Parking valets were great & housekeeping was very efficient and fast. Absolutely the best we have ever encountered at any hotel. The room was clean & the bed was very comfortable. The air conditioning worked great and it was HOT! The location is great, close to everything. HOWEVER, the room was tiny. We've stayed in alot of hotels in Chicago & have NEVER had a room this small. Even historic hotels that we've stayed in had rooms larger than this. It is billed as a corner king room which by definition indicates there will be windows on 2 walls and implies a slightly larger room (as in a "corner office"). Wrong on both counts. If you look at the hotel website there are no pictures of the corner king room. Also there are no pictures of the tiny bathroom sink counter, only pictures of the much larger counter there we did NOT have. It was 36" wide at MOST. There were 2 chairs in the room, one of which was the desk chair. Both were very uncomfortable and not really intended to sit in to watch tv, eat or drink a cocktail. To summarize, we really liked the hotel, but were extremely disappointed with the actual room to the point of feeling mislead.

“Average Hampton Inn Property” Located On Hacks Cross Road across from the FedEx World Headquarters. The property was recently renovated to the new Hampton Inn decor. All the usual Hampton Inn quality and amenities. I does have a small, but nice, separate room for the business office located in the lobby. The staff is friendly. Easy to drive to and plenty of parking. Some shops and restaurants a close drive away.

“OK location, old rooms with a musty smell!” rooms are rather dark and full of dodgy old furniture - maybe I was missing the point and they were supposed to be full of character - wasn't quite sure! There was a musty smell thoughout the room - reminded me of my grandparents house. Otherwise, good service, clean and good location

“Mixed experience at the Grand Hyatt” I just completed a three night stay at the Grand Hyatt in Denver (for a business trip.) I traveled alone. I had a reservation for a non-smoking room with a king size bed.
