Upon arrival I was told that the only non-smoking room available had two standard sized beds (and that a king was not available even in a smoking room.) I took the two standard sized beds. I stayed on the 7th floor. There was obvious smoke smell in the hallway outside of my room as I first moved in, but none inside of my room. The room was clean and the bed very comfortable. I had hoped for a room with a view of the mountains but instead got only a view of the hotel or office building across the street. Oh well. The doors were very loud when they closed but I was never kept awake by them. I saw very little activity on my floor, even though the front desk claimed the hotel was completely booked. I ate in the 1876 restaurant downstairs for breakfast one morning around 9:00. I had the buffet but many of the buffet items had been depleted earlier. It took awhile for replacements to be cooked. Buffet was around $16 as I recall. One evening I ordered a cheeseburger from room service. I had ordered it prepared medium-well, but when it arrived the bottom of the patty was charred beyond being edible. I called room service and they offered to make me something else (with a 45 minute wait), or to remove the charge. It was late and I had them remove the charge and I ate what I could from the meal. The night before I checked out I called to check on the bill and the room service charge had not been completely taken off. The front desk did take the charge completely off my bill at that point. I'm glad I called a night before. On the plus side service was excellent, from the friendly maids to the front desk personnel to the folks helping with cars and taxis... lots of smiles and a sincere attitude of wanting to make your stay exceptional. One note: there is another Hyatt only 3 blocks away, and it is located directly across the street from the Convention Center where my conference was being held. I would have preferred to stay at that more convenient location (my trip was booked through a travel office in my business) and I mention it to caution others traveling for events at the convention center. The walk was not difficult or time-consuming at all, just not as convenient. I walked through the lobby of the other Hyatt once and it seemed very nice.

“Great Location, Good Service” Perhaps one of the best locations if you want to stay in the shopping area. ESPN Zone is nearby to boot. Hotel was very clean and had good service. Met my high expectations for a Marriott level hotel. The only problem was the elevators were really slow. There was a large convention (always a problem on any hotel facilities) so beware for a future visit.

“Hotel is nice but inconvenient” Let's start out with the positives: the hotel was clean, the breakfast was free and plentiful, the room was a decent size (although only moderately comfortable), there was a fridge in the room, and the staff were really nice and provided good customer service for the most part. Now...the negatives. This hotel isn't really near anything if you are visiting D.C. to see the attractions and it is not near a metro stop. The neighborhood seemed safe enough I suppose but you had to drive through pretty rough parts of town to get there. There are fast food and convenience stores within walking distance but I'm not sure what else because I didn't really explore the area on foot. The worst part of our stay was the shuttle service. We flew into Reagan National and took the metro to Union Station. We arrived at Union Station right at 6:00 p.m. and were told that the hotel offered a shuttle service from Union Station to the hotel. I called the hotel and was told where to stand and that the shuttle would be there at 6:15 but they might be a little late because it was rush hour. I told them that my husband and I would be there waiting. At 6:25 I called back and asked if we somehow missed the shuttle or if it was running really late. They made sure we were in the right spot and I told them that I saw the Days Inn and Holiday Inn shuttles so I was sure we were in the right spot but that we hadn't seen a Marriott/Fairfield shuttle. The response we got was that we were supposed to get the Holiday Inn shuttle because they were picking up for them that day. In a respectful way I complained that nobody informed us of that and the Holiday Inn driver who clearly saw us didn't ask where we were going to let us know he was also picking up for the Fairfield Inn. The clerk was extremely apologetic and told us to take a cab and that they'd reimburse us for the expense. So there's an example of the good customer service. We got there and with tip the cab was $15. While we were waiting to check in we grabbed a water and two small bags of chips as a snack. When it was our turn at the counter we gave them the receipt and the lady gave us $15 in cash. When I went to pay for the snacks she told us not to worry and to accept them for our troubles. Again, another example of good customer service. After we dropped off our bags and cleaned up we wanted to go back to Union Station but we were told that they only provide service to Union Station on the hour and pick-up at a quarter to the hour (although I got mixed messages on pick up times when one person told me the shuttle left at a quarter after and picked up at a quarter till). Union Station is only 15 minutes away so I'm not sure why the shuttle can't run every 15-20 minutes? I guess that's how they schedule the shuttle so we decided to take a cab back to Union Station and pay the cost out of pocket because we didn't want to wait 30 minutes to leave on the hour. Be aware that to get a cab to the hotel you have to notify the hotel when you want to be picked up and give them about 30 minutes to get a cab to the hotel . You have to make sure to plan because you can't just go out and wave down a taxi in this neighborhood. The next day we got the shuttle to Union Station when it left at 11:00 a.m. with no problems. We met a friend for a quick lunch at Union Station but needed to go back to the hotel quickly for something. We caught the 12:15 back to the hotel and then wanted to head back to Union Station at 1:00...well, the shuttle doesn't run between 12:30 and 5:00!!! So we paid another cab to take us back to Union Station. In my opinion, if you are going to D.C. to visit attractions this might not be the best hotel for you unless you just plan on leaving the hotel in the morning and then picking up the shuttle at the end of the day. Just don't expect to go back and forth with ease. Again, it's clean and there's good customer service but it is not iconveniently located to anything and the shuttle service is so spotty it doesn't help. If the hotel ran the shuttle service every half hour all day and it was reliable then this hotel might be worth it if you get a good price. But if you are like me and try to pack in as much as possible and are planning on using shuttle service/public transportation then this hotel will leave you frustrated because you'll either have to plan around their limited shuttle services or pay for a cab.

“There are better hotels than this” I squeezed into my tiny queen bedded room to discover there was no desk, no where practical to place luggage and not even a luggage stand. This is not a cheap hotel and if you're on a business trip, no desk is ridiculous. It turns out there are double bedded rooms with desks, and the staff at the front desk politely allowed me to change rooms. The room with 1 double bed was equally as tiny. I discovered the TV behind the large basket of in-room food and moved the food into the closet. It was nice to have a bathroom gown, however, it disappeared after the first night and was not replaced. The phone next to the bed didn't work. Yes the decor is wonderfully boutique and there is free wireless, but I don't think I'll be back..

“Decent Hotel” Stayed in this hotel travelling through Charlotte. It was one of four hotels we stayed in while travelling and I would rate it average, third on our list of the four we stayed at. I don't recall the staff being overly friendly, room was clean and comfortable. I was disappointed in the price given the economy and time of year we were travelling (and in general, the hotel was starting to age slightly and had cheap decor that will not last) - I would have expected a better deal. In general though, it's OK for a one night travel through stay.

“Stanford Court -- Good place for the money” My wife & I spent a few days in SF. The hotel is in a great location on Nob Hill. It's within walking distance to Market Square & several great neighborhoods. The lobby is not visitor friendly b/c the entrance is partially hidden & there's a long, empty generic hallway that leads you to the front desk. The staff was courteous & professional. The room was spacious & clean. But some hiccups. The key card didn't work for most of our stay. It wasn't just our room but several floors. The hotel staff did its best to accommodate guests. But the problem lingered for days. That's a problem. WiFi is NOT free. A big minus. Many hotels offer FREE WiFi. Stanford Court should reconsider its policy. Overall, we liked the hotel, in part, because we got a great rate. But we didn't love the hotel.

“Nice sleep, park and fly options” We picked this motel because we were looking for a place to park our vehicle while we flew out of town for 9 days. They were the only one that let you leave your vehicle there that long. Front desk was very nice. Breakfast did not start till 6 and we had to leave at 5:20. Pool was nice but door handle was broke. Afternoon shuttle doesn't start till 4:30 and we arrived back at 3:00. They did provide early pickup when I called. Farther from airport than expected.

“Very Average” I was disappointed in this Westin. Usually I rave about the brand, but this property is tired and in need of freshening, at least as far as the rooms are concerned. No Heavenly Shower, for one thing. The hotel had almost no hot water at 6:45 am on a Tuesday. I told the front desk, and, to their credit, the problem was resolved by Wed. morning, if not sooner. The sink in my bathroom would not drain properly. Maintenance came and fixed it during the day on Tuesday, so, again, not a big deal, but still somewhat surprising. The lighting in the bathroom left a lot to be desired. It felt a bit cave-like. The view was a plus - lakeview, with a decent look to the north and Lake Michigan and the beach area. I didn't try any of the on-site dining, so I can't comment on that. Getting my car from the hotel parking lot took between 20 and 30 minutes on Wed. evening. Definitely annoying. I don't know if the hotel owns the lot, or what their relationship is with the lot, but that should be addressed, particularly at $55/day for parking. Overall, this was an average stay. The hotel was so-so, but the location was good, so getting to meetings at the Peninsula, Ritz, and other properties was pretty easy. The Michigan Ave. location was also nice, especially with the great weather during my stay.

“Nice Stay, but not many amenities” We were part of a group reservation. It was a nice stay. Staff was really nice. They addressed every thing we asked of them, and did it with a smile. This is an older property, and it could definitely use a renovation. But it was comfortable and clean. Its right next to the freeway, so its a bit noisy. Not in the best neighborhood, but we walked around with no issues. Its not really near much, so you have to walk a ways to get to the main activity areas, and restaurants. Little Italy seemed to be the closest area, and it was 5-6 blocks. You have to walk by some homeless people, which is a little disturbing, but they didn't bother us. The location is about 1-1.5 miles from all the activity down by the conference center/gas lap area The room itself was nice. Beds were comfortable. Nice crisp bedding (I like that). The bathroom had a tub/shower, toilet, and a sink with a nice size counter. There was a magnifying mirror that you could use, which was a nice touch. The towels were fluffy and smelled nice. There was a flat screen tv, which we didnt use. Nice dresser area with drawers to put clothes, also a armoir type unit with an area to hang clothes. I think there were 8 hangers in there. Only 2 plugs in the whole room, though, so bring a power strip. (we did). The carpets were a stained and could definitely use a deep cleaning or replacement. The interior halls of the hotel were kept warm and felt almost moist. Not sure what that was about - the rooms were fine. Each room has an easy to adjust thermostat, which was nice. Small restaurant downstairs didnt have much to choose from, but the prices were decent and the service good. No breakfast included here. Pool only, no jacuzzi. But the pool is quite warm. We heard its heated to 80 degrees. We were the only ones in there, so it was nice. Parking was $17 per day, not as steep as some other hotels in the area, but still a lot! What would I have liked? A bar area to sit and relax and talk to other guests (they do have a little seating area in the lobby), breakfast of some sort included, cheaper parking, and either a deep-clean or renovation. Room rates were high, and I dont think it was worth what we paid, but we did enjoy our stay.

“Can't get excited!” After reading the reviews on this website my expectations were high. The hotel didn't strike me as very architecturally interesting either inside or out. Surely not in the league of the Plaza in New York, or the Palace in San Francisco. Front desk didn't have a non-smoking room in our room category so we were downgrade to a regular room. The room was large but plain, with not much of a view. Hotel is not very user friendly, newspaper delivered on Saturday but not Sunday, no coffeemaker in the room, not much of a selection in the mini-bar. The most attractive public space, the Terrace Room is not available to guests, only private functions. The breakfast restaurant was empty, I guess the prices keep non expense account guests far away. As I said, can't get excited!

“Wonderful Chicago; Just Okay Westin” We just got back from a quick weekend trip (Jan 6 and 7) to the city to take in the sights, see a show, and visit a new restaurant. We love this city and go there about once a month. We have stayed at many of the MIchigan Ave., Loop, and River North hotels. We do not feel that the Westin is a 4 Star hotel. However, it is very nice and would return again, but it would not be our first choice. As other reviews state, the rooms are a bit dated. Our room was on the 4th floor and overlooked the roof of the neighboring building. This roof and vents that roared constantly. If staying here, request a room on the south side of the building. I can compare this sound with the sound of traveling on a plane, I kept asking my husband when we were going to land. I think we may have assigned this room because we booked on Priceline. However, we have never had this happen to us before when staying at even nicer hotels in Chicago. The hotel has a great location! As someone else stated, who stays in the room while in such a wonderful and vibrant city? We did visit the bar. Nice and they made the best cosmo I have ever had!

“OK Stay” This hotel is located a bit out of the way if you're staying in Houston. It's also a bit difficult to find currently as the freeway is under construction. The exit we needed was blocked off due to roadworks, so we had to stumble our way through unfamiliar and dimly lit streets, but we eventually found our way there. This isn't the hotel's fault, but worth mentioning to travellers as the road construction looks like it will be going on for a while. As for the room itself, one issue we had was that we booked a non-smoking room and although we got one, they couldn't hide the fact that someone had at one point lit up in that room. The smell was faint, but it was there. Other than that we found the room to be very spacious, clean and comfortable. It was a standard king, but we had a separate sofa area sectioned off a bit from the bed, which was nice. The bed was comfortable and If you can forgive the tacky palm tree painted on the wall near the bed and go so far as to enjoy sleeping near someone's misguided artwork, you'll sleep well! The bathroom was clean, even if the toilet acted up a bit and you had to jiggle the handle a bit at times. You truly do get what you pay for sometimes! Tv was full cable, wi-fi was fast. We used the guest laundry and everything was in working order, as was the ice machine. The breakfast area was clean and roomy. Food consisted off coffee, juice, cereal, fruit, bagels, sausage biscuits and a waffle iron in the shape of the state of Texas. Overall, a decent place to stay for the price.

“Clean and efficient” Stayed here while visiting family in the area. Check-in was efficient and pleasant. The room was clean and efficiently organized and appointed. We did feel somewhat claustrophobic as the room was on the small side and there is a lot in it. It felt very cold (not temperature) and sort of clinical. The mattress was firm and pleasant. The bathroom was clean and the towels were nice and large. We did not like the shampoo/bath gel in large dispensers in the shower although we do understand the concept behind it. The hall noise woke us up 2x during the night so if you are a light sleeper and there are boisterous neighbors, that could be an issue for you. We did not eat there although there is food available (not a restaurant) for purchase.

“Very thin walls” The staff of this hotel is excellent, very friendly and very helpful. The rooms are clean and well maintained. The breakfast is just average. BUT I wouldn't recommend this hotel because the walls are paper thin. I am a very sound sleeper....so it surprised me how often I was awakened. Someone drove outside my window and I could hear the gravel moving!! I could hear two guys talking in the hallway...and they were just having a normal conversation. I just thought maybe because they were just outside my door, but when they went into their room ACROSS the hall and CLOSED the door, I could STILL hear them talking!!! Thank goodness, they went straight to bed. In the morning, I didn't have to wake up to my alarm, the jets taking off in the morning were loud enough. Another thing I didn't like is that there is no computer for guest use. I travel alot and every hotel I have stayed in has a business center....even if that means just one computer in the lobby. So no printing boarding passes in advance or checking your flight. Just one of those courtesy things that most hotels do now. And then my pet peeve. Housekeeping knocks on your door before check out time. Why can't they check with the front desk to see if someone has checked out. Because of the paper thin walls, I had to listen to them knock on doors and yell "housekeeping" all the way down the hall.

“Not My Favorite” Stayed two nights for a business trip. This hotel is affordable for the loop area, but it does have some drawbacks. The room was small. There was a very small TV over the desk - the remote only seemed to work if you sat right by the TV - it did not work from the bed. The bathroom size was OK, but there was no tub - only a shower. There is no hotel room service, only menus for a couple of local restaurants that deliver in the area. I ordered dinner one night and it came without any eating utensils. There was also a $2 charge for calling the restaurant to order the dinner. The room was also noisy - you could hear every time that someone in the next room opened their door. Good choice if you are really looking for no frills, but you get what you pay for.

“OK, but not great.” I stayed at the Sheraton Chicago Hotel and Towers on business. I chose this hotel because I was getting in get in late and needed a full-service hotel. I found this to be a disappointing Starwood property. Before my arrival ---I received a very nice email confirming my stay and my Starwood preferred account. I asked for a king, non-smoking bed on a quiet floor. I got a very prompt response confirming my request. I didn't get to the hotel until 10PM. The valet was very nice and they kept asking if I wanted to self park. I didn't think anything of it, but opted to valet. Check-in went smoothly and I was checked into room 2718 (the Starwood preferred floor.) The room was very large with a nice view. The hotel itself isn't brand new and there was some wear and tear, but overall the property does seem well maintained. The bed was comfortable. The work space was very large. The seating area was great. The bathroom was spacious and clean. They stock the regular Sheraton bath products. The towels and robes were clean and plentiful. They also have a safe in the closet that will easily accommodate a laptop. I went downstairs at 10:35PM and found out that their Shula's Steakhouse closes at 10:30PM. There are no restaurants around that hotel that serve late. The concierge suggested PJ Clarks...I went and everyone I saw was smoking and drinking pints. It looked fun...just not for dinner. I went back to the hotel and found out that the late night menu also starts at 10:30PM. The menu is VERY limited and the food was not good. It was very disappointing. I went to check out the next morning and found out that valet parking is $41/day. That explained why everyone kept looking at me funny when I said I wanted to valet. I wasn't even paying and I find $41offensive. The front desk girl said it was stamped on my valet ticket. We looked and mine wasn't stamped. She also said their was a sign out front and pointed to it...the sign was no where near where valet had me pull up to or where I walked in the hotel. I'm a valet-parking, downtown hotel staying person and I'm used to high prices...but I think this is outrageous. Obviously lots of people before me have complained because she automatically went into the details about how they have compared other downtown hotels, blah...blah...blah. The lobby and lobby bar were packed with business types. I guess if everyone from your company is staying there it is OK. However, if you are an individual traveler looking for a business hotel...I found this Sheraton to be lacking. I stayed at several hotels on this last trip and I was most looking forward to my stay at the Chicago Sheraton. I also paid the most for this hotel. It was the only negative experience I had in five hotels. I emailed the woman who originally emailed me to confirm and told her about some of my issues. I never heard back.

“Nice hotel, convenient location.” I stayed at L'Enfant Plaza while visiting customers at the Naval Ship Yard. I chose L'Enfant Plaza for two reasons: 1) central location to DC, Reagan Airport, and the Shipyard, and 2) easy accessibility via Metro. I had some difficulty locating the hotel after getting off at the L'Enfant Plaza metro stop because I went out the wrong exit. Advice to future travelers: exit via "the mall" (not the Smithsonian mall but an actual underground shopping mall). The hotel is located directly above. I took the long scenic route in the 20-degree weather--oh, well! The staff was not overly friendly but still pleasant upon check-in. The lobby itself was rather opulent and it appeared that many guests were moving in and out. My room itself was fairly standard, if not a bit old. Nothing really of note--I felt like I got what I paid for. What WAS odd was that the desk was located between the two queen beds and faced the wall opposite the TV. Not a big deal--it just meant watching all of my broadcasting in reverse. :) Be aware that, while the hotel is centrally located and convenient to the mall, there aren't too many dinner options other than the in-house restaurants. The area itself is populated more with businesses. That said, it's incredibly easy to catch a Metro train to another part of town. The L'Enfant Plaza station actually serves four different lines and is only 15 minutes away from Reagan Airport. If I had to visit DC again, I would consider staying here again but would also consider other options just as fairly.

“Affordable hotel in the back bay area” Rooms are small but stylish. Not suitable for more than one person unless you like being in a confined space. Service was adequate. A little bit too much attitude from the front desk clerk but suspect they aren't aware how they come across to guests who actually expect a friendly welcome at a hotel. Overall adequate hotel in reasonable location.

“Acceptable for Broadway” If you're going to see a Broadway show and want to be "right there" this is a good place to consider. However, if you're looking for anything other than your standard hotel stay, this is not the place. This hotel is very similar to a large convention center hotel - it's an assembly line process with too many people and too few staff to devote too much attention to guests. Odd are you'll have a decent amount of wait time if you want to check in at a peak time, have bags taken to your room, etc. The rooms themselves are fairly simple. They have "modern" hotel decor though it's got a very strong Ikea look to it. The bathrooms are adequate, though my tub looked like it could have used some a stronger dose of ajax cleaner. Some of the towel were old and a bit tough, while others were new and very soft. I'm sure the views from the room vary, but I had a good view of times square and could see down Broadway to Central Park. The hotel had wifi for a nominal fee. I got a strong signal and a good connection. Normally I don't eat at a hotel, but for some reason or another I had a free breakfast, so I decided to give it a shot. It was a breakfast buffet and the food was ok. (It's hard to mess up pancakes, muffins, fruit, and cereal). The service left much to be desired, but as I mentioned - this is an assembly line hotel. If you want to be close to Broadway and won't be doing much but sleeping in your room, this hotel will probably work just fine. If you want a nicer hotel, I'd consider some other choices.

“OK for a business trip” I have stayed here a number of times for work. They are making updates. The first one is the workout room. It is really above par for a hotel. The rooms are still a bit worn. However, I am a Hilton Honors Gold member so I get the best rooms. Before I was Gold the rooms were hit or miss. The front desk staff is really nice. They try. The buffet in the morning is also above par for a hotel buffet. There too the staff tries to make it good. My only big complaint in the wireless network. If you are in a room at the end of the halls it can be slower than if you are in a room by the elevator. The beds are clean and of high quality. It can be difficult to get to if you don't know exactly where to go. The road in front of the hotel is one way. If you can get a good rate and need to do business in the area this is a good place.

“The good, the bad , the ugly” I recently had a two night stay at the La Quinta Inn & Suites San Antonio Airport location. First off, the location is about 20 mins drive time to the river walk and about 30 mins to Sea World, Fiesta Texas. I really liked the location since it was close to several restaurants and there is a Wal-Mart about a 5 mins walk across a parking lot away. This hotel/motel is ideal for families on a budget, in fact on my stay that’s all I saw. The have a decent free breakfast in the mornings which include make your own waffle station (although 10 min line for that), cereal, yogurt, toast, fresh fruit and donuts juices coffee ECT...the rooms have a microwave, and a small fridge that’s empty so you will be able to fit alot of food /drinks in there if necessary. This is where the Wal-Mart location to the hotel comes in handy, very easy to stock up on snacks and drinks. The walls of the hotel seem to be paper thin, you can hear talking and walking in the halls, slamming of doors, peoples conversations in the next room if they speak above a whisper. Not good if you like to sleep in on mornings. The sheets, pillow cases, and most of the bed is as cheap as it can possibly be, they need to update their sheets,, they were thin and had a very cheap feel to them, im sure they were just old and need replacing. They do have a shuttle that will take up to 3 miles to a nearby restaurant if need be and an airport shuttle. They did have internet connection and in room movies and about 10.99 each, of course basic cable and HBO were free. They did have in room video game for a fee. There was not an in room safe anywhere to be found. The pool area was nice, small patio with a few chairs and tables with umbrellas and the pool was small but nice, they had a Jacuzzi area but full of kids as to be expected at this type of hotel. All and all this hotel best suited for families, easy access to all San Antonio areas , free parking, no crazy resort fees to be paid. Staff seemed to be a bit robotic in checking in but was sold out the weekend I stayed so im sure they had to repeat alot of info that day. They were pleasant the next time I had to ask for directions and gave me a map of the area which helped redeem themselves. The entrance to the hotel is a bit strange, located on a side road with only one entrance, a bit confusing the first time you get there but ok after you figure it out. This hotel not a bad deal for the money as long as your not looking for the over the top amenities.

“It was… pretty good.” Driving up to the Crowne Plaza Jacksonville Riverfront is a lovely experience – a nice looking river-side hotel with a beautiful lobby and exciting surroundings. After the first few steps inside beyond the lobby; however, the experience became a little less “lovely” and more and more “blah”, as the hotel really is nothing too special. The front desk staff was friendly, but I wouldn’t say professional. The elevator ride up to the room was eerie, as these could use a definite upgrade – as could the hallways, which obviously haven’t been renovated since the 70’s. The room was dark because there were not enough lamps for the size of the room, and I thought it was strange that I found two of the lamps and the TV unplugged (took me a moment to figure out why these things weren’t working). The view from the room was really great, and the bed was very comfortable! Another plus, was that the room was quiet, you are not able to hear the noise from outside. Possibly the best part of all, is that every room has a balcony! Awesome! One more redeeming factor was the price of the room service. For about $14 total I had a full breakfast delivered by room service, which included eggs, potatoes, sausage, toast, juice, morning flowers, and a huge pot of fresh coffee- this just made my day! I would conclude that this hotel is just “ok” by luxury standards, but nevertheless the overall experience was pretty good!

“Nice location, bad advice” We recently stayed at this hotel and have mixed feelings about it. The facility is nice but not as nice as some other Sofitels e.g. Philadelphia. It is better in terms of condition than Madrid, Geneve and some others. What bugged me was the way they kept saying, "Our desk staff know everything about Chicago" when they clearly did not. We had bad advice about outdoor markets, locations of attractions, and average time on the trains to the airport. It is nice but I think you can do better.

“Anemic air conditioning” Spent 1 night there between flights (actually, more like 8 hrs), so didn't see much of the hotel in gen'l. AC in my room was pretty much useless-just ran & ran but didn't seem to really reduce the temperature. Bathroom is among the smallest I've ever seen-you can either sit on the toilet or have the door open, but can't do both. Did not sleep well, but I suspect that was more a reflection of the time of flights than anything else. It's fine for a pit stop between flights, but would not want to stay there long-term.

“Great staff, ok rooms” My husband and I spent three nights in September at the W City Center Hotel for our anniversary. Although we are fans of the W Hotel chain in general, we booked this room because we got a great $179/night AAA rate. The location is fair. It is in the business area of the Loop and is VERY quiet on the weekends. The rooms are dark as described in previous reviews. I asked for a room facing the street facing the inner courtyard as I thought this would result in a light filled room. However, the room was still dark because of the tall buildings surrounding the hotel. It was nicely decorated and the bathroom was a good size with Bliss products. The best part was the bed which is very plush and cozy. The staff was also exceptionally friendly from check-in, concierge, and housekeeping. Overall, I would choose to stay in a hotel next time closer to the river or the Mag Mile. I felt a little isolated at the City Center but the price of $179/night could not be beat.

“Clean room in a convenient location” I was traveling for business and there was not a lot of availability for that evening in DC. The Washington Plaza was clean and in a convenient location. It is a bit tired and could use some updating especially in the bathroom but it was clean. The hallways were purple - bit odd. The staff were very friendly and helpful. I wasn't looking for much more as it was a single night stay for a business trip.

“Does not live up to its reputation” This is a luxurious hotel, with an imposing lobby and pleasant guest rooms. The front desk staff is helpful and efficient. However, some of the "suites" for which one pays extra are really imaginative arrangements of odd-shaped space. Telephone service is slow and inefficient, so that during our stay callers who tried to reach us were misdirected and in one case disconnected. The in-house restaurant will serve you a bagel with smoked salmon for breakfast for about $25, but 20 yards along 44th street the same breakfast costs $10.50. There are only a few French-speaking staff members, so the ambiance is not that of a French hotel. I greeted staff politely in French, as one would in a French hotel, and got blank looks. So this is a nice property, but one can do better at these prices. Try one of the Kimpton hotels, for example.

“Great Location - Mixed Service” My family and I stayed at the Marriott for 3 nights to start our Northwest vacation and our review is mixed. Although I made one reservation for two rooms they put the rooms on separate floors. We had to wait past 5pm for two rooms on the same floor. Then the air conditioned in the second room would only blow hot air. They did correct the problem by giving us an awesome corner room (very spacious with nice views of Pugent Sound). In the end it was a great location. The cafe had excellent food selection and prompt service. The restaurant was the complete opposite. We have terrible service; our waiter finally admitted to giving our food to another table when we asked him why our meals were taking exceeding long (we waited over 30 minutes for french toast and an omelet). In the end the food was mediocre at best. So, I would recommend staying here for the location but just don't eat in the restaurant.

“Good location, somewhat dated” The location is good in that it is right on the Riverwalk, however given the size of the overall Riverwalk area, as long as you have a hotel in reasonable distance from the Riverwalk you would be alright. You are going to be walking so I wouldn't necessarily stay right on the RIverwalk next time if it meant saving a bit on the room rates. Also made it a bit noisy when trying to sleep with revellers right below us. The lobby area, breakfast room, bar and all of the ground/first floor are very nice and modern, but that doesn't follow on to the rooms. The room we had was adequate, fairly sized but very dated. The carpet was on the worn side and the bathroom could do with an update. I certainly don't need a brand new room whenever I stay in a hotel, but i expect massive groups like the Marriott to spend on updating old rooms when they charge high rates. If I went back to SA, I would stay here but the rates would have to be massively discounted.

“Very Comfortable but Let Down by Breakfast Service” Stayed here to be close to downtown. Large, well presented clean room. Comfortable bed. Good sized bathroom with double sinks/vanity unit between bedroom and bath area. Room overlooked street and main police station, but I didn't notice any disturbing street noise. Found the large kitchenette very well equipped. Selection of food from hotel's own market area was poor however, but I didn't starve the one night I didn't feel like going out. Did try the restaurant at adjoining Marriott-group hotel. Food was good, but service was poor. Friendly, welcoming staff. Watch the hotel main entrance door. It's set so close to the street that the automatic door opening sensor has been angled so you litterally have to have your nose up against the glass before it will open. Amusing if only slightly inconvenient. My only real disappointment was the free buffet breakfast. The selection and quality was very poor and regardless of the time I ate, the food was not very hot - the coffee was also luke warm. I realise that it was free, but I still think you should enjoy what you're eating. If I am in Houston again, I may stay elsewhere, but only to compare the breakfast with another hotel's.

“Large Rooms, but it ends there” Let me first say we never stay in Midtown, but we had 2 Broadway shows in 1 weekend, so decided to stay in touristville and the London had nice reviews on T.A. The rooms at the The London are very spacious, almost empty, no artwork or prints on the wall, very cold and sparse. Terrible check in. Young girl checked us in, telling us our room was not available at 4 pm, because the current guests have not checked out as of yet. ?????? Well then, it's a 500 room hotel, find us another room. Duh! She was a dope. No customer service or smile or kindness and no upgrade. Made us stand there while she called a someone. No HD tv's in the room, and the wireless had to be hooked up by calling an outside I.T. tech that was not located in the hotel. More headaches. Last thing, I am a New Yorker and have never spent $21. on a cocktail in my life. Even in Paris or London. Can you say RIP OFF? Bar is filled with guests in sweat shirts and hoodies, while other people are having high tea. Makes no sense. How about a dress code? Gordon Ramsey would be appalled. If you are looking for a $349. bargain price and close proximity to the theatres and midtown, then this is a fine choice, if you like mediocrity. I suggest you stay at the Trump Soho and take a cab to your show, same price and a fabulous hotel who appreciates their guests. PS. the lights on the desk did not work either. Such a shame. The Rhiga Royal was a swanky place.

“Shabby rooms, good staff” This W really is not up to snuff. Rooms and baths are small, which is expected in NYC, but also shabby and outdated. It's as though all the attention has been lavished upon making a cool lobby and bar. The staff is very helpful, however--it's just that a renovation is desperately needed.

“Suitable” I stayed at the Hilton one night for work. Had a great view of Coit Tower. Room was clean and had a chair to sit in, but the TV was not flat screen, room was small, and the location is great for the financial district but it's not on a very attractive street abutting Chinatown. Free internet, though. I had stayed in the Fairmont the week before for about $100 more and the room there was three times better but it was full this time.

“Beauty - but blips” The experience at Hotel Commonweath had pluses - but also minuses. On the plus side: --The rooms are nicely designed and well-furnished --Linens and bath towels are good quality --Size of hotel is comfortable But - minuses made this less than a four-star experience: --Cleaning equipment of staff left in bathroom --Movies (DVDs) offered as available upon request (but titles were not available) --Items ordered through room service were missing from the tray on *two* separate orders. This is to be weighed against the cost -- which is "much more than moderate." One can do better in Boston.

“Good location, poor service” A typical large Westin, the check-in is up an escalator which is not ideal but the biggest issue of mine was the room. Although a decent size I was very annoyed to be given what was obviously part of a bigger suite with a pull down bed (large single size) rather than the king size bed that I had booked months previously and as I specify as my preference on their Starwoods loyalty scheme. On complaining I was told my room had been given away earlier as I'd checked in towards the end of the day (having previously informed them that I'd arrive after midnight) which I don't think is acceptable. As I was on a business trip alone it wasn't too much of an issue but had I been with my 6ft 5 husband there is no way either of us would have got any sleep. As an apology I was offered breakfast vouchers, usually a bonus as Westin breakfasts can be great but there was only a Starbucks style cafe which was pretty dire. The location is good and the pool (although tiny) was very clean with well kept changing rooms but I was pretty fed up by the time I checked out of this hotel. Best thing was Lola's cafe for breakfast just up the road - not to be missed!

“Nice, but not all that I expected” Just returned from our stay in Dallas at the InterContinental. Overall, this is a pretty nice hotel. The lobby is beautiful and it looks like it's a very nice place to have wedding receptions, proms, or other events. The rooms though, are just average. Not exactly what I'd consider to be worthy of the 4-star rating it was given. We had a room with 2 beds. Every hotel I've stayed in over the last few years has 2 queen sized beds. These were double beds...almost more like a super single. This would be fine for just one person per bed, but sharing a bed with my teenage daughter was cramped. The bed itself was comfortable, but the sheet had a hole in it (must've been the same sheets another reviewer had!). The tv was an old, 19 inch. Not the flat screens I've become accustomed to in other hotels. And the curtains only partially covered the large wall of windows...full curtains over each 1/4 end, but a sheer curtain across the middle section. There was no closing the curtains all the way, so that meant the room was lit up at night and there was no need for a wake up call due to the sun beaming into the room the next morning. Water pressure in the shower is a big deal to me, and this shower didn't pass the test. Also, I've become accustomed to just using the shampoo/conditioner provided at the hotel, but this hotel only offered shampoo. Not an all in one version, just shampoo. Luckily I tossed in some conditioner when I packed. The toilet is extra low-flow, so you have to hold the handle down until it flushes completely. And when there was noise in the hallway or in the parking lot, you could hear it in the room. Luckily it wasn't a noisy weekend. Probably the biggest issue of all was parking. The hotel has a nice sized parking lot, but the majority of it was blocked off. There were cars parked there, and it didn't seem like it was for valet, but we had to park far from an entrance. The 2nd night when we returned to the hotel there was a military ball going on and there were twice as many cars in the parking lot as there were spaces. I mean cars EVERYWHERE! We left and came back, finally found a parking space, but again it was far from an entrance. We could've used valet, but they were so busy with the ball guests, there didn't seem to be time for us. So self parking, yes they had it, but it wasn't convenient or very user friendly. Staff was very nice. Overall, I guess I'd just say that this hotel needs updating. It's clean, has nice features, its just not quite up to the standard I've come to expect from a 4-star hotel...which is what this one is supposedly rated.

“One of the most difficult properties I have reviewed...” I have reviewed a good number of properties, and the moment I unlocked the door to my room, I said to myself - How in the world am I going to review this property? The property is a little hard to find - you can see it from the interstate, but it's down a side road, so my GPS put me on Zumstein Dr - but it didn't take me TO the property, I found it after assuming that it was further down the road. Upon arriving, looking at the outside of the hotel I asked - What did I get myself in to? The property is an old Residence Inn by Marriott - it was Marriott's first concept for an extended stay property. It almost feels like a timeshare resort when you pull up. The welcome I received from another guest was the first indicator that this would be an overall odd experience - "Can I have a cigarette, buddy?" - Uhhhh - yeah, I don't smoke. Very tiny lobby some basic food and drink items available for purchase in the shop in the lobby. Along with some personal care items locked with a chain in a glass case. The young lady that checked me in was very busy - but she was very polite and checked me in very quickly, explained how to navigate the property - and I was on my way. The hotel is built like an apartment complex - there are 1st and 2nd floor rooms, no elevators to 2nd floor rooms. So, if it rains or snows - you're walking from the parking area in the rain or snow. All around the resort you can see why Marriott would have sold the property - it is in rough shape. The steps up to my room on the 2nd floor were crumbling - and the wood landings were less than well maintained (peeling paint, over-sprayed blue spray paint outside the door) Some of the sidewalks were crumbling, and the building exteriors weren't very fresh in appearance. I had reserved a Queen Bed Studio room - I was upgraded to a suite - 2 br - 2 ba - kitchen, fireplace, and living room. As soon as I walked in I was hit with cooking odors (fried onions) - not a pleasant smell! The upstairs bedroom is loft-style, with a double bed (it looked like a double anyway) - and the master bedroom had a king bed. Since it was just me, I slept in the master bedroom, and the bed was very comfortable. The chair and sofa in the living room were very well used and broken down. The seat back of the chair was almost completely collapsed, and the arms were very stained and dirty looking. The sofa was VERY uncomfortable, very sagged in the center. Overall - was the resort clean? Reasonably. I say reasonably because the surfaces, bathrooms, linens (except for a cigarette burn on the bed runner), carpets, draperies, and walls were all clean. Were they spotless? No, but they had been cleaned - and the carpets and window coverings are all fairly recent replacements. Overall the units are dated and in need of maintenance - the secondary lock on my door was broken. The area seems very prone to vehicle break-ins, and they make sure to collect your vehicle information at check in. The hotel is near the end of a dead end access rd. At one time this property was amazing, you can tell that it was cutting edge in the extended stay business when it was built. It is still a nice property. Would I suggest this property to someone else? It totally depends on what you are looking for. If you are OK with a great value priced hotel that is a little rough around the edges - then by all means, this property offers an excellent value! If you are a very picky hotel guest and totally freak out when something isn't as clean as it would be in your own home... then this property would not be a good match for you. If you are looking for a temporary long term corporate rental on a limited budget, this property provides a great price and plenty of space for the price paid. The accommodations are clean, comfortable, and livable. However, don't expect the same type of accommodations that you would find at a Homewood Suites or a Candlewood Suites. I only stayed for one night for an overnight through traveling through the area - but it met my needs, was very easy on the budget, and they did upgrade me to a huge suite! I can't lie, I wanted to go buy a couple fire logs and enjoy the fireplace - it was snowing during my stay. The free wi-fi worked well, there is free breakfast but I didn't take the time to stop into the gatehouse for breakfast. If you aren't incredibly picky when it comes to hotels, give this property a shot - as I rated, it is an average property - nothing stellar.

“Great location but pricey” The hotel's location is excellent, literally just a few steps from Times Square. We stayed on the 19th floor which was nice and quite. The rooms have a good size and are clean. Bathroom is a bit outdated and small though. The services staff is friendly and there's free internet access in the lobby, also wireless! In the room you pay $14 per day. The shop is expensive though, if you want to buy a drink, do so from the vending machine, they are about half price! All in all a good experience.

“Great location, neat and clean, outdated” We stayed here before an early morning flight out of IAH. The location is perfect for the airport (don't be mistaken, Downtown Houston is quite a drive from the airport). The hotel has clearly been built in the 80s. It has features like an indoor, but open-to-the-lobby pool on the ground level that are outdated. However, as old as the design and features maybe, they are kept very nicely and mostly everything is clean and neat. Rooms are of average size and quiet with an updated design. The bathrooms are clean but could use a renovation. There is free WiFi in the lobby and also computers for customer use. Parking is free right outside the hotel. We paid 60$ per room via Priceline. For this money the hotel is a steal. If I had to pay rack rate, I would probably consider one of the nearby hotels of the Courtyard class, since on a short layover most of the services of a Sheraton are not needed.

“Mediocre business hotel in a great location” I've stayed in numerous downtown Los Angeles hotels, and never chosen the Sheraton. But it was the hotel for convention I attended, so there I was. The Sheraton's location, at 7th & Hope Streets, is great. 7th St. is one of the liveliest parts of Downtown LA, with lots of restaurants and bars. 7th St. Metrocenter rail station is across the street, 4 metrorail lines go out from there to Hollywood, Culver City, Long Beach, and Koreatown. Numerous bus lines from all over Los Angeles stop nearby. For conventioneers, it's maybe a 15 minute walk, or a one stop Blue/Expo Line ride to the Convdention Center. Bottega Louie, the great bakery/pizzeria/restaurant, is a block away at Grand. Locations in LA don't come much better than this. As a hotel, the Sheraton has some advantages. It's clean, it's quiet, it's dark at night (and adequately lighted in the day). Rooms go up to the 24th floor, but that doesn't give you the view it might (at least facing west) because there's a taller building on the same block. My room was good sized, not that anything particularly interesting was done with the space. Not so good: Slow elevators which all can stop on each of the 24 floors. A completely uninteresting restaurant--in Downtown Los Angeles this is practically criminal. Lots of nickel and dime charges for things--most egregiously $14 a nigh--$14--for wireless in your room. At this point, charging for wireless in the room is just ridiculous. There';s a small group of computers downstairs one can use, which is fine (if somebody's not playing games on them), but no substitute. I had a bumbling check in which took almost 10 minutes because they had me down as a "no show:" from the day before. I had called the day before to tell them I was coming a day late, which eventually seemed to show up in the records. Mostly there's a whole lot of blah--notably completely blah decor in the room. I don't think business hotels have to be this way. The Omni isn't a brash boutique property, but it is a smooth running operation that makes you feel taken care of, not merely extracted from. There are a lot of better hotel choices in Downtown Los Angeles..

“Acceptable Only if You Need Accomodations in the Area and Book Cheap with Hotwire” Because I book many hotels on Hotwire for the great prices, this review is based on the low price I paid. Had I paid the hotel's "rack rate" on their website, the review would have been 2 stars. But for $58/nt, it's pretty much the best deal you can find in decently Central/North Dallas for clean accommodations. Frankly, I think Starwood makes a mistake in branding these old, outdated hotels Westins. I remember not too long ago when a Westin meant something special and contemporary; now it seems to be their stodgiest brand, based on several recent stays in different cities. The rooms' decor was rather shockingly 1980's. The curtains, with their dark red floral patterns, were laughable, as was the outdated sink, shower, and bathroom. The windows looking out were filthy; apparently window washing when out the door at some point in the 90's. All of that said, the Starbucks in the room was nice, the staff was friendly, the common areas and parking clean. Didn't use the gym this time, and it's annoying to have to pay $12 for parking in such a parking lot of a city, and $10 for slow internet access is still a rub. But you can tell that they're just trying to get whatever extra fees they can, since they have to offer such low nightly room rates. All in all, it beats the Super 8 or Travelodge experience, but not by much.
“Average but great staff!” The hotel was average in cleanliness and had a peculiar smell throughout the lobby...however, wonderful staff in all aspects and convenient- across the convention center.

“Day Rate Stay” We stayed at the Sheraton Gateway on a day rate as our flight came into LAX at 9am and our flight to Auckland didn't leave until 11:30pm that night. Called the day before to reserve and upgraded to the club level. This included breakfast and hors d'oeuvres with drinks at 5. The day rate club level was $170 for 4 people-1 room. Took the shuttle from the airport to the hotel, checked in. Room was not ready (even though they had said our rental was from 9am to 6pm) so we left our luggage and went up to the Club Level room and had breakfast. Got into our room and after luggage arrived we headed out to catch the trolley to Manhattan Beach. Enjoyed the day walking the beach and pier, having lunch along the beach and enjoying a few drinks at a couple of the bars. Took the trolley back to the hotel, showered, changed clothes and enjoyed a couple of cocktails and the hors d'oeuvres in the Club room, then checked out. Caught the shuttle back to the airport. Had a couple of minor issues with the hotel - first the room wasn't ready upon arrival even though they specifically told me the rental was from 9am to 6pm. We almost missed breakfast because they quit serving at 10. Luckily we got there just before that time so were able to take advantage of the breakfast that is a part of the Club Rate. Second issue was the number of towels in our room. We specifically said we had 4 people in our room and we paid extra because of that fact but they only had 2 bath towels in the bathroom. We called for more towels but they didn't bring them until after we had to be ready to check out (two of us dried off with the hand towels). Not major issues but irritating at the time. We were happy that we had a place to leave our luggage so we could do something other than hang around the airport all day/evening.

“It's all about expectations” I booked the hotel through a convention (ASCO) despite the generally bad reviews on this site. I figured if the place was as bad as the reviews, ASCO would find somewhere else for me to stay. No need as the place is fine. If management is reading this, my advice to you is to spend the money to get a carpet cleaner and regularly use it. Almost every review here mentions stains on the floor and my King+ room also had two not so nice stains on the carpet. It's an impression thing. Pros: The bed was comfortable, showers hot, AC worked, TV worked (though no CNBC?), WiFi worked, and for a Chicago hotel a block off Michigan it was surprisingly quiet on the 15th floor. Safe in the room was big enough for a larger laptop. Closet was adequate, drawers worked, and the front desk staff was presentable and nice whenever I had a question. Price in comparison to Chicago rates. Close to some fabulous restaurants (Heaven on Seventh 2 blocks away is like falling into New Orleans!). 20-30 minutes by convention shuttle bus to McCormick Place. The Cons: Stains on the carpet were unsightly, but my white socks got no dirtier walking around the room than any other 3-4 start hotel of similar age I've been in. The cleaning staff forgot to replace the shampoo, but a note left on the bed fixed that. No CNBC on the TV is a problem for business travelers. The walls are thin, so if you have rowdy neighbors you're not going to get sleep. I paid $169/night for this hotel. In Orlando, San Diego, or smaller urban areas I would strongly have felt I paid too much. I think that's where most of the bad reviews come from. People figure if they are paying nearly $200/night they should get 4-star accomodations. Well, not in downtown Chicago baby... I'll book the same hotel any time I'm in Chicago for a conference.

“Grand Architecture, Outdated Rooms” Upon arrival, I was struck by the guilded ceilings and grand architecture on the first floor of the hotel. However, the rooms were in much need of renovation. The first room they gave me looked as if they hadn't finished decorating it (no pictures, tape on the floor) and it had an older TV (not a flat screen). The second room was better but there was still no flat screen (in fact the TV was even smaller than in the first room), the bed was lumpy, and there was an annoying fan tied to the light in the bathroom. Lastly, given the age of the hotel, it's not completely ADA compliant (you have to go up 2 steps to get to the elevator from the front desk area). I was there for a conference and if my visit was restricted to just the first floor and the meeting rooms, I would have rated my overall experience higher.

“Good Value” The suites are big and very good value, but they are a little tired and need a renovation. The beds are really comfortable and the aircon is supremely efficient. The suites are clean, have a good fridge and coffee maker but the bathrooms are small and old, and the furniture was visibly worn. The staff in the bar (particularly Katerina from the Czech Republic) are delightful, and cannot do enough for you. The food is of a high quality and the people here are really what makes this a good place to stay. Thanks so much to the team who turned this from average to nice.

“Not bad but not great” Here are the good things - great location, very comfy bed, friendly staff. Clean. I actually like the toiletries in dispensers - much greener that way. Coffee in the lobby this morning was good. On the down side, the furniture in my room was banged up and there was peeling paint around the windows - only one elevator to the fitness room -- there is a reason there is no picture on the website. Not the worst sweatbox but not great - there was a wait for equipment.

“Good location, small rooms” This is billed as a resort, I suppose because they have two pools. However, I have stayed in larger rooms in Manhattan. The basic rooms are cramped, especially with two beds. On the positive side, the TVs are among the best I've ever found in a hotel--so good that we stayed in two nights to watch movies in the room. Located on the bay but not on the beach. Should you be going to Sea World, this would be a good location with a free shuttle.

“Good Value, Clean ; Breakfast jsut OK, surrounding area not great” I stayed at this HIE for 13 days in early November. It was clean, quiet and fairly well maintained. Staff was friendly and I heard them assisting many with directions and recommendations. Pros Nice value, easy access to downtown & Market area Easy on & off highway I had a King Suite, very nice size Excellent water pressure Cons Breakfast was iffy; eggs tasted like too much water was mixed in them before scarmbling most days Immediate surrounding area was mostly warehouse, small businesses. You could walk in the day to the Market area, but some may feel uncomfortable because it is a bit deserted. Transit to downtown & Riverwalk was about 1 1/2 block walk. I had a very strange occurrence. My first day, they had no shampoo for the room. The clerk check some unoccupied rooms, but said they had already borrowed from Peter to pay Paul, so he didn't expect to find any. The 2nd day, still no shampoo to be had!! Overall. not a bad stay, some bumps in the road, but comfortable and always clean.

“Pros and cons - just the facts” Pros: 1. Nicely decorated rooms 2. Comfortable beds and bed linens. 3. Friendly valet service 4. Easy access to I-5 and area attractions Cons: 1. Smarmy employees at check in (long lasting impression) 2. Expensive valet parking (usual for downtown)- do not recommend area parking lots!! 3. Horrible maid service (towels, toilet tissue and Kleenex NOT replaced, just a few of the many unpleasant experiences) 4. Bland, expensive food at the hotel restaurant 5. Lots of street noise. My room was on the 6th floor. 6. No fridge=more hassles than you can imagine I always walk into a motel/hotel with a positive mind set. My reviews are usually fair and positive. However I can not give this hotel a positive review. I frequent San Diego and will not stay at this hotel again.

“Loved Location - Hated Hall Noise” Hotel location is excellent. Good access to all public transportation. Rooms are small, but nice. Short on drawer space. Stetsons food and service are excellent, but pricey (as expected). This Hotel has the WORST hallway noise in the room of any hotel I have ever stayed at. If they put you in a room next to the elevator, RUN to the nearest Motel 6.

“Good cheap date” Premier location on Michigan Avenue. Great old building. Attentive service. But there is alot of competition in this 4-star category in Chicago. The rooms are small, but nicely done and very clean. I was recognized at check-in as a Priority Rewards Platinum and told I had a "special" room reserved for me, but then found out when I got upstairs that it was literally two feet from the elevator in the old tower. Little touches are lacking. After wandering two floors trying to find an ice machine, I finally just went down to the bar in the lobby. The faucet in the bathroom sink was missing the "H" and "C" tabs on the knobs making it look like it needed repair. $2 charge for dialing toll-free numbers. Who does that anymore? If you can get a good rate (which I did in the middle of winter in Chicago), it's a good choice. But if not, I would shop around. It's not a bad choice. Just not the best choice.

“Beyond Overrated!!!!” I was really looking forward to this one night getaway from LA we were going to have and I just got back tonight. I have to say from the moment we arrived my experience began to go downhill. When we pulled up at 8PM on a saturday night there was no valet or bellman to greet us. I simply opened my car door and my girlfriends and opened up the trunk and got my luggage out and waited for a few minutes and finally saw someone and I said, "Excuse me we are checking in." No one opened the door for us or anything. We finally got to our room and I have tosay the room besides the very nice TV looked like the room PRIOR to the multi-million dollar rennovations. The outside and inside decor of the whole hotel resembled a motel. HONESTLY!! The pools were outdated and had no real ambiance at all. The sheets and pillows were the worst I have slept on in so many years. The massage today was pretty good but I can tell you one thing, the spa that is supposed to be #1 in America is definetly not #1 in America! The food was actually pretty good and this morning we sat outside and had breakfast in the Veranda and the nest thing we all knew, a golf ball came flying at our heads. No warning or nothing so be careful. I am a golfer but did not golf this trip and the greens were nothing of a private country club that it is said to be. Very inconsistent with color and a mix of brown and dried grass every few feet. Overall, I have been to some pretty amazing hotels and this was suposed to be a great one, however I have truly no desire to go back here again and would be truthful to say I wouldn't feel comfortable reccomending it to people who wanted an incredible experience. Decent at best.

“Seen worse” The hotel is conveniently located near the airport. Check-in process was quick and efficient, nice customer service. The room doesn't live up to expectations when compared to main hall. My first room didn't have a functioning LAN cable, and wireless wasn't stable enough. Asked to move, which they agreed to without questions. Second room didn't have any internet problems. The corridors had a nice perfume, not the usual musty smell of huge hotels. The bathroom is the most disappointing part of the room. A/C wasn't noisy, which is always nice in a hotel room. I couldn't get to any TV free channel. It seems like modern trend is to charge for anything and everything.. Newspaper service is USA Today, but you can get a real newspaper (Financial Times) in the Hilton Club on the 16th floor, or in one of the restaurants. I tried their restaurant ("The Cafe"): the salmon was just barely ok, but the veggies it came with were great. Again, good customer service. What I don't like is this modern trend for dimly illuminated restaurants.. They should invest a few $$ and call a lighting PRO. Breakfast buffet mediocre, I'd rather go with the free continental breakfast at the Hilton lounge if you have access to it. Bar is expensive like any hotel bars..

“Adequate but overpriced” The public spaces and the restaurants are excellent, but the room itself was extremely small (likewise the bathroom), and the mattress not especially comfortable. At $269, a poor value.

“Average Place to Stay” Just finished a 14 night stay here and if I had to do it again....I probably wouldnt. All was not bad here...but let's do the good first: I felt the staff in the morning for breakfast downstairs was very good most days. In particular, Hiemi (?) sorry if I misspelled his name. He's very personable and was a joy chatting with in the morning before heading out.; Excellent wi-fi coverage throughout the building; location, location, location....hotel less than a mile from St John Town Center with lot's of places to eat and shop....something for everyone...Cheesecake Factory, PF Chang, Crispers...you name it; minutes away from 295 and 95... Bad Issues: The room walls are paper thin...i could hear a regular conversation in the room next door; filters in air conditioning units need to be replaced, air was very stale when ac was on...my room was quite dusty including a layer of dust on the desk and chairs; my floor wasnt always vacuumed daily and the sheets either didn't fit the mattress or weren't put on properly because they would come up off the corner during the night. I didn't have an issue with being a pet friendly hotel, but i think pets should be limited to rooms on the 1st floor. I was provided an upgrade mid-way through my stay and after the general manager received word of my prevous issues, the housekeeping level provided to my room was highly improved. I hope this level of attention is now the standard and is being received by every guest in the hotel. The suites back up against the elevators. Normally this would be an issue, but the elevators are pretty quite and the living room is in between the room and the elevator shaft. To be fair, there's not much they can do about the thinness of the walls, but getting all employees on the same page as far as their attitudes, and level of service they provide will go along way to making this hotel a really nice place to stay.

“Good Location, Average Accomodation” Stayed one evening only, while attending an event at Baltimore Convention Center. Can't beat the convenience of the location for attending events at the convention center, with the skywalk connection. Check in was fast. I signed up for the Starwood rewards, and they threw in a breakfast, which was nice. I asked for a 1PM checkout, because we needed to attend an early session at the convention center expected to end at noon. The desk attendant countered with 12:30, but then gave 1PM. Nice that they were willing to help. We had room with two double beds, for two adults plus two kids (14 and 11). The rooms are on small side. Same for the bathroom. While clean, the bedrooms and bathrooms are otherwise fairly ordinary for these times. At least the beds are relatively firm and comfortable, albeit small for two people when you are accustomed to a queen or king. Although it was perhaps in the 40's for outdoor temperature, the room was warm, and too warm to sleep, even though the heat was not on. We had to turn on the air conditioner, which worked fine, although a bit noisy. Breakfast buffet at Orioles Grille was OK in terms of food, but our waiter was very helful. Checkout was very fast, with either printout or emailed receipt. All in all, a solid experience and place, just hard to take it to next level of very good, on an overall relative basis.

“Great health club” I got this hotel on Priceline for $265 a night. I was in NYC for work. Hotel guest have access to a nice health club/ gym with a pool. The hotel has a lot of room and the rooms are pretty big for NYC standards. The location is obviously great. I have been to better hotels in NYC, but the Crowne Plaza Times Square is a good solid choice for business travelers as well as families visiting NYC.

“Small rooms with Old TV and uncomfortable bed.” The rooms are very small and in top of that they haven put a plasma or HD TV. The bed move because the legs are not very strong. The rooms are not ugly but it will be nice to put a plasma TV.

“Nice Hotel but over-hyped” As others have said, the lobby is small but the hotel has character. We had a "King Suite" and I was shocked at how small it was. There was not even room for a sitting area. I was a little worried after reading that there was no AC but that was not a problem at all. The bed was comfortable and the room was clean. All in all this is a decent hotel but we definitely did not get the service other reviews are raving about. The front desk always seemed understaffed. When we arrived it took a long time to get bell service and valet and when we left we ended up just having to go get a luggage cart and bring down the luggage ourselves after 2 calls asking for assistance. We called in advance and they asked when we needed our car and bell service but 20 minutes after the requested time we had received neither. The wine reception and breakfast were nice touches but the areas where these are held are tiny. Not really big enough for more than 5 people. Like I said, it's a decent hotel but should not be at #3 given all of the other options in San Francisco.

“small gem...even smaller rooms...overall not too bad” first of all keep in mind this is a very OLD hotel!..it's very quaint, in a GREAT location, but it is based upon the "old" TRADITIONAL hotel style...the beds are very comfy(not too soft - i detest a too soft mattress!) however the bathrooms are VERY small...some have no tubs only a shower unit..if you with children, you might want to ask for a tub. the elevators are slow and heaven forbid you are on the opposite end of the hallway - pulling luggage along the heavy carpeted floor can be a pain! so many restaurants and bars within walking distance..easy access to the trains too. a solid 3 star hotel...if not for the tiny rooms another star could be added.
“standard Marriott - pricy but efficient” Good location, clean, good breakfast, busy lobby, close to central downtown. and expensive.

“Average” Spent 3 nights in late June. My experience with Millennium hotels is that there is always a line-up to check-in since it seems that only one person works at the reception. The worst is to line up just to ask a question. The concierge doesn’t seem to be on her station often. Since this was an old building, the rooms are smaller than the average rooms in more modern buildings so there is a disconnect between square feet and price charged. The bathroom is updated with modern fixtures and a rain showerhead. The mattress and the sheets were excellent but the pillows has absolutely no firmness. I am not sure what are in the pillows but they provided no support to my head and neck. When I lay my head down on them, my head just sank to the bottom. I woke up with neck strains every morning. The air conditioner was noisy so I turned it off every night before going to sleep but there was also a loud humming noise from the mini-fridge that comes on intervals. Don’t expect to have great views because it is a low rise building. The area is near upscale shops but it is not vibrant. There aren’t many eateries nearby so you might have to make a short walk to Rush\State Street if you want better selections. All in all it was a confortable stay.

“Room noise too loud” Book the hotel through Priceline for $122 plus taxes. Not a bad deal, but if I knew it was this hotel I would have book a 3 star and would have saved $40. I book 20 nights a year through Priceline.com and this is at the high end of what someone should pay for this star rating. The hotel has little noise insulation and you can hear every door slam and noise from the room next door. If you require parking I suggest Central parking 213 East 43rd, in from 3PM-3AM and out by 8:59 AM $11 plus Tax. Make sure not to go past 9AM if you do the rate soars to $50.

“Acceptable but needs upgrading” I had an early morning business meeting in the area, so booked the nearest hotel to the meeting site. It was acceptable: room was clean, WiFi good. Breakfast was the standard almost inedible American offerings (when will American hotel chains send their operators to Europe to see what real breakfasts can be?). I can't say I was greatly disappointed; but the hotel could certainly use updating. Also, you will need to use your car to get dinner: the nearest restaurant is not comfortable walking distance.

“Great Hotel - Good Price Value in Chicago” For inner city Chicago this Expedia special price was very good. The rooms are VERY small and cramped with the TV/Bar literally 10" away from the bed. The wired internet service is tremendous though. The hotel is running low prices because it is in a major construction area. Each morning the workers right outside my window started at 6AM and WOW what a racket they make. The manager's nightly reception is easily the worst I have witnessed in Chicago. I asked for a refrigerator and microwave which was added to my room at no cost. The fridge is barely large enough to hold a small bottle of milk at one setting - FREEZE! Try pouring frozen milk on your breakfast cereal in the morning. The hotel is conveniently located though and I may stay here again depending upon the prices of other local hotels. In my opinion, Amalfi will need to keep their prices lower than $150 per night to maintain a steady client base.

“conference 2010” I have stayed here many times,The hotel is friendly,quite in general and central and for the conference good value $79 i would not pay more than this. I have been coming here since 1999 and since its upgrade not much has changed,The rooms are small and T.V.s need upgrading,my air con was broke and nights were cold as they had gone back to sheets and taken away the duvets. The milk and cookies are great but you have to be quick as people you have not seen all day swarm like locusts when they arrive,Breakfast is free and enough to eat some cold meats would be a help and cheese. THE BAR is the same as it has ever been overpriced and not run by the hotel not open on a sunday or after 22-00pm and dont stay Thanksgiving nothings open mind you to be fair a lot of the hotels are like this now in Dallas,I would say this to the Lawrence,Tidy the place up Get the Bar and Resturant under your control and make sure everything works in the rooms

“Below expectations” I stayed at this hotel while traveling on business for a meeting and found it to be not up to the standards I expect from a Holiday Inn. While the front desk staff was good, and the restaurant was very good, the rest of the hotel had issues. The fitness room was a disaster, broken equipment, no towels on two of three days, no phone, and no cups for water. The meeting room carpet was very dirty. Guestroom was ok at best. A real lack of attention to detail going on at this hotel.

“Stunning hotel, unfortunate experience” I am checking out of this hotel today, after arriving on Monday. The hotel is lovely and for the most part, so is the staff. The president of South Korea happened to be staying here on Monday. I was not aware of this at check-in. I went out to dinner with colleagues and when we returned at 9:45 p.m., we were not allowed to enter the hotel for at least 45 minutes while the president was arriving. This was disappointing to our group as we all had traveled from the east coast that morning. 9:45 PDT was 12:45 EDT. We got no apologies or any explanations from the hotel. Throughout the day on Tuesday, elevators were intermittently shut down while the president was moving around the hotel. We were even locked in a meeting room while the president moved through nearby hallways. I understand this is largely out of the hotel's control, but a note under the door explaining the circumstances would have been helpful. The fitness center is standard for a hotel, yet there was a $15 daily charge. Disappointing. A silly gripe, but there were no laundry bags in the room. I don't like to pack my sweaty gym clothes with my clean laundry, but that's my only option today. Not sure why this standard feature wouldn't be included here. I requested a 1pm checkout for today as I'm taking a red eye back to the east coast tonight (want to change into casual clothes after meetings end at noon) and was told this would not be permitted. One hour, after all of my inconveniences? The answer was no. After I again reiterated my inconveniences over the past few days, I was granted an extra hour. I'm soured on this hotel and while the property is beautiful, I won't recommend this hotel, nor will I stay here again.

“You can do better in Union Square” The Hilton is just off Union Square in a pretty seedy area. That part would be OK as it does not feel unsafe. The hotel is huge so you are almost always walking to your elevator bank - and then waiting. The rooms are tiny, even by San Francisco standards. Amenities are so-so. Service is OK, but just that - perhaps typical of a high volume, not high end hotel. One gets a very anonymous feeling of being lost in the crowd from the moment of check-in and all through the stay. The service is not bad; it just lacks any sense of the personal. And that may sum up the whole experience at this hotel - it's not bad - it just lacks any sense of the personal. I'm Hilton Gold and so stay at Hilton's a lot. I also go to San Francisco a lot and try to stay at the Hilton Financial District which I consider to be a much nicer Hilton - better scale - better service - better views - and generally a better price.
