I only stayed here this trip because the Financial District was sold out. I'll not make that mistake again. Just not my style. There are so many choices for hotels in this part of town that you can do much better.

“$100 or less/night, ok. Over $100? No.” Southwest Airlines had a great deal on this property. I paid about $100/night INCLUDING the outrageous $25/night parking fee. If I paid anything more, I would not be happy at all. **Make sure to sign up for the President's Club on the website. Well worth the time. (Complimentary WiFi etc...) The moment you arrive, it is overwhelming. Before I even knew what was happening, they had my bag and whisked it away to check me in. By the time I got out of my car, I was nervous about where my bag went! Fortunately, it went to the front desk. The room was a decent size, but the bathroom was tiny. The bathroom had one of those old school flushing bars that you would find in a kindergarten class of the 70's. The room smelled old. It smelled like mildew. I thought maybe that was just Dallas and the humidity, but I stayed at the Aloft last month and those rooms did not smell this way... Oh, and the pillows smelled REALLY bad. Not sure I have ever had that problem before. WARNING: The following should make you mad. Well, it makes ME made just reliving it. I ordered food delivery from outside the hotel. It was a long travel day and I was EXHAUSTED. When the food arrived, I received a phone call from the concierge. I was told I needed to come down to "pick up my food" from the delivery person who was waiting at the concierge desk. I was told the delivery person was NOT allowed to come to my room to make the delivery. So after hours of travel and exhaustion, I was forced to get dressed, put on my shoes and make the trek through the busy lobby to pick up my food! It gets worse. There was a very large convention of business people going on. I was surprised to see no less than 100 people in business suits, roaming the lobby as I walked through in my raggedy jeans and T Shirt with a bag of food. I am pretty sure most people thought I was a food delivery person. I made my way to the elevator and found A LINE! A LINE OF BUSINESS PEOPLE, IN SUITS, AT THE ELEVATORS! I stood in this line for 15 minutes! Once in the elevator, of course, it stopped at every single floor. When I FINALLY arrived back at my room, starving, the food was, you guessed it, ice cold. The robes in the rooms were pretty bad. VERY thin, rough, and had a broken loophole. Why bother. The bed, sorry to say, was not as comfortable as it should have been. KEURIG! I must say, GREAT JOB on having a KEURIG machine in the room! Love that machine and love the coffee it makes. $7.50 bottles of water setting on both sides of the bed. Yuck. The gym seemed pretty worn for this type of hotel. The cardio machines served the purpose, but the only OTHER machine I tried to use, the arm curl, was broken. Overall, the staff were very polite and courteous. Very willing to help, unless you order food from outside the hotel. This is not a bad hotel for $100 or under, but if you have to pay more, go stay at Aloft.

“Decent basic accommodations....” I stayed here on a 2 day pre Alaska cruise weekend with my partner & 2 sets of parents. We had no real problems, except I thought the one elevator was mighty slow. Took the stairs most of the time. Service was friendly & pretty efficient ( when I needed extra pillows they were promptly delivered to my room). Breakfast was a nice variety of things including eggs, bacon, freshly made waffles, etc. Enough for morning sustenance. I got a great rate on Quikbook.com of $95.00, which was a bargain for that area. We walked to the Space Needle, the monorail, & also walked downtown both days. It is a nice walk & I felt safe no matter where I was in the city.

“soulless convention hotel, but great views” typical Hyatt Regency property; standard room was good size, but with slightly unusual set-up in that the vanity unit/sink is in the main bedroom, behind a divider. The toilet and shower are in a separate, very small bathroom. There are a restaurant, a bar, and a coffee shop, all of which have the charme of those you find at airport concourses. Upsides: if you have business at the McCormick Place, this hotel is the obvious place to be as it is virtually a part of the convention centre. If you do get a North-facing room on the upper floors, the views of the Chicago skyline are fantastic. The staff were super-friendly.

“Good but not worthy of 4 stars” Second stay at the Knickerbocker. Happened to go on one of the busiest weekends of the summer. Tall Ships, Lolapolluza, Art Festival, Cubs and White Sox all going on. The room we stayed in was clean and nice. The only downfall is the fact that we had to sleep in a Murphy bed. No 4 star hotel should have a murphy bed. Beyond that, the staff was very helpfull and made the stay enjoyable.

“For business travel and location” Stay here if it is close to where you need to go for business. It is right next to Harvard and a few minutes away from eating/shopping. The hotel is plain; and old Embassy Suites now a DoubleTree. Service is fine; dining is fair. When I was there; the hotel had a fire in the basement and NO fire alarms went off and I had to go down 12 flights of stairs in darkness as the emergency lights were not on either. Probably multiple code violations with four fire trucks waiting outside. Other than that...a nice place to stay if you don't spend much time there.

“Nice features - but strange blips” Westin Chicago-River North has some nice features: 1) the upper-level rooms have good views; 2) the beds, as at all Westin properties, have the 'heavenly' trade-mark; 3) the in-room coffee-tea service is well-equipped and re-serviced daily; and 4) my room was spacious and well-furnished. Plus: although this Westin hosts conventions, the feel of the place is not 'commercial' and the public areas are furnished tastefully. But strange blips occurred: After mid-night the phone rings with a question about water leaking in the floor below. I checked the bath in my room, saw no problem, and reported this. Then, early the next morn, the phone rings, and it is apparently an accidental ring. Try to get back to sleep . . . and the phone rings again ! This time, the front desk wants to send someone up to service/fix my bath. I inform the time when I will be leaving the room (that is, later in morning). A few minutes pass, and the alarm clock goes off! Apparently, set by a previous guest, and not turned off my housekeeping. The story of the bath resolves when the engineering staff finds some missing caulking around the faucets. The experience at Westin is mixed - and in my stay, rather unsettling.

“Often a two, sometimes a four, thus the three” Blah. We stayed at the Clift a few years ago and really liked it, overlooking some problems (terrible bathrooms). But this time around -- boy oh boy, do things look dated. We were in town for a big conference and were staying four nights. Our first room was a bust. You could smell cigarette smoke in the lobby (on the ninth floor). Our room was tiny. The bathroom was TERRIBLE. You could barely turn around in it. The worst thing? You could hear the person flossing her teeth in the next room. While that is a slight exaggeration, the walls were paper thin and we could hear her phone conversations, her TV, her sighs. Not good and not great for four nights when we needed to be bright and chipper in the morning. Rating so far? One star. We politely complained and the assistant front desk manager was great. He promptly said we could change rooms and generously gave us a suite. Rating for service? Five stars. Good stuff: The king bed was very comfortable; good linens; great pillows; very quiet. YAY! The concierge staff was very helpful and kind. Oscar and Erica (?) were lovely and helped us find some nice restaurants. Front desk staff and door staff were pleasant but distant. They warmed up once you engaged them though. Bad stuff: The bathrooms are terrible. Tiny, depressing, this side of dirty (despite being cleaned -- they just look grungy). Liked the toiletries a lot and the shower pressure was great. Lovely thick towels. Only one robe. Grrrr. No fan so it got pretty foggy in there. The decor is starting to look dated as well -- lilac walls, Ikea-like desk, orange plastic cubes for tables. That's the problem with trendy hotels -- after awhile, their cutting edge decor looks very dull indeed. Other issues: I HATE paying for Wi-Fi, especially in tech cities like SF. Want some ice? Perhaps some wine glasses? Not provided. You have to call room service. Be prepared to wait. And they hover at the door for a tip for something that should've been provided either nearby or in the room in the first place. The bar is nice. But it's expensive and boy, are there a lot of hookers hanging around. Makes for some very interesting people-watching. Liked the security that made sure you were a guest if you wanted to access the hotel rooms. On our last night there was a fire alarm at 2 a.m. Not fun when you have a 4 a.m. wake-up call to catch a plane. Some drunken bozo (not a guest of the hotel) threw his jacket on the gas fire. The alarm went off and at first they told us to stay in our rooms. We opened the door and smelled smoke -- very acrid and strong up on the 10th floor. We evacuated. Can't say the staff was very helpful. Nobody to guide us out and there was confusion near the second floor (which was the right door). Nobody really gave us an all-clear when it was safe to return either. Not very impressive. I think this hotel should really conduct a thorough review of emergency procedures.

“OK, Somewhat Blah” I stayed here in September for one night... took my mother out to dinner for her birthday at the wonderful Coco Pazzo Cafe that is less than a block away from this hotel. When I checked in I was told we were getting a junior suite, but the room was not a suite. The next day when checking out I told this to a manager, and he did give me a little bit back, although he pointed out that on my online reservation it did not say I was getting a suite... it said it was an expanded room. Still, he didn't have to refund any money so it was nice that he did. The room was overpriced for what we got. It was nothing more than a typical hotel room, clean, and decorated in a very bland color scheme. I would not have called it an expanded room, even though there was extra seating in the room. It was not spacious by any means. We paid about $270 plus tax for the one night. There was no view, we were just looking out onto a lower level roof and across at some other rooms in a different wing of the building. Actually it was probably good that we weren't facing the street, because the room was very quiet and that neighborhood has several hospitals and sometimes it is possible to hear ambulances if one is on the wrong side of the building. Overall, I was not that impressed with this place and would not stay there again unless there was a really excellent room rate. There are many far better hotels in the same neighborhood.

“In need of renovation” We regularly stay at Residence inns, so were a little suprised at how outdated our hotel room was. They are clearly in a renovation programme - and it needs it. We had a 2 bedroom suite which was a good size for five people but with only one bathroom it was not ideal. Our suite had everything else we have come to expect of Residence Inn's - it was just old fashioned. It was clean, comfortable and quiet - which are always my most important factors when chosing a hotel. It is in a great location too. Given that the rooms are being updated - I would probably stay here again.

“I should have stayed at the Westin...” If you do decide to stay here, dont get a room in the tower... Its literally across the the street from the main hotel.. but that's not the end of it. Its also a remodeled office building. I usually ask for a king, and I got one this time.. problem was that the king bed took up about 75% of the room. This is supposed to be a business friendly hotel, room, and a preferred starwood room - there were only two outlets for electronics, not counting the bathroom outlets. HVAC is problematic as well. Sounded like a 747 taking off all night long. Getting to the room is a bit of a hike or circuitous walk. Take elevator to concourse level, walk to another set of elevators about 1/2 block away and voila - you're in the tower. Didnt have the opportunity to partake in any of the resturants or bars in the hotel, so cant comment on them. Did not get a wake up call as asked for - good thing cell phone was charged and used that as alarm clock. I was finally told that if I wanted a larger room, I should have taken a double queen in the main hotel. So you future folks - keep that in mind if you have to stay here. And finally - the wifi in the room was so sporadic, i found one spot in the room where i had a consistent 4 bars - unfortunately it was in the bathroom - at least there I had two outlets to plug my devices into. More and more I'm realizing to stay clear of the older Sheraton's.... Sorry, to be so blunt, but the management needs to understand the needs of the modern biz traveller.

“Do stars even matter?” I am unsure of what "star" this place really is. 2.5 star? 3 star? They let us check in at 1pm. We thank them for that. Although, there was a HUGE line to check in or check out at the front desk. That always makes me wonder. Why, at a decent hotel, would there be a line of 25 people just to see the front desk? Understaffed? Guess so. Hotel seemed dated. So did our room. They also offered us an upgrade to a suite for $50! We took it, as we have 2 little boys and the thought of an extra large room was just what we needed. The "upgrade" included the hotels $27 parking fee $12.95 wifi and a complimentary bottle of water in the room! Ok, just kidding about the water. The water was $4.95. OUCH. Come on! Throw in a bottle of water! So really, we were paying around $10.00 for the upgrade. I am glad we only paid $10 extra dollars, because this was not a "suite". Maybe an old Jr. Jr. Suite. Basically a small room with a VERY COMFORTABLE King bed and a living room that held a table and a couch that converts to a lumpy "bed". Yes, the King bed was VERY comfortable... Slept like a baby. When they mentioned "upgrade to a suite" I had visions of a whirlpool tub, robes, nice comfy towels etc... Yeah, well, none of that was there. Bummer. Oh, and you HAVE to see the safe! An old school turn nob with numbers! The bathroom was no larger than a regular, small bathroom and the towels were ridiculously thin. I mean, I have had better towels at a Motel 6. No joke. I liked the shower head. Nice flow of water. But this was no "suite bathroom". It was a bathtub shower! There were no pillows for the couch bed and no extra blankets. Not to mention I had to hunt down a cleaning person to grab extra towels as only 2 bath towels were in the "suite". The light next to the bed was not working. Tried calling the front desk, but the phone rang about 20 times, so I gave up. They really must be understaffed as it took a long time to get a bellman to take my bags to the room and then to bring them down the next day. Oh, and a new pet peeve. WHY do they only have 1 regular coffee packet in the room? My guess, is that this "suite" normally has at least 2 people. So what is the deal with only ONE regular coffee packet! Are my wife and I supposed to split the one? The Aveda products are nice. But unsure on a couple "fee's" upon TV checkout (The TV Checkout did not work) A "TOUR" fee of $0.75 and a CA "TOUR" fee of another $0.14 cents. Sure, who cares right?

“Not the Worst, but wouldn't come back” I stayed at the Westin on N. Michigan Avenue during Memorial Day Weekend. First off, we landed in O’Hare and took the subway to the hotel. After switching trains in downtown Chicago and walking 6 blocks we finally arrived at the hotel. There are only two things going for the Westin on Michigan Ave, it’s location to shopping and the Westin Heavenly Bed. One of which you could get at another Westin or Starwoods property and the other via taxi. Check in was quick and since I am a “preferred Starwoods Member” I was told I was upgraded to a higher floor reserved for “preferred members”. The room did not appear to be “preferred”. It was directly behind the service elevators and I could hear the elevators operating all day and night. Luckily I brought ear plugs to wear while sleeping otherwise I would have gotten no sleep. Additionally, the rooms themselves are not quiet. You could hear anyone and everyone in the hallways (and there were lots of unruly screaming children running down the halls too). The room itself was on the smaller side, a king size bed, two night stands, a bureau with TV on top, desk and soft chair with ottoman. My one complaint about the furniture, which I don’t usually comment on, was that there were not drawers on the nightstands only doors that opened to the space below. Additionally, there were no drawers in the desk either. The only drawers in the room were the 4 small drawers in the bureau under the TV. The other part of the bureau housed the refrigerator with stocked overpriced items. The bathroom was standard for a hotel room and appeared clean although the housekeeping staff never gave us an extra towel or soap or shampoo. Being a preferred member I also got free Wi-fi access, however, the wi-fi here was pathetic. I had faster service on my 3G phone than the wifi, it was a worthless benefit. A big beef I have with hotels is that the beds are not completely made. After sleeping in the bed once I once again found that the sheets did not reach the bottom of the bed and the mattress and the small mattress pad were exposed. I had to pull off all the sheets and covers so that the staff would correct it. Additionally, the Westin usually gives you extra pillows in the room, this Westin did not, however, housekeeping did provide us with a few extra pillows. Westin offers a workout facility in each of their hotels. I’ve been to some really nice hotel facilities and some not-so nice ones, this hotel ranks in the middle. They did provide dumbbells but had no cable machine and 4 plate type machines. There were also a couple of aerobic machines (treadmill/ellipticals) but not many. Our room did not have a view either. We overlooked another building across the way. As I stated in the beginning, the Westin Heavenly bed was the only plus to our visit. Would be stay here again? No, while we like Starwood properties, we would try another first. When you pay more money for a Starwood property, you expect higher service and quality. This property did not deliver.

“Slept through the storm” Stayed here while in town for Seahawks game, also turned out to be the night of the BIG storm. At the airport the next day found out we we're one of the only ones who had power all night and the next day. The wind was crazy, but the room was still quiet enough that we slept right through it. Room was nothing special, nor was the breakfast buffet. Stay at the Embassy Suites nearby instead.

“Could have been cleaner, nice location for convention” This stay was very average for the Hyatt. The checking-in process was amazingly easy (all online); however, there was a line almost to the door during the busy times in the afternoon. Obviously, there are some staffing issues that need to be addressed. The hotel is very busy during my stay; there were at least three other meetings besides my own. Room service was quick and friendly, but I have to agree with the other reviewers who state the food is awful. I ate other food provided by the hotel during my meeting and found it to be equally mediocre. On the plus side, the coffee shop does a wonderful latte, and the staff there was excellent. My room needed a new shower curtain (many rust stains) and the shower vent needed a thorough cleaning (caked with dust). I requested this be done after the first night, but it was never done. We also had to request for tolietries to be replaced which is a huge pet peeve of mine. Why is this so hard for housekeeping staff to do especially when there is a $5 tip sitting next to the empty bottles? The bed was average. I liked the flat screen TV and the desk set up in the room. It was great for our laptop and eating room service. The location is the main appeal of this hotel. I was so happy to be staying close by when I was hobbling along in high heels. It is a short walk to the 16th St mall and all the other fun downtown sights.

“The good; the bad; the ugly” The Good: >OCOTILLO was beautiful and run well...Leo and Kim were outstanding and Hilton should be delighted to have them. We felt the rooms were nice; the Executive Club was well run (obviously Leo/Kim were involved). Book your room in the Ocotillo if possible! >Rob (server) also did a good job at the Ocotillo but his "historic tour" of the Biltmore was outstanding--make sure you do your tour with him! Wow what great history >The bar restaurant was good for lunch---good servers and we enjoyed being in there >Appreciate Shane, in management, trying to resolve some issues we had--never got totally resolved but he tried The Bad: >Cleaning of the rooms were off; never did the 'evening turn down' even when called to do so. Plus we felt that the towels were worn and needed to be replaced. >No protein at breakfast in the Executive room--NONE!! Come on add yogart; cheese; and maybe some hard boiled eggs---all sweets and all carbs---those were good and we ate them but they really need to cater to guests with some good proteins! The Ugly: >First day the hotel let in a dog to the Executive room--said it had papers to do so but no collar to say that; they let the dog run without restraint and the dog ate off the plate of the woman who brought the dog into a public room were people ate; NOT GOOD!!! >The pool area management and the Spa management is and was TERRIBLE!! Never seen something so poorly run and managed. >The therapist were NOT GOOD---spoiled with our therapist back home but this was one of the most expensive and most poorly done therapy's we have ever had. For a resort like Biltmore this is a real issue! Plus total miscommunication in what they were to do and they seemed not to care. Be careful with the spa. >The Spa was so bad that ALL of our services were TERRIBLE--management tried to resolve it but it never worked--to pay that much money for service that was not good is not right. Seemed to be allowed by management to get away with it even tho we were compensated. Poorly run for sure! >We had a horrible time with the man at the main pool in assisting us--he put it all on us to do something that clearly was his responsible to do. Little service or concern for the guest. >The work out gym needs new equipment and new cardio machines--it is dirty inside and the locker rooms were well worn--for a 5 Star there needs to be some monies put into this >The issue is service--there were few guests here the week we were here and the pool and Spa service got worst and worst as we were there. Again little attention given to guests or serving them. To us this starts with the leadership in the Spa/Pool area.

“Good Location but Snobby Staff won't go back” Front Desk Staff (all three we encountered) were super snobby. The location of this hotel was good, but there are so many quality hotels in NYC that the location would not draw me back considering our experience with the staff. The room was fine. I t was clean. We had no view where we were, but I hadn't requested (nor paid extra for) that so I am not surprised. Here is another place where you can't put your own item in the minifridge without the sensors charging you for a bunch of stuff. Shouldn't their be a sign warning guests of this? I noticed a higher credit card charge than what was on the bill (after a week at home). But I wouldn't be surprised if many people don't even realize the difference. (10 - 20 dollar. I also had another odd ball charge that they couldn't explain the origin of. Both were removed without a problem from the accounting personnel I spoke with. All in all this is not the Loews experience I was hoping for.

“Great location. Good staff. Average sleep quality. Minimal privacy!” Pros: Great location Good, friendly staff. Clean rooms. Comfy beds. Very good breakfast. Tech savvy!! The room TV had my name on it with a welcome message just when I stepped in. And every person on the phone knew my name & stay period very well, liked it. Cons: Noisy rooms - I could hear the shower 2-3 rooms out. Just couldn't sleep despite the comfy bed. No privacy - strangely I could hear the discussion that my neighboring room guest was having almost all morning. The sound insulation is very poor. Shuttle - The hotel does have a local area shuttle, only problem, average wait for a 1-2 mile ride, 40-60 mins.

“Not walking distance to anything” The hotel sounds on the website as if it's close to lots of attractions...and in terms of miles it is...but it's not walking distance from anywhere and the traffic is so bad in the area (and dangerous) that even driving 4 miles takes half an hour. Also the local neighborhood is very dodgy and dangerous, I wouldn't walk outside anyway. Booked through their website on a rate reduction due to staying more than a night and didn't get the rate advertised when I was charged - they then charged exorbitant taxes ( about 4 different taxes in all per night - far more than anywhere else in California charged) to justify the cost so it ended up being the rack rate anyway. Room was nice; bathroom and shower were good. Parking at $18 a day plus tax was a rort given there was nothing really in the area to justify that price and it was just outdoor self parking. Buffet breakfast was reasonable but cleanliness and freshness of some of the food/utensils was a bit questionable. Good for an included breakfast. If the hotel was in a better location, I'd probably stay again but not a good area.

“rooms are huge but can be noisy; no door between the sleeping and sitting areas” first off--the good: the rooms are enormous and nicely furnished and the location is very convenient. it's walking distance from many of the downtown restaurants, just down the block from a mall w/a nordstrom's and carson pirie scott, and an easy drive to the zoo. we used the valet parking and it was great--well worth the $22. the $15 that the hotel charges for parking w/no in and out privileges is the same as what you'll pay at the surrounding garages and lots. breakfast was well-stocked and not crowded. and there was free internet in the room. however, it can be quite noisy esp if you get a street side room. we were on the 2nd floor, right on meridian and both fri and sat night the noise of bikers, revving car engines, thumping music, etc. lasted well past midnight. also, one of our main reasons for getting a suite is to be able to stay up after we put the baby to bed. however, there is no door in these suites between the living area and the sleeping area. the 2 are separated by a bathroom/closet area so you could sit quietly on the couch and read w/a dim light w/out too much light filtering back to the bed area, but still--it's essentially one big room (the rooms are laid out in a straight line, living rm/bath/sleep area). otherwise, the decor was quite nice and everything else was in excellent condition.

“Great location, ok hotel” I stayed here for four nights on a business trip; the hotel was selected by my employer. On the plus side, the location is terrific, just a few blocks from the White House. I had no problems with the service. I had to call and request new pillows (all the pillows on the bed were down and I am allergic) which were promptly brought to my room, along with a new blanket. Although I had not asked for a blanket, I had not yet realized that the comforter on the bed was also down, so I appreciated this consideration. The room and bathroom were nicely decorated and very clean. On the downside, the walls in this hotel are paper thin, so be sure to bring some earplugs. When people were talking out in the hallway it sounded as if they were right next to me in the room. I was awakened by the sound of the phone ringing in the next room at 3am. On the morning I left, at around 8am the housekeeping carts started rolling by in the hall and I was thankful I was not still trying to sleep because it was very noisy. Also on the downside, rather than just a fitness room the hotel has a fancy athletic club and spa- which costs $10 a day just to use the facilities. I did not want to pay $10 just to use a spinning bike for a half hour. The breakfast prices at the hotel restaurant are outrageous! Fortunately, there are numerous other places to get breakfast in that area. The hotel seems to have all outward appearances of being quite swanky, but once inside the rooms are nice but nothing too special. If I were selecting and paying for a hotel in DC myself, I would probably look at other options, although the location of this hotel is great.

“Nice Hotel but you can hear the planes” Hi, I agree this is a very nice hotel and I would stay here again but unlike some previous posters you can hear the planes. It is right between 2 run ways. They do seem to stop using it so much after 11:00p or so but I was glad I brought my ear plugs. Parking can get tight if the hotel is full. Aside from the noise which can be expected at an airport hotel this hotel is a solid choice if you need to be near here.

“Nice But Not Quite JW Quality” This hotel was a nice, nice location, trendy, but didn't work for me. The rooms were okay but not great! I've stayed in nicer SpringHill Suites. The staff were impersonal. The pool was underwhelming. The conference space was okay but not great. Disappointed by the valet only parking. The parking staff upstairs and downstairs where the friendliest folks in the hotel. Overall this didn't feel like JW Quality to me. That said, I love marriott resorts, but would not have stayed here unless I was attending a conference at this hotel.

“3 star hotel, 2 staff, 1 star service” I had read a lot of bad reviews about this hotel and was very scared to stay here initially, but it’s not a completely horrible hotel and was actually a nice building with okay rooms. The lobby is very pretty, the rooms are about a 3 star but the staff makes the hotel about a 2 ½ star. Basically the staff/service is what ruins this place. The overall staff/management is unprofessional and clearly untrained. This hotel used to be a bad dive hotel until it was bought by a different hotel company and renovated. It’s a pretty building and has decent rooms now, but the mistake they made was apparently keeping the old employees from the previous dump hotel. At least I certainly hope this isn’t new staff! They have a total “No!” attitude, act ignorant in general and incompetent for no reason. It’s REALLY bad. As for room size, the “medium” and “large” are fine (and normal small) for NYC. We were fine in those. The “small” is ridiculous and a closet and should not be sold to any guest. Our friends stayed there and it’s a rip-off. It is only good for 1 tiny person with no luggage. No joke. Don’t say you weren’t warned. While this hotel definitely wouldn’t be my first choice based on their staff, it wouldn’t be my absolute last either if I got a very cheap “large” room. I would just ignore the staff and pray hard I don’t need anything from them. I would also make sure my room was on a low floor because their elevators totally suck. THE GOOD: Very pretty lobby and restaurants (newly renovated, pics on hotel site are accurate for the way it looks but deceiving on size) Fast check-in (but rude as heck staff) Housekeeping staff slams doors at all morning hours but at least said “hi” if you said “hi” first. “Medium” room type was good size for 1 person or loving couple (lol); “Large” room decent for 2 people Great location for tourists (right next to Time Square, Radio City, etc.) Nice robes/towels/soap but only basic amenites (don't expect shower caps, etc.) Okay room service menu; slightly limited food choices; very limited hours (but it’s NYC, call a restaurant for delivery) Big nice flat screen TV Room was neat and clean with nice radio/phone, etc. Air/heat worked great and was easy to control Good water pressure and heat in shower THE BAD: Definite language barrier with about 70% of the staff so it was hard to get help at times because they didn’t speak English and I didn’t understand their language Front desk staff was very rude, acts like they can’t be bothered to answer a question and likes to pass buck vs. solving even simple issues (gave guests stereotypical New York bad attitude for every little thing) Bellstaff not available to help with luggage at check-in (he was standing there and literally pointed which door to use when he saw us struggling big time with luggage) Hotel is clearly not set up for adequate/basic room service (no tables, no trays, plastic cheap silverware, no food coverings) Room service food was decent but staff was again, incompetent with orders, delivery Internet is $10/day and they ended up overcharging us No bathtub and very tiny bathroom (shower looked old with water stains but clean) Toilet took 15 minutes to stop running loudly No space for personal items in bathroom outside of window ledge One very very tiny closet to hang items up (my coat took up ¼ of it alone) No dressers/cabinets so nowhere to put clothes/unpack (your room will get junked up and crowded very easily) Iron in room was nasty dirty all over and broken in pieces; ironing board built for people under 4’ (ala very short) Small elevators and hotel staff has to share (and the elevators are super slow so prepare to wait or walk up/down flights of steps) Very poor lighting in bathroom made it hard to see No premium/pay movie channels on TV Beds were okay but you will hear EVERY little noise/bang in hallway and outside on street (they should have installed sound proof windows since they’re in tourist area) and they need to train housekeeping to not slam doors/talk loud in hallways in early morning Paper thin walls between guest rooms (get ready to hear your neighbors and their tv/radios) “Queen” beds aren’t true queens so don’t be fooled. They’re queens based on the tiny room. I find this deceptive and they should have told us.

“Good location for sporting events” The Crowne Plaza is located about a block away from Nationwide Arena and right across the street from the convention center, making it a good choice if you are in town for an event at either of those. Otherwise, it is several blocks from the State Capitol and most of the major office towers in downtown Columbus (although it is right across the street from the Nationwide Insurance HQ). There really isn't anything special about this property, but no real problems either. Just an average mid-level hotel on the edge of downtown.

“Decent accommodations.” Stayed here for 4 nights over Memorial Day weekend. -Parking is valet only at $25 per weekday and $14 per weekend day -This hotel is located on Dallas street which runs directly into the convention center. -Try Guadalajara Mexican Cantina restaurant down the street (Dallas) for great food and drinks. -Wifi is complimentary for Hilton Honors members ($10.95 per day if not). We stayed on the 17th floor and had a very weak signal. -Room service at the hotel was prompt and plentiful. No fridge or safe in the room. -Beds were comfortable and clean. Elevators were quick and efficient. -Guests may use the pool at the nearby Hilton hotel (no onsite pool) -This hotel does offer a complimentary "on-call" shuttle (Mercedes GL450 SUV) to drive you around downtown. Enjoy!

“Thank goodness for the great restaurant.” Francesca's is fabulous, we love it. The food was great, Texan with a twist, and service there was fantastic. The rest of the hotel, not so good. The service certainly does not match the cost. We had to ask repeatedly for an extra robe to go to the whirlpool ( which closes at dusk - why? Surely 6pm is not too late to go for a per-dinner soak?) . Turn down in the room consisted of dumping a plastic bag with two chocolates in it on the bed and nothing more! If this was a $49.95 per night motel we'd understand but it is supposed to be a classy up-market resort. Go for dinner but stay elsewhere.

“Not bad” Thanks to US AIR, I spent a quick night at Springhill Suites. All things considered, it was a nice enough stay. There was a party going on at the other end of the hall, but once I closed my door, I couldn't hear them. There was an issue with the bathroom light. Other than that, the room was fine. Basic suite. Airplane noise wasn't a factor, as I was tired, it was late and my flight out was at 6AM. Might stay here again.

“Nice but pricey!” Pros: Lovely in many ways. Lots of hospitality and high end toiletries. They provided me w/a free NY Times when I asked about one. Excellent breakfast buffet...experience it once but see my suggestion below. Cons: Everything from the coffee in the gift shop to the restaurant to the business center were too costly. A better bet for a quick & affordable breakfast is the Starbucks in the Marriott across the street or the Denny's a block away. The business center needs to be more efficient, especially for the costs. Servers in the restaurant put the napkin in your lap...too personal.

“eh” this hotel advertises as completely renovated but is actually still under construction. the rooms are nice enough but aren't super awesome. kind of snooty area and not a lot going on at night. probably better for older people not really my scene but not all together a terrible place.

“Decent, would have been upset if I paid full price” Booked three nights via Priceline. Check in was quick and front desk staff very friendly. Room size was a bit on the smaller side, with a view of a wall in the courtyard. Room was 2 double beds, with a small desk, and seemed to be fairly recently renovated. Windows did open about a foot however, and it was nice to get some fresh air in the room. The shower in the bathroom was VERY light the first 2 days, but all of a sudden was full power the last day, which was odd. I just figured that it was a "green" showerhead and didn't complain. The worst part was both mornings, (Sunday and Monday) there was loud banging starting at around 7 or 8 am. Enough to wake me up and keep me from getting back to sleep. There was a sign outside of the hotel that said they were doing construction, but it didn't click until I called the front desk at 7:30 AM on Monday to complain and the noise stopped within 2 minutes. On a side note, my friend did a priceline bid for the same price and same star level (3) and received the Holiday Inn across the street. His room wasn't nearly as nice as the Hilton. It was in need of renovation and sort of dingy. I was satisfied overall with my stay here.

“A Place To Sleep” If you're looking for a top notch five star hotel, then look elsewhere. The St. Giles is a more than decent place to rest your head for the night. The elevators can be a tad slow at times, so we opted for the stairs. The rooms are quite large as noted by other reviewers. The furnishings are not brand new and even have a couple of rips here and there. The linens are clean and crisp. The shower curtain could be replaced with a more durable material that keeps the water in. There is construction in the area, but the air conditioner can help with that. The temperature in the room seemed to always get hotter, hence using the AC in November. If you are a light sleeper, i would suggest requesting a room away from the street. The best thing the hotel has going for them is the location, it truly can't be beat! Tons of bars, restaurants, coffee shops, pharmacies... etc. within walking distance. I wouldn't hesitate resting my head here again. Reasonable rates also made this hotel a decent choice. Enjoy your stay!

“Nice Staff and Bed but Needs Remodeling” The TVs are older non-flat screen variety. Carpet in lobby and in rooms smell musty and water damaged. Don't know what happened. My co-worker said his room smelled water damaged as well. The towels are nice and organized. The bed is ultra-soft and comfy. The room was cleaned immaculately each day. The room service is terribly expensive, especially for Memphis. One regular entree with ice water with no dessert or anything else was $42.00. The staff was very friendly and very efficient.

“good staff” Old refurbished building. Large enough rooms and baths. Valet parking ($) only. Handicapped travelers may want to avoid this hotel, as the lobby is on one level, and access to elevators requires using a staircase up or down. Staff was very helpful. Carpets need replacing in public areas. There is an indoor pool, fitness room and business center. There is a breakfast room, where I was told my room rate did not qualify for free/included breakfast. Free wifi (and wired) internet. This is a servicable and decently located hotel near the arena in Columbus. Cab to airport appx $20. There is rather a lack of restaurants nearby, and an absence of grocers or convenience stores. I imagine that on football weekends the city is probably more crowded and vibrant, but it was a ghost town in late May.

“Other options are much better” I stay in DC frequently, and recently my company moved to a location near this hotel, so I gave it a shot. It's perfectly fine, but overpriced. Being an older hotel, the rooms are quite small, and I thought the decoration was quite stodgy. Also, my room was on an interior light well so was fairly dark. If you've stayed in older urban hotels, you know what I'm talking about. Still, the room was comfortable and modern, very clean, with a pleasant bathroom and nice bedding, and plenty of stations on the HDTV. The iron was a piece of crap but I don't think hotel management can monitor every iron and would depend on user complaints to keep up with this - so not their fault. No minibar, which is a minor inconvenience as I'm unwinding for the evening. $14/day for internet access - I detest this rip-off, when a lot of hotels are waking up and providing it for free. On the plus side, I arrived on a red-eye flight and they had a room ready for me at 8:30 AM, which was highly appreciated. For some reason I got a really good corporate rate, but most of the time rates are at least $100/night higher. If you are on a corporate account and it doesn't matter what you spend, this is an acceptable hotel - business travelers generally don't spend much time in their room anyway. But if you are encouraged to get a good rate, this may not be the best choice - in the future I'll stay in one of the many, many other hotels a few blocks away along M Street and in Dupont Circle, and will walk the few extra blocks. If you are a tourist in DC, this hotel has the advantage of being near the white house, but so what? The DC metro is fantastic and their are 3 different metro stations near the white house. Choose something with bigger rooms and better rates, particularly if you are traveling with kids. DC can be expensive, but their are plenty of hotel in the same general area that are cheaper and offer more amenities.

“good location to walk to the game” the hotel is within walking distance of the baseball and football fields. loved the pillows here. the furniture was worn, the a/c unit was in disrepair, the window had a bullet hole in it. the grounds were tree covered, but the property backs up to a cemetery. would not stay again.

“Clean older style motel” Room clean and serviced daily, good location, helpful staff, room is as you see it on the website. Only a 15 minute walk to walk of fame etc, some good cheap restaurants nearby. Complimentary continental breakfast included in rate. Laundromat right next door which was clean and cheap.Overall reasonable value. Would stay there again.

“Great Lobby, rooms could use a remodel, lots of room for improvement” We recently stayed at the Marriott downtown Detroit. My husband travels frequently and has Marriott reward points, so we are able to stay here for free, we were also upgraded to a one bedroom king suite with 1.5 bathrooms. We stayed in a suite on the 62nd floor. While the views out the windows were fantastic (Detroit River, Windsor, Canada, etc.) the room itself was substandard. I felt like for this location and the potential that this hotel has, the room was a total let down. The couch was circa 1978 floral Victorian or something similar, the rest of the furniture looked like it belonged in a Motel, not the Marriott at the Ren Cen. The bathrooms were fine, nothing to rave about, but had clearly been updated somewhat recently, no pizzazz however. The room really was sad, it was huge and had french doors and really could have been spectacular, but wasn't. I understand that Detroit isn't exactly a "hot spot" these days, but I have stayed at the casino hotels, and they are fantastic (and cheap, and have a better location) If Marriott wants to compete, they need to up the status of their rooms. The hotel staff were great, the lobby was spectacular and I would love to spend some time there, it has computers in the lobby bar which is really a great concept. The hotel was clean for the most part, our room was very dusty and I literally had dust on my phone when I woke up in the am, which is kind of disconcerting and when I went to use the lotion they provided, it was half used already, gross. We used the fitness center, which was REALLY SURPRISINGLY HUGE AND NICE, but there's no pool or hot tub, again, LET DOWN. We went to Coach Insignia which was a really great restaurant, located in the Ren Cen on the 72nd floor. Scary glass elevator ride up but totally worth the views. Its a shame this hotel isn't nicer, next time I go downtown for something, I will stay at the Westin Book Cadillac across the street, where I know the rooms will be much better, plus they have a pool and hot tub. Every time I stay at a Marriott, I am not wowed, COME ON MARRIOTT, its time to remodel your hotel rooms!!!

“Great location, but lacking in other areas” You can't beat this hotel's location. Very central to the top attractions/restaurants/things to do in Boston. However, it is a VERY large hotel, so if you're not lucky, you may end up needing a lot of time to check in. Also, their room service is not the greatest. It took forever for them to deliver fresh towels to our room (~50 minutes from the first call). I stayed at the Towers level, and it was great to have breakfast and the space, but the staff in the lounge isn't the friendliest. The hotel/rooms are also a bit outdated, though, if you look at the pictures before you book (on TripAdvisor), then you shouldn't be in for any surprises. I'm undecided on whether or not I'd stay here again. It is SUPER convenient in terms of location, and if I was able to book a room at a good price, then maybe. Otherwise, I'd think about some of the other hotels in the vicinity that are on par or nicer.

“Undifferentiated Washington Hotel Experience” Pluses: Check in was quick, bed was comfortable, room was functional, close to DC Metro Station (L'Enfant Plaza) Minuses: -This is a tourist hotel not a business hotel. I was in DC on business and there were plenty of kids running up and down the halls (which understandable because there isn't much to do in this section of town at night, but annoying if you want a business hotel experience). -Restaurant and Bar: Just OK. The Bar has a limited menu, the restaurant was something I wouldn't consider because it seemed to trumpet it's buffet. This section of town (as many have reported) is not the place to stay if you are looking to go out at night and be able to walk to a restaurant. To get to a decent place to eat, you need to take a taxi or get on the Metro. -The DC Metro isn't what it used to be...I mention this even though this is a hotel review because if you have any difficulty climbing escalators, you really need to stay in a different part of town. (Climbing escalators? Yes, because of the lack of repair and work on the metro, the escalators and elevators are often "out of service", so be prepared for that additional inconvenience). Bottom line: If your main interest is seeing all of the tourist sites, stay here and you will wind up STAYING here. Otherwise, go to a more active part of town where there is nightlife and metro to this area for the museums, mall, Capital Building, etc.

“OK Hotel.” We stayed at the Sheraton on our vacation. The location was "safer" than normal (any where you stay in Philadelphia will have it's "dark" streets and homeless people. The hotel is near the Franklin Institue and Phil. Museum of Art. There is a subway (red link) a and a Philly Phlash stop (cheap public transport that shuttles to all major attractions - HIGHLY recomment), a half a mile away. We stayed in the deluxe standard room. It was average. Parking is expensive, so research parking garages close by for cheaper rates (we saw some for $10/day). All in all, the accomodations were OK, however I will note that I expected more because this is a Sheraton hotel.

“Fine budget choice for Times Square” I try to avoid Times Square when in NY, and Novotel would not be my first choice in New York, but business-related appointments forced me to this location and a budget-friendly hotel choice. While the decor is a bit tired and perhaps a level below typical business class standards, it's a fine choice. My room was quiet and thankfully looked a little more updated that the hallways and common areas. There is a mini-bar and safe, although the safe is in an awkward location. The towels and bedding are fine. Shampoo and soap in the bathroom but no lotion. Great views down Broadway to Times Square from rooms 02 and 03. I'd avoid rooms 08 as they are by the ice machine. I recommend nearby Vice Versa restaurant on 51st between 8th and 9th and Thalia at 8th and 50th.

“Right over 42nd Street, not 'over' -- but very close to -- Times Square” Our room "faced" Times Square and while you can look down and see some lights of 42nd street below you, the real action (and craziness of Times Square) is happening on Broadway. So, marketing aside, you're actually a half block away from Times Square. The crush of people in front of the easy-to-miss 42nd Street entrance can be really overwhelming at times. It's not any criticism of the hotel, but with the sheer amount of people and activity going on around Times Square (especially in the evenings), I don't think it would be a safe, memorable or pleasant place to bring kids. On the plus side, a subway entrance is only a half block away too. Once you're in the hotel, your entrance is not discrete (in other words, you won't be able to sneak in or out :-) as you exit the two ground-to-lobby elevators and walk in front of the front desk to get to the elevator bank that takes people up to the guest rooms. The lobby is nicely sized, with the breakfast / lunch seating area taking up about half the space and a bar / seating area taking up the other half. The length of the lobby has large windows looking out over the view of 42nd street buildings. I noticed the tasteful artwork placed around the building (bronze sculptures outside the front door area, distinct paintings above the breakfast area, modern prints in our room). The guest room we were in (on the 28th floor) was generously sized for New York. The cabinet hiding the TV also had drawers to hold clothes / whatever, and underneath the TV is the minibar fridge (the type that appears to charge when you touch any of the items; no room for your own stuff) which also has a built-in safe underneath the fridge. The minibar / safe combination is a little bit confusing... hit one set of buttons and you can punch in a 6 digit security code for the safe, another button allows you to type in a four digit code. In the closet you'll find an iron, an ironing board, and a hair dryer. The window in the room opens just a bit (enough to get a hand through), but no wider. For summer, I thought our guest room floor was pretty chilly in general but the heating/air conditioning unit in our room is easily controlled and has a mildly loud fan (so the white noise helped me sleep; all that seeped in from outside was a couple faint ambulance sirens periodically). The bathroom came with three big fluffy towels and three hand towels, as well as three washcloths. The shampoo, conditioner and skin creme were all of the Crabtree & Evelyn's "La Source" brand. There was a sewing kit, shower cap and shoe polish cloth on the tray in the bathroom as well. The coffee pot sits right next to the toilet, which lots of hotels like to do, but in the narrow space between the toilet and sink I thought the coffee pot placement was a wee bit foul. Breakfast buffet is pretty standard, served in a small "nook" off to the side of the lobby floor's restaurant. When you walk in it'll be oatmeal on the left side, along with breads, bagels and pastries. The hot dishes are straight ahead of you (eggs, scrambled "tex mex", bacon, sausage, etc.). Cereal is in the right corner. Cold plate stuff on the right side. They did switch the selection a tiny bit from day to day, but I've seen much bigger breakfast buffets at other Hiltons (e.g. in Köln / Cologne). Sunday morning the servers acted overwhelmed (even though everyone was just doing the buffet option), there was a lineup of people waiting to get seated and too many tables waiting to be cleared. We stood in line for between 10 - 15 minutes. Internet is wireless or wired (ethernet) in the guest rooms and cost is $10 for 24 hours of access. The "bill to room" and "pay online with credit card" options weren't working during my stay (turns out the internet provider billed me multiple times for my attempts to log in, and their 1-800 technical support number is out of service... booooo!), so the front desk provided me with a username & password ("hilton0706" for both fields, in case it helps anyone :-) to get logged in free with no hassle. Front desk staff is excellent and very accommodating.

“OK choice near the airport” We've stayed in Embassy Suites in a number of different cities, and this one is just OK. Website says the hotel has been recently redone, although the interior was not as nice as in other Embassy Suites we've seen. Rooms were quiet and comfortable, but plumbing and bathroom fixtures were cranky. Front desk personnel were friendly but not very knowledgeable about the vicinity of the hotel and provided inaccurate directions to a nearby attraction. As other reviewers have stated, the pool is small and can get crowded. The eating area for the complimentary breakfast also was smallish, having to share space with the regular restaurant/bar.

“Great bargain & great location!!” Went here with my best friend for my first trip to SF and found this hotel right in the heart of Union Square. Super great bargain for a fantastic location. Was disappointed when I checked in to find out that they oversold my room, however, they upgraded me to a 1 bedroom suite but that didn't exactly work for 2 girls, we ended up sleeping on a roll away and the couch. Room was right on Powell Street and had a decent view. Hallways smelled musty and the elevator was SLOW!!!! The continental breakfast was pathetic - burnt muffins, flavorless cereal and crappy bread for toast. Would have expected a LOT more from this place. Also, was out until late at night and had to wait outside of the hotel for about 20 minutes for somebody to finally let us in after buzzing forever...... Overall, a great deal and an awesome location. We weren't in our room that much so it didn't really matter but still some good stuff to know.....

“Fine choice next to airport” I stayed one night here. The rate was okay--$158 plus tax--but not great. The location is excellent--across the street from the airport. I was able to check in early, at about 1pm, so that was nice. The employees were uniformly pleasant and friendly, and check-in was very quick. The room was large and clean. There's a good sized work area with free internet (and several computers in the lobby, if you don't bring your own). The decor is worn and dated, especially the carpet. But the bed--a sleep number bed--is extremely nice. Nice shower head, too. There wasn't much airplane or hotel noise, although someone was being loud with their car in the parking lot for a short while. The room heating/cooling system was noise, too. It kept making loud clanking sounds. I had dinner at the restaurant, which was okay. Breakfast, too. They have a breakfast buffet which is completely blah and not worth the money. Canned fruit, packaged pastries, crusty oatmeal, etc. Skip it. Check out was extremely fast. Overall, a perfectly acceptable experience, if slightly overpriced. Would be better if they updated the room furnishings.

“Great location but the room was sort of dreary” The location of this hotel is really great. Right in downtown Chicago close to fun places to eat and drink and an easy location for the usual tourist things. The room was big, clean and modern, but really had a spartan air about it for some reason and it seemed a bit dreary to me. The room window faced the lake, but the sun shades had been set so that they would only open about half-way (even with the curtains wide open) so the beautiful view was quite obstructed.

“Great location, room needs fixing” I was looking for a clean safe place for a couple of nights. red roof fit the bill. The building is aging, the room is in need of fixing but it was priced just right. Would stay again.

“Ok for the Price... Great Staff” This isn't a bad place if you want to save a few bucks and don't need a lot of room. The studio rooms are very small, but have a kitchen which is nice. Request an inside room to cut down on the noise from the street... 71st is a busy road. The people at the front desk really aim to please and that's what make this place a pleasant place to come. Good location, just enough off the HWY to make it easy but not too noisy.

“good location - some issues” liked this hotel as it is close to my office, and not so close to the mag mile tourist traffic area. the staff in the hotel is very friendly - when i checked in they were going thru an upgrade on their system, and doing things the manual way took a bit longer than normal, but not too bad. upon entering the hotel there was a man that "appeared vagrant" sleeping on the couch in the lobby - he didnt bother me per se, but he was bothersome looking... the room itself was nice - this is an older hotel and the tv, carpet, etc were actually quite fresh looking so that was a treat. the only other room issue was the bathroom - the tub had some black crust that washed away upon turning the water on so not sure where that came from... the shower did not work very well and there was a lot of water that came from the spout and shower, so you had to take a shower/ankle bath at the same time, not enjoyable. but again, overall with these minor hiccups a moderately priced hotel and pretty decent deal for me.

“Affordable basic accomodations.” My partner and I booked this hotel to see a concert at the Auditorium Theater. We were only staying for one night and we wanted to be downtown near the venue, but did not want to spend a fortune for one night. We chose this hotel because it is less than a block from the theater, and, as it turned out, we could see the theater from our room. This hotel is budget priced for a downtown hotel. It is a bit on the minimalist side with the basic ammenities needed to be comfortable. We had a nice corner room with windows facing two directions. The room was cool and comfortable. The bed was soft for my tastes, but quite acceptable. The bathroom was small but adequate. Several of the ice machines were broken when we stayed and it was a bit difficult to find ice at times. Also there are only a few vending machines with very limited selections, so if you have snacking or beverage needs you will probably have to venture outside the hotel. In short, we werent expecting a luxury hotel. We wanted basic accomodations at a good price for one night. The travelodge was perfect for this. Im not sure that I would stay at this hotel if I were on vacation for a week and planned to spend significant time in the room. However, for basic accomodations for short stay such as a business trip or a quick get away to see the sights in Chicago, this place is ideal.

“Nice option outside the city!” Recently spent one night at the Courtyard Boston-South Boston. Selected location because of the FREE parking and proximity to city. My GPS did not recognize address but if you call the hotel they'll give you a different address--Allstate Street. The hotel is behind a Best Buy and central shopping plaza. There is an Applebees, Panera Bread and Olive Garden at the plaza so you can easily find places to eat or grab a snack. I did use the internet while there and found it to be quick and easy to access. Overall hotel is clean and well maitained. Couch in room was "worn" but for a one night visit that was okay. Excellent option for thrifty travelers seeking a safe, reliable and convenient location while in the Boston area.

“Average hotel” My husband and I stayed at Nikko Hotel from Dec. 23 to 27, 2011. I was looking forward to stay in this hotel after reading the good reviews on tripadvisor. As everyone says here, this hotel is in great location, close to Union Square and Cable car stop. Upon check-in, the hotel tried to sell us upgrade which we did not take. We travel quite often and usually other hotels provide free upgrade so we were surprised that Nikko tried to sell us upgrade. Our room was standard and acceptable size. There was no fridge in our room. There was one time that cleaning lady did not throw garbage and wash glasses. We ate at a restaurant in Nikko hotel. It was a relaxing atomsphere but nothing special. There are plenty of restaurants around the hotel so I would suggest to try other places.

“Very Nice Hotel, But Our Room Felt Tiny” The Royalton is a nice hotel with wonderful service. The rooms are clean, the bedding is awesome, the bathrooms are amazing, and the location is perfect. We would have given the hotel a higher rating but for the fact that our room was unusually small, even by NYC standards. We checked in late and the hotel seemed rather full, so we suspect we were assigned one of the least favorable rooms, which is understandable. But we had a hard time not tripping over each other as we moved about the room. Based on other reviews, we suspect that most rooms are larger than the one we had, so we wouldn't discourage others from giving the Royalton a try.

“Great location, but guest room is like a 3 star hotel...” I stayed at this hotel for one night last November on vacation and one night in June for a trade show at convention center. I really like the location; it’s very close to China Town where I love exploring food and only a block away from convention center. However the room I stayed at this time was terrible. The bath room is very outdated with a very cheap sink like you may only find at a motel. To my disappointment, the bed was not only uncomfortable, but a bit unsafe in my opinion with the sharp corners of the steel bed frame sticking out (bed frame is oversized for mattress). When passing the narrow area between the bed and work desk, I bumped into the steel corner of the bed frame and bruised myself. I reported the incident to the hotel management for them to rid this safety concern. Anyhow I guess I will try to avoid this hotel next time even the location is such a plus. By the way, D.C. hotels in summer time can be very expensive. If you're planning a vacation there, I'd suggest avoiding summer.

“Nothing great - parking is a ripoff!” There is nothing warm about this Hyatt - the inside area like the front of the elevators, coridors, etc are dark giving a dingy feeling and with dark carpets, it adds to the dismal look. Beds are fine with the rooms being smallish, nothing to look at out of the window - you will see the windows of the across the street buildings. They have valet parking at $45 plus tax and the internet is $10. When is Hyatt going to realise that wifi is here to stay and is getting cheaper everywhere - most of the hotels today offer it free and with the high room rates paid here why cant they include free wifi? There are lots of other fine hotels nearby on this street and they offer cheaper parking.

“Dated, bland, but comfortable stay” Interested in this property mainly for being dog friendly. Confirmed this over the phone but phone agent neglected to mention size restrictions (40 lbs) and that the dog must be with you at all times (you can't leave it in the room by itself). These details were listed on their website but we went off the agent's description and booked prior to reviewing the policy on the website. There was easy 5 min. parking in the front of the hotel near valet. Check in was easy - agent mentioned "is dog less than 60lbs?" (conflict of policy again) - and we received a $15/night parking pass. Note on parking: we continued to have to get tickets every time to enter the parking lot. The attendant sees your parking pass and lets you leave without fee each time. Seems like a waste of tickets to me. The attendant was also only there about 50% of the time (arm left open when he was gone). Hotel was very dog friendly in terms of space for them to walk around outside and there were dogs everywhere at the property. Requested room during reservation that faced lake; rec'd freeway view. No problem there. Room itself felt very drab and dated - lacked color. There were contemporary furnishings but textiles really blew the design and were just sad feeling. The bed was slightly "crunchy" - the coils crunched every time we sat on the edge. Otherwise, comfortable to sleep in. Bathroom was nice: the tub looks like it had recently been retiled (grout was very clean) but tile floor seemed very old - dirty grout, slight black mold, wallpaper peeling at tile. The location itself was convenient for driving around downtown but in 95+ degree weather walking 1.5 miles to campus was out of the question. For the same price I'd prefer hotels a little closer to the lake or 6th St.

“Unremarkable & Odd” I travel quite a bit and have stayed in a lot of hotels over the years (mostly for business). I took a chance on Aloft because of the great reputation of the "W" hotel brand. While not a bad hotel, it was an odd stay. It's clean and the staff was great. But the hotel itself was very strange. It was impossible to find and parking was horrible. Don't expect to get in and out quick. The rooms are starkly decorated. If felt like a jail cell. There was almost an inch of room under the door, so the noise in the hallways was crazy loud. There's no closet in the room, just a small curtained-off area. The shower has one wall that is frosted glass which faces the rest of your room. What? I understand that Aloft is not a traditional-type of hotel. It's "chic." But they missed the mark. It feels more like a cheap imitation of IKEA. It's also quite worn already. Lastly, there's no free breakfast - just a little store where you have to buy your breakfast items a la carte. I'd never stay here again. Very noisy, dark, and just plain odd. I suppose the only good thing about it is that it's located in the center of downtown. So everything is walking-distance. And again, no complaints about the staff or cleanliness. Oh the bed was comfortable.

“Nice hotel for convention attendees” I was attending the convention at the next door and this hotel was extremely convenient to the exhibition hall. The room was nice and clean but the view from my room was terrible... Also I found it a bit annoying that in the morning I checked out the cleaning crew kept knocking my door asking what time I was leaving the room. I recommend this hotel if you are attending the convention.

“Clean and convenient” I stayed here overnight because of a business meeting nearby. I was a little nervous when checking in because the location didn't look so safe. I was surprised by my room. It was spacious, clean and cool. I walked to a restaurant to have dinner and felt safe. The breakfast buffet in the morning which is included in the price of the room was delicious. The scrambled eggs, sausage and coffee were great. I would stay here again.

“Decent for the price” Was attending a concert at Staples Center and my go-to hotel had gone 'upscale' and to pricey for my needs of simply needing a 'bed to sleep in'. This was an old hotel which has been remodeled into a boutique hotel. Very small street-front, you would miss it if not looking for it. A small hotel with an adjacent independant parking structure ($11.00/day or $20.00/day for in and out priviledges). Very easy check-in and check-out. I had their cheapest room ($98 + change) which was smaller than my apartment, but all I needed to simply spend the night. Very comfortable bed, in-room mini-fridge (which I was told was being switched out so I brought a cooler anyways), coffee maker which I had to move to the floor to make the cord reach an outlet. Bizarre shower fixture which sprayed water into the bathroom since there is only a half-panel glass for the shower. The water sprayes into the toilet area which is only closed off by a semi-luminescent (?sp?) sliding door. Hardly any shelf space near the sink for personal items. No 'guide book' for hotel features, ammenities, restaurant/bar menu, etc... Clock radio had no directions as to how to set the correct time (it was incorrect and I had to call the front desk) or how to 'program' the AC/Heat unit. The hotel does have a bar and restaurant but they included none of this information in the room. They did advise me of the complimentary breakfast buffet which was nothing but juice, coffee, bagels, and dry pastry. I had to leave the lights on 24/7, even during the day as the 'window' was nothing but a 'trough' looking at the walls and air-conditioning pipes. I heard the people above me constantly, not partying or being wild, but just what appeared to be walking around, as well as people on either sides of the room. All in all, even though I was only there to rest before a concert at Staples, and get a nights sleep before driving home, it was an irritating time. I never used their bar/restaurant, there is a Subway, iHOP, and Ralph's just a block away. When I was told there may mot be a mini-fridge I brought my cooler, with ice, as there are no ice machines available.

“Fabulous beds, pricey location.” Houston's Galleria is known for great shopping and Westin is known for heavenly beds and dual-head showers, but if you're headed to stay at the Westin Galleria, don't expect to find any bargains (except in the mall parking garage, where hotel guests can self-park for free.) The hotel room was spacious and well-appointed, but smelled musty and mildewed. The legendary beds were wonderful as ever, but the floor to ceiling windows were covered by custom blinds that had seen better days and the wall above the fire alarm was badly stained. The room did have a mini-fridge but it was inoperable. This hotel has wonderful conference facilities, but hotel hallways were kept at near-arctic temperatures, which oddly did nothing to chase the stagnant air. The workout room was closed for remodeling, and the hotel has no onsite restaurant, referring guests instead to the Daily Grill next-door, where breakfast entrees with eggs start at $12.95 and dinner entrees run twice that. To get a late night drink, we were directed to the lobby bar at the Westin Oaks property (also at the Galleria) where a single vodka shot cost a whopping $9. (Helpful hint: pack a flask and skip the lobby bar!) The Westin Galleria is in a prime location, but one may find better-scented, full-service luxury accommodations nearby for less.

“Not so Grand a Hyatt” Certainly up to Hyatt standards, but I'm unable to see much to merit the "Grand" designation. For a 9 PM check-in, there were two desk clerks trying to serve 15 guests; average wait time was 10 minutes per guest. No managers seen at any time. Clerks attempted to pacify guests with extra coffee coupons, but as a previous reviewer has noted, a more "grand" attempt at service would be to do what most 3-star properties do and supply a coffee maker in the room. My clerk tried to pacify me with a "secret" (undisclosed) upgrade to a suite; when I arrived at the door, my keys wouldn't work, so it was back to the lobby for another 15 minute wait, as the lines had not improved. Finally, upon entry to the suite, I was fine with room size and decor in general. It's green, green and green, with a bit of rich wood and way too much black marble in the bathroom. Sticking out like a sore thumb is the armoire/TV cabinet in the suite's bedroom, which is painted wood, apparently either from Ikea overstock or built from 3/4 inch plywood by the property's engineers. Couldn't check out the minibar automation noted in earlier reviews, because my suite lacked a minibar completely. Significant plaster dust still coated the edges of power outlets - the rooms hadn't been punched and cleaned well for the original opening. TVs are LCD flat panels, but too small for their distance form the bed and living area sofa; and no HDTV or digital channels are provided. Spending $200 per room less on the Samsungs and investing that in other areas would have been more prudent long-term. Beds are firm and comfortable; toiletry amenities are a skimpy 1.5 oz each (most 4-star properties are in the 2 oz. range). The fitness center has interesting flat screens on each cardio machine - except that they control only your fitness program; you can't actually watch TV from any of them. A single wall TV provides distraction for the entire center. The rooftop pool is simple but you would indeed get great views of takeoffs and landings if that suits your fancy. At $199 a night, I believe there are many more interesting choices for an overnight in Dallas; choose the "Grand" Hyatt only if the convenience of remaining on the airport property overrides any other consideration.

“Gorgeous hotel, with one complaint” This hotel is absolutely beautiful, with inspiring decor, very modern, and elegant. My only complaint was that our room was right off of the courtyard. At first I was very excited about this, since we had beautiful french doors that opened to the courtyard (at night there was a beautiful roaring fire). But people stay out there, hanging out, ALL NIGHT LONG. We were woken up numerous times throughout the night by laughing and chatting. Although the people were removed after I made a phonecall to the front desk, the staff's response at checkout was somewhat snobbish. By all means, stay in this hotel, but ask for a room very far away from the courtyard.

“Not all that....” As a former SF resident, I always assumed Campton Place was one of our little gems. The bar is great and you can't beat the location if you need quick hits and shopping, etc. Sadly, I'm not impressed. Front desk reception seemed undertrained, clueless, and insincere. The first room I was shown after advising of the importance of quiet for my steady stream of business calls was directly on Stockton with bus and constant whistle and traffic noise. I was told there was only one other room available in the hotel and I did end up moving, but to a floor with rowdy, partying folks next door - not Campton's fault, perhaps, but not the guest profile I was expecting. My internet didn't initally work, requiring a call and my remote control was broken - another call. They couldn't even get me a San Francisco Chronicle for the day - despite paper boxes less than a block away having them (I know b/c I went walking the streets in search of.) and my explained need for one as soon as practicable for business reasons. The room is fine but thin walls and I still hear a lot of noise outside and I'm not that sensitive to street noise. I wouldn't return. One thing I am happy with - the Indian food I ordered for room service. I've had good stuff throughout India and elsewhere and the curry was lovely. Wish I could love this hotel more but I can't.

“OK, but lacks a few things you would expect” The Doral Tesoro has a somewhat secluded location, near Texas Motor Speedway north of Fort Worth. If you are using it as a base to explore the attractions of Fort Worth, be prepared to drive. The hotel itself is rather bland on the outside, and the interior is finished in a combination of art deco and Texana. A bit of an odd combo. Staff is friendly, but not always knowledgable. A few things that are missing: 1. Valet parking (they have it sporadically, but there are long stretches where the bell stand is not staffed). 2. Gift/Sundry shop. There is a small "closet" beside the bell desk with a few items, but selection is very limited. 3. Minibars and vending machines 4. There is no spa, is a smallish workout room. Rooms are comfy and fairly large. Ate dinner at the restaurant, faire is primarily fish and steak, with a few other selections thrown in. Again, the selections seem to lack a common theme. But the food I had was tasty and service was OK. All in all, this is one of those hotels I would not go out of my way to return to, but if I needed to go there on business or otherwise, would not be upset about it.

“Okay hotel” Stayed here for a night with my wife, for Valentines day. Room was very small and was nice but nothing exceptional. Partly chose this hotel because of a Valentines package which included champagne -- when we arrived, the champagne was not there and I had to ask the front desk for it. Not appreciated. Location is very good (didn't matter so much for us, but could be useful for someone visiting the city for business or sightseeing)

“High Ranking Is Not Justified” Referring to Tripadvisor reviews, I booked 4 nights in December 2009, 16-20. On our arrival, the room we reserved was not ready, and they placed us in a room that was below what we had reserved without telling us, but assured us that the room would be changed to a very nice room for the last 3 nights of the stay. The room we changed to was much nicer, and appeared to be what we had reserved in the first place. Believing that we were overcharged for the first night of the stay, we pursued rectifying the matter with the front desk, but instead the front desk insisted that both rooms were of the same class, but it was very clear to us that they were not. Given the opportunity, they decided to not rectify the situation, which negatively effected my perception of the stay. Pros: Good water pressure and great hot water, very comfortable bed, very clean bathroom, very quiet room, good HVAC, good room service for dinner Negs: Dishonest front desk, dated tacky decor (from the early 90s?), dirty appearance of rug in both rooms Will return to the London NYC next year, methinks.

“Average hotel” Hotel was average; it is an older Holiday Inn Express but it was clean. The staff was very helpful and friendly. The hotel is very convenient if you are going to Methodist Hospital ; it is located a block from the Methodist Hospital. There isn't much within walking distance, but restaurants are close by.
