“GREAT HOTEL - CONVENIENT - SERVICE - BREAKFAST!” I stayed at the Elan as a last minute Saturday night in LA (we came a day earlier than we had planned for a week trip). All the other hotels in the area were at least $100 more! We actually booked that morning - they had a couple rooms left. This is a great area - convenient to West Hollywood, La Cienega, and Beverly Center. We arrived at 8pm, and immediately after check in took a cheap cab to the Sunset Strip as it was my first trip to LA. On a nice night you could actually walk to the Strip, but it was cool and getting rainy (plus its an uphill walk). The room was ok. Our 1st floor room had a slider to the side walkway of the hotel - I didnt like being that close to people walking by, but I wasn't at the room very long, and I dont people generally walk out there anyway. As long as you are on a higher floor it wont be an issue. the bathroom was huge and the robes nice. The best part of this place besides location was the breakfast. Wow - I was expecting coffee and a banana when they said continental, but this was great. Selection of coffees, OJ, Lemon Water and some others. Boiled eggs, Bagels (with toaster nearby), jam, oatmeal, yogurt, fruit, pastries and muffins. I think I am leaving out some stuff. Anyway, I was impressed this was included as part of the price of the room. This spread at a diner or coffee shop would have been at least $15pp if they had this selection. Unlimited made it even better! For some this may not be important but I was on a long flight to get here and had lots of things planned so it was nice to get a solid - quick breakfast without having to fork out more money. A few Newspapers were available for free as well! The breakfast area was really nice too - some tables, couch with coffee table and a couple flat screen tv's. Also a few computers were available for use. Overall seemed like a glamourous budget hotel, safe, clean, well situated and staff very motivated to help. No real amenities like a gym or pool but like i said, a great base and good service. We spent the next 3 nights at the Sofitel down the street which was REALLY nice, with pool, gym, spa, and on-site restaurant / nightclub, but you'll pay 20-30% more on any given night. We got a good deal due to it being the week of thanksgiving so it was worth it. If you like to shop, the Beverly Center and Nordstrom's Rack are right there. Melrose Ave is a few blocks north. Robertson St with all the new designers is a 15 min walk, and the Grove about 25 min walk the other way. I'm not big on buses or public transportation, but did take a bus down Melrose Ave one night home from Pink's Hot Dogs (to Melrose at LaCienega) for $1.50 each, because we were sick of paying 10x that for cabs to go just a mile or so down the street. Overall I would stay again, but if I were spending a lot of time at the hotel and got a good deal, I'd upgrade to the Sofitel.

“Fine Stay” This is not truely an airport property but it is the closest Full service Marriot to the airport. I stayed here for only one night. I do like the free parking and the hotel is easy to navigate. Typical smalller Marriott, nothign great but nothing bad either. Rooms are fine. If you don't have one facing I-35, the noise is not a factor but you will be looking at a parking lot of the roof of the building. But you don't stay at this type of property for the view. Food is good, room service is fast too. Not bad expereince, cost was also good.

“Quality is declining a bit, but problems handled well” I have stayed at this hotel countless times for a variety of conferences (my first time in 1999). I always enjoy staying in the "old part"--the Wardman Tower--because I love the charming details of such an older building. However, on this trip, it became really clear to me that that side is desperate for a makeover. (My friends' rooms in the Center town were more recently renovated, but they are a lot darker and smaller than on the Wardman side.) My first room was large, but, during my second day there, it developed a leak from the ceiling directly over the toilet. I discovered this right before going out at 5:30PM, so I called down and told the desk. Well, when I got back at 10PM, it still wasn't fixed. I called to complain, and they moved me to a full-sized suite, with a balcony. That was great, and I really enjoyed the extra space in that room. (Although it was inconvenient to find that the "wet bar" wasn't wet at all--there was no sink! and the fridge had been removed as well--I had had one in my first room.) However, both rooms were frayed (one of them had a lamp with a literally frayed shade), dingy, and definitely in need of some fabric and carpet upgrades. They were clean (I obsessively check for bedbugs everywhere I stay, and I found zero evidence in either room, nor anywhere else I was in the hotel), but old. For the first time, I actually thought to myself--should I not stay in the Wardman tower? That's sad, because I love its big old windows, crazy chandeliers, and old school crown molding. That being said, I was happy that they upgraded me instead of just not fixing my problem, and the service in the hotel was good--room service was decent and arrived quickly, bell service was efficient, and the location of course is excellent for access to the Red Line Metro, walking to Adams Morgan, etc. The internet service is expensive, but it is fast and reliable when you sign up for it. I still like this hotel, but next time, if they haven't renovated the Wardman Tower, I will ask for the Center Tower--which seems such a shame. I can stay in a generic Marriott anywhere--but there's only one Wardman Tower, with its history and charm.

“Disappointing-not up to standard.” My husband and I have stayed at other Springhill Suites and were quite satisfied with our stay. The hotel is dated, which is not a problem, as long as the customer service aspect is maintained. My husband lost a pair of sunglasses, he called the front desk to report the loss. He was told that all lost items were locked up and only housekeeping could access the room. He was pomised a call back which did not happen. He had to call twice AND go back to the hotel for resolution. The walls were very thin. We could hear the people in the next room having a normal conversation. My husband asked to be moved, which he was, to another room. The toilet would not flush. We had to move again. The hotel needs a renovation at most. I normally rate my experiences with the Marriott chain on a high scale, however, this property did not meet my expectations.

“average” Average in every way. It really didn't make any particular impression on me. The room was enormous though. We had 6 huge bags, so it worked in that respect. The location is excellent. . Easy access to Loop and Magnificent Mile., and near several El lines.

“Renovation lacks frills, attention to detail” The property looks stellar from the outside with the white stucco walls and beautiful views of downtown. But if you're looking for the Dallas version of Austin's mod motor court, the Hotel San Jose, you'll be somewhat disappointed. This renovation lacks the same attention to detail that Liz Lambert took with the San Jose's. Instead of polished concrete floors and Bertoia chairs, the rooms sport thin rec room carpet and original cracked bathroom tiles. The effect feels unfinished rather than charming. My room also had a balcony, but instead of outdoor furniture, it featured only industrial black rubber mats. In terms of the basics, this place was clean, the staff were friendly and the value was good. It's also a super spot if you plan to spend time in the Bishop Arts District or downtown but want to do so without having to deal with Dallas pretense or the W party vibe. In short, I would recommend it but with the caveat to manage your expectations.

“Alright rooms not in the best neighborhood..” However, this HGI is fairly priced and isn't too far from the historic district (About 1/2 mile to the Liberty Bell). It is located underneath the convention center and directly across from a large bus station so the location is not prime! If you are looking for clean rooms at a decent price it's really not a bad place to stay.

“Surprised and Disappointed” Usually I find Homewood Suites to be the best value and stay for the price in the Hilton chain. However, my opinion of this brand has been seriously eroded thanks to this property. Stayed for three nights but treated by the front desk as a stranger with each nightly entrance. First night, a huge cockroach crawled out of the tub and startled me in the middle of the night. I understand this can happen anywhere (although its a first for a Hilton hotel and I stay at 60+ per year, including many on the equator) especially in the American southwest, but this 'encounter' created suspicions about cleanliness levels. There was also no evening 'reception' in the lobby while there...perhaps the staff was on 'holiday' along with the pest sprayers. The property is hard to find from the highway and difficult without GPS or a good map...perhaps they are keeping the place a secret until they lose their affiliation.

“Odd” Request a street facing room. The enclosed court facing rooms are completely sunless. The Mall on the first level makes if difficult (apparently) for bellmen to identify guest trying to check in. I had to tote my luggage up to the lobby level. The health club is one of the best in the country.

“Small, tired rooms, but decent staff and a good location” I stayed at Hotel 57 during January's Snowmageddon. On the whole, I found the staff to be equal parts delightful and helpful. The rooms, on the other hard, are a bit banged up and poky. Upon check-in, I was upgraded to a larger room because so many rooms were unoccupied. All I have to say is that if this is what passes for a larger room, then I would hate to see how small the smaller, normal rooms must be. One other quirk: the room I was put in had no in-room safe. When I reported this to one of the receptionists, I was told that there should be one in there. Odd. By the way, there might be some collusion between the doormen and certain cab drivers. One driver, who gets a lot of business from a certain doorman, immediately pressured me to agree to a flat rate $30 fare to LGA. The doorman told me that I should be suspicious of anyone who tries to charge me any more than $30; that $30 should be about right. Given the agreement between the sums quoted by the two gentlemen, I wonder if the doorman isn't getting a cut of that $30 to keep referring fares to the driver in question. Now, I know that it isn't unusual for cabbies to give themselves a bit of an income boost by doing off-meter runs, but this seemed to be a bit too cute by half. I wonder if the fare would have been any less had I told the cabbie to run the meter?

“A Little Tired” This Hotel was billed as a 4 star Hotel on Hotwire. I would guess that that was true about 10 years ago. First the good: It is in a great location particularly if you are doing business in the financial district. It is also close to China Town, the Ferry Building market, the waterfront and plenty of public transportation including the California street cable car. Like any Hyatt, it has a very impressive atrium housing a couple of restaurants and a cocktail lounge. Many of the rooms have balconies and many of those have water views. The problem is that the rooms are just beginning to look tired. The carpets are somewhat worn, the furniture has its share of scratches, no flat-screen HD TV's or DVD players, everything just needs to be updated. While the beds are generally quite comfortable, on my last trip one side of the bed had a distinct sag. Also be forewarned that the rooms on the Market St. side of this Hotel get a lot of street noise if you are on one of the lower floors. Like any business hotel, they are geared toward people on expense accounts so be prepared to pay through the nose for anything extra. Wireless Internet service is $10 per day, parking is about $50 per day and how about a couple of poached eggs for $19 bucks ... you get the picture. All in all it was worth the $110 I payed on Hotwire, but would require some updating to get me to pay anything like their rack rate of over $200.

“Cheap, convenient, (mostly) clean.” Spent two nights here before heading to downtown Memphis. This hotel is conveniently located to the airport and the all-important Graceland. Upon arriving at the airport, you must call the hotel to get the shuttle to come get you. It is free, and the wait is only about 7 or 8 minutes. My king room ($70/night!) was not huge, but would fit two people comfortably for a couple of days. The furniture, bathroom and walls/doors are showing a bit of age, but the place was fairly clean. In room coffee maker, microwave and fridge were handy to have. As with most hotels there weren't enough electrical outlets within reach, but a person can make do by shoving furniture around. My view was of an industrial site next door, but at least it wasn't loud. Noise from hallways was minimal but I was tucked down a small wing so that may be why. There is a free breakfast available from 6 to 9am. Typical cheap hotel fare, though there is a good selection. Going late means getting last scraps. Don't look for any food after 9 am -- it's cleared away completely! There is a small "mini-mart" of snacks available on the first floor, as well as a small "gym" containing a treadmill and one piece of workout equipment. Front desk staff were fairly helpful and polite. Don't be thrown by the fenced parking lot. It's common in Memphis. If you don't have a car with you, make use of the hotel shuttle -- they'll take you to Graceland, the airport, and other major sites in the area. Going further? A cab downtown is about $25 from the hotel. As others have said, you can also get the free pink limo to and from Marlowe's, which is a legendary BBQ joint out past Graceland.

“Nice Hotel, but noisy, noisy, noisy...” This is a decent hotel with friendly and capable employees, but the walls must be paper thin. I could hear everything at night: people in the hall, the next room's tv, and EVERYTHING going on outside. I could hear sirens, horns, and buses like I was on the street, but I was on the twelfth floor! They have Sleep Number beds and they hawk them like crazy everywhere in the hotel, but they actually are very disappointing. Nothing special to them at all. Overall, I would stay there again because it is a nice hotel, but hopefully I'd get a room with a little more noise protection.

“Ok stay...” I stayed at the Hampton Chelsea for two nights for work - I've stayed here before and was a little disappointed the company had picked this hotel over the Hampton Times Square North. My stay was "ok" but nothing to write home about. The room was clean and the staff did their jobs but no one seems to care much more than going through the motions of their job. My co-worker who booked all our rooms spent far more time than she should have in trying to straighten out reservation issues. I wouldn't not stay here but if I can stay at one of the other Hamptons, I will.

“Nice hotel, rooms are efficiently laid out - however, WTC construction is loud” This is a nice hotel. The staff at the front desk is nice (though a bit hurried when I checked in b/c a ton of people -seemed like a convention - was checking in at the same time I was). The rooms are very efficiently laid out (NYC hotel rooms are small in general, but this hotel did a great job with the layout). Very nice touch with the free water bottles and filtered water on each floor! My only problem: WTC construction. My hotel room was overlooking the WTC site and there was construction going on from 6am - midnight. Not just a slight hum in the background, but full on jackhammering until midnight. Started again at 6am on the dot the next morning. I had a big day of meetings the next day and I was not prepared b/c I couldn't get any sleep. It would have been nice for the front desk to hand out ear plugs or something when I checked in. No mention from them whatsoever of the noise.

“Disappointing” We were expecting luxery but were disappointed. First, registration clerk was rude. He chided me for parking on Congress. Note that there is no "Registration" sign and address is on Congress so it was understandable mistake. On it went. We are platinum level customers so I would have expected a somewhat different reception. The room is badly in need of update both in terms of style and wear but whole hotel begged for decoration and touches of luxery. Another negative is everything is extra--from parking to Internet. They did, however, offer cool water and coffee in llobby along with a fruit bowl. Best plus is LOCATION which is fab for restaurants and clubs.

“Unless House of Blues is in your cards - the hotel is a WILDCARD” Although very cool with hip decor - I could envision having a party here, but not a long weekend with my girlfriend. UNLESS, i was in a band playing at the House of Blues then it would be perfect. I can smell the place now just thinking of it - if youve been there, you know the smell - just kind of an odd place - not bad, but certainly not my taste

“Great location. Not so great bed or room. Not horrible but not good.” I guess all of new york is over priced. The location is second to none. Desk was great and friendly. Rooms were small and the bed was really uncomfortable. Was clean and had good ac. Room was older and halls were shoddily remodeled. Ripples in carpet and sloppy paint. Again though great location. Think next time will stay at mariott Marquis next door.

“Location/price in NYC” This hotel is basic, but it is clean and safe. At the price, for NYC, anyway, it's a good option. There is no real lobby, but the reception is nice enough. The room was small, the sheets clean, but the blankets allergenic. The bathroom was ok, at least it was inside the room. NYC is another universe for hotels, this is a reasonable, clean, safe option, but it is quite basic.

“Really no reason to stay at this hotel (unless you really like 2 bathrooms in the same standard room)” This relic of the depression was pretty depressing. Yes, it is very nice that they claim to be the first hotel that invented some crazy gizmo on the room door that allows the cleaners to return your laundry without disturbing you , but that same gizmo is a nice metaphor for this place - currently useless, out of service, and ugly. This is a big airline and convention hotel, so be prepared to wait at reception, for elevators, etc. The staff have been an interesting combination of rude and completely unhelpful (with the exception of a nice IT guy, without whom I would not be submitting this review). The rooms are "restored" to what they may have looked like in 1927, but really they seem more caught in 1996, when the restoration was done. Ancient TVs, clocks, etc. (no modern fixings like flat screens, iPod anythings, etc). Bathrooms are nicely tiled but have many plastic fixings, recalling a motel six (for some odd reason, there were two in my standard room - I'd have preferred one larger one that could not be spanned by my arms in either direction). So, too, is the gym stuck in 1996 - it is a very small gym for such a large hotel, and is crowded with minimal equipment. Other ammenities like wireless internet are not available (and if you paid for internet in your room, you must pay again to use it elsewhere in the hotel). Location is nice, but there are at least 10 hotels in spitting distance and I've have to think that there is another one that offers a better stay for a similar price.

“Don't pay for wifi, ask for free wifi and you'll get it” Booked via hotels.com, nice hotel in a great location, my room was big, big tv, al though when it rains the tv reception stops. Air con worked perfectly, comfy bed, nice working area, big shower. They charge for wifi but just ask at reception for complimentary wifi and they will give you a free password. The maids don't bother to give you shampoo etc when you use your allocation up, you have to chase them in the hallways and ask. I was surprised that the people staying here seemed to be in their 40's and above, I assumed it would be a younger hip crowd? Doormen extremely helpfull, the female reception staff seem a bit 'over the top' I'd stop here again if the rates are ok, I was just expecting somehing more from the hard rock. My floor seemed to be the only one that had worn carpets and doors, no memrobelia in the halls, maybe it's a floor they allocate to the third party travel sites that charge less?

“very nice hotel but i expected more...” When you think of top-of-the-line hotels I usually think of the Ritz and Four Seasons among others. Perhaps I am wrong but this hotel was very nice- on par with the nicest Hilton or Westin for the most part. The rooms were nothing special however and the hall ways felt like I was in the Shining right down to the carpet being from the era. The location of the hotel is well situated and is walking distance to most anywhere in the city. It is perhaps a bit of a haul to Old City but still doable. The best thing about the hotel I believe is the staff who were incredibly friendly from the guy opening the door to the room service deliverers walking the halls. Staff is definitely an A+. The lobby is very nice but nothing spectacular and has kind of a strange layout. The bar seemed pretty busy though I never made it in. There is a very nice gym on the basement level which is found by going through the spa. The rooms however were very average. There is a bathtub shower and the rooms felt barren. Maybe they need more hangings, more furniture, or simply an update. Again they were nice but I thought it would be a bit nicer considering. Overall very good place to stay but I think there are likely at least half a dozen hotels if not more which could give similar quality overall and perhaps without the four seasons rate.

“Clean, comfortable and convenient” The Best Western Mikado was perfect for us. Besides the fact it that was a five minute walk to our son's apartment (and how often do you get that lucky in LA), we found the hotel to be clean and well kept and the front desk staff to be helpful even if a bit reserved. Keeping in mind that we are talking about a mid-range hotel chain and not the Ritz, our room spacious and internet access was free even in the rooms (and I can't say that about the convention hotel we stayed in for the rest of our stay). The hotel breakfast buffet was hot and hearty and we felt comfortable and safe in the neighborhood. Provided my son is still living in the neighborhood on our next visit, we will stay here again; it was just right for us. All the good stuff said, I must warn you that if you can't deal with street/city noise, this hotel is not for you. It is not a quiet location with the 101 freeway right out the back door and a major through-street out the front. While it didn't bother us, there are those for whom it is an issue.

“Family-Friendly Value Hotel with Convenient Location” Stayed as a solo traveler for three nights in May. Got a terrific price using Travelocity's Top Secret Hotel feature. Hotel is centrally located to many San DIego attractions (beach, Mission Bay, Balboa Park and Old Town are only a few minutes away by car). Although the property is very close to Interstate 8, traffic noise was not a problem inside the hotel. Check in was friendly and efficient (front desk staff always had smiles and were helpful). The property is well maintained, with the glaring exception being the elevator off of the reception area: It is quite beat up and gives a very bad initial impression, but don't be put off by it, because the rest of the property is in better shape. If you park on the property there is an additional charge, but I was able to park on the street and avoid the expense. The rooms are more or less oriented around a central pool area, with the rooms on each floor in several buildings that are connected by a common semi-circular hallway. At the beginning and end of each floor the corridor and room entrances are inside of the building, otherwise they are outside. The latter rooms also have a window facing the hallway. So, if you don't want a room with a window and door opening onto an exterior hallway, you should specify a room at either end of the corridor. The rooms are set up in a suite configuration, but my room seemed to be the reverse of the usual layout, with the sitting room on the interior side and the bedroom by the entrance (in other words, you had to walk through the bedroom to get to the sitting room; and someone staying on the foldout sofa in the sitting room would have to walk through the bedroom to get to the bathroom). Not an issue for a solo traveler or couple, but not optimal for a family. Each room was tightly packed with furniture, which was generally in good shape. Amenities included in room coffee, fridge and microwave. Maid service was satisfactory. Good complimentary breakfast, with indoor and outdoor seating, although the first morning was slim pickings as the hotel was jammed with families for the Memorial Day holiday and the staff couldn't keep up. Complimentary Wall Street Journal on weekdays. Health facility is a joke if you want more than a treadmill. I would not hesitate to stay here again at the right price.

“Location, location, location” The location right on the riverwalk is the best. The property is a little dated and could use a general overhaul. It is typical Hyatt which isn't bad but is a bit of a cold environment that is very 60ish. I had a very ordinary room, but comfortable. Hallway sound easily filtrated into the room. There was some inconsistancy on the part of service provided by the staff. The British Pub onsite was very unfriendly and seemed very uninterested in service. I was told it was seperate from the hotel, in which case, I will not hold the hotel accountable. I have made several businesstrips to San Antonio and have found it to be rather over hyped. The riverwalk is really not a big deal and I would hardly call it a river. But, if you feel the need to be on the "river". The Hyatt is the place to stay and you should find it comfortable and well served.

“Hot/Cold” The hotel is labeled a "boutique" hotel although it lacks character. The hotel hallways are exceptionally small and slightly crowded. BUT the hotel was very clean and the room service was excellent. The Inc. Bar in the lobby is EXTREMELY loud on the weekends - has a "club" feeling. (good nightlife!!) If you are looking for a unique boutique hotel, I wouold recommend the Night Hotel in Times Square over the Time Hotel.

“Great hotel with problems” Our first stay at the Carlton was both a disaster and a triumph. Our king room was gotten for $229. on a Travelzoo promo. The size was okay, but the heating was broken. After a sleepless night I told the clerk we wanted to change. He said no, they'd look into fixing it. I insisted I wanted to change (couldn't trust another sleepless night). He was surly and ignored me. I saw an asst. manager who was very apologetic and moved us to a much larger room (1107), where we stayed 2 more nights. She also sent up a fruit plate. Most staff there are just fine, but the doormen are absolutely worthless, standing on the curb yakking, even if you're struggling through. Only twice of my 4 nights did one grab a door/call a cab. While the decorating of the rooms is very, very nice (hand made silk bolsters, e.g.), the construction is garbage. So much so that I will not be going back. One example is the walk in shower of room 1007, which is canted away from the wall. The bathroom literally flooded. Glad I wasn't in 907. (this time I paid $460). Now, the showcase of this hotel is it's exquisite lobby - timeless, elegant and fresh design. The bar has a very clubby atmosphere that feels Edwardian, yet not stuffy. I suggest staying at the hotel now before it falls apart in a year.

“Good hotel, shame about the noise” Stayed in this hotel for 5 nights in Nov. Now the hotel has several good/very good points: - the shuttle bus to Universal and the metro - the gift shop where knowledgeable staff will book you trips - the pool and fitness centre - close to a great Ralphs store for your grocery needs - the large rooms and comfortable beds However you need to consider the downsides before deciding if this is the location for you: - the noise from the nearby freeways/motorways. We were aware of this from previous Tripadvisor postings and therefore 3 months before our stay asked for a quiet room. When we arrived the desk clerk assured us that room 611 would be perfect and noise free. It was on a high floor and overlooking the pool so we thought that would be fine. After 5 nights of having to sleep with ear plugs in we shudder to think what a room not considered noise free would be like. - the bed linen is not changed as advertised every 3 days, as ours was never changed. So go to this hotel if you want enjoy all the benefits shown above but unless you are able to sleep through any noise then it is probably best to avoid. Shame as it could have been good

“Good value at the weekend” I needed somewhere to stay for a few nights in Manhattan and wasn't too fussy about location - given most hotels in New York are, if anything, more expensive at the weekend this seemed to be a good choice as, given its business location, it was a great price at the weekend ($130 + taxes per night on the IHG Friends & Family rate). The hotel is tall and narrow (20 stories, 5 rooms per floor) and you could easily walk by it without noticing, particularly given the scaffolding that is still up around it. I'd been staying in another hotel the night before so arrived at the appointed 3pm check-in time only to be told that there weren't rooms available - there seemed to be a few people in this situation and, as others have noted, the lobby is pretty small so by the time you have a few travellers with their luggage it gets a bit cramped! They took my luggage and I came back later, but the room still had to be "inspected" so another few minutes of waiting around. Taking one of the two elevators (never seemed to have a long wait, which was great) to the 18th floor I found the room to be absolutely fine - a bit on the small side but comfortable bed. It was good to have an iron and coffee making facilities in the room, and the free wi-fi (that other hotels are charging $15 for) was a real bonus, but a shame that there wasn't an in-room safe for passports etc.. The room was quiet, but with no views. It was generally clean, but there did seem to be an issue with the toilet plumbing which meant it wouldn't empty - not very pleasant :-( The hotel itself if just moments from Century 21 / J&R (shoppers' paradise!) and there are a good number of drug stores / fast food places / coffee shops within very easy reach. Whilst you have to get the subway to virtually everywhere, the good thing about the downtown location is the large number of subway lines very close to the hotel, including the A train to JFK. Overall, although the experience wasn't overwhelming I'd certainly stay there again if the price was right.

“Good Service, Affordable” Hotel was reasonably priced for the Labor Day weekend. Convenient to all forms of public transportation (subway entrance is right in front of the hotel). The location can be a bit slow on nights and weekends. The room, although small, was fairly clean, the bed clean & comfortable, with a down comforter. There is a mini-fridge and coffee maker for your own use. The staff was very accommodating and friendly. I didn't take advantage of the hotel's pricey room service, but opted to eat out instead. My only real complaint, and the reason this review only gets 3 stars is that the bathroom fan is really loud and NEVER SHUTS OFF - at least for me it didn't. So it kind of made me feel like I was sleeping in mission control or something. Also, the tv was not really working right either. Other than that, I might consider staying again in future.

“Not bad for the price” I stay here everytime I go to Baltimore because it is pretty good for the price. It's not the greatest like a high end room, but if you are looking for a decent, clean hotel to sleep in, it will do. Just don't eat the food there. It is awful and the staff in the restuarant could care less about you.

“Beautiful grounds” The grounds of this property are the most beautiful we have experienced in the Phoenix area. Unfortunately our room, a valencia casita, was not the most beautiful. I made the mistake of not reserving a designer casita, which apparently are updated. Our casita was old, the lay out was odd and the bathroom was just like a best western. I really enjoy having a beautiful room with a great large bathtub in the bathroom. We were offered to upgrade to a terrace room but it was a bit small, the japanese soaking tub in the room was like a small jacuzzi but the way it is you are not able to lay down in the water. You have to be sitting upright as though you are on a step in the very deep end of a pool. Our lunch that we had in T-Cooks was good, cocktail hour in the bar was fun and I will definitely be back so long as I book a designer casita. I was sad to leave the gorgeous grounds.

“Perfect for a quick Getaway” This was for a quick getaway to get away from the rainy weather in WA and get some sun and shopping in. We stayed 4 nights on a buy 3 get 1 free deal from Vacations to Go. Great Deal as always when it comes to Embassy Suites. Typical room for them included a sitting area with hideaway bed couch, desk and bar area with sink. Micro and fridge are great for an extended stay. Bathroom is seperate from the bedroom so the setup is great for families. The service here was better than the average Embassy Suites. The wait staff learned our names and really made us feel welcome. Right next to an outdoor mall, restaurants, and movie make the location good also.

“It was so noisy we had to checkout early” My sister and I stayed at the Sofitel Los Angeles for 2 nights. We had booked in for a 5 night stay but we had a few issues with noise from a screaming baby to parents yelling and noisy partygoers. The hotel staff were very helpful but unfortunately as the hotel was well booked they were unable to move us so we made the decision to move hotels. This is something we have never done before. I never expected that we would be checking out early from a Sofitel. The hotel itself is very nice it is just unfortunate that we had to deal with so many noise issues. They really need to soundproof the rooms better.

“Decent Hotel Near Space Needle” If you want to stay near the Space Needle and Experience Music Project, this is a nice hotel with good rates. The beds are very comfortable and the bathrooms are really clean having been renovated recently. I would definitely consider staying here agin.

“new york getaway” We stayed at the Affinia for 5 nights - the staff were friendly and helpful, even though building work was going on. The location is great - short walk to Times Square - our room had a brilliant view of the Empire State, Madison Square Garden is outside the front door. Our room was noisey - nearby Church, Police station and Fire station, but it's New York. Room was big with a kitchenette area - bathroom and shower were small - lucky we're only small people! The room was cleaned and bed linen changed daily - a good hotel.

“Great value, tiny room” I had a great rate (under $100 a night), which was a superb value. If I had paid a lot more, I might have been disappointed in the absolutely tiny room. The room did have everything I needed (free internet, extremely comfortable bed, large flat-screen tv, iron and ironing board, etc.). The bathroom was well appointed, but it wasn't spotlessly clean. The hallways are also very small, which means that all of the room doors are relatively close to one another. Doors are opening and closing all day and night, of course, and you can hear conversations in the hallway as if they were in your room. Each morning, the housekeeping staff was camped out on the hallway floor folding towels and sheets, etc., and talking very loudly. In summary, it was a great deal, but the room was small and loud.

“A real surprise” I have to confess that I wasn't expecting much. I was landing late at LAX and needed to book somewhere convenient. I'd stayed before at three or four other LAX airport hotels. Whilst this wasn't up to the standards of the Sheraton next door, it was a real surprise and very comfortable for the money I had paid around $60 on Priceline for the night. I picked up my rental car the following morning, so didn't have to pay for parking. Very good sound insulation, and free wireless in the rooms.

“Nice Hotel with Just Nice a Room” I must start off by saying I had a "special corporate discount" to stay at this hotel which was quite a good value at under $300 a nite. However, with that said, I didn't realize that they assign rooms based on the rate you pay. Although this sounds logical it should not be that obvious. Now, don't get me wrong...the room was quite nice....for what you would anticipate if you were staying at a hotel chain such as a Marriott or Sheraton. But this is supposed to be a Ritz Carlton! It did take quite awhile to be able to get online through their WIFI which was annoying. Meal prices are quite high so I ate at better outside restaurants and walked outside to get my breakfast. The room was adequate...a typical desk, king bed, flat screen TV, small sitting chair with a lamp behind it and very nice bathroom. It was clean, and ample....not spacious and definitely not as luxurious as you might expect. I would stay here again for business...now that I know what to expect and not expect. However, I still was disappointed. Saying you are staying at the Ritz Carlton inferred a much higher expectation than was delivered.

“Fab location, not a bad hotel” I had low expectations, honestly. But this was a decent hotel in a great location. The hotel shows some wear, but it was very clean and adequate for a great shopping trip to the city. Great value this time of year too ( ny in December is very pricey).

“Price-location-value” It ws a last minute trip, so it was not that easy to find an affordable hotel. The location is fantastic, walking distance to almost everything, and at night we did not hear any noise. Our room was located in front of the elevator, but we did not hear a thing. it was a quite spacious room with two double beds( we were 3 in the room) and we had a "view" of the construction on 54th street. This room was supposed to be an upgrade to a premium room from deluxe..... The hotel is clean and well maintained, a lot of staff. with the staff it's a bit hit and miss, some are great others less so. Our room smelled very bad like mildew coming from the bathroom curtain and our safe did not work. after several visits from 3 security personel and 2 engineers over the whole day, we were told to use the one at reception.... Breakfast was good, but be prepared for the mindblowing high bill. 2 eggs, 4 coffees and an orange juice for 54 dollars! There is a starbucks around the corner. Would I go back? I think so, because besides these problems it is a very good price for the location, will you find better if you have time to plan? I would say so. If in a pickle to find an affordable place, definitely recommendable, if you have more time or a bigger budget I would say pass and go somewhere else.

“Disappointing for this hotel” I had stayed here three years ago and was impressed by the level of service at this hotel. Not any longer. For its location, price and reputation, there should be a wow factor when you stay here. That was not present. Service was there but not attentive. To me attentive service includes being called by name when I call guest services. Here when I called they did not know my name and did not really seem to be concerned with what I needed. At checkout, I requested a copy of my room charges be emailed to me. The person at the desk even confirmed my email address and promised to email them promptly. Four days later I finally got the email. Room service was an extreme disappointment. When you pay over $50 for breakfast, you expect that the food would be fresh and not stale. The room was large and comfortable. The fitness area was bright and sunny, but the cardio equipment is old and needs to be updated. In fact, that was the overall feeling for this hotel. It was tired and needs to be refreshed. If you need to stay in downtown LA, the location cannot be beat. Just don't expect a lot, which is disappointing considering the price.

“I miss the Westin!!!” Maybe I'm spoiled, typically when we travel to NYC we stay at the Westin. however, someone else in my family made these arrangements and cost was a big issue with several people in our group. The proximity to Central Park is the only thing it had going for it. The front desk had a 4pm check-in..VERY FIRM. I have a hard time believing EVERY ROOM was occupied and that they ALL wouldn't be ready until 4?? To add insult to insult, they would gladly hold our bags for $4/bag. Since we had 5 rooms booked, we quickly learned, that some had "extras" like coffeemakers and some didn't. The hotel was rundown and noisy. The restaurant/bar was very over-priced...even by NYC hotel standards. We were there for a family vacation, and did not let the hotel detract from our time together, but I will NEVER stay there again, nor would I recommend, there are several other "economical" choices in Times Square.

“An average "W" experience” GOOD: Staff = very friendly and helpful without that "W" attitude Acura shuttle service was a plus Location = very close to everything, easy access Beach/Bar = roof top beach/bar was cute and fun Lobby = turns into a club/lounge on Saturday nights. Music was quite loud. AVERAGE: WET = It's more for looks, way too small for swimming SHOWER PRESSURE = on Level 6, not very strong BAD: Our room's windows were very dirty (see pic), did not expect this from this level of hotel. Parking must be done by valet each time, all courteous, but a bit annoying to have to wait for them to drive the car around the block. Furniture, Decor - were a bit beat up.

“Not Bad” When I found out my company had booked me in the Hampton Inn, I wasn't thrilled. However, this hotel exceeded my expectations. Like the Sheraton Four Points it's right across the street from a really great Whole Foods which really opens up your options in terms of what you can eat. Also, this hotel offers a pretty decent free breakfast (eggs, yogurt, sausages, toast, etc.) and has free WiFi - not bad! The only thing I'd really knock them on are the beds. Lumpy and extremely uncomfortable. The linens aren't the greatest, either.

“Good rooms, disorganized restaurant” Stayed here one night on business. Rooms are medium sized and well appointed, including a built-in PC. LIghting above average. The room was quiet except for the occasional passing siren (Philadelphia seems to have lots of sirens). Good hot water supply and comfortable beds. Maintenance seemed good but not immaculate. Downsides: the staff seem more obtrusive than in most hotels -- there always seemed to be people with large carts in the halls and elevators. Housekeeping knocked on my door quite early, even though I had not picked up the paper just outside. Breakfast in the restaurant was decent, but the staff seemed shorthanded, disorganized, and overwhelmed. In the morning, the lobby was very crowded, mostly with people with very large backpacks. Overall, I would recommend it, but avoid the restaurant. There are many restaurants and cafes in the immediate area.

“Very nice, with a lot of exceptions” We ended up here after deciding to gamble on Priceline. We were impressed at first, but there were a few surprises and disappointments. The Good: Very pretty grounds with lots to do and 2 restaurants Large rooms Pool and jacuzzi were nice The Bad: *Parking fee (for us it was $32, but I heard another person get charged $27. This was on top of Priceline fee.) *"Passport" Fee (this is $15/day per person on top of our Pricelined charges... would have been fine if we had arrived early enough to use the services or if we had just known that was a charge on top of the Priceline fee.) This fee is for using the grounds, like playing tennis/etc. The Annoying: When we arrived, we instantly liked the hotel and decided to ask them if we could stay another night for around the same price that we got on Priceline. We weren't expecting to win a bid on a hotel with so much to do (spa/tennis/ping pong/pools/etc.) so we thought we might like to stay another full day so we could actually enjoy the hotel instead of just sleeping there one night. The woman at the front desk was friendly but said she wouldn't be able to let me know until later that night or when the manager came in the next morning. I didn't hear from them in the morning, so I called the front desk. A different woman told me that she would need to check, but no matter what, she would call me right back. She did not. I finally decided to pack up our stuff and check out. We were disappointed to leave, and wondered why no one ever got back to us. The hotel did not seem very busy, we only saw a handful of people during our stay... an extra night seemed like it would work well for everyone, especially if we kept the same room. Upon check-out I was told that we couldn't have the room another night because there was a conference coming in and all the rooms were taken. I didn't believe this last-minute excuse because if all the rooms were booked, then why didn't they just say that when I first inquired? The woman at the front desk said she was sorry, but whenever I wanted to come back, she would make sure we were taken care of. Sadly, I don't think we'll be going back. It was a cute place and we were excited in the moment about spending the day in the spa and using the Passports for tennis, etc., but we wouldn't go out of our way to return. Tips: Ask for the parking fee to be waived. I just happened to read the reviews on Yelp and a few people mentioned the ridiculous parking fees. A few people said that if you asked about it, they usually would waive the fee for you. I did this and it worked. $32/day was a hefty hidden charge in my opinion.

“Beautiful Building...rooms show the age” Stayed because of the reviews, Some what disappointed. Check in was slow, room was not ready. So we dumped our luggage at the front desk and checked out the riverwalk. When the room was ready they called me on my cell phone to let me know the room was ready. Upon returning, it took a good 10 minutes to find my luggage. Our room was located in the San Fernando tower which was adventure to find, no help from the front desk. Had to take the main elevator to the sixth floor and go on a maze like adventure to the elevators for the SF tower. The room was huge but dark and dated. Valet parking was quick and prompt! Would look to stay somewhere else, now that I know the lay of the land around the riverwalk.

“Not Outstanding Reservation System” I went to book a room at this hotel because of all the great reviews. Their web site showed no Executive Suites available although Expedia did. So I called them and they said they were not sure why their web site was not showing available Executive Suites. They would however match Expedia's rate which just about every hotel will. However they would not guarantee me a high floor. They said I could call the day of to see if I got a high floor but since they gave me the cheap Expedia rate they would not guarantee me a high floor unless they had a room on a high floor the day I was to check in. Yes they gave me the Expedia rate but they didn't have to give Expedia a cut since I was booking through Sofitel and not Expedia and they didn't even show anything available on their site. In any event they were pleasant just seemed unorganized, not helpful and did not behave like an outstanding hotel.

“I was not impressed...” This is my first negative review - and it is mild. The room was clean, but the shower faucet leaked so bad it woke me up a few times. The elevator placement is odd - there were elevators right next to my room, but we had to walk in a big "U" shape to get to the ones that were operational. I found the staff to be a bit cold - not the "golly we're glad you're here" that this midwesterner expects... The plus side is that the decor is modern - the price is fair, and the location is excellent...

“Run down and In Need Of a Remodel” I stayed here on October 3rd for 1 night. While the Room was modern and nice comfy bed flatscreen tv The rest of the hotel is run down. THERE IS NO ELEVATOR AT ALL. To get the rooms you have to walk up 1 set of stairs then across a open area then another set of stairs just to get to the rooms. Its like this hotel used to be a run down motel and they converted it into a hotel. It needs allot of work. The personal were nice but the hotel needs to be re-modeled big time.

“faded glory” decided to try the fairmont, at the end ofour holiday instead of usual places like the grand hyatt or mark hopkins. the building itself is beautiful and the lobby area and laurel court are amazing. check in was friendly and we were soon up to the room in the main building. it was a reasonable size and the decor was old world to fit with the building. the view was disapointing, we could see a bit of the bay but mostly we were looking at another building. the main problem with the room was the cleanliness. there were bits of biscuit on the floor, the sheers were dirty and the window, on the ouside was filthy. we reported this and the head of housekeeping responded quickly and a deep clean of the room was sorted for the next day. they even sent us a bowl of fruit to say sorry. after the deep clean we checked the room again, the back of the toilet behind the seat, the sealent around the bowl, the sheers and the window were still dirty. the positives were the concierge who got us into a nice restaurant and the staff in the coffee shop cafe centto. the bell desk when checking out and leaving our bags were quite abrubt and not friendly. overall really disappointing given our expectations. if you want somewhere nice with a view and clean rooms, go to the mark hopkins or the grand hyatt.

“Great Place but Internet was bad” I just came from EL PASO. I chose this hotel simply because that it was the nearest 3-star hotel from the Airport and the reviews in Trip Advisor were generally good. The staff was very kind and polite and he gave me a map of the hotel to guide me to the room. The room was clean and comfortable and no problem for the hot water. :-p They provide computers and printers to use for free. Here are two thing I dissatisfied. 1. I ordered my breakfast next day, the price was $13.90(before tax) like american style breakfast ,which was different from what was on tag $12.85 or so. I asked the room service agent, but hesaid this was the only kind of American style Breakfast. Even more suprised, I saw a coffee cup sold for $3.95on my bill. I was shocked that the hotel did not only sell breakfast but also sell coffee cups!! I thought I should rejoice that they didn't sell the breakfast bowl or dishes to me. 2. The internet was incredible bad.... still the next day I checked in, in the evening, most of computers could not be connected to the hotel's internet. Even the technician couldn't tell why. I tried several place, because in my room the wireless signal was really poor, but my computer still failed to connect to the internet. I spent a boring night.

“Very nice hotel, undergoing renovations, great service” The Copley is an historic property that is undergoing major renovations. I am sure it will be a very good property when finished, but for the moment I rank as average. My room was great. I was told I was only the third guest to have stayed there. Though the sleeping rooms are good, the bathrooms are small (historic property). The service is excellent with good attention to detail and attentiveness. The downside is the hallways smell like paint, work is going on in very near proximity to rooms that are being used. The business "center" is open to the lobby so no privacy or real quiet. The Oak room is closed, but the St. James is a nice substitute. Drinks are expensive and short, for the price one expects a better pour. For a night or two of business travel it is fine, would not book a group. Give it 12 -18 months and I imagine it will be back to the Very Good range.

“Factor in all the fees when comparing rates” The Hyatt in the Loop has been a Chicago fixture for years and is a well-run hotel with a professional staff in a good location near Michigan Avenue, the lake, the art museum, etc. Rooms have been updated and we had a pleasant stay overall. However, hotel nightly parking is $50, there is a charge for Internet hookup in the room and of course the lodging fees and other fees really add up here. I complained about the Internet fee as being ridiculous for a Hyatt signature hotel like this, and I received a courteous response that the hotel does have Wifi in the lobby. Of course, that doesn't help you in the room.

“could have been better” Not really the westin standard. Location is excellent the view from the sqaure side rooms is wonderfull. The room s were really smaal. the bar staff not friendly. The frontdeks and concierge were excellent but the other staff was not really nice. we stayed here in the busy season between christmas and new years.

“Very Clean. Not a 4 star.” Stayed with my family over an early Spring Break in April. This is not a true 4 star. It felt like a 3 star. Not plush in any way. Very basic. Plastic cups in the bathroom. Nothing special. Though the hotel is nice and clean. It is an uneventful place to stay. It is walking distance to some good restaurants. But you have to get in your car to go to any other fun places in the city. Parking is $24! My 7 and 5 year olds enjoyed having the marina to look out to every morning. Other than that, there was nothing for them to do in the hotel. As the weather was drab. We stayed in the new building. I was told the older building had more to it. Starbucks and such.

“Ok rooms, thin doors, nice smiling staff, great location” This hotel is nothing special, it’s simple, the rooms are ok but not flashy and some improvement could be made regarding the old furniture, especially the doors…the room doors are so old and thin you can actually hear people talking and walking whenever they are in the corridor even if they are far away. The air circulating system at this hotel is not good, if the old-looking air/con system is switched off, it is actually difficult to breathe so we tried to stay out of the room as much as possible. There is free-wifi in the rooms which is a plus. All Hilton Garden Inns provide shampoo, conditioner, mouthwash and body lotion, but no shower gel….they give you soap… The location of this hotel is great, there is a subway stop just outside the door but the hotel is close to everything, so you can walk everywhere too. No noise coming from outside of the hotel. The staff is always smiling and nice, very welcoming and helpful, especially the girls at reception from Montenegro and the guy at the hotel entrance door. The Web Grill restaurant is very nice, we had breakfast there twice and we liked it, the price is ok and the food is good.

“Nice hotel; bad, bad lighting; very expensive breakfast” Stayed here for a conference at the San Jose Convention Center. It's a perfect location for that, and not a bad location for anything in downtown San Jose. First good stuff: Location, nice work area in the room with lots of plugs and proper height for working on a computer, comfortable bed, quiet (except for a little plane noise - the hotel is in the flight pattern for SJC airport). Bad stuff: Horrible lighting in the room. The lamp on the desk had two, mostly bare, CFL bulbs with the color temperature of industrial lighting. In fact all the lighting in the room were those same awful bulbs. The bathroom was worse - the light was behind the mirror. The TV didn't work when I got there, but that was fixed. Still the channels were junk and no HD. (how can a $99 Fairfield have great HD channels and a $300 Hilton have none?). It also seemed the AC wouldn't cool the room enough. The Breakfast buffet was $20+ (I ate a $10 egg&cheese bagle off the menu that was fair). We should have walked down the street. Food: We ate at Original Joes down the street. It's lost some of its charm, but the food was still good.

“Bidders beware!!!!!” I stayed here for several nights during the week as a result of a priceline bid. When I checked in - early in the day, I asked if it was possible to have a room on the front, and I was told by the young man checking me in - immediately and emphatically "no", there was no room because they were "sold out". Given that this was only 2:30 pm, I find it hard to believe that the young man behind the desk couldn't accomodate my request, as most folks would not have arrived yet. About 1/3 of the rooms appear to face the alley - so I assume the Priceline or other "bidders" are placed on the back alley rooms - however I was given THE WORST room in the hotel: Room 301. The window is just big enough to jump out of in an emergency, but allowed no natural light. So even if you were in the room in the middle of a bright and sunny day, you had to have all of the lights on in the room. See attached pictures to see what I mean. I'm sure 401, 501, 601 etc. are all the same This hotel is an old building, but has had a facelift. My room was clean and nicely furnished, with large TV - and free wired/wireless internet. It is located on Scott Circle, and the nearest metro, restaurants, stores etc are a 10 to 15 minute walk. There is one upscale resaurant in the hotel, but I didn't eat there. It looks ok. As a result of aged building, the hotel is not very soundproof, and the toilets, elevators, ice machines, stairwell doors all make a lot of noise, so bring your earplugs!! I wasn't near the elevator and could still hear it. The guys at the door are fantastic - always want to help, as are the girls at the desk, however the young man who works at the desk and in the office does not seem very enthusiastic or customer oriented. Anyway - for $77 that I paid on priceline, I guess I can't complain, but if I paid the $239 they wanted on the Marriott website or Expedia, I would have been extremely dissatisfied with my room - but then again had I paid full price, I probably would have got the room with the picture window looking out at the circle!

“How about a smile at check-in :)” The location of this hotel is pretty good for a business traveler. However the hotel is pretty dated. The main lobby has a feeling of old world grandeur which is actually quite nice and takes you back. However, the rooms need a bit of sprucing up. But the worst of it is even as a Gold Starwood Guest both check-in folks on the evening of 2/15 were quite rude and unwelcoming. No smile, no we'll be with you in a couple of mins...they just kept on typing while I stood there for 3-5 minutes....and then one of the guys goes to me, I can't help you....and the lady just gesture for me to approach her. No "Hi can I help you...nothing" no offer of an upgrade or even "sorry sir no upgrade is available". Pros: Location away from Union Square if you want to be away from hustle bustle. Good lobby/entrance - quite grand. Cons: Very disappointing check-in Dated rooms, 3 small pillows on a king bed, unnecessary armoire, etc. No coffee/tea maker in the rooms A pretty cramped room Noisy mini fridge

“Modern style with dark lighting.” I just stayed here one night for a holiday work party. The location of the hotel is decent as it is off of Wacker Drive (South water) and Michigan Avenue. It's just south of the river. Cabs are plenty, easy assess to buses and walking distance to some main attractions and shopping. The hotel was newly opened when we stayed there and we were looking forward to check it out. The decor was very modern and industrial. (Whites, grays, steels, blacks). So not very cozy...but fit the 'rock' style persona. The beds were very comfortable. But the lighting was horrible. It was very dark in the rooms and dark in the bathrooms so it was tough getting ready to g o out to a formal affair with the lighting by the mirrors. There really was nothing special about the rooms for the price. Its really you are paying for the name (Hard Rock) and for the location and because it is located in the historical 'Carbide and Carbon' Chicago building . I wouldn't stay here again, but if you want to stay in a hip type of place and don't mind the darkness, the Hard Rock would be okay.

“Given it 3 stars as there were some issues...” Agree with fellow travellers that the location is good, although W14th is a major thoroughfare and if your room is at the front (which our's was) then it can be quite noisy - and especially so I would expect in summer months with the window open. The room was fine, although the "sofabed" turned out to be a single day couch. Two other issues: we requested a wake up call at 4:45 am as we had an early flight and it didn't happen until 5 am - and as we had a car booked at 5:15 this proved a problem. And lastly there is a lovely cat there called Charlie, but as one of our party is quite allergic he had real problems as the cat has free reign over the place. Everyone was friendly and helpful so would give it another go on balance.

“Not a great performance” I've stayed at the Hotel Felix three times, when the price is right. I prefer the Dana, which is around the corner, on a number of levels. Nicer rooms, better views, better service. For this visit the service at the Felix reached a new low. I called the day before to let them know that I would be arriving late, and was transferred 3 times from reservations (not at the hotel) to the front desk, back to reservations, and back to the hotel. Finally the desk clerk said he would make a handwritten note! Not reassuring. When I finally got into the room, it was not ready for prime time. There were no hangers, nor glasses, nor any stopper in the sink. The bedside lamp was bolted to the wall at 10º off plumb. The pillows were old and lumpy. After multiple calls, we did get a sink drain, hangers, and two dirty glasses that we had to wash to use! Never got better pillows. The rest of the room was fine, although the window looked out directly into another building under construction, so close we could have touched it. We also ate breakfast in the cafe. They were out of several dishes. The coffee was delicious, and so was some of the food, but the rest was cold. I guess they do not give Hotels.com guests their best rooms OR their best service. I won't be coming back.

“Didn't meet Expectations..” When we originally booked this hotel we were so excited about coming because we had gotten the Presidential Suite. Well when we checked in service was slow and uninviting. The staff said it was renovate from a nursing home.. and you can tell. The Suite had so much extra space which was not needed, the air conditioner was louder than a plane, and the shower was dirty. Once again I hate writing bad reviews but this hotel was not what the website showed us.

“Nice hotel with one major flaw.....” This is a new hotel on the southbank. Good location to downtown and reasonably priced for the area. The hotel is new and clean with good quality ammenities. The rooms are well appointed, the furniture is comfortable. I only noted one problem but unfortunately its a deal-killer - they sliding glass door leading out to the balcony is very thin. What this means is you hear every car that passes on the highway and every conversation going on by people passing by (even though I was on the fourth floor). Because of all of the noise I couldn't sleep. I checked out early and changed hotels. It's a shame because otherwise this is a good place.

“Good location very average hotel for a Westin” I stayed for 3 nights for a business trip and picked it for location. The hotel is fine if the location suits you although not the usual high standard you would expect in a Westin. Positives - very comfortable westin bed, good gym for a city centre and easy walking of all main places. The rooms are cleaned well. The room service was good quality and arrived promptly. Downsides- even though in a preferred room, it was tiny with no storage for clothes other than one rail. The bathroom was dated and shabby. The queues for checking in were long and I noticed that was the same every day. The concierge appeared bored and as though she was doing me a favour providing directions! the restaurant and baths a very limited menu. Overall an average experience.

“could be better” Nice upper mid level hotel in a good location. However some of the rooms are showing there age; also no coffee maker in the room and really expensive internet ( why do hotels marketing themselves as upper end insist on massive internet charges when almost every budget hotel has free internet--it seems that the more expensive the average room the more the more the hotel thinks it can charge for wifi). Some of the upper floor rooms have a great view of central park. Service is good but not great, the Burger joint is good but not worth the long lines that it sometimes has. Just an OK value

“Smokers not welcome. Nice decor.” This is an unusual hotel, in the Japan Town part of SF. The decor is Japanese, with lots of woodcut images in the rooms and public spaces. Unfortunately, the air conditioning in my room did not work. There is a bar/restaurant in the hotel which produces rather unauthentic Japanese dishes, as well as American ones. Fortunately there are other options nearby, in particular Japanese ones. Smoking is forbidden in all of the hotel and the smokers' area is outside, with no cover and no seats - another leper colony.

“Convenient stay!” Overall, we enjoyed our stay here. We stayed here on a Saturday-Tuesday, and every front desk person we encountered was extremely helpful and friendly. The only issue I did have was that our room did not get serviced until Monday, which would not have been a huge deal except we needed towels. In the hotel's defense, Sunday we may just have missed our service opportunity. We had do not disturb on the door in the early AM and assumed the room would be serviced while we were at breakfast and had removed the do not disturb, but it was not. When we left the hotel for our day's activities, it still had not been serviced when we returned. On Monday, I asked could the room please be serviced. They did not clean the bathtub though.The breakfast included in the cost of the room was decent, and we would stay here again for the cost. It was also in reasonable driving distance of everything we needed to do, which was great for our gas budget!!!

“Convenient Location but Some Walls Too Thin” This hotel is conveniently located near several major public transit access points, including Penn Station. The room was comfortable and very clean, and appeared to have been recently constructed or remodeled. The mattress and pillows were very comfortable. The small refrigerator (which was nearly empty, rather than filled with high-priced snacks) and microwave oven were appreciated. Staff were all helpful and friendly. However, there were a number of problems: - Walls are VERY thin. The neighbors' conversations in their rooms and all the activity occurring in the hallway were audible in my room. Some street noise, such as garbage trucks, could be heard from outside as well, but it was much less annoying than the noise from other occupants of the hotel. Earplugs were provided, but they don't help when you are trying to watch tv or hold your own conversation (or if you want to be sure to hear the alarm clock go off in the morning). - Shower pressure was pathetic. - The shower curtain had an off smell when I arrived and needed to be changed. This is the kind of detail that housekeeping staff should recognize without prompting. - Housekeeping forgot to leave cups in the room for several days, so I mistakenly thought cups were not provided as a policy of the hotel (foolish of me since there was a coffeemaker in the room). - Exercise room is very small with just a few pieces of equipment. The equipment all appears to be new. There is a large multi-component weights machine that was actually too complicated to figure out how to use, despite the instructions posted on the wall (and I've been using weights machines for years). Would consider returning if I could get a very low price again (I visited during a low point in the year for tourism). But would probably look elsewhere, due to the thin walls, if only their standard rates were being offered.

“Inexpensive, clean but dated"” I concur with the previous reviewers that this hotel is very difficult to find, even with a GPS. At one time, before the expansion of the Austin freeway system, this Holiday Inn fronted an easy access road. Now it is located in a pit of one-way streets backed up against a subdivision of cul-de-sacs. But if you are on a budget then you might consider staying here because to entice customers the room prices are low. With that said this is a dated property with some touches of modernization. Why did I pick this hotel, you ask? HA! I was on the Holiday Inn website planning a 10 day Texas State trip. I just picked it and never read any of the Trip Advisor reviews. After 30 minutes of driving in circles trying to find this hotel, I thought, why did I ever pick this Holiday Inn . . . Pluses: Price, nice beds, not too many guests so the entire hotel is quiet and plenty of free parking. Minuses: Worse location in the world, older property, very expensive on-site restaurant, no close off-site restaurants nearby,

“Not worth it” I booked a room through hotwire for around 170 euros/night. When I had waited 30 minutes at the front desk, they gave me a better room as the one I booked was "not so nice". The room I got didn't have a holder for the toilet paper roll, enough room in the bathroom to put down your toothbrush (!) and was very dirty and old. The view was straight into another poor travellers room. Also, the only place with enough room to open my suitecase was my bed, which I had to use as a work desk. Weak. I upgraded to a minisuite which was only available after the first night. The information given at the front desk was very confusing, many of them were very impolite and the hotel seemed to be full of drunk teenagers and families on holiday. The concierge lady (not the young one) was great though. I would not stay here again unless guaranteed a mini suite and for at least half the price of any well-rated chain 4 star highrise in the city.

“Great bed!” I was upgraded to the Club floor so my experience may have been better than other peoples. The king room was on the small side although with a good view. The bed was very good, as good as the Westin Heavenly Bed. The bathroom was past it's best, especially the shower/bath which definitely needs a refurb. Other than the slightly shabby condition though, the room was clean. The breakfast buffet was very good and I found the service good as well.

“Poor housekeeping...and watch the mini bar” This hotel is OK if you can get a good discount but not if you pay the rack rate. The location is excellent if you like the seedy fringe of Soho next to China Town (which I do), but not if you need to be in mid town for an early meeting or are nervous about the dingier parts of Manhattan. The rooms are small and comfortable but the housekeeping is consistently poor. The lobby and hallways are grimy and in need of refurbishment. On a recent stay the cleaner removed the soap and the toilet paper and two light bulbs, and did not replace them. On another occasion, the television remote control was missing and a replacement never arrived. After my last stay there mini bar charges were incorrecttly added to my credit card one week after I had left. I never use hotel mini bars but when I contacted the hotel they refused to reverse the charges and I eventually gave up trying to do anything about them.

“Platinum member review” No platinum up grade. Platinum membership was not acknowledge and had to explain our points gift. This is an average hotel, not a family resort. Great location if your shopping in the galleria mall. Otherwise, just an average place that could use some updating. I would recommend platinum members use another hotel that better appreciates SPG membership.

“Mixed reviews” The hotel is clean and modern. The staff is helpful and courteous. Unfortunately, our stay was marred by an A/C unit waking us up, requiring a room change in the middle of the night (from a requested king room to 2 doubles). And an 8 am wake up by the housekeeping staff to "check on the mini bar". So, this hotel gets 3 stars for the mishaps that should have never happened in the first place. Pros: - Convenient location with Dunkin Donuts, deli, Lemograss Grill, and Duane Reade nearby - 2 blocks from 4,6 subway - Clean with duvet covers...no icky bedspreads to deal with! - Spacious rooms with full kitchen. Large desks for working Cons: - See above - No free wifi, except in lobby We were compensated $50 for these problems that made our stay undesirable. However, the original bill included a mini bar and snack bill that was a little dubious since they were then taken off and not on the final bill. There are so many hotels in Manhattan. Unfortunately, this one will never be on my list again.

“Not as bas as many reviewers want you to think.” Stayed here for one night for Obama's ralley. Stayed in a king size room with lakefront view. Beautiful view of Grant Park and the lake. The bed was very comfortable. Room was clean. There was a Flatscreen TV. Bathroom was clean, but old and dated fixtures with some wear. Baseboard in room had been newly replaced, but was not painted yet. Room was large with huge closet which contained iron and ironing board. Furniture was basic, but comfortable. Thought price was really fair for room quality and location. Public spaces in hotel are fairly basic and dated.

“In need of updates!” I will say the hotel is currently going through remodeling, so they are making efforts to update the hotel. I booked my room through a travel site and they were offering a deal. I was there for one night and I did get a good price, but it's clear that the reason they were advertising on the travel site is because the hotel is going through remodeling. Many of the floors were closed, my room was pretty "tired" and overlooked the side street where all of the dumpsters are located for the construction. I will say the staff were very friendly and accommodating, trying to make the stay as comfortable as possible. I hope it gets the face-lift it is in need of. For the price and the fact that I was only there on night on business, I rate it average. If I had paid full price, I would have been pretty unhappy.

“Convenient location” This was my second stay at this hotel. We were with a group for a wedding and received a group rate of $85 plus tax per night. This location is very convenient to the interstates and the Galleria. We had a regular room with a very comfortable king size bed, sofa with coffee table and desk, in addition to the dresser that held the TV. Nothing fancy, but good for the price. Only complaint was the "low flow" toilets which clogged on each stay. Although the "hot" foods on the breakfast buffet were from the frozen food case, the other items were excellent (especially the banana nut muffins). There was a very large variety of cereals, muffins, cakes, breads, fruit, yogurt along with juices, milk and coffee. There is also free popcorn and cookies in the afternoon. One warning - we were approached several times by the same panhandler in the parking lot. His story is that he is staying at the hotel next door and his wife is receiving cancer treatments, but he needs money for gas & food. We saw the same man eating at the breakfast buffet the next morning - only to see him carry a large plate of food out the door when he noticed us talking about him to the other guests in our party. That time the hotel staff did nothing. Later that afternoon, he walked out the hotel eating popcorn and approached us for money again. This time the staff went looking from him and found him soliciting money from another guest. I was told they got his license plate number to contact the police. I hope they did, because I beleive the same man approached us on our past stay at this hotel in 2005.

“Wee-ooo wee-ooo wee-ooo” That's the sound of the firetrucks that go by on a regular basis... all... night... long..., otherwise, excellent, attentive staff, nice bed, all the necessities. Inexpensive with a view of night-time goings on across the street. Window coverings not appropriate for a hotel, they are just wood blinds that don't provide much darkening, nor privacy when the room next door has windows facing yours. Unusual restaurant in building, offers adventurous choices.

“Pretty happy overall” I stayed here for a week in March. I'm a bit fed up with paying top-dollar for big-brand hotels that don't offer much in return, so I thought I would try something more like a boutique. The location is very good, with all my mid-town meetings within a few blocks. Staff were very welcoming on arrival and were sufficiently organized not to have lost the presentations I had delivered to the hotel, which was a relief. I was on the 10th floor. There is only one lift and the week I was there must have been spring break because the hotel was quite busy and at peak times the wait for the lift was occasionally pretty long. Room was a pleasant surprise in terms of size: I had something approaching a junior suite, with a separate dressing room and decent sized bedroom. Bathroom however was a bit dated in appearance and pretty small. Wireless LAN is available free throughout the hotel which I have decided is a 'must' for all hotels I visit, I resent paying hundreds of dollars per night for the room and then being asked to pay another $20 for WiFi. If Starbucks can do it for nothing, so can hotels, right? My main issue with the hotel was the noise: I guess I was overlooking 54th St and every morning around 5:30 or 6:00am the traffic noise was horrendous, with trucks sounding their horns etc etc. If you like to lay in late in the morning, ask for a room somewhere quiet or don't stay here. The hotel wasn't really all that geared up for business travellers: breakfast was served in a lounge on the first floor, which was fine except that because it was included in the price (which was a plus), it was not really possible to have a breakfast meeting in the hotel. I tried one morning and the doorman pretty much tried to turn my colleagues away!

“Nice hotel, let down by restaurant staff” Great location, nice rooms excellent bathrooms. No hassle at all - would have scored 4 until final breakfast where appalling staff spoiled the experience. Only myself and one other person but the staff's loud personal conversation was more interesting than ensuring I had coffee or juice or my needs were satisfied. Food was also poor.
