“Close to airport, never received wakeup call, need better breakfast hours” I had a flight that was delayed by over 4 hours into Denver, causing me to miss my conneciton and was put up in this hotel by Southwest. It was almost 2 a.m. when the shuttle I got on arrived and a lot of people had 6 a.m. connections the next morning, and fortunately I got on the shuttle, but others were told they would have to wait for the next shuttle due to the van being full and it was the only van they had running. I requested a 5 a.m. wakeup call which I never received. I have learned to always set my cell phone alrm for 5 minutes past a wake up call as sort of a snooze feature and if I wouldn't have that stay, I would have overslept and missed my flight. The breakfast needs to start earler. This is an airport area hotel and it would be nice to have access to breakfast. I was on the 5:30 a.m. shuttle and no breakfast and no coffee. I only was in the room a few hours and had no problems with noise but I was in an end room available from the elevator. The front desk clerk at check in was friendly. Room service was not available and would have been great seeing everything at the airport was closed that late.

“Lots of hype not as high end as you'd expect” Maybe I'm too old for the W. It is a scene. The entire lobby. Think Hard Rock hotel style. When we walk in the hotel lobby was a party pretty much of a cross of industry people, hipsters, college co-eds and cougars. Very fancy decor and lots of good people watching. The rooms were so-so. The furniture was uber modern and some of it could've been from IKEA which is fine just not expected at the W. They did have a perch of a couch which doubled as a single bed when we had a friend that was unable to drive home stay. All the bathroom products are Bliss products so that was nice. We had a lovely view of the Valet. In terms of location, it's right on Hollywood Blvd in the middle of everything. There's a farmers' market a few blocks away on Sundays which is one of the best in LA. The Palladium is only 2 blocks away. So if you are looking for a scene you will get here. Go to be scene.

“Wouldn't be my first choice to stay again at IAH” We grabbed a room at this hotel in a pinch when we missed a connection at IAH. I have stayed at 2 other hotels at IAH - the Sheraton and the Hyatt Place and would prefer to stay at either of those again over this hotel. I thought it was a bit beat up, the staff were a bit like they were doing you a favor rather than being friendly. My first room smelled like smoke even though it was designated non-smoking. The staff did quickly get me into another room and I appreciate that. I also thought at $168 a night we overpaid - this room was worth about $75. Yes, we were in a pinch but I think I paid about $88 at the Hyatt for a better room and better service. The staff on the shuttle were very friendly and efficient.

“Shabby, but you have to go” Let's be upfront - I was thrilled to be booked into the Waldorf Astoria, even though anticipating that it would be a faded and worn shadow of its Thirties glory. And it was, but I would still go again with the family just to share with them a New York landmark. Stayed in three rooms over 4 nights. The first room was tiny with two double beds lacking any form of back support. Was moved to a quirky mini-suite overlooking the front entrance. This is the sort of room which makes staying in an old hotel so memorable. It had an entrance foyer, bedroom, a huge dressing room (large enough for a small couch, dressing table and two armoires) and an art deco bathroom on a raised platform. Incredible. The third room was a nicer version of the first. All the rooms were worn and in need of repainting, new furniture and carpets. But it was all well worth staying for the fireplaces in the halls, lobby area and the ability to say that you stayed at the Waldorf=Astoria.

“Great location and service” This hotel is situated on the Georgetown Campus, near the medical center and a few steps from the Admissions Office. I agree with other reviewers that the rooms are a tad shabby. For example, there was a worn patch in the carper in my room. None the less, the location is terrific and the staff is very friendly. I would stay here again on Georgetown U business due to its convenience. I am in DC on other matters I would probably stay elsewhere. The staff pointed me to the free Georgetown University shuttle bus that leaves every 5 minutes for the Dupont Circle metro station. This makes all of Washington, DC very accesable.

“Extremely crowded, average hotel.” The thing I hate most about this hotel is that it is PACKED with crowds. Fisherman's wharf is a very crowded touristy place. But I feel like this hotel is overly crowded. The line for breakfast in the morning seriously went through two rooms. I would say it took 10 minutes to get through this line and by the time I did, many of the options were gone. All the bacon was gone at 9 a.m. and even though the breakfast went until 9:30, they said they were not bringing more out. I waited 10 minutes to get a bagel and some cereal. Then when I got through the line, there was literally nowhere to sit. In the morning every single table is taken, every piece of furniture. There are people literally sitting on the floor in a corner eating ... or standing up and eating. After the first day, I said forget it and bought breakfast outside of the hotel. There were groups of kids there as well ... I would suggest if you see large groups of middle school and high school age kids hanging all over the lobby, you should ask the front desk to put you on a floor away from them. They get loud. Also, in the mornings and at night, the elevators get packed and crowded. It takes several trips of people jamming into them to go to your room. And of course many of the European tourists don't exactly grasp the concept of waiting in an orderly line, so many rush into the elevator even if you have been waiting there before them. A lower floor would probably be better. The service here is poor as well. I asked for an extended check out time and they would not give me one, even though I am a top tier rewards member. I am supposed to get a 2 o'clock check out if I request it. Not so at this hotel. Also, I am entitled to a room upgrade, if available. Not only did they not have a room upgrade for me, they said that they did not have any king beds left when I checked in. When I told them I was sure that I requested one on the website, they told me they were sorry but the hotel was full. So I got a room with two small beds. I was dissapointed to hear that there was no wireless internet. There is a free wired internet access port in the room, but that means you will have to sit at the desk if you want to go online. Another annoying thing is that there aren't many cable stations at all. There around 11 channels. 3 are sports related and 2 are hotel/local area related, leaving around 6 stations to watch. The hotel is clean and in a great location, right on fisherman's wharf. Every other hotel chain has a hotel in this area. You can easily and safely walk to the wharf. At night there are lots of homeless people who sleep in the allies near the hotel. This might be a concern for people with kids. These people aren't aggressive for the most part, so I didn't feel threatened by them. However, fisherman's wharf isn't the nicest of places after 11 o'clock at night when the crowds are smaller. You can walk a few blocks to the wharf or In N Out Burger or lots of restaurants. I love the location of this hotel. The lobby and furnishings are nice. The hotel is new. Valet parking is $30 per night. Kind of a rip off considering the hotel has its own connected lot. So keep that in mind when booking ... you are spending $30 per night extra on parking. Pretty standard for Fisherman's Wharf. I think there may be a cheaper lot connected to Enterprise Rent a Car on Beach Street, a block away, which might be worth a check out. Overall, this is nice and clean and in a good location. However, I would much rather stay somewhere with wireless internet and less crowds.

“Decent hotel for the money-great location for Tigers game” Stayed here as part of a last-minute deal package with travelocity-As a single woman traveling around the country to see all the ballparks I was a bit leary about Detroit. The hotel is located perfectly to take in a ballgame - about 1/2 mile. Easy walk - safe during the day and at night if people are walking back from the game - the area is a bit destitute - what do you expect for Detroit ? The hotel was better than I thought it would be - I was in room 1525 - nice size and clean - the breakefast was adequate and pretty varied. Nice spread for being included . The staff was attentive and helpful when I posed questions. Parking is a bit steep - $18/day but you do have in/out privileges. It's valet because of the area- be thankful it is. Detroit is pretty expensive in general - surprisingly so - especially parking - All in all, I would reccomend this hotel and would stay there again if I went back to Detroit.

“Good Renovation, Average Stay” So it appears that some La Quinta's are getting a makeover, and this one is one of them. It was actually being worked on while I was staying there, but that wasn't so bad. It smelled like fresh paint, and they were replacing tile and furniture in the breakfast room, but the guest room was already finished. I think they're going for the clean look with the bedding, but there isn't really a comforter, just a thick blanket that I can't imagine can be washed very easily. Other than that, the room is comfortable. Breakfast doesn't have much of a selection, and the internet was pretty slow most of the time. Also, the service is a little less than desirable. The front desk seemed to be overly concerned with answering phone calls rather than helping people actually at the counter. Check in took a long time, and at one point I saw 6 people waiting in line.

“Caveat Emptor” I just returned from an underwhelming experience at the Burnham, considering the glowing reviews it usually gets. Pros: Clean, comfortable bed, water was hot enough, L'Occitane en Provence soaps and shampoos, air conditioning worked well and was quiet, most of the furniture in fairly decent shape. Centrally located in the Loop across the street from Marshall Fields/Macy's, the forty bazillionth Old Navy store franchise, and surrounded by the Nordstom Rack and Walgreen's. Washington Red Line Station right outside, easy walk to Art Institute, Millennium Park, etc.. Building has an interesting history of restoration which is nicely documented on the first floor public area. Cons: I got the room via Priceline, which requests a non-smoking room but does not guarantee one - good thing, because I was stuck in a second floor smoking room (202). The air conditioner running full blast cleaned the air, but it sure stank when I first entered the room; otherwise, the hotel was sold out, so no change was possible. If you nudged the desk/table between the beds, the whole thing shook back and forth, I thought it was going to fall apart, the phone wasn't plugged in correctly, and the lamp wasn't plugged in at all. The ambient noise from the streets below might bother some people. The "complimentary Internet service" in the lobby is at the check-in desk - you stand next to the incoming clientele - no chair, not sure if it was attached to a printer. Not that this mattered, because the server only worked on the evening I arrived and not for the rest of my stay; they told me a serviceman was coming to fix it on the day I was leaving; it was obviously not a priority. Thanks to Tonya, one of the concierges, who allowed me to use her desk's computer to print out boarding passes for the trip home. And be forewarned, hotel guests have no priority at the attached Atwood Cafe - if you don't make dinner reservations you're toast. I did have breakfast the first morning I was there - greasy eggs and sausage, coffee and OJ for $19.50. The elevators in this building made the ones at the Ambassador East seem jet-propelled. Here being on the second floor was an advantage and the stairs worked fine. I wouldn't ever pay their advertised rates to stay here, and if I got the place via Priceline again, I'd sure be more proactive in ensuring satisfaction, instead of expecting the hotel to provide it outright. This place has a serious case of unwarranted smugness. Boutique shmoutique!

“Not quite what I expect from a Fairmont” Finished a 3-nighter at the Chicago Fairmont about a week ago. Overall, the experience was okay. Unless I need the stay credit, I don't think I'll stay at this hotel next time I go to Chicago. Drive-up: Taxi pulled up to the hotel. No doorman in sight. It was 3 pm. Perhaps all occupied with other guests. Don't know. Good thing I only had the one carry-on. Check-in: Line-up was not very long, but it took a while. No check-in packet was prepared ahead of time with my info, etc. on it. First time I experienced this at a Fairmont. Person was pleasant enough, though. Room: Used an upgrade coupon and supposed got an upgraded view room. Well, the view was still primarily the building next door, though I did catch a glimpse of the park. Furnishing looked fresh and new. Maybe a bit too "new," in the sense that it doesn't have the typical Fairmont flaire, but felt more like the normal upscale business hotel. Like perhaps a nicer version of a Westin. Pretty small room, though. Checked the floor map thing on the door, and it seemed to me that this FPC Plt was in one of the smaller rooms on the floor. Well, I was alone, so it's not that big a deal. But certainly the upgrade cert was wasted. Never was offered a further upgrade (not even for money), electronic or otherwise. Bathroom was good-sized. Surprisingly, not even mouthwash in the room. That's a first for me too. Housekeepers are friendly and nice. Coffeemaker is the Nespresso thing. Pretty cool. Large flat screen tv, probably too large, considering how small the room itself was. Closet was absolutely TINY. The Lobby Bar: Indifferent service. Very indifferent service. Breakfast at Aria's: Greeted with great apathy. But waiter was fine. Food was okay. Not great, but it's only pancakes and stuff. Never mind. I think I'd rather go to the Hyatt next door and pig out for the same price. Overall, not a bad experience. But really, there was a reason why I switched from a lot of business class hotel chains to Fairmont. The Chicago Fairmont would not justify such a switch in my mind. It's all about expectations, I suppose. Properties like San Francisco, Washington, heck, even the old Frontenacs and Chateau Lauriers, they have a certain character. This is greatly lacking in Chicago.

“Great location for Boston, Just OK, overpriced!” We stayed at this Courtyard by Marriott for 5 nights while attending a convention at the Hynes Center. It's in the heart of Boston's Back Bay and Copley Place which is central to all of Boston. The rooms are clean but do not offer the amenities that the other comparably priced hotels in the area do. Again this is an average/OK hotel by Courtyard standards, just that the price does not measure up to what is offered. For example, we stayed on a Sunday through Friday. We were charged $120 extra for the Wednesday and Thursday nights ($229 vs. $349 possibly because the Boston Marathon and opening day of Fenway). The restaurant is overpriced for breakfast and offers typically what you would get at a "complimentary breakfast offering". Lots of history to this hotel (over 100 years old). Not a bad place for Boston if you want to be "in the heart of things". Just be aware there are better places for the pricing and value. I'd look around at the other hotels in the Back Bay/Copley Place.

“Mix of good and not so good” Convenient Shuttle to and from LAX is the best thing, just like others said. Staff was helpful. Drop off and pick up area is NOT good so if you have a big old SUV to deal with, this might not be the place for you. The good -- staff, location by airport, shuttle, free breakfast that was pretty good. (Worth about $10 all in.) Price is OK. The rooms are pretty new with decent TV, small bathroom, OK beds The not so good -- slow elevators, funky parking, sketchy neighborhood at night, HARD pillows, run down hallways and carpet. The tub and shower worked poorly (plumbing loose). Because this place is a decent value for the area, it is probably going to be full a lot like it was for my stay. This means lots of tourists, football fans, odd-ball conventions, etc. If you want something more upscale in the area, there is a Holiday Inn very close and a Marriott just a block away on the other side of the blvd.

“Phoenix Airport” The hotel is close to airport....I stayed at hotel for 3 days while in Phoenix on Business. The hotel is a little dated and needs some upgrading. Room was clean but, the sink drained very slow. Wasn't too happy with the daily parking fee of $5 a day.

“Don't Be Scared Off...” I recently stayed at the Hudson, in spite of all the negative reviews I'd read on Trip Advisor. After finding a great promotional rate through the hotel's own website--the rate included overnight parking, which is usually an outrageous $50!--I booked a standard room. The hotel's lobby is beautiful, as are most of its common areas, and the rooms, though small, are aesthetically pleasing. I can't say that the rooms weren't small, but, you know, in almost any comparable hotel, you're not going to get any that are much larger without paying a good deal more. My room was appointed with a low queen bed, a small desk and chair, two huge wall mirrors, and three small lamps (there was no overhead lighting, which was annoying). The only place to really sit in comfort was the bed, and there was just barely enough room on either side of that to access the small end tables. The bathroom was likewise small, but clean. On that note, I'd like to issue a word of warning to anyone traveling with a companion, which involves the fact that the bathroom is separated from the rest of the room by a wall with a floor-length window, and might cause some issues for modest people (there were two thin curtains to cover it up, but they didn't really do much). The service at the hotel was not bad--certainly not the snobby, pretentious type encountered by many other reviewers--but I see how it would be easy to be intimidated by the young, hip staff. The Hudson Bar, by the way, looked to be peopled mostly with tacky types and wouldn't probably have held enough to interest most people outside the Schrager scene, but the Library Bar in the hotel was much more laid back and relaxing. In short: don't go here if you're looking for lots of space or wonderfully attentive, friendly service, but if you're young and don't mind being a little cramped in order to experience a trendy, unique hotel--and you get a good rate!--go for it.

“Not bad.” Here are my pros and cons... Pros: Clean, fairly new hotel; attentive staff and management; choice of pillow types; nice pool and hot tub; comfortable beds; quiet location. Cons: The location is not convenient to the downtown or Lake Travis area. It's about a 15 minute drive to town and 45 minute drive to the lake. The breakfast was adequate but to call it a "hot breakfast" is a bit of a stretch. One other annoyance was the multitude of big screen TV's all over the property. There are 6 in the breakfast room alone, one in each elevator, one outside of each elevator, a couple in the sitting areas. It was strange. Finally, I felt that the price we paid ($100) per night was a bit high given the type of hotel and it's inconvenient location. All in all not a bad place but do keep in mind the location.

“Early morning wake up!!” Stayed during our visited to Indy for the Van Halen concert. Room was nice but had a smoky smell. We found the beds very comfortable however I don't believe they were truly full size..My only complaint was that we had housekeeping knocking at 8:00am!!! I thought we had slept past check out!! Very annoying...We have never had that happen that early in the morning....

“Just Okay” We stayed here the week before Thanksgiving. I agree with some of the more recent reviews. The downside: The front desk staff was not nice - they seemed rushed and impersonal. THe exterior of the hotel was really shabby - it looks like something right out of the 1970's. I didn't even know they had a doorman! There always seemed to be employees standing around the lobby but no one ever bothered to help open doors or assist with luggage. We stayed on the 11th floor in tower A. The interior of the hotel is shabby. The carpets were old and the doors to the actual rooms were horrible. They stopped about 2-3 inches above the carpet so the light from the hallway comes into the room at night and you can hear people in the hallway like they are in the room. The also were steel/aluminum doors that look like the door to an elementary school - they were all dinged up and the bottom of all the doors on our floor looked like they had been kicked open by every vistor who ever stayed there. When we got to our room, the door looked so dirty and dingy that we were afraid to look in the room. The sink faucet never stayed on so when you turned on the water, it slowly got slower and slower until it stopped. Our room was very hot - we kept the windows open the whole time! We just couldn't seem to get the room cool enough. The upside: The room was alright - it was very large (we had a King-size bed). It was clean and the cleaning staff was really great. They were pleasant and nice, always said hello and left more than enough towels. We had no problem with the shower at all. The shower and toilet are separated from the sink so it was nice. Overall, there was nothing wrong with the room - it was just the impression we got from the appearance of the hallways, elevator and outside of the building that made it somehow seem dirty when it really wasn't. The location is great - close to subway (2 blocks), Central Park, 5th Avenue shopping. I recommend 9th avenue for eatting though. There are so many places to eat and great bars for watching sports. I would stay here again now that I know what to expect.

“Air tight concrete” The good. Nice newer property, staff is friendly, good customer service. The down side is the rooms are a bit small for a new property. The property is concrete and steel with sealed shut windows so although it is on the bay you get to breathe the same stale air inside the hotel. Hallways are already starting to smell musty. At minimum hotels should put windows in that have a vent of some sort for those of us that like a bit of fresh air? Easy parking in the garage that has a walkway to it. Skip the valet parking. Short walk to convention centre (10 minutes) about 15-20 to the gas lamp area where all the restaurants are. But to get to the gas lamp you have to go down the street a bit to a crosswalk and sometimes have to wait for trains to go by. They are building a walkway closer to the hotel but it is not completed. There is a sports bar on the lowest level on the bay front but you have to go outside the hotel to get to it, same with Starbucks, have to go out to get to it. The hotel restaurant was dead most of the time as the prices are the usual Hilton “you have got to be kidding” prices, wait staff needs some training on customer service and seem to disappear for extended periods. Room service prices are again a bit high but that is what you get when you stay at a Hilton. If you ship anything to or from the hotel for an event be prepared for the usual gouging from them for looking at your package. Suggesting shipping off site. Even the UPS store on the property slaps on a hotel fee.

“So-So all the way around....” This property is directly downtown, a high-rise hotel. No free parking, valet only for $22. Average sized rooms, typical of Courtyard. There doesn't seem to be alot to do around this area but I attribute that to downtown Houston. It does seem like there is a transient issue around the hotel, but I would not say there are any safety issues on the property. Otherwise, I rate this as an OK choice if you have to be logistically downtown. I was booked for 2 nights but chose to check out after one...

“Beautiful place, but with a snag in the reservation” First let me say that the rooms are spacious, clean and comfortable. the location is easy to get to and there are a few restaurants nearby. The breakfast was good and the service friendly. I had researched many of the hotels in search of a two-bedroom suite because I needed the space and the # of beds, but wanted all of us in one room. I made this reservation 2 months in advance. When I arrived, they said, "oh, we are short one 2-bedroom, and we can put you in two rooms." They were apologetic, but did not understand that I was very upset since this was the primary reason for coming to this hotel. Their original financial offer was not at all acceptable, since I had to split up my party and there were minors involved. They do not have adjoining rooms. We finally reached a "reasonable" compromise, but I was nervous the whole time. I cannot prove it, and although they said this "rarely" happens, I had the feeling that they had someone who wanted to extend their stay for a longer period than I was staying, and they made a management decision to keep that tenant and take their chances with me. They could have contacted me by telephone, but waited until I arrived at the hotel at 8:30 at night in order to inform me of the problem. They were aware, because they already had an offer ready.

“Great Location, Reasonable Hotel” The location of this hotel is simply not beatable. It is an easy two block walk to the tourist sites in Hollywood. Usually you would have to pay a lot more for a hotel with this location. Having said that, it is Hollywood and not really all that it is made out to be. Be very cautious walking in the Hollywood area at night. The hotel is clearly an older property and most of the styling is very old and dated. The carpets have about had it and everything has seen better days. However, the rooms were clean and comfortable and offered good wi-fi, microwaves and mini fridges. The room I stayed in had a shower that was very nice but no tub. Some of the rooms look out into a middle courtyard with the pool and all seemed to offer sliding glass doors. Breakfast was nothing to write home about as it was very basic, but it was free. Overall the hotel is worth the money as the location just cant be beat for the price I paid. I dont think you can expect a four or five star hotel when you are paying just over $100 a night in Hollywood. This is a perfectly good hotel as long as you realize it is a Days Inn and not the W. Set your expectations accordingly and you will be fine.

“Hotel Sax Needs to Turn on the LIghts” When the House of Blues underwent renovation and became the Hotel Sax (elongate that "a" when speaking to your children!) we were intrigued by the relatively reasonable rate and the chance to see the refurbishment. We saw what we could, given that "mood lighting" pervades the hallways and the rooms themselves. From the stark white of the lobby, where twenty-somethings with asymetrical haircuts waited companionably with chubby middle aged midwesterners, we ascended to a dim hallway where we used our car-key flashlight to insert the key in the lock. Nearby, prints of Old Masters hung benignly in curly red laquered frames. If you have ever seen the movie "Beetlejuice" you will have some sense of the post-modern frou-frou that defines the decor. The key feature of our smallish-but-adequate king room was a large wing chair upholstered in snakeskin vinyl. Next to it was a midnight-blue floor lamp with matching shade. Ah! Light! we thought, but how much light does a nearly-black lamp give you? The paisleyed wallpaper included a startling flat gray silouette of a chandelier. Oh that it were light-emitting. Bedside lighting next to the black padded headboard finally proved adequate and the bathroom was large and clean, although without an adequate surface on which to park a cosmetics bag. The king bed was comfortable and the flat screen TV worked fine. One look-see into the bar on the first floor left us shuddering at the updated cathouse decor -- enough red velvet to sink a ship. Edgy, yes, but it is all going to look merely dim and dated in a couple of years. We're still glad we went, and as others have commented, the location is great for restaurants.

“Ornate, terrific staff, great location, limited amenities” Hard to know how to rate this fairly. On one hand, this is one of the "grand old hotels", but also reminiscent of a Manhattan hotel. The room (828) was on a corner, limited view, but quiet. The bathroom was small, 48" wide, and the toilet blocked the door from opening all the way. Huge closet, but unnecessary unless you travel heavy and plan to stay a month. Windows of the old metal tilt out style and drafty, transmitting some outside noise. The lobby is two stories tall and impressive, the furniture is stylish but uncomfortable. At its core, this is an old building very well updated, but still limited by its core architecture. Parking ($48 daily) by valet is a necessity. It can be nerve wracking to pull up during busy times since it requires double parking on a busy street. It's worthwhile, though, because the brightly liveried doorman has a personality to match. San Francisco jsut is not parking friendly. There are a number of restaurants and high stores in the area, as well as Union Park. The restaurant next door, Scala's, connects to the lobby. It is pretty good, but there are many otehr options nearby, including Lily's Diner which is a 50's themed diner with moderate prices. It's a small thing, but there is no coffee in the room. I just hate having to deal with room service or restaurants when I first get up; but frankly, there isn't much room for a machine. If you want this style of hotel and need to be in the area, look also to the Westin Drake just down the street. If your here for the business district, I like the Palace better.

“Their website is DECEPTION” I have real mixed feelings about this place. The location is absolutely brilliant. Right in the heart of the downtown action; between the start of the powell line cable car and union square. The room was clean. BUT the linens are threadbare; the bathroom (shower that you cant turn in), loo and basin in a room the size of a shoebox; closet teeny tiny; no aircon, just a roof fan and open windows (smoke smells and noise central!). The price was excellent and we were really taken in by their impressive website = It is professional and the pictures are just wonderful. What they dont tell you (until you are actually in the lobby looking at a display of their PLANNED renovations) is that the "photos" on the website are prototypes / artist impressions for what they are planning to do next year! There is no breakfast incl, but at least they do have free wifi in all areas.

“Great Service” I stayed at this hotel while attending a conference at the Los Angeles Convention center. The hotel was definitely adequate. Clean, Safe, quiet at night. It filled all of my needs. It did not surpass any of my expectations, but if you are traveling for business it's a good choice. It is connected to a small "mall" shopping area which is convienent. What did impress me with this hotel was their customer service. The front desk was awesome! There was some confusion with my reservation and even though the hotel was sold out, they worked their magic and helped me out, and the people were friendly and helpful. The valet and roomservice employees were the same. Helpful and smiling.

“Still "W"orking it out” The new W downtown will have amazing views when the freedom tower is finished but for now it is next to a construction site with all the dust and noice thta conveys. Like other W's you take the elevator up to reception. The rooms are typical in that they are comfortable but kind of small. There is a BLTSteak in this hotel and while the food was pretty good it was expensive and there are far better steakhouses downtown. My overriding sense was the hotel was still on its maiden voyage and was working out the kinks. I am sure given time thta this property will meet the standards the brand usually delivers

“Centrally located and full of History.” Stayed at the Algonquin for one night during a freind's Bachelorette. The hotel is right next to Times Square. A bit of a fiasco to travel to if you're driving. But if you're looking for an authentic NYC experience, you can't go wrong here. We valeted our car for $50/night next to the hotel. Bellman was so helpful and friendly. Staff was great too. We checked into our tiny room and were happy with the decor, linens and quality. I loved that the hotel had an old time feel about it but be warned that the rooms are tiny. Even for NYC standards. 3 of us shared a room and I brought an airbed that I squeezed next to the door that night. The elevators are old too and take a while to arrive. But the unique charm and old fashioned tranditions, make this a special place.

“Overpriced Hotel Next to Convention Center” Stayed there in December last year for CFA exams. If you just go to Chicago for business in McCormick Center then it'll be your best choice. But if you also want to see around the city there might be some trouble. Public transportation only includes buses but no subway there, and you'll have to grab a taxi. Food is not so good so you better go to MCD near the hotel. And the waitress in the restaurant was weird and didn't smile for the whole lunch. Didn't know what was going on with her and that definitely made my stay less cheerful there.

“Solid stay. Nothing special, though.” I flew into Dallas on business and chose the Hilton Garden Inn because it was near the airport. There was nothing bad about my stay, but there was nothing special about it, either. It was average in the most true sense of the word. I was checked in promptly. My room was clean. If you need a place near the airport, this place is fine.

“Good services shame about the basic rooms” This hotel is close to the White House. And you can hear road traffic noises from the window. Room has rather basic settings. It was very average. But the customer service are very good. They have a members lounge with very basic complementary breakfast for members.

“Great location Satisfactory hotel” We chose this property for its location and wanted a good value property for a weekend break and were not disappointed. Our room was good size and quiet location as requested-Its an older hotel-I stayed here when it was a Howard Johnson maybe 25+ years ago and it shows its age. The good things were the beds and staff. I slept very well-the staff were very helpful. Less good was the tiny bathroom-everything worked fine but it is small. Breakfast was the usual hotel fare and met out expectations So would I recommend this hotel-yes if you want a modest price but a great location-front rooms might be noisy as you are above the Subway line and 8th is a busy Avenue.

“Adequate...at the moment” The Distrikt Hotel is tall & skinny - literally, a very skinny building that rises about 30 floors above the Port Authority building in Midtown. It's new - and so it's clean at the moment. It's also adjacent to three other new and more upscale hotels. Literally, it's like they're all glued together along West 40th, with the Distrikt being the skinny little sibling of the four. The good news: the Distrikt is new and clean, and its promotional pricing is attractive. The staff is very friendly and helpful. My room - a Deluxe King - was fairly roomy by NYC standards, but would be a standard room in a hotel is a different city. Free Internet is nice. (I'm using it now.) The TVs are smallish, but high-def, which is also nice. The bad news: well, there isn't any terrible news, but you may find it useful to know: - There are no 4 star amenities here. The fitness facility is off site. The lobby is tiny. The computer/business area is literally a tiny strip of 3 or 4 machines by the lobby windows. - The Distrikt is a "boutique hotel" only if "boutique" means "small". In my mind, "boutique" means having a unique style or ambience...but the Distrikt feels fairly standard, IMO. The room furnishings are pretty simple. - The location isn't great. West 40th between 8th and 9th seems a bit transient, although I wasn't bothered or harrassed during my 5 night stay. It's relatively easy to get to Times Square and the Broadway theaters. It's very easy to get to one of the main subway stations (A train). Overall, I'd call the Distrikt average. During its promotional pricing phase, it's a reasonable place to stay. But in a year or two, when it no longer needs to promote itself, I'd suggest looking around.

“Expected more.” I really wanted to love the W. we were having a mini in town vacation while floors sanded. Had a suite. Was plenty big, with a big terrace, but many things didn't quite work. Door to terrace wouldn't lock. A molding tile missing in bath. Door to room stuck. Carpet not perfectly clean. The pool area was cool, but really for twenty something's. Not one comfortable chair in the pool area to read. Recliners had no settings and chair backs too low. Room service breakfast was awful. Dry omelet, pasty pastries and expensive. Bell guys for parking were great. Very easy and fast. Spa was very nice, if a tad expensive for Dallas. Rooms that look at city are good. Suite 315 costs less than terrace suites and has a big terrace, although the furniture on it is not comfortable. More for posing on than using.

“OK stay” Stayed here the night before a morning flight out. Booked a AAA rate of $69 a night. Dropped my rental car off at Thrifty and the Pear Tree shuttle came to the car rental location and picked me up which was nice. TIP - while construction continues at SAT - do not rent from Thrifty - they are off property and IMPOSSIBLE to find - and slow- both picking up and dropping off - and gave me a car with no gas...I could go on and on. The Pear Tree was ok for the price - older, not very comfortable beds, thin thin towels. Did have a computer in the lobby free to use to print out boarding passes. Also has a.m. breakfast but I took off too early to have any. Quick morning shuttle to the airport.

“Great location, decent price - there are better properties nearby.” We stayed at the Chancellor for a night based on good reviews on here. It's a smallish, 15 story hotel at Union Square. Room rate was good - competitive for the smaller, independent hotels in this area of San Francisco. There is terrific food and shopping nearby and the hotel had a package that included off-site parking in the room rate. It is clearly an older property - the rooms and common areas reflect the age of the hotel. Our room was small, but nicely furnished. Good flat screen TV, comfy chairs, even a window that opened a little. Bathroom was very, very small - immaculately clean with nice toiletry products. The king bed was disappointing - two twins put together with one of those 'joiner' strips - boo. You should at least get an excellent quality bed at this price point, but this one was lacking. There are some excellent and recently renovated properties in the same neighborhood that are a lot better value even at a slightly higher price. The Chancellor is definitely not in the top echelon when it comes to delivering excellent value for dollar spent - it's a budget hotel that looks and feels like a budget hotel. There are others that provide much better accommodations for only a little more money.

“The location is its strengh” We have family in the area so have stayed in quite a few of the local places. This was our first visit to the Inn at Venice Beach. We were hoping it would be a little more like an "inn" than a generic place but while we had no major problems with the place, it was just about as generic as staying at any of the mid-range chains. Our room was an okay size and very clean. There was a tiny balcony overlooking a side street which was fine. The bathroom was very small but clean. Our sink did make some odd noises at various times when it wasn't even in use. We told them about this at check-out, so hopefully it will be fixed. They offer a continental breakfast which was almost exactly what you'd find at any of the chains. It would have been nice if they'd had a bowl of cut up fruit instead of just a few whole pieces. There is a little courtyard area where you can eat and that was pleasant. I would stay there again if the rate was good but I didn't feel it was worth any extra money.

“Value for money, yet no extraordinary things here for savvy travellers” A frequent traveler to New York, I still have not found my hotel yet. A friend recommended this hotel to me, advertising it as a hotel where you generally get good rates for decent quality. And that is what it is. The hotel is located at the upper west side, so depending on where you have to be this could be a bit far if you like to go out or shop in SoHo, or other lower Manhattan places. Yet it is in a very attractive neighborhood, close to Amsterdam and Broadway, Columbus Circle and Lincoln Center. Be picky in choosing your room. The hotel seems to largely cater to a tourist audience and is not much of a business hotel. However, I was served very well when I got a larger suite after I complained about the room I stayed in, as the curtains were hanging half way, not closing properly, the bathroom kind of small. The other room they put me in (make sure you are not having a room opposite the elevators they make way too much noise!) was adequate and spacious, yes, spacious, and that for New York! Two queen size comfortable beds, a working place (yet a TV that was standing about 8 meters from the bed on the table which the hotel was so kind as to replace), so you need very sharp eyes). A relatively spacious bathroom, too. Do not expect a contemporary hotel(room) it is rather dark, it can leave you a bit of a depressing impression when you first come in, due to the dark colors of the interior "design", where the color brown dominates. Do not expect any views from your window, there aren't any. A good choice when you are a tourist, spending most of your time outside, as the room is what it is: comfortable beds, large bathroom, service is good, be it that there is no breakfast, no restaurant but there is a very good breakfast restaurant just opposite the hotel . The hotel is glad to connect you to the outside restaurant which brings you your order to your room, (pay cash for the delivery). The price-quality ration of this hotel is very good, the only thing is the ridiculous habit NY and other major cities have introduced of having the wildest price swings for your room depending on the dates. In general good value for your bucks but do not have too many high expectations if you are a spoiled hotel guest.

“Let down” This hotel needs renovations and the staff was not very helpful except for Russell at the front desk. Self-Parking is $15 a day- not bad, buts its a short walk to your car. The hotel bar is open weird hours and the bartender was not the friendliest. Things to check: -When checking in, please check the bathroom. We checked in, dropped our luggage and left for an appointment. Upon our return I showered and as I was drying my hair I noticed spots on the wall that was either dried blood or old rusty water stains. This grossed me out and is something that should have been cleaned. Upon further inspection, I looked and noticed black hairs on the walls. It seems the maid wiped the counter and then wiped the walls with the same towel. -There is a note that says leave towels on the floor if you want new towels. We left two towels on the floor thinking we would get two back. No, we had to call to get them to bring us up one towel since they only left one in the room. They did bring it up fast and provided a follow up call. -The sleep number bed is a joke because it did not work. -Make sure you don't forget anything. We left in a rush and realized we left a bag in the room. I called within a couple hours of checking out and was told the bag should still be in the room since the room was not cleaned yesterday. I was told I would receive an immediate follow up and never did. I called back today and am getting a run around. I told the hotel exactly where the bag is in front of the desk, but I’m guessing someone took the brand new in tissue paper banana republic pants. One tip...spend a couple dollars more and go to the Hotel Monaco a block down. Its worth it. If the hotel was renovated and taken better care of, this would be a great hotel.

“Average, expensive, older boutique hotel” My wife and I stayed here for one night after returning to NYC for a cruise. We normally stay at The Michelangelo but I wanted to give another hotel a try. I regret that this hotel is not as good, nor worth the price, of several others at which we have recently stayed. Although it wasn't "bad", I won't stay here again, simply because there are better, similarly priced and located hotels. We found the lobby small, narrow and cramped, although nicely appointed. The concierge and front desk staff were more aloof than friendly, although they were professional and efficient. The elevators are old, very small, and slow. The hotel itself is rather narrow, so the upstairs hallways are short, dark, and narrow. The room door-locks were very modern - you need only place your key near the flat sensor to open the lock - a nice touch. The furnishings in our one-room suite were older but serviceable. There were very modern fixtures in the bathroom and mini-bar area and the TV's were flat screens of good quality. The complementary continental breakfast in the attached Abboccato Restorante was decent - good coffee, fresh fruits, bagels, muffins, and breads. The service was average and unenthusiastic. It isn't a bad place to stay, just that I have stayed at better for the same price or less, that are more modern, friendly, and slightly larger.

“Obviously, luck has a lot to do with it” Having read the other reviews of this hotel, I feel we were unlucky... I accompanied my husband on a business trip last week. We arrived to a charming welcome and told we had been upgraded and put on the 7th floor instead of the 3rd. Well, it was late at night, so what did we know about it until the morning when I found both windows (a corner room) looked out on dark walls. I dreaded to think what the third floor was like. Then after four nights we unexpectedly had to stay on one more night. I had vacated the room early, but at 1pm (their usual checkout time) I was told by phone the new room was ready for me and my bags were in it. Not quite true. Although the usual check in time is 3pm, my room wasn't ready until 5pm. And it was on the 3rd floor (also dark but not noticeably worse than the 7th). When I asked to check out the next day at 3pm, the answer was a great big 'No'. I didn't feel very loved after spending several thousand dollars with them over the week. Basically this hotel is beloved of anyone with a room or suite on one of the upper floors, and rightly so, because if the room is right, everything else follows. Both our rooms were large by New York standards, but size isn't everything. Service was great and the location is fine, but give me the Four Seasons every time. Oh, and charging for internet access in the 21st Century???

“Pretty, but loud” Super nice staff, great gas lamp location.... The bed was very comfortable.... but omg the noise! I realize this is the hard rock, but screaming girls in the halls and drunk loudness at 2am didn't make for a great stay. Ask for a room not facing the pool since there are night time parties with loud music on weekends. The suites looked nice and quieter. The doors provided no insulation whatsoever to the hallway noise. Even neighors doors closing and people talking at normal levels, it sounded like there was no door on my room at all. Bathroom lighting was dreadful at the mirror. Great shower though with two heads, one on the ceiling. It's a good property, but I should have known... I'm too old for this place. I moved to the Andaz after two nights.

“Good, but Not for a Kimpton” I stayed at the Allegro for two nights in early September. I've stayed at the Monaco and the Burnham--other Kimpton properties--and this is probably the shabbiest of the three (despite the recent renovation). It's an old building so the rooms are small. The bathroom, in particular, was very small for a hotel bathroom. (Although I thought mine was wisely done--a pocket door, I think.) Nice Aveda bath products. Free NY Times delievered every morning. I love the free wine reception. And they also have free wireless. I lived in Chicago for 8 years so I feel comfortable saying that the Allegro--while decently located if your business is in The Loop or if you're there for theatre--is not super-convenient to lots of places. (Although it is convenient for all the restaurants on Randolph Street. Take a cab though.) I like The Monaco's location because it's right at the foot of Michigan Avenue. I like The Burham because it's right across from Marshall Fields and you can grab any of the buses up State Street. This is a good hotel, don't get me wrong. You'll be very comfortable here. But go expecting a small room. And check The Monaco and Burnham first.

“Excellent location, adequate accomodations” This was my second stay at Radisson Lexington, the first time was perhaps in January 2010 when I got an exceptional deal which included breakfast and parking for $150/night. I wasn't impressed with the hotel first time around, so I didn't have any intentions of returning to this property. However, a last minute trip to NYC with the need to stay nearby in Midtown resulted in my redeeming a free-night certificate for a room here (which otherwise would have been over $350/night during this time). Even though the room was "free", as a Club Carlson member I got an upgrade to a "large" (by NYC standards) room (#1102) with two full/double Sleep Number beds, a sofabed and two bathrooms! The stay was only for one night, but we were appreciative of the upgrade even though like most NYC visitors, we were only in the room to sleep or to change clothing. Like the first visit two years prior, we realize that this is an older building and an older hotel. Bathrooms at this price point could stand a renovation but were completely functional. Carpeting could have been vacuumed better before our arrival (if it was done at all). Housekeeping skills were just adequate and marginally acceptable. Rooms really need a deep cleaning which probably hasn't been done since the last renovation. TV remote did not work. No coffee maker in room for those who require coffee upon waking (Starbucks in lobby, though). My request for a 1-hour late check-out couldn't be granted (probably would not have been a problem in a smaller, standard room), but I made the 30 minute extension I was granted work well enough for my schedule. Would I stay here again? I didn't think I would after visit #1, so who knows about the future. At the right price, the place is adequate. But I know that there are both newer and cleaner options often available at competitive prices. The location is great for Midtown, but be prepared for a lot of street noise depending upon your street exposure. Both times at this hotel and I did not encounter any bedbugs (I checked out the beds and sofa thoroughly upon arrival)--in NYC these day that's about as much as you can ask for in hotel (no guarantee other rooms are the same). Hotel is frequented regularly by flight crews--probably a significant source of steady revenue for a large, older hotel.

“Fair” Stayed here on business for 2 nights recently. A few comments. Location - very central to downtown and historic locations Service - fair at best. Desk help was surley. Room - Beds were very comfortable. Room was very quiet. Appointments dated and tired. Bathroom was odd - the sink was at child height. The flooring looked new, but the shower tiles were right out of the '70s, including the mildewed grout. When I went to fill the in-room coffee machine, the coffee packet from the previous guest was still in the machine. Restaurant - breakfast only, but the buffet was very good. Food good, service very good. There are better hotels in this area.

“Great Location, Needs a little TLC” If you have to be in the medical center area for a reason, this is the perfect location. Service was great, only reason it got 3 stars was our ceiling looked like it had gotten wet at some point, and the texture was peeling off

“Careful what you wish for...” I rubbed the Priceline genie bottle. My wish: a 3 or more star hotel near Times Square for $200/night. My wish was granted and I was awarded with 2 nights at this hotel. The "rack rate" for this hotel is about $200/night, so Priceline didn't do me any favors this time. Moreover, I think William Shatner and I need to discuss the definition of a 3 star hotel. I don't think this hotel qualifies. It is fine for what it is, a decent hotel for $200/night at Times Square. Given that the other hotels in the area go for $300 and up, one should not be surprised that this is not the Ritz. It is a bit frayed around the edges, but overall it works fine. Pluses: location, location, location. Front desk staff were friendly and helpful in the little ways that can set the good apart from the bad. They seemed to actually care. Negatives: not the cleanest hotel experience you will ever have. Hot water took about 5 minutes to make it up to my 6th floor shower and the in-room internet was a very weak connection indeed.

“Nice Staff, But Some Problems” We stayed at the Mission Valley Sheraton for two nights after booking it for $105/night on Priceline. Although the staff was uniformly helpful and friendly, and none of what happened was their fault, we had a very troubled stay and probably would not stay there again. First of all, I don't care for the Mission Valley location. It is conveniently located to a lot of attractions, but I find it very sterile and prefer to stay in the Del Mar area, or even downtown. The worst thing that happened was when we exited a side door to go get dinner one night, a huge snake was coiled right next to the door. It seemed to be almost 5 feet long. This of course was not the hotel's fault, but I have no idea whether this is a common occurrence or not (probably not). There are hills around the property and I guess there are snakes in the hills. Anyway, suffice it to say I almost had a heart attack! Also, we had to call housekeeping three times - once the toilet wasn't working, once there was no hairdryer in the room, and once to have the batteries in the remote control replaced. That's a lot of calls to housekeeping for a two-night stay. I don't want to put anyone off from this hotel, because the odds are you would have a nice stay. The hotel itself and the room was nice and everything that happened to us probably would not happen to you.

“Worms in the pool; 3 rooms in 3 days” It took a while to get to writing this review. First, let me start by saying that the Hyatt (after our return and after I sent a letter), really made things right for us in the end but... I had planned this trip as a girls getaway for my three daughters (ages 13, 10 and 6 at the time). We arrived on a rare day when it was raining in San Antonio. The pay-per-view movies weren't working and the tv kept losing its signal. The kids were getting more than a little stir crazy. I called down to the front desk and they told me they would send a signal and it would take a few hours to be fixed. After a few hours, we were still waiting (it was POURING outside; to get to the game room, spa or fitness room you have to go outside which is just weird). I called again, maintenance came up; we sat there akwardly while they fiddled with some cords. Nothing. Said it would be fixed later. Finally someone from maintenance said they were surprised we were given this room because the tv never works right...hmmmm. We went out to dinner and were told the issue had been fixed when we came back - a pay per view movie was even on. Next morning - no tv. We were moved pretty quickly but had to pack everything up and tip the bellman again. Went to the gorgeous pool - lazy river, volleyball net, basketball net. My daughters then said there were worms on the bottom of the pool and held up HANDFULS of worms! I couldn't believe it. Apparently the rain had washed them into the pool by the bucketful. It was so incredibly gross. The hottub was freezing and had worms too. But, kids being kids, they didn't mind (and I tried not to look). I signed the girls up for the kids club, had a beer and planned to take a nice, warm bath in our new room. When I got there....there was water raining from the ceiling in the bathroom. Seriously. I called maintenance and they came up. I sat there akwardly in my bathing suit for an hour or so while men trooped in and out making a hole in the ceiling. The supervisor was extremely nice though and actually apologized for my inconvenience (which goes a long way with me). Guess what? We were moved again. Although it was supposed to be an upgrade, it looked the same and we no longer had a balcony. It didn't really matter, though because the tv and shower worked. The facilities supervisor sent up milk and cookies for the kids which was nice. When I complained at check out, they took a movie we were never able to watch off my bill and never apologized or anything. As I said, the manager did contact us and give us Hyatt rewards points after we returned home. We laugh about this stay now and I can't imagine anyone will have the same experience we did. I was told that this resort just isn't "on" anytime other than in the summer. Rudy's bbq around the corner was a huge hit with us and we really enjoyed the Riverwalk and our stay at the Watermark in San Antonio. The Hyatt rooms are fairly dated and not very lux but the property is beautiful in the right weather and the family-friendly activities sounded great (most were not held because of the storm but s'mores was fun).

“Disappointed. Not up to Marriott standards.” Checked into the Marriott on Saturday, October 24th. No king bed available despite my Marriott rewards status and my reservation for a king bed. Finally found us a king bed in the "business wing" which required many steps and no elevator. Room was fine. Very average to below-average for a Marriott. No wireless in room, no ethernet cable and when I called for one, was told there would be a wait. Bartender at hotel bar (Sam) was less than friendly. Menu for room service and hotel restaurant was barely adequate. Was in town for the Marine Corps Marathon and was very disappointed when we tried to order spaghetti for room service the night before the marathon and was told, "Oh, we're out of spaghetti sauce." I said, "So you have a hotel full of marathoners and you don't have spaghetti sauce?" Woman on room service line said, "Yes, we've been out since yesterday." So I got a bowl of plain pasta and my husband got a small personal pizza. Personal pizza appeared to be a frozen microwave pizza and tasted that way. Overall, the only highlight of the hotel was the extremely friendly "Lobby Ambassador" Joe. He was kind, helpful and very friendly. Rest of the staff was eh, barely acceptable. Disappointed for a Marriott.

“Convenient, great concierge but needs a little updating” Hotel staff was extremely helpful. The concierge made some excellent recommendations for dinner. Rosebuds and RL. Both were great. RL was fantatic. We had a larger room, but it needed some updates. It looks a little worn, but it was clean and convenient. Don't go to the contemporary art museum, waste of time. But the See It All city tour was very good and it was recommended by the hotel. The breakfast French Toast was excellent and again wonderful wait staff.

“Spacious suite, debateable location, poor service” This is a slightly dated property, but has been updated with some newer furniture, so the rooms in general are pretty decent, the suite is very spacious. Not sure if the living room has a sofa bed but if it does have one, then I would say it would be a good deal for a family. I believe all the rooms come with an open balcony, mine did (which is a nice touch) and decent size kitchenette with microwave/fridge (no stove). The rooms are not as sparkly as the professionally shot pictures show. The location is okay I guess and the views may be nice depending on which floor you are on and which way your room is facing - I wouldn't count on it. I was supposed to be on a 20-something floor, which was smoking and the only non-smoking room they could find for me was on the 9th floor. Views not that exciting! The choices of nice restaurants within walking distance are poor. The one Chinese place (Asia on the Parkway) that delivers is pricey and the quality of the food is low. Other choices are TGIF (go figure!), no nice steak/seafood place. The service was really disappointing, first it took for ever to check me in, then I was booked in a smoking room supposedly by my booking tool (which has never happened in the past), then when I asked for the free water for Hilton silver members, I was told it's not in my profile and I need to go online and update it (again never happened in the past, always get the water sometimes without asking at all Hilton chains). They do offer free made to order breakfast (location of the restaurant is inconvenient, 2nd floor) so if you are up there with your luggage now you have to wait for the elevator for just one floor. They also offered managers reception - so free drinks I guess? I didn't take advantage of it. The snacks are no good though (chips and pretzels). Parking: No self parking, valet only @$45 Yup! So make sure you factor that into your cost.

“Not that impressed, especially for the price” You really can't beat the location of the hotel... It's literally next to Fanueil Hall. However, this was a pricey hotel. Our room got no sunlight and stares into a wall of another building. Staff was not very helpful and one of the receptionist has a shilling voice. It would have been an ok hotel if it wants 300 dollars a night - really not worth it at all.

“Another attempt at remodeling” An OK hotel. Another less than effectively remodelled Holiday Inn - stained carpets, fixtures that don't quite fit, and the-always-present noisy window air conditioner. As with all remodeled HI's there's only one outlet at the desk, half used by the lamp.

“Neat base in the Big Apple” We found ourselves looking for a hotel in New York with only one day's notice and spent hours trawling the internet for a room for the night that had it's own bathroom, wasn't totally full and wouldn't make Donald Trump wince - it took a long time to find the Sohotel but it was a good thing we did. It was $230 a night - a decent rate - and got us a room that looked very chic with a fine bathroom and a view of a brick wall (which we found funny!). There was no breakfast provided but we were able to grab a coffee before we hit the streets. The hotel was clean and there was a 24-hour reception which was very helpful. Service was friendly and location was great.

“Don't get caught on the hide-a-bed!” My backs killing me as I write this! Admittedly, we were supposed to check in on Thursday. We were renting a block of 10+ rooms for the Equine Show (everyone else was there on Thursday). We showed up on Saturday and the only room left (according to the Front Desk) was a suite without a bed. We slept on the queen sized hide a bed. The manager offered a food/beverage credit, free Internet, and reduced parking which did smooth us over (somewhat). We asked housekeeping to make up the hide a bed, the linens were lousy and thin and they only brought one pillow! My advice to the hotel is to not offer that room. It's a nice room but the "bed" is a joke. I didn't like the front desk, but the rest of the staff was awesome! Loved the girls at the lounge. Guacamole was yummy!

“Strength is its location, a pleasant place to stay” I stayed here two nights during my visit to the University of Texas at Houston, it was a very convenient and short walk to the university. If you are visiting this or any other institutions in the medical area, that is a good reason to stay here. Otherwise, the immediate area is not that interesting, busy with traffic during weekdays, very quite on weekends. The hotel and my room were fine, clean, pleasant appearance. The service was friendly and excellent; when I merely inquired about the cost of internet access on check in, the person gave me free internet access. The gym facilities were nice, a reasonable set of weight machines and aerobics equipment (multiple treadmills, elliptical machines, cycles). Overall, a positive experience, a quite room, a good nights rest, I would certainly stay here again if in this area for business.

“No frills, good location, friendly staff, quirky little room!” We went to NYC to see and experience NYC, not to stay in a 5 star hotel. We wanted a safe, clean, well located hotel. That's exactly what we got! It was quirky and had little frills (except the bathroom seemed recently remodeled and was great!-but they only gave us two bath towels). The staff was nice and helpful (we were able to leave our bags there before and after check out). Our view was into the neighbors apartment - which was amusing! Our room was very small - my husband was able to touch both walls when his arms were stretched out! It just added to our wonderful trip to NYC. We'd stay there again!

“A typical chain hotel” My husband and I stayed at this hotel during a business trip for one night last May. The hotel definitely needs a facelift but it still provides guest’s basic needs just nice. The bed isn’t bad at all, the bathroom worked okay but the room service foods tasted nothing special. If you’re looking for a place to stay where you want to stay close from Manhattan crowds (Fifth Av, Time Square & Central Park), this might be a good place for you. don’t forget to taste the infamous gyro street vendor parked beside the hotel every night after 6PM! One of the best foods I’ve tried in NY only for $4 (so long Gray’s Papaya!)

“Very close to Airport nice bed” Checking was easy and completed in 20 mins. The best part of all holiday inn are the complimentry internet and nice and comfy bed which I found here too. Parking was expensive but considering about proximety to LAX, it was fine.

“Fire Station next door can be very annoying” Our family just returned from a holiday weekend in downtown Chicago. We've been to Chicago at least five times and really enjoy visiting this wonderful city. We booked our stay at the Hampton after reading the reviews, We got a great rate including parking for the holiday weekend. Upon our arrival I asked for a suite upgrade and it was handled wonderfully by the staff. Overall we were happy with the room even though it could have used some upgrades. We found the staff very helpful during our stay and the breakfast offered each morning was decent. The proximity of the hotel to Michigan Ave. was pretty good, about 3 blocks away. For the price we found the hotel to be in a good loaction with good access to all of the attractions via walking, bus, taxi or the subway. Ok here is our BIG GRIPE about this hotel which will prevent us from staying here again. Directly across the street from the hotel is a working FIRE STATION. If you've ever been to Chicago you know how frequent these vehicles operate. Anyway, throughout the night (and average of 3 times per night) the trucks would roll-out of the station blasting their sirens and horn. I can't begin to explain how loud this was during the middle of the night. There is no way one could not be awaken by this noise. I don't at all blame the firemen as they are doing their jobs, but again it's not the best combination tom have a hotel next door to a firestation. Just be aware if you do stay here you're going to have to deal with the extreme noise from the fire trucks across the street!

“Classic but Cramped” Stayed three nights related to the RIMS conference in Boston. Location was good and had what you would expect from a historic hotel, quality of furnishings, TV and bedding you would expect from an Omni. My main complaint was that room was very small and bath was tiny. This was fine for one business traveler gone most of the day but would have been crowded with two people for a weekend. Service was good and room service ordered came in a timely manner and was tasty.

“A bit wierd” Bouyed up by my previous Kimpton experience (in Philadelphia) I booked into the Helix for a one night stay on business. Firstly, I don't know DC's geography very well, but it feels a bit remote. Maybe everything in DC is remote. Secondly, there was only one guy doing check-in and he was on the phone - and when he got off the phone, despite having acknowledged my presence, he wandered off. I was less than impressed. I found the room a bit wierd. They have tried to be funky in a 1970s way - a lot of lime green, orange etc. The bed is curtained off in a little alcove and there are no doors on the wardrobe, just a psychedelic curtain. Overall the room size was fine and it had all the things I needed - internet, TV, bathroom, bed etc. But it was definitely at the wierd end of the spectrum for me. I didn't eat in the restaurant but the bar looked lively and as usual they had the 5pm happy hour where they offer wine & sangria gratis for an hour which is a nice touch. I doubt I will be back.

“Nice hotel, just noisy” I spent two nights here on business and have mixed feelings about the place. Overall, it's nice -- very clean, the rooms are well-appointed, and it's close to the airport, downtown, shopping, beaches, and anything else you would want in San Diego. However, the proximity to the airport means that sleeping in is a problem, because a bank of flights departs starting at about 6am, and at least on the side of the hotel I was on, it was pretty loud. And if you want to sit outside near the pool and have a conversation, you'll be pausing periodically to let the planes pass overhead. The rooms are also rather small and cramped -- it would have felt crowded with another person. My room on the third floor had a rooftop view and the housekeeping room was nearby, so I heard lots of noise from that also. And there was only one small elevator at my end of the hotel. I'm not sure if there was another one at the other end, but it did get slow and crowded in the morning when people were checking out. Most of the staff was friendly, and the shuttle to the airport is free and quick. It's an okay place to stay if you need convenience, are traveling with one or maybe two people, and aren't going to be there for more than a night or two.

“Odd but cool and good” The lobby is big with a big bar. The floors have a strange floor plan. The rooms are standard, clean and have the typical modern amenities. I didn't have any issues at all during my brief stay and I would have no problem recommending this hotel to interested parties. An interesting note would be the amount of weddings this place holds seems constant!

“A good property that misses on the finer points, with poor work area” PROPERTY: This is an older property which has been well cared for and still looks fairly current. It has fresh bright colors which help it look newer than it is. I stayed in room 602 which was a double/double. ROOM: The room was clean and the décor looked fresh and bright. The room had its own, window mounted A/C unit which worked fine. The furniture was in good condition and had a 32” flat screen. The bathroom was large and clean. The ironing board cover was heavily soiled and embarrassing. I actually put a towel over the ironing board to prevent staining my shirt when I ironed it. BEDDING: The bed was fair and had good pillows. The second bed nearest the window had a visible “bow” in the center which I did not use. The bedding was good, but not of the same quality as a other mid range hotels like Hampton. WORK AREA: LaQuinta is obviously not trying to cater to the business traveler, which is OK if you can get enough recreational business. The work table is small, the mismatched chairs are useless for laptop work. There was only ONE HALF of an outlet for laptops and electronics which was troublesome for working. The staff was friendly, especially the shuttle driver who had only been on the job 3 days! Great job. RATING: Overall I would give the property an 78/100 and 85/100 for value. I would consider staying here again, but would also look at other properties nearby. PROS: price, location to airport, good overall condition CONS: HORRIBLE work area.

“Great location and service but Dirty rooms” I am a Hilton Honors member and this Embassy is definitely not up to Hilton standards. The service was very good, we used the hotel shuttle a few times and the front desk manager and shuttle driver were very nice and polite. Once we arrived at the Galleria, we tried to tip the driver and he declined saying he was a manager. I called when we were done and they arrived to pick us up within just a few minutes. The inside of the hotel is nice, swans are beautiful and setting is park-like. Our room was icky. The shower had mildew on the walls and some of it looked like it was even covered up by caulk. Brewed coffee was left in the pot. When we got ready to go to bed, we pulled back the sheets and they had spots and stains. (looked like blood!) We called the front desk and told them our sheets were dirty and they sent someone right up to change them. We have always been happy with Embassy but this location needs some new management in Housekeeping. Ick!

“Okay for one night” Stayed at this hotel in early October with several business colleagues. The hotel is very close to Seattle airport and offers complimentary transportation. Check in was pretty smooth and the front desk staff are pleasant. The hotel itself is certainly nothing special. The rooms are small, and the shower appears to be nothing more than a stall, however, once you open the door there is a small bathtub. The beds aren't that comfortable, and the pillows are really really tiny (very odd!). Quite cramped however. There is no complimentary wireless internet here ($6.95 charge) which is disappointing. There is a tiny "business centre" on the 3rd floor which is complimentary. For me, this hotel might be okay if you are stuck at the airport overnight, and will be leaving first thing the next morning. Don't consider this however, for longer than an overnight stay, and only if you need to be right near the airport.

“Fairmont only fair.” We checked in Labor Day afternoon. Just to stay overnight was $209 not including the parking fee and taxes, which brought the total to almost $300.00. While the room was spacious and clean, it was just okay. And, we only had luke warm water for a shower after checking in. Something about maintenance cleaning out the system. Since the busy holiday weekend was over, the hotel was like a tomb. We saw maybe a handful of other guests the entire 24 hour period. Then what's with the exorbitant rate? It was nice to be within a couple blocks of Original Joe's, but I'll stay elsewhere next time.

“Let's see what happens when the renovations are done” Stayed three nights at the Doubletree in February 2005. The room was clean and the bed very comforatable, but they squeezed a king bed into a room too narrow for it, and the desk chair filled the space between the desk and the bed so you have to climb around it to get to the window. A lot of the hotel was under renovation: the "business center" was closed, and a couple of other common rooms on the first floor were blocked off. I was not able to get internet access in my room, and when I called the internet provider at the hotel was told to go to the business center to make sure the problem was not with my computer. When I called back to tell them there was no business center, they insisted there was one. In any case, it turns out the internet was down for two days hotel-wide. The hotel failed to inform people of this, which was the only service failure I experienced. I am sure a lot of guests wasted a lot of time on the phone with the internet provider who wouldn't have if they'd been told that the problem was hotel-wide. It was clear that they were still working out some issues in the rebranding from the old Loew's brand to the Doubletree, so I'll try again. It's very convenient to the Park Avenue business and has great potential

“Luxe hotel? Not sure...” Value: Average boutique hotel in West Hollywood/Westwood area. I stayed here for work and felt the accommodations were average. Not thrilled about the valet parking. Location: Hard to locate the place from the street. Right off the exit for 405. Centrally located, minutes from everywhere. Hotel: If you stay at the main lobby you have to take a cart to the pool/gym - FAIL! Rooms were spacious. A agree with other review "walls are paper thin". I enjoyed the hotel bar, had a little band there at night.
“Indifferent staff” Bottom line- had to sleep on the floor. The room, ammentities and property don't warrant its 5 star status. Better can be found in a better location for much less.

“Beautiful Hotel in a Great Location” We stayed at this hotel for two nights with our sons, ages 16 and 8. Our room had a wonderful view of the beautiful City Hall. The front desk and bell staff was so friendly and helpful, we felt welcome from the first moment we walked in. The location is perfect for us as it provided quick and easy access to the subway and a trolley stop. This was our first trip to Philadelphia so we were in awe of all of the wonderful history and architecture right outside the door. The little indoor pool area is small and only three feet deep, but is very charming looking, has a nice view and comfortable chairs,and was a perfectly fine place for us to relax and for the kids to unwind a little. The hotel seemed to have mostly business travelers and seemed to be very business-friendly. Since we were only there for a couple of days and were out and about most of the time, the fact that most everything there was geared more for business than family didn't bother us at all. If we were there for longer, I might have selected a hotel that had things for the kids to do and a bigger pool area. All in all, this was a really nice little hotel and we were very satisfied with everything about our stay there.

“Great location and free laundry” Great location-- walking distance to the Galleria mall, across the street from a couple great restaurant-bar spots, and a few short blocks from a 24-hour CVS. The biggest plus for me was the free laundry, especially since I stayed for almost two weeks. I'd stay here again.

“Nice clean motel-in process of upgrading” Motel was in good location and antiseptically clean. Desk clerk worked an 18-hour shift and was very bubbly and friendly. Very attentive to our needs. The landscaping around the motel was well-kept with palm trees along the east side. Motel is in process of upgrading with new carpeting and furniture. New earth-toned carpeting already in hallways.
