Clerk informed us that rooms are next and will also get new furnishings. Our room was very clean but bland. Could use some more paintings or something. New furniture will be nice when installed. Bathroom was immaculate. Very nice shower head with curved shower curtain. Breakfast was adequate. Breakfast area was very small and easily became congested. Overall, very nice for the price. We'll be back in March 2006.

“Another Red, White, and Boom” Another stay at the Courtyard for the July 3rd for the downtown fireworks. Again this hotel was a great location. The parade ended at the hotel, so we just walked outside to see it. Then we came back into the room and ate, then walked straight down Spring Street for the fireworks. The room didn't have the extra towels in like I asked but it did have a full size refrigerator. I would not stay in that room again (204). It was one floor above overlooking the interior courtyard where the smokers go. I was awakened at 3 a.m. by a rowdy bunch in the courtyard. After half an hour, I went down and asked the front desk to please have them quiet down, and the front desk clerk did just that. One thing I dislike are the stairs from the front desk area to the elevators. they seem to be a bit steep. I am so klutzy, I fell UP the stairs in the morning. From now on, I will ask to use the handicapped elevator. The valet is now $18, and the breakfast is now $8.95. Overall though, the hotel was still convenient and clean.

“EXCELLENT LOCATION!” This hotel was conveniently located in the heart of downtown Houston; we could walk everywhere, from the restaurant strip near the theater district, down to the aquarium. Although everything closed early because of the weekend, there was plenty to do at the hotel. They had a very popular bar ( which was full until closing at 2 am)- it created some noise throughout the hotel, but gave it a very party like atmosphere. Furthermore, the pool was spectacular! located outside on the 6th floor, it was overlooked by the other highrises of downtown. A really great place to relax! Only issue was parking; the hotel lot was full Sat. night.. so we were left with the city owned lot one block down ( only $8 overnight- a much better bargain than their $16) Do not fall for the parking trap- on the weekends there are plenty of other places to park! But otherwise would definitely go back!

“Loved this hotel” Great hotel. rooms are a bit small, but it worked fine for me. Staff was very courteous and helpful. Ate in the sports bar one time, very expensive. There is a drug store and liquor store close by if you want food, drinks for room. Restaurants within walking distance. I used the workout facilities twice and they are very nice. Clean with lots of up to date equipment. The only drawback is it is a bit of a walk to the Metro and coming back it is up hill. I rode the Metro everywhere & only used a cab one time. Highly recommend Bucca di Beppo restaurant just a block from the hotel. Would stay here again for business, but if I went with family I would stay elsewhere as the rooms are small.

“The best hotel in DC” To say we fell in love with The Jefferson when we visited last year is no lie, The whole place reeks of understated glamour and just plain old-fashioned service. Check-in was super smooth at one of the little desks in reception - and because there is no big reception desk is does feel more like visiting a friend. Our suite was gorgeous and decked out in very good (replica) period furniture. And the bathroom with (yet another) TV and a huge tub/separate shower was perfect. The staff were all really helpful - from room service waiters to bar staff and concierge. And although it's pricey, we thought it was absolutely worth it. Location-wise it's definitely a winner being only 2-3 blocks from the White House. We are already planning our stay this autumn!

“Great place esp if you want to be near Inner Harbor or Conv Center” I stayed here for a conference just recently. The hotel is very new and modern. I'm a Hilton Honors member, so I got free internet and access to the concierge lounge on the 18th floor where this is breakfast and snack [but a cash bar :(]. The housekeeping was superb, and my room was made up by early morning. I valued this because there are often times during a conference that I want to go back to my room to work on things. The proxmity to the conv center is a big plus. I had meetings in the early morning or late at night, and it was nice to be so close to my room. Every part of the hotel is in good shape. The things I disliked were (1) the bar is kind of small and out of the way (2) The Diamond Tavern really is not very good. (3) For some reason the shower head is really high. I'm not tall, but not that short either (5'10"), and still was a bit of a reach to adjust. Finally, the room rate was $224 not including taxes. Because I was there on business, it didn't really matter to me, but if I were paying myself, I might try to explore some other options. But all in all I would recommend this hotel to business travellers or people who want to be near the Inner Harbor.

“What the Doctor Ordered” My parents have been staying here for many years when coming to MD Anderson. I was able to arrange to stay here on a Saturday night recently and now understand why this is the place to stay when visiting MD Anderson. First of all, guests have to be patients or family members. Therefore, all of the staff is kind and helpful. Everything is geared to making the patient comfortable. There is an extensive reading as well as DVD movie library. There is entertainment several nights a week in the lobby. The restaurant is happy to accomodate special dietary needs. The rooms are extremely comfortable and quiet. Many rooms have kitchenettes. Hotel shuttles are available to take guests to area restaurants and stores. Access to the various clinics and the hosiptal is very easy.

“Good Option for Sea Tac Area” Stayed one night b/c arrived late at Sea Tac Airport. Shuttle very convenient (courtesy phone located at ground transport at airport if you don't see van). Hotel has Pacific Northwest theme. Staff (from shuttle driver to front desk) very friendly. Used Marriott reward points for 1 King room. Very small. If you look on floorplan on back of door, there are just a few of these smaller rooms on each floor - book 2 queens for more room or ask for larger King room. Also, we had interior courtyard view (overlooking indoor pool - no natural light). Fine for one night, but would have been bummed if more than that. Room was clean and looked newly refurbished. Had breakfast at on-site restaurant next day. Pricey, but lots of choices, inc breakfast buffet. Also coffee bar w/pastries, muffins open in am. Took shuttle back to airport in morning to rent car for week-end - so we avoided paying for parking at the hotel which is expensive. As we drove back to airport next day, noticed that Marriott Sea Tac seems like one of nicest options on airport strip of typical chain hotels.

“Trendy stay near Union Square” If you like trendy hotels, you'll probably like the Clift. I don't always stay at places with this trendy of a feel, but it was a nice change of pace. I like the location close to Union Square. The rooms and hallway have a cool, older vibe with typical Ames style decor. The room itself was very simple and I found the bed very comfortable. All the staff were very friendly. I'd likely return.

“Hip, modern, comfy, but not pretentious.” Stayed here for the first time this week and it has become my new Dallas spot. The W is too cheesy, Zaza WAY too cheesy and go figure, the cheapest out of the three has better service and more character. The rooms are basic, but nicely appointed with retro modern style furnishings. It kind of has a W Miami style feel with outdoor entrances and marvelous landscaping. The hotel bar is nice, but wasn't crowded when I was there. However, the view from the patio is great as was the view from my room (deluxe in the bungalow section - $139). Smoke is the adjacent restaurant and is great if you like meat and whiskey. They have other things, but that seems to be the two most popular items. All in all a cool hotel. Cool enough for me to waste 10 minutes writing this review at least.

“Great location and friendly staff.” I stayed at the Stanford in September 2012. The location is excellent, a short walk to subway, Empire State Building and Times Square. The staff are fantastic, very friendly and helpful. The rooms are small, but that's to be expected in New York. Housekeeping are excellent, the room was always spotless. Great wine bar on the first floor, definitely make a stop there for happy hour. We stayed on the 10th floor and out our window we could see the Empire State- magical! The breakfast is very basic, coffee/tea/juice with one choice of fruit and bagels. It's enough to get you started, there are plently of other restaurants around if you dont want to eat it. Highly recommend this hotel.

“My room was huge and the bed comfortable...” My room was huge and the bed comfortable. The bathroom was outdated and dirty. I noticed a lot of toothpaste splatters on the walls surrounding the sink. Not up to typical Hilton standards. The gigantic lobby is quite lovely but I didn't spend anytime there.

“Nice hotel, perfect for concention goers” The Grand Hyatt is located on the same block as the convention center, so it is conveniant for convention goers. The rooms are decent size, we done, and the bed is comfortable. Of all things to complain about ... I was not a big fan of the soap the hotel supplied. It made you feel greasy. The pool is nice, but the pool area is somewhat small. There is very limited shade for those who burn and don't tan. Food/drink service at the pool was a nice touch. Check and check out went smoothly and all the staff was friendly. Food and drinks were a little pricey, but thats typical for an upscale hotel.

“Out of the way, but worth the savings” i have stayed at the gem hotel in chelsea a few times and since my meeting this time was close to penn station i decided to try the gem in midtown. the rates were around 20% less than chelsea. the location, on west 36th was convenient for my meeting, but certainly does not have the charm that the chelsea location has. however, that being said, the staff was courteous and knowledgeable, the rooms were "gem" clean and it was a very pleasant stay.

“Odd place, but overall a good experience” The first thing as you go in the door is that you are at the bar - and have to hunt for the reception desk. From there, it's a hunt for the elevators. Make sure you ask for a room with windows that face outside - or you could be in a room that looks out over an inner lobby, especially if you are on the 5th floor where the business center and fitness centers are located. So those are the negatives. The positives are that the staff are extremely helpful; the rooms are quiet; the bathroom is huge; and the bed(s) is so comfortable it's easy to get a good night's sleep. I really like that you can choose to not have housekeeping, and then can use the credit in the restaurant or get extra Starwood points. I really don't need clean sheets and towels every day, so I appreciated being able to make that choice, and being rewarded for it.

“Pleasant, fairly convenient hotel” The Churchill is a pleasant hotel, a 10 minute walk uphill from Dupont Circle metro, and if you get a good deal on the rates, it should satisfy. The lobby is clean and welcoming. There's two computers with free internet access in the lobby; otherwise wifi is $10/night. The first room we went into was like a sauna - bizarrely hot! We immediately phoned the lobby and within about 30 seconds they obligingly switched our room to one of normal temperature; this was probably also an upgrade. Our room was spacious and comfortable, with an American King-sized bed, two side tables with lamps, a big desk with TV on it, another desk, plenty of drawers and wardrobe space, lots of windows, and a coffee maker with coffee replenished daily. The bathroom could do with a renovation, but is perfectly clean and sufficient, though rather small, particularly if you happen to be a large person. Good water pressure. Everything was efficient, the bed fantastically comfortable, and we were happy with our choice, though it was a little bit of a walk. Breakfast not so speedy if you're trying to take away - I had to wait 10 minutes for the server to lift a muffin from a plate and give it to me!

“Clean, affordable lodging near Old Town” thought about bidding on Priceline for a hotel in downtown or in La Jolla but I started adding up all the extras-parking, breakfast and even charges to use the health club at one of the hotels in La Jolla and decided just to book a regular hotel. The Old Town Inn doesn't charge for anything except the room, the parking is free, there is an included breakfast and they even have a computer set up where you can check your email or directions for free. The only downside was that it was a little noisy with the freeway traffic/Pacific Highway traffic and occasional planes overhead but that decreased as the night wore on. It's not actually inside of Old Town, when I was driving there I thought I was in the wrong place because I was on a stretch of highway with some industrial property. But it's just a block from the trolley station and another 5 minute walk and you are in Old Town. What attracted me to this property was it's location near Old Town, convenient to the Old Town trolley station, close enough to walk to Old Town plus the added benefit of free parking and easy access from I-5 if you are driving. By trolley it was only about 10 minutes to downtown so the location was very convenient. The rooms were spacious and more than adequate for a place just to sleep in, it wasn't charming but it was clean and the bed reasonably comfortable. I had to change rooms during my visit because the cheaper room was booked for part of my stay so I transferred to a double queen smoking room. The room smelled a bit but it wasn't something that really affected my stay. The 1st night was $69+tax, the 2nd two nights $94+tax. The bathroom was clean and the shower was fine, bring your own toiletries as all they have is bar soap and shampoo. There was a hair dryer in both of the rooms. The included breakfast is a nice way to start the day, you can make your own waffles, they also have pastries, fruit, cereal, toast, juice, coffee and tea. There is an outdoor pool but I didn't use it.

“Sheraton figured out how to do it right.” You can't help but notice a large trophy on the twelfth floor lobby desk of the Sheraton. The staff is proud of their service and intend to keep the trophy by staying friendly, keeping the rooms clean and attractive, providing internet access/boarding pass printouts in the lobby, taking care of problems right away such as replacing batteries in the TV remote. There is one set of elevators from street level to the lobby and a second set from the lobby to the rooms. Reminded me of Tokyo hotels that occupy a few floors of a high rise. Always wanted to stay in one and now I feel like I have. We hung out for a little while in the small lobby sipping complimentary lemonade. Central location. Weekend street as well as hotel interior parking. It's a new hotel and Sheraton figured out how to do it right. The suites are very well designed to maximize space while providing kitchen area, sitting area, sleeping area, desk and bathroom with tub. Coincidentally a friend was staying at the hotel the same nights we did. We were all raving about how nice the hotel was. Nice workout room on the rainy day. Quick drive up 163 to Balboa Park for a run on the sunny day. There were very small problems such as occasionally hearing our neighbors and dry air.

“Spacious room” Stayed here for a meeting. Location can't be beat - right on Michigan Avenue and across from Nordstrom. We arrived at about 5 pm and there was just one person at the check-in and a longish line. We were able to check in with the Ambassador person as I have a Priority Reward membership. We got an upgrade to a large room with huge bathroom - I love a walk in shower and I was not disappointed. We were in the older tower and this was convenient because my meeting was in that tower too. Internet was expensive (these hotels that have lots of conference travel manage to do this with impunity while cheaper places give it for free - go figure!). I really didn't interact with staff at all so can't comment on that. Also didn't eat in any of the restaurants (why would you with so many great restaurants in the city?). Would stay here again for the location.

“Great Hotel” This is a lovely hotel, the room was spotlessly clean and the beds very comfortable. The buffet breakfast included is very good quality and there is a lot of choice. The staff were friendly and effificent. It is in a very good location near Dupont Circle. Will definitely be staying here again.

“Great location, nice hotel” This was a really good hotel for the price. Clean, comfortable, and affordable. Great location right in the center of DC. Check-in staff was extremely friendly and helpful. My only complaint was the heater in the room was noisy and it was a little bit difficult to regulate the temperature in the room. Even though it had a thermostat, it would get really warm when the (loud) heater kicked on, and then cold quickly when it was off.

“Great Hotel and Great Location” I had stayed at this hotel several years ago because of it's location downtown. My daughter was participating in the state science fair that was located at the Henry B. Gonzales Convention Center. While there were other hotels that were closer, they were all twice as much or more! As it was, we were only about 6 blocks from the convention center. If you don't want to walk, the trolly stop is about 1/2 block from the motel. I found the staff to be polite and helpful. I was able to check in an hour before the posted check-in time as the room was ready. Another plus was that parking is free! The other motels had $20-35 daily parking fees! You can park in a 3 tier parking garage for motel guests only. The Riverwalk, Alamo, mall, restaurants, and other attractions are all located nearby. The only improvement I could mention was the breakfast. It is listed as continental, which is fine. However, we were there for 3 days and they had the same flavor of muffin each day (they also had 2 cereals, fresh fruit, and bagels). They also provided free wireless internet.

“Very Classy hotel” I've stayed at the Grand Hyatt two or three times before, both personal and business trips, and it continues to be a very classy hotel. I never actually saw them, but I heard that the Yankees were staying there at the same time we were, and some in our group reported riding up the elevator with Kate Hudson (who is dating Alex Rodriguez). I guess if the hotel is good enough for them, it's good enough for me. Self parking is available in a garage behind the hotel (entrance on 7th Avenue) for $28.00 a day and no free in-and-outs. It's pricey, but not bad if you plan to walk most places. Valet parking averages about $38.00 a day with in-and-out privileges. The sleeping rooms have a nice, modern decor with a flat screen TV. I liked the large, well lit bathroom with a big bathtub and separate glass enclosed shower (nice soothing spray). There were lots of amenities that you don't get everywhere, like toothpaste, an umbrella, bathrobes, and a lint remover. I found all of the staff to be helpful, courteous, and friendly. They went out of their way to try and beat me to the front door so they could open it. I liked the boarding pass kiosk in the front lobby, but didn't like that I had to go to the front desk for my bill when checking out (the hotel is trying to be green). The Grand Hyatt is in a nice downtown location within easy walking distance to lots of places to eat, and about six or seven blocks from Pike Place Market. Room service for dinner was OK... not spectacular. There's a Starbucks attached to the hotel, so each night I went there and bought cakes and pastries for breakfast the next day (to eat with my in-room coffee). This hotel continues to be an excellent choice in downtown Seattle. The Hyatt at Olive 8 just recently opened within a block of the Grand Hyatt. Our conference was located there, and it looked very nice also. One word of warning - the desk clerk at the Grand Hyatt said the Olive 8 is trying to be even greener than the Grand Hyatt, so be forewarned!

“a good value” I found this hotel to meet my expectation for a Holiday Inn Express. It seems like it is an older hotel, but clean and the staff is very friendly and helpful. The pool was closed during my stay, but the staff offered the opportunity to use the pool at another Holiday Inn close by. The work out room was small (treadmill bike and stairclimber), but I had no competition for the equipment. The parking lot is adjoining with a Wendy's which I found to be very convenient. The breakfast was very nice and the eating area was clean. I would stay there again. I (a single female business traveler) felt very safe and comfortable there.

“Very comfortable!” We stayed at Lakeway Resort after abandoning another hotel that was unacceptable. This resort is right on Lake Travis and offers spectacular views. The room is very well appointed, with a flat LCD TV, bath robes, Starbucks coffee, and free internet. Beds are very comfortable. The only minor gripe we had is they would not allow an early check-in. Surely there would be one clean room that would be available. Nevertheless...we will come back to Lakeway Resort.

“Wonderful!” Beautifully rennovated downtown building. Massive room with separate living room/desk area. Really great exercise room. Attentive staff. Exceptionally clean. Nice to see an older building restored to its former glory.

“Nice hotel” We stayed at this hotel for 3 nights while in LA. We found the downtown location very convenient, once we rented a car, and it was easy to drive to wherever we wanted. Check in was relatively easy, and the rooms were nice and well appointed. The bed is heaven. This is the second Westin we stay at, and we find their beds always comfortable, with very nice linen and pillows. The bathroom is a bit small, but on the other hand, the shower is great. We stayed at a high floor and had nice views of the city from our window, which was great. The hotel lobby is gourgeous, and the panoramic lift was such a nice touch. The only cons we have about this hotel are: 1) Cost of parking - found it extremely expensive. OK, I know we're in LA, but c'mon.... 2) No self park - nothing against vallets, but we find self-parking super easy and convenient ( =no waiting in line for your car) 3) No wi-fi in the room (only in the lobby). I still don't get why hotels offer free wi-fi as a complimentary service... Nowadays, free wi-fi should be a must, and nothing to distinguish one hotel from the other. Everybody is wired, so why charge for you to have internet in your room? 4) Room service: we ordered some soups for our first day at the hotel, once we arrived in a holiday, with very options to eat nearby (this must be another con about staying downtown). The soups were tasteless, and considering the amount we paid we should've gotten something much better.. Also, be prepared to stay at least 30 min over the phone in order to place your order. Room service is definetely a NO at this hotel. Considering the price we paid for the room, and the opportunity to stay at such an iconic hotel, we would come back, but would certainly try to find another option for parking.

“Very nice stay” My husband and I stayed at the Renaissance Chicago in Nov. for 5 nights. The hotel was clean, had nice sized rooms, coffee makers, and the normal amenities that you would expect in an American hotel. We did not try the restaurant, but there was a Starbucks in the lobby that was very convenient. If you walk out the back door of the hotel you are right on a major shopping street with Macy’s, and a number of others stores—it was a nice surprise as I was more focused on Michigan Ave. and did not even realize this when I booked the hotel. A short walk away is a nice little bakery and sandwich shop called Corner Bakery, my friends and I enjoyed eating there a couple of times. The best part about Chicago though is Michigan Ave. The hotel is at the base of this long wonderful street, if you make it to the other end and can’t make it back—call for a taxi, they are every where! Would I stay at this hotel again? Yes. It was very nice, the staff was helpful and they were very courteous and efficient.

“great place - 4 years in a row” This is the fourth year in a row that I have stayed at Hotel Metro. It is in a great location, right near Macy's and the Empire State Building. It appears that the hotel has now completed it room remodeling, which is great. The staff is nice, and the rooms are sufficiently large. Try to get a room away from the street side, and you'll sleep better. The hotel is always clean. I will book again.

“Solid Hotel in Heart of DC” The JW Marriott is a great hotel with a lot of amenities. My favorite part is that it is located so close to so much. It is within a few short blocks of a Metro station, the White House, the Treasury Department, the Aquarium, a movie theatre, restaurants, Smithsonian museums, and more. We had our car valet parked and didn't touch it for two days. Our gorgeous room had views of the Washington Monument and the classic Willard Intercontinental Hotel. The concierge was very helpful in printing us materials on the Supreme Court, which allowed us to take a tour that very day. The lobby's free wireless Internet was very convenient for me and my laptop. The new elevators cut down on waiting and were very fast. A full-service Starbucks was located on the second floor lobby and was private -- it didn't have an outside entrance like many other hotel Starbucks. My partner used the fitness center, which also included an indoor pool and whirlpool. In our bedroom, the sheets and pillows were very comfortable. While a bit small, the bathroom was furnished nicely and the shower was terrific. Although our bedroom was on the 12th floor, my partner still heard some street noise, but it was minimal. The hotel offers fruit-flavored cold water in the lobby, which was refreshing after a hot day touring. We ate breakfast at the buffet one morning. It was fairly tasty, but on the expensive side. Beware of the honor bar technology in the bedrooms. As soon as you move an item, even if you put it back, you might be charged for it. Be sure to call the front desk to alert them if you moved anything by accident. Better yet, ask the hotel in advance to remove the honor bar altogether, especially if you have kids or don't want to be tempted yourselves. A top of the line hotel, the JW Marriott has the benefit of being in a great location, staffed by very friendly people, and modernly styled, safe, and clean.

“New hotel. Great value in El Paso” This hotel is very new and is a nice place to stay if you need to be on the west side of El Paso. The rooms are clean, spacious and very accomodating. I ended up with a king suite and it was well work the extra money in order to get a slightly larger room. The shower was even a walk in style, which I really liked. The breakfast selection was ample and the internet service worked wonderfully. The only downside to this hotel is that it's a bit far from the center of the city. However, if location isn't a concern, you can't beat the deal here.

“Outstanding!!” Just returned from an impressive stay at this hotel. Hotel prices, in NYC, are notoriously steep during the Fall and Holiday season, so we weren`t hopeful about finding anything decent for under $200. Imagine our surprise to find Travelzoo offering this hotel with an upgrade to a superior room for a remarkable $159. The same room through the hotel website and through various so called "discount" travel sites was $399. Needless to say, we jumped at this opportunity and couldn`t have been happier with the results. We arrived in the beautiful marble, art deco lobby 4 hours before check in time, but the efficient and friendly front desk staff had a room ready for us. The elevator literally whisked us up to our room on the 49th floor. We gasped when we entered to find a corner room with floor to ceiling windows (meeting at the corner) with drop dead gorgeous views of midtown, Times Square and the Hudson River. There was 3rd window, as well, with equally stunning views. As if that weren`t enough, the room and bath were beautiful, immaculately maintained, and tastefully decorated with subtle Asian touches and provocative lighting. There was a flat screened TV, coffee maker, iron, ironing board, daily newspaper, abundant towels and bath amenities and a minibar. The king bed was firm and extrememly comfortable and everything was very quiet.....not a bit of street noise. Our request for bathrobes had someone from housekeeping knocking on our door, with 2 luxurious robes, within 5 minutes of the request. All the staff here is amiable and helpful. We met friends who were staying at a nearby, well known, but shabby hotel at nearly twice what we paid. We sensed their envy when they stopped by to visit. This was an exceptional hotel experience....not to be missed.

“High value 3.5-star” Relatively new hotel, seems like they are 'dressed to impress'. Room was spotless and large for mid-Town. Free breakfast AND free beer/wine/apps (weekdays) in the lobby area. A big plus - I barely ate out. Helpful and knowledgeable staff. Roof-top lounge for the attractive 20-something set. One downer: I *lost* my gold family signet ring on this trip. Pretty sure it was in this room but will never know. Hotel management was at a loss - all they can do is check the laundry and lost and found. Its melted down by now... :(

“Good hotel with a great location” We stayed here for the pre-Christmas time season. Overall it is a good value. it is clean, efficient, and a convenient place to stay. SERVICE: The front desk personel are very quick and efficient and are friendly as well. They will help you find sights and are easy to deal with. They ask for you to leave your key with them before you leave (for security purposes - they said in case you lose your key). There is someone at the front desk 24 hours a day so leaving the key did not seem like a big deal to me. They buzz you in past the front lobby and that made me feel safer. A quick aside, they list an airport pickup service called AirLink at the Murray Hill. Don't use them, we almost missed our flight because they picked us up an hour late. LOCATION: A little past 30th and Lexington. It is a very convenient mid-town location. It is 2 blocks from the 28th street station for the 6 train. You can reach Macy's in about 8-10 blocks. There are few cabs on 30th but hit Lexington and it is much easier to get a cab. There are plenty of cafés and restaurants close by. The hotel is on a quiet street (except on Friday-Saturday nights) near residential brownstones. The neighborhood is very safe in my opinion and I never felt uneasy. The hotel has no elevator and staying on the 4th floor means going up some steep stairs. This isn't hard unless you have luggage. They do have a porter during the day and I am sure he could help with luggage. There is a good Italian place called Caio Bella Italia on Lexington and the Bagelry has good bagels and great coffee. ROOM: We booked the queen room with a front view. This is the largest room they offer. It has a clean but somewhat hard queen sized bed. They do provide plenty of pillows. It has a wood floor and dark wood furniture and a small but usable closet. The bathrooms are new and have a good sized shower and are larger than you would expect. Our room had a 21" flat screen TV which was nice. There is a mini-fridge in your room so buy your soft drinks and water at Duane Reade and that can save you some money. Keep in mind that it takes 5-10 minutes for the water to get hot, so be sure to run the water before taking a shower. We were there in the winter and they run the boiler quite a bit. Our room was a bit warm most of the time but it is better than being cold. The boiler is a bit noisy and can be annoying when you are trying to sleep. My biggest complaint is that the smell of cigarette smoke came through the boiler vents and that was very annoying. They are a non-smoking property but I think many of the guests ignored that rule. They refill the towels and clean the room very well. The street side rooms can hear road noise from Lexington. Even though they are double paned windows you will still hear outside noise. That is the only downside to the front view rooms. PRICE: During the winter it is $189 a night and I believe it is $209 for the weekend. During the spring/summer it goes down to $169 and $189 for the weekend. We paid an average of $210 a night with taxes for 4 nights. I would recommend the Murray Hill Inn as a good priced, reasonalby nice accomodation in the Mid-town area.

“Perfection” My husband and I stayed here for 2 nights with our 3 daughters. The room was exceptional - loved the outdoor temperature reading right by the unit door, the wall controls for all the lighting next to the beds, the tv in the bathroom and the sound system. The beds were so cozy, the welcome amenities for the children were delightful and the furnishings in the room lovely. As someone who hates indoor pools, I found this indoor pool in a category all it's own. It was beautiful, the furniture comfy and the wall of windows overlooking Michigan Avenue was unbelievable. We spent hours there and I still didn't want to leave. My husband treated himself to a massage which he was very pleased with. We did eat in the Shanghai Terrace, which was not great with kids. I highly recommend this hotel. The service, decor and pool are impeccable. It is my favorite hotel ever....

“Great location, not the most functional rooms” This hotel is an LA landmark, and I've stayed there a few times. The iconic nature always gets me. The location is great, however the rooms in the round towers are limited in size. Granted you don't spend a lot of time in your room in LA, but the small size also required the AC to be directly over the bed. The pool area is beautiful, but the exercise room basically puts you on display in the hotel. In the past I've stayed here when the Standard was full (across the street), and that will probably continue to be my policy. Good value in a good location, but not my first choice.

“wow.” Checking in at the lobby desk made me fear the worst, but once I reached my room on the 11th floor, it was like hitting the jackpot! The rooms are very masculine but luxurious. I had one of the suites with its own living room. The city views made me feel like I was back in Chicago. The hotel offers a free breakfast in the restaurant every morning and it had lots to offer. It was also great getting to spend some time in the revitalized downtown area...so much to see! Make sure you have dinner down the street at Bottega Louie, you won't regret it!

“Good, but not amazing.” We chose the Westin Times Square specifically based on the good reviews here at Trip Advisor. We stayed for 2 nights in a Club level room (1424) which was a larger corner room. It does not have amazing views being relatively low on the 14th floor. As for city noises, it was quiet enough. We heard sirens every now and then but not "regular" traffic noise. The Club lounge (on 8th floor) is not extraordinary.......it offers a continental breakfast (only warm item was oatmeal) and then an evening hors d'oeuvres offering, which was much better. Free teas, coffees and soft drinks are available all day long. The location of the hotel is excellent........it really is in the thick of it, and maybe even too much for our tastes. Times Square was crazy crowded even just to cross through to get to other midtown locations. There are lots of dining choices, movie theatres and subway stations just out the hotel doors. We normally would stay at the Rihga but it is now "The London" and not family friendly any longer. We had 2 kids and this room had plenty of roll-around floor space for them. Each window had a window seat for looking out and they liked that. There is also one club chair and one desk chair. We ordered dinner room service and used the beds for seating purposes. Hotel parking = $45 per day......the steepest we have ever paid in NYC. My only real complaint is that the bathroom door is glass and anytime someone turned on the light during the night or early morning, the room was lit up as a result. I called for a night light but there were none. A night light would easily fix the problem. The double roller blinds do an excellent job of making the room dark. Enjoy your stay.

“Friendly Staff, Great Location” I've stayed at this hotel a few times and enjoyed it each time. Good fitness center, nice rooms, typical but tasty room service, and for me - most importantly - an ideal location one block away from the Metro. And, I've always been very warmly greeted by staff at the check-in desk. They seem to very customer-focused at this hotel. This is definitely a business hotel - the lobby is pleasant but won't blow your socks off - but it has a warm and hospitable feel to it. I look forward to staying here when I travel.

“Solid Hotel with Marvelous Location” Stayed here 5 nights during a convention. Everything worked for me. Enjoyed Shula's steakhouse on premises. Walked two blocks to board the Architectural and Historical Cruise operated by Chicago Line Cruises that the Concierge worked on very hard to find me a seat. Room and internet worked perfectly. Walked minutes to the main shopping street - Nordi's on Michigan Ave. Lobby bar served a terrific Manhattan but offered very limited food selection. No complaints whatsoever.

“The Hudson is fabulous!” The Hudson is not for everybody. I repeat: The Hudson is not for everybody. But I absolutely love it. LOVE IT! When I travel I don't like to stay at chain hotels if possible, and I especially love hotels with style. The Hudson obviously has plenty of that. Yes, the rooms are small. But when I'm in NYC I don't plan to hang out in my room much. I'd rather stay in a small, fabulous room, than a huge, floral bedspread-clad one. Just a personal preference. The Hudson is in a great location, right by Time Warner Center and Columbus Circle. But that obviously doesn't matter too much, since you're in NYC and you can take a cab or the subway somewhere else if you'd like. If you feel cramped in the small rooms but you want to hang out at the hotel, just grab a chair in the lobby and relax there. Great music to listen to, which is also a plus for me. For anyone interested in a generic chain hotel experience, The Hudson is not for you. If you want a swanky, modern hotel, go with The Hudson.

“Chicago Business Travel” I scheduled a business trip with the additional purpose of entertaining clients in the evening. Overall I found the hotel clean, good location, helpful staff. But what made this trip the most worthwhile for me was dining in the Michael Jordan Steakhouse in the hotel. Definitely a top notch experience all around.

“Clean room and excellent staff” The hotel itself is a typical budget Marriott hotel -- clean rooms and spacious enough for 2.5 people to be comfortable after a full day at SeaWorld. I would say the best part of this hotel is that the staff was excellent and very friendly and helpful with any questions or issues. This - to me - makes a hotel worth coming back to next time we are in the area. Their prices are very reasonable, especially considering how well kept the hotel is in terms of cleanliness. The pool was a nice touch in the San Antonio heat. It is not quite as big as the Courtyard next door, but less "crazy" and pretty quiet. We heard music from the Courtyard pool and they had a swim up bar. Pretty cool, but depends on your interests. The free breakfast each morning had a good selection -- sausage/egg biscuits, waffles, breads, cereals, fruit, yogurt, pastries, etc. When I stay at high end hotels and they offer "free" breakfast, it is usually cold stuff, so I appreciate these hotels more sometimes. Only beef I had (and this is actually not the fault of the hotel) was that sometimes you hear kids screaming down the hallway at midnight with the parents not saying anything. I didn't mind it much, just because this hotel is geared towards the SeaWorld crowd, but my 3 year old woke up a couple of times to the noise. The free shuttle is a nice touch also. There was relatively little wait time (5 minutes) after calling the shuttle in the evening to pick us up from SeaWorld. Just make sure you book the shuttle early enough the day before to get to the park.

“Fab Stay” Had the pleasure of staying at this hotel in June this year and enjoyed it a lot. Fantastic location. Great employees who smiled from entry to exit and who were always there to help out. Special kudos to the Concierge team who were just amazing! Fun bar ambiance and great cocktails. Enjoyed the fitness facilities which are very large and well maintained. My room was a little tired and could have done with a little more tlc. Will certainly visit again next time I'm in the city.

“Best W Hotel in the Country!” I have stayed at the W Hotel in DC over 20 times this past year and it keeps getting better and better. The hotel is the ultimate combination of elegance and style. It has it all; wonderful sleeping quarters, the most happening DC evening bars, a top notch restaurant, and some of the best customer service in DC. Rarely do I leave the hotel except to go into the office. As a matter of fact, most of my traveling colleagues have switched hotel chains and have started staying at the W. Frequently, my DC resident colleagues join me for drinks and dinner at the hotel. They love it! Customer service at the W has reached a very high level in it's short life as a Starwood Hotel. The hotel lobby and roof top bar look like a picture out of a magazine. The view for the roof is the best in the city. The outstanding setting and great people watching crowd makes the price of the drinks worth every sip. The entire W Staff is always working to meet your every need. W Insider Desmond McKenna is a seasoned hotel manager who is excellent about anticipating your every need. Don't forget to use the Acura Experience for free transportation within a five mile radius of the hotel. No other hotel in DC offers this service. I have stayed at many hotels in the DC area and the W Hotel truly has the overall best accommodations in the city to offer the sophisticated seasoned business and leisure traveler. If you like to be pampered and have a fun time after a busy day in the office, stay at the W Hotel in DC. You'll love it.

“Fabulous stay at an amazing hotel!” My daughter, granddaughter, and I recently stayed for 4 nights at the Conrad. This was our first trip to Chicago and we chose our hotel from the reviews on Tripadvisor. So very glad we did. What an amazing hotel! It is plush, comfortable, inviting, and has the best employees I have seen in a long time. I love being called by name and being recognized by the staff. This may be a small thing to some people but this staff cares enough to get to know their guests and treats them like they are friends. I have traveled extensively and when I come across a hotel that does this I sincerely try to let them know how much this is appreciated. My daughter was blown away everytime they stopped us to ask how things were going and see if there was anything they could do for us. From the moment of check in, Eloy was amazing! He always greeted us with his fabulous smile and answered any requests we made. The nice touch of cookies and milk for my granddaughter was really special. The concierge, Chis, was wonderful. He helped us constantly with directions, reservations, tours, and anything else we questioned. We asked and he delivered. And Benjamin was always there for us to give us important advise, suggestions, tips, you name it. He became a dear friend very quickly!! I would list the negative points also, but I really can't think of any. (Except the weather that turned brutally cold but this is Chicago afterall!!) The Conrad delivered the perfect stay for us and the location could not have been any better. Being able to walk from the hotel directly into Nordstroms is truly a plus! I highly recommend the Conrad and hope to visit them again soon!

“Great Location and Service” We stayed here on Friday, April 1st and was very pleased. We live in the suburbs, but were planning on a late night in the city for the Cubs home opener and for a concert that evening so we decided to Priceline a room. We got a room that had a pretty nice view for about $98 with taxes. We stopped there at about 9:00 a.m. to see if they would hold our bag so we didn't have to take it with us. I was so surprised when she said she would check to see if a room was available so we could just check in. There was one available on the 26th floor so it turned out very convenient for us! The room was clean and comfortable. I like that they had Bath & Body products. It's in a great location in the city, there is an El stop right there. Would definitely stay here again.

“In the heart of the city” This is a hotel far above what you might expect of a Holiday Inn - not only is the location at the heart of the city unbeatable (great restaurants and clubs; a block to the arena, 15 minute walk to the stadium), the hotel is beautiful - modern and trendy (not your Daddy's Holiday Inn!). Had a business meeting in a suite - unbelievable service and attention to detail. My room was all new, upscale bedding and bath, flat panel - everything you might expect at a hotel for $50-100 more... And the restaurant is great - not just for a hotel, but great standing on its own.

“Excellent Stay” I got a great deal on the internet for this hotel. The room was lovely. The restaurant was exceptional. There is a small fitness area. The staff at this hotel are very attentive particularly the hard working bell/valet staff who are happy to arrange tours. The parking is expensive but on par for the DC area. There is not much to do in the neighbourhood after dinner time but hotel staff will make suggestions. I would gladly return!

“The best in San Antonio” I have had to be in San Antonio 3 or 4 times over the past year or so and have stayed a couple of different places. The last 2 times [within the past 45 days or so] I have stayed at the Mokara Hotel. By far, the pick of the litter in San Antonio. I travel externsively for business and pleasure and what impressed me the most about the Mokara is the warm and professional staff there. Some places you stay yo get the canned lines like "my pleasure" or :have a nice day." Each of the last 2 times I have been there I felt an unusual real, sincere desire to serve from all I met; from check in to the valet. The rooms, especially the ones on the river are large and clean. I can't speak or rate the spa or restaurants, but I highly recommend this hotel. Thanks!

“High Style...Great service” The Palomar is a high style and service conscious hotel located around the corner from Philadelphia's famous Rittenhouse Square (and the wonderful Parc restaurant). Interesting art work abounds, cool jazz plays, while hotel staff are cheerful and professional. Our large king room featured comfy bedding, subdued colors, and the usual amenities suitable for business travelers. I wish there had been some brighter overhead lighting, but that seems to be the problem in most hotel rooms. Also, there was no coffeemaker though once I requested one, it was brought to my room immediately. Because I had signed up for the Kimpton InTouch Program , I received a ten dollar credit for the minibar. The bathroom was extremely roomy with upscale amenities and two hefty terry robes in wild animal prints. Every afternoon, hotel guests are invited to a free cocktail party in their modern lobby. On the two evenings I was there, we were offered a choice of wines and peach sangria. There's a clean, well-equipped though small fitness room with stretching area and the breakfasts were delicious and featured many healthful alternatives (e.g.organic oatmeal, soy milk, fresh local berries). I would highly recommend this hotel.

“Thanks for the great room upgrade Hilton!” We stayed here three nights in order to be close to UCLA (which it really wasn't - poor research on my part) and Universal Studios (right next door). Since my husband is a Platinum Hilton Honors member, we were upgraded to a wonderful Executive Suite. Thank you Hilton!! The huge living room, huge bedroom and two part bathroom (separate sink and toilet/bathtub areas) made for a wonderful stay. Plus, the breakfast vouchers (for either a plate of continential breakfast or a discount on the full buffet) plus drink and snack coupons (plus their complementary happy hour food available to everyone) kept us full and saved us money. Some parts of the hotel are a bit dated (decor) but it in no way interferred with our stay.

“my favorite” I reviewed this hotel last year and just want to confirm it is even better. The hotel is spruced up here and there and it looks great. The service is superior in every way. I stayed one week and came back after 12 days for a second week. They reserved my favorite room and greeted me warmly on my return. I travelled with my husband and child and they were treated like visiting royalty. The bar is great -- really friendly bar tenders, great choice of wines, comfortable seating. Just as we left, they began renovations to turn the restaurant into a new space focussed on local, fresh food. It sounded really appealing. It is located in the middle of downtown so convenient to many things. I can't think of anywhere I would rather stay. I return regularly to Charlotte for business and I look forward to staying at the Dunhill because the rooms are well appointed, the beds are great, it is quiet and the service is warm and attentive. What else could you ask for?

“Great Place To Sleep In a city That Doesn't” Times Square is a very busy, congested area so creating a tranquil, calming oasis in the midst of it all is no little feat. The Westin is a perfect hotel for business. The staff is well trained and attentive, the rooms are spacious (by New York standards) and are outfitted with a large desk and high-speed internet. The gym is OK and room service is average. I often rotate among the Westin, The Marriott Marquis, The Hilton Times Square and the W Times Square. I'd give the Westin the top grade among these otherwise fine choices.

“Nice Hotel in Times Square Area” Check In and Security: We walked in at about 8pm but did not see the Ambassador check in area as it was not clearly marked. We checked in at the front desk instead. Being an Ambassador I was not addressed by name even after the check in staff saw my membership card. We were assigned room 2210(an upgrade due to membership). Employee did not mention that only the last 4 elevators service the higher floor, had to go back and ask security how to get to the 22nd. Elevators do not have a security card swipe system to get to your floor, as when we returned at 2am from dinner there was no security in the lobby except a lone policeman outside the hotel entrance. Employees: I want to thank Liliana the Customer Relations Manager for all her help with my reservation and keeping my ordered items in a safe environment. For the rest of the employees what I noticed is alot of chatter and not acknowledging guests who may be in the lobby or waiting to speak with staff. While in the Intercontinental in Japan the opposite was observed, the employees were always on hand to assist you with an umbrella and even your luggage as you arrive in the lobby area. Breakfast: Our disappointment was that this property does not have a Club Lounge but yet again Ambassadors and Royal Ambassadors are not even offered complimentary breakfast. We stayed at a Spanish Chain H10 in Barcelona and even this chain offered us free breakfast and waived the 14 Euros charge per person(see my review for H10 Ithaca). Room: Once again want to thank Liliana for allocating a beautiful suite on the 22nd floor. The suite had a separate seating area. The bed was extremely comfortable. We were given a bottle of water (Evian), a bottle of wine, a cheese tray and a fruit bowl. This was actually the highlight of our stay. We did not watch our free pay per view movie as we had to meet with friends most of the time. Gym: The hotel has a very nice gym facility with free weights and machines. I used the facility and was quite please with it. Overall I was pleased with our stay besides the points I noted above. Thank you IC Times Square (Mr JB Toronto Canada).Check In and Security: We walked in at about 8pm but did not see the Ambassador check in area as it was not clearly marked. We checked in at the front desk instead. Being an Ambassador I was not addressed by name even after the check in staff saw my membership card. We were assigned room 2210(an upgrade due to membership). Employee did not mention that only the last 4 elevators service the higher floor, had to go back and ask security how to get to the 22nd. Elevators do not have a security card swipe system to get to your floor, as when we returned at 2am from dinner there was no security in the lobby except a lone policemen outside the hotel entrance. Employees: I want to thank Liliana the Customer Relations Manager for all her help with my reservation and keeping my ordered items in a safe environment.

“Very Nice Hotel, quiet, great location” This is a very nice hotel in the Cherry Creek area of Denver. It is pretty quiet, and you can walk to great spots like the Cherry Cricket (best burgers in Denver) and Whole Foods. The rooms, lobby, and hotel are clean and new. Staff is great. Only room for improvement is dated and tired cardio equipment, which is in major need of updating and/or repairing.

“Great, great value for the L.A. area!” I stayed at this motel for five nights, and it was a real find. It was by far the most inexpensive stay I've had in L.A., and I sacrificed very little in terms of comfort. It is definitely a motel and not a hotel, so be prepared for that style of arrangement, but the rooms are spacious with a contemporary and generously sized bathroom. The bed was quite comfortable, the free Wi-Fi worked, and the room had a flat-screen television and a small fridge (perfect when your budget is tight). There's not much to distinguish the appointments in this room from a much more expensive hotel. With the free parking and basic continental breakfast (juice, coffee, pastries), you have an unbelievable bargain for SoCal. If you want to stay near the beaches and/or Orange County, this is a great location; the area is very commercial (not glamorous), but gas stations, groceries, restaurants, laundries, etc. are close by. A short drive down the PCH puts you in Long Beach; you will drive through an industrial area, but after that, a string of attractive beach cities awaits. The proprietor of this Rodeway is a very kind and professional gentleman who keeps everything in tip-top shape. Note: the parking lot has plenty of spaces but is compact, so don't bring a tractor-trailer truck.

“Excellent for business or pleasure” I have stayed at the Le Meridien San Francisco numerous times for business and recommend it highly. The service is very good, check-in is speedy and courteous and the concierges are very knowledgeable and helpful. The beds are very comfy with great linens and pillows. The bathroom amenities are just ok, but they do have a nice lemon verbena scent. The location is the number one advantage to staying at Le Meridien SF. It is a short walk to North Beach and the Ferry Building. The Embarcadero Center offers all the retail one could ask for just steps away. The Embarcadero trolley line is also just a short walk away, as is BART. The price varies wildly, as with so many urban hotels. This past weekend my Superior King room was $239/night prepaid, however I've stayed other times when rooms were going for $369 and much higher. Great for business when the boss is paying and sometimes great for pleasure on your own dime, as well. Le Meridien SF also has a very good hotel gym, open 24 hours.

“Third time we've stayed here and we still love it” Staying at this hotel has become a holiday tradition for my family. We have family in the Boston area and were looking for a good hotel at a decent price when we first came here three years ago. We loved it then and we love it now. We arrived rather late (10 pm) and were greeted with a smile and an upgrade to two queen sized beds (instead of one king). My daughter was thrilled to be able to sleep on a bed instead of the sleeper sofa. Loved having a fridge in our room and thought we would use the little stove (but didn't this time around). Room was clean and spacious - it was nice to be able to spread out in the living room to visit with our cousins. Breakfast buffet was slightly different the two mornings we ate there. Nice selection of hot and cold food. It did get a bit crowded around 9:30 or so - breakfast ended at 10. Valet parking a bit pricey ($35/night) but convenient. We are planning on staying here again next year.

“Nearly flawless hotel” We typically don't spend this much on a hotel room, but we may in the future after staying at the Conrad. Everything was superb. My only tiny criticism is that they do not have much of a street presence. You take an elevator from a modest lobby up to the real lobby on the fifth floor, and then up again to your room. Other hotels like the Raddison have more elaborate street level grand lobbies. But in every other regard, this hotel was spot on.

“Beautiful Hotel” I don't know how anyone could give this hotel a negative rating. We stayed on the 19th floor and our rooms were clean and updated. Parking is free in the Galleria - park next to Macy's/Saks for a location closest to the lobby - you would be crazy to valet. We only slept there so I can't give any insights into the hotel amenities (pool, etc.), and we walked into the Galleria food fair to eat. One bonus was 2 free bottles of water in our room - we are used to paying $5 a bottle in an upscale hotel.

“Great stay at Windsor Suites” My family (husband,10 yr old son and myself ) spent 4 nights at the Windsor. Everyone was very nice and helpful from the front desk to the engineers. If we asked for something it was always there within 10 minutes The hotel is within walking distance to quite a few historical sites also. The only thing we didn't like about the location was that everything was closed by 6 pm so you had to go out of the area to find something at night. But all and all it was a nice stay and I would book there again.

“Got the Best Room in the House--4036!” My husband and I just returned from the Marriott Marquis in NYC today. I wanted to write this review while I still remembered every detail of our visit. We stayed for 4 nights and had a fabulous time. The hotel was very clean, quiet, and not any more expensive than the other hotels in the Times Square/Broadway area. If you are looking for a hotel to spend New Year's Eve in, this is the place. They have "Ball Drop View Rooms" available for New Year's Eve that can be booked by calling the hotel directly. I am sure they are EXPENSIVE, but this hotel by far has the best view. Actually, the ball drop is filmed for TV from this hotel! I was torn between rating this hotel as "excellent" or "above average". We only had two problems during our stay. The first was at check in. After navigating the subway from JFK, we arrive at the check in desk only to be informed that the room we reserved was not available. Well, let me explain. It was available, but it would be "$60 dollars more per night." When we reserved a room, we called the hotel directly. My husband was on business and got a special rate that was offered through the company he was coming to visit. The lady on the phone said that the rate quoted was for a "city view room." Well, when we got there, ready to check in, I asked if they had any rooms overlooking Times Square. The man at the desk said, "Yes. For $60 more per night. You can't have the Times Square view room for this company's rate." And, I said, o.k. then, we'll just take the "city view room" that is included in the rate. And, again he says, "No, the Times Square view room is $60 more per night." And, I say, "Well, what is a "city view" room?" and he doesn't answer. He just stands there looking at me. Now, I know there is a difference between a "city view" and "Times Square" view room. I knew that much going into it. There are 4 different faces of the hotel, some looking in directions other than Times Square. But, obviously, this man thought they were one in the same-that "city view" and "Times Square view" were one in the same. I had just heard (via TripAdvisor) that you could ask for upgrades sometimes, especially if you were a Marriott Rewards member-which we are, and they would let you have them. The man at check in acted like I was a complete idiot for mentioning that I was a Marriott Rewards Member and said, "You don't get an upgrade for that!" Well, according to TripAdvisor, lots of people do. But, we must not have been one of those people. So, if you expect to be getting freebies just because you are part of the "club", I wouldn't count on it. Well, the guy at the desk finally asks if this is our first time at the Marquis. When we said yes, he said, we'll I'll go ahead and let you have a "Times Square View" room then since it is your first time here. Well, finally......Again, I wasn't asking for the best room in the place or anything, I just wanted the "city view" room we had reserved. Meaning, I would like to look at SOMETHING within the confines of New York City. Considering that some on this website have said they got rooms over looking steam vents, I just wanted to make sure we got a room with an actual view. Well, the poor guy must have not understood what I meant, but my complaining paid off! When, we stepped into Room 4036, I about died! We were on the 40th floor, looking DIRECTLY at where they drop the ball for New Year's Eve. Two days before this room would have cost $1000 bucks or more! We had the best view ever and I was so glad I had a bit of a tiff with the guy, if this was my reward! We could even see the Statue of Liberty from this room, as well as Battery Park, and even a slight view of the river from the right side. A few nights, my husand and I turned the couch around to face the window and just sat and stared! Very cool! The other problem is that we were charged more for our room, by about $50 a night. Then, when we checked out, the charges had been corrected. We didn't even have to say anything. But, it did put a hold on our bank for more money than we had anticipated. I would check into how much money they are going to put on your credit card/debit card before you leave the desk. Our rate was $215, but we were charged more than the standard tax and fees. But, miraculously, it cleared itself up. We didn't bother to ask what had happened. As far as the elevators go, they were not a problem. I think people bring the elevator problems on themselves. If you expect to leave 10 minutes before your show and get there on time, you are pushing your luck. We never had a problem with the elevators, save for once, and that time it was only a 10 minute ride or less. We went up and down the elevators at various times of the day too, 7 a.m., 12 noon, 5 p.m., and all throughout the evening. The bed is nice, the couch is nice. Hated the pillows. We came back with sore necks because all the pillows were feather and go flat as soon as you lie down on them. The bathroom and room were both very spacious. The towels were some of the best hotel towels I've ever used. Very fluffy and soft. There is a fitness center, but we never used it. There is no pool, which could be disappointing to the kiddies. But, the view was fantasic and we would go back--just for the view and location of the hotel alone.

“Staff has can do attitude, clean, rooms quiet & comfy” Are all Embassy's the same? Absolutely not! This one is a cut above the rest. Why? Staff -- all my encounters were pleasant. From Robert who shuttled me from airport the 1st day (he's a very special individual -- good guy!) to the checkin at the front desk, to the perky bartender at the Mgr's reception (love her "tower o' one's"... how fun for both her and us!). Heck, even the busser who cleared tables at breakfast was cheerful and pleasant. And a huge shout out to the folks who worked front desk in the evening! I had forgotten to pack my BB charger -- she cheerfully lent me her personal charger to use -- WOW! That's trust and service. It's the little things in life. Rooms: Beds comfy. Place is quiet (visited during the week). Rooms nice and clean -- they have good housekeepers. Next time I'm in the Columbus area, I will book again. Keep it up!

“Great X'mas stay” We have stayed at Humphrey's Half Moon for three nights in December 2003. It has a great location, convenient to everywhere in the city. I love its restaurant with a wonderful view of the marina. They have live Jazz band almost every night and those band are usually pretty good. Listening to the wonderful Jazz music while enjoying the view of Christmas lights from all of those boats in the marina. What a treat! We were very satisfied with out stay. However, the carpet in our room was outdated, definitely needs to be changed.

“High marks all around” I don't usually give five stars but this hotel deserved it. The room was nicely appointed, with tons of pillows. While neither the room or the bathroom were huge they were adequate size. It was, by far, the quietest room I have stayed at in years. The hotel staff were very nice, efficient and helpful in every request. Perhaps the only change I would make is that the bed was sort of hard, but that is trivial compared to the plusses this place has. The hotel is about 100 years old and has that "classic" old hotel look. It has obviously been refurbished and they maintained the traditional wihle upgrading it. The meeting rooms were, again, quiet and the service was remarkable. Although I did not personally have dinner in the French restaurant downstairs several people I was meeting with did and they said it was elegant and worth every penny. For a business meeting it would be hard to beat this place.

“Good Choice at PHL” The Sheraton Suites, Philadelphia airport is a very nice, atrium-style hotel and you will like it. Large, two bedroom rooms, two flat screen TVS, lots of pillows, above average bathroom, nice amenities, and a friendly front desk staff. My room faced the freeway, but the sound proofing kept it quiet. Included free coffee maker (Starbucks) and newspaper (in the lobby). There is a charge for the in-room Internet, but you can get 3 hours free in the lobby; my 3rd floor room could pick-up the lobby wireless . There is a $7/night car parking charge. The airport pick up was a little slow, so you might call when you land; the shuttle is the same for Sheraton, Aloft, and 4-points. I recommend this hotel as one of the best, especially if you get a good rate Separately, rental cars in Philadelphia are extremely expensive. You can rent from Enterprise at the auto-mall center (not the same place the airport shuttle will take you) for 1/3 the airport price. Enterprise can pick you up at the hotel, or you can walk from the Sheraton in 20 minutes.

“Great place to stay and hold an event” I really like the newly remodeled event room hallway. Looks good and helps keep hallway noise out of the event rooms too. Event staff was - as usual - very responsive to needs enabling us to conduct a very successful event. Guest room was very clean, quiet and comfortable. Another enjoyable stay.

“Nice Hotel, Good Location” Stayed here for one night while on a business trip in NYC. The room was clean and comfortable, staff was friendly, and the location was within walking distance of a number of tourist attractions in NYC. I was attending a conference at the Jacob Javits Center and chose to stay at this hotel since it was within walking distance to the convention center. You can walk to the hotel from Penn Station in less than 15 minutes. When you arrive, there is a small check-in area on your left. Upon check-in, they give you a delicious warm chocolate chip walnut cookie. The check-in process was quick and they had me on the 11th floor with a king sized bed. There are two elevators and I often found myself waiting a bit for them, especially during busy hours like mornings and late afternoons. The hallway to the rooms was bright, clean, and smelled fresh. Like most rooms in NYC, the rooms are on the smaller size, but I was more than comfortable staying here. My room was clean and everything generally seemed to be in good shape and in working order. You'll find the usual stuff inside your room. They also provide a mini-fridge for your use, a small safe, iron, hair dryer, full-length mirror, coat hangers behind the front door, and a small coffee maker. What you won't find though is a luggage rack. The workspace was sufficient for doing some work. Plugs were easily accessible and there was sufficient lighting. There is no free WiFi in the rooms, but there is free WiFi in the lobby. Internet fees were around $15 per 24 hours. The HVAC system worked great in the room, but for some reason it didn't seem to work in the bathroom as there was a noticeable difference in temperature in the bathroom (it was quite warmer). It wasn't so much an issue in the morning when you were taking a shower, but it was a bit too warm the rest of the time. The bathroom had a decent size shower, but you have to reach in quite a bit to turn the shower on, so you get blasted with cold water just trying to turn the shower on. I also found that quite a bit of water leaked out thru the glass door and onto the bathroom floor, so be careful! There is not a whole lot of counter space to put your toiletry items. There are about 45 channels to pick from and they do offer HBO as the premium channel. If you have kids, they do have Nickelodeon and Cartoon, but no Disney. If you have the Lodgenet app on your smartphone, then you can control the tv using the app rather than having to use the remote. All in all, I enjoyed my one night stay here and would not hesitate to stay here again.

“Wonderful Room, Wonderful Service” I stayed here for a week while travelling on business. The room was wonderful - particularly the luxurious bed and expansive bathroom. Service was also great - from check-in to check-out. Lastly, I appreciated the building's LEED NC certification and the opportunities that they have taken toward incorporating green practices into their building operations.

“great girly fun” very feminine hotel with all the touches including nightly turn down service with cookies, bath robes lush bath products, black and white dvd collection. right next to kenmore T and great coffee downstairs too,

“If you like old school hotels then you will be thrilled. Great location too.” If you like the charm of older hotels with charm then you will enjoy this hotel! It has a great location, beautiful lobby. The rooms are quite nice and larger than most hotels in Chicago. The price is fair. If you ask nicely they will usually accommodate you with a view of Michagan Ave. or the lake. You really can't go wrong with this hotel. The service is amazing too. If you are looking for a brand new, cool, trendy hotel with nightlife then this isn't the place for you. This is more like the Fairmount in San Francisco (although without the amazing views of the Fairmount), then you will enjoy this hotel.

“Great hotel!” We arrived earlier than check-in time and our room was not ready. So, we waited till check-in time and it still was not ready. Front Desk then gave us an upgrade to the Executive Suite - 1 King bed and 1 sleeper sofa, huge bathroom, desk and chairs. We valeted our car but the wait was quite long. It's a nice downtown hotel. We stayed there 'cos we wanted to go to the Greek Theatre. It was about 20 mins drive via the city rather than via the freeway. There was a restaurant at the hotel and the food was good. There was a buffet for breakfast on Sunday and we enjoyed that.

“Good hotel, incredibly nice staff” It has nice not extraordinary rooms and riverside rooms have a great view across the St. John River towards most of Jacksonville's high-rises. Internet access and parking free. But the big plus was an incredibly outgoing, friendly and helpful staff. The were superior to the staff at any boutique hotel we've visited.

“Very good convention hotel” The hotel handled our very large convention group with ease. Rooms are pretty standard, but the bed was comfortable, everything worked and the room was clean. Wireless is pricey and parking is exorbitant, but other than that I had no complaints. Rates are high, but considering the superb location and overall comfort of the accommodations, there was value given for the price. Fitness center was well equipped, and the pool and hot tub were fine. If downtown noise (sirens, horns honking, etc.) bothers you, ask for a high floor (it won't eliminate the noise altogether, but with the windows closed, you ought to be OK).

“Good Experience” We had a nice stay at the Hilton Garden. It isn't the most exciting property out there, but there was little to complain about. The staff were very friendly at the front desk and elsewhere. Everything in our room worked well and the tv was modern. Given that I had to work one day in the room, a bonus was the ergonomically friendly desk chair. It was good to have a microwave and large fridge, and free wifi. Our north facing room had a decent view as well. Our bathroom was average size but one small issue is that the plumbing was somewhat noisy. The fitness room was acceptable and it looked like there is an adjacent pool area. There is a Weber Grill onsite - there was an hour wait so we ended up carrying back to our room. Location is excellent - many nearby restaurants, bars, shops and a Trader Joe's and Jewel within a block. The Grand Red Line Station is directly below the property. We received a great value for our room and were pleased with our stay.

“Typically Good Hyatt Hotel” Stayed here for one night on a business trip and won an excellent rate on Priceline. Service was excellent throught out. I wasn't even finished paying for my cab ride before the porter had my luggage at the front desk and practically checked in. Even though I was slumming with the priceline bid, they graciously honored my request for a harbor view smoking room. Since it was pouring outside I ordered room service and the food was pretty good and service was great. Although typical high prices with all sort of fees attached to the actual delivery. Room itselt was your typical Hyatt with sleek finishes, flat screen TV, comfortable bed ect. If you look closely though you could see that there are some places that could use some fresh paint etc, I suspect this is the reason it's a priceline hotel, but still, it wsn't a big deal. Also they charge for internet access. They should really just stop that practice already. It's like charging to watch TV. My only issue is with Priceline not the hotel. This should not be designated as a downtown hotel. I did walk downtown, but it was a good 15 minuute trek. Still, would not hesitate to stay here again.

“Nice Hotel” This hotel is conveniently located across the street from the convention center and has easy access to historical downtown areas. The hotel was very nice and the staff helpful. Wi-fi is available in the lobby and there is a nice bar and restaurant in the lobby. The first room I was placed in had a heater that sounded like a freight train, so they moved me into a different room with no problem. The room that was given to me had beautiful views of the city. The room was clean and roomy. The only negative was in the bathroom. The way that the shower door was designed allowed a lot of water to get on the wall and floor. This continual damage was evident by the peeling wallpaper on the affected wall and puddle of water on the floor after a shower. Other than that, it was a great hotel.

“Great hotel, fresh design” Spent a couple of nights there on a Rocky Mountain trip - what a great hotel! Its location is perfect, in a great area for wandering around. The bathrooms were very modern - glass sinks lit from behind made for a cool glowing effect and the rock wall behind the tub really fit the local style. I'm now hooked on TVs built into mirrors too. The pool was great and the hot tub nice and toasty. Housekeeping added the little touches. The Edge bar is an extremely happening place on Friday nights - was great to sit and watch some games, eat some great food with excellent drinks among an upscale crowd. The bar tenders were top notch too.

“LOVE LOVE LOVE!!” We love a nice short weekend trip to get away from it all, and the Hyatt at Olive 8 is a great place if your destination is downtown Seattle. It is a very new hotel, and were fortunate enough to try it after winning it on a bidding website (the price was still above average, but this was a crazy weekend in Seattle where barely anything could be found for under $300/night, and this is an above average hotel). Worth the splurge, and we felt we got our money's worth. If only our stay was longer, but there's always next time. A true pleasant surprise. We were welcomed upon check in with a map of the area (nice gesture), and we arrived in our room to be wowed by such a nice room we wished our stay was longer. The location was next to none, right next to Pacific Place (a shopper's paradise), and only a short walk from everything else downtown Seattle has to offer. We had previously stayed at the Westin, and this is a much nicer hotel by a long stretch. The bathroom was so nice and modern, and we loved the shower (no tub--which we actually loved). They even had my favourite toothpaste!!! Love the space saving, modern sliding glass door (wish we could do that in our condo back home!) They have free wifi in the lobby, and we wished we had a chance to try Urbane, which was always bustling. We wished we had the time to try the steam room/pool, but there was so much to do (Seattle has so many nice restaurants--try the Ponti Seafood Grill--a drive away in the University district, or walk to the Hunt Club in the old Sorrento Hotel for the $30 prime rib special). Would be back in a heartbeat! TIP: If you are on a budget you can self-park overnight in Pacific Place (2 blocks away). It was very secure, and even though the overnight rate is $28/night we lucked out and only paid $11 and we entered before the 5pm!) The people in the parkade were a bit confusing, but I think it was a summer parking special. The rate is cheaper if you enter after 5pm I believe.

“A Somewhat Dated Classic” The location is great. The staff is attentive, and the rooms are comfortable. Some areas feel like they need a renovation, but overall I was pleased with my stay.
