There's a more formal and upscale bar called the 720 South Bar and Grill as well as the less formal Kitty O'Shea's. The latter featured a live Irish band the night we were there.

“Great Hotel - quieter than you think!” I spent 4 days at the Millennium Broadway - The Premier Hotel side. Dispite the close proximity to Times Square, this hotel was nice and quiet. If you are in the main tower you have great views of Times Square, which is just a few steps from the hotel's entrance. The room was clean, airy and bright. Huge windows (floor to ceiling) lets alot of light in and you can see the action below. The bathroom was emmaculate, fresh towels and the bath ammenities are very luxurious. The bed was very comfortable and I loved the down comforter. The concierge and other staff are all very friendly and pleasant. I would highly recommend this to anyone who is traveling to NYC for business or pleasure. Access to shows, restuarants, etc is excellent. For those driving, there's a parking lot one block over that has 10.00 over night parking.

“Verified - a Great Super 8 with Unexpected Touches of Luxury” Not only was this hotel new, fresh, clean and super quiet, it was very reasonably priced and offered such unexpected luxuries such as a pillow menu, bathrobes (!), a free breakfast that included fresh waffles, eggs and bacon; and a free shuttle back and forth to the airport. Rooms include refrigerators and microwaves. A small nit is that everything closes down - including the hamburger fast food next door and all of the food deliveries - by 10:00 at night. When we arrived at the Austin airport at 8:30 pm there was no way to get ANY food (we found this extremely odd). There are a few items behind the desk but without a car it is easy to starve on a later arrival in Austin!

“Fabulous front desk staff!” What a great find! The location is just brilliant, plenty of great restaurants and bars within an easy walk and the trolley right outside the door. Although our room on the 6th floor actually overlooked the trolley stop it wasn't noisy at all. The only fault about the stay was the sporadic internet on our floor--we had to go to the lobby to get a decent connection. The front desk staff were superb. So friendly and welcoming was sad to leave. What a fabulous advert they are for this place.

“Nice, like most of the newly remodeled Expresses.” Excellent rooms, newly furnished. Better than average breakfast. Not close to anything interesting though. Also, in the rooms with two beds, the beds are full size not queen, so if you have two teenagers like us, you will need two rooms, or squeeze into those tiny beds. I've noticed more hotels are doing this.

“Everyone Deserves an Executive Level Stay: Add to your bucket list!” Full disclosure: I have stayed many times at the Palmer House Hilton when I lived on the East Coast and visited Chicago frequently. Most often I utilized Priceline and other on-line services because I am an seasoned bargain hunter. One cannot imagine a more grand lobby, which harkens back to the days when craftsmanship and style were appreciated. The rooms have indeed varied in size as pointed out by many reviewers. However, I won a Mother's Day prize from this hotel and took my Mom for an overnight. What a tremendous experience, filled with delightful surprises from start to finish! Dianna Freiss made the arrangements for us, and even after some changes from my Mom Dianna remained the ultimate gracious professional. The lobby, always a selling point before, was taken in methodically during our afternoon tea. That is the perfect time to study the architectural details which put a smile on my face. Each time I looked up I saw something new, or at least saw it in a better light. Our waiter was cordial and charming, and offered my Mom some champagne. The champagne was at the level one should expect from a luxury hotel, and Mom's cheeks were pink from either the alcohol or the smiles. The service was precise, the offerings for tea featured some brands I have not seen in my travels (order the citrus tea and your eyes will roll back in your head), and the selection of sandwiches and sweets was well balanced. We were offered a room on the Executive Level and having experienced the difference I will not waste quality time haggling over a few dollars on the internet ever again. Two full beds featured triple sheets and down comforters with emblematic French tapestry reflecting the other French accoutrements of the room. Mama bowed out of plans to tour the Art Institute because she realized how this special upgrade was to be savored. We each relaxed in separate full baths until it was time for hors d'oevres and conversation one floor above ours. Both of us are people watchers, and were fascinated with the myriad languages we heard and the stories we designed in our fantasy world. Although the small tables were all taken when we arrived, by the time we made our way through the buffet seats were available. We easily struck up conversations with other women travelers who elicited advice on sites in downtown Chicago that should not be missed. It felt like a lovely cocktail party and we stayed for at least an hour. Returning to the room, I noticed the added level of security for the Executive Level: a separate elevator that required a room key to operate. I consider this an important feature for females traveling solo. Naturally, Mom was impressed with the inroom safe for the same reason. Back to the room: each of us had a separate closet in addition to the abundance of drawers in the TV armoire. There was also a comfy chair and what appeared to be a pull-out sofa in front of the wide screen TV. The desk was equipped with wifi options and electrical outlets were plentiful: perfect for a business traveler or a long term stay. I will return with my hubby when he can free himself up from work. It will be such a treat for us! It was also a comfort to note many security guards who were very attentive. Indeed, I spoke with Dave and told him I might apply for a part-time position undercover! This is an environment I could drink in while working.

“Unbelievable room in an unbelievable location!” My wife and I were booked into a room at this hotel by our cousin, for one night the Saturday before Christmas. What a room! It was a suite with an incredible view out the window, looking down onto TImes Square. The staff was friendly, efficient and top-notch, which was especially appreciated because we arrived late in the day and the lobby was under construction (in the midst of a huge renovation), conditions that usually lead to a long wait in line and abrupt service. In this case, however, everything was perfect.

“Awesome hotel - but the noise !!!!” This Hilton is in an awesome location. I stayed for 6 nights and enjoyed it very much apart from one check-in issue and the noise from the heavy rail line. The hotel is located right at the gateway to the Gas Lamp Quarter restaurant area. A very short walk to Petco Park for Padres baseball and Convention Centre is right out front across the railway and trolley lines. The trolley station is right out front. RAILWAY NOISE: The trolley service (light rail) passes right beside the hotel and is great for getting around and for the most part this is a very quiet service. Unfortunately the heavy rail line also passes alongside the trolley tracks and the train drivers blow their very high pitched air horns numerous times as they pass by the hotel over 2 level crossings. There are numerous late evening and early morning trains that pass the hotel and this is very loud. My room was very good and i enjoyed the western view. Bed was comfortable and windows opened to allow fresh air and a respite from the constant air conditioning. The high speed internet is pretty fast both ethernet and wi-fi available although it is no longer complimentary. I booked the room at the Hilton website six weeks prior to my arrival and i was advised that internet was complimentary. Upon check-in I was advised payment was required for internet. I queried this with the check-in staff and she checked with supervisor and i was still asked to pay. I insisted and she asked supervisor a second time and complimentary internet was finally granted. This was my only hiccup at this hotel.

“Great hotel, full of "extras"” The Fairmont is a pretty reliable higher-end hotel. It had really intricate Christmas decorations in the lobby, a HUGE room and bathroom (although maybe I'm just biased from recent Europe travels), and friendly staff. However, the things I really enjoyed were the extras that didn't really have much to do with my room. The lobby provided live entertainment each night I stayed there (e.g. dueling pianos playing Coldplay, jazz band, etc.) and the lobby has a ridiculously long (500ish or so) martini menu. And the steak restaurant (Grill On The Alley) provided a very delicious meal, with all the balsamic you want for your bread (a plus in my book). It felt very business-y and is a little spendy, so I wouldn't likely stay here casually; however, for business or if you have the funds, the Fairmont San Jose is a great choice.

“A Nice Stay and a Good Location” Even though we live in the DC Metro area, we decided to spend a night in DC for two reasons: 1) we were seeing an evening performance of a play and; 2) we needed one more night to maintain our current level in the Marriott Rewards program. Ten Marriott properties were showing availability on the night of the play and the main reason we chose this hotel was price---it was the cheapest of the ten. However, before booking, we checked the previous reviews on this site and found that, overall, they were good. The hotel is a five-minute leisurely walk from the Gallery Place/Chinatown Metro station. If you do use Metro to get to this hotel, be sure to use the 9th Street exit. After exiting, just walk two blocks to the hotel. You'll know if you're heading in the right direction if you cross G Street. Check-in went smoothly and the desk clerk was friendly and helpful. We were given a room on the 9th floor of the Club Tower which is accessed by a separate bank of elevators. I don't know if there really is any difference in the rooms in this tower as opposed to the other tower. From seeing pictures taken by other reviewers, I'm guessing there isn't much--if any. However, in the Club Tower there is a club lounge which is only open on weekdays. Our room had a view of the parking lot across the street and if you look to the left, you can see the top of the Washington Monument. The bed in the room was comfortable. Plus the room was a good size---not cramped at all with more than one seat other than the desk chair. The shower had good water pressure and you are able to adjust the water flow---a nice touch. Toiletries included, lotion, shampoo, conditioner, "boot butter" and a "basic beauty kit" (2 cotton balls plus 2 q-tips!). We requested a refrigerator and the hotel honored that request. When we made the reservation, we were told that not all rooms had a fridge, so if you want one, be sure to request one when making your reservation. In addition, there were 2 plush bathrobes in the closet. The closet was above average size when it comes hotel room closets. We ate breakfast at the hotel restaurant which offered a breakfast buffet with eggs cooked to order. Service was great and the food was quite decent if overpriced (which is often the case in hotel restaurants). I feel that the hotel does have a captive audience at breakfast time since there appeared to be no restaurants in the immediate vicinity that were open for breakfast. Otherwise, there are some highly rated restaurants within walking distance, such as Zaytinya, Oya, Ella's Wood-Fired Pizza, and Matchbox---to name a few. If you take the Megabus to DC---there is a drop-off and pick-up point in the parking lot across the street. Would we stay here again? Certainly! The place was kept very clean and it more than met our needs. Just note---this Renaissance is a 3-diamond property. That's my one beef with Marriott---they have set up Renaissance and JW Marriott as their upscale, luxury brands yet not all are 4-diamond properties. I do wish Marriott was more consistent when it came to this. Still, we did enjoy our stay here.

“SUper location, walking distance to shopping and restaurants” Room was comfy, two double beds, but no slippers. Great bar/restaurant inside hotel for late lunch. They triple charged internet because of three devices, but then took two off when we checked the bill. All ok.

“A real find -- homey feel in a wonderful location” The Magic Castle is a real gem. Less than two blocks from the Kodak and Grauman theaters in Hollywood, but it feels like you are staying in a local apartment complex with a very friendly landlord. The rooms are a bit worn and scuffed, but that's OK given that they are spacious, clean and comfortable. The staff is extremely friendly and helpful. Our kids loved the free snacks and DVDs, and the coffee provided with the continental breakfast was as good as the best coffehouses. The location can't be beat -- walk to Hollywood Boulevard, and a short drive to Burbank, Griffith Park, Beverly Hills, or downtown L.A. We would definitely stay here again.

“Well located, comfortable and Spacious rooms” I stayed at Sofitel Los Angeles for 4 nights with my wife. We enjoyed a lot! Wonderful building, spacious rooms, comfortable and getle staffs! Located infront off the Beverly Shopping!

“Okay, but not up to par to other Kimpton hotels” My husband and I travel quite a bit and have started to prefer Kimpton hotels. We stayed at the Palomar on business, because of its location to our conference. The staff at the Palomar are fairly responsive - especially the bus & valet staff. The evening wine reception is nice as is the lobby area. We did eat at the restaurant, which was good. Even though we booked under two different room rates (one rate for 2 nights, a second rate for the 3rd night), we were told by the reservation agent that we wouldn't have to change rooms. However, on the third day, we found our room keys did not work in our lock after we returned from working a long day - the front desk staff (I assume) had essentially checked us out (without leaving any messages for us) and we had to get new keys made twice, as well as have a staff member come up. The rooms are a bit noisy - we also heard doors slamming shut in the hallways, as other reviewers have mentioned. We did not have a coffee maker in the room when we checked in, so ended up ordering very expensive continental room service the next morning. But a coffee maker appeared the second day without our having to ask, which was very convenient. Other room amenities were up to par for a 'luxury' hotel. We did not have the opportunity to use the pool or fitness room, so cannot comment on those.

“A beautiful historic building that has to be seen” My husband and I have just returned from the Custom House in Boston and our opinion is as follows: 1. Beautifully decorated and comfortable rooms with loads of wardrobe space. 2. Extremely helpful front desk, porters and concierge. 3. Location simply marvellous with wonderful restaurants at your doorstep. 4. Shopping to die for ! if you have a car try to visit Wrentham outlet mall - terrific and no state tax in Boston ! 5. This is a simply wonderful Historic Building right in the heart of the city that Marriott must be very proud to have. 6. This is our second time here and we will, definitely, return. 7. Your towels are changed and your bins emptied every day at no extra charge. I have read a review where the person wasn't happy you have to push a button to open the main door ? firstly, it can be freezing in Boston and this is an automatic closing door that can't be left open accidentally and, secondly, this is for security as if you are out after 9pm you have a pass card to use, if not you shouldn't be entering without first speaking to the valet. On the 1st floor Continental breakfast is served between 7-10am weekdays and 7-11 weekends. This breakfast is more than adequate and has just about everything you could possibly want with free tea/coffee/hot chocolate. There is also a cocktail lounge open from 6pm onwards. Nearby, you have a variety of wonderful restaurants as well as Quincy Market. We walked the whole of the city and thoroughly enjoyed ourselved in Boston. Finally, you can if you have a car take a trip out to Cape Cod or Rhode Island which aren't too far away. Cape Cod is about 1hr and its best to have lunch at one of the restaurants down by the marina as they are lovely and have a view of the sea. Hope this helps, when I have loaded my photos onto the computer I will post one of the inside of the Custom House which will show the beauty of it.

“Convenient place for us to explore Phoenix” We stayed here for a week with a good coupon rate. The location worked great for us. We had a room with a king size bed, desk, fridge, microwave and a comfortable chair with a foot rest on the top floor facing North. The room itself was a little on the small side, but comfortable.We could park our car under our window, the lot was well lit. The breakfast had quite a bit of variety and the area was pleasant and clean. We were told the pool would be heated but it was not. The hot tub was fine. The staff was helpful and great to talk to. The only negative thing we had to mention was a very inconsiderate janitor.

“Great location!” My boyfriend and I stayed at the Omni 2/21 – 2/24 (Thursday – Sunday). I found a great rate of $219/night – probably due to it being off-season. I’m an Omni Select Guest member and we were upgraded to a deluxe King room. I requested to be away from construction as I had read of some complaints. We were right on 52nd street and didn’t hear a bit of construction. The room was quite large for NYC and had a sitting area with loveseat. The bathroom was clean and included a shower/bathtub combo. The TV is a bit small, but when in NYC, who watches a bunch of TV? As an Omni Select Guest, you get a free newspaper and 2 free beverages in the morning (you can pick what time they bring it). I thought this was a very nice touch and they were right on time with our coffee and juice each morning. There is an umbrella in the room, which came in handy on our trip. My only minor complaint about the room would be the towels and bathrobes seemed a bit dingy for a 4 star hotel, but really not that big of a deal. Turn-down service is offered nightly. The location is great, just a block off of 5th Ave. There is a subway station very close at 53rd and 5th Ave. that has the E line. There is also a close subway station at 51st and Lexington that has the 6 line. Since the weather was very cold on our trip (the biggest snow storm in 2 years!), we decided to cab it to Broadway shows at night. I think this could be walkable in better weather. However, there were often not cabs available and we often took the town cars that wait outside the hotel (for probably double the rate). This is probably not the hotel’s fault, but I wondered if there is some deal with the town cars and the hotel. Or maybe it was just the bad weather causing a lack of cabs. We were able to check in right away (even though we arrived at 11am) and also were granted late check out on our last day. We didn’t eat at the hotel, but the Fireside restaurant looked nice. I would definitely stay at this hotel again if I found a good rate. Any questions, feel free to PM me.

“Best resort in Texas and one of the top resorts I have stayed at.” Spent 4 nights at this awesome resort the weekend of the Texas Valero open. Ironically I was not there for the golf tournament. First I have to say the service was excellent, as good or better then a four seasons resort. They could not have been more helpful or attentive. Came from Houston, quick drive. From the moment we arrived, the valet and bell service was very helpful and fast. Check in was a breeze and on a busy weekend we recieved and awesome Junior suite. Room was very well appointed and the beds were comfortable and bathrooms overall rooms were big. The restaurants were outstanding, the sports bar was the coolest I have ever seen, The pool is the highlight, lazy river, slides you need tubes to go down, adult pool and hot tub. Did I mention how family friendly this place is. The sports bar/club is so cool with its 150 foot televisions.. What I was most impressed with the physical structure, design and materials used. Just beautiful and first class. The kids club and the employees were awesome, so much so when given a choice of swimming or the club, they chose the club Did I mention that there is great shopping near by and if you care to go to the riverwalk, it is 20 minutes away with no traffic, but why? Did not get to use the spa, but they have a nice workout room and I here the spa is the best in Texas.

“Very nice” Great hotel, comfortable beds...what else can you ask for? The rooms were pretty small. We were upgraded to a King room (thank goodness for gold membership), and that was small compared to other Marriott properties in NYC, so I can only imagine what the other rooms looked like. The bathroom was very small as well. The hotel was decorated very nicely and was clean. The elevators and halls were kind of narrow, but I realize it's an older building so that's to be expected. The worst thing about our room was there was some sort of generator outside our window that ran all night. Once we were asleep, it didn't bother us. We were on the fourth floor, so you can definitely hear the sirens and horns and crowd across the street at Pranna. But it wasn't too distracting. Just reminded me of what I've missed since leaving NY. We did not get a chance to eat at the restaurant or enjoy the lounge, but it seemed pretty nice, from just peeking in. Would I stay here again? Yes. Would it be at the top of my list? Probably not. I like coming out into the action, and it was a little too quiet for me.

“Great value for this area, consistent with the Hyatt Place brand” Great value for the price. As with all the Hyatt Places we have been, the rooms are great. The layout is very similar just like if you are visiting Target stores across the country, you can find your way around easily. Beds are comfortable and bathrooms are clean. This one is no exception. We were able to use the exercise facilities and pool and took advantage of the free breakfast which were all decent. The hotel is a bit older than some other H.P. properties but you can't notice much of a difference. Did not interact with staff much but the housestaff kept the room clean the whole week we were there so that is a plus. We didn't experience any problems so overall a great value for the price paid.

“Perfect for business or city weekend” I have been trying different locations in Boston and this is clearly a greta hotel in Boston. Location is perfect as you are in the centre of Boston walking distance to most things, including the subway. The complex has the Westin at one end and the Marriott at the other end with a great mall in the middle, with trendy brands like Louis Vuitton, Boss, Zegna, etc and department stores like Barneys or Neiman Marcus and adjacent to the Prudential Center and convention. There are a number of restaurants in the gallery just by the lobby of the hotel before entering the mall, so everything you need is very handy. I was lucky enough to be upgraded to a junior suite due to my gold status and got a great room in a Preferred Guest floor , the 35th floor, so the views were spectacular. See my pics attached.The room was large with a sofa and coffee table besides the desk and the large bed. There was an Ipod/iphone charger and radio, lcd TV, bar, coffee maker, etc. Wifi is not free and you pay for 24 hours or more. I could not get wifi in the lobby, so not sure if they have a free service there. The bathroom was a bit too small for the room, but adequate. The price was excellent and more so if you factor in my free upgrade. I used a Special Offer code I saw here at tripadvisor, so I got the second night at 40% off and same for the 4th night. Great savings. In-room dining was a bit sparse in its diversity but good quality. The lobby bar is a good hangout after work to relax with a drink and catch some sports on their TV. The only thing I do not like, but nothing you can do about it, is that the entrances is one level below the lobby, so you need to go up the escalator to check in. When I arrived no one picked my luggage at around 8 PM (no big deal). But the rest of the days I was there I always saw doormen on call, so I guess I was just unlucky. I plan to go back and next time I will be platinum so I am hoping for a larger suite :-)

“Very good base in Philadelphia” We stayed here for a weekend of sightseeing, with our three children in connecting double bedded rooms. This is a fine central location, next to the glorious city hall and Reading Terminal Food Market (fantastic -- don't pay for Marriott breakfast, go there to eat anything you like!) It's walking distance to all the historical sites and Rittenhouse Square area. The hotel is set back a bit, so there was a nice bright view of surrounding buildings outside our window, and it was quiet for sleeping. The rooms were clean and upbeat -- good Marriott beds, etc. My only complaint is that in spite of our "preferences" in our Marriott reservation, no rooms were assigned until we actually arrived -- ie, if there had been no connecting rooms left at the moment we arrived, we would have been separated from our children. (I have found the same problem before and often call the front desk a day in advance to have them block rooms; still, what is the point of the hotel asking for our preferences if they don't actually use them until we ask for them again at check in??)

“Friendly and Wonderful” This hotel is located in an area that is close to the downtown, riverwalk and other attractions. We stayed in the double bed room. This room had ample space where you and another person could relax and enjoy. The room had a safe, flat screen tv(with several channels), ironing board, hair dryer, refrigerator and a bath room with two shower heads(a regular one and a removable one). Staff was very friendly and food was great. Greated with a smile every morning in the restaurant. If there is one thing they should improve one: Parking. You have to drive up a very narrow ramp and there seems to be only 2 levels for parking. Oh you will have to write a note for the "do not disturb sign) one is not provided. This is a very nice find.
“Great Location” Nice Hotel, best of all the staff. Very helpful. Good area to walk to the waterfront and some nice restaurants. We found absolutely nothing wrong with this hotel.

“Superb Experience” No surprises here. The Four Seasons experience is something special, and they deliver the goods. Hotel is extremely well located. Physically, a beautiful grand place that is well-maintained. Redundant staffing is always available to make your stay pleasureable, but is never intrusive. Great Chicago informality, but still invested in giving a high level of service. Seasons offers true fine dining. Check in was easy, and we were given an upgrade. Tasteful room was as silent as a vault, and included a humidifier, which was a great touch in Chicago winters. Room service was excellent and timely. Highly recommended.

“Nice Airport Property-Quality Marriott!” Stayed at this property with my wife for one night before an early AM flight. Won this property on Priceline which I was very pleased about. Have stayed here before and enjoyed our stay then, as much as this time. Arrived very late so didn't get to experience anything extra at the property. However on previous stays enjoyed the pool (indoor very nice) and the lobby bar also very nice. The lobby bar when we checked in at midnight was packed. Very busy, but I view that as a good sign. Check in was incredibly quick, with very nice folks working. We stayed on the lower floor all the way in the back of the property, which is to be expected for a Priceline win. Room was typical Marriott quality so was not disappointed at all. Was not bothered by any noise or door slamming throughout our short stay. Checked out very early and hopped on the 5:45 complimentary shuttle Shuttle leaves every 30 minutes which works great for the short trip to Seatac. There is not much super close to this property besides a 7-11 convenience store, so plan accordingly. I would for sure stay at this property again for a quick overnight stay. Stay here with confidence. Great job as usual Marriott.

“A great choice near the airport!” This hotel was outstanding - I stayed in 5 the same week and this one was the best by far. When I checked in they upgraded me to a "conceire level suite." It was extremely nice - many beautiful pillows, marble bath, nice furniture, nice office area, large tv, nice amenities, etc. The staff were very helpful and prompt ever time I dealt with them. The complimentary breakfast buffet (with my room rate, not all stays) was great. The hotel has a beautiful atirum in the center with a nice pool. Overall, it was an excellent stay - I would definitely stay here again and recommend this hotel!

“Excellent Choice!!! I will definately return!!!” I stayed at the Warwick Hotel from March 4-7th, 2010. I was attending a conference at the New York Hilton but opted to stay at the Warwick which is directly across the street. I made a great choice. The Hilton was nice but, extremely crowded and noisy. I like a smaller hotel. I couldn't wait to get back to the room after meetings and all of the crowds. I felt at home and very secure at the Warwick. The entire staff was extremely friendly and helpful. The room was large and clean. I had a regular room with 2 queen beds. The bedding and linens were quite comfortable. I didn't pay for a view because I knew that I would never be in the room except to sleep. The furnishings were a little dated but, that is the charm of an older hotel. There was a large flat screen TV with many channels.The marble bathroom was really nice. I didn't eat at the restaurant but, the bar was great. There is free internet for guests near the front desk. The Warwick is really one of the nicest hotels in that area. It is close to everything. The MOMA is right across the street and, it is in the vicinity of St. Patrick's Cathedral, Radio City, American Girl, etc. Everything is just a block or 2 away. I gave this hotel excellent reviews because I had the most enjoyable all around stay. I am a native New Yorker and visit quite often. I used to stay at larger hotels but, since I found the Warwick, I will be staying there!!!!

“Airport Convenience” Did park and stay here with an early flight. Very nice facilities, larger rooms, usual amenities all of which was somewhat wasted on us as we got in, slept and left. That is the only reason I didn't rate them tops on value, I wouldn't mind fewer amenities and a smaller room for a smaller price - oh well, it was the best deal amongst the competition that I found. The value gets better of course the longer you park - I think they will give you up to 10 free days parking for 1 night lodging if you're a Choice Gold or better. Speaking of our primary purpose the shuttle to the airport left right on time. We got lucky on the return and only had to wait about 5 minutes for pick-up. One other minor fringe benefit of parking here as opposed to the city economy lot (which otherwise is one of the better I use) is heading to the beltway you don't have to take that left turn off Greens onto JFK which I find challenging at the best of times and really problemmatic in the dark when jet-lagged.

“Exactly what I hoped it would be” As you can see there are so many positive reviews of this hotel so I figured I couldn't go wrong. I'm glad I chose the Pod. I was in the city from July 30 - Aug 1 on my own so I knew I did not need a large room. My twin bed was the perfect size. I liked the fact that the room had a sink so I didn't have to go to a bathroom to brush my teeth or wash my hands. Housekeeping was provided daily with fresh towels. The bathrooms were very clean. I checked out 3 of them on my floor ( I was on the 5th floor). The showers were wonderful. I do have 2 minor complaints about the bathroom though. There were no paper towels or even paper towel dispensers in any of the bathrooms. I found this very strange b/c there was a soap dispenser by the sink. Weird and inconvenient. Also, I had to pull the doors with both hands to close it. It seemed as though the doors had swollen so they were very hard to close. Once I put the deadbolt on it was fine though. I read a few negative reviews about the front desk staff being rude. I never encountered this. The 2 gentleman that checked me in and out were friendly enough. The concierge was also very helpful in recommending lunch options for me. I highly recommend this hotel if you are only looking for a clean, safe place to sleep and shower while in NYC! I will be visiting again.

“Pleasant stay, wonderful breakfest, attentive staff.....best kept secret in fort worth..” Staying over the weekend due to power outage throughout the are (snow) attentive staff, helped out with needs and special requests. pleasant atmosphere, nice rooms. A must stay when your in Fort Worth.,

“Charming Downtown Boutique” The Madison is an interesting boutique hotel in downtown Memphis. Built in an old bank building, the hotel utilized the vault as it's gym. The lobby has a grand staircase, and the rooms are large and comfortable. Additionally, the bathrooms are very nice (which my wife really appreciated.) The service was good, not great, and the location was pretty good for access to Memphis' street cars. If you are traveling to Memphis and want upscale accomodations without the Peabody price, the Madison is a great alternative.

“Deca is a delight!” Props to Priceline for turning me onto this great boutique hotel. I got a great rate on a wonderful hotel in a nice location. I reserved a room with a king, but when I checked in they didn't have one available. As a result, I was upgraded to a suite with two queen beds. It was a great room and I have zero complaints. Staff is very friendly and quick to respond to any requests; I forgot a toothbrush (doh!) and one was brought to me within minutes. Parking, internet access and breakfast are complimentary. The wifi connection is available throughout the hotel, which makes sitting in front of the fireplace in their gorgeous lobby to catch up on work a nice option.

“Nice addition to Denver!” My husband and I live in Denver, and had the opportunity for 24 hours on our own while family members watched our kids, so we decided to try out the Ritz. Generally speaking, we try to stay at Four Seasons when looking for a luxury experience, but of course that's not an option in Denver. This Ritz actually surprised us - it's much more Four Seasons-like than the other Ritzes I have been to. Very contemporary and more understated than the typical Ritz. Valet was friendly and prompt, no problems there. Valet was $25 overnight, but it's a Ritz and it's downtown, what do you expect? (As a side note, if you go there to use the spa, valet parking is free.) We were offered bell services but didn't need any assistance since we had one tiny suitcase between the two of us. Front desk staff were very professional and friendly, very easy check-in process. The rooms are huge with unique and beautiful hardwood entry. Beds were comfortable with very nice linens. Flat screen HDTV I think was 32". There was an espresso maker in the room - we didn't use it but what a nice touch! The view was of another building - the location of the hotel isn't great for mountain views and I was told that the only rooms with mountain views are the suites. I see the mountains every day so I didn't care much, but it's too bad that out of town visitors won't get a nice Colorado view. Bathroom was very nice, separate shower and large tub, double sinks and separate water closet. Shaving mirror in the shower was nice for my husband, and water pressure was fine. Frette towels were terrific and the toiletries smelled great. I loved that they had a full sized Ionic hairdryer in the room. I have to admit I am a bit perplexed by the location. The hotel used to be an Embassy Suites so I can see the appeal of renovating an existing building, but I can't say I'd expect to see a Ritz directly across the street from the Greyhound station. While the location is pretty good in terms of being a short walk to many attractions, restaurants, etc., you're still stepping over a lot of homeless people and the bus station and immediate area is a bit sketchy, particularly at night. We ate both dinner and breakfast at Elway's - the only restaurant on site. (Though there are many others close by.) We weren't terribly impressed with the dinner. The food all seemed to be overseasoned and the tuna appetizer we ordered was just OK - lacking in imagination. Our steaks were both overcooked. The manager came over (we didn't really complain, just asked that our steaks be redone) to apologize and comped our entire meal other than drinks. It wasn't awful - I'd give it another try if Denver didn't have so many other choices for a steak dinner - Morton's, Sullivan's and Capital Grille are all superior choices and all reasonably close. We had dessert via room service - a warm brownie with ice cream, and it was delicious. The breakfast, though expensive, was quite good. We both booked appointments at the spa. I have been waiting for a luxury hotel with spa to open in Denver because the day spas, though plentiful and many upscale, don't give the same relaxation, in my opinion. The Ritz spa has a beautiful locker room and two relaxation rooms - one where the therapist comes to get you for the appointment, and the other where you won't be bothered at all. (Different rooms for men and women.) The locker room has several showers with dual shower heads, a steam room, whirlpool, and plenty of space and products to get showered and dressed. Towels and bathrobes were soft and fluffy as you'd expect. Relaxation room had cozy chaise lounge chairs, magazines of course, fruit water, tea, nuts and fruit. I discovered a few minor problems and all were taken care of immediately by the attentive staff. My massage was wonderful, and I'd highly recommend the lime blossom scalp treatment - smells amazing. We did not use the gym, though it is a gym that my husband used to belong to before it was renovated and linked to the Ritz. We did take a walk through it. It's a full-service gym, you won't be waiting in line for anything or find that it's lacking in equipment. Overall, I loved it and would recommend the Ritz Denver to anyone. We were also astonished at the price - $199 a night! The hotel was booked solid when we were there, so I'd be surprised if that price sticks around long. If we have the chance to stay again we definitely will, even if the price does go up.

“A True 4-Star/Great stay.” I got this place through a priceline bid for 99$ and it was definitely worth it. Hotel has kind of a business/boutique feel to it. They granted early check in and I received, big, comfy, trendy room/bathroom on 17th floor. View faced south so not much there except for other buildings but views on north side were probably quite nice with Coit tower and the Bay/Alcatraz. I liked the old school honor bar that allows you to store leftovers etc. without tripping a sensor that adds an immediate charge. Nice plush bathrobe and umbrella provided. No coffeemaker in room but there is free Starbucks provided in lobby in the AM which is actually preferable to the the non-dairy creamer/not enough sugar kit that one usually receives with the in-room coffee set-up. The hotel is located in the heart of the financial district about 1 block east of the TransAmerica tower. I think many tourists are turned off by this area as it's sort of dead on weekends and opt for hotels in/around Union Square and personally I hope it stays that way. I think you get more bang for your buck staying in the financial district and the proximity to Chinatown and North Beach make the dining options far more desirable than the bustling Union Square. Proximity to BART/MUNI is also a plus and you avoid the very aggressive panhandlers that populate the Powell/Market area.There is a movie theater right across the street form Le Meridien along with the Embarcadero Mall. I highly recommend this hotel.

“Perfect location - lovely hotel” This hotel is perfectly located for exploring the interesting city of Seattle, about half-way between Pioneer Square and Pike Place Market and only two blocks from the waterfront. The hotel is in a lovely old building and the rooms are decorated beautifully. My room , 401, looked out over 1st Avenue. If you keep the windows closed, you will not be bothered by the busy traffic below. If you want to keep the windows open, ask for a room away from that street. My room had a living area with a fireplace, couch, two chairs, coffee table and a second TV. It was very nice, although somewhat dark because the room was a narrow rectangle with windows at the narrow end. Fortunately, there were plenty of lamps. The bathroom was not large but was adequate and was nicely equipped with a great showerhead. Towels were thick and fluffy. I have learned that I must ask to have a coffee maker brought to the room as they are not furnished as a standard feature. I also always have to ask to have more than the one or two coffee packets provided each day. The staff was friendly and efficient and responded promptly to any request. The breakfast, which was not included in the room rate, was first rate. Because the servers at breakfast do double duty as hosts/hostesses, on two of my three mornings there I had to wait for some time for someone to acknowledge me and seat me, because they were busy serving people or in the kitchen. A host/hostess would be nice. This was only the second Kimpton I have stayed in and I am quite impressed with the level of service and the uniqueness of the properties. You never feel like you are staying in a large chain hotel. I highly recommend it.

“Great stay!” Had a work christmas party/event in Seattle and wanted to stay the night in the city so we chose Inn at the Market after hearing great things about it. We are very happy we did. What a nice hotel! The checkin process was easy and they even had warm freshly baked cookies at the desk to eat. The room was pretty nice with everything we needed. The bathroom was a nice size. We had a city view room due to all the water view rooms being taken already. The only odd thing about the room was that the bed wasn't facing the tv. But certainly no biggie there. Both the room and lobby were very clean. Location is nice despite the many homeless people you tend to see outside the hotel. Not a bad place to stay at all. I'd recommend it to anyone staying in Seattle.

“Anniversary Weekend Getaway "Stay-cation"” Wanted to take a quick "stay-cation" in Denver. We decided to stay at the Hyatt Regency. We booked using the AAA breakfast rate which included a full breakfast the next morning. When I booked the room I had requested a high room with city views not near an elevator, ALL of which they were able to accommodate. I also spoke to Kahlan (spelling?), concierge, who was able to find 2 long stemmed roses for my wife and wrote a card. She did an outstanding job of making our stay memorable. The only surprise during our stay was the parking cost, it was not clear on the website that parking would cost $25.00 for self park or $30.00 for valet parking. I expected to pay for parking, but this was higher than I had planned for. Please be aware of this when booking. That being said, the valet employees were efficient and pleasant. We checked into the front desk with Jackie, she used our names several times, wished us a Happy Anniversary and also re-confirmed all of our requests and that they had all been met. We were on the 36th floor and had AMAZING city views (see attached photos). If you are afraid of elevators, I would NOT recommend staying above floor 25 as the elevators speed from floor 1 to 25 on the upper floors on a separate set of elevators, so fast that it pops your ears. The room was beautiful, we had a King Bed room. The bedding was soft and high end. The room was exceptionally clean and well maintained. Flat screen LCD TV and available internet @ $10.00/day for standard speed and $13.00/day for higher speed. The window can open to allow fresh air which is a nice amenity. The hot tub was on the 5th floor with the health club outside. The hot tub was metal which looks nice, but is very slippery so it makes it difficult to sit back and not slide off the seat. Hot Tub hours run until 8:30PM for everyone, and open until 10PM for adults over 18. This is NOT enforced as a group of 8 young teenagers came to the hot tub around 9:15 and were loud and obnoxious. After dinner at the Yard House on the 16th street mall, we had dessert and coffee at Perks Lounge in the hotel. It had amazing views of the city and was quite busy. We were greeted by a pleasant waitress who brought us waters and a jar of assorted nuts and snacks. We ordered the Fondue dessert which was decent, but over priced for how little fondue we got. Breakfast the next morning was very good, it was what you would expect from a higher end breakfast buffet. They had a large selection of fruit, cereals, waffles, pancakes, scrambled eggs, hash browns, pastries and juices. The waiter was also very nice, they honored our AAA discount without question. Overall it was a great stay and we will be staying again when in Denver.

“Quiet Hotel with Great Staff” I was pleasantly surprised by my experience at the Moderne. The nice-sized room was spotless...the king bed "heavenly." The all-marble bath was as nice as hotels I've stayed at 3 times the price. Lots of steaming hot water too. With just a few rooms per floor the halls were quiet. Yes the elevator is a bit slow but, with only 7 floors I never had a long wait. Also there's a nice coffee lounge on the second floor, overlooking 55th St. The phone had a data port and voicemail too. Yes, the window looks out to a light shaft. But try to get an "o1" room - such as "301"...those tend to have windows looking onto 55th, and are larger. But the staff is what made my stay outstanding. The two young men who alternate at the front desk could not have been more helpful. They really came through was when NYC experienced a serious cold wave just as I was checking in for my 4-day stay. The "high" that day was 4 degrees..with wind-chills at minus ten. I phoned the desk because the room was chilly and, within 15 minutes, the day engineer arrived to adjust the heating unit and clean its filter. But that didn't seem to help so I called the front desk again. In less than an hour someone knocked at my door with a newly purchased portable radiator. Yes, they had actually sent someone out to get this one just for me. The Moderne isn't fancy and there are a few signs of wear. But at the great rate I found thru Hotels.com it was an uncommon value for NYC. And to be just 2-3 blocks from most theatres, numerous restaurants, and two subway stations....I'll be back!

“Absolutely Perfect in Every Way!” We recently stayed at the Hotel Commonwealth while visiting BU with our 16 yr old. ( Note to parents of BU prospective students or current ones, this hotel is directly across the street from campus. Very well located for visiting!!) From the moment we pulled up to the moment we departed, everything at this hotel was perfect! The front desk was wonderful, our room overlooked Fenway Park, and we had a huge room with two large beds and a sitting area as well! The women at the front desk were very friendly, helpful, and very welcoming. If I could live at Hotel Commonwealth, I don't see why I would live anywhere else! ha Book it now. You won't regret it. ( yes the parking is steep, but it is Boston. We paid a little bit more for NYC the next day.)

“OK hotel, clean but showing its age...” I was lucky enough to win a priceline.com bid @ $59 for a 3-star hotel and ended up here at the Omni Southpark to visit friends who were in Austin for the week. With rooms normally in the mid-$100 range, I felt this was an amazing deal! As such, I will try to be unbiased in my review and use the normal going rates to judge the property. This hotel is clearly geared towards business travelers attending conventions or businesses in the area. Despite that, the pool area is quite good. The pool itself is neat in that it is both in and outdoors, separated by a swim-under flap. There is a great sauna and hottub inside, and plenty of chaise lounge chairs to sun yourself on. Detracting from the otherwise nice facility are cars and semis zooming by on I-35, which is a stone's throw from the hotel. The rooms were clean, although showing their age. The bathrooms especially could use a makeover since they have old tiled tubs and not the greatest shower heads with lackluster pressure. The bed was comfortable but not as much so as any of the Hilton chain beds. Service at the Omni was outstanding. The front desk accomodated my request for early check-in at 11:30am, and the personnel were very friendly and personable. I would definitely stay here again if on business in the area, but for a leisure visit to Austin, I reckon there are better hotel options to be had for less money.

“Excellent” I was not sure what to expect from this hotel since the reviews were mediocre. I thought everything about this hotel was great! The room was perfect! The location was definitely amazing. The staff was very nice. Check-in was fast and easy and we got the exact type of room we were hoping for.

“All around, a very nice hotel” I stayed here for 20 days over the last year, so it obviously is a favorite of mine. I also found some great deals to stay here. The rooms are large, modern, and comfortable. This is expected at a St. Regis. The restaurants are both very good, with excellent organic produce, fish, etc. The Remede SPA is a must. It is a bit expensive but you will find that the services are worth it. I like that this place is not like the hotels near the square and it does not feel like a tourist trap.

“Nice business hotel downtown” First off, I was impressed that when I got to the hotel at 10 a.m, they had a room ready. I was expecting only to drop my bag and head to a meeting, so I was pleasantly surprised that I was able to put my stuff in a room. The rooms were typical for a business class hotel. Comfortable beds and bedding, clean. The bathrooms were oddly shaped and small, but functional enough. The HVAC seemed a bit noisy but not too bad. There is a Starbucks across the street and Lexi's diner next door for a good,quick breakfast or lunch.

“Read Reviews - Sorry this is Great Hotel” Don't believe the reviews. The check-in staff are great, the rooms are good and they have a free business center! I was a little worried after reading the reviews, but I have to say Crowne Plaza Austin is a very good value hotel.

“FINE HOTEL IN DALLAS ARTS DISTRICT” The Fairmont is a fine hotel in downtown Dallas. Keep in mind that even thought you're in the so-called arts district, good restaurants are hard to come by and the hotel's Starbuck's has limited hours so nighttime repasts are a bit of a challenge. You can have nice bar food in the overly-lit hotel bar (the staff here is the hotel's weak link, with a somewhat attitudinal bar staff) The rooms are clean and comfortable (how I wish the windows would open, however!), ther terrace pool is clean and large and the staff is friendly and helpful. Overall, a fine stay.

“very exceptional hotel” Stayed 2 nights 7/31 with a teenager while on business. Had a double room on the Club floor- Everyone- from check in, to valet, to bellmen and wait staff were extremely friendly and professional. Room was large, and while it had no real view- just inner courtyard, was very clean and comfortable. Housekeeping was more than adequate as was room service. Location is excellent- you are across from the heart of the Inner Harbor. The Club Louge had a nice assortment for breakfast and decent pastries late in the day. Food at hotel restaurant Windows was wonderful- this was especially appreciated after a Disasterous experience at Legal Seafood across the st- and the view is amazing. Yes, carpets in hallway are worn, but so what. This is a really nice hotel. Phillips is a fun place to eat also. However, strongly advise Legal Seafood be avoided. Highly recommend this hotel.

“Awesome for the budget minded!” My friend and I made the decision to stay at the Travelodge after researching on Tripadvisor, based on the cheap cost, amenities, and reviews. We didn't regret it! We paid about $70 a night overall (Thurs-Su) through Travelocity) and stayed 3 nights. It was a great location - right near the Marina, with several cool eating places right near the motel. The guy at the desk was super nice and helpful. I had booked a room with 2 queen beds, and asked for it to be as far from the road as possible (some reviews said it would be noisy, which it really wasn't). The room was great, except the a/c/heating unit didn't work when we got in there, so we just moved into the next room. The staff was very attentive and helpful. The room had a nice big bathroom with a great shower and was super clean. The place also had tv, cable, refrigerator, microwave, hairdryer, coffee maker, ironing board/iron, daily maid service.. just about everything you'd need. There was free parking (so hard to find in SF, and yes, the spaces are small but it's FREE) and free wireless internet, although it didn't work well so we ended up using another wireless signal in the area. The beds weren't great - the mattresses were really spongy and soft - but it was fine for the few nights. You're so wiped out after the day, it's easy to crash. There were bus stops all over near the motel, and we also walked about everywhere, so it was very easy to get places. And the area is safe. All this for about $70/night? Incredible. I mean, unless you plan to stay all day in your room in beautiful San Francisco, how can you beat this deal? We were only in our room to sleep and for a little down time. The Travelodge rocks and I would definitely go back.

“I'd Stay Here Again” Had the pleasure of staying the night here with my service dog. I like the place and I would recommend if going to see performance at the Kennedy Center. I hope to be back and next time I should order their cannister of Doubletree Cookies.

“Elysee is more than a "hotel"” Stepping into the Elysee is stepping into a special place that is private and quiet, and at the same time, courteous and friendly. The furnishings, artwork, and lighting are a tasteful mix of older pieces that work perfectly toward a "residential" atmosphere. Nothing is "commercial" or "hotel standardized" -- everything is comfortable. The breakfast buffet is totally fresh with good selections - and the wine reception on week-day evenings features prosecco wine, olives, cheese, bread, crackers. Guests include both those younger and older, singles, couples, and families, some on business, others on leisure, and from all parts of the world. This makes for a great social milieu of the club room at breakfast, and at the wine reception. Elysee in unique in NYC !

“Times Square Trendy and Pricey” If you want Times Square with a trendy vibe, this is a very good option. It is a bit pricey. If you're willing to be 5 -7 blocks away the price drops significantly by $100 - 150/nt. The staff is courteous and helpful. It is very well insulated against the bustling street noise...I heard no sirens or honking horns from my room. They have a roof top bar that's good for after dinner cocktails.

“Unique, Botique Vacation Club Experience” I have wanted to experience this club since visiting Boston many years ago. My wife and I use points to stay here. We used Boston as base for our 5 New England Tour. We were greeted by friendly valet staff who gathered our luggage and watched the rental car even though we were not parking. The posted charge was $13.00 for 0-4 hours but there was no charge (I did tip). The lobby is nice! Very historic and old marble and granite. The front desk clerks were very friendly. Checkin was smooth and quick. Our room, 2301, was one the highest floor with rooms. We were pleased with this on late checkin. The clerks made good suggestions for dinner and provided directions. The entire stay was very helpful throughout our 3 day stay. The room is a small villa and oddly configure but should be expected for it's location in the building. It was Rey comfortable for two but would not recommend with children. The view was awesome giving us three sides of the city. Water pressure was good in the bathroom. Microwave and small frig were sufficient. The views from the 26th floor deck are dynamic. The club has a very modern fitness center. We watch a movie in a very comfortable 9 seat theater. Popcorn included. The location is great to Fanuel Hall, Quincy Marketplace, Boston Harbor and the Freedom Trail. I definitely recommend this property. Good stay.

“Very nice hotel at an affordable price” Stayed here on business and it was great. Got a room for a very affordable price of $95.00 and it has the look and feel of a 5-star hotel. The only negative was the location. It's kind of in the suburbs so it's a little far from everything. I don't know the area very well, but I actually had a hard time finding a fast-food restaurant nearby. But other than that, everything else was great.

“Best NYC Area Hotel” have to say I absolutely agree with all the other reviews, the Ritz Carlton Battery Park is a great find for a stay in the city. We selected the basic City-View room on the Concierge floor and were not disappointed. We even had a side-view of the Staten Island Ferry’s coming in. Here are some of the highlights: *Rooms are large and spacious for NYC standard. *Rooms are quiet especially on the weekend (no street noise to be heard or minimal compared to mid-town). *They thought of all the little touches when doing the remodel, dimmer switches on all the lights, plenty of closet and drawer space, great working area, flat screen tvs, etc. *The beds are sensational. These days all the hotels have great beds but this one was really exceptional for comfort. *The bathrooms are very spacious, good lighting, separate areas for shower, tub, toilet, vanity, etc. *The Concierge Level service is top-notch. Literally you could not have to eat any meals out if you didn’t want to. Breakfast, while stated as “Continental” included things like hot and cold cereals, smoked locks, fresh meats and chesses, hard boiled eggs, fresh fruit, mimosa’s, etc. Snack service during the day also had salad, sandwiches, cookies, sides, etc. The evening reception offers wine, champagne, fruit, heavy appetizers, etc. Additionally there is use of a laptop and printer and the service on the Concierge Floor is outstanding! They really have great people who work at that property. *Location, a lot of reviewers had concern that is was far from Mid-Town, however it is one block away from a subway/train station that gets you anywhere you want to be in minutes, i.e. Mid-Town, Little Italy, Up-Town, etc. I love NYC public transportations, it’s quick, cheap and as long as you are smart, safe. Cabs are also plentiful. There is also some shopping and restaurants in downtown, albeit quiet on the weekends and some are not open but plenty to do. *Battery Park is right outside your window and you can walk all around. *One more tip, I highly recommend the Carmel Limo and Car Service for transport in the city or airport if you want a private car. Very reasonable in price and consistent, I often use them at least for airport transport. *The gym is definitely decent. It has a view of the water, comes with all the standard cardio equip plus free weights and weight machines. I was definitely able to maintain my workout routine here plus I could run through the park. It did get a little busy at times as it’s not super large (but more than adequate) but I was able to get machines, etc. *There is only one restaurant and two bars on property and we tried them all. I would not necessarily “rave” about it but they were above-average for hotel properties. The 14th floor bar is definitely lively on weekends and hip.

“Huge and quiet hotel with great rooms” This is a huge, full service property close to SeaTac airport. You get what you´d expect from a 3-star airport hotel: convenient parking, very confortable rooms, easy access to the terminals. At first the property seems a bit old (carpets are not in the best conditions in the hallways), but rooms are impeccable. Our rooms were very spacious and confortable, with great beds and big desks. Bathrooms were very convenient as well. We also had small balconies with a nice view of a lagoon at the back of the hotel. Everything is perfectly clean. Wi fi is complimentary on common areas -it worked well, but the night I stayed here there was a blackout. Quite a creepy experience going back from one of the lobbies to my room, which seemed like one block away. Staff is friendly. I would undoubtedly stay here again.
“Nice Rennovated hotel” We have family in the area so my husband and I have stayed several times at this hotel. Since it's been refurbished it's been much nicer.

“Excellent for someone who never cared for Hong Kong” I spent 2 night at Conrad Chicago for business and was impressed. This is place is really nice with all the things you want and need in a hotel. They even have an umbrella in the closet which proved very useful. For the HH members they offer a free breakfast that was a little disappointing; you have too choices, the pastry plate or the french toast plate. Both days I chose the pastry and it was good, but I would have preferred more choices, however, it was free so I am not complaining. The TV is excellent with lots of channels and HBO. The Internet is also free, which is nice. The room was large, clean and the bed very comfortable. The bathroom was great with tub and shower and really nice toiletries. The location is also great, next door to a mall and many restaurants. The hotel staff was very professional and accommodating. I will surely return.

“Excellent location!” I stayed here in Oct 2011 when I was attending a conference in the connected convention center. The location of the hotel is great-- right in downtown San Jose and walking distance to many bars/restaurants. The light rail stops right outside the conference center, which makes it easy to get around to neighboring areas/Caltrain. The rooms were very modern and clean. The front desk was attentive and helpful.

“A nice, relaxing hotel with very spacious rooms” We stayed at the Affinia Gardens for 7 nights. We had a very large room with two queen size beds, a nice recliner chair, a vanity area, a large desk, and a very functional and well equipped kitchenette. The bathroom was very large, with all the necessary amenities. The room was more than comfortable with good quality beds and linens. The cleaning staff was extremely helpful and took care of several of my requests with a smile. The front desk was very personable, efficient, and professional. We liked the location, a little out of the way for some, but perfect for us. We like to walk and within minutes or short metro rides, we were everywhere we wanted to be. My only two negative comments: the room should come with free internet and the cookies served during tea time in the lobby should be of higher quality, just a small detail that would make a great difference.

“Pure Magic!!” Check In We arrived at the hotel at 10am, this wasn’t an issue at all as our room was ready for us. The check in was a very friendly and welcoming experience; I was given a glass of complimentary lemonade and also an overview to the local area. I was also informed of the complimentary 24/7 mini bar! My initial impressions after the check in were very positive. Hotel The room itself was not a suite, but a king bed. The bed was very comfortable and it actually has a proper duvet as opposed to a single sheet that is very common in hotels. The bathroom was also nice, particularly the shower which was a large walk in style with sliding doors. The stairway leading up to our hotel could have done with a paint job and a bit of an update, but a minor complaint in such a fantastic place. Also provided was a large LCD and DVD player. Don’t forget to ask for a free DVD rental at reception! They have a large selection of complimentary DVD’s that you can watch in your room. Overall the room was average looking and could probably do with an update, but it was adequate for our needs and we felt very comfortable. Glancing round the hotel, the suites look very cool! We also had a fridge freezer in our room, but no other kitchen facilities, useful for keeping our drinks in and that was about it. There is a well sized heated swimming pool in the centre of the hotel, which is an attractive feature to glance at when you walk through the reception area. The rooms are kind of built surrounding it and if you are lucky you will have a balcony overlooking the pool. The hotel also has a very secure and cosy feeling to it when you are roaming about. Breakfast is also included and is a very relaxing and fulfilling experience. They have a continental breakfast on display which was very satisfying. We relaxed by the pool enjoying our food with other guests, everyone seemed to be very happy and this created a positive atmosphere for your morning meal. A great start to the day! Another thing worth mentioning is the free mini bar they offer. You can go to the front desk and ask for anything off the menu for free. It is a good selection of snacks and drinks, very impressive and served to you with a smile always. The free wireless internet access was the only real upset here. It was a working service, but was very slow pretty much every day. It was useable, but not as fast as other hotels I have stayed in. It is also worth mentioning that as the hotel is small and cosy, the noise can sometimes be a bit frustrating. The main thing is slamming doors. Pretty much every morning I could hear doors slamming at early hours, I guess some people are just inconsiderate to others. Some hotel have devices on the doors to prevent them slamming, something the Magic Castle may want to invest in perhaps. Staff 100 percent the best hotel staff I have ever experienced. All of the staff at the Magic Castle are exceptional and provide the best service in any hotel I have stayed in. They all deserve a pay rise and are the backbone to this hotel. Every single person I spoke to was extremely helpful and also happy to listen to what I had to say. They also demonstrated going that extra mile on many occasions, Example 1: Myself and my partner were relaxing by the pool when one of the staff approached us offering us bottled water or a popsicle!, perfect to quench us whilst bathing in the hot sun. Example 2: I went to the front desk and asked for a DVD for the evening, the lady then said ‘how about some popcorn to go with that?’ I actually didn’t have a microwave in my room, but don’t worry they then offered to microwave it for me and bring it to our room! 2 minutes later there was a knock on the door and we had our delicious popcorn ready to eat. Outstanding customer service and what was more impressive was the fact we never actually had to request any of this, it was simply offered to us. If you want to feel welcome in a hotel this is the place to come! Another thing I found quite nice was a knock on the door each night with a card detailing the weather for the next day and also some free chocolate! Location We arrived at Union Station by Amtrak rail and the cab was 25 bucks to the hotel. About 8 miles I believe. Not too bad! The good thing is that this hotel is just round the corner from the main walk of fame strip in Hollywood. It was very convenient to go back and forth from the hotel to the local attractions on offer at Hollywood Blvd. Perfect location for what we wanted. Overall This has to be the best overall hotel experience of my life. Whilst not necessarily being the best hotel in the world, The Magic Castle compensates by offering exceptional service and value for money, whilst also providing a location 2 minutes from the main features Hollywood has to offer. I would recommend this to anyone visiting Hollywood and I most certainly will return here if I am ever in the area. An absolute pleasure from start to finish.

“I liked this hotel” This hotel was in a great location. Very close to the Galleria and Memorial areas. The rooms were very well kept and maintained the bathroom was spotless, and all of the necessary amenities were provided. The bed was EXTREMELY comfortable. The internet access was a little odd, as the login screen kept interupting my session, however. I never had that happen ANYWHERE before. The service was very good, especially, in the restaurant and the bell service. The grounds were very nice, and the pool looked nice (though I did not use it) and clean. I would recommend this hotel.

“Marriott Marquis Times Square -Great Location for Tourists” I spent 2 nights this past week at the Marquis. I was in NYC for a training and spent a Wednesday & Thursday night. I got a government rate due to my job so my rate was significantly cheaper than the going rate and I booked directly through Marriott.com. I took Amtrak in to Penn Station and I am pretty comfortable traveling around NYC so I took the subway, 1 stop to Times Square and then a couple block walk to the hotel. The check-in desk in on the 8th floor which was a bit odd, but no big deal. Check-in was far and away the worst part of the whole stay. 3 clerks were working when I arrived, each was busy. A line formed behind me as we waited for our turn. 2 of the 3 clerks were dealing with different problems with the guests. The 3rd clerk finally finished with their guest and told us to wait for someone else, and he walked away. That was really annoying. I proceeded to wait a total of 15 minutes before I was checked in. Too long to wait at 8pm at night after traveling and with luggage. (Frankly, too long to wait any time of the day!) The clerk who checked me in did not impress me with his customer service, but I wouldn't call him rude. My room was on the 39th floor, 2 Queen Sized beds. The elevator was a little slow for me since I was on one of the top floors. Someone has to stay on those floors, though-right? My room was impecably clean. The bath products were Bath & Body Works. There were 4 fluffy towels in my room. There was also a coffee maker which I didn't use. Large flat screen LCD TV was great, got most channels I wanted except no Food Network or Comedy Central. Oh well, not there to watch TV but they are basic cable channels so I was disappointed. The view was of Times Square and I didn't even shut the black out curtains at night. The view was great and the lights did not bother me at all. The bed was comfortable, the pillows were a little bit mushy for my taste, but workable. There was an i-Pod docking station/alarm clock which I thought was a nice touch. The internet was WIRED and cost $16.95/day-at least it should have been wireless at that price! What a rip-off. And it goes noon to noon not 24 hours from when you purchase. I was NOT impressed with that. I like to sit on my bed and do work when I travel as many others do, but that wasn't possible with wired access. I was able to pull it close enough to put my feet up on a bed but that was it. The connection speed was mediocre at best. Again for the price it should have been much better. So that was a little disappointing. The AC was fine, I like the room pretty cool so it was hard for me to tell if the AC wasn't working well or it was me. The room was around 67 the whole time, I would have preferred 65. With my TV on I couldn't hear anyone else in surrounding rooms. There is a Starbucks on the 8th and 1st floors of this hotel as well as numerous restaurants. For $10 I was able to eat a decent Starbucks breakfast each day of my stay as compared to the hotel restaraunt buffet at $28pp plus tax and gratuity. (Welcome to New York my friends!) The cheapest thing on the a la carte breakfast menu was a $10 fruit cup! So Starbucks it is! The room service menu was as expensive as can be expected, but you are in NYC, in an expensive hotel and in the middle of Times Square. There is however a shop on the 8th floor of the hotel, honestly the prices were much more reasonable than I expected in the shop. Snacks, soft drinks and gift items. You can eat for less money in this area, but you really have to look for it. There is a deli on the corner of 49th/Broadway with great sandwiches-$10 for lunch... So all in all the room was clean, I slept well. I don't think I would have stayed here at the $400+ a night rate, but for $210 a night it was fine. Very upscale for foreign tourists and high-end business class. With my little ol' government rate I didn't quite fit here, but that was ok. Very convenient to where I needed to be.

“Great staff and perks” I spent two nights at the Salomar and I loved it. They have a great pool deck and bar and the design of the hotel is great. Kimpton has some great perks such as a $10 mini bar credit, free coffee in the morning, a free wine hour in the evening, and free wireless for members. If you are traveling with a pet it seems that they do quite a bit to cater to them. Located in the Gaslamp district. The good: hotel looks fairly new and is in good shape, pool deck area is very nice and includes a bar that also serves food, bathroom was nicely designed, bed was comfortable, and the perks that I noted above. Best of all is the staff - extremely friendly, helpful, and nice. The OK: I had a deluxe room and I thought that it was pretty small compared to other hotels, took a long time for housekeeping to service my room (by 4PM I contacted the front desk to get housekeeping to clean the room). The bad: nothing.

“If you plan on spending less, read the reviews of other national chains, you'll stay here” Even though I have done over 50 motel reviews in the last six months, I seldom read other reviews prior to staying at a motel. My first two choices tonight in Phoenix were $29 motels, one no longer had an airport shuttle and the other had one bad review out of five but it gave me an uneasy feeling. So I called one of the national chains to make a reservation, but because they did not have food nearby I told them I would eat at the airport first and call back for a shuttle ride. But while I ate, for the first time at an airport restaurant I took out my laptop and looked at Trip Advisor for that motel …. ‘Awful’ … ‘The place should be torn down’ … ‘won’t be coming back’ … ‘Filthy’ … ‘Stay Away’ … ‘If you value your safety – DO NOT STAY HERE.’ Not a single good review in the last year for that motel. So, that is how I ended up at the Sleep Inn … I’ve stayed here before and and I will say it is ‘great’ … ‘new(er)’ … ‘I will be back (2nd time here in 3 months)’ … ‘Clean’ … ‘Do stay’ … ‘quiet industrial area, Hilton across the street-safe area.' … Yes I paid more than $29 … I paid twice that, but you get what you pay for and even for someone who is as cheap as me, it was worth it. (I’m now writing 2nd reviews, to see if my first review was the exception)

“Owwwwww! Really great stay.” Great hotel. Modern and classic-chic. Very good location just one block from the waterfront and great restaurants. Really nice and big room with super confort bed. Room with lots of amenities. Nice bathroom. I had a great view from my room. They also let me check in at 8am. They have a great restaurant inside, a Starbucks and a guy in the lobby that can help with maps and info about the area. Really close from South Station and the Silverline stop right in front the hotel. I ordered room service (food) and the only complaint is the 4$ they charge for delivery (which is not great cause the restaurant is inside the hotel). Maybe a 10 min drive to the airport.

“Good hotel but location can take some planning for transit” Friday night stay, king bed non smoking, was on 16 of 16 floors with high sided balcony overlooking river and skyline (H-Honors member). Spacious standard chain room. Balcony was fun and helpful as Mars was very visible and got some great shots. Hotel has Jazz bar onsite and bar and food. Location is not the best but there is a free shuttle with scheduled pickups from Harvard station and drop off locations to Quincy Market, Copley, and 2 others. Cabs are very expensive and not recommended. I took the subway to Harvard and got picked up from there. Shuttle drivers seem flexible to drop off anywhere along the standard drop off route. This was the high point, the shuttle due to the northeast location. Get a free cookie for checking in :) Water pressure and noise were no issue. Hotel is recommended if the location is not offputting to you.

“What a wonderful stay!” I read about this hotel in a travel magazine, and after reading all of the positive reviews I decided to book our stay in the Park South. My husband and I (with our two daughters) spent four days and three nights at the Park South--and it was as wonderful as we had expected. There appeared ro be a problem with our reservation when we arrived--but it was immediately taken care of and the rest of the stay was without any glitches. The room was a nice size, and VERY clean and well kept. Yes, the bathroom is small, but that has been our experience with the nonchain, unique NYC hotels. But really--it wasn't that big of a deal! And the bathroom was kept really clean, too--which IS a big deal! This hotel is a great find, and I would highly recommend it to anyone wanting to stay in more of a neighborhood area, and way from the bustle of the usual main areas of the city. And everything is in walkining distance, so you sacrifice none of the convenience of being near the main avenues. There is also a wonderful breakfast buffet every morning which is a great touch, and much appreciated so that we were able to start our day in a leisurely fashion. Great find!

“Great hotel and outstanding location overlooking Inner Harbor” Stayed 3 nights in this centrally located great hotel across from the Inner Harbor and the Aquarium. The only unusual aspect of the hotel is that some of the rooms are a long walk from the elevator, our's was only 10 rooms away. Everything is within walking distance, restaurants, entertainment, water taxi, aquarium, and Camden Yards. The best method to get to the Inner Harbor is to take the light rail train from BWI Airport to the Convention Center stop and then walk about 5 block to the hotel - taxi service is also available from the Convention Center.

“Location and Super Customer Service” Have stayed here numerous times and always have a great experience. The suites are nice but you are better off in a regular balcony room or regular room. The bathroom in the suite is super small compared to other rooms I have had there. But the front desk and housekeeping staff are wonderful, polite and friendly. Very clean hotel.
