First rate breakfast really, as far as free breakfast goes at a hotel. A lot of variety. Yes, it is loud, you may want to ask for an interior room, but that is the joy of Beale Street. Very safe walk from Beale.

“very nice hotel” I stayed here for a work conference and had an excellent experience. The hotel room was comfortable, the meeting rooms were spacious and accessible, and the location was fantastic. There were multiple dining options in the hotel as well as within a 10 min walk. The staff was friendly and helpful. I would highly recommend this hotel for both business and personal travel.

“Finally found a hotel in Phoenix where I will return” I've stayed at the pretentious Hyatt downtown, the Doubletree near the airport, and the Marriott Residence Inn near the airport. From here on out, I'm staying at the Homewood Suites in the Biltmore area. It is quiet! My room was excellent -- configured beautifully. Had TONS of space. There is a grocery store within walking distance. The area is safe, and the staff was REALLY accommodating and helpful. The location is also just a few minutes from downtown and all the other major corporate areas for Phoenix. I actually prefer staying at a place that is more like home ... away from home. The bed was comfy. The place was VERY clean. I have no complaints.

“Convenient, Good Location, but soooo Busy.” This is the second time I have stayed at this hotel in the past year. This hotel was extremely busy for my most recent stay - Feb. 11-15. In the four nights I stayed there there was 1) CPAC, 2) a Community College Trustee convention, 3) a Religious convention, and 4) a high ranking Chinese official staying there. I could hardly believe the activity. On my stay, it was for the most part fine with one exception - at the Stones Throw restaurant, we had ne night of bad service. Otherwise it was fine. Pros: Harry's Pub is open late and moderately priced (although food quality is not stellar); Stone's Throw Restaurant is good (great Turkey Club!) and fairly well priced, although 21.00 for buffet breakfast was a bit steep!. LOCATION is excellent for the national Zoo, subway and other nearby sites and sounds. Cons: WAY too much security - I was turned away fro several entrances during the events mentioned above - felt like a second class patron while still paying $250/night. Front desk people were not very helpful, perhaps they were too stressed out, I don’t know, but again for $250/night, I expect to be treated with some respect. TIPS: there is a CVS store about a minute away - outside of the back side of the hotel - GO THERE for water, snacks and other needs. Also there is a Chipotle and McDonalds right outside the hotel. The national ZOO is about a ten to fifteen minute walk up Connecticut Ave. The Subway is right outside the Hotel and there are plenty of Taxis waiting outside the main entrance all the time.

“Good clean hotel/good location” Wanted to be close to 6th street but not in the middle of all the craziness. Staff was very friendly, room very clean and easy access to everything in Austin. Price was right, will stay again

“Classy hotel w/ new rooms” In a newly-remodeled king room which was spacious & very comfortable. Big enough for a leather couch against the window. Starwood beds typically very plush. 3 sides to the hotel, & I definitely thought it worth the $15-20 extra bucks I spent for an awesome view of Capitol Square & downtown Columbus. Best city view I've had in awhile. Not much to the lobby, other than open air computer area & Starbucks. No pool. Looked as if they were updating restaurant as well. I skipped basic breakfast buffet, only o/w tried a pricey cookie/ice cream dessert for a late night sugar craving. $25-30 will get u here from CMH via cab. Would certainly stay here again.

“Slick, Modern Hotel with Good Service” This full-service Hilton is connected to the San Jose Convention Center in downtown San Jose, California. About 12 years ago I stayed at this hotel and it wasn't memorable in the least. This visit, I was very impressed to find the hotel has upgraded its amenities and best of all, the decor of the rooms. Whoever did the redecoration did an excellent job, using chrome, leather and glass to replicate the experience of San Jose both as a city and a symbol of technology. It was as if the room blended perfectly with my panoramic city view (ask for a high floor if you want the view!) The beds were of excellent quality, the bathroom stocked with high-end personal items. Parking wasn't free, nor was WiFi as is the case in many full-service hotels these days. General guest service was unobtrusive but also unremarkable. The convenience of the location and the clean lines of the room made my stay rewarding. I ordered room service one night - took a chance on a rib eye. It was very good, with fresh asparagus, mashed potatoes and fresh salad. I didn't visit on-site lounge or restaurant, but there is Peet's Coffee and Tea situated along the inside walkway from the Hilton to the conference center and guest parking that offered fresh baked goods, some sandwiches and of course tea, coffee, iced drinks, juices and so on. A nice stay, and a hotel I will return to should business take me to downtown Jose again.

“Did I stay in a different hotel than the past reviewers?” I normally stay at the Airport Marriott, however for various reasons I stayed at the Renaissance for the first time. Yes, it is in the middle of nowhere, but it is an airport hotel. I did not find any of the age and wear and tear as did the other reviewers. I was greeted very warmly, arrival gift was not an issue, and given a lovely suite (220) which had slightly worn carpet, but looked fresh and was very clean. I did not find magazines, nor anything else in the bed which did not belong there. The wireless internet was quick, quicker than many properties at which I have stayed. No, I don't think you are going to choose this hotel if you are here for the Liberty Bell, but for a quick stop and to be close to the airport it is great. The Airport Marriott still beats it though as it is IN the airport!

“nice enough but a little battered” I stayed five nights recently with a small group from work. We're Marriott Elite members so had access to the Concierge level for breakfast, which was convenient. The attendants had a hard time keep up with the crowd at peak times but did their level best. I had a corner room on the 16th floor. The bed was very comfortable and the room was quiet, at least until Thursday night when the partiers arrived for Labor Day weekend. Housekeeping was excellent. I was surprised to find the paint peeling quite a bit on my bathroom ceiling, apparently from a water leak; I don't know and they really need to check things like that. Also the lobby area really takes a beating. It's a high traffic spot right in Center City and it shows. Staff I encountered was competent and friendly. The lobby bar is REALLY expensive ($15 + tax for a glass of wine?!) but there are plenty of place to drink in Philly so avoid that. All in all, it was acceptable. But if I were travelling by myself, I would probably not choose it again unless I got a really good deal on the room rate.

“Oasis in the Desert !” We have stayed here on many occasions over the past 10 - 15 years. As Australians we were unsure of NYC to start but have come to love the place. This Hotel has played its part in this feeling. It is situated virtually in Time Square - metres from everything - Theatres, subway/underground, bars, restaurants, transport, etc etc. And shopping - much to my wife's delight. It is also just a tad away from the Station - so if coming to NYC think about using Amtrak. No lines, no security, comfortable seats, AND you arrive in the middle of the City. So - no long taxi ride. You walk out into the teaming masses and its all at your feet. Noisy, fun and people everywhere ! A world of excitement. You go back into the Hotel - its quiet and relaxed and you just stand for a minute and enjoy the calm ! The Hotel is not easy to spot the first time - look for the clock - and has a great little back door for getting in and out. It is like an oasis in the desert however after a day in the City. You enter the ground floor - lift to lobby - then your rooms. All the noise, dirt, and hubbub of the City is gone ! Views are awesome and staff very good. Lovely spot to start the day with brekkie too. And - a nice - if expensive - bar. But - you don't need to eat or drink in the Hotel as you are close to everything. So, get out and explore. Grog shop around the corner - so buy a 6 pack for later. We aren't about much after 12 midnight - 2am - unless at a show - so found the City VERY safe. Witha policeman on virtually every corner its wonderful - and they are wonderful too. Always ask a cop if you can't find somewhere. Very helpful and polite. also willing to have a picture taken if you are so inclined. We like the NYC police. The theatre district is across the road and easy to find. The subway/underground is either way - and you can go up or downtown for about $2. Yankee Stadium is very easy to get to - as is Wall Street and the Twin Tower Memorial. Don't be afraid to use the train - as it is easy to use and clean and tidy. People are vbery friendly. Rooms are excellent. Large with good bathrooms. Good lifts and great views. The place is clean and tidy and makes you feel welcome. Taxi to airport is regulated - ie set charge. My only tip - watch the porters. They are very good - but there are 3 sets - meet and greet, ground floor, and lobby. If you have wheels - pull your own bags is my advice. They are very good but tipping 3 times is a bit much. Maybe just use the meet and greet ones. A good security system set up at gropund level too. So - don't be annoyed if asked to show your card/key. Back door is best for taxis.

“Pleasantly Surprised” After reading mixed reviews on this place, I wasn't sure what to expect. I booked a room using Priority Club points for one night, as we had Tiger tickets for 2 days in a row (night game Saturday followed by a day game Sunday). As a Priority Club Platinum member, we were upgraded to a VERY LARGE suite, perhaps the largest suite at a HI Express that I've ever had. It was a corner room, and appeared to be 3 times the size of a normal room based on the floor layout map on the door. Check-in staff was very friendly and the process was efficient...I believe her name was Angie--what a sweetheart. The decor was slightly dated and the bed a little 'off', but not bad by any means. There was a fair amount of road noise coming from downstairs (we were about 8 floors up), but I don't travel without ear plugs. Breakfast was as good as I've had at a HIX before. Your only parking option is to valet at $17/day. I figured they'd double-hit us because we exceeded 24 hours (not picking up our car until after Sunday's game, around 4PM)...But were only charged for 1 day. It's a 10-minute walk to Comerica Park or Ford Field, I will concede it was a little scary at some points, but we never felt threatened by any means...All in all, I'd do it all over again and might try the same thing next year, if the Tigers make it worth driving down for! :)

“A Courtyard” Stayed here on a freebie certificate. Easy to find and very close to the airport for our early flight to Hawaii. Clean comfortable rooms. What you have learned to expect from Courtyard. Check in was simple. Staff was friendly. Drink prices at the bar/food counter were a little high for wine but it is a hotel. I’d stay here again before leaving on a trip out to SJC

“would stay again” Stayed for one night. Easy to access by train and underground from airport, only $2, stop at chicago and walk 1 block. Staff in reception pleasant and helpful. large reception lobby pleasant with restuarant, didnt eat there. Had breakfast (as cheaper ) at Diktaas just next block. Room very clean, smart with large very comfortable bed and HDTV. Easy walk to hancock tower and michican ave, very central for seeing sites. would stay again

“Great hotel and excellent location” Recently stay at this hotel during the hottest days in Chicago. We stay at the new tower on the 25th floor. The room was small but nicely decorated. The a/c fan was non-stop and it was noisy, but it kept the room cool. The heated pool was excellent for lap swimmers, very ornate and old world. The location is excellent. Hightly recommend for touris and anyone want to stay in the middle of the action.

“A very decent stay” My family with children stayed here for a school related event near downtown. Check in was very speedy. You could tell the place has been renovated- there were a few small signs in the hallways of an older hotel, but overall a good remodel job. We were able to park near the entrance to our upstairs room. We found the hotel convenient to the Stockyards and downtown area- a quick trip away down the highway. Our room was clean and tastefully updated with white linens and modern furniture. The view was to an open field toward downtown. The bathroom was nicely tiled. The curtain rod was not hanging correctly-a bit broken. The sleep number bed was bit awkward- kind of kept running out of air- felt a bit gimickly and didn't contribute that much to comfort, but I slept well enough. The kids enjoyed the small indoor pool- we had it to ourselves, so that helped. It was clean around the pool area and towels were available (even though I don't find indoor pools in general have the best atmosphere). Staff was helpful/friendly. Breakfast is not included and the $10 buffet was too expensive for my family of 5. There are several nice restaurants for dinner just north of the hotel ,near a golf course (chain type, which I usually don't prefer when traveling, but nice) The BBQ place we chose had live music going on their side lawn- nice. Overall, this was a good stay for our purposes- which was a clean place to sleep at night between touring the many sights of Ft. Worth.

“Nice, quiet” I have stayed at this property twice now. Hotel backs up to the interstate on one side, but noise is not an issue. Newer property on the west side of El Paso. There is a multiscreen movie theater next to the hotel, along with several medical offices. There is a Walmart, Home Depot that you can see from the back of from the property, but noise & traffic is in the front of those properties. Cracker Barrel a few doors down, multiple restaurants within 1/2 mile. Nice exercise room. Breakfast was adequate- typical Fairfield fare- no pre-made oatmeal or pre-cooked meats, all we're heat & serve. Overall a nice quiet stay.

“Very nice hotel” Stayed July 30 thru August 1. Beautiful room for the weekend rate I received. Large bathroom with separate shower. If you join the Omni Hotel Select Guest Club, you receive complimentary morning beverages which we enjoyed. I agree with the previous poster who noted a car in LA is a must, so staying downtown was not much of a problem for us. Would definitely stay here again if I got the same excellent rate.

“Pretty good but not perfect” I have stayed at the Westin a couple times of the past couple year it also was the site of my companies holiday party the past 2 years. It is generally what you would expect from a Westin; great quality, up to date and clean. Two complaints: First the Westin Georgetown is NOT in Georgetown, near but not in so the name maybe a bit misleading . Expect a decent walk or a short cab ride to visit destinations in Georgetown. The second complaint stems from one bartender working my companies Holiday party at the Westin. Generally the service is phenomenal at Westins, this one bartender in particular was the antithesis of that (I wish I got the guys name, I would have filed a complaint against this guy), he was very rude to everyone his rudeness came up in party conversation it was so bad, him poring you a drink was like he was doing a favor for you.

“Incredible Hotel Chain” I stayed at this hotel for one night in November 2012, for business. This was my first time staying at a Drury hotel, and this is now my favorite hotel chain. The location is directly off the freeway. I was only there one day, and I didn’t see any restaurants or other business within walking distance. The entire staff was very friendly and professional, and seemed to really care that we enjoyed our stay. I saw the manager working the evening happy hour, and then again helping out with the breakfast the next morning. He was always courteous and genuinely seemed to want to make sure the guest had a good stay. The property is very well maintained, and had a very nice open air lobby. It reminded by of staying at an Embassy Suites type hotel. I liked everything about his hotel. The hotel had a pool, jacuzzi, a semi-private computer room with 2 stations and a printer, small gym, and a small mini-mart next to the front desk. They also served hot popcorn in the lobby every night. The parking is free. The stay also included one of the best hotel breakfasts I have ever had. It included scrambled eggs, sausage, potatoes, biscuits and gravy, a waffle maker, breads, pastries, cereals, juices, milk, and fruit. Everything was hot, delicious, and fresh. I was really impressed with the breakfast. Just as nice was the free dinner!!! The night I was there the buffet included pasta and meatballs, hot dogs, a salad bar, baked potatoes, nachos, and lots of other extras. Again all of the food was hot, and fresh. The free dinner was a nice extra that I have never seen before at a Marriot/Hilton/Wyndham type hotel. The dinner is served from 5:30 - 7pm. Also from 5:30 - 7pm is a free drink reception. When you check in you get a punch card good for 3 drinks each night. You can choose beer, wine, or cocktails. I didn’t like the whole punch card thing, but the free drinks were another nice extra amenity for the guest. The room was well decorated and maintained. It was a medium size room with a desk, refrigerator, microwave, medium size flat screen television with HBO, but no PPV. The bed and pillows were very comfortable. The room also had free wifi, with a good strong signal. The bathroom was a little on the small side, but very clean and well maintained. It had a granite sink and shower. I love the fact that this hotel gives you so much, and doesn’t nickle and dime you like other hotels for parking, wifi, gym, etc. In my future travels, I will check first to see if there is a Drury Hotel in the city, they will always be my first choice. I strongly recommend this hotel to family and friends. This is a great hotel, especially if you have children. I’m looking forward to my next Drury Hotel visit.

“Very Nice After Room Change” My wife and I recently spent a night at the Mandarin Oriental to celebrate an anniversary. We ended up having a very nice time with the staff and the spa being the highlights. To begin with, however, we were placed in a room right next to some kind of a service entrance. We had paid for a relatively nice room so I was disappointed when my brief afternoon nap was interrupted every 3-4 minutes by the sound of a door closing. After a call to the front desk, we were quickly relocated and loved our new room. The spa is among the best that we have been to and the staff throughout was exceptional. Breakfast in the room was excellent the next morning. I would have given five stars except for the initial room placement. Avoid room 520 and you will have a wonderful time at this lovely hotel in a very nice location.

“Wonderful Surprise!” We stayed at the Embassy Suites NW the weekend of 3/6-3/8. We had a room on the 8th Floor - King bed. We are from San Antonio and know that this hotel has been here for over 15yrs so we were not expecting much - and based on some of the Trip Advisor reviews - it sounded like it was showing it's age and had not been updated in some time. Well, when we walked into the room - what a wonderful surprise - it was clean, obviously been renovated in the past year! The A/C worked very well - there was no "pool" smell in the lobby/room, since the pool at this property was seperated from the main lobby so it kept the clorine smell isolated and the kid noise down to nothing. The bed and pillows were comfortable, the couch and furnishings were updated - however, they did not go for the full update and install HDTV flat screen TV's - they still had the old school 19" box TV - UGH! We had room service on Saturday night and again - who would have thought it was great! The staff was friendly, they cleaned the room in a timely manor and gave us extra soaps/shampoo as well. All in all - we had a great time and would stay again - just not during Spring Break - as it was full of families with small children RUNNING down the halls screaming and yelling - thank god we were on the top floor with no rooms above us - I could'nt imagine having children in a room above us - it was bad enough to hear them running by our room door and peeking in thru the sheer curtins! Thanks for a great stay otherwise - not much the hotel can do with parents who let their children run free and wild!

“Convenient, clean, and not ridiculously priced” We were in town for a family event and stayed at the Hilton Back Bay with several other family members. The hotel itself is newly remodeled and has nice facilities overall. My only real complaint would be that the elevators can be rather slow and the breakfast at the hotel restaurant is very overpriced. On the positive side, the location can't be beat.

“Simply the best hotel in Denver by leaps and bounds” I travel to the Denver area at least once a month and stay for a weekend to visit friends there. This time I wanted it to be a special occasion with the holidays coming up, so I decided to splurge and stay at the Hotel Teatro because of the many positive reviews and I simply wanted to try something different than the Westin or Shearton (I'm a loyal SPG Gold). The staff was so welcoming when I first walked through the door and immediately asked if I was familiar with their car service (I ended up using it several times through out the stay) and showed me to the front desk. Again, the staff was so warm and answered all of my questions and concerns. The room the put me in was amazingly beautiful and comfortable. After flying for 4 hours from the east coast on a early morning flight I collapsed on a bed that felt like sleeping in a cloud and had a very peaceful nap. The bathrooms were just as they were on the website spacious and very well designed and of course classy with great Aveda amenities. I had ordered room service several times through out the stay and I can say that the food was very good and was always delivered in under the time they estimated. So enough ranting and raving you all get the point that this hotel is the best in Denver. I have stayed at the Westin, Sheraton, Hyatt, and Ritz Carlton in Denver and can tell you that this hotel is far superior in terms of overall quality and value. I was so blown back that I personally wrote the general manager a note expressing how great his staff and hotel were managed. I will refer friends and family when they travel to Denver on business and leisure. Happy traveling!

“Great Experience” Needed a last minuted place to stay and this property had rooms available. Liz and Sarah at the front desk were among the nicest and most professional I have ever encountered. My room was clean and comfortable. Breakfast was average for this type of property. Nice being here. Thank you

“Overall - very good indeed” We arrived after a long Transatlantic at wine hour and got a good feel about the place very quickly. The reception staff were struggling a bit and our check in was done wrong (only came to like when we tried to charge a meal to the room in Il Pescatore - lucky it did as someone else could have been given a key to our room) Next day, our room keys stoped working even though we were there for 2 days - again a check in error. Had it not been for these two issues I would have given this hotel an excellent rating. The staff were very pleasant, the concierge Daniel made excellent reservations for us and the bed was extremely comfortable. I would recommend an inside courtyard room as we had - so quiet - OK no view but who cares. It was nice to have a personal feel in this hotel rather than a chain activity

“A truly outstanding hotel” We stayed here during Thanksgiving weekend for our wedding anniversary. We booked a "corner suite" and were upgraded to an "executive suite." The room was spectacular. We had a view of the Sound, downtown, and the Space Needle. We had a great view for the fireworks and celebration when they lit the Christmas tree downtown. The room was incredibly large - actually it was several rooms. The executive suite includes a large living room, wet bar, powder room, bedroom, dressing room, and huge bathroom. It had luxurious furnishings in that low key, classy Northwest style. The service was great and everyone at the front desk was great. Breakfast in the restaurant hotel (727 Pine) was great, as was the service. We had drinks there several nights and they were great too. This would definitely be my first choice for a hotel in Seattle.

“Down a star” We still love this hotel and were happy to hear that they are taking the hint to renovate their dated televisions and rooms. They are up to floor 9 as of 3/10/2012 and are working their way up. They also completes some renovations to the pool area- new flooring and new floor to ceiling windows. However, it will cost you! As of February, they now charge $15 EACH DAY you use the pool per room. I found this to be a tough pill to swallow as we stay here regularly and it had been free to all guests prior to these renovations. They have been also adding other vendors such as a nail salon and "dry bar" for hairstyling in the basement- where I, admittedly, have never been. Beware of the prices listed on the mini bar too- I was charge $9.25 for a Heinekin that was on the menu for $8.50. Overdue renovations should not be reason to make your guests feel ripped off.

“Nicest in the Bean” Beautiful Lobby, EXCELLENT Young man at the desk (Ryan?) seemed to always be there weather it was Noon, Midnight or in the Middle, excellent rep for your company and shows what true hospitality is. Nice modern rooms but the best part the unique spa inspired bathroom, Free Globe on the weekend and nice waterfront dining will be back for sure, only this to be aware of as with all high end hotel you have to pay for wireless.

“Nice New Hotel~!” Booked this hotel via Spg website. got an excellent deal for 149/night on a busy weekend. stayed at this property twice, both time got upgraded to a nice corner room (xx25 and xx01) as spg gold. If you are platinum you'll get upgraded to the corner suite (more likely). but the hotel sold out pretty often b/c its right next to the convention center. its an easy 5 mins walk (and safe too) to the bart station and also there are lots convinent /fast food store nearby (quiznos, starbucks, McDs, taco bells and 7-11). CPK is right across the street too. SF shopping center and Union square are approx 2-3 blocks away. There is a big cinema right behind the hotel too. Easy access to the Ferry building/fisherman's wharf via bus / cable car. The room on 22 floors and UP are consider "grand deluxe/premier" room so they have a better view of the city. As other reviewers suggested. This hotel has a nice , new gym at 4th floor, no swimming pool tho (Very common in norcal). But this hotel is mostly business travellers so not likely people will have time to really use the gym facilities. Afterall, this hotel IS a business hotel, so don't expect too much from it. The service was prompted but slow. Most of the people working at the front desk are young so their knowledge could be limited and their attitude certainly needs to polish some more when dealing with the customers. Afterall, this is still a nice hotel, very comfortable bed and AC works great in the hotel, a perfect place for travellers whos visiting SF for the first time!

“Amazing Rooms” We took a last minute trip to NYC last weekend and decided to go all out and stay the the Westin.......I was awesome....the first night we staying in a executive room on the 16th floor. Huge plasma TV, Computer, and spectacular bed.....when they say heavenly bed, they are not kidding. Very clean, modern, and great view. The second night we stayed in a corner room on the 35th floor. It was even more amazing......total of 5 windows including one in the bathroom. Even the shower was heavely with two huge showerheads that dump gallons of water on you.......Overall all experience was spectacular....will always go back to the Westin when we go back to NYC.

“Another Bowden Review!!! Pretty good the place, the La Quinta.” Good place. I got this for $50 on priceline like I always do, because I am highly intelligent. Rooms are generally north of $90. Rooms are clean and modern. It's my understanding that the recently renovated the place. There is a bar downstairs and they serve typical bar food, like burgers and wings. They call it a restuarant, but the menu has like 8 items. Location is good as it's less than a mile to the airport and it's my understanding they had a shuttle, although I had a rent-a-car Parking is $10. Overall its a clean place, good value. Bowden68 gives his thumbs up.

“wonderful hotel stay” We stayed in a beautiful river view room for two nights that was overlooking the bridge to New Jersey and Penn's Landing. We rented a car from Avis in New York, which is conveniently located in the hotel for us to return it because we didn't need it to explore Philadelphia. Upon checkout, I discovered that I left my folder with my return airline ticket in the room and hours later we returned to get it. The staff, especially the young bellman, was so helpful and concerned, and looked everywhere for it until it was finally found on a housekeeper's cart. The room was spacious and had a great bathroom. We would stay here again.

“We liked it, we would stay again” We (mom and two teenage sons) booked through Hotwire and got this hotel on a Friday night for $154/night. The room was clean and definitely big enough for the three of us. The concierge was great, answered all of our questions with a smile. As a matter of fact, all of the staff at the front desk was upbeat and a pleasure to deal with. I loved the hotel lobby, even though it was small, there were lots of simple little white tea lights lit all around and lovely white flowers that really made a welcoming atmosphere when we walked in. Location of this hotel worked out fine for us, plenty to do in that area. We do prefer to stay downtown on the weekends where it is quiet and less crowded in the evening but the Hotwire 4-star hotel with 95% approval rating at $154/night was too good to resist.

“Nice HGI” I just stayed one night while in town on business. The hotel is updated nicely, just like most all the HGI's. The room was clean, updated, and comfortable. They had a very nice gym/fitness center. It included cardio equip, weights, and a cable machine. I would recommend staying here if you are in the Jacksonville area.

“Great value” The Club Quarters Chicago (Central Loop) was quite chic. It was close to the museams and millennium park, but far from the bars and clubs. The rooms were standard size and had either two twin beds or one queen. My only complant is that they don't provide any blankets, so bring your warm pjs!

“Teeny Weeny Room but good location.” Pros: Location, location, location. Multiple subway lines within a 5-min. walk. SoHo shopping during the day, lots of neat little neighbourhood restaurants just to the north of Spring St. that come alive in the evening. Outstanding Staff. Everyone extremely helpful and welcoming. Free breakfast and internet. Those costs sure add up at other hotels. Clean and pleasantly decorated and reasonably priced. Really good value for the money. Cons: This is the smallest hotel room I have ever stayed in. There were two of us and if we wanted to get around the bed at the same time, one of us had to climb over it. We could hear everything. Noise from the hallways, elevator dings, slamming doors and conversations in the next room. The noise really travelled here. The pros heavily outweighed the cons and I would not hesitate to stay here again. It really outranked the 4.5* we had stayed at 2 days prior in every way except for space.

“This is the BEST bang for your buck around USC” We came for the USC-UCLA game. We booked the Vagabond in September. The price and location cannot be beat. It is HANDS DOWN superior to the nasty Radisson down the street. It is literally a block off the northern most part of campus. You can park for free and walk to the game. We stayed here last year. The place looked cleaner this year. The rooms are just basic with reasonable furniture and a fairly comfortable bed. NO BUGS. NO SMELLS. The bathroom is also quite basic but there was plenty of hot water. No exhaust vent in the shower area so things get a little steamy. Keep the window open. AC works well. The folks at the front desk were very nice to us. We used the printer to get boarding passes. Coffee in the am was decent. There was some major rave party going on about a block away one evening that literally shook the floors and the walls. This is beyond their control and had nothing to do with the hotel. It was hard to believe that LA allows permits for 40,000 random partiers. But hey, it's LA. Tip: bring ear plugs, then you won't care about any noise. Overall, you should use common sense when running around at night in the area. The hotel does have security (who were quite visible) and security cameras. Tip: Ask for extra towels when you get there because they are a tad small. And with all that steam, you need more drying power. We will be staying here again for sure. The great change over the last year is that the University Gateway apartment complex is now complete and features many decent fast food restaurants and a CVS within a minute walk from the hotel. Things are definitely improving around the whole area. You cannot beat this hotel for a game weekend or any other USC event. It is not posh but it's so worth it not to waste time in the car trying to get to campus from downtown LA (not to mention waiting to get your car out of valet at say, the Biltmore), And you don't have to pay to park on campus which saves time and lots of money on game days.

“would stay here again no question” This is a relatively new hotel - the rooms (spacious, nice sized washroom), service, and fitness centre (well equipped, has a yoga room with ipod wall plugin) are great. The location is great in downtown Chicago - right at a loop station, lots of good restaurants and entertainment nearby, and a 5 minute walk from Millenium Park, 10 minutes at most to the Magnificent Mile. If you're staying on a lower floor and don't like noise, the noise from the Loop might be a problem. Rooftop patio bar is very elegant.

“very nice hotel, good experience” Stayed here for one night as the Westin Horton Plaza was booked and I also wanted to be close to the airport. This hotel is literally across the highway from the airport, a 5 minute cab or shuttle ride (although the shuttle takes time waiting for others). They have constructed the hotel so that all rooms face the bay or marina and none is facing the airport. I heard absolutely no airport noise. Check in was fast and friendly, stop to greet the numerous and fabulous fish in their tropical tank. I felt the hotel was in pretty good, if not excellent, shape. The room was nice and spacious with a little balcony with a table and chairs. All standard SPG amenities are to be found as well as Starbucks coffee pods for the automatic brew. The shades are perfect for blacking out the room and the bed was standard (i.e. excellent) SPG sweet sleeper. I had a beer and empanadas at the bar, nothing special, in fact the empanadas were a bit dry, but I didn't complain since I was tired arriving at 9pm from NYC. The hotel restaurant and lounges were plenty busy and people were smiling, not sure if it was the Final Four or the food. There were plenty of weights and machines in the gym and it was not crowded for a Sat morning when there aren't too many people awake at 0700. The pool was nice and heated and would be very nice on a hot day. Signage to the gym could be improved as they get you in the right direction and then cease to exist, leaving you (me) wandering the floor hoping to trip into the gym. The location is good if you want to be close to the airport, but I can see how it would be a pain for those hoping to see San Diego. It's only 5-10 minutes to downtown, but this means a $10 cab ride each time you go in and then have to return. Walking would be a nice choice if you have 30-40 minutes, but there's a sidewalk along the bay with a great view.

“Gorgeous property within walking distance of Seattle tourist spots” We had come to this hotel as I was a bridesmaid in a wedding held at the hotel. I will admit, I don't usually think of DoubleTree Hotels as having much character, but the Arctic Club exudes Seattle history. The rooms are decorated with historic relics. My husband and I love hotels which tell a story, and the Arctic Club really does. We were welcomed at the front desk with chocolate chip cookies (I guess it's a DoubleTree thing), and although we weren't able to get into our room immediately, it didn't take that long to get in and we were able to store our luggage. The room used for my friend's wedding has this gorgeous dome, and her pictures were fantastic (for anyone considering a wedding there). Our hotel room was on the same floor as the event room, which usually would bother me, but since I was a bridesmaid in the wedding, it was intentionally done, so that people could get ready for the wedding in my room. I also visited a suite, where my friend (the bride) was getting ready, and it was very nice, with a lovely bathroom and also with a terrace. I read someone's comments about the neighborhood. I would agree that the area can seem a bit deserted at night, and on the weekends, since it is mostly a business neighborhood, but it is within walking distance to the market, and honestly, we felt safe while we were there. We never had a problem at all, and were out pretty late celebrating after the wedding was over. We've stayed at several hotels in Seattle, and this was my favorite by far.

“Loved the Palomar” Stayed at the Four Seasons for a conference, but for personal time transferred to the HoteL Palomar, and like every Kimpton stay this was a great choice. The Hotel: The hotel has the usual Kimpton charm, hospitality and the ability to make travel fun. It is a beautiful space, beautifully decorated, and manages to be modern and hip without being pretentious at all. At check-in we mentioned the secret word (gleaned from the Palomar's Facebook), and received a choice of complementary breakfast or four drink tickets in the hotel bar. (We opted for the drinks.) Didn't try the restaurant but did like the bar. In the lobby there is free coffee service in the morning, hot chocolate during the day, and wine social hour in the evening. The gym was well equipped but small. The business center was perfectly adequate and had free service for airline check in and printing of boarding passes. The location is perfect. It is in the center of a very well serviced area, with abundant restaurants, coffee shops, pharmacies and retail shopping options. It's 30 minutes or less to the airport, with a row of taxis in perpetual wait. The Room: Our room was at the very top level for rooms - the 23rd floor - which made for a great view even though the windows were small. There was of course no street noise. It was about as small as most hotel rooms are, but nicely laid out. The furniture was very comfortable and visually appealing as well. As Kimpton In Touch members we had free wifi, and were given a $10 credit to raid the minbar. The television picture was very good and there was a nice range of channels including HBO. The room had a nice little office of to one side which we actually made some use of, though mostly it was a convenient place to store and charge laptops and other electronics. The bathroom was well sized and the shower did everything I want a hotel shower to do. The towels were a little more sparse than I expected, but this is a modest criticism. On my last night there I heard quite a lot of noise from the room next door, but I think this had more to do with a particularly loud guest. Being on the 23rd floor meant an occasional long wait for an elevator, but that was a worthwhile trade off for me. My only two real criticisms are: * No in-room coffee - my second Philly hotel without this basic amenity * The cooling function which I did use at night was pretty loud. But it was not loud enough to make me choose any other hotel. In summary: I don't think there's a better place to stay in Philadelphia. I was torn between the Palomar and the brand new Monaco, and in the end am glad I chose the Palomar. I'm sure the Monaco is beautiful, and its surroundings in the more historic district are appealing, but Palomar wins for restaurant selection and street scene.

“Friendly Staff” Stayed here for a quick 3 dayer in San Diego. Shuttle pick-up was prompt. Check-in friendly and efficent. They gave us a ground floor room facing the parking lot. We asked if we could have a room facing the courtyard/pool, and that was not a problem. We were in room #210. It needs a little love and affection, as the sliding doors in the closet, need to be re-aligned, as well as the window in the sitting room. The full kitchen is great. We usually make use of them, but being so close to Little Italy, and the Gaslamp area, we decided to splurge. The fridge, though was handy for a beer, wine, and water. Our room was clean, and the bed was the usual "oh so comfy". The Managers happy hour, had draft beer and wine, as well as a light meal. The night we were there, it was burgers and hot-dogs, with all the fixings. We split a dog, as we had dinner reservations up the block in Little Italy. The breakfast was good in the morning, with a nice selection of just about everything. Eggs, sausage, breads, yogurt, fruit, juice etc. So you could fill up or just have something small. The staff at this hotel, were one (if not the best) staff ever. Always a smile, a hello, and answered all our questions with regards to areas to eat, transportation etc. Huge kudos to all of you. We took a trolley tour, but mostly walked everywhere, as we like to see it all at a snails pace. The train that runs behind, and pretty much through the heart of the City, was not really an issue. Yes you can hear the blast of the horn, but we were hardly in our room during the day. At night, they now have a curfew on the horn activity. Kind of adds to the vibe of this great city. One con,(from my wife). She would like to see the hotel use paper cups for the coffee/tea instead of styrofoam, as she feels that it effects the overall taste of the tea. Other than that, it was all good.

“Although I love this place” So, i am a huge fan of the andaz brand, I love the andaz Liverpool street, 5th avenue and wall street but......there is something about the wall street hotel that causes me sleep problems. I think the bed linen is over bleached, or the mattresses are to hard/soft, room too hot whatever - but all I know is that I can't get comfortable and struggle to drift off. The lobby is wonderful, the staff are great and the location is second to none (if you are visiting wall street), food is excellent too. Pity I can't sleep there though!

“Great experience in SOMA” This Westin lived up to the brand's reputation. The lobby, check-in, room, and luggage desk experiences I had were all excellent. The room wasn't huge, but that's to be expected. However, the layout of the room was sensible, it was well-decorated, and the tall windows offered great light during the day along with the good view. My only 2 VERY SLIGHT quibbles - the housekeeping staff replaced perfectly good towels (no eco-conscious towel program at the Westin) and in the bathroom the toilet was super close to the shower, which was an awkward layout. But these minute quibbles underscore how great my stay was - thanks for a great 4 nights!

“Amazing stay at the Adagio!” I had an fantastic stay at the Adagio. They just completed major renovations so the hotel looks brand spanking new. Our room was huge and completely renovated. The bathroom felt really clean too. I'm really particular about bathrooms and I was super impressed. And, you actually have space for your suitcase and enough room to walk around. I also had dinner and drinks at the Bar Restaurant Mortimer's on the lobby level. Food was really good too. Definitely need to try the pizza it was super delicious. Most importantly, the staff was great. Everyone was really friendly and very engaging. Not to mention the location is great. Just steps away from Union Square and all the touristy destinations and the financial district. I will definitely come back and recommend the Adagio to my friends and colleagues.

“Work-ed for me” I was in town for business and stayed 4 nights. Treated like a VIP. Had a quiet room on the 12th floor, cozy but reasonable by NYC standards. Eclectic decoration. Nios is nice for a drink and a snack - try the kobe beef sliders. Staff was very helpful. (It would be a plus to have a business center - I had to email the desk to get a copy of an email printed.) Outstanding location for theater and the local restaurants, walked to everything. Thumbs up and a good value relative to other hotels of similar quality in the neighborhood. Much more character than the megahotels nearby and you don't have to wait 20 minutes for an elevator like elsewhere.

“Chicago in Winter, No other place to go!” When you arrive the the Hampton Inn Majestic, the only thing that it's cold, it's the weather. With a warmth welcome from the Hapton staff, and the like-new rooms, this very well located hotel can not be beat in downtown Chicago. You are only 3 block away from Michingan Ave at the millenium park, and two block away from one of the loop's metro station, so yoou can move around Chicao freely!. Of course the relation cost-quality it's a winner!!

“New Hotel, going through growing pains” This hotel has been open about 2 weeks and theya re still going through some growing pains. Checkin was smooth, parking by valet is $20 per day. Rooms are brand new. Staff is green, but seems to be trying. Restaurant is good, there is not much else around this area. This hotel is isolated, and htere is not much gooing on downtown. It is a nice place. Rooms are great.

“Stay at the Sheraton in downtown LA, if you have to go to LA” Not being a big fan of the city of Angels I still had a nice stay at this Sheraton. Parking is of course expensive, $28 a night. The mall next to the hotel is pretty tired as is the food court. The staff was polite upon checkin and offered to hook me up with a Starwood preferred corner room which was nice. Internet is currently free, but only because they haven't fixed the bugs in the new system, otherwise its $15 a day. The staff at the bar isn't very friendly and they like to close early. They may be on the job less than four hours a night, so its very disappointing when they close up at 11:45 pm. I suggest Wokano, a sushi bar around the corner. Its open until 2 am and has good food.

“very nice hotel, if attending the Mccormick center” This hotel is very nice, very clean, the staff goes above and beyond to be accommodating. They are extremely friendly. If you are working at or attending anything at the McCormick center, this hotel is perfect. If you want to see Chicago, this isn't the best hotel. It is about a $8 cab ride to the loop and a $12 cab ride to Michigan street. There is little to nothing around the hotel, and overall not the nicest neighborhood in the evening. The hotel itself though is very nice, very clean, and very large. The rooms are clean and comfortable. and again, if attending the Mccormick center this hotel is perfect. The $33 self parking fee seems very excessive for being in the outskirts of town. Space is not at a premium here and this just seems very very expensive in my opinion.

“Fantastic Stay....wish I could have stayed longer” we only had one night in Chicago, and regret not being able to stay longer because the hotel was awesome. The valet guys were extremely helpful and were right there when we pulled up. the cost is $46, but you are in the city. I had gotten an email a few months back before their opening and was able to get the room for $89! What a deal for this hotel, it was definitely worth a lot more. Upon check in, we also received a "raid the minibar" coupon for two items up o $10. It was beautifully decorated with flat screen tv. We did not get to enjoy the wine reception at night, but did go down for coffee and tea the next morning in the beautifully decorated lounge area. There was a nice pool on the top floor and also a rooftop bar which was very nice. We did not eat at the restaurant Sable, but it looked very nice. We had dinner across the street at Rock Bottom Brewery and I would highly recommend it. The red line was right next to the hotel and we were at the White Sox game in 15 minutes. There were shops and restaurants in walking distance.

“Smaller hotel, but all you need if you'll be out & about town.” Very clean hotel. Front desk staff are very friendly & outgoing. Gave me great recommendations for dinner options. Free wireless, continental breakfast included in room cost. Courtyard Marriott right next door with a small restaurant & bar. Overall good experience & would return.

“A true find” We stayed 2 nights at the beginning of our California coast tour. The hotel is in a great location, nestled between Hollywood and Beverly hills. Walking distance to the Farmers market. We stayed in a suite and it was very spacious and especially super clean! The room was right beside the elevator, but we never heard a thing, it was a very quiet room. the breakfast is quite big and has a lot of choices. The room has a coffemaker, minibar, safe and a small balcony overlooking the courtyard. The bed was very comfortable and we got little chocolates every day. The best thing is the staff, whatever the request they go out of their way to accomodate you, with a big smile on their face.Thank you Michael and Michael and Paolo. We would return here anytime we are in L.A., it's truly a find and very reasonable rates, including free wireless and the breakfast.

“Location, Location, Location” First off let me say I only chose this hotel based on two things, location and travel rewards points. We were visiting relatives in the area and needed a hotel with a pool/jacuzzi and the prices were crazy high ($329 and up) I realize now that it was school vacation week for lots of the New England/northeast US so the prices were sky high even for Feb. but if you can use miles or can afford the price this hotel is outstanding. AS mentioned by others the location for touring is the best, 1/2 block to metro, 3 blocks to the Mall, across the street from the Spy museum. 1 block from Ford's theater and the Trolley Tour terminal. Every restaurant our relatives suggested we try was at most 3 blocks away!! Cabs are plentiful, MCI center is about 2 blocks away. Safe neighborhood, very safe and secure hotel. Night bell hop and you must use room key to access elevators. Didn't try room service but did have a drink at brewery downstairs and it seemed like an up and coming crowd. Lots of socializing going on. The one thing I did have a hard time with and this is true in all the DC restaurants is the smoke. I've gotten used to smoke free dining up here in Massachusetts and as my middle age creeps in I have to say I really get annoyed when I can't taste my food due to second hand smoke. (Spoken like the former smoker I am!) Everyone in the hotel was happy and helpful which made travelling with my teenagers much easier (who are neither happy nor helpful) Just kidding kids!! Anyway the positive attitude of the staff was much appreciated. The buffet breakfast (in the basement near the former vault) was a bargain at 9.95. It included custom made omelelettes and make your own belgian waffles, oatmeal, great fresh fruit, pastries, etc. Our room was surprisingly small (maybe because I was using travel reward points??) So small in fact that as soon as I saw it I gave up on the idea of a roll away for my daughter because we all agreed there was just not enough room to place it. The room was extremely clean, housekeeping was very good. Others have mentioned the construction noise factor but we were in the rear of the hotel and did not notice it. We did, however, notice a Hard Rock Cafe just behind the hotel and I imagine that could get quite loud on the weekend. All in all another great recommendation from Tripadvisor. Thanks guys.

“Nice facility” A bit off the beaten path, but a very nicely appointed hotel. Staff was very courteous. One concern was the parking since it didn't look very secure but there wasn't a problem. Didn't make use of the shuttle but definitely would if I stayed here again. It is very difficult to park downtown.

“Nice hotel, location okay” The Renaissance Denver is a modern, upscale hotel about halfway between downtown and the airport. Floors 10-12 are Club Level. I have stayed in both Club Level and in the lower floors. Rooms are identical with the major differences being the Club Lounge access and free Internet in room. Being a newer hotel by Marriott, the Renaissance Denver has a 32" flat panel TV, desk with internet jack, video jack for your laptop, and multiple electrical outlets for simultaneously recharging items such as laptop, cell phone, iPod, and GPS. Linens are typical high-thread count. Also, a sofa in king room or easy chair in dual queen room. Overall, room has a comfortable size at 440 sq ft. View from either side of the hotel (residential/industrial/downtown or across the street) is not memorable. Bathroom has marble and Aveda toiletries. Staff from front desk to housekeeping to maintenance were all professional and knew their jobs well. If you do not have Club Lounge access, the breakfast in the hotel is expensive. A good alternative is Panera across the street. With the parking garage across from the main entrance, I have tried both the valet parking and the self-parking. With the garage so close, I could often retrieve my vehicle faster than the valet. If you have a morning flight, keep in mind that the valet shift change occurs at 6:30 am. I had to wait 5 minutes for the shift change. Valet in the evening was pretty good. The redeveloping area of the former Stapleton airport may or may not be a negative depending on how you feel about it. There is lots of new housing and shopping areas across the street. The new Northfield town center/shopping area on the other side of I-70 is a nice place to walk around. The only noticeable negative was the daily freight train blaring its horn two blocks away.

“generally positive, but those elevators!” My business contact in NYC chose the hotel for me. The positives have been mentioned before: convenient midtown location, spacious room and bathroom. Other pluses: I found the staff friendly (by NY standards) and helpful. I appreciated the free internet in the business center; the quiet refrigerator and the microwave in my room; the closet safe; and the extremely comfortable desk chair. Others have mentioned the European-style platform beds and found them hard, but my bed was just the right degree of firmness. Problems: The bed has sheets and a heavy comforter, and nothing in between. The comforter was too hot, the sheets alone not enough. I used the bathrobe (which was supposed to be provided, but I had to request it) as a light blanket. The "easy" chair was remarkably uncomfortable. The beautiful full-length mirror hadn't been hung, just leaned against the wall. It was inconvenient having no drawers at the desk or in the bedside tables. The door connecting to the next room let through some loud conversations, but ear plugs kept this from being a problem. Though my room faced 52nd street, I was not bothered by street noise. Worst of all, there are only two functioning elevators in this 45-story building, making it very difficult/time consuming to go down at checkout time. Solution: ride up to the top, then back down. (For comparison, the building I work in has only 6 floors, but 4 elevators.) All in all, it was a satisfactory stay, but I'll stay elsewhere next time I'm in NYC, if the choice is up to me.

“Really comfortable and roomy” I booked this hotel as I arrived in LA at midnight and was going to Hollywood the next day. I wanted a quiet place to sleep and have breakfast. This hotel really fulfilled my needs! The shuttle bus from the airport was quick and the room was so spacious, the king size bed huge and comfortable! So many pillows! Bathroom was a good size. The only odd thing was that the mirror was partially covered by the big flat TV! Breakfast was included in our rate and it was very nice: omelettes, pancakes, fresh fruit, cheese, and pastries, cereals, bacon, sausage, etc. The waiter though came to us with a bill that I needed to sign stating that breakfast was included and he pointed out that there was a gratuity option! He had done nothing and he wanted a tip anyway! I gave 2 dollars so he’d leave us alone. He didn’t even reply goodbye when we left!

“Great Value” This was a great internet find. Great location to Union Station, Honeywell office, Federal Court, Embassy of Canada and Capital Hill. Room was small but very comfortable and modern. Breakfast was overpriced, otherwise the stay was wonderful.
“Bargain.....” Stayed here for the 2nd time, clean spacious rooms, convenient to airport, bar and food good and reasonably priced...basic but can't grumble at the price for what you get..good choice.

“Great Business Hotel Ruined By Noisy Guests” This Marriott has just been renovated, so the spacious new rooms were a nice treat during my stay for business in Dallas. The hotel is clean, modern and very nice and I am giving all of that 4 stars. HOWEVER, my stay here was absolutely horrible. I happened to be staying here the night of a college prom-like event and the hotel (every floor) was occupied by noisy, drunken college kids. The hotel tried to control them, but there were so many that they could not be controlled and, to be honest, they were paying for so many rooms and suites, I don't think they wanted to loose money and kick them all out of the hotel. I called the front desk 4-5 times and had to move rooms 3 times, to 3 different floors - these kids were SO loud and running down the hallways with garbage cans filled to the brim with beer bottles. I think if I had stayed here any other weekend, things would have been fine (I loved the hotel). Pros: -Clean rooms that are modern and very spacious -Comfortable, clean bed Cons: -Noise (but I think it was just a problem on this particular weekend) -Location as there are not too many restaurants within walking distance

“Pleasantly surprised.” We stayed here on my first trip to San Francisco. My aunt who had been several times over always stayed at the four seasons and wanted to stay there but we were going for a wedding being held at the Hotel Vitale, so we decided to try it because it was so convenient. We are glad we did. Since it was my first trip I am basing my opinion that it was in a great location based upon all of the places we were able to get to either by walking or a short cab ride. Check in was smooth, the rooms were ready, the fresh bath products were a very nice touch. For those of you who are as picky as me, I am happy to report that the showers are great with amazing water pressure. The views from this hotel are spectacular so I totally recommend upgrading the room, the $40 more we paid for our room compared to my aunts was astonishing, we had several rooms and my aunt was the only one who didn't, all of us had awesome views except hers, which was of the air conditioning units, totally worth $40. I know we ate in the restaurant although I have no memories of it, the food for the wedding however was catered by the hotel and the food was delicious. Their concierge was great, my brother forgot to bring a tie and when we went to the concierge to ask where the closest store was, he asked what color suit and shirt it was and was provided about 10 ties for us to choose from to borrow. Overall it was a clean, comfortable, modern, enjoyable stay.

“Venice is Cool” Great location one/half block frorm Oceanfront Walkway, 15 minutes from LAX airport. Cool, hip, modern design. Friendly staff. Large thick towels, smooth crisp bedsheets, lots of pillows. Rooftop bar with view of Venice and the ocean. Good restaurant Barlo off the lobby for meals all day and bar in the evening. Lots of restaurants and shopping on the Walkway and Main Street outside the hotel, and Abbott Kinney Blvd, a few minutes awawy. It is possible to walk north to Santa Monica pier, restaurants, bars and shopping. Very clean. Take advantage of the valaet parking, because street parking is sparse and short-term, and the nearby lots are set up for beach visitors, and have no in and out.

“I love the Historic Wardman Tower” This is an old-fashioned sprawling convention hotel in the leafy Woodley Park Neighborhood. From the sound of the other reviews, the main hotel appears to be a challenge--but the historic Wardman Tower, where I managed to snag a room for only $159 per night, is a real treat. The tower is connected to the rest of the hotel by a sun-drenched corridor filled with comfy chairs, potted palms and what I’m guessing is historically accurate floral carpeting. (The tower is probably a not good place to stay if you hate walking; you might need a sherpa to find your room the first night.) My room was large and beautiful with a walk-in closet. Great view of the city. Water pressure like a fire hose. Real windows that open. Friendly front desk. Metro station right across the street, easy walk to the National Zoo and the Adams Morgan neighborhood. Only downside is that there isn’t a ton of counter space in the bathroom.

“Great service, best price, nice rooms, pool, free wireless--can't go wrong!” We stayed at the Radisson Fishermans Wharf for Presidents Day weekend and had a great experience. I own a large retail store, plus I travel a lot, so courteous service is extremely important to me. The Radisson's employees exemplified excellent customer service. They were so friendly and cheerful that even our teenagers remarked "everyone' is so nice here!" The rooms were just right, nothing fancy, but everything clean and working well. Sleep number beds were very comfy. Nice pool, too. Free wireless internet was a huge plus--usually get charged about $15.00 for that. We paid about $130 per night, which included a breakfast from their coffee cart. Without even being asked, the front desk upgraded that to free breakfast at the ihop next door, when we couldn't get double beds. Our only complaint was the low water pressure in shower.

“Brand Spanking New, Great Staff, Premature Location” Stayed here for 9 days in May 2006. The hotel was just built and opened the end of March 2006- so everything is fresh, bright and smells good. Nice lobby with small bar, dining room complimentary computers and even a free printer. Makes it nice when printing out a Mapquest for a visit or a ticket voucher! Staff seemed extremely friendly and personable, rooms were a bit above average on size with a nice Sofa and coffee table, Comfy all white bed, oversized computer desk, free Internet, Fridge and, my husbands favorite, a nice BIG FLAT SCREEN TV!! The location was a bit odd until we heard that new Nationals Baseball Stadium will be built just down the street. It is mostly office buildings still under construction or nice new ones occupied and new Condo projects. It is just a short 1/2 block to the Metro Subway Station. We bought the 7 day pass for $22 and used it many times everyday with ease and safety. A must as all the museums and sites are really spread out in Wa DC. We dined with a convention most evenings - but had room service once and dined downstairs once and were pleased with both. There is only a Subway store and Five Brothers* and a CVS Pharmacy in the office complex next door so dining/retail choices are limited at the moment. * A wonderful Burger chain - gets lots of awards and I can see why - really one of best you will have - just like Mom used to make.....or better!

“All that we hoped” I know this review is a little late in coming. We stayed at La Mansion between Christmas and New Year's for our 30th anniversary. I like historic hotels and we wanted to see the lights on the River Walk. Everything was perfect. I had read some of the reviews that stated River Walk rooms had trees that blocked their view so when I made the reservation I requested that it be an unobstructed view and let them know it was our anniversary. We got exactly what we wanted. We also booked a package that included valet parking, breakfast, and a river tour. It is right on the River Walk and we were there during a holiday so we expected it to be noisey but it wasn't so noisey that is bothered us. We checked-out the day of the Alamo bowl so during our stay at any moment one of the college bands or Pep squads could break out in a song or cheer right across or under our balcony. All of this actually enhanced our experience and while I know the hotel didn't put this on just for us if you want a exceptionally quiet place this is not for you. We however loved it all! Because it rained one day of our stay we decided to try out the restaurant/bar for lunch. We enjoyed it and would definitely eat there again. Service everywhere was excellent. Thank you La Mansion del Rio

“Great visit...no problems, comfortable stay!” Nice hotel, friendly staff, comfortable room and good internet...that pretty much wraps it up. I would definitely consider the Courtyard for future trips to Charlotte. Close to everything. Free internet is always a good thing. The internet was consistently strong and the cable TV channels was good selection.

“Good Location, friendly staff, clean rooms and good sleep” Was worried about getting any sleep, was on 4th floor (417) view of parling lot. Slept well no problems. room is set up with 2 sinks at opposite ends in the room and is odd but was not an issue. We had 2 bikes and we had to keep them in our room, it was crowded but it was not obstructing the walkway. Older property but centrally located and easy to maneuver the streets. Parking is extra (14) and is in a open lot behind hotel. (no attendant) Breakfast is hot and cold selections. A good value.

“You'll be sad to leave!” We stayed at the Commonwealth for a long weekend for the Red Sox last regular season series - an annual tradition. However, this was the first time we stayed at the Commonwealth and we were very pleased. My review might be biased by the fact that it was some kind of nirvana for me to wake up in the morning and see Fenway Park outside of my window. But, I am a hotel dork (dork, snob, connoisseur...take your pick), so I'll try not to let my that cloud my assessment. The things you would expect to be exceptional for this level of hotel did not disappoint - comfortable bed, outstanding bedding that feels like silk, large bathtub with rainfall showerhead, quality bath products and, of course, a stocked minibar (for that ritual snickers and Heineken!). There was also a luxuriously large bathroom that allowed two people to get ready without bumping elbows and the restaurant (Eastern Standard) is quite a draw all on its own. We were eternally grateful they were still serving food at 1 a.m. when we finally arrived from the airport - a delightful gift of St. Christopher, the patron Saint of travelers. Everyone on the staff that we encountered was very nice and helpful. I needed to send some things back home which they cheerfully helped me with. The restaurant staff was great, and we never got that feeling like, "oh, you're just hotel guests." They treated us like regulars, but that could be because we spent a lot of time at the bar in between baseball games! The neighborhood is great. It just doesn't get easier to walk to the game, but it is really easy to walk down to the public garden, do some (window)shopping on Newbury St. or pop over to Copley Place. The green line is right outside the door to Eastern Standard if you don't feel like walking to the North end (we do, but we walk a lot). Overall, this is a great hotel...whether you decide to venture no further than your room or make it your base from which to explore the city.

“Kimpton excels again with 9-0” I am a big Kimpton fan so maybe I am a little biased but I found 9-0 just about perfect. The location is exceptional, the staff were friendly and professional, and the room was functional and in good condition. I was upgraded from a Queen Deluxe to Queen Deluxe view (1903) on the top floor with view of Boston Common, the State House and Charles River/Cambridge in distance (Thanks for the upgrade Jorge). Request a coffee maker for your room as the lobby coffee setup was not available until after 7am and was out of regular coffee on more than one occasion. Celebrated birthday dinner at Spire-the food and service were excellent. Entrees $25-35. I have read some of the negative reviews about the hotel but aside from the lobby coffee set up and the broken ice maker on my floor I had no complaints. Would happily stay at 9-0 again.

“Top pick for the area” After staying at several hotels close to Georgetown Law (and the capitol building), I rate this hotel as the best. You get a great combo of value for quality, plus the uniqueness that one expects from Kimpton. My only surprise was the limited hotel restaurant menu. Given the location is not easy walking distance to the more lively areas of DC, I was surprised that the hotel really failed to deliver more than a salad with a side of fries on the vegetarian front.

“Mostly good, some things to consider” We stayed here over New Year's Eve, wanting to be down in the thick of things for the festivities and weren't disappointed. The location is superb and our compliments to the doormen for pointing out the $30/day parking behind the hotel. (The Hyatt charges $50/day) We stayed in the West tower, 17th floor. The room was nice and when we checked in they offered an upgrade for $20 to a room with a "water" view, which we took. This is probably NOT worth doing as it's just a slice of the river if you angle your head to one side. Not much to see. FYI- The west tower is the one to be in on NYE. The main building had some traucous party going on and all guests to he hotel had to wear wristbands to show that they were staying in the hotel. Things were much quieter in the west tower, where we were happy to get a good night's sleep after walking back from the fireworks at the Navy Pier. Yep, the pier is a close walk.

“Can not say enough great things about this hotel!” I recently stayed again at the Staybridge Suites in Times Square -New York City and just had to write another positive review of this property. (See my previous review at http://www.tripadvisor.com/Hotel_Review-g60763-d1465162-Reviews-Staybridge_Suites_Times_Square_New_York_City-New_York_City_New_York.html) I really think what puts this property above others in NYC is the staff. They go out of their way to just make you feel welcome and that they appreciate your business. That level of service in the hospitality industry is a rare find these days. Everyone from the bellman to the check-in staff to the breakfast bar team were super nice to me and my family and went out of their way to help in any way they could. Other than the staff, the hotel is just a very clean, modern and comfortable hotel with a great location. Yes, the section of 40th Street the hotel is on used to be a little seedy, (it is directly across from the Port Authority terminal), but we never felt unsafe walking to and from the hotel. There is easy subway access 1 block away to the 42nd Street/Times Square station, and there are great restaurants nearby. (Try Moaz for a quick vegetarian bite). I love that the hotel has a real refrigerator so we could keep our leftovers and snacks cold. Plus, as I've said in my previous review, this hotel has the most comfortable beds I have ever slept in. The high speed internet, is actually high speed (and free), and there is good TV selection. If there are any downsides, it is that the elevator service is quite slow (true for any big city busy hotel), and the shower was a bit on the small side. (But it was modern, hot, with a great shower head). Other than that, I love this hotel and will keep coming back on my visits to NYC with the family!

“Great!!” We loved the Bulfinch. The only negative things that I can say are (1) a couple staff gave us some bum advice about ATMs and convenience stores (they are both available just across the street), (2) the bathrooms can be cold in the summer – with blasting air-con there that you cannot control, and (3) there is almost no closet room. But these are such small things. All else is great at the Bulfinch. The location is great. There are nice conveniences kiddy-corner - - a convenience store with ATM and a nice little place where you can grab breakfast. It is a short walk to the State House and Faneuil Hall, and in the other direction the Garden if you are here for a game or concert. It is a short walk (5 min) to the Haymarket T-station - - and about same distance to North Station, though Haymarket is a better walk at night (I guess unless there is an event at the Garden). The young staff is very friendly and helpful – it is a hotel where you feel a personal touch – after just a day the staff will know you as you walk in. The building itself is also very quaint – sort of a Boston version of the Flairtron Building. The rooms are cool and if you can afford – definitely get a “nose-room” suite. While the room may seem narrow - - but it is long and you have windows everywhere with some nice views. I love natural light and these suites definitely have them everywhere including the bathroom (we could see the Garden from the bathroom – and when we showered I could even see the State House looking into the living room). The bed was big and comfortable. Overall, I really loved staying at the Bulfinch - - I love Boston and the Bulfinch is a great way to stay in this great city.

“Loved It” Wow, what a hotel. From the time you enter to the time you leave you know you have entered a place fit for Kings and Queens but not so snobby children wouldn't also love this place. The lobby was beautiful and was decorated for Christmas; and smelled like spice. Wednesday-Saturday a band plays at the lobby bar and eventhough this is a high class place, the drinks were not overinflated in price. Lots and lots of action at the Hotel Lobby Bar at night. The staff was amazing and I got recommednations for where to dine and where to "party" that were spot on. Because this hotel is located downtown, there is an overabundance of places from which to choose that are within 2-4 blocks from the hotel. My room was wonderful and big and reflected 4 star. Next time I am in San Jose I am definitely staying here again.

“Best Starwood Hotel in NYC” When the price is within my company's affordability range, the Westin is always my choice. The rooms are comfortable and clean. The location is perfect for midtown appointments or catching a Broadway play. Two points off for the following: The gym is a bit crowded and not well ventilated. They closed their Platinum lounge. However, they did say they will be opening it again soon. Bonus Points: The double shade windows help keep out the Times Square bright lights. Luis at the front desk has great customer service skills.

“Nice place, and QUIET!” i was fearing my stay at this hotel, due to it's location on the airport property. but it was very well insulated, so there was no aircraft noise in the rooms at all. Quite a remote location. Nice walking trails alongside the harbor, leading to a neighborhood.

“Might be one of the better Hamptons I stayed at this year” Staying at this hotel was a very pleasant experience. The room was immaculate the staff was very friendly all around. It seems as if this was a newer hotel The breakfast area was very clean and the staff was pleasant. Staying at any airport is crap shoot. They are high turnover hotels and most airport hotels resemble a bad movie unless you can pay a premium price. This place was a decent value. By the way, if you follow my posts you notice I always try to mention the price. I am not cheap but I do own a 1 person consulting show. I don't live off a corporate expense account anymore. That being said, I always try to mention the hotel value

“Great stay in excellent location but room service could improve.” Last minute stay before an early morning flight and as usual, Harbor Island is the absolute best location to spend your last night in SD before an early 6am flight. Wonderful hotel with great views in rooms all of which have a balcony. Only complaint would be the room service menu which offers little for vegetarians. I ordered a $15 greek salad expecting something special but what I received was a few greens with minimal garnishes that could maybe warrant $5 at your local pizza shop. Disappointing.

“A blast from the past” We were visiting San Francisco with our 16 year old son and wanted to stay somewhere other than at the 'popular' spots like we have done before. We could not have been more pleased with the Phoenix. First of all having FREE parking was very nice. Despite what was expressed regarding the neighborhood, we thought it was fine. (Suggestion: If you are using the BART, walk toward the Library/City Hall and pick it up at Civic Center. It will shorter and safer than waking to Powell St.) The hotel totally made my wife and I think of our travels as kids with our parents. It is a vintage travel lodge style converted into a modern art deco hotel. The room was great, there is a pool, heated and continental breakfast each day. We would definitely stay here again. Once suggestion, request rooms in the back away from the pool.

“Great Value,Very Comfortable, Great Staff!!” This was our first stop on a 9-night California visit that included Carmel, Davis, Sonoma and San Francisco. All of our hotels were selected through the Trip Advisor and this property was the best, most interesting and greatest value of the hotels we used. It is not large and the staff was among the best we have encountered in traveling. Jessica at the front desk was especially expert in giving us directions and opinions on dinner at Satana Row and we had an interesting evening of great weather, food and people watching. Our room was very comfortable - third floor with mission-style decor and included a full breakfast and complimentary wine in the evening and $10 of mini-bar snacks. Our room was spotlessly clean with no noise from other guests or the highway. We enjoyed sitting on the pool deck patio with a glass of wine before going to Santana Row for dinner. The mood here is more of an Inn than a hotel - it feels smaller and more cozy than a hotel.
