The hotel facilities worked well, easy WiFi connection, plenty of hot water, comfortable beds, free parking, etc. Breakfast was a pleasant suprise - not the usual coffee and pasteries, but a full meal/buffet of eggs, bacon, sausage, potatoes, fresh orange juice, etc. I've never considered San Jose a destination in itself, but now that I've experienced this hotel I might go back and skip the crowds at Carmel.

“The Best” I agree with all the previous reviewers. Excellent choice for downtown Chicago. If I could remember the names of the staff members I'd list them with 5 stars after each of their names. Very comfortable hotel in a perfect location at a really good price. Would stay here again anytime.

“As expected” Great rate achieved through priceLine, received a room of suite proportions, front office staff very helpful, the hotel actually exceeded expectations, and is very well situated in downtown San Diego.

“Great boutique hotel, though wouldn't consider it a 4-star” The Hotel Felix is a fine boutique hotel in a great location, a few blocks from the Michigan Ave. shopping area, a CTA red line station, and great restaurants including Rick Bayless' famed Frontera Grill. We appreciated the hotel's commitment to the environment and its free wifi -- very nice not to have an upscale hotel soak us for up to $13 per day for Internet service! Web sites including Priceline consider this a 4-star hotel, but I think a 3.5-star or 3-star rating would be more appropriate. Our queen-bed room was one of the tiniest we've ever stayed in, tightly furnished with a bed, end tables, a desk and desk chair. Another chair would have been nice, but there was no room for one. Also, the hotel's "fitness center" was just a very plain room with two treadmills, two cross-trainers and a collection of dumbbells -- about as meager as what you'd find at a Courtyard by Marriott or Homewood Suites, not a 4-star brand such as Hilton or Sheraton. We learned while trying to take a nap that it was best to keep the heating system's fan going and not allow it to switch off, to drown out sound from the hallway that kept invading our room. Guests might want to avoid the hotel's overpriced restaurant, Elate. Our Sunday brunch for two, including drinks, taxes and tip, cost about $75! Our waiter suggested Bloody Marys, we both said yes, but we really should have asked about the price: a steep $12 each. We also were asked for our toast preference, suggesting that our entrees came with toast, so we both chose sourdough. When our meals came, one of us got sourdough on his plate, but the other got wholegrain toast on a separate plate. We decided not to complain about the error -- but were quite annoyed when the bill included a $3 charge for wholegrain toast.

“Lots of charm” Lovely hotel with lots of character. Rooms were small but we expected that and didn't spend much time there other than to sleep. We asked for a quiet room and got a back location where it was peaceful. Unfortunately our neighbours were not quiet and the walls are VERY thin. Cookies and coffee in reception were very appreciated! Reception staff polite and helpful. Got a great deal on travel ticker - $99 a night with $25 credit for food and drinks. We didn't even spend it all before we left!

“Good, reliable airport hotel” The Hilton on Harbor Island is certainly nothing to write home about, but did offer the basic expectations for a Hilton property. Room was very clean, though the furniture somewhat dated. Very comfortable bed; small television. Arrived at 10:30 am and requested early check-in. As HH Gold, she apologized that she didn't have any rooms with a "good view," but since it was just one night and I would be gone all day, I took what she had (an 8th floor room, across from the elevator, overlooking the marina and airport). Despite being right at the elevator, noise was never a problem. The only real complaint I have about the hotel was the loud noises made by the water pipes in the hotel. Any toilet flushing or shower running was very loud. That could have had something to do with location of my room...not sure. Would've self-parked, but felt $17/day for that location was a bit extreme, and opted to return the car to Hertz before returning to the hotel that night. They do have 4-5 check-in parking spaces with a 15-minute limit (I left my car there for 30 mins with no problem). Wireless high-speed at $11/day was reliable. This wouldn't be a top choice hotel for a longer stay in San Diego, but for catching an early AM flight, definitely a safe bet.

“Consistent experience” The Four Seasons are an exemplary run business when it comes to service and attention detail. The hard part is maintaining the consistency. They do it. The spa/gym area is nice along side the door pool. Location is great with many stores and restaurants within walking distance. Great staff. The food was fantastic as I attending a dinner for an event hosted by the hotel (the best hotel food I have had). Highly recommend this property.

“Nice little hotel in the middle of the big apple” It a small hotel on the Manhattan side of the brooklyn bridge that is good for a business or pleasure traveler. Standard Hampton morning breakfast, helpful staff, but very small rooms, so if you are trying to fit more than 2 people in the room, it might be cramped. Walking distance to most lower manhattan toruist sites, and the deli around the corner is very good. Nothing fancy, just gets the job done.

“Pay Attention To The Directions... It's Worth It!” This property is tucked between two other hotels on an access road that's easy to miss without electronic assistance, but it's definitely worth seeking out. We were visiting friends for the night and needed a large room... Hawthorn Suites did not disappoint! Our suite was expansive, complete with two queen beds, a sofa-bed, fireplace, full kitchen and full bath. The room was clean, quiet and comfortable, and the staff (Jen & Wes especially) went out of their way to make our stay enjoyable. The parking is somewhat limited with one row around the perimeter but we did not have time finding a spot. Free wifi and a full breakfast were included (eggs, waffles, cereal, fruit, etc.). There were a few minor drawbacks, including a closet door that was off the track, a curtain that let a little too much light into the room from the side, and most notably the phones did not work. None of these things, however, adversely affected our experience (aside from not getting a wake up call), and when we reported everything to the front desk on checkout the staff apologized and promised to send someone to look at it immediately. For it's location right off the freeway, the comfort and space, amenities and most importantly price... this is definitely a hotel we will seek out the next time we need to stay in the Columbus area!

“Wished I could have stayed longer” The Fairfax embodies service and elegance. It feels like a boutique hotel but seems a little larger than that. I was in a very large room on the top floor overlooking the lovely rooftops of Massachusetts Ave. It felt like Europe. Perfectly lovely decorations, enormous bath, and attentive service.

“Nice historic hotel” I stayed at this hotel for a conference. The lobby is beautiful but the rooms could use some updating. The staff is not very friendly. Most in room coffee makers at other hotels include tea bags as well as coffee, when I asked my housekeeper for a tea bag I was shocked when she told me that I could not have one. She told me only coffee. So, if you prefer tea make sure you bring your own.

“Another Amazing Kimpton Property!” We stayed 2 nights over MLK weekend with our 11 year old son. The hotel is right on the Freedom Trail and a minute or so walk from the Park Street T station. We found the location super convenient for walking the city, jumping on the T and having our friend drive us to/from Logan Airport. Our room was clean and spacious. The bathroom was up to date and roomy. We had a lovely view of the Boston Commons and Charles River. Like other Kimpton hotels, the staff was friendly and helpful. These hotels are beautiful and chic, plus warm and comfortable. We've enjoyed Kimpton hotels in Chicago, D.C., N.Y., and now Boston. Also, the Concierge was quite helpful and recommended an amazing seafood spot for Sunday night dinner, The Oceanaire.

“Great hotel, but......” Every year, a large group of us stay at the Crescent Court for a week professional activities. This is my 5th year. The desk staff are friendly and efficient making checkin and checkout efficient. The rooms are spacious and the minibar fairly well stocked. The beds are VERY comfortable! It is within walking distance to a variety of great restaurants, regardless of your culinary tastes, including a Nobu Japanese restaurant off the lobby. I have never used their spa services. The hotel staff are quite attentive. However, I did get annoyed by the" turndown service", which was almost routinely around 8:30 or 9 pm. Now there are other high end hotels nearby (like the Ritz only a block away), which should increase the competition and improve the service. Don't expect "good views" form ANY of the rooms. You pretty much be looking out at the entrance drive and an office building on one side of the hotel or a small courtyard and a shopping building on the other side. Nothing scenic around it.

“Perfect location, service, great price - highly recommend” I traveled to San Antonio for a conference and there were so many choices... we selected this. Turned out to be the PERFECT CHOICE. 2 easy blocks to the Alamo, about 3 blocks to the Riverwalk.. Throw in free breakfast (and a pretty good one), free Internet, and really nice, clean rooms with a fridge and it's a great choice. I would prefer this over the Hilton Palacio del Rio, where our meeting was (grumbling from the guests all week who stayed there... have to pay for Web access, expensive...) The staff was very friendly, the rooms were very comfortable & roomy. Great to work in or kick back after a day of meetings. Great fitness center. We paid $50 less than the meeting rate at the other place, and had about a 5 block walk (right past / through the Alamo) to our meeting. Again, if you are worried that it'll be off the River, do not worry. It's close, easy access. I'm not sure what else to say other than I highly recommend it. My colleague was very happy with the selection as well.

“Very happy with my stay” Although the hotel was not my choice because I traveled for business, the hotel was very nice and in a convenient location. The metro was in walking distance and there were many, many local restaurants to choose from in the area. We particularly enjoyed Ruth's Chris and went there for two nights out of our 3 day stay. The hotel pub is also nice. I dined there for lunch and had the chef salad. The hotel room was very comfortable and very quiet. The hotel is very large in size but I was located in the center tower which was not far from the lobby area. I would certainly stay at the hotel again if I am ever in the area again.

“Perfect” We got this hotel on priceline for $96 per night and it exceeded our expectation by a long way. Some of the other reviews complain about the view or the price they paid, they obviously can't afford the room and did not look at the hotel from the outside. The hotel is surrounded by buildings and of course would not have a view unless you were overlooking the front street. We had a brick wall to look at but it really did not make a difference. If you are looking for a view you should book at a hotel known for the view...lol. The service was amazing, we were greeted every time we got in or out of the elevator, they offered to move our bags several times for us and the concierge (Shamus) was extremely helpful. I would stay here again and recommend this hotel to anyone. Also, the bathroom was small, but the room we had was just as large as most other hotel rooms I have stayed in.

“A Pleasant Surprise” I found the Renaissance to be a great hotel when you need a place near the airport. Other reviews say the hotel is outdated, but the 3rd floor conference room our group was in was just renovated and brand new, even the restrooms were very contemporary. The food at The Sanctuary was better than I expected. Over the course of several days I had crab cakes, and a breakfast, and onion soup and it was all good. So was the cocktail lounge. The staff was so helpful and courteous, and my room was very comfy and had everything I needed. It was quiet too, except for the night I arrived. Unknown to me, Presidential candidate Mitt Romney was in Philly & staying at this hotel, and the place was buzzing with reporters, his team, and secret service people. Once the excitement from that died down, the place was quiet. If I had to go back to this area for business, I'd go back. By the way, it's about a 20-25 minute drive to downtown or the Rittenhouse Square area.

“Great experience” This review is partly influenced by the fact that we got a great deal through AAA that included parking and a $50 food credit. Nevertheless, the staff was welcoming, the room was wonderful (although the mattress was a little hard for my taste), the view from the room was great and the food at the Griil (dinner and breakfast) was excellent.. It all absolutely felt like luxury. My main criticism is that there is a high charge for WiFi, which is rediculous for a hotel in this class (Or, for that matter, any hotel these days. It's like charging extra for cable TV or air conditioning.) And with such a high parking fee (albeit waived as part of our package), there is no excuse for the valet bringing us to the wrong car.

“Nice spot” I stayed at the Fairmont Washington, DC while attending a recent conference. The rooms were well appointed and fairly large by big city hotel standards. The hotel is about 3 blocks from the Foggy Bottom Metro stop where there is also a Whole Foods and a bike share. I took advantage of the bike share and took a nice ride around the mall one morning. The hotel is also a quick walk to Georgetown and the Dupont area both with great restuarant options. I love Fairmonts, although this one wasn't quite as spectaular as some of the others I have stayed in around the world, it was well above average as far as a large conference hotel goes. I am really bummed that Fairmont has switched out the Miller Harris bath products for something called Rose 21 - just not as good and didn't seem as high quality. If returning to DC I would definitely stay at this hotel again.

“Here's why I rated it as I did....” If you read through the various reviews on this hotel, you'll get a pretty accurate picture of the good and the bad. However, one person's excellent is another's average. Here's why I rated it as I did. Staff - Very curteous and helpfull, always responded to our needs - a "5" Rooms - Very clean and functional. Very small, but you're not in New York for the room if you stay here. On it's own - "2", becasue it's NYC "3". Breakfast - It's free "5", well stocked "5", very busy in the morning with little room "2". Ran out of items because of the crowd "2". Location - Not on Broadway but very close. "4" View - We were on the backside of the hotel, 17th floor. Nothing to see but buildings "2". Overall a "4" because the things we really wanted and needed out of the hotel - good staff, free breakfast, good location, outweighted everything else. To call this a "5" is similar to grade inflation. The property is not bad and I'd stay there again in a heartbeat. However, if I wanted something with more space, amenities, etc. I'd need to look elsewhere. Knowowhat you want before you book here. If you plan to spend time in the room and want to be pampered. Pull out the wallet and spend more by staying someplace else.

“An excellent base for a trip to San Francisco” We stayed here for three nights in order to see San Francisco. We found it friendly and clean and a 'a bit different'. The wine receptions every early evening are an opportunity to share ideas and experiences with fellow guests - the wine was good too. Its position allowed us to walk to everywhere we wanted to go.

“Wonderful Hotel in a Lively Area” This hotel opened 1 year ago (Feb. 2010) in the newly designed LA Live area near the Staples Center. We stayed here for three nights for a conference at the LA Convention Center, which is a short walk from the hotel. As Platinum Elite clients, we were upgraded to a top floor room (2170) and had access to the lovely concierge lounge. The room was very clean, beautifully decorated in a contemporary, yet comfortable style. It had everything one would find in a typical Marriott only more stylish – very comfortable bed with duvet, lots of good lighting, including bedside reading light, contemporary sofa and contemporary, but comfortable chair, large armoire, fine toiletries. The bathroom was roomy, the sink very large and the walk-in shower very large. (There is no tub in this room). Tall people take notice. THIS is the hotel for you. The showerhead was so high that I (5’2”) could not reach to adjust it. With the Staples Center right next door, it is clear that this hotel caters to basketball players. The lobby is magnificent with two contemporary bars and a very good restaurant. Bottom line: this place is upscale “hip.” We appreciated the security of having to use your room key to use the elevator. All personnel – front desk, valet, bellhop, restaurant staff, and housekeeping are friendly and welcoming. The restaurant was quite good with a contemporary American menu that had something for everyone – soups, salads, small pizzas, main dishes, burgers, sandwiches, and small plates. Apart from the noisy lobby bar and loud music, we were very pleased with this hotel on all levels and highly recommend it. The LA Live area is not for everyone. We felt a bit over-stimulated from all the light beams, lighted billboards, crowds and hoop-la going on at that moment due to the PAC-10 at the Staples Center. It definitely is a lively area with a lot going on for visitors.
“Good Hotel, Good Location” This hotel is on a good location, about 4 blocks north of the GWU subway stop. Nice hotel, good rooms, well appointed. Clean and Quiet.

“We had a great time, but our Friends were not so lucky” We came to San Antonio with Friends to visit Sea World, and they picked/recommended this hotel for us. When we got there, we were upgraded to the Top Floor, Room wise you get a few more amenities in the room, and a great balcony to watch the world go by. but as the Concierge lounge is closed on the weekends, not much else. For us the hotel was great!, Room was beautiful, comfortable, a little small but not badly so, Breakfast in the restaurant was good and the staff were very helpful (example - I asked the concierge for the best way to the Target that was nearby and without provocation “I’ll do better than that sir, I will take you there and off we went!). Location was OK for Sea-World but this was more due to construction issues slowing things down. BUT….. We were there the same weekend as some sort of High School Band Competition with this hotel hosting several schools. What did this mean? First off the pool/Hot tub area were turned into a Spring Break, so we could forget bringing our son down there as well as the joys of High School Children running through a hotel (although I cannot say I wasn’t as bad when I was that age!!) The biggest problem was The friends we were traveling with specified that they needed two rooms each with two queen beds. They were both given King Bedrooms, and the although they were initially promised rollaway beds. By the time housekeeping got to them, they had used them all and they had to have air mattresses. Further complaining and stress and Management pointed out the sofas in the room were pull out Beds. Why didn’t they say this in the first place? Overall a very good hotel. I would stay there again. but do bear the above in mind if you need more than one bed in your room.

“Great Hotel in Mission Valley” I have stayed in the Mission Valley area of San Diego several times in the past couple of years for business. In this time, I have experienced a couple of different hotels in this area and I have to say that to date, the Doubletree is my favorite. Overall, the only true negative of this property is the fact that it is strarting to look a little dated. Despite this, the hotel is still VERY clean and comfortable. The decor is warm and inviting. I would however have preferred a proper office chair for the desk. To make a long review short, I will simply list the pros and cons of this hotel from my perspective. PROS: -Rooms are clean and comfortable. -Location is wonderful. Very close to shopping, restaurants, and entertainment. Also, the Trolley stop is just across the street. -i had a great view from my balcony of the vally. -Its a Doubletree, so obviously, the cookies are a great addition. -The staff is very friendly and helpful CONS: -Decor is becoming a little dated. -Parking is an onsite garage. While it seems to be plentiful, beware that the spaces are VERY tight in certain areas. If you arrive back late to the hotel on a busy night, you may have trouble parking that Lincoln Town Car. (You might get parked, but won't be able to open the door).... It is San Diego and parking is limited.... NEUTRAL: -Be aware that Parking is an extra charge, as it is at most of the hotels in this area. They offer a Business plan that can save you money on this by adding in parking and internet. -The Breakfast buffet is adequate, but could use a little more variety.

“Great hotel, but really expensive room service/breakfast” I stayed here in May 2012 while attending a conference. The hotel is really nice, with big rooms, large bathrooms with showers and tubs, and quiet, even though the hotel was full. The concierge was really helpful finding restaurants. Recommended us a superb grill; and a really nice place in Chinatown. Location is perfect for business, close to several investment firms and also South Station. It also has a nice fitness center and heated pool (this last one I didn't use). Only complain is about room service. Even though the food was fine and service was really fast, I found it really expensive, with several charges that in the end increase the bill a lot. Breakfast is average and also overpriced.

“Beautiful luxurious property in OK location” This is one beautiful hotel!! From the moment you walk in, the impressive lobby décor is welcoming and we really had no problems with the staff - they were quite attentive and helpful. The rooms are fabulous – plasma TVs, phenomenal luxury bedding, tasteful carpeting and drapes with every amenity you could wish for in a hotel room (except no coffee machine) and really nice lighting. We loved the lighting in the headboards as well as the stylish individual reading lamps. Robes, slippers, glass scale, organic herbal toiletries – all top of the line, not to mention the marble and granite bathroom with full wide bathtub and separate glass-encased shower, all of which was the highest quality material and really clean. I also enjoyed the user friendly electronic DO NOT DISTURB and HOUSEKEEPING buttons. The rooms were mostly quiet, although you could hear the next room door opening and closing and I could hear the shower on the upper floor as well. There are over 70 TV channels and every amenity in the room, so there wasn’t much more one could ask for, especially paying under $100 via priceline. I don’t know if the hotel will hold up over time, since it is such a new property, but I somehow think it should. We loved it and would definitely stay here again. The only negative aspect to this hotel is the location. It faces a dirt pit of sorts, as this whole area is undergoing much rebuilding and renovation and although not a far walk from Quincy Market, I think it is more convenient for tourists to be situated in a more central area such as Copley. The area is totally dead day and night but you are only a two minute walk from South Station which is so convenient for using the T. We did not mind, as I’d take this kind of luxury hotel any day over the older more run down properties located centrally.

“Reccommended” Hotel is very clean, well maintained, reasonably priced, and well located. This is the second Garden Inn I have stayed at (other was just outside of Times Square in NYC) and both have exceeded my expectations. We started our vacation at the Four Points in Pineville, but were dissappointed in that hotel, and stumbled across this one. The staff was great in accomodating us on short notice, and accomodating the other groups in our party.

“Always excellent” We have been going to this hotel every Thanksgiving holiday since I was about 18. I am now 25. We used to stay at the Marriott or Hilton but my mom decided to stay here to save money. We haven't been back to either of those hotel since. This place is never a disappointment. I always feel right at home when we get here. I love the breakfast, first because it's free, and secondly because I LOVE WAFFLES. You also get free sodas all day and they give free popcorn and nachos in the evening. You are also on the riverwalk and can walk down to watch the river boat parade. I love going to San Antonio for Thanksgiving. I have such good memories! We eat Thanksgiving brunch at either the Marriott or Hilton. I was also allowed to bring my dog Baxter when he was still a puppy. The beds are ALWAYS comfortable! Make sure to go to Fiesta Texas, Sea World, The Shops at La Cantera, North Star Mall, Quarry Market, and last but certainly not least Mi Tierra or La Margarita at Market Square. I have such fond memories of all these places. When I go without my parents I feel incomplete since we have been doing these things since i was just a kid! San Antonio and Drury Inn= happiness

“Close to the Fort Worth Art Museums” We choose the Residence Inn due to its location, close to The Modern Art Museum. We were there to see the Lucian Freud exhibit. The hotel is only a short drive to The Modern and also the Kimbell and the Amon Carter. Check in was quick and easy. We had requested an early check in and this was no problem. Our room, on the east side overlooking Trinity Park was clean and spacious. The bed was comfortable and the extra feather pillows we requested were there when we arrived. The complementary breakfast provided a good selection of both hot and cold dishes. Check-out was easy and our statement arrived by e-mail. The Residence Inn will by our choice when we're in Fort Worth.

“Typical Homewood, in a GREAT location with Wonderful staff” The location is perfect for shopping and eating! The actual rooms were dated but clean with nice large windows. The workout room was big and with a great view, but the AC didnt work at the time. There is a small pool (indoor). Staff was wonderful all around. I will certainly stay here again.

“Nice, clean, friendly hotel” Stayed here one night with my son on Dec 27. We picked this hotel ONLY because of it's proximity to LAX because he loves flying and watching aircraft land and take off. In fact, we specifically requested a room with a view of the air traffic. The receptionist was very friendly and put us in room on the 10th floor facing north. The room was decorated in a modern style and very clean. It was not very big, but certainly not small. The beds were soft and the bath room was nice with plenty of towels. The workout area has about 10 cardiovascular machines, each with it's own TV screen. The bar is comfortable. The pool was about 80 degrees and comfortable. We moved to a different room after I walked around and found that the view to the south (which has more traffic noise...but not enough to disturb you) had a better view of the airport. The receptionist was very friendly and helpful in finding a room with a southern view. Overall, I'd stay again (especially via the Priceline price I got.) Parking is a bit steep at $13.50 overnight.

“Excellent hotel” I stayed at the Omni Houston for 4 nights in March. First of all, I got an excellent rate though travelzoo (75 dollars a night). I had a great stay. The hotel is spotless, service is great. There is a lot to do close to the hotel (good restaurants, great shopping) but you need a car (we had one so we were fine). There's free wireless internet and complimentary morning beverage (you can choose 1 cold and one hot drink, plus a bottle of water). The swimming pool looked great but I didn't use it. Our room was very spacious, good bathroom too. The beds were very comfortable. Parking is expensive but since we got such a great rate anyway, it wasn't a problem. I found the hotel to be pretty quiet except for one night when the was a party going on and I could hear loud voices until after midnight. There were no problems on the other nights however. I had one minor (very minor lol) complaint: they didn't have Comedy Central and I missed my daily dose of Jon Stewart and Colbert. Overall, I was very satisfied with this hotel, especially considering the price I paid.

“Great Facilities for Convention Style Meeting” Despite the stress of a global conference with 1,300 delegates, the staff remained cheerful and eager to please. As far as location goes, being on one of the outlets to Lake Michigan and adjacent to a pleasant promenade seemed like an unexpected bonus. Having a drink river-side was nice. Although the location may seem isolated (the blocks are long ones) a 10 minute walk will put you in the heart of Michigan Ave and plenty of fun places to eat. The rooms themselves are the standard that one expects from a Sheridan, big and comfortable. The pool and fitness facilities are above average, especially for an urban hotel. As part of a huge group meeting, the meeting facilities were excellent. But as an individual traveller seeking the delights of the city, I'm not so sure I would stay at what felt like a commodity (albiet nice) hotel. There are many places in Chicago with more character in more interesting locations at better prices.

“Great hotel close to downtown” I chose this hotel because I wanted to be close to downtown, but I had a car and I wanted free parking. You can get downtown on the bus or trolley, but without a car I think I would stay in a downtown hotel. I found the hotel much as others have written. It is very clean and the staff were all friendly and helpful. My room was very quiet. There was a thunder storm one night during my stay and I never heard any noise. I was near the elevator and vending machine, but I did not hear much hallway noise. I ended up going a mile or two west of the hotel on Madison Av for two meals. There are several good locals restaurants in the Midtown section of Memphis. I had dinner at the Blue Monkey, which is a very cool old bar with good casual dining. I also had lunch at the Bar-B-Q Shop. Parking is free and easy to find in that area and there are many restaurants. It is also a very safe feeling area.

“Really nice staff” I was there for six nights for a conference at the convention center. What a great location - it's catty-cornered from the convention center...couldn't have asked for a better location. And, it's a quick walk over to 16th Street. There's also a church (a Methodist church) fairly close by - a 10 minute walk - if you're interested in making to a worship service on Sundays. When I checked in, the front desk guy, Ari, got me all checked in, and then when I asked about walking around downtown by myself, he assured me I'd be fine. And, then, the next thing you know, he's printing out a map to a grocery store that I'd decided to walk to (so I could get my own breakfast foods). He really did go out of his way to help me figure out which grocery store to get to - and was very helpful in showing me how to get there. The hotel is very nice...nothing extraordinary about it (except Ari). The room (on the seventh floor) had a nice view of the mountains. But, that was really the only thing really special about the room. There was free wi-fi, which is a must for travelers these days. The restaurant (Pi) was fine, room service was quick (20 minutes), the coffee shop was handy (tasty tea!), and the beds were comfy. All in all, it was a nice place to be when you have to be in a hotel for six days. It was quiet - rarely heard anyone else in the hallways and never heard anyone next door.
“Love the Monaco” Great hotel in perfect location. Friendly service and pet friendly!

“Charging extra for internet is so third-world” Nice hotel, all the luxuries you would expect from Hyatt. Had to pay for parking which I guess is to be expected downtown in a big city. But it really frosts me to have to pay $12+ for 24 hours of internet access. Come on, Hyatt, if every dinky motel and rv park out in the boondocks can offer free internet, what's your problem? Here's a tip: one block away is a Paradise Bakery Cafe. They have free internet, good food, and cookies to die for. Spend your money there instead of paying the Hyatt for something that a "luxury" hotel should be embarrassed to charge extra for.

“Solid 3 star but not a 4 star property” Just back from a stay at the Affinia 50. Overall was satisfied. On the plus side, the rooms (at least ours) are relatively spacious. Bed is comfy. Good isolation from noise, which I was not sure would be the case because we were down on the 3rd floor and close to the elevator (though not right adjacent to it). On the flip side, the room was showing some minor signs of wear. In two places the molding of the headboard was noticeably peeling away from the frame. The lone dresser was cheaply made, something you might put in a kid's room, not suspension drawers, and one of them was stuck partially opened, enough so that we just didn't use it. The bottom of the inside of the bathroom door was very badly scratched. One bulb in the bathroom light fixture burned out and remained out during our stay (3 nights). And when in the bathroom, the sound of music clearly echoed into it from some other room, could not tell if was from below (the lounge is on the 2nd floor so probably) or above. But while audible in the bathroom it was not loud enough to disturb us in the main room. I stay in Midtown East a lot, and this location is close to the Divine Wine Bar (flights of wine and tapas-like food) which I heartily recommend, Amma (great Indian food) and Dos Caminos (Mexican) which is also good. My complaints/observations are relatively minor, but they are the type of things separating 3 star and 4 star hotels. There are other hotels in the area (which I won't name, as TripAdvisor has rejected a restaurant review of mine in which I named other restaurants), some of which are a clear step up in quality and can be had for similar prices or even less when they run specials. All in all, if you book at Affinia 50 it seems a pretty safe bet you won't be disappointed, but you won't be wowed either.

“Nice Theatre District property” Whether you are travelling alone or with kids, if you want to be in the heart of Manhattan action, look no further. A two-room suite with a kitchenette at this price in the centre of Manhattan doesn't easily get beaten. You are right on Times Square (which, for some people, may not be the ideal place to stay), within walking distance of most Broadway theatres and restaurants and within walking distance also of Fifth Avenue shopping, the MoMA, Time Warner Centre, Rockefeller Centre, the Empire State Building and Central Park. How do you better this? Our suite on one of the highest floors overlooked Times Square and Manhattan skyscrapers and we loved the view. The suite had a bedroom and a sitting/living room, with a television in each of them, a largish bathroom (two sinks), a kitchenette (with crockery and cutlery available if you wish), a Wolfgang Puck coffee maker with unlimited supplies of gourmet tea and coffee, Neutrogena toiletries, an in-room safe,iron and ironing board, a referigerated mini-bar and an additional empty referigerator for guest use. The hotel also has a very efficient laundry service. All the stuff you need to make your Manhattan stay comfortable. I would have been happier though had brighter colors been used in the suite interior. Dark colors do tend to make the suite less cheery than it could have been. The staff are exceptionally nice to you, at every level. Housekeeping could be better though. Use the Concierge's desk only for information but stay away from it for theatre bookings. Lots cheaper if you call Ticketmaster. If the Times Square action right outside is agreeable to you, this is an excellent option.

“SURPRISING: Nice place VERY helpful staff, great location” If you recall Holiday Inns as a kinda ok place for families, you will be surprised. If you have had lots of experience with ok, but not especially friendly front desk staff, you will be surprised. This is a well managed, attractive hotel that has a great location for several parts of DC, whether business or travel. As others have noted, it is quite close to the metro - but ask which entrance to come out of the METRO - depending on which exit you choose you, could be a 5 minute walk, or a 10-12 minute walk. I think 7th and D or 7th & Maryland is the closest, but check. (I forgot) Unfortunately I forgot tooth brush, tooth paste, razor and shaving cream. Front desk staff immediately provided me with free replacement. Problem with tv? They dealt with hit. This place is across the street from US Dept of Education (where I had meetings) and 2 blocks from Smithsonian Air & Space Museum.

“We liked the Omni, a few opening jitters but great in general” Being from Dallas, I don't stay in area hotels all that often, but with all the hub bub surrounding the new Omni and their opening rate specials, we figured we would try it out for a night. The hotel is nice, new and shiney, I liked the feel of the main lobby area. We also took the escalators up to walk around the open common areas by some of the hotel conference rooms. It was also very nice. It would be a great place to have a conference. The rooms were new and nice as well. pretty high tech when it came to a tv in the bathroom mirror and the room welcoming you when you first arrive. We got a room with a view of the city, and knowing Dallas, I would recommend that over a view facing the other direction if you have a choice. The hotel is next to the convention center and set off a few blocks from the bulk of downtown which actually allows for some pretty cool views of the Dallas skyline and none of the rooms should really have blocked views, although higher is still better. There were three main restaurants that we saw in the hotel. One is Texas Spice which is supposedly local ingredients that come from within 200 miles. Not entirely sure what the menu genre is though. Also there is a sports bar called the Owner's Box which was really neat and had a great feel. Tons of giant TVs. We went in and had a drink before dinner. The drinks were very reasonably priced for a brand new hotel sports bar. The other restaurant is the Bob's steakhouse in the hotel which is where we had dinner. Bob's is one of the oldest and most famous steakhouses in Dallas and now they have a couple locations besides their original on Lemmon Avenue. It is a nice and expensive restaurant. The food was really good and truthfully better than I remember it being at other Bob's locations. The feel of the restaurant was nice. The oddity was the restrooms. To go to the restroom as a restaurant patron, you have to leave the restaurant and walk half way across the main lobby to the common hotel lobby restrooms. For a ground up new construction, someone should be fired for making this happen. In some places that are historic or older, it is kind of quirky and fun that the restrooms are tucked away in an odd places becuase of a strange remodel, but for a very nice resturant in a brand new hotel to have to walk what seems like the distance of a football filed to go to the restroom is ridiculous. The location of the hotel is on the least developed side of downtown Dallas, which the powers that be hope will help spur development in that direction. It is walkable to the main parts of downtown (Main Street, the West End, Dealy Plaza,Victory, etc), but depending on where you are going, the weather, etc, it is also a very short cab ride and you won't be missing anything along the way. I would probably say walk if you are going to Dealy Plaza or the Nieman's on Main Street, but take a cab if you are going to the American Airlines Center or the Arts District. I think this hotel will serve the convention business very well. It would also be a good option if you want a nice hotel in or near downtown. If you are going very high end on a hotel, I would recommend, the Mansion, the Crescent or the Ritz, but it you are going one half star less, or are coming to Dallas for business, than the Omni would be a pretty good option.

“Upscale Courtyard” I agree with most of the reviewers on this site. The location is great...walk to just about everything one would need. Across the street from Trader Joes... I want to mention the breakfast service...it was very good and not the usual buffett. Not sure how parents of young children would like not having a buffett. The person who was taking orders, Chris Pope, really made everyone feel welcome. For business or pleasure, this is a very good hotel.

“Glad I changed my reservation to here” I had a horrible experience at the Reniassance (about 2 blocks away) a few nights earlier so I changed my reservation to this location. The location is great and this is an excellent 3 to 3.5 star hotel. I don't need red carpet, I need good customer service, where the person behind the counter doesn't have a chip on their shoulder. Everyone from the bell to the manager made this experience nice. Great value hotel!

“Not a bad place” got this place via a package deal by UAL. Thought I got ripped off because Expedia had the same package for $30 less. Oh well. Arrived and given a option of three floors for a queen bed. Mircowave and mini fridge included. AC controls work, though the machine is little loud when running. I would not call this centrally located, but with a car, getting places is not a problem. Traffic can be tough during PM commute. Haven't tired the breakfast yet, but I'm using one of their computers in the business center and it's free. Fitness room looks small, but I have a gym membership to the local fitness place 10 min drive tops. So far, everything is ok. I'd stay here again.

“Top Shelf Hotel” The entire experience of this hotel is five star. Great staff, helpful concierge, wonderful rooms with great amenities. I brought my son on his first big trip to Chicago and everyone from the door man to the front desk treated him like royalty. This is a big deal to a seven year old. We stayed in a double room with a great view of Michigan Avenue. The rooms are very well decorated and very comfortable. Great bathroom with a huge tub and plenty of space in the vanity area. I will be back!

“very good hotel” I like this hotel, good location near subway station and 15-20 minutes walk to almost every tourist attractions. The room was clean, old furniture but still in good condition. Very big lobby with internet station, bar- restaurant. Friendly service. The bad is that you have to pay for internet and the parking is expensive, there's parking around the hotel who are a lot cheaper.

“Solid hotel.” Booked this through Hotwire, and got it for 85 dollars...which was a steal. I really don't have any complaints about the hotel....the room was ample, check-in was a breeze, and it's in a great location to just about everything you'd want to see. Parking was 12 dollars, but it's more at comparable hotels, so you really can't complain too much.

“We have had several outstanding stays at the Mandarin” We have stayed at the Mandarin several times during trips to D.C., and, even though the hotel is not located conveniently located near D.C. attractions, we generally use a cab to get around D.C. and it is not any more expensive to get to theaters and restaurants from the Mandarin than from many other hotels in D.C. In some ways, we like the quiet location of the Mandarin. It is one of the few hotels in D. C. where we have actually enjoyed walking around at night. The view down to the Capitol is stunning, whether by day or night, and you have good views of several other monuments.The rooms are immaculate, the restaurant serves delicious food, and the spa is first class, although expensive, like everything else at this hotel. Check the website regularly, rates can vary quite a bit, especially on weekends. We like the rooms on the river side for their views.

“Location, Location” This was my second stay in this hotel and I would highly recommend it for it's location and amenities. It is a 10-minute drive from the airport and close to many popular San Diego attractions. The SD Conference Center, Sea Port Village, the Gas Lamp district, PetCo field, parks, ferries, and access to public transportation are all within easy walking distance. My room was spacious and clean with a balcony overlooking the pool and great views of the bay. I recommend the north tower as the rooms have balconies and seem to be more updated than those in the south tower. The bed sagged slightly on one side but was comfortable on the other. LC's restaurant in the hotel has a great breakfast buffet and there are plenty of other restaurants nearby in the Gas Lamp District and Seaport Village. All of the staff I dealt with were friendly and professional and even though it's a bit expensve I would definitely stay here again.

“great for a short stay, in a great location, staff was great” Hotel 140 is a great purchase if you get it at the right price. Its in an awesome location on Clarendon St. The subway stops are a short walk from the hotel. The hotel staff was extremely helpful with all questions I had. Overall, the room was nice, but the bathrooms were small. The shower was extremly small and when you turn on the shower in sprayed into the bathroom, so beware of that. I would feel bad for a heavier person to try to shower in the showers, but for me it was fine. Parking wasn't as bad as other hotels in Boston $27 for the night. Make sure you get your parking stub validated by the hotel otherwise you'll pay over $50 for the night. The continental breakfast wasn't bad. You have the option of a bottle of juice, water, or soda as well as a muffin or croissant. Thats all I need in the morning. I was very satisfied for the price I paid, and I would go back.

“Comfortable Hotel with excellent service” Stayed six nights at the Intercontinental SF. Upon arrival were upgraded to a one bed suite on the 32nd floor as part of our Ambassador Priority club package. Great room with separate sitting room and one and a half bathrooms, very handy when one of you cannot adjust to time difference and the other is still asleep!! Great views of the city and - when the fog cleared on the third day- a glimpse of the golden gate bridge and the bay. Our suite was spotlessly clean, everything worked fine and it had the most comfortable bed and a wonderful bathroom complete with TV! There was ample storage space with two closets and heaps of drawers. The one cup coffee maker meant having to run it twice to make coffee for two but no big deal. The room decor was distinctly 'Intercontinental' which can verge on the conservative 'grey-beige' but the room layout and views make up for this. The decor in public areas is more exciting. At first we thought the hotel was a little out of the way but after a couple of days we felt that the location was pretty good - very close to the streetcars on Market and the cable cars on Powell. Close to Union Square and of course the Westfield shopping centre. For us, tourists on our first trip to San Francisco, the location turned out to be ideal. The two other advantages of the location are that the area is fairly flat around the hotel if you are not used to the steep hills and you have the great views from the hotel as there are no tall buildings close by. Easy walk from hotel to Museum of Modern Art, the excellent contemporary Jewish museum and Yerba Buena gardens. Streetcars on Market run you to Fishermans wharf/Castro for $1.50. Had breakfast twice at the hotel $25 for the buffet was pretty good with endless coffee and OJ and my partner enjoyed the spa with fairly reasonably priced treatments. All in all a very well run hotel, good location for tourists and great views, excellent service from reception, housekeeping, concierge and guest relations.

“Very nice and comfortable business hotel” The rooms were nicely appointed and spacious. The bathroom was a little tight, but had a separate shower stall and bathtub. The bed was comfortable. About what you can expect from a decent business hotel

“Great place, Great Staff” Great staff are not just found they are developed and this hotel has great staff. Rooms are good but beds are really hard. If I had one suggestion it would be to offer some rooms with foam beds or sleep number beds.

“Fortress Phoenix: The Weakest Link in the Ritz Carlton Empire?” We booked a mountain facing room for a week after finding a very reasonable deal with Expedia. We upgraded to the Club Lounge for the last 4 nights. Whilst we had a wonderful holiday and whilst Ritz Carlton still remains our all time favourite hotel group, Phoenix lacked the sparkle and devotion to customer service that is normally associated with this seriously upscale hotel group. Expedia thought it merited 4 and 1/2 stars, which initially greatly surprised us. However, on reflection Expedia's assessment was about right. Basically, the hotel had staffing problems and were twice unable to offer breakfast at the stated times or have the lounge vacuumed in time. The breakfast downstairs at Bistro 24 was little better. The menu was heavily itemised and not particularly good. You could easily spend $35 per person for a very average breakfast and not even be offered a second glass of orange juice. The Club Lounge staff operated a type of 'siege mentality' against its guests, locking doors and preventing access points at many times during the day. Many of us felt the service was hostile where guests were not encouraged to ask for service (indeed, 'tutted' at in one instance) or make requests for a glass of wine. Basic concierge services such as the posting of mail were met with replies like 'You need to walk down to 20th Street.' Most disappointing of all was the failure to book our New Year's Eve dinner tickets despite the concierge emailing confirmation of this event several weeks beforehand. I know people lose patience with reviews where the comments are little more than a long series of whinging. So to be fair, after making these observations to the Duty Manager, we were offered the most generous farewell lunch with wines of our choice at Bistro 24 that more than made up for our 'gripes.' Additionally, our Club Lounge upgrade rate was completely removed from the final bill. So we left feeling warm and still in love with Ritz Carlton despite the drawbacks. A new General Manager, Christoph Roshardt has just been appointed, so the hotel is absolutely ripe for management led initiatives. So what of Phoenix itself? Hotel Location: Excellent. Opposite Biltmore Mall and a whole host of upscale restaurants. Weather: We were cold and went to Macy's sale to stock up on padded shirts, hats and jackets (also necessary to wrap up for Grand Canyon) Best Restaurants: Ruth's Chris Steak House. Just around the corner from the hotel. Best Fillet Mignon in the world. Ritz Carlton could not hold a candle up to the steaks here and we issued Ritz Carlton that challenge too! The mashed potato and creamed spinach are similarly awesome. T Cooks: Excellent ambience and superb food. Very popular. Book early. We spent Christmas night here and loved the roaring fires and Mediterranean ambience. Best Gallery: Phoenix Art Museum: Some fabulous exhibits but star of the show was Yayoi Kusama's installation 'Fireflies.' Get lost and feel your way into this sensory experience of light, darkness and colour. Check out local artist George Thiewe's abstractions too. Taxis: Unbelievably expensive. $28 for single trip downtown $20 with Discount Cabs [--]Ask for Steve, ex stand up comedian! Downtown: There isn't one. Phoenix is dead. Dead as a hole in a Seguano cactus. Hyatt have a top storey spy hole to drink cocktails from but it's not open until 5.30pm. There are some vibrant statues by the theatre and there's a Hooters (See below) with cold beer and sexy waitresses. Best Lowlife: Hooters. What an outrageous bar. Sexy service of what must be the coldest beer in Arizona. Check out the annual calendar, possibly the most unhelpful organisational tool in the history of the personal planner. Reality Check: The Buses: The buses are $1.25 per trip (exact change needed) and very regular. However they are also serve as an excellent Ritz Carlton reality check. The bus drivers were the best. They were all immensely friendly and helpful. Huge respect is given to disabled people where the driver moves seats back and makes special provision for wheelchair bound passengers. Buses: Turn left out of hotel and sit in shelter opposite Starbucks. Take the Blue Line for the Heard Museum and Phoenix Art Museum. Best Tour Operator: Detours Jeff Haflett, the CEO of Detours braved the snows of Sedona and talked us through the Grand Canyon with immense knowledge and good humour, not to mention the best turkey sandwiches on the planet. Jeff was a real local expert, deeply passionate about his environment. See Photo 6. Best Jaw Drop: The Grand Canyon. We took our first helicopter ride with Maverick Tours for an awesome close up of this World Wonder. See Photo 5 Best Museum: Heard: Improve your knowledge of Native Americans. This museum is accommodated within a beautifully designed piece of architecture. The Heard Museum has many exquisite staues throughout the entire area. The guided tours are excellent.The main restaurant is popular and serves tasty food. Desert Botanical Gardens: We loved the Seguano cactus,the all round Arizona icon. There are many outstanding giant Seguanos here living and breathing in real life and not just in some Western movie. Fabulous celebration of the spikey 'teddy bears' too. Cholla, cholla, cholla: Do they jump, don't they? Highly imaginative variety of Desert trails highlighting the many varied properties of the cactus. 'By the time I get to Phoenix, she'll be risin' ' Hey, we lived the song and loved it. Recommend you do too!

“Decent airport hotel” The Doubletree Seattle Airport is a large hotel convenient to the airport. We stayed there for one night after arriving on a late flight, and had gotten a very affordable rate on Hotwire. The room was very large and clean, and the warm cookies on arrival were delicious. The bed was quite comfortable. We also had our own balcony overlooking a pond. This property is quite large (900+ rooms) and is very spread out. Our room was about a 10-minute walk from the front desk. While we didn't mind the walk after our long flight, travelers who want an easy trip to and from their room should request accommodations that are as accessible as possible. All in all a fine experience. I would stay here again.

“Great stay, wonderful hotel” Stayed a week at the Double Tree Suites Columbus Downtown in mid-August. With the exception of just one incident my experience at this property was one of my best hotel stays in a while. First, as other reviews say, the location can't be beat. The hotel is in the heart of downtown Columbus with a covered walkway linking it to the Huntington Bank building (the high-rise behind the hotel in the pictures). All major downtown attractions are within walking distance, including the Statehouse two blocks behind the hotel, the Supreme Court across the street and the Scioto River with its beautiful renovated riverwalk two blocks west (See the replica of the Christopher Columbus flagship Santa Maria on the river - open Wed.-Fri. 10 to 4 oin summer). This part of downtown is also home to various theaters and restaurants, and the Brewery District and don't miss German Village arer about a 20-30 minute walk or an easy cab ride (more great restaurants - try Schmidt's in German Village). The ama- zing COSI Science Center is a short walk across the river. Also, the Arena District is walking about 10 minutes north and the chic Short North District (with great shopping and restaurants) is another 15-20 minutes up. So, the location is great - Columbus is a very walkable city - and if you don't feel like walk- ing, the cab rides will be short. I frankly don't understand the negative reviews I've read - perhaps said guests just had bad luck and should give the DoubleTree another try if in the area again. I will say now that the building has an un- usual layout in that the lobby is on the 7th floor and the rooms start on the 10th floor (which guarantees magnificent river and city views from even the "lowest" floors.The downside to this arrangement is that you msut use two elevators, one to reach the lobby level (for check-in and restaurant) and another to reach your room. However, even though the hotel was super busy while I was there - a slew of wedding parties were going on - the elevators were rarely slow. And do expect this hotel to be busy on a regular basis due to the location, which is ideal for both tourists and businesspeople. My check-in was smooth as silk with the irresistible Double Tree cookie (yummy!) and I was up in my room in no time. Because of my budget, I stayed in a standard suite with a river view. No complaints here. The suite was huge, exceedingly comfortable and made me feel right at home. The living room is huge, with a kitchenette (with free coffee and tea replenished daily), a large sofa, easy chair with otto- man, coffee table, desk with phone and a 37" flatscreen TV, and two floor to ceiling windows with jaw- dropping views of the river (even more beautiful at night with the Broad Street Bridge lit up). The bedroom had a very comfy king bed, a large dresser, the usual nightstands, a large alcove with a dressing area including a hairdryer, towels and a mirror, and yes another 37" flatscreen TV on the dresser. A chair in the bedroom would have been good, but this is a personal preference and I didn't miss this. Another plus is that the bedroom and living areas are separated by French doors more more privacy if traveling with others. Also, the windows have thich blackout curtains to allow hopefully for a little more sleep in the morning. And speaking of the windows, the bedroom features the same terrific river view as the living room! The bathroom was spacoius and fully stocked with all the nesessary items (towels, toiletries, etc.). As mentioned earlier, the fact that the rooms start on the 10th floor means that as long as you are facing the river or have a corner room, spectacular views are a given. I am not sure if there are rooms in the back of the hotel facing the Huntington Bank, so be sure to ask when you reserve - these rooms, if any would not have any sort of a scenic view. The hotel restaurant was a good option for staying in, but I only used it frr dinner one night. Though the food is good, the menu is rather limited - there is also a bar which is open the same time as the restaurant. Speaking of hours, please note that as in many small and mid-size Midwesten cities, small businesses and restaurants (esp. coffeehouses and fast-food places) close at 5 P.M. Mon.-Fri, and at 3 P.M. or 4 P.M. on Saturday abd Sunday. Some smaller establishments are closed completely on these days. Breakfast in the hotel tends to be pricey - I would recommend having breakfast at Danny's Deli just a couple of doors down from the hotel - just make a right out the door and look for the red awn- ing. Prices are ridiculously reasonable for a very filling breakfast or lunch and the service is courteous and attentive - Taylor, my server most of the time was especially good. Please note though that this gem of a diner is only open Mon.-Fri. 7 A.M. to 3 P.M and closed all day Saturday and Sunday. The staff at the DoubleTreethe hotel was one of the best I have encountered at any time. Special thanks to Amanda amd Michelle for their invaluable sightseeing and restaurant tips and furnishing me with the necessary directions and public transportation schedules ( esp. to the Columbus Zoo, don't miss destination). Alia was freindly and efficient at check-in and check-out and for holding my luggage on my departure day till I was ready to leave (reluctantly), and lastly Sarah Keitt for helping me additionally with all of my above needs and especially for rectifying a housekeeping problem I had over the weekend when my room was not made (to be fair I had mistakenly put out the do not disturb sign outside the door). But when the chambermaid refused to do the room even thohg she was right outside, that's when Sarah came into the picture and fixed this problem. So, thank you again, Sarah and the entire slaff for your excellent freindly service and the knowledge and pride you have in their city. So if my plans bring me to Columbus in the future, you know where I will hope to stay - the DoubleTree Suites Columbus Downtown. Others may carp at the furnishings not being super fancy or museum quality, but if you want a comfortable, efficient hotel with all the amenities where you will feel at home and not out of place, the DoubleTree is the place to stay in Columbus.

“great spot!” i was in philadelphia for work and decided to head over to DC for a couple of days before going home. my husband flew out and met me...we had such a great time! everyone here was very friendly and helpful. its literally walking distance everywhere. if you feel you need a cab, its a $5 ride to most main areas, from the hotel. we walked to the capitol in 20 minutes, walked to the mall in 15, great little stops along the way. i recommend this place!

“Great location, right across the street from Galleria mall” Large spacious room, good staff and great location. I was very impressed with the size of the room and the quality of accomodations. Everything a business traveler needs is all there.

“A great windy city pick!” The Hyatt Chicago was a great stay. I was here for a conference and stayed four nights. The lobby, though often very busy and noisy, was cool spot to hang out with a 24 hour coffee bar. The location of the hotel is pretty good-- a little bit of a walk to restaurants etc, but nearby Millenuim park and a great walking/running trail near the water. Rooms were nice size, clean and updated. Even on the 24th floor, the views are often still of the inside of other buildings but something that can't be helped in a large city center. Rooms and corridors were surprisingly quiet. Check in was quick and easy. Service was great.

“great location” We checked in late on the night. We had booked a deluxe room, but on check in we were upgraded to a concierge level room on the 7th (top) floor. The room was lovely. The views of the water and aquarium were great and there were no noise issues. I was impressed with the continental breakfast the following morning. There was a wide selection of pastries, fruit, breads, cheeses and meats, and the concierge lounge has a wonderful view over Boston Harbour. In terms of location, this hotel is fantastic. We were staying so that we could visit the aquarium and do the whale watching tour, so the location could not be beat. It is only a short walk to many restaurants and other attractions as well. The only slight disappointment was the fact that I had requested a room on the other side of the hotel with views of the park and harbour, but was given a room on the opposite side - but I guess that is down to time of arrival and availability.

“Trendy hotel” Great location, beautiful interiors. I stayed there twice once as a tourist in NY and once in June 07 when i was in NY for business and i didn't think there were set up for business traveler. I called at 6 a.m and asked for an iron and i left my room at 7 and the iron was not there yet. Internet conncetion was very bad and no one there to help. I couldn't check my email for 2 days i was there. As a tourist the first time i loved it, everything was great.

“pleasantly surprised” to be honest I wasn't expecting much for $175 in Manhattan bt i picked it based on the proximity (across the street) from Penn Station. However the room was large, with a nice sofa and a desk, in attractive, contemporary design (they must be upgrading the rooms- some reviews talk about run-down rooms but mine was fresh and beautiful). Nice touches were the iPod docking station and the windows that open for some fresh air (and NYC noise). The gym was adequate. I wouldn't hesitate to stay again, even if I don;t have to be at Penn.

“The Plaza is perfect. Just perfect.” This was our fourth stay at The Plaza. Our first was in 2009 when we married here and loved it that much we insist on spending the last week of our annual month-in-NYC here. Coincidentally, we had our wedding anniversary during this stay :) We usually stay in an Edwardian Suite, but booked a Rose Suite this time (kindly upgraded to a Deluxe Rose Suite on arrival). I was nervous about the room change as the Edwardian Suite is something to behold, but the D. Rose Suite was perfect for us. In fact, this will be our room of choice from now on. More than enough room for a couple (and our four suitcases!) plenty of wardrobes for hanging space and the bathroom is divine. We are a contemporary-furnishings type couple, but adore everything about the more classic style of The Plaza. The bed is comfortable, the linen is perfect, housekeeping is absolutely faultless (and it's nice to be in a hotel who makes your room before midday!). Since our last stay, the hotel has introduced iPad technology in each room - you can control the lights and heat/cooling, as well as access internet, book a time for housekeeping and turndown service, order room service. Very clever, very savvy. Excellent technological move, The Plaza! It's also the little things they still do - having a refreshment stand in the lobby in the mornings with bottles of water for you after a morning Central Park run (as well as a Runners Map if you're not familiar with the Park) and apples and bananas. I also get my hair cut at Warren Tricomi every year we stay here - my original stylist, Kyung - who did my wedding hair and make-up, is still there and that lady has SKILLS. My only gripe is the gym (or lack thereof). La Palestra was supposed to be available for guests last fall I believe and while La Palestra is now in the building, guests still cannot access it for another few months. It wasn't explained why... The Plaza doesn't try to be high-class and luxury - it just is. It always has been, it's in everything they do, it's location, it's history, it's staff, the furnishings. It is the very, very best of its kind. The Mandarin Oriental, Waldorf Astoria or The Surrey don't even come close. My favourite hotel in my favourite city.

“Great inexpensive, central location in El Paso.” We stayed here while attending a wedding in El Paso. It was great because the hotel is right in I-10 making it impossible to not find your way back. It's clearly visible from any direction. The hotel itself is nicely updated and the rooms are very effecient, yet comfortable and stylish. I was able to get a good sleep in the bed ad the room temp was very consistent which, if you travel frequently, you know is rarely the case. The lobby is nice and very easy to relax in. The pool and hot tub are small but they serve their purpose and the outdoor patio is a great place to enjoy the warm El Paso nights. Food, gas, airport, and shopping are all very close. The food selection is limited and expensive and there's no continental breakfast to be had. We have family throughout the area so we still didn't spend much on eats, but if you don't be prepared to shell out $$ for every meal. You can request a room with a fridge, but none have microwaves. For the price you can't beat it. Probably the least expensive but the mos modern hotel in the area.

“Great Place with the Right Room!” Me and My husband stayed here for a relaxing vacation fairly close to home. When I booked a room here I requested a room with a view. When we arrived the line at the front desk was extremely long! We waited patiently, got our room key and were off to our room. After finding our room (lower down the hill fairly close to the large pool and also had a smaller pool right outside our door) we were Extremely disappointed! The elevator to the second floor was disgusting, the room had very little light coming in and the only view we had was of the parking lot on one side and the smaller overcrowded pool on the other side! Also the amount of noise coming from the pool was insane, there wasn't going to be much relaxing going on here. This room had the feel of a cheap apartment not a resort, so, I went back to the front desk and asked for another room! There was no room available but I was told that if we waited about 1-2 hrs there would be one available farther up the hill so we waited. In 1-2 hrs I received a call that a room was available and returned and picked up our room key. This room was as far up the hill as you could get, right below the different point of view restaurant. The parking for our room was at a steep angle and the feel was much better of this location. It seemed cleaner, newer and much more peaceful! No overcrowded swimming pools nearby and a great view! Our room was full of light, a peaceful hallway with interesting plants out front and a beautiful view from a large patio in the back. Our Suite had a flat screen tv, fridge, bar, desk, and comfy couch in the living room and a Comfy King bed & standard tv in the fairly large bedroom. The Bathroom was a bit weird, the vanity was located on one side of the hall, plenty of space on the granite countertop but a noisy air conditioner vent overhead... the shower/tub combo and toilet were on the other side in a pretty cramped space, when you open the door it nearly touches the toilet. It was really clean but could use some new fixtures in the shower/tub, they were really covered in hard water. The view from 'Different Point of View' is great, you can see downtown Phoenix from here. We didn't eat at the restaurant, just took a drive up to look around. We didn't do room service either so I can't comment on that. We ate out while staying here and it was quite a drive to find something. Make sure to plan ahead if you are going to eat out as options in this area are pretty slim. Overall we really liked our stay here and it was very relaxing, I would return to this resort as long as we got a room in the same location... the rooms lower down the hill are a big disappointment!

“Pleasant Stay in S.F.” Perfect location on the northeastern side of Union Square, very safe, convenient to everything, near all the best shopping and close to Chinatown Gate. Everyone who worked there was most pleasant, friendly, and helpful. Rooms were very nice. The fitness center is one of the best I've ever seen at a hotel. My only complaint is that the breakfast room is much too small, resulting in waiting times of up to an hour for a table. This really threw off our plans every morning. They need to serve breakfast in a much larger room. The breakfast buffet itself is excellent, and the staff there are very very kind and friendly. The elevators also required quite a wait sometimes, as this is a very large hotel for only 5 or 6 elevators. Overall, we really enjoyed staying here, but don't pay extra for the breakfast- you'll waste a lot of time in the morning waiting for a table; just eat at any of the coffee shops or diners surrounding the hotel.

“Good hotel and good location.” I stayed three nights at this hotel in early January. The room was typical of New York (on the small side), but was clean and well appointed. There was a good breakfast included every morning with plenty of choices to start your day, and internet was free also. There's a small exercise room on the bottom floor with a few pieces of cardio equipment and a selection of hand weights. My only complaint is that my room (5th floor, on the back side), looked directly into the windows of a yoga studio in the opposite building, so quite often during the day when I put up the window shade there would be a dozen or so sweaty yoga students looking back at me. But the room was clean, quiet, and very close to subway stations and a good selection of inexpensive restaurants, so I would stay here again.

“Very Nice Property” I recently stayed here for the better part of a week for business and it was a very clean, comfortable, and well run property. The restaurants, bar, common areas, and grounds were all extraordinarily clean, well maintained, and well decorated. The location is fantastic being only a block off of the famous Austin 6th Street. I only had two issues with the property and one of them is - admittedly - kinda minor. The most serious is with the bathroom in my room. For such a nice place, I find it absurdly bad to have a tub/shower without the "bowed out" curtain! Personally, I think all hotels should be equipped with only stand-up showers, but if you've got to have a tub/shower combination, it should at least have the curved shower curtain so that you aren't in a constant battle with it! My other gripe is somewhat minor, but worth mentioning. This property went up to Floor 26 with the guest rooms starting at Floor 9. I requested an upgrade to an "Upper Level" floor and was told upon check-in that my request would be honored. Well, I was on the 15th floor. I'm not great at math, but even I could do that math. At least I didn't pay extra for it...

“Excellent Hotel” Booked through Priceline, great rate, and the hotel was able to accomodate our bed choice. Good: -Facilities were very nice - the fitness centre and lobby area were clean and luxurious. -Staff were very friendly and respectful in all encounters -Concierge desk was helpful in providing directions and a map -Free lemonade and ice water in the lobby was great considering the extremely hot weather -Room size was nice, beds were comfortable, and everything was clean and nice -The building is a restored old skyscraper - it was very cool, and it was clear the Loews did a good job restoring the building -Great location in Center City Bad: -Free internet is only available in the lobby -Annoying charges for local phone calls Overall, an excellent hotel. This was my first stay at a Loews-branded hotel, but will definitely not be the last. I was impressed.

“IMPRESSIVE!” From the minute I checked it, I realized this not the usual Candlewood. The lobby is bright, clean and the front desk associate was extremely pleasant and friendly. The room (studio) was very spacious and very clean. The bathroom was better than a few full service hotels I've stayed in. The room is equipped with everything someone on an extended trip will need. Everything was good quality and well kept. The bed was comfy and it was very quiet despite being that close to I-10. This is a good choice for short or long trips to the area. There are several restaurants in the area and everyone is eager to help should you need advise on dining or directions. This one just a gold star for being squeaky clean and for having some of the friendliest staff I've encountered at any hotel.

“For a convention hotel, this one is good!” Arrival experience: Great! Walked from the train's Grand Station, arriving at the automobile court. Several bellhops immediately inquired if I needed assistance with my two bags (one on wheels, the other tethered to it). Lots of smiles and a warm welcome, with specific instructions on where to find the reception desk. Checkin experience: Neva was so cordial and friendly! She upgraded my room on the spot when I requested it. Room: Typical of large-city hotels, the room was rather small, but more than adequate for my needs. I had a king room on the 37th floor, with a west view. Floor-to-ceiling windows added to the breathtaking view! The bed was incredibly comfortable and loaded with extra pillows. The linens were in excellent condition and spotlessly clean. The desk was a bit worn, and the room safe took a while to locate... it's in what used to be the bottom drawer of the nightstand: the drawer has been turned into a door. :) Bathroom: Perfectly clean, but tiny. And I mean tiny. The door barely clears the front of the toilet seat. Single sink vanity with lots of counter space. The tub seemed a bit old, but it was spotless. Curved shower rod with updated shower curtain. Public areas: Clean clean clean! Elevators are "divided" into low-rise and high-rise. Conference center: Confusing! There is an extreme lack of signage and wayfinding - to the point that Marriott employees were actually always on-hand to guide people to the correct rooms/floors. Seems to be a waste of human resources, when appropriate and adequate signs could provide that service! Escalators in the conference area totally skip the 6th floor - and I never found the stairs so getting an elevator was sometimes a challenge, especially during busy times. Lobby bar: Great service, even when it was packed with conventioneers! I highly recommend the chips-n-fondue and the mini Chicago-style hotdogs. Be sure to try their site-made honey beer (there are 100,000 bees on the roof of the hotel). Harvest: Second-floor restaurant. Great food - superb service. Chef's salad was a bit of a disappointment, though - I was expecting something other than iceberg lettuce. The chicken & mushroom sandwich is very tasty. I had the house-made potato chips, but my traveling companions had the garlic cheese fries and said they were quite good as well. Checkout: I requested a late checkout of 1:00 (normal checkout is noon) and was immediately accommodated. When I realized 1:00 would really be pushing it, with my conference schedule, I called to see if I could back it off until 2:00 and was denied. I checked out with three minutes to spare, and stored my bags at the bellstand - as much as that goes against my grain. Departure: Bellhop hailed a cab the instant we walked out the door, telling the driver which airport we wanted, and double-checking that he took credit cards. All-in-all, I'd definitely stay here again. As always, the biggest downside of staying at a Marriott is the ridiculous daily charge for Internet service (here, it's $14.95 for noon-to-noon service).

“Thumbs up” A group of us booked three rooms/suites here. We had a studio, which by NY standards, seemed huge. We had a corner room in the back, which was a) quiet and b) had two big windows! and an actual view, i.e., sunlight, and not a brick wall. Our friends had a suite on a high floor with a great view of the Chrysler Building and other people's roof terraces. (As a former New York resident, I am still not immune to real estate envy.) The galley kitchens are a great amenity, even though we did not use ours on this trip. (Our friends, who were traveling with kids and stayed longer, made good use of theirs.) Rooms were attractive and clean, and the front desk staff seemed very pleasant. The location is convenient. Altogether, a good choice.
