“nice all around” We are Residence Inn fans, and this may have been a step above the typical. Quick shuttle to the airport. Very nice pool and hot tub. Cute open "mini rooms" adjacent to the dining area if you want some privacy for a small group of 4-6. Helpful front desk. A great idea that should be copied is their dining guide. They list the close restaurants in many categories, their distances, and then list the best in three different price ranges. What a great idea! We can vouch for the Chinese restaurant directly across the street.

“Good experience” I had a meeting in this hotel and therefore stayed here a week in September 2008. The hotel was above expectations. Very comfortable spacious room. Nice fitness area and swimming pool. Excellent breakfast buffet for a reasonable price. Free coffee in the morning and ice drinks in the afternoon in the lobby. Wireless internet for a reasonable price. The only big disadvantage is that you are trapped in the hotel if you don't have a car. The hotel is in an isolated place just between Dallas and Fort Worth and there is really nothing in the surroundings. With a taxi it costs at least $ 40 one way to go to the city and at rush hour it takes a long time.

“A Classic at its Best” The Omni Shoreham is a truly classic 4-star hotel that is well run and maintained in the elegance it deserves. Built in the 1930's, this grand hotel has since been renovated to modern standards while preserving its historic charm. Located on a quiet side street just off Connecticut Avenue in Northwest Washington, the hotel has a large and maintained garden next to the Rock Creek Park and guests truly feel like they are in the country because of the views of trees and the non-existent traffic noise. Restaurants, pubs, and small shops are nearby (avoid the evil vixen at Petit Plats though!) so there are plenty of dining options within walking distance. The hotel's rooms and bathrooms are large, roomy, and well maintained and the service is exceptional. We called for additional towels and they were delivered within seconds, and seconds after that a follow-up call was made to assure we were satisfied. We called for a corkscrew (for grape juice of course) and it was cheerfully delivered to the room immediately and presented to us on a decorated plate. The south-facing view of the room was beautiful, with nearby trees, some more distant buildings, and the Washington Monument in the background. The Easter-weekend flowers were in full bloom in the garden and it was a challenge to not just stay on the hotel's grounds for the entire weekend. Valet parking was cheerfully available and the return time for the car was less than five minutes - try that in Manhattan! The only negatives were the constant door slamming and the lack of a refrigerator in the room. Until the world teaches courtesy to the barnyard rubes who relentlessly slam their doors maybe the maintenance team can install felt bumpers on the doors to deaden the noise. The key-lock mini bar/cooler was a bit tacky and they really should have a small fridge in the room. These small annoyances pale in comparison to the overall experience of staying at the Omni Shoreham and nobody should ever decline an opportunity to visit this grand and charming palace.

“Perfect Hotel!” I stayed at the Hampton Inn & Suites during a business trip in January and I was very impressed with the staff and the rooms at this relatively new hotel. The hotel is right off the freeway (I-25) and very easy to find. The rooms were very spacious and included free internet. The free breakfast was also very good, and I would definitely stay here again.

“Great Place.” My aunt & uncle and I were taking a road trip to Arizona and stayed at this hotel. It looked like a small, standard Doubletree. However, when we got in we were really amazed. The staff is really great - warm & friendly. The hotel has a boutique design but with nice sized rooms. The bar was busy so we sat & watched a ball game. Try the burger...yummy! We also really liked that it was close enough to downtown to (long) walk but far enough away that it wasn't noisy. When we came back to the hotel to relax, we could actually relax. Overall this is a really great place at a good price. I'd definately stay again.

“Wonderful Stay!” Wonderful, warm service and a unique hotel. The views were incredible! Located in the heart of everything. We had a wonderful romantic weekend, - everything we did - great restaurants, shopping and a concert at the Kimmel Center were within walking distance or a short cab ride. The only downside was that the room service took longer than expected once, and the meal was comped because of the delay anyway.

“Great little hotel, will return” My friends and I had a mini-college reunion in Aug in NYC. We were alerted to good deals at 70 Park Avenue via the Jet Setter website and were so pleased that we selected this hotel. It is an excellent location at 38th St. Good for walking and subway. I had a king room with an interesting dark brown/purple decor on the 15th floor, it was great. Comfortable bed, min street noise. We liked the 5 pm wine reception and the all-day lemon and orange water. We had help with advice, maps and directions from their staff which was appreciated.

“Nice location” Just returned from a 3 night stay. Hotel was nice but the rooms were very small. Only 2 double beds for 4 people which I find surprising in nicer hotels today and we could not get a rollaway for my teenager due to fire code (even though they list this as an option on their website). But the beds were comfortable which was a nice surprise. Furnishings were a little dated but clean and in good condition. Pool was warm and excercise area was nice with good equipment. There is a Starbucks onsite and the onsited Hertz rental car was great for renting a car for a day or two to explore the area. Room service was prompt and cost reasonable. Desk clerks were a little snooty and not terribly friendly or helpful. Location was easy to find and there is a small mall across the street with several very nice restaurants, a movie theater, and a Macy's. Easy to walk to with the family for dinner and shopping. A Denny's is down the street for a good breakfast if you don't want to pay a fortune at the hotel. Overall I would stay here again.

“Best Hampton Inn I have stayed at” Better than many expensive hotels. Standard Hampton Inn room but service is well above. Great location in the middle of town. Just one block from Congress and lots of dining options around.

“Ethan's on the road again” Well, This motel 6 was nice, but not as nice as the ones we stayed in on Broadway and Scottsdale Road. they are so dog friendly with nice lawn areas and close by places to eat and drink. The room was bigger, but the bathroom could have used a little plaster and fix up. The AC was super cold and as usual, the people that checked me in were very friendly. We were surrounded by other hotels. It was tough to find a bar and grill within a few miles. Fast food readily available around us. All in all, it's a good place to sleep, but just did not have the stuff my owner and I look for when we try to get away for a night. But then, can we really complain. I stay free!! It is close to an amusement park if you have kids

“Great staff, hotel bathrooms could use a renovation” Hotel staff at this hotel is great, gym is adequate and breakfast buffet was delicious. The view of Boston is awesome from your room. The bed was comfy. My only 2 complaints: 1) Bathroom needs a renovation. Not a big fan of old tile and shower curtains. 2) Sheets looked old. I don't like when sheets start looking a little yellow.

“Small, highly-personalized luxury hotel” The Huntington is member of the "Small Luxury Hotels" - and it deserves it well. No name-tag bearing business guests, but style, classic charme and a highly-personalized service. And a breathtaking pool and spa area! One of the best 5-star hotel bets in San Francisco. Location: On top of Nob Hill, across Huntington Park. Short walking distance (or cable car) to Union Square and restaurants. Neighborhood and location can't be better. Building/public areas: Classic grandeur, with antiques and oil paintings in the lobby. San Francisco's best bar (very popular with locals). Rooms: We had a freshly renovated, mint-colored room which was spacious, with a two-room marble bathroom and all modern amenities. Pool and Spa: Just beautiful. The indoor pool could be a little larger, but it is just a wonderful area with great views, an outside terrace, a gas fireplace, complimentary beverages and fruit throughout the day, sauna, steam room.. everything you want. Service: We loved the Huntington's service. Everybody was most welcoming. We always had chats with the bell boys and they gave us good tips. Extra-wishes were easily satisfied. Dining: We had no chance to dine at the Big 4 restaurant, but breakfast was always excellent. And the bar. The bar! The bar!! Outstanding. Value: We got the room at an unbelievably good rate. Valet parking is convenient but expensive. If you want to save $7 per night, you can park your car by yourself in one of the two adjacent public garages. WiFi cost $9.95 per 24 hours.

“Wow, Awesome Rooms!” Just what you would expect from a trendy Beverly Hills Hotel. The rooms were full of high tech trendy devices like the HD TV's and the LED lights throughout the room. The shower in my room was out of this world. The location is also what sells this place, you are right across from the mall and it has plenty of food and shopping within a few minutes walk. Highly recommend.

“Beautiful hotel, issues with service” My wife and I stayed at the Waldorf-Astoria for two nights in late January 2009. We made our reservation through American Express for a room listed as “1 King Bed Concierge Level”. The Waldorf had always been a hotel I wished to stay in so I was excited about the visit. The hotel is truly magnificent. Staying there really takes one back to a time when a visit to a hotel was an EVENT, not something we do simply as a necessity. I was taken thinking of how my parents or grandparents would have felt as a guest there, and how much the hotel has changed in the past century, but how little (overall) the Waldorf had managed to retain the grand charm of days long past. If for no other reason than connecting with history, staying in the Waldorf is an experience one must do at some point in their life. The room we were given was in the Waldorf Towers and we were very pleased with the room overall. The size was exceptionally large for a New York hotel room. In addition to the main bedroom, there was an entry foyer, a kitchenette area, a dressing area, and a very large bathroom. The fixtures were a nice blend of old and modern, from the trio of closets to the multi-jetted shower. The condition of the room was excellent and all the linens and amenities were of superior levels. The view was a decent view down Park Avenue but nothing postcard worthy. The Concierge Level lounge provided a very nice continental breakfast each morning in a private room. The quality of the food and the selection were excellent, even if you had only a moment to grab a coffee to go. The staff in this area did a nice job of helping with most all requests. The area is small though, so don’t be shocked if you have to wait a few moments for a table. The main amenities of the hotel are all superior. The fitness facility is very modern and well thought out, even providing guests with fitness gear in case you have left yours at home. The concierge is most helpful, providing good information and reviews on local restaurants. The shops and business center are well done and very convenient. And the location of the hotel is hard to beat. My main complaint with the hotel is one of attitude towards guests who are younger than, say, 50 or 60 years. Although they were always polite, the staff seemed to be uncomfortable dealing with my wife and I (both in our 30’s but looking much more like two people in their 20’s). From the front desk to the bell attendants, there seemed to be this underlying sentiment of “are you sure you are old enough to be staying here?” whenever we dealt with staff members. Given that we are polite, courteous and professional people, it caught us very off guard. Overall, this is a fine hotel and well worth a visit. I would recommend it to anyone, especially those over the age of 40.

“Not quite as nice as Grand Hyatt, but plenty nice” Stayed in October 2011. For an extra $20/night we got an over-sized queen, which had a lot of extra space, but nothing useful in it (i.e., a huge entryway, but no furniture or a closet or anything else to do with it; a standard sized bathroom; a lot of empty space by the corner). Everything is nice and new. This is just two doors over from the Grand Hyatt (the Paramount Hotel is in between), two blocks from the Seattle Convention Center. Very nice 24h fitness center. A sort of mini-Starbucks for morning coffee & snacks. My only complaints: first, the LEED certification evidently left the hotel wanting to only include low-wattage lighting, and only desk or floor fixtures (no overhead lighting in the rooms). Overall, there was just not enough light in the room. Brighter (CFL) bulbs would help, so would some overhead lighting. My other complaint, which applies overall to Hyatt: please, get some better toiletries. In the world of business travel and TSA grope-fests, I try to travel without bringing my own shampoo etc. The Hyatt Portico brand is consistent with 2.5 star hotels, and they should do better. Enough whining for one review. This really is a very nice hotel, with some nice touches for their LEED certification. It's not as fancy as the Grand Hyatt, but a tad cheaper to make up for it.

“Nice Fairfield” As a Platinum member for Marriott I get the chance to stay in my fair share of Fairfields and this is one of nicest ones. Appears to be very new and the room I was given was very nice and spacious. Definitely would stay here again. Opt for this property and not the older full service Marriott across the parking lot.

“One of my fav hotels in NYC!” I stayed there for 3 nights over the summer during a business trip. The hotel was top notched on many levels! You cannot beat this location in NYC! It is right in the meatpacking district which is close to many great restaurants and shops. The staff were friendly and helpful. The rooftop was beautiful. My room was spacious by New York standards. I will stay there again for sure!

“Best by the Inner Harbor to be sure” Third time staying here on business and I always find this well kept, with well trained staff and really comfortable rooms. I love the quirky old railroad charm and grace of the building. Can't wait to bring my wife one of these days.

“Odd Amalgam, But Very Good Overall” What's in a name? This is a Four Seasons Hotel that uses the Ritz Carlton name as a doing-business-as type arrangement. That's not a problem, unless you have a goal of collecting or using Ritz Carlton frequent traveler points on a stay here--they don't apply. The hotel, adjacent to the old Water Tower is well run with the usual amenities one expects at a Four Seasons or Ritz. The configuration is a bit odd, however. On arrival one must take an elevator to the 12th floor lobby to check in, and then a separate bank of elevators to rooms on floors 13-31. Check-in and out were flawless and the staff does try to call you by name. The lobby and meeting rooms are well appointed, and catering for business meetings was well done. Our group of 25 held 3 days of executive business meetings here. The higher floors (above 31) of the building are private residences with separate elevators/entrances. The location is convenient to many sights and shopping opportunities. My room (2721) was well furnished, clean, and well-maintained, but a bit small for this level of quality and the shower was a bit cramped next to the toilet in a small room off the double-lavatory area of the bathroom. This would not seem a big deal in many lesser quality hotels, but seemed a bit off for a Four Seasons or Ritz. Catering for our meetings was generally quite good with some odd exceptions. For example, a request for iced tea at a meal took 10 minutes and resulted in a beverage clearly made from a powdered mix. Not what one would expect at a hotel of this genre. The service was generally first rate, although one day (out of 4) my room had not been made up by 2pm. When I called housekeeping that was quickly remedied. I would have rated the visit excellent apart from the room size/configuration, nasty tasting iced tea, and missed housekeeping day.

“Great location, nice rooms, good value” Our experience here began badly and got better. It's never a good start when you're waiting at an empty reception and eventually someone comes forward to deal with you unable to stifle a yawn. I had requested adjoining rooms to be near the two children I was with: straightaway I was told there were none. OK, how about rooms at least on the same floor? An endless search in the computer ensued and finally two rooms were found, but one hadn't been cleaned. It was already 2.15pm; I was told to come back at 3. In fact it was 4.15pm before I got access to my room. Our first afternoon in Philadelphia was pretty much a write-off. So that was the bad part: once in the room it turned out to be recently refurbished, well appointed, and with a great view: definitely above the standard you'd expect of a Holiday Inn Express. There was free wifi internet and a paper at the door in the morning. Finding that breakfast included was a bonus, and it wasn't at all bad: there were cereals, omelettes, bagels, fruit, muffins, juice, tea and coffee; and unlike many roadside inns, there were enough tables to cope at peak times. The location is unbeatable: walk two blocks and you're on Broad Street; six or seven blocks the other way and you're at Independence Hall and the Liberty Bell. There are loads of restaurants and bars in the area. Parking is expensive though: they charged $21 a night, even though my confirmation said $18: the line at reception was so long when I left that I couldn't be bothered disputing it. Shame about the small annoyances, but overall the combination of location, high room standard and breakfast make this a good choice for seeing the best of Philadelphia.

“Met Expectations” I stayed at the Inn @ Penn for almost a week and had a pretty good stay. The service was excellent and the hotel looked great. The rooms were decent, other than getting two twin beds when I have one King saved on my reservation. Remember - this is a full service Hilton, so there are extra charges for breakfast/internet. Overall, it was good and I'll stay there again.

“Delighted with my stay” I was booked through Priceline and stayed at this three month old hotel. Excellent in almost all respects. The hotel room, while not what I would call lavish, was one of the best I have stayed in anywhere and was in pristine condition. I give out 5 stars for rooms sparingly, but this room rated. The staff was fine. My only criticism was that at breakfast on the third morning, the French toast and sausage were almost cold, and told the front desk about that. Fortunately, I had not driven to San Diego, so did not have that high parking fee. Even the dining room manager at the Solamar Hotel across the street ( where I stayed a year ago and is a hotel of which I think well of ) spoke glowingly of the new Residence Inn.

“lovely location” We booked 3 nights here as we liked the look of the location and the hotel,when we arrived the reception staff were very nice and said they had upgraded our room,the room was gorgeous with lovely decor,it was very large with 2 huge beds that were very comfortable,the room was very clean,the wardrobe was a very small cupboard but had iron and board and the room also had a hairdryer and a coffee making machine.we had a little patio area with chairs, but now the down side ,the disappointment was we vizualized sitting out on the patio looking over the harbour or the marina with a nice drink instead we had 7 foot bushes and through them was a car park.To say we was disappointed was an understatement so I strongly advise to book a room on a higher floor if a view is important to you.On the plus side the car parking was free.

“Reliably great hotel” I had a standard room. Lighting is excellent, bed very comfortable, everything clean and working properly. The front desk staff is great. The workout room was in good shape with a nice range of dumbbells, exercise balls, and the usual cardio equipment. Room service was prompt and food was great. I try to stay here every time I'm in DC.

“Classy hotel.” We stayed here for 3 nights on a 3 city trip to USA. This was the best hotel. The bed was very comfortable with quality bedding & pillows. The bathroom had nice toiletires & a curved shower curtain rail. The 2 bottles of water every day is a really thoughtful touch. The receptionist was friendly & helpful so were the men on the door. The concierge was helpful, friendly & easily approachable (which i cannot say about the hotel in New York we stayed in) when we asked him to telephone to check our airport transfer times he did it immediatlley with a smile. The lobby, bar & lounge were beautifully restored. The hotel has a designer interior with sculputures but is comfortable and inviting .We loved their large Christmas trees and decorations. Everyone was helpful & polite, especially a senior looking suited lady who took our photo by the fire. Our only grumble was the restaurant prices seemed high so we did not eat at the hotel. Maybe a speacial deal for hotel residents would have encouraged us to eat. (the menu had really tempting dishes on it). We would recommend this hotel and stay there again. It is convenient for all tourist sites. Boston is a clean city with interesting achitecture & lots of history. The duck tour was funny and gave a great insite to Boston. It must take a long while to put up all the christmas lights.

“Great location!!” Stayed here while in town to see a Patriot's game. This hotel is the absolute best location in Boston, adjacent to the train station (perfect if you are arriving by Amtrak, which we did). The hotel is also adjacent to the train station where you head out to Gillette Field. The hotel is large and connected to a mall, which is convenient and also gives you a good amount of restaurant options without having to actually go outside. The guestrooms are fine, nothing special but clean and decent size. The hotel lobby bar itself was great, a sports atmosphere with tons of large screen televisions. I would definitely stay here again, especially if going to a sporting event.

“great location, good price for NYC....breakfast” Good price through Priceline for NYC. Rooms are a bit small, to be expected in NYC. Hotel seems clean, staff helpful. I've stayed a couple of times with no complaints. The breakfast is very good. Pleanty of space. Free wireless internet.

“PERFECT LOCATION FOR STAY NEAR BOYSTOWN OR WRIGLEY FIELD” Charming European style boutique hotel within walking distance of Boystown or Wrigley Field. The hotel was clean, quiet, sophisticated and understated. The hotel is a historical landmark located on a quiet tree lined street, two blocks from Lake Michigan. We had a 3rd floor Executive King which was spacious, clean and quiet. Parking was a good bargain at $18 a day with in and out privileges. Coffe available 24 hours in the wonderful lobby. Free WiFi.

“Always superb” This property is relatively new, and always in tip-top shape. Situated just off of I-95, the hotel is tucked away on a quiet street that is very close to White Marsh Mall. There are plenty of nearby food choices, including both chain and local eateries that provide reasonable variety and a comfortable range of prices. For those interested in using your room's full kitchen, Giant Supermarket is only 2-3 minutes from the large hotel parking lot. I travel extensively on business, and have spent the last year working in the Towson area. This is my favorite hotel: the rooms are top notch with far more room than a normal hotel room, the quality is excellent and you experience a clear sense of privacy and comfort.

“Why Stay Anywhere Else?” I stayed here one night while in town with my sons (11 and 8) between business trips for an Astros game and other Houston area fun. This hotel is less than a year old and is great! I am almost overwhelmed to describe everything, so here goes: Suite - As my son put it, this really has a super-modern theme to it. Everything was clean and in good working order. The bed was comfy; the foldout sleeper sofa was ok. The bathroom door was interseting - it was a sliding door that didn't latch and could be pushed out slightly at the bottom - sort of hinged at the top where it slides along the wall. The bath towels were plush and thirsty. Flat screen tvs in the bedroom and living area were just the right size and there was a great selection of channels. The microwave was just the right size for some left-overs or a bag of popcorn and the fridge kept water bottles cool. Breakfast - The dining area is very large and although there was a considerable line later in the morning, it moved well and there was always a table to be found. The bacon was very good - thick, not that thin microwaveable stuff. Bear with me here, while riding the shuttle back to the hotel, we were stoppped at a red light and a car pulls up next to us and the driver signals to roll down the window. I obliged and the driver asked, "did you have breakfast there this morning? (The Cadillac Escalade shuttle has the Embassy logo on it). I replied that it was our first day there and had not been able to yet. He introduced himself as Gregory, the omelette chef, and said to be sure and see him in the morning. Wow, talk about someone who loves what they do and loves to make people happy! Gregory is a hoot! He knows how to cook and go ahead and try his secret seasoning if he offers it. Needless to say, breakfast was way better than average. The coffee was delicious and the juices were not watered down like at some places. Swimming pool - How cool is it to have a tropical oasis in the middle of downtown Houston? The outdoor pool, surrounded by palm trees, is located on the 3rd floor and is bigger than the average downtown hotel pool anywhere I've been. The water coming into it was actually heated, so it was the perfect temperature. The hot tub seemed nice and hot to the touch, though I never got in. There are some sitting and lounging areas around the pool in full sun, complete shade and under an arbor for partial shade. Parking - relatively steep when you consider it's $28 and valet is the only option. Service - Everyone was friendly and had that "how can I make your stay more enjoyable?" attitude. I was met with smiles and greetings from the moment I drove up to the unloading area, at the front desk, and by any employee I saw. Cesar, the weekend shuttle driver, is a wonderful person who genuinely enjoys making people feel at home. The free downtown area shuttle is great in case you don't want to make the relatively short walk to or from Minute Maid Park or other downtown locations. We did have one problem during the stay, nothing completely horrible or anything, but when I brought it to the manager's attention, he quickly remedied the situation and was glad to do so. He wants everyone to enjoy their stay and return. I know I will any time I am going to spend the night in downtown Houston and I recommend you do as well!

“Very comfortable stay” We booked our stay at the Renaissance Hotel Chicago O'Hare through the website www.parksleepfly.com because we were going to Austin and coming back in the evening. I thought that we got a good rate of $107 plus tax for 4 nights parking (which could have been 14 nights for the same rate)and a lovely room. The room was quiet (which I requested), the beds and pillows very comfortable, the room was extremely nicely appointed with a sitting area aside from the bedroom. The check in staff was friendly and competent. The shuttle was reliable, but our timing might have worked with the 20 minute departures and pickups. They had the nicest toiletries I have seen. I have stayed at some very expensive hotels and I would put these accomodations up there with some of the best. The worst thing was just finding the shuttle pick up point at O'Hare which is supposed to be easy to find by the red foot prints. What red footprints? And it was a good walk from our baggage pick up.

“The best place I have found to stay in New York so far” We have stayed at several places the last year or so for overnight trips to see shows and this is the nicest we have found so far. We made the trip with 5 teenagers for a birthday celebration and rented two suites. The rooms are large and comfortable by new york standards. the bathrooms were nice and everything was very clean. There are two elevators and they work well getting people up and down. The staff is friendly and helpful, they also provide free luggage storage. all in all a really nice hotel. the hotel is an easy walk to Times Square and the Theater district

“Excellent hotel with great food” I stayed at the Peninsula Chicago for two nights in October 2008 while on business. Had a room on the 15th Floor with views of the Water Works. Everything about this property was wonderful. The lobby and conference areas were beautiful and put together really well to host a large event with multiple meetings. The quality and selection of food made attending meetings a real treat, and room service, salads and burgers at least, were great. Now for the room: it was huge! The bathroom had its own couch! Excellent desk and business set-up with extremely comfortable bed. I don't even think I used every piece of furniture in the room it was so big! Can't beat the location either - you're literally steps away from Michigan Avenue shopping and world famous pizza.

“Best location for theater goers” This is the second time I've stayed at this property. I was impressed the first time because the location is right next to many theaters without being directly in the swarming hoards of tourists in Times Square. 8th avenue abuts the east side of Hells Kitchen, which is a much more interesting area when searching for restaurants and a more genuine New York neighborhood feel. The staff there is exceptional, and unlike most Hilton Garden Inns, there are bellmen and a concierge, if you need them. The room itself is an average size - which means large by New York standards. It has all of the Hilton Garden amenities including a small fridge, microwave and that wonderful Hilton Garden adjustable mattress. My room was on an upper floor on the rear side of the building. The only view was of the water towers of the buildings behind but it was quiet. There was complimentary Internet which had decent speed and the flat screen TV actually had some hi-def channels. There is an attached restaurant (Pigalle) which seemed to be popular with the pre-theater crowd. If your Hilton status or plan includes breakfast, they offer a breakfast buffet, which was pretty good. If you need/want to be in the Times Square area but (slightly) away from all the tourists, this HGI is definitely worth checking out.

“Its a Great Place to Stay” The hotel still has the new feel to it. The staff is always accommodating and welcoming. I usually wind up in Chicago twice a year and this is the only hotel I will stay. Without naming names, all others at this level do not match it. The health club and pool are excellent and the rooms are extremely spacious and comfortable. The staff took me on a tour of rooms to pick out the one I liked best. I highly recommend the King 1 Bedroom Suite. Everytime I go back they try and give me the same exact room I picked out as there are several 1 Bedroom suites with different layouts. The hotel was the silver lining of my flight being canceled during a snow storm.

“Great Views, Clean Room, Convenient Walk To L.A. Live” As a preface, I travel to a limited degree to review rock concerts, and have begun to include hotel and resort reviews as well, which I am republishing here is modified form. This review is for The Westin Bonaventure Hotel & Suites in Los Angeles, during my recent Los Angeles Trip (February 2012). Room Type/Class: Traditional Room Date: February 7-10, 2012 Overall Rating: 4/5 This trip was explicitly to attend two concert events - one at Club Nokia and the other one in Hollywood. I lived and worked in Los Angeles for many years while I was in graduate school, so I'm really familiar with it. Since Club Nokia is part of L.A. Live, I thought it made sense to find a hotel that is within walking distance of L.A. Live, which put me downtown. I considered the Marriott and the Ritz-Carlton that are part of L.A. Live, but they were much more expensive compared with The Westin Bonaventure's Hotwire price. I ended up deciphering a "hidden" discounted offering on one website to purchase on another, and found that The Westin Bonaventure was the hotel being offered within that class range for a highly discounted cost off the base rate, and booked it. So the hotel has valet parking, but it is an additional $35 per night. If you don't mind walking a block or two, I noticed that there appeared to be some other public parking alternatives that would be cheaper; I ended up using the valet, which is underground and you walk down a hallway adorned with movie poster one sheets of films shot at and around the hotel (see photos below), and up an escalator toward the main entry level where the front desk is located. Check-in was quick and otherwise unremarkable. I had originally booked two nights, but one of my events was canceled and rescheduled... I asked if I could add a night at the discounted price, and was told they couldn't sell rooms at that price, but the guy at the front desk looked in his computer to see their occupancy for the desired night, and more or less indicated that if I went on that reseller website again, I would likely be able to add the third night at the same reduced rate (when I went up to my room, I was able to do this and add it on). I was actually really excited to check out the elevators, as there is a scene with Arnold Schwarzenegger in True Lies where he goes up one of the elevators on horseback; the gentleman at the front desk was able to direct me to the exact elevator I was seeking. As for the room itself, I had the basic/base room, and was pleased that it was on one of the higher floors (better views). While on the small side, it was very clean and nicely appointed, as I've learned to expect from Westin properties. Maybe because it is an older property, the shower and bed are maybe not as "Heavenly" as some other Westin properties, but overall the room suited my needs perfectly (traveling alone) with king-sized bed and computer desk. Internet connectivity via WiFi was good but not spectacular. For me, the best bonus of the room was the view. Most of the outward facing wall is glass floor to ceiling, as the view was spectacular, particularly at night. There are some amenities in the hotel that I just didn't have the time to use - restaurant, bar, etc. As noted, I had come to L.A. for a concert at L.A. Live, and found that it was definitely a reasonable walking distance from the Westin Bonaventure - maybe too far for some people's taste, but I walked back and forth several times and I don't think it took more 15 minutes. Overall, I don't have any complaints at all, though it would be nice if valet parking was included, but I knew from my research ahead of time that was a cost to factor into the overall value proposition of the stay. When I attend a future event at L.A. Live, I would likely return to the Bonaventure, unless there is a special deal at one of the competing properties.

“Great hotel, tiny room!” I liked the hotel very much but the room was small. Room was large, though, compared to the bathroom. The staff was great, they warmed up to you, the longer you stay. Excellent location for business mixed with pleasure. Would stay here again with a larger room!

“Amazing, but I wish I had known . . .” All the reviews are correct. It's an amazing place to stay! (Though I didn't have a flat screen TV - for the money we paid, I think I should have a flat screen.) I liked that the windows open. Coming from a cold New England January, it was great to open the windows in the morning feel a cool 60 degree breeze flow in. It felt like summer to us. The access to Seaport Village and the boardwalk leaves you with no shortage of options. Less than two miles from the airport and conveniently on North Harbor Drive, you'll have access to anything and everything, including a quick shot to Coronado - our favorite thing to do while there. (You must visit the Sundeck at the Hotel Del Coronado where you can enjoy a nice pastry or ice cream on the outdoor sofas by the fire pits). I wish I had known that there was a newer wing to the hotel; that there was a beautiful pool area above the lobby that we never knew existed because we assumed the pool we saw from our window was the main pool area. The main pool area is exquisite! I wish I had know a coke from the hotel bar would be $4 and parking in the hotel would be $17/night. Overall, San Diego turned out to be a little more expensive than I expected. Being from Boston, it's hard for me to get sticker shocked, but at times, I was; e.g. $24 for a pizza at Village Pizzaria in Coronado and a $7 eclair from the Hotel Del Coronado. I regret not trying the buffet at Lael's, a restaurant located in the hotel. Overall, I would definitely recommend the Manchester Grand Hyatt if you want to be close to it all. FYI - we ate at a place in the Gaslamp district called Chianti. Knowing good Italian food, this place was ok, but maybe it was stellar by San Diego standards. I recommend Gaslamp Pizza for a late night snack!

“Heritage hotel close to White House” Well appointed rooms to suit this heritage hotel. Staff very attentive, great service, good restaurant, Starbucks attached. A short walk to the metro, only a few blocks from the White House and walking distance to other memorial attractions. Plenty of reasonably priced restaurants within walking distance. Would definitely recommend this hotel.

“Stayed while at a convention” Very nice Marriott property. Located close to all major tourist attractions and plenty of dining places of all price ranges nearby. I was there for a convention and the hotel connects to the convention center. Very handy if the outside temps are not suitable for sidewalk travel. Rooms clean and all staff very helpful. During conventions - front desk can get VERY busy but staff seems to be able to handle the flow well and extra staff seemed to be available to help.

“Wonderful stay, fantastic location, great staff” Stayed here for 3 nights (during the week) while in Philadelphia on business. Picked the hotel primarily based on location, price, and overall prior TripAdvisor reviews. Short Review: Stay was great, staff across the board were really professional, courteous, and competent. Restaurants (Standing O and Academy Cafe) were above average for hotel restaurants, fitness center was amply set, and location was near perfect. Cleanliness and noise were non-issues. Long Review: Everyone with whom I dealt (with hotel operator one time being the exception) was very friendly, courteous, competent, and professional. From check-in to bell stand, to restaurant staff, to concierge staff, to hotel manager and security (someone turned in my coat, and they got it from lost-and-found for me) - not overstating this - they were all way above average in terms of customer service. The room was decent; not huge, but certainly more than adequate size. Plenty of room to work at the desk, and it was NOT right next to the AC/Heater vent which so many of them are (don't like it when the air is blowing directly on you while you try to work). The hotel architecture is also kind of interesting in that all rooms have kind of a "corner view" with the angled windows. They jut out some so that you can see more than if it was just a set of flat windows. Also the room was very quiet - didn't notice noise issues of other reviewers, although a lot of that can depend on the people in other rooms. The rooms - and the rest of the hotel - had been updated recently. There was a sign/picture in the lobby that stated the renovation completed in June, 2009 (I believe). The hotel and rooms especially had kind of a contemporary clean look to them. They have pictures/drawings of this type on most of the hotel floors as well. All in all the hotel seemed quite clean, although yes, there were a few marks in the carpets here and there, but seldom do you find a hotel without that. I ate at both restaurants, the Academy Cafe (2nd floor) for breakfast each day, and the Standing O which is in the lobby. The Academy Cafe has fairly priced ($8 - $13) menu selections, or the continental/buffet breakfast you can choose. The wait staff did a great job of service and keeping things moving. It was nice to see, at the Standing O, that there were theater patrons who would have lunch or dinner there before/after a show. Must be pretty decent if it attracts people outside the hotel regularly. It's got kind of a sports bar setup in the front, then regular restaurant seating in the back. Same here, prices pretty good for hotel prices (esp. in downtown Philly). They also have a gift shop in the lobby that sells some snacks as well as the ubiquitous T-shirts and other souvenir type items. I used the fitness center every day as well; good setup with 4 treadmills, 2 ellipticals, 1 stationary bike, then free weights and a nautilus machine. On the same floor, all in very close proximity were the pool, hot tub, and sauna (across the hall). Having the 4 treadmills was nice since those are usually the first things to get used; I never had to wait for one, either in the morning or the afternoon. Got to try out the concierge lounge - they had light breakfast in the morning and light snacks in the evening; it took up a smaller area on two floors, the uppermost of which was also a "business center" with a workstation, printer, and free internet. The staff there were very competent and friendly, and it was open every day (maybe this is just during the week not on weekends, not sure about what another reviewer mentioned). The location was near-perfect if you are staying downtown. The surrounding area is great - it's right in the heart of the theater district, and within walking distance of many other attractions, the downtown businesses, and literally hundreds of places to eat. There are several great places within just a few block radius, and all different types of food. I didn't have a car, just took the shuttle to the hotel from the airport and walked everywhere I needed to go. Shuttle/cab note: The hotel recommends Lady Liberty shuttle vans to/from the airport. They are constantly at the airport - didn't have to wait but about 5 minutes, and then they stop at the Double tree every half hour on the :00 and :30. It's only $10 each way, and the cab is $28 each way (fixed price). Have cash for the shuttle van - they say they take credit cards, but the driver gets you to the hotel front door, hands you your bag(s) and no cc reader in sight. So, it's a lot less expensive, but you also have to wait (both ways) while the van picks up enough people to fill it up (holds 8 or 9) and then go the circuitous route to get/drop off everyone. Net - about $25 rt with shuttle and $64 rt with cab. So if you don't mind it taking an extra 30 - 40 minutes, you can save ~$40. Net it out - this was the kind of stay that was so rewarding that I hope to get to Philadelphia again just so I can stay here. Not trying to snow any readers, but this particular stay was that good. Didn't notice the problems of other reviewers, maybe it was just luck, but I don't think so - the fact that really every facet of the stay was far above average made me feel that this is the norm rather than the exception.

“Pleasant Stay” We stayed one night at the Ritz for an event we were attending in Dallas. The hotel is nice but a little ordinary. The room was nice; the bathroom was beautiful. The bathroom had a window next to the tub that had great views of the city. This Ritz property has a house car (a Bentley!) that can be used for short transfers on a first come first served basis. We used the car to our destination and the driver was very friendly and accommodating. We had breakfast at Fearing's and it was wonderful. About $75 for 2 people. Fearing's is a first class restaurant that we have dined at for dinner several times and it never disappoints. I don't feel like the tables are too close together as another reviewer discusses.

“Nice location and spacious room” It's been a while since I stayed at this hotel but I still remember the experience. The room I was assigned to was super big! It was almost like an 1BR apartment. The room was nicely decorated too. The staff were friendly and price was reasonable. I'd like to stay here again when I visit DC with my family.

“A Grand Hotel in a wonderful city!” I have stayed at this hotel on many occasions for business and once with family on vacation. If you are watching your budget, this may not be the hotel for your next trip. This is a hotel from a bygone era. Don't let the modern facade of the building fool you. As soon as you enter the hotel and make your way to the reception desk and see the vaulted ceilings and furnishings, you can feel yourself going back in time. The front desk staff is most attentive and often have people from all over the world working there. They are quick to help and guide you on any question or concern. The location is right in downtown San Diego. You can walk to most anything. Shopping, eating and site seeing can all start from this location. Restaurants abound at all prices, cuisine and ambiance. Shopping is nearby and again in different price ranges. When you step off the elevator and circle around to your room, you know you are in a very nice hotel. Each two rooms share a single "keyed" entrance to an anteroom. Then you enter your own room. Spacious is the word. The decor is beautiful. Everything in its right place. The bathroom is as big as you will see. Comfortable bed and heating/air-conditioning. I haven't used the hotel eating facility, because of the large number of choices nearby. I would recommend Maria's Mexican Restaurant at 1011 4th Avenue. It's a hole in the wall, but the people are very nice and the food is quite good. The workout room is well maintained with good equipment. The USS Midway is a "must see." There is a showroom with restored cars (for sell) in the wonderful gaslight District that is well worth visiting. I would not hesitate to stay here for business or pleasure.

“Good stay” I attended a conference at the Baltimore convention center and priceline assigned me to this hotel. The lobby is quite classic and magnificent in a way. I had no problem with elevators. Although I was traveling alone, the room was large even from the standards of traveling with family. I believe it was not a corner room. The room faces streets so it was somewhat noisy at night, but not anything significant. The sleep number beds were very nice. The staff were very kind. Location was quite convenient, just two or three blocks away from the convention center and very close to the harbor and all other downtown landmarks. Metro was right in front. The only little complaint is that wifi was somewhat weak in the room. It worked at desk and not well at beds. Considering the price I paid, I would definitely stay here again.

“gem of a place!” This is a Beautiful California Inn. Maybe 4 miles north of downtown, close to the 5 and 8 freeways. Newly renovated, well maintained. Friendly staff, great location. Good value. Close to old town restaurants and park. Very comfortable beds, really accommodating staff

“Great hotel. Very nice. Excellent Location” This hotel is remodeled. It is excellent. The doors are somewhat old, but the infrastructure--bathroom, beds, etc.---have been remodeled. The elevators can be slow during "rush" hours, but otherwise, they were very reasonable. The location is just across the street from the Art Instittue of Chicago. Overall, this is a very nice hotel, and I was very pleased with it.

“Shocked it's #207?! This hotel is incredible!” Stayed here for the 3rd time and still like it. Went downstairs to have brunch w a friend and there was a street fair right outside the door... For tourists it was well appreciated. This time around though I do have to say the bell man at the front was very unprofessional speaking loudly on his cell phone while I was trying to catch a cab on my own...when I came back he didn't open the door acted like he didn't even see me. Everyone should be treated equally a guest is a guest no matter what. Clearly I can do this myself but why is he standing there and Working for the hotel if he's not going to do anything? My only complaint though. I will be staying here again!

“Amazing nights sleep!” i had no idea the highway was that close when i got to my room! We upgraded to a suite which was nice to have the two rooms. We had the baby so she was put in a crib and it was the most comfortable of all the hotel cribs during our stay in Texas, she slept all night! (3 months old) the parking lot had security which was unnerving but also reassuring. We could tell the hotel had recently been remodeled because it was VERY nice inside! I would stay here again if we were to ever fly out of Hobby.

“Nice business hotel” I stayed at 3 different Marriotts in San Antonio and this is far better than the other two. The room and property is well maintained. The receptionist remembered my name and gave me an upgrade to a suite. The room was quite and had a very good sleep. The concierge lounge could add a little more variety beyond the bare basic. The gym was not large but much better than Marriott Riverwalk.

“Clean and comfortable stay” I stayed here for 4 nights at the beginning of July. I was there for work 2 days and then stayed for a long weekend. It was the weekend of the 100 degree heatwave. My room was really small but had everything I needed. The bathroom was almost as big as the sleeping area! The room had an ironing board, safe, air conditioner, mini fridge, double bed, desk and closet. There was no dresser or drawers to unpack clothes, so you either had to keep them in your bag or hang them in the closet. Since i was only there for 4 days, it wasn't an issue for me but if you're staying longer, you'd have to be ready to live out of your bag. I found the air conditioner to be very powerful and it allowed you to set the temp as cold as you wanted it. I didn't find it too loud and it didn't interfere with my sleep. My room was on the 9th floor so I didn't notice any street noise. The room was clean and the bed was very comfortable. The bathroom was cleaned each day and had enough room/shelves to stash all my makeup/hair stuff. They provided shampoo, conditioner and a hair dryer. The building is old and the hallways are full of twists and turns - I liked the character of the building. The hallways were always clean while i was there. It's true the lobby is under construction but it didn't inconvenience me in anyway. Overall, i really liked this hotel and i would stay there again if I could get a good price. The location was excellent - close and convenient to buses/subway lines I needed for work.

“Nice hotel, good location, but siren noise is a negative” I have stayed in several hotels in Foggy Bottom and this is one of the nicest, but also the loudest by far. Positives: Large, clean room with full kitchen and separate bedroom. Convenient to Foggy Bottom Metro and Georgetown and Bus Stop. Very close to Starbucks, Bruegger's Bagels, Trader Joe's and other small take-out places. All of the staff that we dealt were friendly and helpful. The internet was free and worked fairly well except the morning it didn't work at all. Negatives: Sirens were very loud and frequent. Both L St and Washington Circle have a lot of traffic. The bed wasn't very firm. The stocking of bathroom was a bit odd. We had 2 or 3 bottles of conditioner and never got a bottle of shampoo. The kitchen was stocked with coffee beans and a coffee grinder, but I don't like the hassle of grinding the beans and I often drink decaf and the only decaf was instant. I would have preferred packets of both regular and decaf. I would recommend this hotel, but would warn them about the noise.

“Texas touches” The Omni is located right downtown - a $25 cab right from the airport. The atrium consists of glass roofed space between it and the large office building next door. This gives a light an airy feel during the day. At night I found it rather dark with small pools of light at the restaurant and reception etc. Check in was fast and friendly. Another reviewer mentioned a smell and when I arrived on my floor it seemed that the carpet had just been cleaned and large fans were being used to help dry it. I lucked out by getting a large corner room with views to the outside rather than the atrium. I was a little concerned to see a notice warning me that since Austin was the capitol of live music it may be noisy at the weekend and they would try and help if you complaints! The room had some charming Texas touches - a leather chair with a cowhide-covered footstool, and some other elements of the decor. For once at a large chain hotel internet was fast and free. Good bathroom but a rather dark shower- plenty of hot water however, and good sizes shampoo bottles etc. Free coffee, although it took me a while to work out that you had to remove it from the closet and find a plug elsewhere.. All in all outlets were rather scarce especially near the nightstands. Good 32" flat screen TV with most of the usual channels.The linens were ironed and the bed was very comfortable. A nice touch was a bottle of spray starch in the closet with the iron. Concierge staff were very friendly and helpful. The state capitol is a few blocks away so very convenient for those in Austin on state business. The Omni offers a generous government discount as an additional bonus!

“Great location, amenities and staff” Had two suites for a recent girl's weekend. The hotel is very convenient to BART which really saves on ground transportation costs. The location to shopping and sites can't be beat. We walked to the Ferry Building Farmer's Market and it was a quick cab ride to the War Memorial Opera House for the ballet. The rooms are exactly like the photos on the Web site. It was great having the bar sink, fridge and microwave in the room since we could snack while we visited. The rooms are very spacious with nice big windows which let in lots of natural light. One night we brought in food and just watched movies. The hotel has a huge selection of premium movie channels: HBO, Showtime, etc. The complimentary morning breakfast is a nice touch as is the club level lounge and terrace and the complimentary WiFi. Housekeeping was excellent and the front desk and the concierge really went out of their way to be friendly and attentive. This place gets a big thumbs up from us and we're a picky group!

“Friendly service sets the tone here” I was able to stay here in January when the rates were lower. Hotel George is a mid-size hotel. I stayed in a mid-size room with a marble restroom. The bed was very comfortable and I especially enjoyed the wool throw blanket that I used while sitting in the easy chair. The staff members were helpful and welcoming, especially when my flight was canceled. I did eat breakfast at the attached restaurant and the service was surprisingly quick and the food good. The location is about two blocks from Union Station Metro.

“Great Motel” We stayed for 3 nights and found it very nice, very clean, great breakfast, good beds, and very friendly staff. Highly recommend it. We got the special AARP weekend discount and that is the main reason we stayed here. We had never been to Houston so everything including the motel was hard to find at first but it was very easy the second day after we got used to things. Would highly recommend this motel.

“Great Hotel, what about the free movies?” I am a guest at this hotel as I write this, and stay at Marriott properties about 150 nights a year on business. The hotel is in a great convenient location, and although not new, is still very fresh and has a nice range of facilities. The view from the city view rooms is great, and my colleague, who has a water view room, has a beautiful view of the harbor and passing boats. The rooms have new carpet and the new Marriott beds. The bathrooms have also been re-done within the last few years. My only critique is that the credenza, desk, etc. are a bit dated. I read the review a few posts down before checking in, and laughed about the woman who was all worried about the "soft core porn" available in the rooms. So I went to the TV to see what she was talking about. The Marriott TV has exactly the same set-up as every other Marriott everywhere, and it's very obvious that the pay channels are being accessed. There's also a very clear menu option that allows you to lock out adult channels...and none of the previews that are available show any nudity. So, my two cents' worth is that it's not quite what you read below, and I wouldn't worry if I was there with my children. Overall, great hotel and feel free to watch the TV without worry.

“Greast Staff, Clean Hotel with Hardwood Floors” What a great find! Great location with many reasonable priced restaurants; relatively large room (for New York), very professional and helpful staff, the rate included a very good continental breakfast. We arrived around lunchtime and were allowed to check in to the first available room on the same floor as the lobby. The room faced the back, so no noise, smell, etc. which one tends to associate with Chinatown. Close to subway, within walking distance to many great restaurants. I will definitely put it on my list of hotels for New York.

“Downtown Dallas” Checked out this morning so this review is fresh! Attended a conference with 300 others for 4 days. Rate was acceptable for this hotel. While the concierge folks were very polite and helpful but sometimes there just wasn't enough information given. For example, steering a lone female to a park nearby. I couldn't imagine going to a park by myself near a freeway by myself on foot. What I wasn't told that it was the new Klyde Warren Park (later I learned that it was new, spanned a freeway, and was heavily policed). Missing information several times. This hotel is nice, worn as previously stated in some areas. There is nothing to do in the immediate area except eat and drink. No shopping, just art, museums, etc. The rooms have been updated, beds are nice, pillows fine, flatscreen tv, and are, in general nice rooms. Hot water and faucets in my room were challenged however. I had to let the water run for about 10 minutes to get any hot water, pressure was poor. Staff there seems to be hardworking, however, maybe just not happy, except for the fellow in the lobby that helps everyone beyond belief! He acts like he loves his job! The wake-up call lady and the lobby guy are the hotel's two best employees and to me, exhibit true Texas hospitality. Really, this is an old downtown hotel that was abandonded by everyone else except high rise business. This would be a great place for a wedding, meeting, conference, business lunch, etc.

“Very Nice Chicago Hotel” I stayed at the Renaissance Blackstone Chicago Hotel while attending a conference at the McCormick Center and was impressed. The hotel is in a very old building however the rooms were up to date, comfortable and had obviously gone through a recent renovation. The bathroom was especially impressive with an open style shower and very nice black and white tile. The location is perfect if you know how to use the CTA. I was able to only spend $14 for a three day pass and get everywhere for the entire trip. It is a short walk to the “L” so no need to take a cab from the airport or to get over to Navy Pier. The hotel is also just a short walk to the Museum campus which includes the Adler Planetarium, the Shedd Aquarium and the Field Museum of Natural History. I didn’t utilize the restaurants during this trip so can’t comment on the food but the service from check in to check out was great and I will certainly stay at the Renaissance again next time I am in Chicago.

“Fantastic hotel, repeat visit confirms” After a weekend st this hotel at the end of April, my wife and I returned for one night this past weekend. Our circumstances dictated that we ask for an early early check-in, since we were coming in from a red eye flight from the west coast. I put a request for consideration in my reservation, and when I appeared at 630am the desk clerk went out of his as to accommodate us. Our reserved room type was not available. Til afternoon, but we were offered a great substitue which we graciously accepted. The room was quiet ( great sound deafening windows) and the hallway noice of maids, and visitors cming and going , didn't seep into the room as it often does at lesser hotels. I should say that I am a platinum Ambassor with intercontnenta Hotels, and I can say it is one hotel program that has rank bless point system, but definitely provides the perks on staying at their hotels. The early check in, and late departure stereo as well as free Internet, and a nice fruit bowl,along with a usual room upgrade. While this hotel is busy, and it's location at 8th and 44th could be considered 'in the middle of all the noise of Times Sq, this hotel is a quiet oasis in a busy noisy section of the city. Also the subway station for the 8th ave line is s few steps from the hotel door, a d is a short ride of one stop to Penn station and a long walk in the subway statin to the shuttle train to grand central. All make it very accessible. We'll be Back.

“Excellent hotel , great location , awesome beds” Stayed here from september 7 to 10 and really enjoyed our time at the hotel . The rooms are very well appointed , with a flat screen HD TV and also a handy kitchenette with a coffee maker . The alarm clock radio with ipod dock was very handy too for charging the ipod . The bathroom was of a good size , no bath though , which may be of a concern for some . Free wifi (which i found worked best on the terrace) and free local phone calls also came in handy . The bed was incredible . Seriously the most comfortable bed i've ever slept in . Just awesome . It was also quite a nice touch from the manager , Colin , to seek us out personally to ask if we enjoyed our stay and to see if we had any complaints or criticisms . The location is fantastic . 2 blocks west of times square . Close enough to be in the action and far enough away to not hear the noise . Broadway Theatres literally at your door step as well as all of Restaurant Row's finest dining options . Subway also only two blocks south on 8th ave . My only advice would be to request a room away from the elevator , simply because the ringing of the bell when the elevator stops at each floor is quite loud . All in all , we thoroughly enjoyed our stay and will definitely stay there again and will/have recommended it to friends .

“Great location, great stay” We spent a week in SF and the Argonaut is perfectly placed. We had a bay view, looking out on Alcatraz and the Golden Gate Bridge. We were on the 4th floor so it was quiet, too. The windows opened to get the beautifully cool air and ambiance from the street. Some decent restaurants in the area. Easy to grab a cab, street car or sightseeing tour bus. You can easily walk to Pier 39 and to catch the boat to Alcatraz. The housekeeping staff is very good and almost invisible. There is free tea in the afternoon and a wine reception at night. The Blue Mermaid restaurant, attached, has pretty good crab and corn chowder - good for when you're too tired to go anywhere else. Nice bakeries for breakfast in walking area, too. Would stay here again and would recommend it without reservation.

“Sharpest of the Club Quarter hotels I've stayed in” The Central Loop CQ is the cleanest, most polished and well-serviced of the CQ I've visited: NYC (all of the hotels), DC and Chicago. The best word I can find is "sharp." The feeling you get is that the people here care about the place, take pride in it, and want to provide you with the very best experience possible. The sitting room off the lobby is quite comfortable and the "living room" downstairs is about the best club room I've seen in this chain. Yes, the rooms are small. But you don't go to Chicago (or NYC or DC) to sit in a hotel room. You're there to sleep and shower. Maybe work a bit. And the Central Loop CQ's club rooms seem to be a bit more spacious than those in the other hotels. The staff is pleasant and helpful. (I had a problem with the valet staff, but it was handled quickly and resolved to my satisfaction.) The location cannot be beat. You are steps from most of what the Loop has to offer or within a block or two of access to the El for more distant destinations. We were in Chicago for a wedding and MOST of the guests invaded the hotel for the weekend. I really expected some kind of slowdown or hiccups with the service, but I experienced nothing but first-class service. So why not FIVE stars? I had problems with the online reservation system. I originally reserved rooms over the phone. When I discovered that we wouldn't need to come into Chicago as early as I had expected, I went online and modified the reservations. WARNING: do NOT trust the online system to process your request. My changes were NOT processed and I paid the cancellation penalty. I was a bit nervous the night before we left, so I called CQ to confirm the modification in our reservations. Wendy, the CQ rep I spoke, couldn't find the changes but she helped me greatly in guaranteeing the balance of our reservation -- I did not want the rooms cancelled on us -- and she called the hotel itself to make doubly sure we were in good shape. She admitted to me, however, that the online reservation system isn't reliable. So take that as a warning. Always call, always ask for a NEW confirmation number, and always note the date/time of the call and the name of the rep who helps you.

“great for families” We stayed here for 5 nights in the middle of November and absolutely loved it. We stayed in a 2 bedroom condo. We arrived very late at night and were had to phone the security to obtain keys but this was very easy and the chap was helpful. The condo was brilliant for us, 2 bathrooms and 2 bedrooms large kitchen and living room. We also loved the washing machine and dryer which came in handy with two young kids. The place was also spotless which is always nice to see. The only down side was that the resort was quiet and the lazy river was cold but thats not the fault of the resort. Its a stones throw from seaworld 5 to 10 min by car. The shop was expensive for food so be sure to bring all the essentials with you. The best bit was definately the heated pool and slides. We went there every day. Shops and restaurants are a short drive away, we didn't eat at the resort it was a bit expensive.

“Nice hotel with good service” I had to go to San Antonio for 2 days on business. I'm not a fan of the Riverwalk but I had to be there. I went during spring break and the city was CRAWLING with families vacationing. I was amazed at how well this hotel is managed. The property is clean, kept up, and the staff seemed eager to please. This hotel is not cheap but it is nice. It is located right on the Riverwalk, you can walk right out the backdoors and be on the cattle trail with all the other people looking for a daiquiri or a plate of Mexican food... The hotel has a good amenities, a nice bar, Starbucks, many restaurants, and many other services. Its a big, clean, safe, nice Marriott on the Riverwalk. The hotel was very busy, but well managed. The rooms were surprisingly quiet and comfortable. If I had to go back to the Riverwalk this is the place I would stay again. The hotel room was comfortable, clean, well kept, and provided all the amenities for me to get one of the better nights of sleep I have had in a hotel in a while. Other than having to be at the Riverwalk I had no complaints about this hotel at all.

“Felt like home away from home” I had stayed at the Hotel Rex about 7 years ago and had good memories of it... I just stayed there again for a week and quickly fell in love again. My particular room was a little bit of a cave..with only a brick wall for a view, so therefore was a little dark and I didn't get cellphone signal in the room.. BUT it was very quiet and cozy. The staff are lovely and helpful. A great hotel all around.

“Enjoyed our stay” Arrived late due to flight delays. Even though I had confirmed directly with the hotel a couple of days prior, I felt compelled due to an earlier review to call the day of arrival after I realized we would be arriving really late. Spoke with front desk and they said I was guaranteed and not to worry. So at check-in around 10:30pm, I was surprised when I was informed that the room we had reserved(exec.,2Dbl beds) was not available; however, she did accomodate us with an exec., king suite( 1 bed and a sleeper sofa- my 2 sons didn't appreciate that). She did offer to switch us the following morning, but we decided to stay put. Also watch your bill. We were charged $30 for parking each night and we did not have a car. After several phone calls, I believe it was resolved-I haven't checked my bank statement yet. Besides the above two aforementioned problems, the rest of the stay was pleasant. It was relatively quiet. Actually what train noise I did hear was more like white noise and was restful. Note, since they are no longer a Crowne Plaza hotel, they no longer offer the CD, ear plugs or eye mask or atleast that is what I was told. The breakfast, though limited, was delicious. The croissants to die for. cereal/hot oatmeal, fruit, yogurt, coffee/hot chocolate, fresh juice and milk and individualized preserves. Rooms clean and comfortable size. A little dark, but the high ceilings and large windows helped. Turn down service with cookies at night, great touch. Felt safe, esp. with the keycard and security on the ground level. Lobby on "lobby level "was cozy with fireplace and piano. My boys enjoyed playing when we returned in the evenings. Self serve coffee throughout the day. Conveniently located to millenium park, Ford theatre, restaurants, and shopping. Everything else including airport, easily accessible with train right outside your doors. The blue and red line approx. 1-2 blocks away-easy stroll. I would definitely stay here again, esp. for the $115/night rate received.

“Great Stay” I had a great stay at this Hilton. The rooms were very nice, staff was friendly and helpful and overall everything went great. I had friends staying in other hotels and their stays were not as pleasant as mine! I would definitely stay here again.

“Great staff- trains not too bad” Other trip advisor reviews warned that trains passed directly behind the hotel and were noisy. This is true, but it was not as bad as I suspected and in fact never woke us up, or disturbed us in hotel sleeping, intenet acess etc. The staff and the hotel shuttle service was great . Staff always willing to provide advice and when I asked for rooms close to the front of the hotel when I chechked in - to mitigate train noise -a tip I picked up from previous Trip Advisor reviews - they accomodated . Breakfast was as good as it gets in those hotels who provide it in the lobby as part of the room price The van took us to Balboa Park (zoo, Museums etc) and was efficient from the airport. We left early morning before shuttle service started and staff arranged taxis. Great location - on trolley line ( the same tracks where the trains run) , near many restuarants (Little Italy and Waterfront)., downtown etc. Overall a good experience.

“Still Understaffed” Stayed here with wife for a convention. The hotel is huge with numerous outstanding amenities. The pool area may be oversized for the staff/plan, however. Like 2 previous stays here, the property is still understaffed and undertrained. In the summer, the Schlitterbahn-like pool area is a zoo with guests competing for the few poor overworked servers' attention. This was completely unlike similar resorts in Vegas, Phoenix, etc. where the service is practically falling all over you with help. Unfortunately similar issues with front desk and maid service not up to the standards of a destination resort hotel. So all of this tends to stress up your getaway time, especially considering the price and "resort fee" you're paying. Let's face it, most of us just want a comfortable spot to lounge with a book or adult beverage, without having to fight for it. As is written by others, the hotel is about 30 minutes from the River Walk, in a residential neighborhood on the outskirts of San Antonio. If you're taking a family trip, the Hyatt Hill Country (adjacent Sea World) or Westin La Cantera (adjacent Fiesta Texas) offer better locations. The JW Marriott is more of a golf/convention meeting hotel.
“A little bit different - in a good way!” Easy walking distance to UCLA, shops and restaurants. Funky decor and great service! Would definitely stay here again.

“Great gem in great locale” The Doubletree Suites Chelsea on 29th is a great secret find and can often be booked at rates far below it's sister hotels on nearby streets. When you do a search on hotels, even if you go through the Hilton site, you'll get several Hilton properties that pop up including four or five in the same area. But this hotel stands apart from those for these reasons: 1. Location on a quiet midtown street. 2. Boutique feel. 3. Incredible location near several different subway lines. 4. Free Wifi for HHonors Members. (Slow, but free.) The rooms are typical NYC size, but not ridiculously tiny especially if you only have 1-2 people in the room. Plenty of space in the built-in closet and cabinets for things. Ample in-room safe will accommodate laptop plus other personal electronics easily. Blackout shades work well and noise from the street is not a problem, even on the front of the hotel. One of the things I love about the hotel is that each nightstand offers two A/C plugs--great for charging electronics. The staff is excellent. It's a small lobby so when a large group arrives it can get busy, but everyone always has a smile. Overhearing that i was going to a local department store, one front desk staffer brought me a special coupon gift card for that store and had written down the closing times for the length of my stay. Very nice. The cons of this hotel are very few and don't come close to being important enough to not stay here. But they are-- 1. Not enough shelf space in the bathroom. Could be easily remedied by adding a second shelf on the wall. 2. Feather pillows only. The hotel clerk told me they are attempting to get foam pillows soon. There are ample pillows on the bed, but they are all feather. 3. Only 2 elevators. Elevators all feel crowded and slow.

“Wonderful spa” I didn't stay here, but spent two glorious hours in the Spa. The facilities are brand-new and beautiful. The women's locker room is carpeted and furnished with full-length wooden lockers with digital locks--no key to keep track of, and you set your own combination so you'll actually remember it! There's an area with hair dryers, curling irons, complimentary hairspray and other toiletries; the immaculate showers are stocked with excellent shower gel, shampoo, etc. Oh, and the steam room! Gleaming porcelain and eucalyptus-scented steam...The only thing missing was robe hooks outside the steam room. Did I mention that the robes are thick and sweet smelling? I had a massage and a facial. Both were perfect and the providers most proficient. Even the obligatory new-age music was less annoying than usual (much of it was based on classical themes instead of endless appeggios). Altogether, a most highly recommended spa.

“Trendy New Hotel” When we entered our room my wife said "Isn't this the grooviest room ever." With retro furnishings Austin Powers would feel right at home with and ultra chic touches everywhere, this place really screams DESIGNER. I found it all a little sterile but functional and comfortable none-the-less. Fortunately, they got all the important things right. It was quiet, the bed was comfortable, there was a 42" HD TV, they had a nice ipod dock radio/alarm clock, the bathroom was spacious and the shower was nice and hot. We ate at the restaurant in the hotel and it was quite good. There is a real scene in the bar on the weekends and it is in the middle of everything LA Live has to offer. I would skip the $38 a day valet parking, there are plenty of much cheaper parking options within a block or two of the Hotel, plus, even though I called 15 minutes ahead to have my car ready, I still had to wait another 15 minutes for it to be brought up. Finally, it really irks me that this hotel charges $12.95 a day for wireless. Hotels that charge less than half what this hotel costs include it in their nightly rate.

“Great Location, Great Value!” We stayed here for 1 night after Christmas, but before New Years. For $297 (we had discount from the Entertainment Book, so it actually cost us only $277) you cannot beat this Times Square location. Any other decent hotel in the area is way more expensive. We arrived a little early, and the front desk attendant, who was very busy but still courteous and patient, told us he'd have our room ready in 30 minutes. He then offered us some tea and coffee from the breakfast room. I could not even finish my tea because our room was ready in about 15 minutes! The hotel is clean and the employees actually care about the guests and want to do a good job. The bellman referred us to an excellent pizza place for lunch and that made us very happy! Our room was situated so that we could not hear all the noise from Times Square, so it was very quite. The hallways are narrow, but we are skinny so it wasn't a problem. The room was small, but that is to be expected in NYC. Our only complaint is that you can hear everything in the hallway from the room. The walls are quite thin and we were awoken a few times by slamming doors. Overall, this is an excellent hotel with excellent staff! We highly recommend it!

“Fun, Spotless Hotel with Amazing Service” Another excellent Kimpton Hotel! We recently stayed at Hotel Rouge. Excellent, excellent service--an employee from the bar who knew that I had a cold later brought a thermos of hot water & tea up to my room (without any request on my part). This is extraordinary service. Service was intelligent and friendly--the staff members talk to you and if you ask a question, someone thinks about it and gives correct and useful advice. And: you will find a spotlessly clean and LARGE room, a comfortable space to sit for two, with a lamp and ottoman, a very comfortable bed and a large closet area.
