Hotel has lively cocktail hour with wine and snacks. It also has an on-site restaurant/bar open. We didn't eat much in hotel but was more than fine for breakfast. As for location, it's a pleasant 20 min. walk to Smithsonian Mall, easy 5-10 min walk to Dupont Circle. Lots of shopping, restaurants there. Hotel is on quiet, safe feeling street. We had a dog with us. Totally easy to travel with pet at this hotel. This hotel is a gem.

“Excellent View” We stayed at this hotel for two nights during a quick vacation. Hotel was great, clean, and modern. The amenities were quite expensive though. Internet in the room was $15 a day, parking was $50 per day, and drinks at the bar were also quite pricey. This hotel seems more geared to business travellers than vacationers. We stayed on the 25th floor and the view of the city was fantastic!

“Great location, great staff, great choice” I chose this location based solely on the brand, and guessed which ES I wanted...this one or the "downtown" one. Very pleased with my choice. The only snag was the sky lobby, where you have to take an elevator up to the lobby, then another set to the room. The lobby elevators from the street level were slow, and at least one was out of service the two days we were there. And thats it for complaints! The rest was just what I have come to expect from this chain. Registration/check in was great. Some sort of conference going on, throngs of people milling around the lobby, and I still felt like they were waiting for me to arrive. Right up to the room in the coolest glass elevators looking out over the city, and to the room, which was clean, comfortable, well appointed, and matched my room request perfectly. Beds were comfortable, and room was dark and quiet. The location was convenient, just a couple of blocks in any direction to most everything...Magnificent Mile, Navy Pier, Gino's East for the best deep dish, and all the other tourist attractions you's need. We were there for Major League Baseball, and it was just a few stops in either direction to both Wrigley and Cellular One field. (Concierge was great with directions and suggestions.) Breakfast was also great, and typical, it the best way possible. Nice seating area, plenty of hot and cold choices, and staff always around to clear a table or assist in any way necessary. Check out was also simple, everything on this trip went very smoothly.The hotel was at or near capacity, and it was never a problem. Even the bellman who held our bags for the last morning of our trip was pleasant and professional. Would stay here next time I am in Chicago.

“I will be back.” Best part about this hotel is location. Immediately off the 405 and Ventura Fwy make this a great place to stay on the west side of the Valley. Room was standard and clean. Interesting fact, I am 5'9' and I could barely reach over to access the bathroom sink.... Hum. Otherwise, stay was great. The parking garage had 24 hour security which is nice for a female traveler. The workout facility was first class. Don't forget to stop and see Maurice at the lounge. He fixes a mean drink, AND try the grilled vegetable sandwich. It is truely terrific. Free internet access in the lobby is also nice. All was well with this hotel.

“Great hotel! Walking distance from the airport.” I had a last minute business trip to Boston. A majority of the airport hotels were sold out. This hotel is very expensive. (I paid over $275 for my stay.) The signage from the arrival terminal to the hotel is nonexistent, I had to call the hotel and ask for directions. The room was clean and cozy. I had room service. The service and food were excellent. There is a bar, restaurant and coffee bar onsite. Service was nice and everyone was friendly. It was a great stay!

“Traditional Elegance at The Fairmont” My husband and I stayed at The Fairmont over Valentine's/President's Day weekend and loved every minute of it. The hotel is elegant in the traditional sense - understated, not over the top like The Fairmont in San Francisco. Our room was good-sized and well laid-out. And the bed! One of the most comfortable I have ever slept in! Loved the white marble in the bathroom. My only criticism was that the curtains were a little too flowery - traditional decor can become old lady with too many flowers. The hotel has a wonderful gym with a view over the indoor pool and beautiful arched windows. We appreciated the very fast, and free, Internet service. The hotel staff was attentive, but not overly. Dinner at Shuckers was amazing, and they had the best oysters we tried in Seattle - and we ate them at quite a few different places. The hotel is well-located downtown, and we could walk to everything except Fremont. Would definitely stay again!!

“Very Good for the Money” Outstanding value, very clean, super location, walkable upscale neighborhood with tons of nightlife, shopping, and restaurants. Drug store nearby. Short walk to metro station plus excellent bus service. Great for any business travel, extended stay or leisure travelers who like a great room that they won't be in much.

“Very Good-New with a few issues to work out” Brand new hotel that just opened two weeks ago. Everything was very nice and the location is great. The staff was very friendly and helpful. Not much is needed to be said about the rooms as they are brand new and beautiful. The beds are a little firm but that is a personal preference I guess. Everything about this hotel was nice, but there were a couple of issues that need to be addressed. They are minor and I believe a result of the hotel being so new. They just need to get the newness worked out a bit. The first issue is that I had no bars of soap in my room. Shampoo and conditioner where there, but no face or body soap. Also there is a paper card in the bathroom that explains the "leave the towels on the floor if you want them washed..." policy and this card was water stained and looked bad. It should have been replaced. There were no trash bags in the trash cans, not really a problem but the can looked dirty from not having bags in them. One of the worst issues was when I got in the shower I found a used washcloth hanging over the shower curtain. These are all housekeeping issues and I am sure that these will be worked out as the crew becomes familiar with what they should be doing. Forgiven this time and I hope on my next trip these will be resolved. One other new hotel issue was that I went ot the "Market Place" to get an ice cream and found that all the ice cream was melted in the freezer. I notified the front desk and they thanked me an apologized , saying they would address the issue. I assume they did because all the frozen items were melted or thawed and could be a major health issue. All of the above said this is still a very, very nice business or family vacation near the Alamo and Riverwalk. I would highly recommend this hotel and I am sure that all the issues mentioned above will be remedied. One last note, I am not sure if you can self park here or not. I thought when I made the reservation that it said free parking, but at check in the only option seemed to be valet parking at $21/night. There may be self parking, but there was no indication of it and it was made to seem like valet was the only option. That is not so much a problem if valet is the only option as that is what you find in most city locations.

“Okay” We travelled across the USA on a tour organised by Great Rail Journeys of York between the 7th and 27th October 2009. We stayed at the Holiday Inn Golden Gateway on Van Ness which is close to the cable car terminus. Our room was one of the smaller rooms we had experienced on our trip, but it was clean and comfortable. It was quiet and everything worked. We slept well in the large double bed. It was not well serviced on one of the days of our stay with glasses and cups left uncleaned. Our room overlooked the 6th floor swimming pool which gets sun in the morning. We breakfasted in the hotel on one day – we had the continental buffet for $14.25 which was reasonable value though the range was restricted. You can catch the California line cable car or the bus right outside the hotel. There is a grocery store nearby (south on California) which was very nice and good value. You can buy a Municipal travel Pass in the hotel gift shop. That was well worth it. To ride the cable car one way it's $5, for Bus it is $2. We paid $18 for a three day (unlimited rides) pass and definitely got our money's worth. As we left early on the third day we handed our pass back into the Gift Shop in the hope they could recycle the unexpired portion to another visitor.

“Recommended” There are lots of hotels near the airport but it's hard to beat this one for convenience, the free breakfast, the 24-hour free shuttle to the airport and the size of the 2-room suites. We have 3 kids and we need the pullout in addition to the two large beds. We were there for two nights and flew out in a blizzard (no exaggeration -- the day we left was the worst weather of 2009) so we wouldn't have made it out in time if we had stayed further away. Kids loved the pool complex and the breakfast. Staff was friendly and helpful. It's a long way to downtown and you need a car to get there.

“My new favorite hotel in NYC!” After leaving the W Hotel on Lexington Ave. between 49th and 50th Streets (see scathing review on that one), the San Carlos seemed like a palace. Stayed three nights, June 21-23, and will stay there next time I go to New York City. All of the staff were friendly and courteous. We stayed in an Executive King Suite (Room 702) and it was bigger than some New York City apartments! Upon entering, the first room had a bar with two bar stools, a stainless steel sink, microwave, refrigerator (for your use, not the mini bar) and cabinets filled with everything you might need including real china, utensils, a corkscrew, cloth napkins, wine glasses, drinking glasses, coffee mugs, etc. The second room was a living room with two chairs, two end tables, a sofa, a coffee table and the mini bar. The third room contained a king size bed, a nice dresser, two nightstands, a pants press (which I used to press shirts and skirts as well), and TWO closets. The bathroom had a tub and shower and a full length mirror. The air conditioning worked great and had a thermostat for better control (not just off all night so you are hot or on all night so you freeze). I could have stayed there indefinitely. The hotel had an excellent location in heart of Midtown East, one block from subway and an easy walk to excellent restaurants. They even had complimentary continental breakfast which is exceedingly rare in New York City. The price was $30 per night less than the horrible W Hotel. Of course, at just under $500 per night, it was not inexpensive, but for the location and the quality it was worth every penny.

“Great location” This hotel is really nice in the heart of downthown Chicago. You could walk to many of the popular spots in the Chicago. The rooms are nice and clean. The staff is nice. The fitness center is somewhat small for the size of the hotel.

“Exotic gem” First, the basics: comfy bed, great shower, immaculately clean, fine location (near Times Sq but not too noisy), small room but perfect for solo traveler Next, the extras: nice free continental breakfast, fun flashing of Times Sq neon in my window at night (there was a shade if needed), privacy curtain for shower (Shower is actually in the room, toilet is only additional room) Last: the sensational: the staff, friendliest I have ever encountered and this says a lot as all boutique staffers seem to be trained in the same wonderful hospitality school; the decor, with Indian references and homey gas fireplaces scattered throughout, making for a happy relief coming in from the rain. I booked via Sniqueaway and had gotten a reasonable rate of $174 not including taxes etc Just a lovely all around experience.

“Superb - no hesitation in staying there again” I usually stay at the Hilton Garden across the street, but they were full midway thru my visit to Chicago, so thought I would try the Hampton Downtown. I was not disappointed - booked a suite and were given a corner suite on a higher floor,which had full kitchen, complete with pans, plates and flatware, dishwasher etc, also lounge, bathroom and kingsize bed. The room was spotless and cleaned and vacummed thoroughly each day throughout. Front desk staff were very friendly and helpful, allowing us early check-in and late check-out. Being on a higher floor we did not hear any of the sirens or club noise that other reviewers mentioned. Breakfast was free and plenty of tables available with a fair selection of hot and cold, and as usual with Hampton Inns, free coffee / tea 24 hours a day. The internet access was free and was quick and easy to connect any time day or night with fast speeds. Easy access to Michigan Avenue, and may eating places nearby, also the Red Line Chicago stop is only 1 block away. A bonus, as I was away from home for some time, is that they also have a laundry room on the 3rd floor with two washers and dryers which is open from 8am - 10pm. Would have no hesitation in staying there again.

“Grand Old Luxury Hotel” Hay-Adams is grand and luxurious in everyway. I stayed here as part of a small group holding a meeting at the hotel. Was informed at check-in that I had been upgraded to a "junior suite" - lucky me! The room was large with a seperate seating area, finely furnished, clean and comfortable. I enjoyed the Bose Wave CD player provided with a selection of CD's. Nice touch. Comfortable bed. Bathroom was functional and modern. Public spaces are beautiful and reminiscent of a bye gone era of quality construction and great attention to detail. The view of the White House from the roof top is unique for DC. Front desk staff was professional and helpful. Overall I could not ask for a better experience.

“Absolute best hotel in Chicago!” Last year, my husband booked the Hyatt on Wacker Drive for our five day stay in Chicago during his ASCO conference. This year, I insisted that we upgrade to the Park Hyatt during our prerequisite ASCO trip in June. I had stayed at the Park Hyatt years ago (right after it opened), and it was just as I remembered - and so much more! The building has 18 floors of hotel rooms with private residences built on top. (There is a separate entrance for the hotel.) The lobby is serene and quiet (the complete opposite of our experience at the Hyatt, which was beyond chaotic and noisy). There was no line to check in when we arrived, and we were ushered up to our room (1808, a corner unit on the top floor) immediately. The room was well layed out with a foyer area leading to a long hallway past the closet, minibar, bathroom, then into the bedroom. There was the most fantastic view of Michigan Avenue & the lake from our windows. This surely ranks high on the list for reasons to stay at the Park Hyatt! There are sheer and black out shades for all windows, which can be operated by controls by the nightstand. The room was well-insulated from hallway noise; I couldn't hear much in the hallway, though it helped to be in a corner unit. I never got the sense that the hotel was fully booked even though I am sure it was packed with 45,000 attendees in Chicago for ASCO. The king-size bed was excellent and super comfortable, the LDC TV was fine (the DVD player an employee brought up and hooked up to the TV was much appreciated), the Herman Miller Eames lounger and ottoman were amazing and stylish. My husband is such a fan of the lounger that he wanted to buy one for our condo as well - until he realized the price! We loved the small but thoughtful touches in the room - complimentary bottled water every day, Frette bathrobes, complimentary guest services office off the lobby on the first floor (for computer and printer use), extra toiletries in the closet. Housekeeping was thorough and neat in general. My only complaint about housekeeping is that they aren't particular or prompt about clearing room service trays that are ready to be taken. We had an instance or two in which housekeeping left the trays & tables and cleared the entire room otherwise. Just made it seem less clean. The spa on the 7th floor didn't have availability for the day I requested, so I instead visited the Peninsula's spa, which is wonderful and just a block away. I would recommend the Peninsula in general for their spa services, but I personally didn't have the most relaxing experience. My aesthetician was efficient and quite forceful; the manicure I received was fine but I didn't feel relaxed until I lounged on their outdoor terrace post-manicure. Anyway, the Park Hyatt's spa, fitness center, restaurant (nomi) and their outdoor lounge area (nomi garden) are all located on the 7th floor. Drinks at nomi garden were pretty good; not going to lie though - paying $20 for a drink was a surprise, even after living in NYC for five years. We ordered from room service three times, and all three times, their estimated delivery times were spot on. Everything we ordered - 800 burger, buffalo chicken wings, chicken caesar salad, sushi from nomi, etc - was pretty tasty. Note: there is an automatic 17% service charge for all room service orders. On our last day in Chicago, my husband and I reserved two biked through concierge at the Park Hyatt and went biking along the lake for a few hours. It was so lovely to be outside on bikes for a change! We recommend guests at the Park Hyatt make use of this offering. The bikes were in okay condition (mine had handlebars that were unbalanced and the bike creaked quite a bit), but overall, it was fine. They provide helmets, locks, bottled water, etc for the four hours you're allowed to take the bikes. Of course, there is a waiver form to be signed by everyone using the bikes. We loved our stay at the Park Hyatt. It was luxurious, comfortable, quiet, elegant - we felt very well taken care of during our five days there. We would recommend the hotel to everyone - friends, acquaintances, colleagues, family. Make sure to ask for a room with a view of Michigan Avenue & the lake - it was spectacular!

“Easy & Convienent” Close to the airport, without any airport noise, this place fit the bill for a one night stay. Bus to & from LAX was easy & quick and my room was big and comfortable, with a shower that really rocked. Only negatives was the slow check in and only one restaurant. We ate at the bar because the restaurant was a 20-30 minute wait, not because it was full, but because they didn't schedule enough wait staff.

“Still Great” The Peninsula is a fabulous hotel. I have stayed here many times in the past but it has been several years since my last stay (for convenience only). I had read some reviews stating that rooms were tired and in need of a redo. My room was not this way. It was perfect and did not feel dated at all. The rooms are large and well appointed. The bathroom is spacious with separate tub and shower as well as a separate dressing area. The staff and service are excellent. The location is great for shopping and restaurants. I was travelling alone and went to The Bar for a drink and dinner. It was very good. It’s old school with dark wood paneling and a fireplace. When I was there it was not crowded. I ate at the bar and felt totally comfortable alone. The bartender was helpful in a meal selection. Overall I can not recommend the Peninsula more highly.

“Almost Everything a First Class Hotel Should Be” On a business trip in Boston's Financial Center I found the Intercontinental to be excellent. The meticulously-clean and spacious rooms, clever layout and amenities, splendid views and superb business location made it a perfect choice. The only negative was the absence of a hotel directory identifying the hotel amenities - the fitness center and other facilities. When I asked the concierge about a directory, he advised that it was on one of the television channels. During my stay the television channel was off the air although there was a general Boston tourist channel and a hotel events channel, but no directory on any channel. As a result I was unable to identify or use many of the amenities at the hotel.

“Glad I Tried It"” Stayed at the Omni San Francisco for one night while on business. I usually stay elsewhere when in town but thought I would try the Omni as the location was very close to my business appointments for the next day. Turned out to be an excellent location for business travel. Very, very nice. Public areas are nothing short of beautiful. My king bed room and bathroom were absolutely spotless. The desk in the room had really handy outlets right on the front of the desk, no crawling aroung looking for an outlet! Bed was comfortable, but just two flimsy pillows on the bed just doesn't cut it. I like a bed with lots of comfy pillows great for propping up to watch TV. That's really the only thing here that was anything but superlative. Not a deal killer. Front desk staff were very pleasant and aimed to please. Bob's Steakhouse located in the hotel was so good I ate there twice in 24 hours. The bar looked like a fun place to watch a game with colleagues. It's safe to say I will be back at the Omni San Francisco!

“Exceeded expectations in every way!” Great stay from the minute we arrived and valet took the car to the doorman who treated us like old friends to the front desk who asked about our plans and then sent up a welcome packet specifically tailored to us. Requests for the car were easy and super quick. The customer service ethic here is above and beyond. Room was beautiful and extremely comfortable. Room service was prompt and delicious. Eastern Standard for cocktails and dinner was fantastic, worth every penny. Would recommend this hotel highly.
“Best staff” Stayed here a night before flying out and the staff was great! Everyone was friendly and helpful. I would recommend this hotel to anyone coming to Columbus.

“Quirky and refreshing” This is a fun, eclectic hotel. Every floor has its own theme. I was on the sci fi floor with movie posters up in the hallway and pictures in the room. I stayed here on a business trip for 3 days. The room was spacious. I would definitely stay here again.

“Interesting historic hotel with a funky modern update” This is a great hotel if you don't want to be right in the middle of shopping and would rather be closer to museums, universities, etc. Do ask for a room with a view and you will wake up to Grant Park and Lake Michigan. Everything about this hotel is unique (including the metallic gold tufted couches in the lobby). The rooms are very modern and have tremendous bathrooms. There's a Starbuck's in the lobby and a great tapas restaurant. Parking was expensive, but it's expensive everywhere in downtown Chicago. My daughter and I walked to shopping and restaurants and saw the Chicago River turn green. It was a great place.

“Yes the rooms are small - and there are other small issues. However...” I am a picky traveler - no two ways about it. I was dubious about a hotel in NYC for $150 a night (not to mention that their parking is only $30 ... compared with upwards of $50 most other places). However, I was pleasantly surprised ... my requested room type was arranged without hesitation from the staff, the front desk clerks were VERY friendly and helpful. The room is small, but it was a one-night stopover en-route from Philadelphia to New Hampshire, so space was not a requirement. The room was comfortable and well-appointed (NYC chic). I did take issue with one thing, however. Per the terms of HH Diamond membership, Doubletree properties are supposed to provide internet free of charge to members (either that or breakfast). When I contacted the property, they indicated that I would have to pay the $11 access charge for the internet ... I found that to be irritating, but would not stop me from returning. The location, at 50th & Lex is right in the heart of things, with a subway stop literally right outside the door. The staff was able to direct us to a great little area for a late dinner (midnight on a Sunday night) called Little West 12th St, in the meatpacking district. VERY hip and trendy. Overall a pleasant experience.

“Excellent Value” Stayed here for three nights in early December 2010. The location is perfect, very close to the subway system, Macys, and the Empire State Building. The check-in was fast, and the elevators were efficient even during the busy period. Room was very compact in the typical New York manner but was clean and functional, nice comfortable bed, adequate lighting, with a work desk, flat screen TV, and nice bathroom with adequate lighting. Beware of noise from the street late at night due to garbage pick up; rooms on the backside of the hotel would likely be quieter. My room had an incredible view of the Empire State Building, and it was worth it being on the street side, but I do wear earplugs at night when I travel to busy cities. The maid service was not up to par as the shampoo, and coffee packets, cups, and cream and sugar were not replinished satisfactorily. The breakfast buffet was excellent with several hot items and some healthy fruit and cereal options. I would definitely stay here again without question.

“Great rooms and good tennis” The Fairmont Hotel in San Jose was one of the hotels featured on the SAP Open website and offered a reasonable rate of $119/night while attending the tournament. We reserved the room for a Tuesday night and found the hotel extremely busy. The front desk ladies were a bit brusque while informing us that our room would not be ready until 3pm. They did offer us a room in the south tower but after reading the reviews here, we had requested a room in the main tower. We had some trouble finding the bellman to store our luggage while we took a short walk. The Asian Art Gallery next door featured interesting contemporary art and is definitely worth a look if you have time. Our corner room on the 15th floor was ready at 3pm as promised (#1501) and was well worth the wait. With over 400 sq feet, it was very spacious with large sunny windows and a nice sitting area. The room was immaculate and the bathroom was nice and large with a separate shower and bathtub, two robes and even a nightlight. The water pressure is excellent. There is also a separate area for dressing and a large, well-lit, vanity area. The only thing missing is a coffee maker, though the cafe right outside the side door of the hotel is very convenient. There is an honor bar in the room, but the items are very pricey and you will want to check the bill before leaving in case the computer has automatically charged you for something you did not have. I made the mistake of moving a few items around to put my own water in it and found I was charged for the items I had removed, even though I returned them before we left the room. However, the front desk was very apologetic and quickly removed the charges. It was the first time we attended the SAP Open and we enjoyed the tennis (Andy Roddick and James Blake were featured players) and found it was easy to get good seats. The HP Pavilion is very close, definitely walking distance from the Fairmont. It was so late when we got back to the hotel after the match the only dining option we had was room service. The food was good and service fairly quick, but $50 for two cheeseburgers seemed a bit over the top. All in all, it's a beautiful hotel with lovely rooms and we will definitely try to stay there again next year.

“Omni Oasis” Houston in late August can be, well, miserably hot. The Omni makes a 107 degree day more bearable. The property is centrally located (about 2 miles from the Galleria) and while it sits close to major roads, the surrounding trees and the fact the property sits back makes it very pleasant. The room I had (1110) was spacious, clean, with a comfy bed and a decent size bathroom. The rooms and property are a little older, but tha is not a detraction. Self-parking is a 30 second walk to the front door of the hotel and it is covered, so no need to valet park. The staff is very helpful and check-in and out went smoothly. The hotel has a small gift shop which serves Starbucks drinks and a more formal dinner restaurant. One work about dining: the dinner memu was somewhat limited and if you do not plan to dine at the property you will need to drive. Other good restaurants are whinin a 2 mile radius - just be advised! The hotel has a real outdoor pool (one you can actually swim in) and a three-year old spa. I had one treatment at the spa and found the price reasonable, the service relaxing and the staff very courteous. The spa is not that large and doesn't have all the bells and whisltles that you would find at a Ritz Cartlon or Four Seasons spa. This again is not really a negative, just an FYI. The business center is small and charges a fee to use the internet - a pet peeve of mine. Comeon Omni join Hilton and Hyatt and start offering free internet! In summary, this property is functional, quiet, with great staff and a decent location.

“It is the standard for Excellence!” The Burnham is an exceptional hotel experience. From the moment you see it, you know the place is unique, warm and welcoming. The location can't be beat, the rooms are spacious and well appointed; you could easily stay inside your entire trip. The Atwood Cafe gets better each time you go there. The complimentary wine hour is a very nice way to get to know other guests. The real key to the Burnham however, is the outstanding team of people working there. On this trip, I got to spend time with Emil, Darnell, Kelsey, Terrell and Vane. Each of them are extremely professional, gracious, and clearly proud to be part of Team Burnham!

“Nice Stay and Great Breakfast - Air Is Noisy” I received a very nice upgraded room and was completely statisfied with every aspect of my stay. The staff was courteous, the breakfast buffet include cooked to order omelets and was completely pleased. I personally experience nothing to indicate the the rooms were in need of update or "tired" - an overused word on this forum in describing upscale hotels. Only observation that could be negative - air conditioning is noisy.

“Central Location--Clean Room” I stayed at the Courtyard in Downtown Austin last month for business. The hotel was packed; however, I was there for a convention, so I'd assume any time you are there for a convention it will be packed. The staff was friendly, my room was clean, and the hotel is litteraly across the street from the convention center! My only complaints, the walls were thin and the line at the Starbucks in the lobby was always long... at least a 30 minute wait.

“Cool scene in a cool town” Great location two blocks off union square. Room was big as we took the 29dollar upgrade offer via email. Only neg was could hear the service elevator through wall. Fortunately we sleep heavy after hanging in the bar and enjoying the people watching. Don't miss slanted door restaurant or Gary Danko both great and worth the money. Also get to muir wood early very limited parking. Breakfast at the hotel not great. Went up to a coffe shop on Taylor good fast and reasonable. Door man told us about it.

“Charm, friendly staff, value and location!” What more could you ask for? The historic Algonquin Hotel is conveniently situated in mid-town Manhattan -- walking distance from Rockefeller Center, Radio City Music Hall, Central Park, Times Square/Broadway and the Empire State Building or a short subway ride to anywhere else. To top it off, the recently renovated hotel has nicely appointed rooms and friendly and attentive staff -- right down to Mathilda, the resident cat. The standard "deluxe" rooms are cozy (i.e. small), but it provides everything you could need, plus charm -- all at a reasonable rate (for New York City). We did not use the bar/restaurant services during our three night stay (9/5 - 9/8), but if you need an inexpensive breakfast, a few doors down the Red Flame Diner had fast and tasty service.

“beautiful, large hotel with nice veiws” This was our second stay at this hotel. Our first stay had a westward view of Shaw Tower. For this stay, we had a view of 6th Street and the top of the capitol. I preferred the view of the Shaw Tower, especially at night. If you can't get this view from your room, go to the rooftop pool. The rooms here are very nice and I recommend staying here, especially if you can get a moderately priced room.

“All round nice hotel..” I got this hotel through priceline.com and paid $70 a night. This was a great deal because it was priced at $199 - $299 on the website. Hotel was clean and modern enough. Located in the heart of downtown Boston and sandwiched between Chinatown and the Theatre district, the Hyatt provides easy access point to these two locations as well as to the 'T'. The hotel room was smaller than the Hyatt's I have lived in but the room was nice. The bathroom was smaller than I was used to as well. So, with two people wanting to use the bathroom at once could be quite cramped. However, room was clean, had a coffee making machine, a TV with all channels working (not a flat screen) and equipped with Nintendo 64 gaming (at $7.00 an hour!). Also had a bar, iron and board and a robe to use (if going to use the swimming pool). Decor was slightly 80's style mixed in with the new furniture. One thing to be aware of is the LOUD banging of the doors! Around 9-11pm, 7-9am, you will be woken up for sure by other people so bring some ear-plugs if you are a light sleeper! I got a room on the 16th floor and got nice views around the city. Staff were super friendly at the check-in desk. Couldn't say the same for some of the concierge/bell boys. Other slight criticism is the funny layout of the hotel. You enter the side of the hotel and go down a few steps to the Lower Lobby only to have to go up 3 floors to get to reception and to get to your room. Overall, a nice hotel although slightly weird in design and layout. Great value for money (for what I paid) and location for a great night out in the town. Recommended!

“Great Place to Stay!” This hotel very convenient to all things downtown. Being on 2nd and San Jacinto, it is very close to a lot of nice restaurants. PF Changs is across the street and Fogo de Chao is around the corner. There is a great restaurant in the hotel called Cafe Crepe. You can valet park or self park in the garage. Valet is $23 a night. The rooms are very nice and clean. The beds and linens are wonderful. Internet works well and is free. Breakfast is free and has lots of selections including fresh fruit. They have a shuttle service that they contract with that will take you just about anywhere downtown for $5. We had business in the Capital so that was convenient. I really enjoyed staying here and will stay here again.
“Very nice. Marriott standard.” Marriott's best. Very nice for conference venue or just for vacation. Excellent location close to zoo and metro. Beautiful lobby.

“The secret is out!” After zealously researching DC hotels, I decided on the St. Gregory - and was not disappointed! This hotel has a fabulous (and safe) location, and is a quick 5 minute walk from Dupont Circle (and the Metro). The suites are well-appointed (I had a Jr. Suite); the bathroom was spacious!; the staff friendly; and housekeeping efficient. I was fortunate enough to have Club access - which was attended by the remarkably friendly and courteous Miguel. I did book directly through the hotel website, after comparing prices with the typical Internet site discounters. Overall, a gem and a serious alternative to the "mega-conglomerate" cookie cutter hotel room experience!

“Outstanding” The location was great in terms of where my client was, so this will now be my new Houston hotel. Clean. Sleek. Trendy. Great rooms. Awesome bar. The restaurant was packed and there was one poor guy working his butt off. My steak was pretty average. But that's the only possible thing I could take issue with. I'm a fan.

“Definite Return Trip to this One!” This was a really terrific hotel that I will definitely frequent again. My husband & I come to Chicago every year at Thanksgiving for my birthday so we have stayed in many places over the years - Hampton, Monaco, Hotel 71, Hilton Garden Inn, Wyndham, Four Points Sheraton, etc. Knowing my way around Chicago, I chose to try the Springhill Suites on Dearborn and am I glad I did! Although the location is great, just a couple of blocks off Michigan & State, it's actually easy to miss the hotel - the signage outside is quite plain and it shares an entrance w/ Residence Inn. The actual lobby for both chains is on the 2nd floor. Check-in was great, staff very accommodating -- I even got a bottle of wine for my birthday. The elevators are the fastest and smoothest of any hotel I've ever stayed in. The hotel offers a nice hot/cold complimentary breakfast as well - a bit early for a "leisure" trip (6:30-9:00 a.m.). We had a "studio" double room. It was perfect, very chic and modern. Sitting area had a desk, chaise, and sleeper couch and was separated from bedroom area by frosted glass. Plenty of lighting (which is a big complaint w/ me because most rooms are just too dark). We had a microwave, frig, and coffee maker. Bath area was good size and vanity area was separate w/ plenty of top space to put items. The only issue I had was the lack of good sized drawers for clothes that you didn't want to hang .. there were only (2) very shallow drawers. I would rate this hotel as EXCELLENT.

“Lovely! Perfect Business Hotel” The Sheraton Four Points Metrocenter is a perfect place to stay on business. It has a nice restaurant (I ate there for breakfast and dinner), pool, outdoor jacuzzi, FREE wireless Internet access, Wednesday evening reception for corporate guests, and the rooms are modern and cheerful. The staff is definitely friendly and are very cheerful with guests. I definitely plan to return.

“Great price, excellent location” We stayed two nights at the hotel to help our daughter move into DC area house. The suite was just twenty dollars more than a standard room which was also a bargin, had a kitchenette and a good view. The room(s) were large for a downtown hotel and was in easy walking distance of everything. The staff was fine if not especially gracious. Everything worked which you can't always say. We will look here first to see what deals are available for our next trip.

“Small rooms, but very central” Yes the rooms are small, but it's NYC! We had a smoking room (we are not smokers) and couldn't smell anything. The rooms were clean. A/C is a little loud at night though, as the rooms can get hot, you needed to leave it on throughout the night. Breakfast is included, which is great! Not a huge variety, but enough to get you on your way! Cereal, toast, bagel, pastries, tea/coffee, juice. Not a very big seating area though as tour groups stay here too! Most of the staff were friendly, except for one on the later night shift. Very rude!!!!!!!! But the loation is fabulous, you can walk anywhere from here.

“Time to get rid of the Smoking rooms” This is California and the smoking rooms must go! I will admit that it was my mistake when I went to choose this hotel that I picked a room on the top (4th) floor the day before I checked in via E-check in, not knowing it was smoking. I just find it hard to believe that properties have smoking rooms to begin with and on the top floor, which is desirable to many travelers. I didn't realize my mistake until after I unpacked. The room did not smell that bad, but the hallway was atrocious. To the Hotel's credit, they did offer to move me the next day, but at that point I did not feel like packing up and moving. The hotel is decent, but showing some signs of needing updating. Older cabinets, carpeting and cracking grout in bathtub. I agree that not having wireless in the room is a little odd. The room was the standard Homewood Suites layout with nothing to make the property stand out. You do need a car for this location. Nothing around it at all. The breakfast had a nice selection and the evening meals were not bad either. Definitely a "can do" staff attitude as well. I was debating my rating, but as of now, I will still rate it as very good.

“Simply brilliant!” This entire hotel has been beautifully and tastefully updated and our room provided a quiet, comfortable, modern oasis from the busy streets of Fisherman's Wharf outside. The bed and sofa bed (which our son slept on) were very comfortable and the room was spacious, as was the bathroom. While there is no swimming pool at the hotel and the restaurant has limited opening hours, there is no actual need for either. The location of the hotel is perfect, both for the attractions of Fisherman's Wharf and for quick eats - an In 'N' Out burger is on one corner and a Coldstone Creamery (delicious ice-cream) on the other corner of Anchorage Square. It is about a block to both the cable car turnaround and, in the other direction, the streetcar stop and you do not need a car (if you do have one, as we did, parking, although convenient, is expensive as is the norm in San Francisco). We would return to this hotel without hesitation and highly recommend.

“Great hotel, would have given it 5 stars but for one guy on front desk” We stayed here on the next to last leg of our USA road trip. Rooms were great, 99% of staff first class, and they have a great free drinks reception at night. Only small downside. On the morning, I went to my car four times, having been give nthe key to pick up/drop things off - no worries. Last occasion, different front desk guy who insisted on me being escorted to my car, with a security guard who undid my car, etc. This wasted 10 mins or so for me, was a waste of the security guys time and for no reseaon whatsoever, hence not 5/5

“Average Hilton but really no complaints” I stayed here one night for business and had rented a meeting room the next morning as well. Nothing real spectacular at this full service hotel, I've definitely stayed at nicer, cleaner Hiltons and would probably stay here again (if I can get a quieter room with a good ac). I had issues with my ac and it was loud and it drives me nuts when I'm trying to sleep with a loud ac that keeps shutting on and off. That's my biggest gripe so I hope they resolve their ac issues expeditiously.

“High end hotel” The hotel is in a great location and is next to Pike Place Market. I stayed for a few nights and found my stay to be very comfortable, the level of service is high and for that you pay a premium. With the lcak of quality hotels in the area this is a very good choice if you can get a good deal.

“You could see the Space Needle and the next hotel's occupants...” Stayed here since it had a special hospital rate. Not sure how that is calculated but we didn't get the same rate, but still an okay value. They offered a free shuttle to hospital but anywhere else was about 10-15 bucks for a few blocks or to go to a Mariners game or to one of the popular piers. Located down town and just a few blocks from the Space Needle. A few more blocks to major attractions downtown. The ladies that checked us into the hotel were friendly and gave some good information about hotel and it's resources. The morning managers on the other hand were, not quite rude, but frustrating in trying to get them to give information such as shuttle times, wake up calls and checking out. The room is super small. The dresser drawers couldn't open all the way because the queen bed was occupying the same space. Found a random earring on the dresser. Uses deodorizers so if you're sensitive to extra fragrances it might be difficult but otherwise it was pleasant and not overly perfumey. Overall a fair price for an okay room in a great location I'd stay here again because of price and hotel/ hospital shuttle but am willing to spend a bit more for next time.

“Love the location and historic architecture.” Second time staying in this hotel. Love the building and location. Staff was very helpful. Only knock on the hotel is the limited parking means you have to valet, which is time consuming. I've stayed at the Residence Inn next door and they have the same issue, so I'm not blaming them. Just give yourself 15 minutes padding before you have to leave.

“Magical Christmas at The Michelangelo” The Michelangelo was absolute perfection, it made our Christmas in New York memorable. This is a beautiful hotel, from the gorgeous lobby to the large and nicely decorated rooms to the delicious complimentary breakfast (biscotti and Italian coffee, yummy!). The staff are personable and helpful. There is twice daily room service. The hotel is conveniently situated in theater district, which unfortunately also makes it noisy especially at nights. My only criticism is lack of coffee making facility in the room. However, overall I highly recommend this hotel. I have stayed at a lot of hotels in New York and few match the high standards set by this Italian haven. I will definitely stay there again.

“GREAT base of operations” My wife and I and our two kids (ages 11 and 9) stayed here for a weekend. The purpose of our trip was just to enjoy New York City. The hotel was in a wonderful location, in the heart of touristy NYC. In choosing between this property and the Marriott Marquis across the street, we decided on the Doubletree because for about the same price we got a 2-room suite. We all sleep in the same room at night (two double beds), but it's great to have 2 rooms and 2 TVs so we can spread out during downtime. It was a surprising touch that small sections of windows opened, so that we could enjoy the sounds of the city. I was especially impressed by the fitness center. It wasn't big, but was great for a hotel gym. It was almost identical to the fitness center in the Doubletree in Philadelphia I stayed at the week before. The front desk staff, overall, seemed annoyed at life and indifferent to their jobs. By contrast, the Bell Services staff (luggage assistance, doormen) were friendly and attentive. By the way, there was a great sandwich shop just down 47th Street across 7th Avenue, about a third of the way towards 8th Avenue. Made-to-order sandwiches and wraps plus a buffet and loads of cold drinks and bakery items. Not only was everything fresh, but the prices were actually very reasonable, not your typical prices you'd expect in that location.

“Smart hotel right in the centre of it all” Parc 55 Wyndham is located a stones throw away from Market/Powell St BART station on Cyril Magnin St so it is close to everything. If you are arriving by air, the BART should take approximately $8.25 and it's a 30minute ride or thereabouts, when you leave the station, it's easy to spot. Looking over to Market St, you have the Westfield Shopping Centre with all the stores you could possibly need for a spot of retail therapy. The Powell/Market cable car stop is at the end of the line or beginning, however you'd like to look at it, is nearby the BART station and hotel. There are various restaurants in the Union Square area and surrounding streets of the hotel, so there are lots to choose from and you will find something you fancy. As you enter the hotel on the ground floor, you can take the lift or the escalator to the 1st floor to where the reception area is, along from the reception area is the Cityhouse bar and restaurant, the bar have some great cocktails and bar snacks it has to be said. Check-in was of the usual professional standard that one expects, efficient yet courteous. After a long day of travelling from the east coast, we wanted to relax and unwind. The room was located on the 24th floor, we had booked a deluxe king room which was very spacious and afforded some nice city views - namely of the Transamerica Pyramid and a bit of Union Square. There was no complimentary wi-fi available in the rooms BUT, located on the 4th floor at the business centre are a bank of computers where you can check emails etc. There are also 2 additional computers located on level 2 opposite the gift shop, however there was no codes or passwords to enter so it seemed that anybody could walk in off the street to use them. Be mindful though, that there are a fair share of homeless people in and around Union Square, so of course, near the hotel, every city has it's problems but to me, this is something that is very noticeable. Having been to San Francisco on a few occasions, I accept this and don't let this bother me or get in the way of having a good time. The hotel is conveniently situated for anyone who is looking to use the cable car a lot and do a lot of shopping and of course use the BART/local transport. I had stayed at another property on Powell St during my previous visit and most definitely prefer this hotel, so I would consider using again in the future.

“Fancy...and a price to match” Okay, so most Fairfield Inns are slightly glorified motels. Yes, many across the country are being redecorated and upgraded. But this property in downtown Chicago in more like a cross between a fancy Marriott resort and an upscale apartment building. Clean, modern and efficient. I stayed only overnight, but it would be comfortable for almost a week, if need be. Oh yeah, the price matches many other nicer hotels downtown.

“Big but Personal - They found my forgotten laptop!” I have stayed here many times over the years and while it's not my first choice for a New York hotel, I must say that has consistently delivered - and the service is always good. During my last trip, I was in a hurry to leave and left behind my laptop. The concierge called security but nothing had been turned in... As I was flying out of the city in a few hours, I pressed the concierge to check the room immediately - She sent me up with another employee and the nice cleaning lady had taken the laptop and carefully wrapped it in a plastic bag with my room number on it to turn it in to security - she just hadn't done it yet. I was thrilled. The Bull and Bear continues to be one of my favorite restaurants in all of NYC, with equally good service and the lobby and old pictures remind you you're staying in a living part of history in NYC.
“A True Sanctuary” Enjoyed the cool room, the friendly staff and the great location. The bed was comfortable and the room had everything you would need ...

“Couldn't be more convenient, great staff, average rooms” The hotel is connected to Terminal B at the Airport by a walkway. This makes it incredibly convenient for meetings, or just for an overnight stay. You can also walk to the SEPTA train, which gets you to downtown for $7. Buy an "Independence Pass" which gives you unlimited use for a day for $11. The meeting facilities are good, and comfortable. Had a very nice group dinner, white glove service. The public areas are very nice, the room is the standard marriott room.....club chair with ottoman, desk, dresser, no minibar, and a comfortable king bed. The shower was hot and powerful. My main complaint (and suggestion) is that they get WIRELESS INTERNET! This is pretty much the first Marriott (other than Fairfield, etc.) that only had wired internet. Not much help for a tablet user. Given that I am sure they cater to business travelers, this is really expected in a hotel these days. By the way, if unable to walk from the airport, they offer a shuttle to and from. It clearly meets the need, and then some.

“Great location, small room” The room was very nice and in a great location if you are looking to walk on 6th street. I thought the price was kind of high but I booked this hotel very last minute and there wasn't much available in Austin. The bed took up most of the bedroom, I am not sure how big this room was but it seemed very small.

“Good location and value” Stayed here on Dec 2, 2008. Very nice property in downtown. Room was a little tight, but it was just me. If I was travelling with spouse or kids the room would have been small. They also offer a free dinner and breakfast. I skipped the dinner and hit the Cheesecake factory a few blocks away. Hotel is right next to the convention center. Fitness center is very nice. Very clean and newer equipment.

“Great Location & Great Staff!” My huband,our daughters & I recently stayed at the Nob Hill Motor Inn for 3 nights recently. We were completely happy with our stay. We reserved a Junior Suite & the room was large & comfortable. Two Queens & a Sofa Bed, it also provided a fridge, microwave & coffee maker. They also offer free WiFi which was always working properly. We never had any trouble connecting. Included in the price is a continental breakfast, just pre-packaged pastries & juice, coffee & hot cocoa. Free Parking is another plus. We had a car that lived in the garage for most of our stay. We mainly used public transport which was only about 2 blocks to the cable cars and less than a block to the bus stop. Excellent value for the money!

“Great price and great location, huge rooms” I got a really good rate through travel-ticker.com at this hotel. It's located across the street from Carnegie Hall, near two subway lines. Staff is friendly at the desk. Used to be apartments for the church next door. Microwave, sink and refrigerator in the room. Nice amenities. Lots of closets, large bathroom and large room. Flat screen tv. Request a high floor - window air conditioner so the windows aren't total soundproof. Heating is via a radiator and only control is to turn it off. Still too hot, and we had to open the window. Beds were very very hard. No free internet or free wireless internet. Price was great for the location

“Nice safe business hotel” I stayed here for a business meeting. I have no idea about the location, except that it was about $45 by taxi to the airport. This is a very nice business hotel. My room was large and comfortable, and the bed was as nice as anything else I have slept on in similar hotels. The decor was blandly modern - not my taste - it was pretty ugly. I arrived late in pouring rain and was forced to use room service. To my pleasant surprise, the $10 burger was amazing - 12 oz, cooked really well, with great fries and all the condiments. Probably the best and fairest priced hotel meal I have ever had. Also, there is free internet in the lobby to check your return flight - a nice touch, since most hotels in this range ask $10 for the same privilege. In all, a nice pleasant business hotel, with adequate meeting facilites.

“A Rare Good Deal in the Loop” I was excited to win this hotel on Priceline given it's good reviews. It does live up to the reviews. The hotel is bright, clean, and modern inside and out. Hotel staff was friendly during my minimal interaction with them. Our room was large, and appeared even more spacious due to the high ceilings and large bathroom. There is a large stand-up glass shower. We had a king room with mini-fridge and microwave. Our room looked over Franklin street. The only complaint I had was that the room doors slam shut very loudly and can be fairly bothersome if you're nursing a hangover early in the morning. You could loudly hear people talking in the halls. There was also some traffic noise from the street, even 5 floors up. Otherwise, the hotel was very good. I would highly recommend.

“Good, not great, but would stay again” I stayed in 1408 in a regular room with 1 bed. I thought the room was fairly clean (not spotless), which was fine for me. The room isn't the newest, but the bed was comfortable. The wireless wasn't that straightforward for some reason, but I paid $32 for 3 days. It worked fine after I set it up. I also found out that it was cheaper than the Hilton's cost for 3 days too. The only negative was that I heard some music outside at night (10pm) when I was trying to go to sleep on a weekday. That must have been the club or bar other reviewers have mentioned? The in and out self park was a good deal too. The staff at the front desk was great! With the deal I got on Hotwire, it was worth it. I would stay there again.

“Good Homewood Suites” Although a bit expensive, I would reccomend this particular Homewood Suites. With the exception of the top of the TV cabinet, the room was quite clean. It was a bit price, as Homewood Suites go, but this is one of the nicest Homewood Suites I've stayed at multiple Hiltons around the country. The hotel overall looked very modern and the pool area was nice. We had a good experience. Staff was very nice as well.

“Great starting point” Stayed here with family for the beginning of our vacation. Hotel has everything a vacationing family is looking for. Besides all the amenities like a great pool, outdoor basketball/tennis/volleyball/horse shoes court, it's also in an ideal location. The re-energized SeaPort Village is at the hotel doorsteps, as is the beautiful boardwalk along the marina. We also walked to the GasLamp District and a Padres game. The Zoo and Coronado Island are a short cab ride away, so that was easy too. Hotel staff were pleasant and accommodating throughout, and we're responsive days later when we realized that we had forgotten something in the room when we checked out. It was there and staff offered to bring it to us at our next location. Anyway, good choice and worth it.

“Heart of the Theater District Gem” I recently stayed at the Hotel Allegro for a one night business trip. The hotel is conveniently located in the Loop, an easy walk from several "El" stations. I was greeted promptly at check-in by a very friendly front desk clerk who was able to put me in a room even though it was only noon. When I expressed concern about noise from the "El," which runs next to part of the building, she assured me that noise was not a problem, but that she would put me in a room away from the tracks. The room itself was on the small side, as others have indicated, and the bathroom was great for one person, but might be a problem for two. That said, the room was immaculately clean and had everything you come to expect from a Kimpton: an interestingly stocked mini-bar, the animal print bathrobe, and strong WiFi. My only complaint about the room is that the king bed was a bit saggy on one side. Since I was traveling alone, this wasn't a problem, I just slept in the middle of the bed! Overall, I would not hesitate to stay at the Allegro again on a future trip to Chicago.
“Perfect property!” Great location, very nice rooms, the staff could not be nicer.

“Good value and nice location” I stayed here for 1 night with a Contiki tour. I usually stay Best Western so i was interested to see how this would be since it was a tour and usually the rooms are average. The room was nice, I slept well and there wasn't a whole heap of noise even with the lift right outside. There were vending machines right outside the room too which was good when you needed a drink. I ate dinner in the room, which was convenient since it was just downstairs in the hotel. There is an asian style restaurant and they have wraps and fruit too. I had sweet and sour chicken with rice. It was actually really good!!! I was really satisfied with that meal! Location is right across from the park obviously, and it isnt a long walk into the main area of Chicago, so you cant go wrong staying here. Wifi was good. Rooms were spacious and clean and i was impressed with this hotel, especially since the rates were quite high for a best western, but obviously the location and room standard is reason why. I would stay here again, and enjoyed my time here.

“Nice hotel, nice location, wish service were better” Overall this is a nice hotel in La Jolla. The layout is typical for Embassy Suites but we did not notice excess noise from the courtyard. Rooms were clean and reasonable in size. The living area is in the front half of the room, with couch and chair, work-desk, phone, flat screen tv, small fridge, microwave, coffee maker and sink. If you are having an extended stay, you could keep some food/drink in the room but it's not a kitchenette. The bedroom was comfortable with its own flat screen tv and the bathroom was clean and modern. The breakfast is excellent and free, and the service staff was friendly and efficient. The fitness center was nice too--a decent size pool and modern cardio equipment with some hand weights. Our only complaints were the extra (and in our minds, excess) daily charges for what many hotels include for free: $19 for parking and $14ish for internet, and the lack of responsiveness from the front desk. When we complained about the internet charge, the front desk mentioned they had a business center where we could use the internet for free. It's not the same. Also, we had a few issues with our room--the phone in the bedroom would not call the front desk and the bathtub would not drain. We called about both and neither was fixed nor was there a follow-up call to verify the isses had been addressed. The coffee in the room was never refilled. Upon check in, our Hilton Honors membership was not recognized nor does it get you anything other than points. So, if management would encourage their front desk staff to respond quickly and follow up with guests, we would have rated the hotel higher. Otherwise, it's still a pleasant stay.

“Fantastic Christmas thanks to the Doubletree” Having read the reviews on this site I was very much looking forward to my time at the Doubletree. I was not dissapointed. We had booked 7 months in advance, and received a fantastic rate on a conference suite, which was a corner suite overlooking Times Square. The views were out of this world. The room looked "new", good decor, & clean. Bed VERY comfortable. I had been corresponding with the hotel about putting together a "christmas dinner menu" for us. It arrived and was a banquet! we didn't know what to eat first. It was delicious. Whilst we don't usually eat in a hotel, the 3 course meal for $35 was unbelievable value. Other people have commented on the lack of customer service in this hotel. EVERYBODY went out of their way to say hello and make us feel welcome, so we did not experience this at all. Having security check your room key at the entrance, before boarding the lift to go up to reception on the 3rd floor was very reassuring. All in all, a fantastic stay at a fantastic hotel!

“what a deal and what a hotel!!” Absolutely fab stay from the chilled fruited water in the lobby, to the great views, incredible bed, huge well appointed area, and great location!! I had a view of the lake and the surrounding buildings....i could see all the way to the museaum!!The pool/health club area is free and also boasts incredible views. The cozy robes were an elegant touch. Surrounded by construction but i didn't hear a thing....the lobby was quite noisy in the am so maybe request a high room if you worry about that. It truely is "where the river meets the lake" ...and for 109 a nite i was in awe!!

“Stellar location & comfortable beds” I usually stay closer to Times Square, but really enjoyed the proximity to Central Park & shopping. We actually found ourselves taking fewer cab rides this trip since it was so easy to walk to Rockefeller Center as well as Times Square and the theater district. At the end of the evening we really enjoyed the very cozy hotel bar. The rooms were large by NYC standards, and the beds are awesome. The construction noise next door is deafening, however, and it seems Sunday is the only "noise-free" day. Good choice if you are going to be out of the hotel all day, but stay elsewhere if you hope to work from your room.

“Westin delivers again” Westin has become a brand we've learned to trust as the Heavenly Bed & Heavenly Shower are 2 things we can always count on. This hotel has once again confirmed this. The building's main floor & 2nd floor lobby both have a contemporary yet warm vibe. The room along with the bathroom were both quite large & very clean. As always, the shower & bed were up to the usual Westin standard.

“This is my GO-TO location for business in Denver!!” After an awful stay at Kimpton's Hotel Monaco in Denver, I sought out the Embassy Suites as an alternative. I'm SOOO glad I did, because not only did I save money but I actually liked the hotel and their customer service MUCH better! I've chosen this location a few times recently and I've really enjoyed the stays. The hotel is relatively new so the condition of the rooms is pretty good. The breakfast is EXCELLENT and unbelievable for the price! The happy hour leaves a bit to be desired (popcorn??) but that's a minor thing for me. This hotel hits it on all major considerations: cleanliness/condition of rooms, bed comfort, ease of reservations, friendliness of staff/customer service and billing/rates. No complaints -GREAT job, Hilton!

“Works for me” The Residence Inn Time Square is an excellent addition to the area. In the past I have stayed at the Marriott Marquis and the Courtyard Times Square. This place is cheaper and quieter than the Marquis and is on par pricewise with the Courtyard. Of course you get the complimentary breakfast buffet which is customary for Residence Inn. The location is good, you are a couple of blocks away from the subway and not too far from everything in Times Square. The rooms are spacious with a flat panel TV (although sound and picture quality was questionable on mine). The bed was not huge, but very comfortable. The staff is very friendly and helpful. I have stayed in a number of Reisdence Inns when I travel for business and enjoy the evening happy hour. The Happy hour here was ok. There is plenty of room in the dining area. The only thing I noticed was that beer wasn't included as it is at many of the RI's I have stayed in. If that's important to you, then I suppose its a bad thing. The rate was $269, which is alright for New York. But its a good hotel and worth the money.

“Great relaxing family weekend getaway at Westin Copley” Travelled to Boston for a quick weekend getaway from NY and found myself staying at the 1st hotel I stayed in more than 8 years ago when I first visited Boston but instead of my parents it was with my family...Drove in and arrived around 3pm on Friday to a full valet lot which had us wait for about 15 minutes until the valet guy collected our car and info...Went to check-in soonafter and was told our preferred room was not available so we went to kill time in the nearby Copley Plaza mall until they called us back to confirm it was ready. After more than an hour of shopping, I was concerned our room was still not ready and called back to inquire and was told our room still wasn't ready!!? I was very surprised to hear this given I didn't request a special room, especially being a SPG Gold Member but before I could react further, the front desk guy decided to upgrade us to a corner junior suite with 2 queen beds and a river view, which was a very nice gesture. As such, we quickly returned and were relieved to find our room on the 18th floor near perfect in terms of space/view/ and decor and promptly we rested finally after being up all day. Otherwise our entire weekend stay was great as the room and the unbeatable views was thoroughly enjoyed by my wife and infant daughter...The bathroom was a bit tight but we liked the overhead rainshower instead of the typical heavenly shower installed...Our queen beds were as heavenly as can be and the pillows were just soft and plushy enough for us. Room service did a great job cleaning our room and replenishing our water bottles and Starbucks coffee regularly! People we encountered from the front desk to concierge to bell valet were all courteous and helpful to us during our entire stay...The Westin is extremely convenient to walk to the Back Bay station and also well connected to the adjacent Copley Mall and other interconnecting shopping plazas so we hardly had to step outside in the chilly weather. Had a minor issue with the double billing on the valet charges when we checked out but it was quickly fixed in a NY minute! All in all though we will definitely return to stay at the Westin Copley again with my family when the weather is warmer next year for sure. Thanks for the relaxing weekend!

“Fantastic Location, A Peaceful Rest on Embassy Row” We stayed here from a Thursday to Saturday in March. We got lucky with beautiful, even hot, early Spring weather. We were visiting a nearby school and just sightseeing. The location really is superb -- within a short walk to Dupont Circle and new downtown, and just a bit more to the White House area. Massachusetts Avenue (Embassy Row) and the streets to the north are quite charming. The hotel overlooks charming (if busy) Scott Circle. We changed rooms after our first room had no light as it looked directly onto the next building (a negative for at least one side of the hotel). The room we ended up with looked over the Circle -- a beautiful view. The lobby is spacious and comfortable, with the usual free internet usage. The restaurant in the hotel is actually pretty good (but about par with other Marriott locations). The staff was nice and helpful. The space was clean, and the room was fine if basic. The bathroom was not spacious or well designed -- typical of these types of hotels. However, the bed and furnishings were comfortable enough. The best thing is the location for the price. Also, it is a comfortable base for exploring the nearby areas. I would stay here again.

“With a little work, could be great” Spent 5 nights here with my family. Got guaranteed connecting rooms! Almost unheard of anywhere else. Rooms were roomy with a decided lack of storage. Noticed one room had an umbrella but ours didn't. We had two glasses but they had only one? Recently updated and adequately comfortable with the exception of lack of control on temperature. loved the burger bar, Knaves lounge, and the ultra expensive and delicious Norma's. Most of the concierge were quite helpful, but ran into some condescension, hey I'm from the sticks and don't understand mass transit. Only real gripe is when we showed up at 3:30 they said our 2nd room wasn't ready? How is this acceptable and what were you willing to do to compensate us? Never got an answer.

“Excellent all around” If you've stayed at one Hyatt Place you've pretty much stayed in them all--and that's a good thing. Hyatt Place hotels have similar layouts in the lobby, breakfast area and guest rooms and everything is geared toward the budget-minded business traveler or for families. Still, this one was a cut above the others I've stayed in, in service, cleanliness and facilities. The guest room was typically spacious, clean and well maintained, and had a wet bar with a fridge and sink. The free wifi worked well. The fitness room had 3 treadmills and other cardio machines and was pretty well equipped. The setting is a corporate office park, far enough from the highway so there is no noise. There is plenty of parking and Jock n Jill, a sports bar, is a short walk away. I drove a few minutes to Mar Y Tierra for fresh, delicious Mexican food--I think it's a family-owned place. It's a ten minute non-highway drive to the downtown area so if you don't want to pay downtown hotel prices, this is a good choice.

“Fantastic remodel” After a long trip from Jordan to Boston, via London, I was ready for a good nights sleep before heading to San Francisco the next day. I arrived at Logan airport around 8pm, very tired. The Hilton is the closest hotel, located on the airport grounds. I located the hotel board near the exit and called to see if they had any rooms at the Hilton. Thankfully they did. A van was there to pick me up in 10 minutes. Check in was smooth and I was soon off to my room for a much needed rest and shower. When I entered my room, I thought I was placed on the executive floor. (I wasn't) My room had just been remodeled. It is the most modern hotel room I've stayed in, the furnishings, design, pictures, large flat screen HD TV, coffee maker, large king pillow top bed, even the trash container and ice bucket were modern stainless..... the soaps, etc in the bathroom were boutique, actually, the entire room felt as if I was in a boutique hotel, not the usual Hilton. The only problem was I had to leave early the next morning! I wanted to stay in this comfortable, beautiful room longer!

“Great Hotel, but bad check out procedures” The Chicago Hilton at 720 S. Michigan Ave. is a very elegant and comfortable hotel. We had a room with 2 beds and 2 full bathrooms. The beds were well equipped with several pillows, very comfortable mattresses and a wonderful down comforter. Got great sleep in this hotel bed. The bathrooms were very nice as well. They had wonderful modern tile and looked very nice. I must admit I thought having 2 bathrooms for 2 people in a hotel was a bit extreme, but my husband and I enjoyed each having our own bathroom with room to spread out our own toiletries. The only complaint about the hotel is that the check out procedures were annoying. We were given an "invoice" under our door on the morning of check out that didn't show a zero balance. It showed no number at all and I wanted to make sure I wasn't charged anything that I shouldn't have been. We were given 3 options for checkout: on the TV, by telephone, or self service kiosks in the lobby. I tried the TV which froze up while trying to locate my account (twice). Then decided to try the lobby kiosks which were all off-line. Finally just left my keys with the concierge and asked him to let registration know that we were checking out. Never got confirmation that I wasn't charged anything extra. Overall it took us over 20 minutes to try to check out between waiting for the TV, waiting for an elevator and trying to get the kiosks to work. Twenty minutes of annoyance wasn't enough to ruin our stay though. Overall, a great hotel!! Highly recommended.

“Great Atmosphere - Great Staff” I stayed here 2 nights while visiting clients and passing through for connecting international flights. Really the kind of thing i expect from residence inns, excellent! I arrived pretty late on both occassions but the front office staff helped me get checked in super quick and organised some food for me. The daily managers food/beverage hours are great, with a fantastic spread of food M-F!

“One night stay” This hotel caters to those who are flying out of the airport and only need a place to stay for the night. They have a dedicated line for airline flight crews. The line to check in when we arrived in the evening was very long and they didn't have enough front desk presonnel to cover it. We only stayed one night and didn't see much of the hotel. The rooms were average for a Westin. Nothing too special, somewhat older bathroom that looked like it had been remodeled, but was starting to show some age. The rest of the room was fine, but nothing better than average.

“Very nice - Great location - Big room - Recommend” After reading reviews of many Georgetown hotels, I booked Monticello Hotel for two nights in July. Very nice stay. Boutique-style, looks like a private apartment (no pull-up loop but they offer an unloading on-street parking spot). Valet parking ($30/night added to bill). Located almost at the corner of Thomas Jefferson and M Street; fabulous location! No in-house restaurant but the hotel offers a delivery service if you'd like. MANY restaurants and bars within close walking distance. Booked two double beds. Room was large with 4 windows looking out over the street and side (Room 501). Corner room may have added more room. Bathroom is separate with the sink in a separate area from the toilet and bath/shower (shower has a door; sink area does not). Big! Room had a wet bar with sink, fridge and microwave. Also, wine and champagne glasses and cork screw. Beds could be better. One of mine was pretty mushy and low. Bedding was nice. Check the windows to make sure they're locked (this is an OLD hotel; old windows). Umbrella in the closet which I used. Continental breakfast off the elevator (muffins, donuts, milk, coffee, cereal). A previous poster said the elevator was small and it is SMALL. Fits 6 people at most without bags. 4 at most with bags. And VERYwarm when we were there. But it didn't bother us. I would stay again due to the location and I enjoy the smaller, boutique style hotels. We walked to the White House and it was very easy.

“Recently Remodeled with a great location” We picked the hotel as it had a great location on Michigan Avenue as well as a " stay 3 nights get 1 free" promotion. The property was very clean with a staff that was very friendly and outgoing. The concierge was dead on with 3 dining recommendations. One was a local shop specializing in the Chicago "Deep Dish" pizza and he indicated it was favored by locals. The room was on the 17th floor and we had a great view of the lake. The room was clean but was warm and stuffy despite having the thermostat set to 65 degrees. We finally turned off the heat and that seemed to help. Only thing it was missing was a mini bar-but that was a minor inconvenience. we'd definitely stay here again.

“Typical Embassy Suites Stay” This Embassy Suites location was exactly what I would expect from the hotel. Every employee I encountered (front desk, valet staff, bell staff) were very friendly and willing to help. You are about a 10 minute walk to Chinatown from this location (you can practically see the edge of Chinatown if you have a room on the east side of the building). This is nice because Chinatown seems to have bars that are not as expensive as you may find in other, nice parts of the District. But, the one downside to Chinatown is don't expect to eat late (past 10pm) at a restaurant during the week. The fitness center at this location was one of the nicer, on-site fitness centers I have seen in awhile. First, the fitness center is open 24 hours with your room key. There are 2-3 treadmills, about 2 elliptical machines, a stationary bike, nice free weights, various weights for medicine balls, yoga mats and balls, along with a couple other items I associated with a recent trip to the physical therapist. This fitness center overlooks the east side of the building onto the street and you can also see a large (about four block wide) construction site underway just to the south of the building while you are on one of the machines (I saw a crane moving a port-a potty while I was on the elliptical machine... insert joke about what a mess that would be if the port-a potty fell while hoisted in the air). Plus, the cardio machines have televisions attached. This fitness center room is long and narrow, making it nice if you want to do lunges or some other type of exercise that requires more than the typical amount of room you may find in a hotel fitness center. The price was right for my business trip. I may look at staying somewhere else that may be close to other late night dining options (I usually don't get room service, but I do believe they offer it at this location). But this was only my second trip to the District, so maybe the late night dining options I am accustomed to finding in another large city such as Chicago do not exist. My main complaint about this location is lack of wireless internet in the rooms. There is wired internet (which is usually faster than wireless), but I just acquired an iPad, so wireless would have been ideal. Wireless is available in the lobby for a fee (wired internet in the room also requires a fee).
