“My favorite place in Boston” I like this hotel because the rooms are pretty amazing. I like that you can open the bathroom window to get natural light and they provide both a bath and shower. The bath is super clean , unlike most properties with a bath tub , this one actually gets cleaned and is clean when you get there. The bell staff to The front desk staff are excellent and the best is the hotel has very fast elevators. My only complaint is with the room service. I found the food to be average to below average which is a change from previous visits where for example the breakfast was the best I ever had. This last visit the room service was a little below average and the restaurant in the hotel was below that. The "specials" were reheated frozen items instead of freshly made unique items and that the freezer taste to them. Also, in the past you could email the manager for a special occasion (this was my anniversary) and get a response and I mailed the manager 2 times over 2 months ahead of the trip and never got a response back which is unlike every other year. The hotel is still amazing and of my favorites, just a lot less personal and unique.

“Funky, fun and free of pretense.” Stayed here for two nights for a girls weekend- loved the cool vibe! Walking distance from the metro- great lobby with a wonderful, authentic restaurant- food straight from mexico city. Yummy maragaritas and excellent guacamole. Rooms are nothing fancy- but are comfortable and well thought out. Ask for a room that faces the pool area- be sure to check out the great views from the rooftop. The front desk folks are extra helpful- feels like they actually like their job. Check it out!

“The grounds are very well kept.” Stayed for two nights in Apr 24- 26th. Booked on Hotwire for $68.00. We had a bayfront room that you walk onto the patio and into the water of the bay we paid to upgrade to a water front room at check in for an other $35.00 a night. Best of all is there is free parking and with the bay front rooms you park right at your room. The room was a good size and it had a fridge in it. This room still needs to be updated and the shower did not drain very good at all. The room was clean and had a very good a/c in it. It is close to Belmont park and to the beach it is walking distance. The seals at the hotel is cool as well. Overall this is a nice place and will be even better when the upgrade is done.

“An Average Hotel with Friendly Staff in a Good location” We stayed at this hotel while visiting Houston for 2 nights with our two young children. It was conveniently located near the museums that we were going to be visiting so we decided to give it a whirl. The hotel is a bit older and the rooms could use a little sprucing up, but it was clean and the staff was very friendly. We were put into a 2 room suite which was great. We assumed that they had just upgraded us. UHM that wasn't the case. They did remove the extra charges without any argument so I am glad we asked about that. This Hilton doesn't give children under 5 breakfast for free. Just FYI. Most do, but you will have to pay for your kids even if you have Hilton honors coupons. It really wasn't a big deal on the day of the buffet, but they charged us for adult meals on Sunday when they don't have the buffet. The hotel was quiet. There really weren't too many people staying there and you could really just relax there if you wanted. We spent most of our time seeing the sites so we were just happy to have a nearby hotel to rest and sleep.

“Wonderful stays each visit” I've stayed at the Mansion four times, and each time was wonderful. From the time that you enter the lobby the service is attentive and accomodating. I usually stayed after appointments all day so returning to such lovely accomodations was a welcome respite. The food was always wonderful, concierge extremely helpful with great recommendations, and the rooms were luxuriously appointed. The room was always very quiet as well...which is a huge plus for me. If I am going downtown Dallas, this is my favorite place to stay. You cannot beat the the quaint atmosphere of feeling like your staying in someone's home and the courteous service.

“Good Location, Property and Service (Especially Housekeeping)” I recently stayed at the Park Hyatt Washington for four nights for a combination work/personal visit. The location of the hotel is great and close to the downtown, restaurants, museums and nightlife. The hotel grounds are well kept and very clean. I stayed in a suite which was spacious, clean and had a modern decor. The bed was extremely comfortable. The hotel gym is large by hotel standards and has adequate equipment for a good workout. One downside to the physical attributes of the property was that the internet service was spotty at best--both wifi and ethernet. This was problematic because my internet connection kept dropping while I was attending work-related webcasts. Another downside is the noise. Because most buildings don't exceed a certain height in the District, the rooms are relatively close to street level and all of the traffic noise. I believe this is a common problem with District hotels, especially if you are a light sleeper. The hotel restaurant--the Blue Duck Tavern--seems to get rave reviews. I ate there a few times during my stay and it was good, but a bit overhyped. As for the service, it was good and met my expectations for a Park Hyatt. The doormen and front desk staff were attentive and friendly. Everyone was quick to acknowledge and recognize my Diamond status and the perqs that go with it. The Diamond breakfast was great and generous. The only criticism I had with respect to the breakfast is that management should let Diamond members enjoy it wherever they want--whether it's in the restaurant or brought to their room. On some of the days I was able to get my breakfast delivered to my room, but the staff made such a big deal about this and they seemed to have to jump through so many hoops to make this happen. As the Hyatt's top guests, management should let us enjoy our perqs wherever we like as some other high-end Hyatt properties do. In my opinion the highest marks go to housekeeping--they bent over backwards to cater to my needs and did a great job of keeping my room and the property in great shape. Few people realize the critical role that housekeeping plays and I hope that management will reward the housekeeping staff for doing their job consistently well. I'll be back.

“Welcoming and warm, like your own personal club.” We had the opportunity to stay at the Arctic Club Doubletree before and after an Alaskan cruise. We would definitely recommend this hotel to anyone staying in Seattle. Staff: All of the staff members--front desk, bell staff, restaurant workers—were extremely friendly and service-oriented. They all express great concern about customer satisfaction and take steps to ensure that guests are having a wonderful time. Facilities: The hotel is beautiful. It was re-done in 2008. The Polar Bar in the lobby exudes warmth and comfort. The grand ball room is stunning. The rooms are warmly furnished with comfortable beds, overstuffed chairs, flat screen tvs and wonderful pillows. The style is so warm and inviting that I felt at home right away. I had a corner room on the 8th floor and another corner room on the 5th floor; noise was not a problem. The tilework in the bathroom was so neat, I want to use it in my own home. I can’t say enough about how much I liked the style of this place. Highlights: The décor is stunning. Be sure to check out the relief walruses on the outside of the building. Areas for improvement: The elevators were a little slow, but otherwise, I cannot imagine any improvement. Overall impression: Wonderful staff who know what they are doing in a beautifully restored facility make this place a “must stay” in Seattle. Nearby transportation: Downtown transportation tunnel is across the street. Buses run right down Third Avenue. A short walk to the Monorail, or take the transportation tunnel. 20 minutes to airport, 15 minutes to cruise terminals.

“Little gem!” What a little gem in Foggy Bottom! We were uncertain as to what we would find since we paid only $99 for a suite in D.C., and we felt our spirits lag when we saw the aqua paint color showing through peeling paint on the outside of the building, but all changed when we walked inside and met the friendly staff. We were a little uncertain again when we received a key and entered a room that was already occupied, but the staff explained the computer didn't show the room occupants were still there and they apologized profusely and sent us to another room which was empty and comfortable. The bed was outstanding and it was so quiet in the neighborhood that we received all the rest we needed after walking all around D.C. during the day. The only downside was breakfast. Overpriced and not so good. We ate there once and it cost $37 for a mediocre meal. Staff was friendly but the food was dried out and not so pleasant. Breakfast aside, we will stay at the River Inn from now on on our frequent trips to D.C. Fantastic location, wonderful room and great staff.

“WONDERFUL HOTEL!!” My husband and I recently spent six nights at the Hotel Palomar. There was an initial problem with the reservation but it was handled promptly, professionally and much to our satisfaction. As with most Kimpton hotels the room was impeccibly clean and nicely appointed. Daily the room was cleaned perfectly, was done very promptly and caused no inconvenience to us. The nightly turn down service is nice. Although our room looked out over Market Street, we heard no noise, nor did we hear other guests inside. The beds were great and the linens are fantastic. Newspapers that were requested were delivered early each morning. As pointed out in previous reviews the lobby is very, very small (about three adults can sit in it). The staff at the desk was very professional, but we did not have any dealings with them except for check-in and check-out. This hotel is a great peaceful escape after running around San Francisco all day. The location is great and the lobby exits on Fourth Street right at a very busy bus stop. We were able to walk to Union Square several times, the Curran Theatre and Yerba Buena Gardens. The BART Powell St station is less than a half a block away. The Westfield Shopping Center is right next door. I am not a shopping-type person but that is a must-see. What a gorgeous mall!! The only negatives we felt were the size of the fitness room (very small with one treadmill and limited weights). I know you can go to another fitness facilty down the street but it is much more convenient when you can use the hotel's fitness center. We missed the nightly wine gatherings that we have enjoyed at other Kimpton hotels. It is so nice to relax with other guests, but the Hotel Palomar does not offer that amenity. The restaurant dinner menu was very different -- not what most people would eat. It is obvious they know this since the dining room is very small and never crowded. We had breakfast there a couple of times and it was very good. We would definitely recommend this hotel for the high quality and great location that it has. Kimpton does a very nice job taking care of their guests in a subtle way.

“great hotel and location” We decided to stay at this hotel because of the location, price and because it is close to our daughter. The hotel staff is very friendly. Our room was clean and very spacious, except for the bathroom which is a little on the small side (but hey... we're in downtown san francisco). The wine reception every afternoon is great! My husband only comment is that the tv channels aren't HD. We would definately stay here again.

“A little too modern for Boston, but quite nice none-the-less” A friend and her husband were stopping in Boston on their way to a New England and Canada tour. She wanted to get together and hoped I'd show her Boston which, I confess, I don't know well. The main reason that I can't figure out which way the roads go... at least not easily. So I suggested I meet her in Boston and we take a Duck Tour (to which I've given a rave review in another post). I'd already suggested she and her hubby find a hotel near Boston Common, which she'd agreed to do, but wasn't forthcoming with the name of the hotel. Thus, I was on my own as far as choices went. I opted for The Revere because the location (and price) were very very good for Boston. I arrived at the hotel via taxi, and was disoriented right away: there are concrete walls and seating areas an no visible front desk from the door I entered. I had to ask where to check in. But check in was fine, despite the lack of warm decor, and the room was great: wonderful view of the city and the bay, big space, comfy bed, all the amenities except a stocked 'fridge. No prob. I met my friends in the lobby as previously agreed, although not sure at all where the "proper" lobby was. I finally found a seat with views of the main doors (there are two I think) and happened to catch a glance of my friends as they entered on of the door (good thing I wasn't reading or I'd have missed them). There's a HUGE cement circle thing in the lobby which block the views and seems incredibly uncomfortable to sit in, so I was outside of "the cage" in a chair I hoped would work. It did. But know this: there are not plants in the lobby, and nothing to make you feel you've arrived at a cozy place. For Boston, it's out of sync: where cozy and old and history are already there as the springboard for interior decor choices. But the designer, in this case, might have been from Afghanistan, although he or she forgot his or her rugs. I WON'T dwell on the miserable lobby any longer. The room was scrumptious. The smell of vomit in the hallways (which I'd read about in other reviews) wasn't on the 23rd floor. Nor did I notice a "wonderful smell" in the lobby. They all smelled about the same. But back to the room: the bed was fabulous. Yes, the shampoo and conditioners are bolted to the wall, so you won't leave with any goodies. Still, it's a nice stay. The restaurant is across a "U" shaped driveway, and serves up very nice food for lunch and breakfast. The hotel itself is right across the street from a Legal Seafoods, which is where we had dinner, and that was perfect. So all it all, it was a good stay. If they'd convert the lobby to something more... well... Boston-like, it'd be all the better.

“Wonderful hotel” I stayed here for one night for a short business trip with meetings in Dallas downtown. This was part of the Starwood Luxury Collection, but having been dissappointed many times before, I did not expect much. Turns out I was way wrong. This was probably one of the best Starwod properties I have stayed in the last year. The hotel is about 40 minutes from DFW airport in downtown Dallas. Check in staff was extremely courteous and actually escorted me to the elevators (instead of saying "turn left, then right..." as the front deks often does). The front deks area is not huge, but has a farily open seating and meeting place. The room was spacious enough, with a big glass wall on the outside, a 42" flat screen TV, and terrific lighting arrangements that allowed you to adjust the brightness in various parts of the room. The bed was very comfy. Everything was clean and well maintained. The bath and toilet were divided into two separate rooms, and the sink area was separate. This can be useful for couples staying in the room. There was a complimentary bottle of water, and toiletries were top notch. There was a nice collection of magazines in a rack next to the toilet bowl! Internet cost the usual $12 to $14 a day. Just one downside. The area around the hotel isn't exactly swanky. There are a lot of office buildings, but the place really seems to die down after 5 PM. There is a Neiman Marcus and a decent Mexican restaurant next door, but there's also a boarded up building.

“Convenient location” For the price, you can't beat the Magnolia. The location is ideal. We had the queen suite on the 17th floor with a decent view. Beds are comfy. Kitchen was well stocked. Lots of nearby restaurants/bars. Neiman Marcus is very close in case you want to shop. Convenient to all major Dallas freeways.

“More Positives Then Negatives” I can see where people would pick up on the age. There were a couple of crimescene-like stains on my carpet that I tried not to contaminate with trace evidence by stepping in. The WiFi shuts down if too many people are in the hotel. And the hotel was PACKED so it was pretty spotty. And I was on business, so THAT really didn't help. The guys from engineering did something like re-boot the transmitter and it popped on for about 24 hours. They were the ones who acknowledged that the system is deficient. You don't want to be on the northside. You get train AND highway noise. Upside? Beautiful atrium. Very very nice employees. Great buffet and...wait for it...and GREAT non-chain steakhouse on the property.

“Monaco was great” I stayed with my teenage daughter and niece at the Hotel Monaco June 30-July 2. I printed out directions, we were coming from the Field Museum, but after 1 turn the street was blocked off for Taste of Chicago. So, it took us about an hour driving around downtown in Friday rush hour traffic stuck behind a bus, but we finally found it. We opted for the valet parking at 36 dollars a night. It seemed high, but when I checked with a nearby parking garage the fee was 27 dollars for 24 hours, so the extra few dollars was worth the convenience. Check in was painless, and our bellman was very pleasant. I thought he was going to unpack our luggage for us! The room was huge, two queen beds, etc, but no window seat, which was my determining factor for choosing this hotel over it's sister hotel, the Burnham. I called down to the front desk, and the very efficient clerk assured me that I had a really nice room and I should stick with it. If i wanted to switch to a room with the window seats, it may not be as large, and I may not get two beds. I didn't feel like making a fuss, so we stayed with our non view room. As I said, it was quite large, with 2 small tables with chairs, two comfy armchairs, one with an ottoman, and the cabinet in the corner with tv, honor bar, and cd player. The bathroom was especially large also, with nice size tub and shower. I was happy to see the magnifying makeup mirror, but the bulb must have been burned out. The extras like cotton balls and cotton swabs were provided, that was a nice touch. I signed up for the Kimpton customer loyalty program, and was pleasantly surprised to receive a tray shortly after we got to our room with a personalized card, a bottle of Fiji water, and a biscotti, as well as a complimentary menu item should we go to the restaurant. The beds were comfortable, one had a down comforter, one had a blanket. The decorative pillows were kind of stained and gross, but we always just toss those to the side as soon as we get into the room anyhow, so no big deal. We faced out onto an alley, and the first night I was awakened by garbage pickup in that alley, never heard a peep from other guests though. I didn't take advantage of the wine reception in the evenings, or Starbucks in the morning, but other people seemed to be enjoying them. We were in the room the first night when the turn down attendent came, so she just left ice and candy. The second night we got back late, and I was expecting to come back to a dark room. I was pleasantly surprised to come into a dimly lit room with the relaxation channel on the tv, and a chocolate surprise on the pillow. We had a problem with the toilet not flushing efficiently, and practically before I could hang up the phone, an engineer was there, plunger in hand, and had the problem taken care of. When I returned home, I received an online survey to fill out. I dutifully fill those out, as I have gotten them at other hotels I've stayed in. I was honest, and to my surprise I got an email back from the manager saying he was sorry my stay wasn't flawless, and should I stay there again, make my reservations directly with him, and he would do everything in his power to make sure I got my 2 beds plus the window seats. That was refreshing. I've had major problems at other hotels before, and no response back from management. To have this personal reply to my minor disappointment made the difference for me between looking at another hotel among the many fine ones in downtown Chicago, or going back to the Monaco. To sum it up, the location was great for the theatre, 3 blocks to theatre where Wicked is playing. Garrett's popcorn is right next to the theatre, Marshall Fields is right there.... We'd planned on going to Water Tower place for shopping, but ended up in that same little area of State Street every day. There was plenty to do. So, try the Monaco. The staff are so friendly and efficient, and their commitment to customer service is exemplary.

“More than we bargained for” Another of our last minute getaways and we booked a room based price and ratings. It was about 10 miles to downtown (that's why four stars from us) but in a very nice business area. The location did not turn out to be a problem. Check-in was quick and Lori was very, very friendly and helpful. We got to the "room" and realized it was a mini-suite. A sign on the door said that this property was a "host hotel" for model suites for sister brands. Our room turned out to be a "model room test" for future Embassy Suites designs. We were guinea pigs! The room design was very modern and trendy. We had a great wet bar with cabinets, microwave and mini fridge; very, very comfortable king bed with plush pillows and adjustable LED reading lamps; 46" HDTV on a swing arm; comfortable work/dining table with an ergo chair and two conventional chairs; a full sized couch with two ottomans; a small dressing nook with built in drawers and mirror. The bathroom was large and one space. The sink had plenty of counter space, but with the dressing area near the bed, two or even three people could easily get ready at once. There was a nicely tiled walk-in shower with both a standard shower head and a hand-held shower near the built in bench. Everything was a modern design, which leads to our very minor complains: the couch had square, wood arms which look very nice, but are equally uncomfortable. My wife's concern was the way the TV stuck out when turned toward the bed. We occasionally get up in the middle of the night and this is an obstacle. So why risk it, stay in bed, right? The breakfast food was good with the usual selections and included eggs and biscuits and gravy. Everything was fresh. The lady in charge was having a hard time keeping up with the crowd, but she did what she could. The dining area itself was kept clean and was very spacious, well-appointed and comfortable. More tables were available on the attached patio, but it was already too hot to eat outside. There was a small, basic business center (computer and printer), a workout room, and a very small pool. There's a small selection of snacks, drinks and sudries available for purchase off of the front desk. We used the free wi-fi, which was fast and secure. There are plenty of good dining choices nearby or within a short drive. Based on the staff and common areas this would be a good choice for most anyone, although the pool area is probably too small for kids to have much fun. Room 506 was atypical for the property, but is very nice for even an extended stay, whether business or pleasure.

“Nice hotel, cool lobby” This is a typical W hotel, which, for us, made it a LOT of fun. It's got a great, hip lobby with lots of stuff going on all the time. They have a good restaurant, and it is right within walking distance of lake Michigan and Navy Pier. The Mag. Mile isn't too far (several blocks), so it is a little trek...but if you're young and don't mind walking a lot, then it is doable. The rooms are fantastic. The beds, as always are wonderful. The view was good, as well. Overall, if you can find it at a good deal, I'd recommend it. It was a little pricy though.

“International Class Hotel” I must confess this booking was an exercise in nostalgia as much as anything else - I stayed in this hotel while in college, with my late parents, 17 years ago when it was still a Kempinski property, and wanted to see what it would be like, especially given an attractive rate on hotels.com. I, like other reviewers, had stayed in other downtown SF properties and found many of them wanting in some crucial aspect (room size, service, etc). The rooms and floorplate were from an earlier era, when luxury hotel rooms (and some of the people staying in them!) were not so big. However, I was curious to see whether my fond memories of a stay long ago were justified. When I arrived, the doormen smartly attended to my baggage, and escorted me to the front desk, where there was no line. I was given a room key. I suppose because I'd booked on hotels.com perhaps I was not given a particularly choice room, on the 2nd floor overlooking the street, and not far from a function room where a party was being held. The noise from the hallway was noticeable but as a sound sleeper at that point on east coast time, it did not prevent me from dreamless sleep. The insulation from street noise, thankfully, was almost complete and unnoticeable. The room itself was smallish but tastefully decorated, with attractive lighting, cozy bathrobes and linens, and a modern bathroom with some nice Molton Brown toiletries. With a nod to high Asian service standards and amenities, it offered complimentary shoe shine service, of which I availed myself. Early next morning I hit the gym, which is open 24 hours. The room itself is not large or impressive (it is something of an insulated tent on a higher floor) but it had all the latest equipment and was equal to my needs. Without winter outdoor workout gear I certainly had no intention of going outside for my run! The service quality overall was excellent, and of an international standard. It also offered all the services you would expect of an internatonal hotel despite the small size of the property. The location is pretty unbeatable, you could even take the subway to the hotel from the airport. I would stay again, although I probably wouldn't be willing to pay the rack rate.

“A true New York City hotel” Most out of town tourists stay in one of the concrete masses in Time Square for its proximity to everything touristy. But if you want a true sense of NYC and are interested in staying in a brand new, 5 star hotel....I recommend the Cooper Square The service here is impecible. The ambiance is first class, and you feel like you are staying with people who have "been to NYC before", versus cattle call hotels full of tourists and kids. You are a 10 minute walk to Greenwhich village, 5 minute cab ride to Little Italy restaurants, and there is a subway stop less than 200 yards away. Overall..a. great stay and I'd do it again if had the opportunity

“Great Old Hotel” Great prices for this beautiful old hotel. We always use the Camino Real as our base when visiting Southern New Mexico, and El Paso. For a small price you can include breakfast, which we always do. Great front desk, extra large rooms, good beds, and excellent AC.

“Nice Older Hotel in Great Location” The room was clean, extra-large and very comfortable. Their staff is very pleasant and helpful; the breakfast deal is terrific; we had a great stay. Our room was on the front of the hotel and, even though we were on the 11th floor, it was a little noisy but it didn't prevent us from getting a good night's sleep.

“The Coolest Hotel in Downtown Phoenix” Phoenix is a city of resort hotels -- grandes dames like The Biltmore, The Royal Palms and the Phoenician, and downscale "family" places which are no more than a bunch of nondescript rooms around a pool. As such, a critically important segment of the hotel market was ignored in Phoenix -- the interesting design hotel that had no claim to grandure, but saw itself as more interesting a destination than the typical Marriott familyplex with free eggs and bacon for the kids. Ignored, that is, until the Clarendon came along. This is a well-designed hotel with all kinds of interesting touches -- from the sliding light screens on the windows to the quality and quantity of the in-room magazines. Chic lighting? Check. Plenty of closet space? Yep. Awesome outdoor rooftop lounge? Oh yes. And the pool! Large, cool and smack-dab in the center of it all. Also recommended -- by locals I was visiting -- is the restaurant. Interesting art in the public spaces, comfortable beds, strong showers and quality toiletries finish off the superiori physical attributes of this property. Last but not least is the excellence of the staff. Friendly, young and always eager to help -- including the late night shift, which is typically staffed at most hotels by junior-junior, inexperienced and not-all-that-helpful sfaff. I was pleasantly surprised from the friendly "Welcome!" to the "Thanks for staying with us!" I can't recommend this hotel more. I am a many-miles-traveled businessman and would be pleased to call the Clarendon home at the end of a long work day -- luckily, though, this trip was all fun and the Clarendon was a large part of that outcome.

“Best downtown hotel. In the middle of it all.” Used to live down the street. So when we went back for the weekend, We knew right where we wanted to stay. Awesome staff. Great bar up on roof. Free passes to roof and skip lines if hotel guest, a big plus. Rooms were great. Right by red and brown/ orange line trains and short walk to state street shops / mich ave and millennia park. Can't wait to stay again soon!

“Great Hotel!” A very beautiful hotel if you like modern design (like we do). The restaurant, RICE, is wonderful and all the hotel staff were very friendly and polite. The beds are also very soft, though not quite as nice as Westin or Sofitel beds. Three downsides: the pool is very tiny-- not a good choice for families; music from the lounge plays ALL NIGHT LONG and you can hear it in the perimeter rooms; the front desk forgot to give us our wake up call on the morning of our flight home. Hotel is 2 blocks from the water/port and 3 blocks from Horton Plaza (great shopping). A great hotel for couples or business travelers.

“Consistently good hotel” I have stayed at this hotel a few times and keep coming back. The rooms are comfortable, the shower heads are at a height that works for a 6'5" guy and it is walking distance to a number of great restaurants. During my last stay, I found a billing error after I checked out. I contacted the hotel and they put it right immediately.

“Highly Recommend this property!” I needed to attend a conference at the Washington Hilton approximately a mile North of this property (uphill). They were booked on the first night so my original plan was to book the Topaz for one night and then move. But, the price was better than the Hilton conference rate and the website description intrigued me. After reading the reviews here I changed my plans and decided to stay at the Topaz for the entire stay. I think I made a very smart choice! First, I asked for a high floor and a quiet room and I was given just that. The room faced the street and had good windows. I thought the room was larger than many urban hotel rooms I have had in the past. It had a desk with a study area in the L-shaped floor plan. There was a sofa with a coffee table. There was a large armoire at the foot of the bed and the TV could be rotated so it was viewable from the bed or the sofa. There was another easy chair and the bathroom had two rooms--a seating area at a dressing table and then the room with the fixtures. The shuttered closet contained robes in wild prints as well as a safe. I appreciated the safe and used it. It was easy to operate. There was a well-stocked mini-bar with much more than food and drinks. There was a razor, toothpaste, shaving cream, a first-aid kit, an intimacy kit, etc. There was a small bag of stones on the bed with a note about totems and a folded horoscope. All in all it was funky as promised but also designed to provide a relaxing retreat....and it had free internet!! I did not utilize room service but I did stop at the bar and get drinks that I took to the room. The staff was friendly, calling cabs when needed, and answering my questions. The room service is a little spartan. I wanted eggs one morning and they only have cereals, pastries, and granola on the menu. Just next door inside the Old Tabor Inn there is a restaurant that serves a full breakfast so I walked over there. The best find is the Iron Gate Restaurant directly across the street. There you dine under a grape arbor covered by an old grape vine. It is a very beautiful setting and the food is superb. I put the privacy card on the door and it was honored. No one called me or knocked on the door. I loved that. If I need a place in the Dupont Circle area I will return to the Topaz. I highly recommend it to you. If pressed, the only negative thing I can say is that the elevators are very slow. Other guests remarked on this as well when I boarded it and others were on board, but all things considered this is a minor inconvenience. On this trip the Topaz helped me to slow down and I needed the respite.

“Would be a great place to live” Very small, very intimate place. The guys who run it are very friendly and accomodating. The rooms are nice and have a boutique feel. You don't have all that extras that would come with a larger hotel, but that's okay. Wish it was a little less expensive. Nice, comfortable. Because it's so small there's a very nice personal and intimate quality to staying here that you wouldn't get anywhere else. It's one of a kind in NYC. Recommended.

“Perfect location” Everything that you've come to expect from the Hilton chain. Decent sized rooms for New York City. Ask for something away from the elevator as it can get noisy. Can't beat where this hotel is situated, walking distance to all the sights and subways

“Five star stay - Probably the best hotel experience I've ever had (ROOM 957)” I've been traveling for almost 20 years, and never have I been so lucky to stay at a true Five-Star hotel (The closest in my distinct memory was The Crowne Plaza in S.F./Union Square in 1994). My family was treated with respect by a truly professional staff starting from check-in on Sat. 09/19/2009 through our check-out yesterday 09/25/2009. We had two separate rooms booked through United Vacations - My parents had Room 955 and we had Room 957, with Stunning views of the 'new' Downtown Boston skyline and the new BFD HQ's building across the street (The occassional Fire Engine Siren didn't bother us). Honestly, It was fun to watch the Fire Dept do their thing and I went across the street to meet them (They allowed me into the garage and see the Big Red Engines =) Very nice). The rooms were simply luxurious from the wonderful work desk and flat screen TV to the nice bedding and inviting all-glass shower stall in the oversized bathroom stocked with amenities...PROBABLY THE FINEST HOTEL EXPERIENCE I'VE EVER HAD!!! To add what other reviewers have noted, this hotel will charge you for basic goods (However, in a strange way my parents wanted a coffee maker and were willing to pay for one, the hotel provided one to their room at no charge...) I used the bathtub and used it a container to stock my sodas and milk and fill it with ice (Saved $$$) The parking is CRAZY at $39 a night, but we knew it and had no problem with in-and-out privileges (We made the valet folks work O.T. =) We're from L.A. and this was our first trip to Boston, but we honestly made one mistake from the very start - we had a rental car. We didn't need a car as the 'T' took us to many places (We used the car for Cape Cod and Salem, MA) Next time, TAKE THE 'T' and leave the car at HERTZ. The Pool and Spa was great, as for the RumBA Bar we didn't experience (But quite noisy as we were coming back at night). In closing, I was impressed with InterContinental Boston and If anyone in Management is reading this, Our family wants to say 'Thank You' for making us feel welcome for the six days we were in Boston. Keep Up The Great Work. Peace - JG

“Nice stay at a convenient midtown location” We got our room off Priceline for a great price but I learned pre-arrival that their base room is a Superior Queen which doesn't sleep our family of four. This isn't the hotel's fault because Priceline only guarantees hotel rooms that sleep two but this was unfortunately my first experience with a hotel whose lowest class room is a two-person, queen-only room. I guess this isn't entirely unexpected as it is New York city. Anyhow I called the hotel and they informed me of a $60 upgrade to the Deluxe Double Double. But given that we were staying over Memorial Day weekend and I knew hotels in midtown would not be fully booked, I elected to chance an on-arrival upgrade. The hotel is still fronted by a lot of scaffolding--probably construction from its neighbors. The lobby is small, but new and contemporary. Upon our very late arrival, I was greeted by a guy who was lukewarm friendly at best. We did however get our Deluxe Double Double. I requested a view of the Empire State Bldg and was given a 7th floor room, but "the view" was only of the top few floors and the spire. I certainly don't consider that a view but then again, we got a good price on the room and was upgraded for no charge so I can't really complain. Besides, if you want a great view of the ESB, just go to the roof-top lounge/bar--spectacular view! If you want a room with a view, request something closer to the 20th floor on the front of the hotel. As for the room, it was pretty small overall but we were happy to have two beds for the weekend! Unless our double double was unusually small, I'm not sure how others can say this hotel has rooms that are large by New York standards. Our rooms during our last stay at the Milleninum UN were huge compared to this place. With all that said, the room was very clean, nicely decorated and furnished. Comforters and sheets were wonderful, and my wife really liked the bed and pillows. And the hotel is on a relatively quiet street so noise was not an issue. The bathroom was a standard size but with a large shower area. The sink had very little counter space for toiletries--especially with four of us. Strangely, the large shower used a half glass partition but was left completely open at the far end. You can't avoid getting wet reaching across the shower head to turn on the water! And when showering, the water unavoidably splashes out onto the main bathroom floor. Not sure what Einstein designed this but this was not a good design or execution! Free wi-fi is nice but it surprised me that a new hotel still bothers to install a mini-bar. I don't know about you, but I think mini-bars are an insult, and I don't understand why hotels in the 21st century STILL waste valuable room real estate that could be used to create more drawer or refrigerator space just to try to rip customers off for a $8 beer or $5 candy bar! The free breakfast seems to give a nod to European tastes. In addition to the typical continental breakfast (i.e. fruit, breads, bagels, cereals, yogurt, orange juice and coffee), they also served some small sandwiches such as prosciutto and cheese, and some type of chicken salad on a roll. They just need to add espressos and cappuccinos! The exercise room was small but well-equipped with modern treadmills, elliptical, bike and even a sauna and shower. Except for check-in, the hotel staff's customer service was consistently attentive and courteous. Overall, we had a very enjoyable stay and I would recommend The Strand Hotel for it's excellent value and service in a great midtown location.

“We had a great stay!” We stayed for 4 nights at the Capital Hilton, Washington and had booked an Executive room with access to the Club Lounge. On arrival we were upgraded to a Junior Suite. There was no view but the room was very spacious and well decorated. The Club Lounge was good with internet access and refreshments throughout the day. The staff were very friendly and the location is superb, within walking distance to everything. We took a two day pass on the Double Decker Sightseeing bus and this was worthwhile as we had easy access to the whole city. We needed to travel from Washington to New York and used Washington Deluxe Coaches which charged 20 dollars one way. The coach stops just around the corner from the Capital Hilton and in New York heads for Penn Station, it was an easy 4 hour transfer. We took the advice of other reviewers and tried some of the recommended restaurants, the only one I would personally recommend is McCormick and Schmidt which served superb seafood and is located almost opposite the hotel's front entrance. All in all a great stay and if we were returning to Washington it would be to the Capital Hilton.

“When all you need is a clean place to stay” The Jane is an interesting hotel and lives up to it's micro-hotel status. The abundance of wood in the decor gives it the feel of an older ship and seems to blend in with the atmosphere of the surrounding Manhattan area. Although the rooms are about the size of a large walk-in closet and equipped with a twin size bed, they are clean, comfortable and full of storage space. A flat screen TV and DVD player is found in the room as well, along with an adequate heating/cooling system. It's definitely the kind of place to stay if you are not looking to spend a lot of time in your room and really just want a clean place to stay at a low cost. The communal bathroom is located down the hall with two showers, two sinks, and two toilets. The facilites are definitely clean and I found it no real hassle to walk down the hall to access them. The staff was exceptionally friendly and accomodating to all of my needs.

“Rescued by the Hilton Garden Inn” After booking into a horrible well-known chain hotel in Chelsea, we moved the next morning to the Hilton Garden Inn. The room was twice as large as the previous room. The bed was comfortable and the furnishings looked new and well maintained. The breakfast offered was delicious! The restaurant in the hotel is one of many French restaurants owned by a single company. They are all excellent restaurants. The staff was friendly and took care of all of our needs quickly. When I informed the front desk that the lock wasn't working on our room door, someone was there to fix it in less than 2 minutes. Great timing! The conceirge was able to get outstanding tickets to a musical for us. Overall, a PERFECT stay. I wish I would have booked with this hotel from the beginning! Sadly, we couldn't stay longer because the hotel was booked for the last two nights of our trip to New York.

“Excellent Stay” I was fortunate to stay at the ES Convention Center Denver location while attending a conference and found it be a delight. Here's my summary points; *Complimentary breakfast buffet was great and the customer service provided by Fernando was very good. *Bartender Jim at the Manager's Reception took care of my well drinks; too bad the bar didn't have any collins mix, but I made the adjustment. *Suite and bathroom were spotless, well-maintained and clean. *I'm a Hilton Gold member so my Wi-fi access was complimentary, and the valet parking is $29 a night, but I took a cab and avoided the parking issue because the convention center was just 10 yards away. I frequent the ES brand hotels quite a bit, and I wish that other older hotels would be refurbished (Las Vegas-Swenson, Las Vegas-Convention Center, Temple- AZ) like your Denver location. I would defintely recommend this one!

“Nice place, friendly staff” Stayed here for one night in October before a wedding. Overall, it was a nice stay. I arrived after midnight, and still had no issues quickly getting a shuttle from the airport. Driver was friendly and helpful. Check in was efficient. I got a regular king size room on the concierge floor. Room was comfy -- beds were new and recently remodeled. It's obvious the property is a little older in style, but with the remodel, it isn't that bad. Room was clean and the air worked well (always requirements in my book!) Conceirge lounge is wonderful. They do eggs, bacon, sausage and potatoes along with the regular cereals, breads, and fruits. Service there is great --- very friendly. I've stayed there twice now and have been really impressed. They also have a nice indoor pool in the courtyard ---- we used it on prior visits and it was nice as well --- although like all indoor pools, the smell of chlorine is really strong. Nice place, clean rooms, conveniet to the airport. I'd definitely do it again.

“Nice midtown hotel for families and business.” I stayed two nights at this Sheraton. The rooms have all been remodeled and lived up to there expectations. There target audience are families, business and midtown tourists. However, I changed hotels simply because most of what I wanted to do did not involve the Midtown area. We went to go stay in SoHo where everything was closer. The club lounge was very plentiful and clean. The front desk people were great as well!

“Fantastic Place to Stay” DC has a number of phenomenal Kimpton hotels, and I was recently fortunate to stay at the Rouge on a business trip. Not surprisingly, the experience met with the already-excellent standard that Kimpton Hotels always live up to. The property is unique and interesting; as the name suggests, red is a decorative motif throughout the lobby as well as the guestrooms. The staff at the desk were kind, efficient and knowledgeable about the neighborhood. I'll definitely be back!

“Great Location and Hotel!” Booked this hotel through Priceline using their bidding method of booking and was a bit concerned after seeing the results. We have been to Chicago countless times and had never noticed this hotel before and some reviews we read online weren't too good, but this was great place to stay! It's in a great location in the heart of downtown. An relatively easy walk from Union Station. Close to several L stops including the Blue and Red lines as well as the Loop. Walking distance to Millenium Park. Staff at the hotel was friendly and helpful. They have self check-in kiosks, but because we booked through Priceline, we were unable to use them. When we arrived in the morning, our room was not yet ready, but the hotel has a baggage check that allowed us to store our bags while we hit the town. One of the nice things about this hotel is that it offers free purified water to all guests. There are water stations on every floor where you can grab a bottle and fill it (or refill it) with purified water from a dispenser. A nice perk and refreshing to not have to dish out $2 at a vending machine. Layout of the hotel was a bit odd as it is very long an narrow with little alcoves of rooms branching out from the long main hallway. Rooms were smallish, but nice, clean and well appointed. The bed was very comfortable with nice linens and comforter. The wifi worked well and the room even had interesting reading material as there were 3 or 4 books on the shelf above the desk including a book of firsts (world's first subway, first hamburger, first internet address, etc.) that we had a lot of fun browsing. There's an English style pub next door to the hotel that seemed quite popular. We stopped for a couple of beers there before heading back to the train station on the day we left, but didn't eat there. The hotel lobby was comfortable and welcoming -- comfortable furniture, free maps and brochures for Chicago, coffee station and even a chess board. Would definitely stay here again! Glad Priceline allowed us to discovery this place.

“I was impressed! Great location, service, and amenities.” I stayed in the Omni Fort Worth for two nights/three days. It is impressive from the moment you walk in. The front desk people were exceptional in their service. The beds were very comfortable and the linens were true quality. The hotel is clean and impeccably maintained. The location is directly accross from the Convention Center. You can walk to many restaurants, or chose from one that is within the hotel. From DFW Airport, it was about a 35 minute drive. I would definitely stay here again if returning from the area.

“Historic and charming, with the right touch of modern” In San Francisco for business, I couldn't have been happier with this hotel. The Westin announces itself well before you get to it as it towers above Union Square. From the outside, the front building of the hotel - which is the original dating back to 1904 - looks pretty majestic, followed by an even larger tower behind it, where the newer rooms are. The lobby has more than a touch of the history that this hotel has been through, including everything from old-world chandeliers to glass case displays of old hotel restaurant menus. Adjacent to the front lobby is a much more modern and sleek sitting area featuring the entrance to an equally modern and sleek restaurant - Michael Mina - which looked like a place to be seen. All told, you feel like you're in a place that's both old San Francisco and hip. My room was maybe a touch nicer than the standard Westin I normally stay in, with slightly sharper and more modern fixtures and design, a very attractive bathroom and shower, and a little larger than I usually get. I liked the location in that it's literally in the heart of Union Square, and is near to a number of restaurants and areas you're likely to want to see. It isn't, however, right next to some of the other nice areas to hang out in - Russian Hill, North Beach, or the water etc - so if you're looking for those areas specifically, this may not be your choice. But Union Square has plenty to offer itself. All in all, I'd certainly stay here again, and I'd recommend it for both couples and for business.

“Loved it - best service and huge room” This is a terrific hotel. We stayed during the epic heat wave and still had a great experience. The room (1047) was huge and clean. The bed was comfortable. They were extremely accommodating with all of our requests (for crib, microwave). When they didn't have something, they took the time to follow up and explain why and see if there was anything else they could do to help. The doormen were so friendly -- they seemed to recognize us every time we came back. The pool area was tiny but still fun. The complimentary wine in the lobby is a nice touch and they create a nice environment. I really cannot say enough about how friendly every single employee was toward us, and how quickly they tried to answer questions and help with anything we needed.

“Great Room Second Time Around” My family and I had stayed at the Doubletree a few years ago when we took the Ohio Bar Exam. The room was very spacious which was great because my in-laws met us to watch our daughter while my husband and I took the Bar. Last year while we were in Columbus for an event we stayed at the Hilton and I really wasn't that impressed with the room so when we had to return back to Columbus in December '04 I decided to try the Doubletree again because the Hilton was so expensive. The room was still great (my in-laws met us again to watch two kids while we were gone). The only drawback is that there is no pool. If you want to use a pool you have to pay for a one-day pass to an athletic club. I would have considered taking my kids there but I don't think the club was even open on Saturday. This was disappointing to the kids but there are two TVs in the room so they were satisfied to hang out and watch TV in the bedroom while the rest of us hung out in the living area.

“Excellent accommodations and service” Beautifully rehabbed property on a quiet street in Kalorama area located equidistant from the Dupont Circle, Adams Morgan and Woodley Park neighborhoods. Arrived before the published check-in time - front desk staff were able to get me an early check-in after I ventured out to explore Adams Morgan for an hour or more. I would definitely stay at this hotel again.

“Good Times in room 306.” Past negative reviews on this site are not reflective of our experience in room #306 of Hotel Blake. The mixed reviews do lead me to believe that room conditions can vary. Positive Points: 1. Price - I paid $101/night Canadian. I got this as a package deal on a well-known travel web site. We stayed at the hotel during the March break (week of March 10th, 2008). 2. Size - We couldn't believe the size of our room! We had a King sized bed, a nice bay window with a bench/seat (and a bench at the end of our bed), more than enough space for open luggage, and a super-sized washroom. You can do jumping jacks in this bathroom! There are two sinks, and a large shower stall. 3. Style - It is refreshing to be in a botique style hotel - this gives it charm and character, something you don't get from other cookie-cutter chain hotels. Take a look at the pictures. 4. Location - Everything is within walking distance. Yes, it is located in the southern part of the Loop, but it did not take us long to walk from one end of the town to the other (e.g. from this hotel to the John Hancock tower). It is also close to a couple of transit stops. We took the El train from the Midway airport, got off at the Library transit stop, and walked half a block to this hotel. Negative Points: 1. Internet not working - it is well advertised that this hotel has a free internet terminal available for guests. Therefore we made a conscious decision to not bring our heavy laptop with wireless internet. Well, the hotel internet terminal was out of order during our entire stay. I was annoyed enough to voice my discontent a couple of times. In response, they let us use their own staff computer behind the front desk. Bravo! 2. Ridiculous phone charges - the list of services in the room leads you to believe that you will not be charged for out-going calls placed on a calling card. Well, when we checked out and got a bill for over $20 in calls, we learned otherwise. However, after some more ‘voiced discontent’ (including a reminder to them that we wouldn’t need to be placing these calls if their internet hadn’t been down all week) they dropped the charges. I commend the hotel staff for turning these two negative points into positives. Other hotel tips and tid-bits: · You get some Bath & Body Works goodies in the bathroom (see pic), and they replenish. · Our towels were replaced everyday, unlike some other reviews. · The deep-dish pizza place across the street, Edwardo’s, is really good. And the Starbuck’s across the street is handy. · The exercise room on the 2nd floor has a great panoramic urban view. · If the internet isn’t working when you stay at this hotel, just go to the beautiful library on the next block where there is free internet and many terminals.

“A fine little spot to stay” We came to San Francisco for a pre-Christmas visit with our two teens. We booked the Orchard because of the reviews, the location and a great deal on Hotels.com. Four nights in two rooms -- one King room connecting to 2 Twins. As requested we had connecting rooms and an upper floor. Our rooms were also ready when we checked in around 11:00 a.m. which was much appreciated. Rooms are nicely sized as are the baths. We had nice views facing Bush street and heard only the occasional siren... no sound from other rooms, other than housekeepers in the hallways. Cleaning and turndown were always done while we were out -- nice timing. Everything was clean and linens were good. The lobby is drab, and small - a real turn-off for all of us, and the dining room, while nicely decorated, seemed to have a limited menu and very slow staff (friendly tho'). We ate breakfast there once and chose not to return. The location if terrific for everything -- hikes to Grace Cathedral for the holiday lights, Powell Street Cable Cars, Union Square, great small restaurants, Chinatown -- everything.... We would recommend and would consider returning.... but we also like to try new places :).

“spectacular view & so much more” nice staff, clean property, great location & spectacular views (the Lakeview in West Tower is at the end of the hallway and thunderstorm rolling in was incredible; my riverview room was also just terrific you should ask for the Murphy bed room) - hard to ask for more

“Awesome New Hotel” This was my first time at the IC Times Square and all I can say is WOW !!! I avoid the Barclay and normally stay at a SPG hotel while in NY but this hotel changed my mind... Incredible!! The hubby and I did a short weekend had to use up tons of PC points I had stacking up. We decided to meet in NYC and so here we are. I am an RA and was upgraded to a beautiful suite even though they don't have to do that on points and what an incredibly beautiful suite it is, Huge for NYC standards. Stunning views. The hotel is simply beautiful overall and though the lobby is smaller it is still very grand. Restaurant / Bar is great and service overall has been as good as the Willard, perhaps even better if that is possible. Not many IC's surprise me but this one did. I can not say how pleased I am with this hotel. It is so much better than I was expecting. I have no problem at all recommending the IC Times Square to anyone looking for a great hotel in the heart of NYC.

“Cute little hotel!” Stayed at the Andrews for 4 nights and had a pleasant stay. The hotel is just two blocks from Powell which made for a short walk from the bus/cable car. The room was small and our bathroom was a decent size. We had room 604. There was noise from the road/nearby restaurant but it wasn't unbearable. The walls are a bit thin but luckily our neighbors were quiet. The heater was putting out heat even though it was off but it never got too hot in the room. The decor was charming and the staff (with the exception of the night auditor) was very friendly and accommodating. The continental breakfast was just outside the door around the corner, that, along with the evening wine reception were nice treats! We would definitely stay there again!

“Exceptional views, excellent location” This is one of my 10 favorite hotels. I love the harbor view and proximity to great restaurants, Pikes Market. I had a corner room with the extended balcony. Amenities are all typical Marriott. Too many 'No's' though from the property. No suite upgrades, breakfast, no weekend concierge - I did ask already knowing internet was free to lighten my conversation with the operator. The suite upgrade I quickly got past - I like corner room views and mine was exceptional. Marriott truly appreciates elites worldwide and this certainly absolutely from the front desk :)

“Grand hotel in a grand city” There is a reason why this hotel is the flagship property of the Fairmont Hotel chain. The moment you walk into the lobby, you are transported to what hotels were like in the past. Positively sumptuous. We stayed on the 7th floor of the tower, and we had no complaints whatsoever. From our room, we were able to see the corner of Powell and California, where two of the cable car lines intersect. The Powell St. line took us on one end to Fisherman's Wharf, and the other to Market Street, taking you through Union Square. The California Street line took us down to the Ferry Building at the Embarcadero. While I wouldn't use cable cars as a primary means of transport (make sure you either buy a 1 day or at least a 3 day MUNI passport), being on a cable car is much more enjoyable than walking the steep hills of SF. This is a prime consideration as the hotel is at the top of Nob Hill. Our room was very large, with probably the biggest bathroom I have seen in a hotel that wasn't part of a 5 star resort. The bathroom was lined with marble, and had a huge shower and separate bathtub, along with a semi-private area for the toilet. The king bed was quite comfortable, and there was ample room for a desk and sitting area. There was a 32" LCD TV, and the channels were all quite clear. If there are things to complain about: $50 a night for parking, and then 14% occupancy tax is charged to make the total nightly cost $57. For some reason, the maids were compelled to turn the temperature on the thermostat to the lowest level on the dial (50F, and set to cool), when the temperature outside was never higher than 60F the days we were there. We did not take advantage of any of the other hotel services like the restaurants or room service other than getting coffee at Caffe Centro on the parking level. There were too many great choices for dining that are close by, either in Chinatown or Union Square.

“Great Stay...Restaurant Fantastic” We stayed at the Adagio for 5 nights and would highly recommend it. The room we were given on the 6th Floor was very spacious and quiet. My husband even commented if we brought our two kids along we would not have been cramped in this room. The location is convenient, it did seem close to shady neighborhood, but we just didn't venture there. Several good places to eat nearby, but make sure to try Cortez. We didn't expect much from a hotel restaurant but the food was one of the better meals we ate in SF & we went to several high end places. We had great drinks (love the cucumber gimlet) & snacks one night & it was so good we went back the next night for dinner- equally as delicious. The staff was friendly & accomadating even recognizing our 20 yr anniversary with wine & chocolate. We would not hesistate to go back there again.

“Would Definitely Stay Here Again” I decided to spend 2 days in San Francisco at the end of a conference trip and arrived after 9 pm. First impressions of the location was not so good, probably because most of the shops and restaurants were closed. However, the staff on duty were very helpful and understanding - special mention to Joseph at reception who was excellent with his friendliness and recommendations. During the day, I found it the hotel a very convenient base for most of SF's North Beach attractions. In fact, early morning at Fisherman's Bay, before the arrival of the tourists, provided an interesting contrast to the hustle and bustle of mid-day. I was pleasantly impressed by the decor of the club room floor, especially the corridors which had sort of an art decor look. My room was extremely comfortable and quiet although I was a little surprised that the in-room safe utilised a key lock rather than electronic lock. Breakfast was usually a crowded and somewhat noisy affair with plenty of tour group participants and independent travellers. Nevertheless, a very reasonable option compared to the other hotel chains in the vicinity.

“Great hotel, a few minor "ehs"” I stayed at the Intercontinental as part of a conference in Boston and had a fantastic rate ($189/night). Upon arriving, the bell staf was exceptionally helpful with my luggage and directing me to the registration desk. My registration took longer than usual, mainly because I was having credit card issues. The hotel is within walking distance of the Seaport World Trade Center; they are building the area up so it's not the desolate destination it used to be. I didn't venture out too much to see what restaurants were in walking distance because it was very cold outside. The room was outstanding. Spacious, modern and very clean. The bathroom was enormous for a hotel in Boston, including a deep tub, glass-enclosed shower, and plenty of counter space. What was most appealing was the opening between the bathroom and the sleeping area. There were opaque doors that could be slid closed for privacy and the opening was above the king sized bed, but it opened up the room so nicely! Granted, I was solo for this trip so it being open wasn't an issue. The work area was outstanding. A large desk that had plenty of outlets was a relief since I was there on business and had to setup my printer and laptop, etc. However the $14.95/day for internet access was frustratingly outrageous. Housekeeping was very good and I didn't have trouble with them knocking at odd times. Room service was good, always giving me a time when they were going to arrive. Within the hotel, there is a sushi bar, a rum bar, and a bistro restaurant that is open 24 hours. The sushi bar is nice but very expensive, the regular bar is very loud and usually packed, and the restaurant was surprisingly empty. However, the food at the restaurant was outstanding as well as the service; the prices were high as well. I also had a business meeting there that I planned with their staff. The food was outstanding, the meeting room great, and the staff really worked hard to make this small, simple meeting go well. The reason this hotel doesn't rate a full five stars: * 14.95/night for internet is outrageous. * there was no guest services book in my room but it did have a room service menu. I had no idea where the business center or the gym were or their hours. I had to ask a few times. Finding the business center was a bit tricky since the signs weren't all that helpful. It's a small thing, sure, but not having that info handy was annoying. * the business center. Wow. This is NOT run by the Intercontinental, instead contracted out. The fees they charge for delivery boxes was the highest I've had to pay -- $85 for four boxes. Yes, one of them was heavy but it had rollers! The staff ranged from helpful to belligerent. The hours for the center were NOT posted outside the door. I tried to drop off packages on a Sunday morning because I had been told they were open at 8 a.m. Wrong. They opened at 10 a.m. I managed to flag down a person who worked for the Intercontinental to help me but the person didn't seem all that interested in assisting a hotel guest. Still, I would definitely stay here again if I were attending a conference at the Seaport.

“Very Good Hotel” I booked the Holiday Inn I-95 by mistake, intending to book the FL-9A Holiday Inn, so we were prepared for a disappointment after reading TripAdvisor comments for this hotel. We were quite pleasantly surprised. When I checked in, I commented that some guests mentioned that in-room wi-fi access was slow or non-existent. The man at the desk checked us in to room 106 instead of 510 because he knew the wi-fi signal was stronger in that area, and he was right: the signal strength was "very good." We could look out of our window and see our car parked next to the window. Location The hotel is ideally located next to I-95. It took about 15 minutes in rush hour traffic to reach Ruth's Chris Steak House in the Crowne Plaza Hotel right on the waterfront. The river view and the meal were excellent, and parking was free. The hotel is not far from Deerwood Shopping Center where we found Mandaloun Restaurant that served delicious Lebanese food. We chose the advance booking rate without breakfast. It seemed a good value, although others said they had received much lower rates on Priceline. The freezer in the refrigerator in the room was cold enough to freeze our ice packs. We were granted a late chekout at 1:30 pm when we expected to return from a Segway tour of the Kingsley Plantation. The man at the reception desk had a problem unlocking the computer to check me in but the problem was resolved the next morning. The electricity went out in the neighborhood over a 45-minute period beginning about 8 p.m.. We assume it did not happen often because the hotel did not provide candles. Battery-operated emergency lights went on in the lobby and halls until electricity was restored. It appeared that the hotel's main line of business was hosting conferences and meetings in the numerous meeting rooms. We were sad to find that there was no coffee available in lobby, probably because this was not a Holiday Inn Express. There was a coffee maker and microwave in the room, however, and both worked very well. I suspect that different wings have different levels of service. Our 100-wing had good Internet and a very good room.

“Overall nice but.......” Great location just outside the busy and congested city but only a couple of minute drive to all the city has to offer. All in all, very nice. Big rooms, very clean, great lobby, very helpful front desk employees. Close to a lot of shopping, restaurants, theaters. All right at your door step. The negatives are just a few. Paper thin walls where you can hear people in the bathroom next to you. I heard a whole conversation of where the couple next to us was going to go to dinner. Also, no fans in the bathrooms. And, no refrigerators in the rooms. Old style tube TV's. Was kinda surprised about the refrigerators and the TV's since this is an mid-to-upscale type hotel. Self-parking in $15 per day which always upsets me, but what can you do. It would be different if this were right down-town but it is kinda in a suburban type area so why charge for parking. Oh, you have to pay for the internet in your room too. I think it was somewhere between $12-$14 per day. It's not a cheap hotel, I don't know why they have to nickle and dime you. But, all in all, I would probably stay here again since the location is great for me and what I go to the city for.

“Old world service with a modern flair. Loved it!” I booked this hotel for $75 on Hotwire with mid-level expectations for one night. Totally blown away. Arrived on a Sunday night. Gave car to valet ($51/night). Lobby was a social people watching scene with swank music. Check-in was smooth and easy. I asked for an upgrade and was told no free upgrades to 3rd party bookings. Upgrade to suite was available at a cost. I passed since only 1 night stay. I asked for a nice, quiet room away from noisy housekeeping and ice machine. Received room 10-120. Room was huge with 2 beds. Felt like 400 square feet. Newly renovated last year. Bell hop told me some rooms are very small so I totally lucked out! Service from start to finish was top notch. Everyone had a smile on their face. Always spoke with great respect and made us feel welcome. Ordered room service at 10:45 PM. Arrived in 1/2 hour. food was so-so. Had pancakes in Lockwood for breakfast. Very good food and very good service. Strong coffee. Hotel is right on State Street shopping. FYI - Rooms on floors 15 and below were renovated last year. Rest were done 5 years ago. For the price, it was a great bargain! Only complaint is bathroom is small.

“Great City Hotel” I have stayed in a variety of Chicago hotels but for value and location the Springhill Suites Downtown River North is hard to beat. For those arrriving from ORD it is a short straightforward 5 min walk from the Blue Line direct from the airport. Check in was good and I had a corner suite on a high floor. Room was bigith a seperate sitting area. The bathroom had a double wlak in shower. The bed was really comfortable and I slept really well. Hotel has a great location with most attractions within walking distance or accessed from the L. The great advantage of this hotel is that the rates are often significantly less than surrounding hotels which makes it great value. Definitely be back !

“In the heart of the Financial District” I've stayed at this hote many times since it's only a block away from the Transamerica building. On my walk to the office I have a choice of 3 difference Starbucks and 2 Pete's so everything is right here. Lately when coming to town I have been staying at the Omni, which is just as close. My last stay at Le Meridien several years ago was unpleasant because the staff was on strike and picketing out front. But it's been a few years so I decided to give them another try. I would say I was pleased with my stay. The bar in the lobby is convenient for meeting up with other colleagues who are also staying in the hotel. The concierge was deadon in suggesting a sushi restaurant in North Beach. The room was modern contemporary in design but comfortable. My favorite part of my stay was all of the movie choices on the television. If only I had the time to watch one but I've never seen so many good choices. My tips: Request a room on the upper floors with a bay view. The way the windows are designed, everyone has a corner window view and sunrise is breathtaking. If you can't find a good rate online, call the local number. They will work with you.

“Much better option than it looks” The hotel has a nice location in Michigan Avenue, just infront Nordstroom and Hugo Boss. Walking distance to any place in Magnificent Mile. Staff is friendly and eager to help people. I stayed in a suite, and even when the decoration is not my favorite style, you have all the confort you might require in a upscale visit to Chicago. Try the breakfast at this hotel, it's simple but the dishes are delicious.

“A grande old dame” This is a real winner if you can afford it off of Union Square in the heart of downtown SF. Great views from the upper floors. Quiet, except for the ding's of the cable cars below. A bit of the old and new hotel parts - so I'd recommend a stay in the "new" tower overlooking the square. Close to everything in SF - from Market Street to Chinatown and right on the cable car line. Dont plan to catch the cable car in front of the hotel - as it'll be full of "tourists".

“Comfortable hotel, good rooms” I stayed here on a recent 1-night business trip to Chicago - it was my first visit to the hotel. The room was good, efficiently laid out with simple, functional attractive decor. There is enough room for a playpen or pack-n-play if you are travelling with children. The room offers a microwave, small sink and refrigerator and a small store in the lobby offers a variety of convenient items. The bathroom was client and the shower was good. The desk is well-fitted with outlets and an ethernet line. Slower speed internet is free; if you want to watch streaming movies you'll have to buy the upgraded internet service for $9.95. On the negative side, there is not enough light (a common problem) and the sofa & chaise lounge was too uncomfortable to sit on very long. The towels are thin and course (again, not unusual in this price band), and the automated wake-up system didn't work. I had a later flight so I didn't miss it but it was inconvenient. When I mentioned this while checking out the room clerk offered me 2,000 extra Marriott Reward points for the inconvenience.

“A suite for the price of a room....” Always difficult to find a good price in a great town as San Antonio so we decide to drive to Austin by the Highway I35. Along the Hwy, lot of motels indicate their prices on great lighting signs and we decide to stop at the Howard Johnson at $42 ... but it was not the good price( about the double...) Just on the side Travelodge indicated $39 and, at the desk ,it was not too the good price and finally it was $65... not really happy of that, one more time but the surprise was when we entry in the room (N°160), it was a SUITE.... What a space, a saloon, the comfort, clean, coffee etc... What a surprise, a good surprise and a good deal for the price. Good breakfast and wifi.

“Nice Hotel” The hotel staff were very courteous and helpful at check-in. The hotel was nicely decorated. My room was nice and clean. I had a loud neighbor so I requested a new room. They were very quick to get me a different room without any problems. This room was also comfortable and clean. The only issue I really noticed was that even though I manually turned the air conditioner down before I went to bed, I woke up and it had reset itself back into the 70's, which was too warm for me. I didn't eat at their restaurant so I can not comment on it. Overall, not a bad hotel. I would stay there again.

“Jacksonville Marriott up to par” I make frequent trips to Jacksonville on biz, and I think I've stayed at almost every hotel in the Metro area! Marriott is very consistant, and this one is just what you would expect from a Marriott hotel. (There is also a Marriott Hotel at Ponte Vedra Beach in Jacksonville at Sawgrass [where the TPC is played].. that one is a little pricey, but it's also above the expectations of a standard Marriott and just blocks from the beach.) However, the Jacksonville Marriott is up to par. A lot to do in the area, just a couple exits from Jacksonvilles best mall, the Avenues. Not far from the Tensiltown area of Jax, just a few minutes from Downtown and the Landing.. steps from Dave & Busters.. also pretty close to the beaches.

“Superior Hotel in Upscale Union Square” After spending several nights in a competition hotel up the street, I finally had to throw in the towel and say, "enough is enough." I walked down the street to the Westin St. Francis and walked directly up to the front desk and talked with a very friendly clerk. I explained my situation and asked if there were rooms available. I am a government employee and was on official business, and explained as such and asked if there were rooms available at the government rate. The clerk was more than helpful and was able to assist me. I explained that my family would be joining me on my last night and asked for a family friendly room. She said she would put me in a "special" room that she thought I would like. Needless to say, I was put into a HUGE room that was way more than adequate and way more than what I am used to while traveling on business! My only regret was that I hadn't stayed in this hotel the previous days! The staff at the Westin St. Francis were all more than helpful in helping us and making special accommodations that I had requested - a cot, a refrigerator, etc... The only down side of this hotel was the parking rate - at $49/night, I was a little discouraged. If I were traveling on my own, I would have looked for parking elsewhere, but since I was being reimbursed, it was alright. The bed was more than comfortable and it was the best night sleep I had gotten in almost a week! The only thing I can complain about is that my conference didn't last longer!!!

“Great stay! good location, comfy rooms with fantastic views” I came here for a conference (five nights) at the Hynes convention centre across the street. When I arrived, they actually reduced my rate from 560 dollars to 360 a night because I was staying with a group. They didn’t have to do that (since the group rate rooms had sold out) but I really appreciated it. Everyone was helpful and friendly. The staff constantly saw the big picture and did everything possible to make you happy. My room was on the twenty first floor with a panoramic view. The room was perfectly clean, renovated and the bed was very comfortable. The bed faced three huge windows (floor to ceiling overlooking most of the city)The view was great and the walls seemed sound proof. There was a heavenly double shower in the room (2 jets one on each side) which would be amazing for couples so someone isn’t constantly left out in the cold but was fantastic for one person as well. What an incredibly decadent experience! There’s a Starbucks in the hotel and free internet access in the business lounge but not in the rooms. Sometimes the hotel staff is nice and will give you the access code for the internet in your room. Ask nicely and they generally give it to you. They only disadvantage this hotel has versus the Sheraton is that you actually have to cross the street rather than walk through indoor connections.
