This may be a minor factor in cold or rainy weather. The Westin is also connected through indoor skywalks” but is substantially further 10 minute walk from the convention centre than the Hilton. If you want to zip back and forth from meeting to your room stay here or the Sheraton The only negative was that the panoramic rooms have poor heating in the fall due to a design flaw in the heating coils of the vents. Apparently this is not an issue in the winter when the entire building is heated but is a factor in the fall before central heating is turned on. They sent an engineer right up to make a few changes but it didn’t help much. If you get cold easy and are staying here in October or early November you may want to choose a standard room and forfeit the view. Otherwise they are more than happy to offer an extra comforter. Once the conference, catch a tour bus across the street. You can buy tickets at the hotel concierge. I strongly suggest “Super Tours” over the others because you get a 2 day pass and bonus tour of Harvard and choice of cruises for around forty bucks. There is a great seafood restaurant 10 seconds away from the hotel named “Summer Shack” you can get two whole soft shell (sweet) lobsters for 30 bucks! If you want to head to the huge indoor mall, Hynes convention centre or Copley place just cross the street into the Sheraton which is connected to these structures.

“Hilton on O'Farrell St.; Tower 2 room; review and suggestions” I have a confession to make. I hate San Francisco. But just for the first day. By the end of a week I usually fall in love with the city all over again. Arriving at SFO is a hassle. Finding the sky bridge to the air train to the BART train, and then figuring out the crazy BART ticket machines is always a challenge, no matter how often we visit. Arriving to a downtown San Francisco jammed with summer visitors and then waiting in the long line at the tiny kiosk for MUNI passport tickets adds to the first day frustrations. Which is all the more reason to treat oneself to a really nice hotel room, like ours was at the downtown Hilton. A quiet, comfortable, and conveniently located hotel room is a great refuge from the craziness of the streets below. Especially when it is available at a heavily discounted price on the internet (more about that later). Some people prefer venerable old hotels for their local color. Others prefer trendy boutique hotels for their urban chic. We prefer four star, big box, business class hotels for their worldwide comfort and reliability. The San Francisco downtown Hilton is located on O'Farrell Street (between Mason and Taylor) a few blocks northwest of the Powell and Market Street BART and cable car stations, which is a convenient transportation hub for cable cars, buses, trams, and subway. The hotel is within easy walking distance of the Union Square and Market Street shopping districts. It is a longer walk to the SOMA district and Moscone convention center. It is a short tram ride to the Civic Center museums and concert halls. It is in the middle of the theater district. It is also near the Tenderloin district, which lies between Union Square and Civic Center, a typically American juxtaposition of urban wealth and poverty. As in other cities, the homeless and scruffy street people are generally harmless, but the hotel maintains a reassuringly visible security staff. This Hilton is huge. It fills an entire city block and has several separate towers of varying ages. Even though we had reserved and pre-paid a standard room, we were given a nice 14th floor room in the business class tower-2. An upgrade to a city view room in a higher tower would have cost $75 more, so we declined the upgrade. Best of all, our kind receptionist (Nathan) let us check in early (11 am) after our pre-dawn flight. At the end of our stay we were also allowed to check out late (1 pm) for our afternoon return flight. That is more generous than at most hotels. This review is based on our tower-2 king room. I do not know what rooms are like in the other towers, although they are probably similar. Some rooms surround the 16th floor outdoor swimming pool deck, which is filled with families during the summer. Our room was a bit larger than average, about 300 square feet, and was decorated in pale gold with burgundy accents. Furnishings were in a modern Federalist style. The king bed had a wonderful mattress and ultra-fine linens. Bath towels were extra large and thick. Room amenities included a coffee and tea maker, a mini-bar, an iron and ironing board, a wall safe, a flat screen (but not HD) TV, a large desk with an internet plug, and an armchair with reading light and ottoman. The travertine and tile bathroom had a single sink and a tub-shower combo. There were no bathrobes or slippers, no shaving (adjustable) mirror, and no bedside reading spotlights. A small table near the armchair (for drinks) would have been nice. A USA Today newspaper was delivered to our room on weekdays. The windows did not open, but the climate control worked well, and there was a small fresh air vent below the windows. Our room was wonderfully cleaned and restocked by our housekeeper Arnel. We always leave several dollars with a note each day as a tip for housekeeping rather than waiting till the end of our stays, and this seems much appreciated. We did not use room service or eat at any of the hotel restaurants. The room service menu was limited and rather expensive: soups $12, sandwiches $24, and main courses $36. The breakfast buffet was about $30. These prices sent us to other nearby dining options, which I will describe later. The hotel staff was uniformly friendly and efficient. We had one question each day for the concierge staff, and they were eager to help. They (rightfully) give priority those waiting in line, so our phone calls were occasionally answered by voice mail or placed on hold at peak times. In a hotel with 2,000 rooms this is understandable. The hotel public areas are attractive and quite busy. Although there are lines at the reception desk, they move quickly and one can easily check-out by phone. Hotel parking rates are high (over $50 per night I believe), but the huge parking structure across the street on the north has lower rates. Even if you do not have a car, be sure to stop by the Hilton parking garage entrance (in the southeast corner of the building) to see the decorative and humorous murals -- they are great homages to the San Francisco scene. As I mentioned, we enjoyed our stay at the downtown San Francisco Hilton. Our only disappointment is that most hotel chains (Hilton included) are surcharging and over-pricing more and more amenities, just like the airlines do. For example, use of this Hilton's fitness center is an additional $15 per day for hotel guests. An ordinary candy bar from the room's mini-bar is $7. (At Trader Joe's on Bay street near Fisherman's Wharf we bought two bottles of wine, a loaf of sourdough olive bread, a wedge of brie, a cantaloupe, and a quart of strawberries for the price of two Hilton candy bars). Any personal item forgotten in the mini-bar results in a $12 "cleaning" fee. An internet terminal in the business center costs $24 per hour. Savvy travelers can avoid such high prices and surcharges, but it would be nice not having to worry about being ambushed by them (I always check our folio well before check-out time to assure no mistakes are being made). The price of the room itself was very reasonable since we bid (blindly by hotel location and class rather than identity) on the Priceline website. We paid a non-refundable $85 plus $15 in fees per night for our stay. The Biddingfortravel website documented even better bargains for other weeks during the summer. We often travel for pleasure: so far this year we have vacationed in Paris, Hawaii, London, Shanghai, Chicago, and Vienna. Priceline provided great hotel deals in each location (except Paris which was a disappointment, and Shanghai which we booked directly to assure a convenient hotel location near the Bund). Large business class hotels with excess capacity benefit by selling rooms on Priceline, and we are happy to purchase them whenever we can. As a price comparison, for our travel dates in San Francisco, the usual large internet booking sites were offering the Miyako at $99, the downtown Hilton and the Mark Hopkins at $109, and the Stanford Court at $119 per night (all plus 15% tax and all discount rates non-refundable). Generally, the hotel websites have higher prices, and their "best available price" often is not. For those interested in San Francisco sightseeing and money-saving options, read on: SFO airport transportation: the BART train is still the cheapest option from SFO to downtown at $8.10 per person each way (allow 60-90 minutes for the journey, depending on waiting times). Surprisingly, the SFO BART station has three employees standing about, but they do not sell tickets in the station. One must use the ticket machines (cash or debit or credit card). These machines are bizarre. They automatically start at $20 and like a "Dutch auction" one must reduce the fare by repeatedly pushing dollar and cents buttons to bring the fare in line with one's destination, then push the "print ticket" button. Each passenger must have his own ticket to enter and leave the BART system. Half price tickets are available for seniors and disabled, but one must find a BART agent in the international terminal to purchase one, and they are sold in high denominations (much more than the airport fare) only. Go figure. Any public transportation in Europe or China is easier and more user-friendly than BART. Buses and cable cars: The best option for travel within San Francisco is the MUNI system, which includes buses, cable cars, trolleys, trams, and subway. One, three, and seven day MUNI "Passport" tickets cost $11, $18, and $24. Since the cable car alone costs $5 per ride, these tickets are a relative bargain. Seniors over age 65 can purchase a $15 monthly pass instead. Passport tickets are available at MUNI stations and at the Powell and Market Street sidewalk kiosk or underground visitor center. A MUNI map of the city for $3 is essential to use the system efficiently, since not all bus stops have a map. Sightseeing: The best deal anywhere is the series of free guided walks offered by SFcityguides, a volunteer organization sponsored by the public library. Their website lists the walks, which cover almost every neighborhood and hidden gem in the city. There are usually several walks offered each day. A donation (most participants give several dollars) is requested at the end of each walk to offset their office expenses. We have taken more than a dozen of their walks and have never been disappointed. Free venues: We always enjoy the Ferry building (bus #12 or the F-tram) and its thrice weekly farmers markets. The #28 and #29 buses stop at the brink of the Golden Gate bridge, where one can walk over the bay and along the coastline for fantastic views, if there is no fog. Golden Gate Park has a nice free arboretum and rose garden (in season) near the de Young Museum. The nearby Japanese garden is free for the first hour on some mornings. The huge new downtown public library in the Civic Center area (F-tram) has 15 minute free internet access and occasional free programs. A walk along Stockton Street in Chinatown is like visiting an Asian street market. Some museums offer free admission during the first week of each month -- check your guide book for listings. Fisherman's Wharf is free but junky. The nearby Hyde Street Pier, however, has nice free views of old ships and a nearby free visitor center with park rangers. Food options: We always start our day by taking the Powell Street cable car or bus #30 to Pacific Street just west of Stockton Street in Chinatown for dim sum at Y. Ben (#835) or Dol Ho (#808). The former is a larger, better option for those new to this Chinese tradition. Just take a seat and point at the plates of food you want as they are rolled by. You will be charged by the plate, and we have never been able to eat more than $7 worth per person (each plate is about $2). Our evening meal is usually a picnic in our hotel room. There is an expensive gourmet market in the basement of the Nordstrom (Westfield) shopping center on Market Street near Powell. We prefer Trader Joes or Safeway grocery stores -- check the internet for locations near your hotel. We usually stop at one on our way back to our hotel at the end of the day. Near the downtown Hilton: The Parc 55 Hotel diagonally southeast of the Hilton has a tasty and inexpensive Thai restaurant in its northwest corner (enter from the street level diagonally across from the Hilton parking garage entrance, or from the Parc 55 lobby). Most meals are around $7 and they are open from 11 am to 10 pm. An older restaurant across the street (Thai Siam) has the same name, but we have never eaten there. The west side of the Parc 55 building has an internet cafe which charges $7 per hour (as opposed to Hilton's $24 per hour). A donut and bagel shop is located across from the southwest corner of the Hilton. It looks clean and good, although we have never tried it. Mini-markets and liquor stores surround the Hilton, but we prefer the larger Safeways farther away for larger purchases. Boudin's Bakery has a sandwich shop on the street level at the back of the Union Square Macy's department store. They have famous sourdough bread. Early in the morning (8 am) one can usually board the Powell Street cable cars (without waiting) at the southwest corner of Union Square for the trip to the Chinatown dim sum parlors described above. Enjoy!

“great location!” This is a great location near the Inner Harbor - very convenient. I've lived near Baltimore almost my entire life and it's a great city. The hotel is nice, rooms are clean and comfortable. The service is good, but not excellent. Like another review I've read about Hyatt - you know what you're in for. You pay for what you get. The Hyatt is no different. The rooms are clean and comfortable and most likely spacious. The hotel is almost always very nice. The service is almost always excellent. I've stayed at numerous Hyatt hotels and I'm never disappointed.

“Nice Boutique Full Service Hotel in DC Business District” Spent a couple of nights at the Madison Hotel at 15th & M Streets in DC over Easter weekend. A great location if you are conducting business in the business district though not much in a few block radius in terms of DC tourist spots or restaurants. Had a fine meal in the Hotel restaurant, The Federalist. Food was great and menu very interesting. I also liked the grab & go cafe off the more causal restaurant to the right of the lobby. Food was excellent (I am always in search of fresh berries and Greek yogurt (which is sometimes difficult to find) and they had a beautifully prepared rendition. The room was nicely decorated and the common areas looked newly renovated. The fitness center was "okay". I walked to Georgetown (2 miles) and met up with the wife and kids who cabbed it. Later in the day we all walked back from the Mall which was only about 7 blocks. I will stay at the Madison again and highly recommend it.

“I was pleasantly surprised!” I was not hopeful when I walked into the lobby of this hotel, but my experience was really quite positive. The staff were very friendly and I was greeted with warm cookies. The one-bedroom suite I was given was very nice. The bathroom was dark and small, but the rooms themselves were great. I had a nice stereo, couch, desk, bed (with clean and beautiful linens), etc... The room was great - especially for the price I paid. The hotel was centrally located and had a beautiful outdoor courtyard that is shared with the Marriott Courtyard next door. There is an indoor and outdoor pool, hot tub, patio, etc... I would definitely stay here again.

“Great resort. Super family destination” The hotel and grounds are gorgeous. The architecture is simply spectacular. The rooms are well appointed in addition to being spotlessly clean. The pools are super special. This would be a great place with kids. Tons of activities and the pool area is really cool. The service is top notch. Everyone from the gardener to the waiter was friendly and helpful. No wireless internet, but they do offer wired internet and it's free (a welcome surprise in luxury hotels.) We were a couple without kids and this is a great romantic getaway as well. Our room was totally quiet despite having neighbors on both sides. (I only know they were there because I saw them. I never heard a peep, not even a shower) We ate at Frank and Albert's on the property. The ambiance was wonderful (ask for the backroom with the fireplace). The price wasn't cheap, but was definitely reasonable given the quality, ambiance and location. If you want to go out, Camelback Road is moments away and the options are endless. We were really surprised that this was both a great couples and and family destination. The combination is hard to come by, but this resort pulls it off wonderfully.

“InterContinental Times Square - Third Stay” We stayed here for a third time a few weeks ago. The service was much better than before, when it was the main issue. We had to wait about 30 minutes for our room, but were given free drinks at the bar. We received a double upgrade to a Sky View room (3004). We also received a welcome gift of water and fruit for being platinum Priority Club members. This was a little thing, but they also provided the same number of chocolates at turndown as there were people in the room, which was very nice. The location, is pretty good. We're not huge Times Square fans, but it's central and was close to the theatre were we saw a show. The rooms were what was really lacking. They were clean for the most part, thankfully. But, they were becoming run down. Little things like the soap holder in the shower falling down, the toilet paper holder being messed up, and holes in the sheets were all over. We would definitely stay here, but they need to make sure their rooms are in good shape.

“Nice suprise from a large downtown property!” We took the family for a little staycation and had a great stay at the Sheraton. The rooms are updated and our all had beautiful views of the mountains. The beds were comfortable and the bath was small but well laid out. My only complaints on the rooms for a four star property is that 1- they do not have robes in the rooms and 2 - they lack high quality toiletries. Otherwise I felt the property offered a lot of "bang for the buck". My favorite was the pool! Here it is late March and thanks to the eclectic Colorado weather I was able to enjoy a sunny 70 degree day poolside. I was thrilled to find cabanas and comfy loungers. The norm in downtown is an indoor pool or no pool. The pool offered an tranquil escape from downtown. Then, after lounging one can walk to the Denver Pavillions which is right next door or catch the shuttle down to Larimer for a nice dinner on the town. Overall a huge but pleasant property.

“Good location, good stay” I've know of Affina Manhattan for long while now, but always was skeptical about it. The reviews didn't always seem positive. Also being a frequent New York traveler for business, I try to not use anything but the large chains and brands. Unfortunately for my last trip none were available so opted to try Affina out. Located right next to Penn Station/Madison Square Garden, it offers excellent access to subways, so getting uptown or downtown is very easy. The lobby area is dated, but in style only. The staff was extremely helpful, polite and friendly. The front desk folks were equally nice, however, there was a long line and only two folks managed the check-in so made for a long check-in process. There seemed to be some wear and tear in the lobby area, but nothing to put off the feel. I was lucky enough to get a new renovated room. I heard not all rooms are redone, but mine was. I was small, but well decorated and everything looked fresh and new including the bathroom. The tub was steel, and some of the paint seemed to chip off, but nothing nasty. Bathroom was small, however, and the sink was not easy to use without the counter space. Water pressure and other amenities were acceptable. The TV and the HDTV programming was good to see. One thing discouraging was the window AC unit. I didn't need to use it but I can see it being noisy in the summer time. Shades and window treatments were adequate and working. I did not experience any noise from the street nor the hallways. I was on teh 13th floor however. All in all it was a good stay and a good value for the buck. I did not use any of the other features other than sleeping.

“great locations, swanky, friendly staff - best concierge EVAH!” i stayed here with two friends the first weekend in april for a girls' weekend. my husband i stayed here in june 2008 and were very pleased with everything about it. this time around, we arrived in chicago at 9a - upon arriving at the hotel we were checked in and in our rooms in less than 15 minutes!!! timmy the concierge was the most helpful person on earth to us that weekend, helping us with everything from directions to shopping discounts to letting me use his computer to order delivery for dinner. his recommendations were spot on. we had a small problem with the bathroom lights being out, and this problem was resolved within 30 minutes of a phone call to the desk.

“Typical W, good and bad” This hotel is what I've come to expect of all W Hotels: what I would call business-traveler trendy. That is, just enough trendiness to be hip but with enough amenities to appeal to older business traveler. As with the other Ws I've stayed at, it's not about the nightly room charge, which is reasonable, it's about the extras. Want to park? $44/night. Want internet? $14.95. Want eggs benedict for breakfast? $21. Want that bottle of Fuji water next to your bed? $7. And so on. It's been a long time since I stayed in a room with no coffee maker, and I've stayed in hotels at all price points. There is free coffee in the lobby in the morning but more likely they want you to order it with your room service breakfast for $10. Everything else is fine, the room is a decent size, the bed is comfortable. I had no issues with the service. Just be ready to pay for extras.

“Great Hotel, location aside, would recommend” Stayed for business, got the junior suite. Despite being a bit far from the action on 11th ave (pretty far west) it is on 48th street. Pros: as a kimpton member, free internet access (wifi) + mini bar access junior suite is amazing size despite being far from center... its gets pretty busy, bar and rooftop rooftop view is nice! happy hour (free) wines and coffee/tea in mornings bathroom is large plus bathtube and shower are separate service is top notch, primary focus very close to restaurant row, 9th ave running trail near hudson river comfortable, yet modern room large views and windows taxis are plentiful and wait outside (good for meetings/dinner events) Cons: near the cruise lines, boat whistles before and after departures no coffee maker in room; offers free coffee delivery service??? never used not really near metro line lack of surrounding restaurants/coffee shop/shopping etc near car dealerships hotel food is ehh, ok 15 minute walk to time square area

“New, clean, great location. Full kitchen!” I think that really nice hotels like this Residence Inn get nitpicked by reviewers in an attempt to find something to complain about. While some of the complaints in the previous reviews are accurate (parking fee, long lines for breakfast), many are trivial when you take into consideration the many amenities at this hotel. At the end of this review, I address some of the complaints from previous reviewers as well as add some of my own pet peeves. We stayed here for one week over 4th of July weekend. It is important to note that there are two types of rooms, a studio suite and a 1BR suite. The 1BR is larger and has a divider between the living area and the bed. I am pretty sure you can either have 1 queen or 1 king, but there are no double beds. Some suites have sofa beds, some do not. If you need one, make sure you reserve one. We stayed in the smaller studio suite and found it suitable for 2 adults and a small child. The full kitchen is only missing a traditional oven, but has a full refrigerator, microwave, electric range, pots, pans, silverware and cooking utensils. This was a big advantage for us during our week stay. The location is “as good as it gets” for Gaslamp. If you aren’t familiar with this area, it is the busiest part of downtown with the most shopping and restaurants. However, it isn’t Rodeo Drive. This is "downtown" so you will see plenty of homeless people and drunk rowdy young adults on most nights, especially weekends. Many of the restaurants and bars cater to the party crowds as there are drink specials and happy hours galore. But there are also many high-end and fancy restaurants and others that accommodate families too. The location is within walking distance are the convention center, Padres Petco Park, Seaport Village, Horton Plaza, and the train station. 3 minutes to the zoo. When we arrived on Thursday night at 9:00 PM, there was a guest complaining about a music concert outside. Although the concert was over a block away, we could here it on the 10th floor. Fortunately, it stopped at 9:30 PM before we went to sleep. We didn’t have any other city noise issues for the week. As previously reviewed, the hotel is very clean and very new. The decor and ambiance is really modern and the lobby/lounge area has many places to sit and relax or enjoy a drink. There is also a large communal table in the lobby where there are outlets to plug in your laptop and enjoy the free Internet. The small market has drinks, beer, wine, ice cream, snacks and other sundries. One interesting thing about this hotel is that they don’t offer "Do Not Disturb" signs for your door. At first, I was sure that there was some high-tech way that house keeping could detect the room was occupied when locked from the inside. No such luck. After being awaken by housekeeping twice, I realized the inside lock only prevents them from unlocking the door, not from knocking on it. I guess I could have requested a sign. I believe all Residence Inns allow pets. I was the lucky guest who was woken up 4th of July morning at zero-dark-thirty by two large barking dogs next door. Their owner had gone for a jog and left them to howl for 30 minutes. After I complained to the front desk and the owner, I never heard them again. Another pet peeve (pun intended) of mine are slamming hotel doors. I realize the doors must be self-closing for fire safety, but I refuse to believe that they have to close so violently that they rattle the halls. The doors at this new Residence Inn get the "Best in Show" award for the loudest slamming doors in their class. I wish guests had the common sense to hold the door as it closes to prevent their neighbors from thinking we were having an after-shock of the latest California earthquake. Previous reviews complain about the parking fee and it also gave me pause. But I learned that all of downtown is overpriced parking. Many hotels in this area are close to $30/day and the parking lots are $18 to $25. I figured it was worth the price of valet and was very pleased with the valet service. Even when there were several people waiting for their car, it never took more than 5 minutes. I justified the expense by figuring out I save $30/day with the free breakfast the hotel serves as well as free Internet. We only found long lines for breakfast on Sunday morning (4th of July) of our week stay. This seems to only occur in the last hour of breakfast. Despite the final hour chaos, the hotel has at least 4 employees running around cleaning tables, bringing out more food and coffee. However, we found a place to sit even on Sunday. Taking the food back to your room was also a nice alternative. For the reviewers who thought that there was insufficient lighting to shave or put on make-up in front of the mirror in the morning; open the curtains and let the abundance of sunlight in. I’m sorry one reviewer didn’t think nine dresser drawers and an armoire were enough storage space. Yes, some drawers only pull out half-way to prevent tipping, but they are full sized drawers. You just have to put one or two items of clothing in at a time instead of a stack. For the reviewers who complained that the vanity/sink is outside of the bathroom and that the tub and shower are one unit instead of separate: Clearly, the sink is outside of the bathroom for the sake of efficiency so that one person isn’t dominating all three at once. As for separating the tub and shower: Marriott is trying to do as much as it can with a limited space per room both to make it efficient for extended-stay travelers and keep costs to the consumer down. Remember that full kitchen you get? That is where your separate tub was supposed to go.

“Very Nice, Clean Hotel” My friend and I stayed for just one night, and loved the hotel. It had an awesome water feature in the hotel, and great large bar. Like all Hyatts it had a very comfortable bed, lot's of pillows, and large bathroom.

“This place is a trip all by itself.” I'm a local San Diego resident who recently stayed here for three nights while I was between homes. The Westgate is a 4 star property in downtown San Diego (in a fairly good area) that appears to be from another time. Situated in a relatively modern high rise that appears to have been built in the70's the hotel has an EXTREMELY traditional feel inside - think Palace of Versailles. It's like a time warp. The decor is over the top but not completely in a bad or good way. Large crystal chandeliers and antique rugs and furniture abound (all in a dusty haze that makes everything feel old) I think of San Diego as a young, modern city this place definitely stands out style wise (for better or worse) among the other hotels in the area. Overall I liked staying here but I'm still not totally sure why. Here are my impressions: PROS: - Service - The staff was really great here and this is a place where the "software" (i.e. employees, etc.) is better than the "hardware". You get the feel they work hard to keep up with the place. Valets were EXCELLENT and so was front desk staff. I had to be moved due to a plumbing problem and they handled it extremely well. They had a bellman, and housekeeper who did an instant turn down in the new room within 5 minutes of the call. Room service was also EXCELLENT. CONS: - "Worn" feeling - Even though I found the hotel is very consistent in it's design (which is over the top traditional) it felt worn and threadbare. Especially in the parking garage area where there is a barber shop and gym. You could see the old storefronts that were boarded up and inside are cubicles, etc. The main lobby also felt dusty (even though I'm sure it was in fact very clean.) The furnishings just look worn, and colors desaturated. - Bedspread -The "worn" feeling extends to a good degree to the guest rooms. It's 2012 and this hotel STILL uses an old heavy (and honestly gross) floral bedspread. I pulled it off the bed immediately and it weighed a ton. Worse, is the thing smelled like mothballs and made the pillows / bedding smell the same way. I sent my pillows back to housekeeping after taking a whiff. Seriously the hotel needs to ditch the bedspreads immediately. - Rooms - the rooms are large and spacious but a little of worn. Some of the wallpaper is starting to peel a bit and the countertops/faucets have seen their better days. Still not too bad and everything was clean - it just appears it's getting to be time for a renovation. - Room "Lobbies" - I have never seen this before in a hotel. Every two rooms (except suites) shared a separate lobby secured by a separate door. Kind of a mini lobby between the elevator lobby. Really unique and kind of odd. I think the idea was to protect the rooms from the noise of the main hallways. The problem is that you can totally hear the other guest open their door and then the mini lobby door - I think it's worse than no mini lobby at all. Nothing the hotel could do at this point but really odd and one of those things that gives this place character. - Hidden fees - the hotel charges the obligatory daily "amenity fee" (I think it's $15) and an expensive parking (I believe $32/day) rate. Keep in mind you are looking at an additional $48 over whatever rate you book. The hotel kindly waived my amenity fee after a plumbing incident. - In Room Refrigerator. For some reason there is a mini-bar "cooler" that is not a "refrigerator". This is unacceptable. It will cool a can of soda but not keep milk or dairy items at a safe temperature. They put a note on the unit to warn me. - Power outlets - It's 2012. There should be an outlet near the desk area to plug in a laptop. There were none and the closest was on another wall behind a desk. In most hotels, there is an outlet built into the desk lamp. This was the case in both rooms I was in. Despite the quirks, I would still recommend this hotel. It's really is unique. I get the feeling that the staff does the best it can to keep up with this place despite it's age. That said, to whoever owns this place, it's 2012, please get rid of the old, dusty floral bedspreads!

“Excellent value, very clean and comfortable.” We stayed 5 nights at this hotel. We were pleased with the central location to everything. Our room was impeccably clean and was very comfortable. We would recommend this hotel to friends or family who were staying in the area. Only one minor complaint - the free wi fi internet only worked if we sat out by the pool. For some reason the signal was too weak in our room. But other than that we were very pleased with the hotel.

“Amazing!” I recently stayed at The Peninsula Chicago & had another amazing experience! I arrived quite early around 8:45am & was checked in by Andrea at the Front Desk- she was lovely. She welcomed me back, upgraded me to a Grand Deluxe room with a great view overlooking the Water Tower, & swiftly gave me my key to the 15th floor- room 1505. Andrea was fantastic & was an amazing first impression! Bastian was also great- he gave me a late check-out, which was very gracious & was very kind at departure & assisted me with storing my bags. He was very polite & efficient. My room was quiet, with the occasional siren from outside. I was also at the end of the hallway (which I particularly like) & my room was lovely & very comfortable. The Bed was utterly blissful- amazing, soft sheets (no top sheet, but I'm sure you could request one), perfect pillows & an amazing comforter & mattress- I had an amazing sleep & relaxed the following morning for a while because the bed was that comfy!! The soaking tub & Davi amenities in the large marble bathroom were amazing! I also like their towels & robe. There is a roomy dressing area, with plenty of space to unpack & layout clothing, store bags, luggage etc.- super handy. I also loved the small sitting area with a very comfortable sofa, desk, large flat screen with Super clear reception & plenty of channels, well-stocked mini-bar, incredibly fast internet that was complimentary, the little hallway leading into my room, & the overall feel & colors were soothing. The Food was truly amazing & a particular standout! I had room service three times- twice for Breakfast & once for dinner & dined in their Lobby restaurant twice for lunch during my stay- each time my meals were well-presented & tasted delicious!! I really love their Iced Tea, Caesar Salad, Eggs Benedict, Freshly squeezed Orange Juice (amazing!!), & desserts- it's all so good! I was craving a basic Grilled Cheese & room service made an incredible one!! It's nice to be able to wander down to the lobby & relax in such a stunning space with amazing food- I have had several servers there, but Eric, Karen & John are all fantastic- personable, warm & very efficient- well done! Yvette in Room service was also amazing & so sweet! The location is perfect, with easy walking distance to Millenium Park, the Lakefront, which is amazing, the fantastic shopping on Michigan, & easily accessible to the EL. The spa, Fitness Center & spa are all stunning & first rate! The overall Service at the hotel is really good- everyone is friendly, but I have come across a few employees that seemed a little on edge- nothing major, but just my overall view. For the most part, the service at The Peninsula is on par with the other major Luxury hotels in the city. However, I have seen more Friendly & engaging service at The Four Seasons- again, just my opinion. A few shortcomings- none of which detracted from my stay, just some notes: - the wall outlets by the desk had completely come unattached from the wall, so I had to plug my laptop in by the dressing area; the base boards by the desk were really dusty, the bathroom did not have Q-tips (when I called Housekeeping, a lovely attendant came to my room with one of my requested items, but accidentally sent a Sewing kit instead- no problem, I just ran down to the Spa to get this)- I love this hotel & look forward to returning very soon! It's definitely the best Luxury Hotel in Chicago & has amazing food, perfect beds, Good service & an incredible location~ Best, Patrick Winkler

“Amalfi keeps getting better” Updated info: They're done with lobby construction and the new lobby is very nice with a flowing water feature and updated furnishings. This renovation just happened as they celebrated five years in business. The Amalfi Hotel occupies floors 2-6 or a 17-story office building in downtown Chicago, in a very convenient location... walking distance to Magnificent Mile shopping and within a block or two of five fine steakhouses (Keefers is in the same building, Harry Caray's, Sullivans, Ruth's Chris, Smith & Wollensky are just a block away, Chicago Chop House, Kinzie Chop House, Morton's of Chicago are very short walks). Service is very nice, although I didn't challenge their "experience designers" (why can't we just call them the front desk clerks?). The maids are "comfort stylists", the porters are "impressionists". Are we paying for these words? Sounds expensive. And silly. All of the valet, bellhop and wait staff, regardless of what fluffy title they were given, were remarkably kind for Chicago. The best way to experience the Amalfi is to find your best deal on one of the discount websites (I used Expedia) and call the Amalfi to get a rate match. They will do that. You may see a rate above of over $300 a night, but I just stayed there for $132 a night, and you can't beat that at any other classy place downtown. My personal previous best rate was at the House of Blues before they became Hotel Sax at $145 a night. Valet parking, as it is in downtown, was up there.. $44 a night with in and out privileges. Not a trace of cigarette or cigar smoke in the place... it's relatively quiet for downtown... the infrastructure works well (icemaker, refrigerator, door locks, HVAC, elevators, etc.)... and the beds are the best you'll sleep on (better than I own). The wireless networking was fast and smooth, and no extra cost. The LodgeNet television/in-room movie system is still undergoing a transition to HD, so the TV video wasn't HD and was stretched for now, and the reaction to the remote was slow. They promised this was undergoing improvement soon. I'll stay there regularly unless they charge me rack rates.

“Awesome Choice” Room was very clean. Bed was super comfortable. Soft bedding. Nice staff. About 10 min walk from metro station. Check out all the embassies as you walk to hotel. Dining nearby. I would definitly stay here again. Taxi to DCA was $30 to include tip. Smart design of shower.

“Superb location” The hotel is very nice with friendly staff and a very clean room. The real advantage is that it's right downtown within walking distance to restaurants. Parking is just inconvenient. Overall I was satisfied with my stay

“The BEST of the BEST!” I moved to Houston in 2008 (from New York City) and I thought I had stayed in some nice hotels. Hotel Granduca is amazing with a taste of southern Texas hospitality. We live in Houston and my boyfriend surprised me with a night at the Granduca for our anniversary. And they upgraded us to a suite since it was available. Nice touch. FYI - for returning guests, this 5-star property will automatically upgrade you if a suite is available. The hotel is a bit like the Venetian in Las Vegas (from a decoration and classy perspective) but has the warmth of a private home. It is gorgeous from top to bottom and the service is excellent. If you come to Houston, you can't miss this gem which is part of the Leading Hotels of the World collection. If you are not familiar with Houston, the location couldn't be better. It is across the street from the upscale Uptown Park shopping center. And while you are there, don't miss a trip to Crave Cupcakes, The Tasting Room (Wine Bar) or Uptown Sushi - three of the best in town across the street from the Granduca. It is also about 2 miles from the Galleria Shopping area. If you are looking for privacy, class and top-notch rooms/amenities, then look no further. You may even see a celebrity since this hotel is a favorite.

“Nice but Pricey” Have stayed there several times and while the prices and especially the parking keeps going up the experience seems more and more ordinary. No internet and the elevator situation is in need of attention. The Hyatt almost next door offers better value for the bargain hunter.

“Great new hotel - Perfect location” I spent labor day weekend at this Hilton and it was an absolutely the right choice. Hotel opened in 2000 and it's still well maintain and in a great shape. I got a room on 3rd floor [317] and really recommend this room for anyone. This room has a nice view to the pool and also convention center plus coronado bridge. Lavazza coffee is good. Bathroom products are from CrabTree. Location couldn't be better. - trolley is right there! [orange line] - Petco Staduim is about a block - Gaslamp quarter with ton of shops and restaurants - convention center is right across the street Room was quite small but clean and I like 42" TV (^__^) Front desk and bell boy were very helpful. The room wasn't ready when I got there and the front desk guy even offered to call me and let me know when room is ready. He also gave me a room with sofa bed too! Bell boy also gave me the map and tips to explore San Diego. Pool and fitness room are on 2nd floor. Outdoor pool area was really nice! I was worried at first to have a room facing train tracks for both MTS and Amtrak. Hilton has earplugs ready for guests but I didn't really need to use it. I can hear the train noise on my second night but it wasn't too loud to wake me up anyway. few cons; parking $35/night, no breakfast, free wired internet - wifi only available in lobby area. This is my first visit to San Diego and I really had a good time staying at this hotel. I would recommend Hilton Gaslamp to anyone (business traveler, sport fan, tourist, foodies, bar hopper etc. ) for it's location, room quality and everything else : )

“A Very Nice 4 1/2 Star Gem” Not as elegant as the Ritz Carlton, not as "perfect" as the Mansion, this is still a special hotel. I remember the old Stoneleigh. This is one of the most splendid updatings and renovations of a hotel that I have ever seen. The rooms are fine, comfortable, with many nice appointments of luxury. Room service was first rate, and the food was very good. The neighborhood is cool, close to all the attractions of Uptown but comfortably separated in a near neighborhood. We did not make use of the spa or the main restaurant, so my review does not pertain to them. We had a remarkable room special, which made for a huge value. It may be because of late summer slow traffic. Maybe traffic is down because of the construction noise other reviewers have pointed out. I don't know. But, while I strongly recommend this hotel, if you intend to sleep late, make sure reservations accommodates you away from the noise.

“Great Deal” Stayed in this hotel twice in the last 2 weeks. First time, absolutely wonderful - Hilton Honor Diamond reward in room, awesome fitness center and the staff could not be any nicer. Second stay, no Hilton Honor reward given in room and the fitness room was a mess - told the front desk that it needed to be tended to - the second day, the room was even more of a mess - oh well... The fitness center, even with the mess, is 100% better than most of the fitness rooms in other hotels. Would definately stay here again - travel each week for business and if all that is wrong is as described above - and all for $99 bucks a night - then count me in.

“Go for the Upgrade” We stayed at the Sheraton Gateway Hotel on the first and end nights of our Californian vacation. On both occasions we took the upgrade offer and for 30 dollars had a room on the Club Floor, free appitiser in the evening and buffet breakfast in the morning. Great value. Free internet in the lobby was an added bonus. We found the room to be very comfortable but would recommend staying at the rear of the hotel where aircraft noise was considerably less that in the rooms at the front. Staff were very friendly and helpful and overall we had a very enjoyable stay. This hotel kind of restored my faith in the Sheraton brand.

“Nice Boutique Hotel with Small Rooms; Can do Better for Price” The Fitzpatrick is an "Irish" boutique hotel. The lobby is small (read: tiny) but nicely decorated and had a large flower arrangement. Elevators were similarly small but renovated. Check-in was smooth and the staff was great. The doormen were friendly and one went above and beyond the call of duty to get us a cab. The hotel is small, so there was not always a doorman to open the door, etc. Check-out was simple, too. The hotel let us check luggage for free. The room was tiny, even for Manhattan standards, and the smallest Manhattan hotel room I've seen in years. It only had one chair and the nightstands were tiny. There was a double bed and a small flatscreen TV mounted to the wall, but not across from the bed. The window overlooked a roof and the sides of other buildings. The room had a coffee maker, nice toiletries, a trouser press, and a bathrobe. It was clean and in a traditional style. The bathroom was in marble and small but tasteful and appeared to have been newly renovated. There was no tub, but it had a nice rain shower. The Fitzpatrick is cozy and a perfectly fine hotel. The only reason I would not stay there are 1) the location isn't quite as convenient as some other hotels and 2) for the price, you can get a nicer hotel with more amenities and in a better location. For example, two weeks before, I stayed in Manhattan in a two-room suite in a hotel with a better location (in my opinion) for $50 less per night.

“Not a Bad Place to Be Marooned” I was stuck in Charlotte for the evening and the airline put me up in this hotel. The rooms are really spacious and well appointed, the lobby is nice and the service was really friendly. There is also an Omaha Steakhouse in the building, not a bad option for an airport hotel. If you are stuck in the city due to travel changes or need to stay somewhere for an early flight the next day, I would highly recomment this hotel.

“Great location, overpriced bar and amenities” We booked this hotel last minute using the hotelstonight app so we got a good price on the room. The hotel itself was very nice and the staff were very professional. The room was ok. You can tell it's an old hotel but has been updated. One big disappointment I had was that NOTHING in the room was included. Not even the small coffee packets to make with the coffee pot. There were snacks and liquor in the room, but all were outrageously priced. The drinks were also outrageously priced. We ordered 2 drinks down at the pool. For a small rum and coke in a plastic cup and a mojito it was $35. I have no problem paying for drinks at a bar, but $35 for 2 drinks and one was in a throw away cup? A little much I thought. The upside was that since we didn't like the hotel bar we just walked down the street and went somewhere else :) The location of the hotel is great. It's right across from the Chinese theatre. Lots of tourist attractions and lots of shopping and eating all within walking distance.

“Great location, very clean hotel.” Stayed here for one night in February so that I could attend a two day course in the Microtek building right across the street from the hotel. I got here around 7 a.m. and was going to have them hold my bags but they let me check into a room! Pretty amazing in and of itself. Lobby is large, staff is so nice & accomodating! I felt like they would bend over backwards for me, great service! The room had everything in it you would ever need. Kitchen with full refrigerator, small stove, sink, dishwasher, coffeemaker, microwave, dishes, utensils, pots and pans, wine glasses, wine opener, etc. Small kitchen table that seats two people, work desk, separate living area from the bedroom. Nice large bathroom. I had a rooftop view of the hot tub so no brownie points there, but then again I wasn't in my room except in the evening anyways. This hotel & the rooms are clean clean clean. I always look for "corner dirt" like in the corners of the floor, on the wall etc. And this place was pretty spotless, I was impressed. Very comfortable room. Gym has everything you need for a quick workout. Full, continental breakfast was great. Eggs, sausage, biscuits & gravy, juice, coffee, yogurts, fruit, toast, bagels, milk & cereal...what more could you want/? In the evenings they have free drinks and snacks (changes daily). One night they had bratwurst. Wow. Nice place, kudos. I only rated the value as a 3 because I feel like for the standard person sometimes hotels in downtown Denver are a bit pricey. I got the "microtek rate" of $149 which was quite the steal compared to the rack rate of this place. Within walking distance to shops, restaurants & the 16th street mall.

“Impressive!” I have stayed at the Conrad Chicago twice for business. The rooms are immaculate with excellent bath amenities and luxurious bed linens and pillows. Service at the front desk is quick and efficient. For a leisure trip to Chicago, the location can't be beat. For business, the atmosphere is quiet and serene; perfect for unwinding after a day of travel.

“Great Location” Great location although a little overpriced for this hotel. It has been recently renovated which was nice however the rooms are very small. Was not happy about the staff striking outside of the hotel from 6am to 10.30pm eachday! We could hear the noise which woke me up & delayed us getting to sleep at night, the best staff could offer were ear plugs which I thought was poor customer service!

“Trendy hotel with well-designed small rooms in a great Columbus Circle location” Like most travelers, I scour the web and the guidebooks for great advice when it comes to my hotel stay. This is expecially crucial if I have booked a room on Priceline (as in this case). I want to correctly set my expectations prior to arrival. For instance, I really had to get myself in the SMALL ROOM mindset before checking in at The Hudson. Arrival: The hotel doesn't have a sign. Be sure to look at the pics on the website so you know where you're going if you are coming in via subway train. There was a small line at check-in but the front desk staff did a great job keeping everyone moving. There was one very important woman (a trendy I-think-I'm-20-but-I-am-really-45) who felt compelled to jump to the front "Just to ask a question" which of course was her attempt to jump the line. No go! Yay front desk. I made a joke and they took pity on us and got us into a higher level room facing the atrium. :-) Score! The room: Ok. We know. It's small. It's not the end of the world. Unpack your stuff. Be organized and you have plenty of room. Don't throw you stuff all over the room. Now you'll need to sit on the toilet sideways and take turns in the bathroom but....the good parts? Incredible water pressure and a roomy shower plus a VERY comfortable bed. You didn't come to New York to hang out in your hotel room did you? Well then, the shower and the bed are top notch. Done. My husband and I slept like logs in a Queen size which is usually a challenge. I think its really all about the pillows. Noise: Try to get a room above the 6th floor. There will be street noise. It's NY. Buy some freaking Tylenol PM if it's that big of deal. The bigger issue is the nightclub. It's loud. Very loud and very popular. Therefore if you are below Floor 6, you will probably hear it. Join the fun or get something to knock yourself out. Location: As they say in real estate....This is a superb location. The subway is very close and can get you where you need to go quickly. We walked down Columbus Ave after visiting the Natural History Museum and really enjoyed it. Great shops, bars and restaurants al the way down. Lots of dogs and locals give it a nice neighborhood feel. There's a great 24 hour diner and pizza place right on the corner of 58th and 9th. Both are open late. We enjoyed our stay very much. Appreciated the thought and design work that went into the place. Staff was very friendly except for one woman carrying a clipboard in the AM who looked at me like a deer in the headlights when I asked her a question about check out.. Overall a good bet. An even better one if you can score it on Priceline.

“Nice hotel” I was there for a conference and found the accommodations to be very nice. Everything was clean and well maintained. Staff was curteous. There is a lack of food, however. There is one small restaurant, which is more like a coffee shop and it was quite expensive. There are places to walk to but I did not want to do that before an 8:00 meeting. I did best by walking to Panera in the evening and buying something to eat the next morning in my room. Beware of days when there are baseball games as the hotel is acorss the street from the stadium and it creates a lot of activity.
“Lovely” Beautiful Hotel in lovely Chestnut Hill. Room was tiny, but space well utilized. Room seemed to be newly renovated. Staff was nice & helpful. Breakfast buffet included in room price.

“Everything I expected and more...” After extensive research of the various upscale hotels in San Francisco, I chose the Ritz Carlton based on other reviews and the great location. This hotel was one of the few I have experienced that is as beautiful and stunning in person as it is in the pictures. All of the staff were extremely courteous and professional. This hotel is the true symbol of elegance, and would be my only choice in San Francisco. We were upgraded to a suite upon check in and the room was amazing. There are not enough good things I can say about this hotel, but I highly recommend it and it made my vacation amazing!

“Excellent service, comfortable beds, OUTSTANDING location” I stayed at the Embassy Suites Washington-Convention Center for a conference that was taking place at the Renaissance Hotel about a block away. This hotel was more affordable and MUCH more comfortable. My king room was equipped with a separate sleeping area that was a bit small, but the bed was great. The living room/dining room had a small dining table with four chairs that doubled as the "desk" (this was one of the few drawbacks). The furniture was very comfortable. There is a small "kitchenette" in each room with a microwave and fridge. My bath was spacious, but I wish the towel rack was closer to the tub. You have to remember to put the dry towel on the bathroom counter before you get in the tub. Also, the shower head was pretty pitiful, but these critiques are not enough to deter me from staying here again. There is an elaborate, free breakfast every morning. The staff were ALL very friendly, accommodating, and polite. The location is great. Within walking distance of several museums; including Madam Tussauds, International Spy Museum, and the Smithsonian Museum of Art. China Town is also a short 10 or 15 minute walk away. I really enjoyed my stay here, and would not hesitate to recommend it to others.

“Good overnight stay” I needed a place to crash for a few hours during an overnight layover and the Doubletree looked great, being so close to the airport. It is literally 5 minutes from the airport entrance, so this was great for my 5AM flight. The rooms are decent, probably average for most Doubletree hotels nowadays. The room and bathroom were clean, which is appreciated when I just want to get into the room and get to sleep. My only complaint is the property and rooms seem a bit tired. Other than the bed and bathroom everything seemed a bit worn out. Not a real fault, because everything was still in good order. Overall if I had to spend another night near the airport I wouldn't look anywhere else. A warm cookie, clean room and a great bed is all I could ask for.

“Exceptionally nice rooms compared to most Times Square hotels” I attended a convention here and found the room superior to most other hotels in the Times Square/Midtown Manhatten area. The rooms are larger, newer and cleaner than most. The atrium is light, bright and grand. I'm not crazy about the location, which is right in the center of Times Square - I'd rather be 2 blocks awya and away from all of the traffic - but it's nice to have so many theaters right outside the door. This is a good hotel for someone who wants more than a dated, smallish room so commonly found in this part of town. Be warned: you'll pay a few dollars more than in other properties, but you'll appreciate your stay.

“Great location and service” Stayed 2 nights. Hotel with superb location, close to everything. It was very nice to jog along the harbor. Didn't have time to use the pool and gym, but they looked nice and clean. Food was tasty and at the reasonable price. My room had awesome view of the San Diego Bay (see photo). Loved watching the sun set from my big balcony. Staff was the best - extremelly friendly, empathetic, and helpful in a genuine way.

“Fnatatstic....but.” I have to agree with most of the other reviews on this property. The location is perfect, the staff are mostly fantastic. There are some who seem to be just doing a job but this is compensated by the others who are the best. The food and wine on level 2 is a great option and my kids loved being able to go down and snack. The suite we had was great and the option of the fold out sofa made things better for the four of us. My only negative is that the beds were too short. I am only six foot one, so not overly tall, but my feet were always hanging over the end of the bed which is uncomfortable. This is unusual and may be due to size of the rooms but for such a well thought out hotel, I thought this was a significant issue. Despite this, I would stay at Casablanca again if I was lucky enough to come to New York.

“Great location, wish I could have spent more time in the room!” We stayed here on points, so I don't know if I'd feel differently had we had to pay whatever prices these rooms were, but I found the JW Marriot incredibly relaxing and convenient. The hotel is only a few blocks away from the Washington monument and the white house. There's a food court just up the hill and around the corner with almost anything you could want to eat. I think the only downside is that it's not all that close to a Metro stop. (it's not really that far either, but my feet hurt at that point so I was kind of whiny). Our room had a great view of the monument. The concierge lounge had a great selection for breakfast (don't know about the hotel restaurant, if there was one), and everyone at the hotel was very polite and friendly. And yes, once again, the Marriott beds. I adore them, and find them incredibly comfortable. My only regret was not having much time at the hotel between meeting up with friends and sightseeing.

“Excellent Hotel” Staff makes the experience at this hotel. Courteous, helpful, and attentive. Rooms are fine, nothing extraordinary. Room is small for those traveling with infant as crib is very close to bed. Once child goes to sleep, impossible to do anything without walking up baby. Excellent location, gorgeous grounds. Minor issue with cleanliness of room. Overall, a very pleasant stay.

“I like to walk to the hotel from the airport” This is just one of a bunch of airport hotels at SeaTac but it is the most easily accessed by foot. You just exit the terminal at baggage claim level, turn right, and cross the street at the traffic light; takes all of 5 minutes. I really enjoy having a predictable travel time in the morning when I head in to catch a flight. I get a room on the back side of the hotel. The windows open and there is a mixed view of parking lot, trees, and greenery though you do hear the HVAC gear. Nicer view than the main drag and maybe noise of air traffic on the front side. Wifi works fine, rooms are quite adequate with a good work area. The buffet is quick for breakfast but terribly unexciting. There is a restaurant right next door if you want better food. I also tried the light rail from downtown Seattle to the airport (currently you take a shuttle bus the last few miles). This is a pretty nice way to get to the airport. And the shuttle stops on the side of the terminal nearest the Radisson so quite convenient for me. No reason to be here other than in transit from SeaTac though.

“Good location for mid-town business” This Hilton was updated just a couple of years ago and looks and feels great. It's a busy mid-town hotel with great lobby bars. The rooms are compact, but have all the necessities that you need and some of the luxuries that you want! The front desk is well staffed and the elevators are fast!

“Great place to stay” Just spent a weekend here and was very pleased. Located right next to a Starbucks. Hotel offers free shuttle service, complimentary happy hour beer and wine and milk and cookies. Staff is very friendly. Property is well kept. Rooms are nice as well. Location is 10 minutes from American Airlines Center. 30 minutes from the Cowboys games. 10 minute walk to JFK museum. It's a good place to stay when in Dallas. Has a fitness center. Small hot tub. Flat screen TVs. Spacious suites. Bar. Computers to use. Free wifi. Very pleased.

“Excellent Service Trumps Older Accommodations” Staff was pleasant, polite, and accommodating. However, the sleeping room struck me as pretty drab - standard dark green hotel carpeting, just kind of blah. I had problems with a run-away thermostat on the first day (had to get the engineer up twice), and turning off the shower/tub was a bit tricky. On the plus side, it was a suite with separate "living area", two flat screen TVs, a microwave, and refrigerator... if that's what you want/need. There's a Starbuck's in the lobby, and many places to eat within easy walking distance. The hotel is right next to Sundance Square, "downtown Fort Worth's entertainment and shopping district", as they say. We had a three day conference in this hotel, and my impression is the hotel staff went way above and beyond the norm to make us happy... Including free snacks and a special lunch set-up (at cost) on an icy day when many of us preferred staying inside. I didn't like that valet parking was the only available option on the day I arrived, according to the valet.

“Usual HGI quality in great area!” I frequently stay at Hilton Garden Inns when I travel, so when we were planning our New York vacation this year I was pleased to find the HGI in Tribeca offering a stupidly low price--$158/night, which is almost unheard of for ANY chain in New York. The location is fantastic, literally steps away from the A/C/E trains on Canal Street. We flew in through Newark and took the Airtrain into Penn Station, then hopped the A train down to the hotel (little trick since there's so many exits at Canal--look for the one marked Beach Street. Go up the stairs, hang a left once you're outside and there's the hotel). We got a nice view of the neighborhood from our fifth floor room--I suspect those are the HHonors rooms--and as per usual HGI operations the staff was pleasant and helpful. A special shout-out to Felipe, who helped out when I somehow screwed up the TV! Beds were comfortable, room was spotless and decent-sized by New York standards. If there was any nitpick it was the business center--there's two computers but only one is hooked up to the printer, and invariably said printer-compatible computer was being hogged by a teenager on Facebook. The staff will let you use their printer though, but still. If you want a little night life Bar Artisanal, attached to the hotel, seems to be a pretty popular spot. Tribeca isn't cheap foodwise, but you can always walk a few blocks to the Village for lots of cheap eats. Also check out Kitchenette, a funky little place on Chambers Street that serves great and (for the area) cheap breakfasts. I don't know if we'll ever luck out and get a rate this low again, but if you get the opportunity to stay here do so, it's a great hotel.

“It served our purposes, nothing more, nothing less” My wife and stayed there on April 26th, 2007. The hotel is located two blocks from Midway Airport, and I was worried because I am a light sleeper. But I had no problems. There are several other hotels and a TGI-Friday restaurant, where we ate after check-in, within easy walking distance. Curiously, while the airport noise was not a problem, the noise in our first floor room was. The dinging of the elevator bell is still in my head. And there was a lot of foot traffic outside our room. If we ever stay there again, we will ask for a room on an upper floor and away from the elevator. Everything else was fine. And the location is ideal for visiting Chicago.

“Very Nice” Rooms are very nice size, even including walk-in closet. Super cold a/c. Any problem is addressed immediately. Very nice bar in lobby. Very friendly staff from housekeeping to bartenders. Very good fitness facility.

“Very Nice!” We had a 2 night stay at the Hyatt as we were in town to see the Sox take on the Orioles. The service was very good. Everyone was very nice and very helpful. The lobby and general decor of the hotel was excellent. The room was clean and very nicely decorated. Bathrooms were also very nicely appointed. We had a partial harbor view which was a nice bonus. The location is perfect. Right accross the street from the inner harbor and a 5 minute walk to Camden Yard. The ride up the glass elevator gives you an awesome view of the inner harbor. The rooftop pool and recreation area was nice, but this is where my only complaints are. The life guard was very grouchy! No need for this. He seemed disinterested in being there. Also, there were tennis courts and a putting green. While there were tennis rackets and putters available, they had no tennis balls or no golf balls ... or maybe they did and the grouchy life guard just couldn't be bothered to get them. I would absolutely recommend this hotel. Call the hotel for package deals. We got an aquairium package that included parking and aqairium tickets.

“Wonderful Stay” Stayed two nights at this hotel during a recent business trip. Hotel is located close to the airport, and the room was very nice. Fruit platter/yogurt was excellent and room service was delivered within 15 minutes. Breakfast bar the following morning was also fantastic. My only complaint dealt with a housekeeping issue when I discovered a pubic hair in the tub, and that my car rental program was not credited on my folio. After an e-mail to the GM this was credited, and on my next stay the housekeeping issue was corrected. The walls are a bit paper thin, because I can hear the businessman next door speaking loud with his crew, but overall right place, location and the staff do care about their guests. I would return in the future.

“Very Good accomodations, Great location!” This property is worth raving about, as so many others have already done. Located in the City Center in a seemingly quiet, charming part of town it offers first rate rooms, everything a traveler needs at a reasonable price. It's a short walk to Market Street and the convention center, Reading Rail complex, etc. The neighborhood has an abundance of excellent restaurants, wine bars with excellent food and small coffee houses. The streets are charming, with narrow brick alleys, few buildings over three stories and perfect safety. The only downside we experienced was underpowered window air conditioning units and street noise on Saturday night. If you prefer a firm matress, you'll enjoy the beds - we did not. I would recommend this hotel to anyone because of the location and neighborhood. It's rare to be in a major city for a week and not take a cab anywhere, but it was very easy to walk everywhere. The staff was very accomodating and helpful.

“Great Hotel” Our stay was from 13th August to the 17th. The place was terrific, modest and very comfortable. Try if possible staying in the rear of the hotel, we stayed in room 402 which was very noisy. The rooms on the front side are very noisy. The street is very busy, Garbage trucks pass every morning around 5am. Everything else was great; the front desk staff was very accommodating. We would definitely go back again.

“Great hotel; very contemporary feel” We stayed at the Hilton Polaris while visiting family back in Columbus. The hotel is fairly new and is decorated in a contemporary style. It actually had lots of design elements that resemble the Conrad Hotel in Chicago, which is Hilton's extreme high end division. Service was very good. I was happy they had my Hilton reward bonus ready when I arrived. I usually have to remind them. Our room had an interesting desk that allowed for a very functional work area. The shower was great. Bed was very good. The only downside was the view. Parking lot and i-71. Not very inspiring. The Polaris area is packed with every chain restaurant possible and a huge mall next door which is great if you're looking for a shopping weekend. Location is okay but it seems a bit far away if you decide to go downtown for dinner or something. Overall a great hotel. I just wish it was downtown.

“They are trying really hard” Was in Seattle for business during a week when there was an enormous international convention which completely overwhelmed the city. However, the staff at the W really gave it their all to try to accomodate all their guests and their needs. When the hotel is full, the public facilities (restaurant, bar and public seating areas) are inadequate, but again, the staff ran around trying to keep people happy. I had a corner room which was lovely and a nice escape from the crowds downstairs and on the street. It wasn't my first choice for a hotel (too big and young crowd), but the only one where I could obtain a reservation. I doubt I will return, but the staff really deserves some recognition of the incredible job they did recently. As with many high end hotels, you are nickel-dimed with internet charges. If the Marriott can provide internet for free why not these hotels?

“Nice hotel, clean rooms, good service” I was ready to bash this hotel at first, but thanks to two dedicated employees (Nicole at the front desk and Floyd the concierge) I changed my mind on this place. I would have given it a five star, but still not happy that you have to pay for Internet! This is walking distance to the Lake, very nice!

“Very Nice Hotel in Great Location in Gaslamp District” Hotel Solamar is another fine example of a Kimpton Hotel - chic and swanky. Its location is ideal with respect to the gaslamp district. It is in walking distance to many fine restaurants, a movie theater and Petco park. It is an amitious walk to Balboa Park but it is certainly is an option for most. The hotel was clean and appeared to be newer. The pool / bar area is very nice although I am not sure everyone would be comfortable with the pool area being combined with the bar. The hotel offers complimentary wine each evening in the lobby for an hour. I would highly recommend this hotel to adults. I am not sure it is the best selection for those traveling with children. If you are staying at Hotel Solamar you must visit Heavenly Cupcake across the street and up a block or two. It is a cupcake lounge - serving only cupcakes. A great little treat!

“Terrific x 2” Just completed my second stay at The Royalton. This is a terrific hotel. Nothing has changed near as I can tell from my prior visit, but it remains in good order and very well maintained. What stands out from my second experience is the staff. I cannot fault one of them. Unfailingly friendly, helpful, cheerful. I was only there two night but I could tell they were making an effort to remember their guests by face, at least. Can't think of a single staff member who wasn't friendly and motivated. They are running a terrific hotel.

“Nice enough but a few major quirks” The James is a very attractive property. Aesthetically, it is well designed and the location is excellent for visiting Tribeca and SOHO. The hotel offers some unexpected perks such as complimentary drinks and snacks in the lobby; however, it has some quirks that are unexpected and disappointing: - very few power outlets in the rooms. existing outlets are awkwardly placed making them very hard to use. unbelievable for new construction - an in-room coffee maker is provided but you must place it in the bathroom sink or on the floor near the curtains in order to plug it in - no desk / work area - no kitchen / restaurant I liked the James but wanted to like it more. It is fine if you get a good deal but it would be extremely disappointing if the room rates were above $300/$350 USD.

“Wonderful place to stay” Spent one night at The Argonaut and wish that we could have stayed longer. We even missed the free wine hour but what the heck, the staff was so pleasant and not in a superficial,' I don't mean it' kind of way. Valet was on top of their game and was very helpful with directions or anything we might need. The roofm was super clean and I was looking for dirt in the areas that sometimes don't get the best housekeeping job. I couldn't find as much as a crumb! We were on the fourth floor in a two queen bedded room as we were traveling with our two children. We were upgraded to a Cannery/Alcatraz view because of our membership in Kimpton's In Touch program but it was really just a view of the Mexican restaurant below unless you really, really cranked your head. Still nice to receive. We also had a note welcoming us and a big bottle of water but didn't drink it because it didn't say it was complementary. Overall a great experience and I wouldn't hesitate to return whenever I am in the San Francisco area. Great decor. This was our first stay in a Kimtpon property but I am going to seek them out from now on.

“Breakfast is almost worth the stay” Very nice, small hotel in a terrific neighborhood section of NYC (Murray Hill) with the 6 Subway line a block away. Not far from Grand Central and Empire State Building. Rooms are all right. Bathrooms are a little small. The hotel staff is okay, not the friendliest bunch, but they also weren't rude. Though I will admit, a friendly, outgoing staff does make a huge impression! The best part about the stay was the free "continental" breakfast. It was fabulous. In addition to regular continental fare, it included meats and cheese tray and croissants. That was enough for us until dinner that night.

“Great location - classy hotel” The location for this hotel is fantastic. Less than two blocks from Boston Common and the Park subway stop. Beautiful lobby. Very easy check-in. The rooms were very classy. Yes the traditional double was a bit on the small side but that's just the way things are in hotels of this era. Got a very good rate from an external website (less than $140 per night including taxes). I enrolled in Omni's loyalty programme which provided free coffee delivery in the morning, free internet, and free pressing and shoeshine (though why I would want my runners shined or my jeans pressed I am not sure). Overall a very classy hotel with very helpful staff.

“Great location, modern room, good breakfast” My wife and me stayed after Christmas and had a pretty positiv experience. Check in was smooth, staff is friendly and the lobby is modern. The room is typical HGI except for the size but it is Mahattan. The hotel is clean, one has to have a key to get up to floors. The breakfast staff is very friendly and the food was good. Macy, subway and lots of convienance very near. It is worth a stay.

“Excellent and very centrally placed” We went there on our honeymoon, we found the hotel very comfortable , clean , staff very pleasant.As with most places in U.S.A it was room only, this was not a problenm as plenty places nearby to dine at .Hotel was very busy when we were there but staff were always polite and willing to help us .Hotel got us tickets to go and see a basketball game which worked out expensive, if wanting to do same i would reccomend going to Times Square where tickets for everything availableat a fraction of the price.

“Great Location; good weekend rates” This hotel is a great choice for a visit to Washington DC, especially for a long weekend. Both times I stayed, in July and December 2006, great weekend rates were available on the Hilton website. As a hotel, the property is no different than any other Hilton Garden Inn, other than it is a part of a city block, rather than a freestanding building. Except for rooms facing 14th street, rooms do not have views. My recollection is that the rooms facing 14th Street are slightly larger, too. The rooms are nice - beds are comfortable and the ergonomic chair at the large desk is very comfortable. There is free high speed internet. The hotel has an elaborate breakfast buffet, but can be quite busy. The hotel's best aspect is its location. It is right across 14th St. from the McPherson Square Metro location (Orange / Blue lines), and is within a 5-10 minute walk of the Pennsylvania Ave. side of the White House (via New York Ave). There are numerous restaurants in walking distance, although a number of the more inexpensive / quick service locations are closed on weekends. One exception is Corner Bakery - three blocks south on 14th. The area surrounding the hotel is not the busiest on weekends, but I did not feel unsafe, particularly walking on 14th down to Pennsylvania Ave, etc. With the Metro so accessible, there is really no need to walk to the Smithsonian or monuments, but if you want to do so, it is just over a mile to the Washington Monument and slightly more to the Smithsonian. That said, even taking the Metro to the Smithsonian stop will still result in a walk of almost one half mile to the Washington Monument. As the hotel is across the street from the Blue Line, you can ride the Blue Line to or from the airport. However, unless you really wish to save money, taking a taxi is quicker and should not cost more than $20, even with a tip. This is a great spot to stay for a weekend visit for very reasonable rates. You're getting a great location at a reliable, mid market chain hotel.

“Good location, nice hotel” Stayed here on business for 3 nights.
