Room was clean, bed was comfortable (although not one of those heavenly beds), and room was quiet despite that the hotel was at capacity. Location was wonderful for shopping, walking. Located near great restaurants: Sole Food at the Loews Hotel across the street, Starbucks in the lobby, the Reading Terminal Market has loads of food kiosks--- try the Down Home Diner for breakfast (it opens at 7 AM). I did not eat at any of the Marriott's restaurants, so I can't speak for them. The negatives: When I made my reservation I specifically asked for a room without an adjoining door. I reiterated this requirement upon check-in, but when I got to my room, it had one. So on the phone I called their special number for customer service, and got bounced around to different people. Was finally told to go back down to the front desk (a pain to do with my luggage). I was then given a fine room, but I think they should have had someone come up with the new key. Bathroom could have used a makeup mirror and there was no bathrobe (which they should include since they have a pool in the hotel). Also, one afternoon it poured rain---there was no umbrella in my closet and the concierge did not have any to lend. The concierge service seemed to be understaffed---there was quite a line to ask him a question mid-day. Overall I would recommend it, but will probably try the Loews across the street next time.

“Wonderful stay at 4 Point Sheraton” Spent 4 days at this gem hotel back in July and totally enjoyed the experience. To begin with, New York hotels are expensive all year around even for a single room especially during the summer months. So when I found out this hotel offers a special rate of $140 a night for a nice double room in the middle of Manhattan with free internet included, I had to jump on the deal even it is 3 months ahead! Location of the hotel is simply unbeatable - in the heart of Chelsea between 6th & 7th. Hotel premise is on the quiet W. 25th street, totally tucked away from the busy traffic. So many shops and restaurants around and easy walking distance to subway stations with multiple metro lines (E line at 8th/23rd St. takes you directly to JFK). Definitely a good base for NYC trips. It is a not a new hotel but 4 Points did a good job of maintaining the interior/decor updated. My room was definitely roomy (considering this is NYC and you will pay a premium for space) and nicely decorated with two twin-beds, work station, LCD tv and an OK bathroom. Couldn't be happier with the space. . Hotel does come with a nice bar and a restaurant with outdoor seating which I did not use as NYC is filled with great eateries in every neighborhood so it's best to explore the dining options outside. Internet as mentioned, is included in the rate but there are two free computer downstairs in the lobby for guest use if you don't have a laptop. Many reviews here complained about the front desk staff and service but I did not encounter such problem during my entire stay. In fact, I considered them pretty ok, I guess it all depends on who you ran into. Maid service, on the other hand, could have been a bit better but it did not bother me too much. In all, this is an above average hotel from the amenities point of view. However for the room space you get - if you find a good rate, I must say this hotel provides some very good value. I have stayed in a number of other NYC hotels with smaller rooms, older facilities, mediocre service and significantly higher price before, all I can say is this 4 Point Sheraton certainly beats all of them. I would definitely return in the future, if I can find a special rate again.

“Loved it! Would Stay Again! (for the right price)” I am a native San Jose gal so this was my first time staying at the Fairmont. My sister and I had a double/double room in the main building (supposedly other towers are more expensive because they are remodeled, or something to that affect). I wasn't going to pay an extra $30 just for brand new and I'm glad I didn't. Pulled into valet/check in and only had time to check in before leaving again so the valet kindly let me park for 10 minutes. Check in was easy. Love love love the room. Bathroom, huge! Beds, comfy! Tons of space throughout the room. Everything even looked new so I wasn't feeling left out. There is a huge closet in the vanity area, which is separate from the actual bathroom, which is also separate from the toilet. Brilliant. Now we can all get ready and not bump into each other. Dislike $26 valet parking. Not sure where else you would park though. Dislike the bar in the main building closes at midnight. You can still sit in the round seating around but no drinks or food. Boo. You can however go to the store and buy alcohol to drink in that area..so we did! (huge wedding party not ready for bed yet). Check out was a breeze, they send you an email and you can check out from there. Oh yeah, and free Wifi. Great location for downtown SJ. Walking distance to tons of restaurants. Definitely coming back here if the price is right!

“Great Stay at this Times Square Area Hotel” This hotel is located one block away from Broadway and 48th St. It is a very easily accessible hotel from Eighth Ave and has a lot of great things here. Rooms are very comfortable and the staff go out of there way to say hello and help in any way they can. The front desk staff was just great and kept me entertained each night i was there. My room looked out at Eighth Ave, and to the exception of the Firehouse next door there was no noise that i could hear. The internet access was good and the tv selection was good as well. Only about a 5 min drive from NY Penn Station and less than a 10 min drive to Javits Convention Center. This hotel is very popular with groups and business travelers. There is a business center located in the front lobby and there is a small store that have the usual luxuries. The restaurant is good and if you are a preferred Hilton Member you get a free breakfast included in your stay each day. I would stay here again.

“They took great care of my in-laws on their anniversary” I am late in posting this review, but back in August I booked a weekend for my in-laws to celebrate their 50th anniversary. They had a wonderful time and said the hotel staff catered to their every need. The staff sent up Champagne and chocolate cover strawberries, which I did not request, but they were very helpful in working out the details for me, on transportation to and from the train station, breakfast and dinner at a nearby steak house. My in-laws raved about the hotel, particularly the service. Thanks Hilton!

“Much Improved” This hotel has been updated since the last time here. Rooms are very nice, well appointed. Location to the Theaters and Times Square is great. Only a few blocks away. Breakfeast is a zoo at 8AM, try to go earlier or later. Staff is very helpful.

“Not my type of hotel” This is really not my type of hotel - huge, boring, impersonal, blunt, business-like - but there are a lot of good things to say. The gym is great, which is really important! And there are several great yogastudios nearby, which is even better. The location is perfect and there is a large grocery store across the street, which means you can buy your own breakfast, etc. All in all, for being a type of a hotel I don't really like, it is absolutely perfect! And Boston is of course a wonderful city!

“Excellent value and service” I stayed here one night on a Priceline stay. What impressed me so much as a frequent traveler is that sometimes Priceline guests complain (though I never have) that they are treated different than full paying customers. I called ahead of time, gave them my Hyatt Rewards number and requested a king room in the remodeled west tower. When I checked in Chris K. who provided outstanding customer service throughout the stay, gave me a beautiful corner room on the 30th floor overlooking the city. He also recommended an excellent dinner/drinks place named Sweetwater. I later checked to see if there was somewhere in the hotel to get free internet and they ended up comping that as well. Additionally, there is a great fitness center with numerous cardio machines with their own TV's and free weights and machines. I will definitely stay here again when I return to Chicago. Cheers. Marius

“Nice hotel, desk staff need to try harder” I've stayed here a few times while on business in the Los Angeles area. Let me start by saying that it appears they are doing some renovation to the hotel, which is a plus. The place was starting to look a bit dated. Rooms are like-quality to some of those in Waikiki (rundown, disrepair) but the last time I stayed there the room was awesome and seemed to have been fixed up. I usually book directly with the reservations person at the hotel and she is awesome! The check-in staff however, have ALWAYS been miserable, unfriendly and impolite. Definitely need to fix that! There is a great little bakery in the lobby featuring Krispy Kreme and the restaurant is good too. Beware of parking gouge. $13.95 per night self-park or $23.95 for valet. And in that neighbourhood, you probably want valet so prepare to be gouged. Definitely ask for a room away from the runway, otherwise your view and sound all night will be of planes taking off and landing at LAX. My mistake the first time. Also, this place does not offer free Wi-Fi like the rest of the modern, hotel world. Definitely a knock against a hotel of this calibre. I recommend this place if you are looking for somewhere safe and clean in the Inglewood area.

“Nice hotel but very small room” The hotel is at out skirt of downtown. There is view of downtown but the hotel is not in downtown. Downtown is only 5 minutes away. It’s close to the mile high stadium, the aquarium, and REI. It’s right off Rt.25, very convenient location. There are several hotels next door and a gas station. Since the hotel is not in downtown, parking is free. If you stay at downtown hotel, parking is like $20-$30 / day. The hotel is new and had the modern Hampton Inn décor. Like any standard Hampton In, breakfast area is right off the lobby. Nice continental breakfast with hot items like scramble eggs, sausage, or hams, or home fried, fresh fruits. Coffee and tea are available all day next to the lobby. However, our room 401 is the smallest room we ever stayed at in the U.S. This is like the European size room. It has a king size bed, a chair, desk, dresser, microwave, and mini fridge. Opening of the closet door would block the hallway. There is just enough room to walk around the bed, and enough room for 2 people with 2 suitcases. The mini fridge was very loud. The bathroom is also very small. The saving grace is the room is new and had a view of downtown. Overall, the hotel meets the Hampton Inn standard, which is good quality.

“Better Than Expected” When I pulled up in the front of the hotel. The valet was backed up, hotel guest were standing out front and their children were running around to where I did not want to check in. However, once I surrender my car keys and checked in everything was alright. My suite was comfortable, clean and had all of the amenities I needed. Plus it was quiet on my floor. I had breakfast at the hotel every morning. Coffee was a great way to plan my day and catch up on e-mail. Every evening there was a little snake and the menu was posted on my fridge. The bed was so comfortable. My room looked right out over the ALAMO!

“Suprisingly good!” Thisd is one of those non-descript hotels near an airport. Presumably the only reason you are staying here is to catch an early flight or resting up after a long flight. We took the shuttle bus from the airport (called the hotel, and the shuttle arrived right on time); we checked in (the lobby was crowded with kids in Denver for a basketball tournement) and the room was fine -- and very quiet. No airplane noise. And no noise from the kids playing basketball! The breakfast was really quite good. And the ride back to the airport was efficient and on time. Overall -- it is a good deal!

“Nice surprise” I used points to book this centrally located hotel having just flown in from London. I was not looking to spend money on my first night since I arrived in the evening. What a great surprise, the hotel is conveniently located for Times Square and Macys, it is very well priced. It appears that many stay here for an extended period in excess of a week. The room is clean and has all amenities including a microwave and little kitchenette with a fridgefreezer. Although I was only there for half a day I really liked it, it feels like the way forward for travellers especially in the USA. You get value - including free WIFI rather than having to spend money on these things at the upmarket chains.There was even a DVD collection for those who want a quiet evening. The hotel has many floors and it seems 6 or 8 rooms to a floor so every room is near a lift. It isn't a problem though if you keep normal times. I would recommend staying here, especially if you have points - in which case due to the conversion rate it is probably the best bargain in NY!

“Service is what distinguishes this hotel” It's the service that differentiates Four Seasons & this one is no exception. Very welcoming at check-in and all subsequent staff reinforce service is top priority. Of course, pay higher cost for Four Seasons than other hotels in the area. Great location in the Back Bay, comfortable rooms. I personally like the bottled water at turn down (rather than chocolate).

“Nice stay” Was in town for a game and the stay was nice. What can I say...there was a bar inside and other bars in the vicinity so location was ok too. It's a cab ride over to the game action and once you get back there's a comfy bed to stumble onto and pass out on. Fitness area is adequate and it was nice and clean.

“Location Makes It Work” I did not choose this hotel. It was the site of a conference that I was attending. I expected not to like it very much, but I was wrong. Yes, it is large and somewhat impersonal. Yes, the Sheraton lacks some charm. But, there was a lot "right" with the hotel. First, it is located right on the river and within walking distance of Michigan Avenue and the Navy Pier. Second, the rooms were decent size with comfortable beds, quality flat TVs, and nice views. Third, for the most part, the staff were accommodating, friendly, and helpful. Fourth, there was a pleasant riverside place to have a coffee or a drink and lots of services from restaurants to business center to Fedex location to even a quality shoe shine service.

“Top notch all the way. Great service and views!” While it certainly doesn't hurt to have Gold Status with Marriott, this hotel lived up to and exceeded my expectations for business travel. Prompt, courtesy front desk staff. Great selection of food and beverage in concierge lounge. Wonderful views of the bay. They let me check in at 11am (early), no problems. Great workout facility. Fun and relaxing pool and pool bar scene. I enjoyed my stay here. I would take my family here and stay for pleasure as well. Great experience.

“great W experience” I stayed at the W Dec 17 for 3 days, and really enjoyed it. I had a wonderful room with all the W goodies (Bliss products, flat screen tv, etc) and the signature bed, which was great. The overall vibe of the hotel is very trendy and cool, lots of celebrities and people w/money, but I still felt very comfortable as the staff is amazingly welcoming and friendly. I loved Craft resturant-killer food, and the Bliss Spa is awesome-the girls up there are dolls! Treated me like a queen. But the room service is my favorite: warm choc chip cookies w/organic skim milk! I'll stay there again in a heart beat (My only problem is the location could be more central; but there are plans to build up the area).

“Unbeatable Location” Our best friend from San Jose drove us into the hotel in the evening on a cold day and we stayed here for 4 nights enjoying the fabulous location in the Fisherman's Wharf . We stayed in a double bedded family room which was good for all of us and we enjoyed the fact that very good restaurants were all close by as was ghiradelli chocolate. Check in & Out was smooth --internet facility was a cool plus--Rooms were standard holiday inn fare and cleanliness was normal

“Great gateway to Inner Harbor” This hotel is a hidden chain gem. We were able to check in early after an overnight flight and light rail ride into town. Service was excellent and friendly. The lobby is delightful for breakfast or hanging out. This is converted bank so the lobby has high ceilings and is very spacious. Down a spiral staircase is the small fitness room (A/C problems during our stay) and a cool meeting room inside the old vault - the door is still intact. It's a short walk to the Inner Harbor and the purple line Charm Circulator (free bus) stops nearby. I'm a Platinum SPG member and usually stay at Starwood properties but I'm glad that we tried this Marriott. We'll be back! This is not an upscale experience but very solid hospitality.

“Had a Wonderful Stay” I stayed at the Hotel Vitale for 5 days in late February and recommend it highly. The design of the hotel is perfect for a relaxing getaway in one of the best cities in the world. From the front door to the roof decks, everything is spa-like. (There is also an actual spa at the hotel, but I did not try it.) Our room (a king size, bay view) featured soothing colors, natural materials, and even smelled good (not that usual stale hotel smell). The bed had a pristine, white duvet cover. Bedside table has a CD player (with new age-y CD collection) but you can plug your iPod into it. We had a loveseat and arm chair over in the window nook. The bathroom was large, with a glassed-in shower with rainforest shower head. Best of all, the toiletries were made by Fresh and were lovely. The hotel also has 2 roof decks for guest use and a fun restaurant in the lobby - it has an indoor lounge and outdoor terrace that seem to be extremely popular with young businesspeople. The restaurant isn't cheap, but it's worth checking out. We found every staff person we interacted with to be friendly and helpful. In addition to turndown service, a manager came by in the evening to make sure everything was to our liking - a pleasant touch. The location was great for us - right across the street from the Ferry Terminal, where we found a few good restaurants, lots of great snacks (including Cowgirl Creamery for cheese, a great bread store and a wine shop), and an incredible outdoor Farmer's Market twice a week (Tuesday and Saturday). If you're not a walker, the hotel is about 2 blocks from one end of the cablecar line as well as the Embarcadero BART station, and the streetcars go past the hotel as well. We found it a convenient walk to Union Square, the SF Moma, etc., but we really like walking. The only thing we didn't like about the hotel was the supposedly high-speed internet. The free internet service moved at a crawl, whether you were wireless or plugged in. There was also a paid option. But for the amount the room cost, and how little internet costs, they really should provide genuinely high speed connections for free (as they advertise). You may not have any need for internet, but if you are traveling on business be aware that connecting to the office won't be easy. However, in all, it's a really fabulous place and I completely recommend it.

“Traditional hotel with pleasant staff” LA Athletic Club is conveniently located with an incredible fitness center, warm and welcoming staff with well appointed rooms. While the building is older, the rooms are big, comfortable and allow for a quiet night's sleep. Love the iHome to charge my phone!

“Very modern” Enjoyed our stay at this hotel, it doesn't look that impressive from the outside but the rooms are very nice, excellent decor and a bathroom you could live in. Extremely good location we did not eat in the hotel but others from our tour did with good revirews. We would recommend a cafe called West Egg on North Fairbanks opposite the Doubletree Hotel, great breakfast.

“Great Hotel with Large Rooms” This is a very nice hotel. I've stayed in several Boston hotels over the last few years and I would rank this one at or near the top. Everything was clean and the staff was friendly. The room was larger than most hotels in Boston except for maybe the rooms at the Custom House which are all suites. The location is about a mile walk to Hanover Street which is nice if you want to burn off some pasta calories. While I didn't spend much time in the hotel other than to sleep, it seemed to have an energetic feel to it on the first floor near the restaurant. I had the impression that it is a place where business professionals may go to close out the day. The location is also convenient to Boston Logan. I would definately stay there again.

“Great location, small but comfortable and practical rooms.” I had the smallest room between the 4 of us that went to Philadelphia, but it was clean, it was comfortable, and there weren't many noises from the inside. That being said, our first night in town was a Saturday night, and if you've got a room that is on the side of the hallway that is away from the elevators it is located right over a cab stand. We didn't get much sleep that night, but it was much better on Sunday night. We didn't eat dinner at the restaurant, Davios, however the breakfast was absolutely terrific and more than reasonably priced. Overall I will look for Club Quarters locations when I travel again, and when we go back to Philadelphia next year will make sure to eat breakfast everyday at Davios. Oh, as a side note, you've got to park at the Liberty Mall across the street, as there is no "hotel" parking.

“Best budget choice for SF tourists” I always advise first-time visitors to San Francisco to stay in the Union Square area. It is and always has been the heart and soul of the city, and it remains the most upscale and desirable location for out-of-towners. But I do suggest that they map any hotel they're interested in, because a number of the properties that advertise their location as "Union Square" are actually 5-10 blocks away. In downtown SF, even two blocks can mean the difference between upscale and ghetto. So this hotel receives high marks right off the bat for being in the very heart of Union Square, just around the corner from Macy's, and the Powell Street cable running past the front door. Although this a 100-year-old property, you wouldn't know it from the appearance of the guest rooms. The owners have recently completed a major renovation, with new paint, carpets, furniture and fixtures, eliminating every trace of the musty smell common in these old buildings, and creating a very warm relaxing environment. The rooms are small, no doubt, but perfectly adequate. The majority of travelers, especially those used to the older hotels in Europe, won't have a problem. Our suite was on the fifth floor front, facing the street and with the bedroom sharing a wall with the elevator shaft, yet the room was extremely quiet. If you have kids I recommend the family suite, with one room with two twin beds and a second bedroom in back with a queen. Both rooms have wall-mounted flat screen TV's and phones. The service at this hotel is the friendliest I've experienced in any hotel in San Francisco. The complimentary breakfast is decent cereal, toast, muffins, juice and coffee. It does the job, although some fruit, and maybe a cereal option for kids (rather than just granola) would be nice. The breakfast room is light and airy and enjoys a great view of the action on Powell Street. Overall, this has to be the best choice for budget travel in the city. The location is the main selling point, but this hotel offers clean, quiet rooms and friendly service for a very affordable rate, so I'd recommend it even if it were off the beaten path.

“Clean, great location, excellent breakfast” Loved this new marriott property. The location was great for downtown, within walking distance to riverwalk, river center and many great restaurants. The hotel is very new, and is physically attached to the Fairfield Inn, with a shared pool and workout area. The room was spacious and clean. The breakfast buffet was excellent - great variety of hot and cold items and the famous Texas waffles :) Coffee was available all day, which was great after a long day of meetings. Staff was very nice. i would definitely stay here again. I found a lightly traveled side-street nearby where there were parking meters from 8am-6pm, at 25 cents per hour. It cost $2 to park for 2 days vs $21 for valet

“Good Hotel in a Very Busy Location” We originally had no intention of staying here, but our favorite San Francisco hotel was booked and we were able to secure a very good room rate, so decided to give this SOMA hotel a try. Overall, we were pleased with our visit, with a few reservations. This is an extremely large hotel, near the Moscone Center, so it is heavily utilized by conventioneers and tour groups. Located less than a block from Market Street, the Westfield Mall and near Union Square, the area is extremely crowded and busy with traffic, pedestrians and the inevitable San Francisco street people. The hotel elevators and hallways are like a maze and rather confusing until you get your bearings. However, our room was good sized, clean and quiet, despite the many guests staying over the weekend we were there. The maids were very helpful and accommodating to us. The front desk personnel were also helpful and attentive to all the guests, even when the lobby was packed with people coming and going. Our concierge, Dave, was fantastic, friendly and helpful, full of great, local dining information which we made excellent use of. I also noticed when the concierge line backed up, other staff members immediately came up to offer help to the waiting guests. So despite the large size of the property, crowded with guests in an extremely busy location, the staff helped to make our stay very enjoyable. I would definitely consider the Marriott Marquis again, if our preferred hotel is unavailable.

“Terrific” This is a mega hotel, which I don't usually like, but stayed here for a conference & was very pleasantly surprised. It is worth the extra money for a bay view room, because the view was fabulous. I had a room in the North Tower with a small balcony & it was delightful. The only downside is that all the bay view rooms also face the pool area so you can expect some noise during the day. It also happened that some noisy fools decided to head for the pool at 3:00 AM one night & woke me up. I called the front desk & they responded right away by sending security out - noise was stopped & problem resolved immediately. The room was comfortable, quiet, clean & the decor fresh. The hotel was extremely busy, but I was impressed by the professionalism, and smooth flow of check in/out & the bell men who practically ran to keep everyone happy. Great location - you can walk to Seaport Village & to Gaslamp easily. Overall, definitely exceeded my expectations & I would return.

“awesome service, fantastic spa, great in-room dining” Stayed here for two nights and had a wonderful time. My room was spacious and traditionally furnished. The bed had good quality linens and was comfortable. The robes - plush. I liked the L'Occitane toiletries as well. I ordered room service several times. Each time, the food came on time and was delicious and nicely presented. Try the eggs benedict with smoked salmon for breakfast -- a bit salty but very tasty (the eggs are done perfectly). My favorite part of the stay was a fantastic deep tissue massage I got at the spa (I received a $40 off coupon at check-in). After the massage, which was some of the best I've ever had, I spent some time in the heated pool and hot tub/whirlpool. They also have a steam room, but I could not take any more heat. The ladies' locker rooms are nicely appointed, spacious, and have a good array of creams and lotions. There are carafes with orange infused water, some kind of fruit drink, and a selection of teas with honey. I also tried out the fitness center, which is not large, but equipped with a nice variety of machines. The location cannot be beat.

“Comfort and a big flat screen TV” I stayed there two nights for a business seminar and the staff was friendly, efficient and accomodating to my requests. The room was immaculate, large and comfortable. Even though I did not watch much TV, I enjoyed the fact that the huge flat screen had numerous inputs for various media like my laptop. The price is very reasonable for the high quality provided. The bars and activity are a short trip up the interstate to down town.
“Fun place” Room was a little small, but very nice. Free water was a nice touch. Ask for a room that faces the river. Wireless worked OK. Everything is in walking distance. Staff was FIRST CLASS!!!!

“Older hotel with great service and a superb location” We wanted a place with a more personal feel (rather than those big corporate hotel chains) so we asked a local for a recommendation and she suggested the Park Manor Suites. The hotel is a mix of good, and not so good so I'll try to give both sides. First, we stayed during a period of warmer than usual October temperature (80 F / 26 C) so the most apparent downside to staying at the hotel was the lack of air conditioning. We were on vacation with friends so we occupied a 2-bedroom suite (which had 2 king beds, a balcony overlooking the park, a queen-sized sofa bed in the living room, a dining room and a kitchen. There were 3 TVs but we never turned them on (too busy). Our friends stayed in a 1-bedroom suite which had similar features but in place of the sofa bed was a standard sofa plus there was a "murphy' bed (fold out bed, that was stored in a compartment in the wall in the living room. Both our rooms had whisper-quiet ceiling fans that did an excellent job of keeping the rooms at a comfortable temperature during the day. When I went to sleep, however, I turned my ceiling fan off (since the breeze from it was disturbing me in bed). There was a different fan (mounted on a pedestal) that was in the closet that i could have used but I didn't bother. As it turned out, on all three nights, I awakened in the morning with a "soggy pillow" (so to speak) as the temperature had risen a little during the night (probably from the heat rising from the lower floors of the building -- we were near the top). I could have plugged in the pedestal fan on subsequent nights but I didn't bother -- so, it's up to you. All in all, it wasn't a huge problem. The only other negatives would be that the baths and kitchens are showing some wear. The room was immaculate but the kitchen cabinet doors were a little warped in places, the grout/caulk in the tub had small areas with a little bit of black on them (as someone involved in property management, I can tell you that it's difficult to remove these types of black marks once they "set in"). In addition, there was an occasional rusty spot on some of the old hardware. To me, I didn't consider the room "dirty" because of these small stains but i know there are some that would feel differently. The decor was pleasant, if not a little quirky in places. We noticed a couple of prints in one corner of the living room depicting a woman and a goose in a rather unconventional pose. (Don't get me wrong. It wasn't licentious -- just a little strange! I think they called it "art" in the 1920s/1930s. Our 2-bedroom suite had large rooms: both bedrooms had king beds. There was a sofa and a couple of wing chairs in the living room and the dining room had a table and 4 chairs. The balcony overlooking the park was small (you could stand maybe 2 people) but it was a lovely view. The kitchen had a stove, microwave and refrigerator. I can''t say enough about how great the service was. We were three friends coming from 3 different cities, arriving at three different times and the hotel was great at recommending appropriate room sizes, getting us oriented, suggesting restaurants, etc. Especially outstanding was Joe at the front desk/reception. There was a business center with a PC that you could use at no charge. The rooftop (7th floor) was a restaurant / meeting room / dual balcony areas where complimentary breakfast was served (great views) as well as lunch (extra charge). There is a Friday night party between 5 pm and 10 pm that is open to the guests as well as the public. The hotel does not advertise the party but it is well-known and has been going on for years. It is mostly attended by gay people in the city but my friends and I (as well as other guests we spoke to) felt perfectly comfortable at the party. It takes place on the northeast patio of the roof as well as in the inside penthouse meeting room so there are spectacular views. My "alcohol heavy" mixed drink cost $6 -- a buy. (I'm told that the bartender at the outdoor patio bar pours the stiffer drinks; I guess I got lucky). My friends and I both had rental cars and we had no problem parking in the parking lot (included) even on Friday evening during the party. The parking area is NOT open to the public (in spite of a prior reviewer's allusion to the contrary) but the hotel did explain to us when we checked in that there are not quite enough spaces for all of the rooms but since some people don't have cars it is unlikely that there would not be parking. In any event, except for Friday night, there appeared to be ample parking adjacent to the hotel. The location of the hotel cannot be beat. Literally steps to Balboa Park. There is a free tram that picks up every 15 minutes adjacent to the hotel that stops throughout the massive park. The Hillcrest neighborhood is within walking distance and has plenty of eating and drinking places. Getting to the airport is a snap (I did it a bunch of times, picking up and dropping off my friends). You just drive south on Park to Laurel, turn right and take it to the end. (About 10 minutes) We got to the Wild Animal Park, Pacific Beach and Coronado Island with no difficulty. There is a piano bar and restaurant on the lower level (below the lobby, a tiny bit below street level). We didn't eat there but we heard good things from other guests. All in all, a most pleasant stay.

“Excellent hotel with good service” Four of us stayed three nights at the Kimberly Hotel. The location is near the Waldorf-Astoria. We had two double beds, large living room with pull out sofa and full kitchen with dishwasher. We ate breakfast in every day and one dinner. The hotel has a complimentary three hour cruise with lunch that was wonderful. Our sofa bed was lumpy and if we had said something the hotel would have supplied a roll-a-way. I would highly recommend the Kimberly.

“Decent Hotel on the Boston Outskirts” First off, this hotel is between Southie and Dorchester, Thats not a bad thing, but its really not "in boston". Second off, despite a previous reviewer stating that it was "about a mile" to the JFK T-Stop on the Red Line, its absolutely not. It was a 5-minute walk, 1/4 mile. Very doable, and perhaps the best part of this hotel. The hotel is decent. Stayed on the 6th floor which I guess had been recently renovated. Room furnishings were nice. Bathroom was a bit dated (don't think that had been touched in the renovations). Parking is easy. $10 a day. Probably not worth having a car in Boston anyway, so skip it and use cabs and the T. Warm cookies at check-in. Ask for an extra. Wireless Internet costs money, unless your a HHonors Gold or Diamond member. Free wireless is available in the lobby. The wireless is painstakingly slow though. Don't expect to stream music, or movies or anything. I ended up using my Verizon 4G Wireless card. Starbucks on the first floor. Little Bistro with it as well offering sandwiches. Not a real restaurant, but in Boston, why would you want to eat in the hotel anyway. Take the T into Boston and eat at the TONS of amazing restaurants. In fact, Dorchester offers some quant spots for dining as well. Didnt use the free shuttle, but I suppose its available to take you just about anywhere in Boston. Would definitely stay again.

“Great spot for New Year's Eve and Day” This is my family's 4th year staying at the Doubletree for New Year's Eve and Day celebrations. You cannot beat the location for the mummer's parade on the day or for all central Philadelphia locations to celebrate the eve. The staff is on full force both days with nothing but smiles for all of the guests checking in. It has become a tradition for the children to collect some party favors from the staff that is offered in the lobby and enjoy the fun atmosphere generated by the staff. There is a tremendous amount of security the day of the parade that we greatly appreciate. The rooms are always clean and spacious. The rooms located by the ice machines can get noisy but I like the convenience of having ice outside my door and simply use a sleep/white noise app on my iPad to sleep. We will be returning again next year and I want to thank all of the staff for another wonderful weekend!

“Close to Galeria” Always very pleased with this property - clean, spacious rooms. Friendly, professional staff. Good, diverse fitness center (not just cardio machines). Nice spa (though can be a bit pricey). Close to Galleria, but thankfully not the insane traffic other properties closer to mall have to endure. Welcome drink is nice. Large red delicious apples are always available - nice touch! Great on-site restaurant, a must-visit. Look forward to returning!

“A nice option in the overtly touristic Fisherman's Wharf area” Free wi-fi, standard HI Express breakfast (some hot items), 3-4 blocks from Fisherman's Wharf and the core of the San Franciso tourist area are great assets for this hotel. When you combine this to the fact that most rooms are in great shape (the hotel is either relatively new and refurbished), and prices that are lower than other options in the area (yet still expensive), you can't go really wrong with the HI Express Fisherman's Wharf. Upon check-in, staff was very friendly and did their best to accomodate our early check-in request, which they were able to do. We were two couples/families travelling together and they were able to provide us with facing (but non-connecting) rooms. Upon check-in, I was offered a fridge to keep the baby formula and other baby items cold (at no extra charge) which I found very nice. Unfortunately, I had to ask twice to get it done. Although there were no microwave in the room, the front desk staff also offered to use their own micro-wave to heat baby food/formula if required. Room size was good and amenities as promised. Houseleeping did a good job throughout the stay. The rooms did not offer any views (inside courtyard). AC/heating functioned just fine. Breakfast was nothing to write home about - but at least they had sufficient # of high chairs for the # of families eating at the same time. It was relatively busy in the morning and not always easy to find a table for 4 but it was still reasonable. Quality was ok. Area was clean. One negative, but this is probably going to be for any hotel in the area is the $40+ charged each night for parking - and the valet staff wasn't that friendly nor helpful to start with. Getting to/from the hotel to other location in SF, including the airport was relatively easy. Overall, nice rooms, good staff, and standard HI Express offering and amenities in the heart of one of the great tourist destinations. Could you do better - yes, but if the price is right, a very decent option

“Good For The Money” This was a very good hotel for the money and as i often find with hotels that is an important caveat. I paid 195 per night and 240 for a Saturday night. I would pay more during more expensive times of the year but for this hotel I would shop around. If I got a good rate as compared to other 4 star hotels I would stay there but I wouldn't pay a premium to stay there. The rooms are nice and very very clean. The TVs are rather small and difficult to see from the chair/sofa they provide. However it is nice to have a sitting area in a NYC hotel. The baths are quite nice. I hear what some people are saying about the hotel staff. They are generally friendly but there are a few that are rather abrupt and not that helpful. Service however in terms of things being on time and the twice daily maid service was overall outstanding and very prompt. I passed on the free breakfast because it did not sound that appealing. Instead I ordered in room service. Breakfast was very good although I ordered cereal and berries and coffee each morning which is not too hard to mess up but it came promptly each of the days I was there and the coffee was quite good which is important to me. I did however order a caesar salad and a calamari one afternoon and they were both god awful. I requested a room in the back of the hotel to be away from street noise but be forwarned that there is a wind tunnel back there so you do hear that. However if you are a light sleeper that is better than being on the street side I would imagine. Overall this is a very nice hotel that has earned its 4 stars. It could be outstanding if the entire staff was helpful and friendly and if they didn't have a few curt matter of fact employees and if they improved the quality of the room service food. If they really want to enter the wonderful hotel category I would think they would use a good thck glass on the windows because hearing wind does indicate the existing glass is not all that great. The location is terrific. You're close to everything but not in the middle of the madness as with the Times Square Hotels.

“A pet-friendly hotel!” Stayed at Hotel Monaco Seattle for 2 nts. during the past weekend. We travelled with our son & our 2 dogs (they're both small dogs, a Pom. & a Papillon). Chose this hotel mainly because it's a pet-friendly hotel which didn't charge extra for our dogs, & allowed the dogs to stay in the room unsupervised. We got into problem the first nt. We had dinner at Rover's, which was less than 10 mins.' drive from the Hotel. Dinner took much longer time than expected (fr. 6:15 p.m. to 9:15 p.m.). We rec'd 2 phone calls fr. the hotel complaining too much barking from our dogs. When we returned, we actually saw our neighbour moving out, but we did not hear any barking outside our room. We moved our dogs to the other side of the room farthest away from the door. When we left our room the following day, we left our TV on so that our dogs would not be able to hear noises outside our room so easily. We also delayed the cleaning of our room to mid-afternoon when we went sight-seeing with our dogs. Our plan worked, and we rec'd no more complaints. The hotel staff were friendly in general. The wine-reception was fr. 5 - 6 p.m. Only white & red wine, lemonade & water were served. It wasn't very busy when we went there at 5:15, although all tables were occupied. We didn't bother going again the following day. Amenities were L'Occitane as advertisied, which included shower cap, soap, shampoo, condition & lotion. We asked for toothbrushes (I expected L'Occitane's but they brought Colgate's) & slippers, but housekeeping did not bring toothpaste along. We didn't bother to ask again and decided to buy our own in the Pharmacy near the hotel. The animal-print bath-robe was fun for photo-taking purpose. We joined the hotel's "In-Touch Loyalty Program". Housekeeping left voice-message saying the hotel has amenity kit for each of us & asked us to call back. When we called, they brought us one bottle of Evian & a small pack of chocolate, but NOT for each of us though. The hotel has price-matching policy. They will honour any lower rate available from other web-site. In general, an above-average pet-friendly hotel.

“Great Hotel for Lollapalooza” We stayed here for lollapalooza. The hotel was close to grant park, so we could just walk to the festival. There are also plenty of subway lines close to it. The hotel was clean, Great service from the staff.

“Good Value, Usual Kimpton Nice Touches, Get a Curved Shower Rod!” Typical Kimpton panache and fun vibe with lots of little touches that make you know you've been someplace. The value-priced room ($179) was smallish but everything was well done and space was used well EXCEPT that the small bathroom shower rod was straight instead of curved outward, which meant that the shower curtain that had hugged so many before me was all over me, as well. Gross. I reported this upon checkout. Kimpton does so many things right - Aveda products, free wifi, room service menu that included healthy options, nice decor, manager's reception with wine (although then you have to deal with all the hoardes of people who can't resist a free glass of wine), nice staff that's well-trained. Valet parking was slow and undermanned sometimes, but I came and went during the height of theatre traffic, and this hotel is in the heart of the theatre district, so I don't hold it against them. Valet were very accomodating about tracking down my briefcase that I accidentally left in the back of the car. Great location to walk to just about everything. Rooms adequately soundproofed, everything was clean, a good place to stay for business if you can get a good rate.

“Location, location, quality, quality” Spent 2 nights here with another couple and found it totally satisfying. We'd pretty much endorse others' recent comments - nice sized room, king bed with unusually good support. We were on the 5th floor overlooking Bush St. and found it completely quiet. Staff are friendly and eager to help, including making change for the Muni. Wifi was strong in our room. Can't comment on Daffodil (the restaurant) as we didn't eat there. It's an easy walk (in an SF vertical sort of way) to all sorts of dining, Chinatown, etc. One irritating fact of life is that not only is hotel parking predictably exorbitant ($40/day), the valet requests 30 minutes notice to get the car. No harm done since we walked or took the bus everywhere, but in case you need a further reason not to have a car in SF...

“Solid 4 star hotel at a great price :)” I travel to Philly regularly and am a repeat guest of the Marriott. Their recent remodel is wonderful! Public areas, hallways, rooms, baths and convention facilities are top notch. All employees I encountered were professional and friendly. Got a great deal on price line for $90.00 however would totally go back and spend more for such a positive experience...

“quiet, old-world Upper East Side hotel” We enjoyed a very quick 2-day, 1-night stay here over the July 4 weekend. Since we would be spending most of our time at the Met Museum (Alexander McQueen exhibit) on the Upper East Side, I first booked at the Surrey, where we stayed last year, which is a short walk from the Met. When the Plaza Athenee (PA) came up on a private sale website, I reserved here, even though it's 12 blocks further from the Met. Much to my chagrin, the Surrey came up on the same website a short while afterward, but the website has a no refund policy. Although we were "stuck" staying at the PA, we were by no means disappointed. The stay was quite pleasurable, and although the hotel was slightly more inconveniently located for the purpose of our trip, it is very well located for visits to Midtown shopping and to Central Park. The New York PA is a more intimate hotel than the Paris PA, tucked away on residential East 64th St. (as opposed to busy Ave. Montaigne) in the chichi Upper East Side. The elegant lobby walls are painted with trompe l'oeil murals, you are seated at a desk for check-in. Much to our surprise and delight, we were upgraded from a Classic room (lower floor, interior view) to a Deluxe room with a terrace to boot! This is the first time this has happened using this particular website. The room, on the 15th floor out of 17, was large, especially by New York standards, and recently renovated but classically appointed. I would not say the room was technologically advanced. There is a charge for Wifi in the room, but not in the lobby or bar. There was a wet bar with a sink, mini-fridge and cook-top, but no utensils or dishes. The minibar was in another fridge. The bathroom was quite small, with a combo shower-tub and limited counter space by the sink. The terrace was lovely, south-facing, spanning the length of the room, with potted plants and a wooden table and 2 cushioned chairs. A small glimpse of Central Park could be seen to the west. The hotel's public spaces include a bar, restaurant and business center (complimentary) on the first floor, and a spa, fitness center and meeting rooms on the second floor. We had breakfast at the restaurant after plans to dine on our terrace were foiled by rain and thunderstorms; the American breakfast is pricey ($38) but of good quality and convenient. As a fan of the series "Sex and the City", I was aware that a 2 scenes from the series finale that were supposed to take place at the Paris PA were actually filmed here, in the bar and restaurant. Front desk service was excellent on check-in and check-out. The doorman was a tad surly, the bellmen friendly but not always at the ready (but we didn't require their services). The hotel seems to have a large international clientele. I would say this hotel is for the upscale traveler looking for a quiet, intimate, old-world, service-oriented hotel. While my first choices along these lines would be the nearby St. Regis or Peninsula, I would certainly visit the PA again.

“Westin does it again: Great stay at the Waterfront!” The Westin Boston Waterfont is my "go to" place when I take my clients to the Boston Design Center, but this time my wife and I went to celebrate my birthday. And celebrate we did -- a very special thank you to Donna Frechette and the wonderful folks at the Westin for an unexpected upgrade to a Harbor View Suite (awesome room with living room/dining room and bedroom!) and a beautiful cake and candles waiting when we arrived!! It made for a very happy and memorable weekend at the hotel that was already my favorite Boston property!

“Great Stay!” Very happy with this hotel especially since we got such a good deal on it. Clean, comfortable and quiet! Free Wi-Fi and the parking is reasonable at $10/day. It pretty close to all the attractions (Pike's Market is about a 10-15 minute walk) which is nice. Really good coffee at the complimentary breakfast. I would stay here again if I was in the Seattle area.

“Comfortable stay; great bed!” The Fairfield is a nice budget hotel, and the new bedding is extremely comfortable! I needed to be in the Market Center area very early one morning, and since it was just a quick business trip, I didn't want to spend a lot on a room. This part of Dallas isn't the greatest, but I was pleased with Fairfield's security and cleanliness. My only complaint was the musty, strange smell in my room. Once I ran the a/c for awhile, the smell dissipated (or I got used to it). Based upon my experiences with other hotels in the area, I was thrilled to have such a comfortable bed, a clean room, and a quiet a/c. The available breakfast was a pleasant surprise. Based upon other reviews I had expected limited choices, and was pleased to see cereals, bagels, boiled eggs, oatmeal, yogurt, waffles, fruit, etc. Should I ever have a similar short trip to this part of town, I'll stay here again.

“Much Appreciated Upgrade!” I have stayed at the Chicago Hilton before for the Cubs' convention in January. It is a great hotel right on Michigan Avenue, close to all the Chicago attractions. This year we stayed there because we could walk to Soldier's field from the hotel and enjoy a Bear's game. I used a reward stay coupon for the stay, and I knew the hotel was sold out due to the Bears' game. I was shocked when they told us at check in that we were upgraded to a suite! The truth was that they put us in a suite on the executive floor that was the size of an apartment. It had a kitchen, living room, large bedroom and bathroom. The view was spectacular! The staff was over the top great to us. I felt like Mayor Daley! Thank you, Hilton Chicago!

“Faded yet wonderful” August 15-17, 2005 my husband and I spent 3 nights at the Intercontinental Hotel in Chicago, whose locaiton is perfect for walking to the river, the lakeshore, Grant Park, Mich. Ave, and even restaurants in River North. We opted for the rooms in the old portion of the hotel where room and bath were large, beds comfy and we loved overlooking lively Mich. Ave. Decor was a bit worn but on two afternoons at 3 PM, tired from walking the city, we had their glorious old tiled pool to ourselves and felt like we were staying in the Hearst Castle. It was simply wonderful. Beware the hotel bar which couldn't make a drinkable Manhattan.

“Wonderful for Families” We spent 6 nights at The Grand Del Mar from the 8th July. It was the perfect place to have a vacation with our 5-year old children. The Grounds of this Hotel are breathtaking. The scenery is lush and interesting, and the Hotel itself is extremely luxurious. We booked a Prado Suite and were blown away by the two huge "Master" Bathrooms. They really add a "wow" factor to the Suite. High quallity furnishings throughout the property. Our children enjoyed the well stocked Explorer's Club and Adriana and her team do a great job with their young charges. There are a vast assortment of restaurants within a short distance from the property, and LEGOLAND and the Zoo are about 25 minute drive. We enjoyed breakfast every morning at AMAYA. The food quality was consistently good, but not exceptional. Yes, the Hotel is definitely grand and beautiful, but the most impressive part of it, is the SERVICE! The Concierge Team is terrific. I asked Lynette about tickets for LEGOLAND, she not only gave me prices and directions, she printed out all of the height restrictions for the various rides, so my 5-year olds could plan their day! Eugenia & Samuel were equally helpful, all of the time. We had just spent 5 nights at the Ritz Carlton in San Francisco and I would say the Concierge Team at this property far exceeded the service level offered at the Ritz. The Children found lovely toys waiting for them in the Room when we checked in, and their names spelt out in bath sponges, which thrilled them. Every day, we received an edible treat in our Suite. Fruit, chocolates, macaroons... Bryan, the Greeters and the Valet Guys were always courteous, gave great restaurant recommendations and offered cold bottled water whenever we got into our car. The Family Pool area was also enjoyable. Wish I had the time for a Spa trip, but hopefully on our next visit. I had previously booked the Four Seasons Aviara for this trip, and then changed our reservations to the Grand Del Mar. I am absolutely confident I made the best decision for our entire family, we had a wonderful time!

“Comfortable & Convenient” While rooms tend to be on smalled side they are well appointed and very comfortable. The staff makes you feel welcome and they have a warm lobby area in which you can relax.On nice days the outside bar area is a treat with a great view.

“Very nice -- recommended” I stayed at the Hyatt Regency as a conference attendee. The hotel is very large, but I really enjoyed my stay. Check-in was smooth, no king beds were left, but since I was traveling alone I didn't mind two doubles. The room was clean and each room had an air purifier in it. All of the rooms are non-smoking, which works for me. Lots of restaurant choices on-site, and a lot of places to sit and relax. Location is great as well. Cost is up there...but comparable to everything else in Chicago. My big complaint (and I heard this from others) is massive problems with Internet connectivity. I never was able to connect, but others said I just didn't wait long enough (30 minutes) for the connection to take hold.
“Great Staff, Great RENOVATION!” Great Trip.....room service not quite up to par, very generic. However, the staff and renovation made up for it!

“Very practical hotel” Very practical hotel located in front of the Civic Center in San Francisco Very well connected with SFO Int’l airport (Bart underground from the airport to Civic Center in c.45 mins) Hotel located in a very good position close to all main attractions of San Francisco and also very well connected with Bart underground and public transportation (tram F brings you directly to Pier 39 and nus 76 to Golden Gate) - 5 min walking from Union Square and 30 min from Pier 39 The hotel has big rooms and it is very quiet; small gym available; swimming pool and big roof terrace to enjoy the sun - Definitively not a luxury hotel but very practical and very good price/quality ratio! Suggestion for breakfast: go to Lori’s Diner (500 Sutter St, on the junction with Powell St), only 10 min walking and you will enjoy an amazing typical American breakfast! (lorisdiner.com/locations.html#sutter)

“One of the BEST concierge” I have been staying at the W Chicago since October 2010. The service was also very good. I loved 2 things best - the IPO restaurant and Laurelin Hefter at the Concierge. She was always cheerful, helpful and found the best places to eat. Thanks again the entire W Chicago team. Arthur

“trendy hipster” Please no more "hip" hotels...hip has become a mask for all sorts of hotel evils - snotty disinterested service, minimalistic amenities, cold lack-luster style...not at the Ace! The service is great, the restaurant and coffee shop are major standouts (coffee shop was open at 6:30 am!!) the whole place is buzzing with style and life. Do request a front room with a view. If you have hipster phobias this is not for you. Best location in the city, easy walk to about anywhere.

“Good business hotel, Great service” I stayed here for a conference this past week and found the hotel to be decent. Upon my check in they didn't have a king bed room that I reserved, but the front desk staff was great and gave me 50% off of my room rate for the first night as an apology. That's great customer service. The property seems like an older hotel but is nice. I do agree with the other reviews that they need to do something about the wall paper in the corridor on the floors. VERY dark and dreary! One warning, the hotel fitness center is horrible. Very outdated, non-working equipment. That being said, according to the posters in the lobby, they're going to be upgrading it very soon to a Sheraton Core Performance gym. That will be very nice!

“Great Hotel in the District” We recently had a two night stay at the Topaz. This was our first time at this Kimpton property and we were very pleased with both the hotel and the central location near Dupont Circle. The staff are extremely friendly and professional. Rick will take great care of you at happy hour and Donte makes sure everything runs perfectly. The hotel retains its old style charm but has been completely renovated and updated. We had a huge room with plenty of space to spread out. As another review mentioned the separate vanity area was a real plus. The hotel is in a mixed residential/business neighborhood so there is no traffic noise and even though you are very close to the heart of the Dupont Circle shopping area you really feel like you are away from the hustle and bustle. We will definitely stay at this hotel again.

“Nice hotel, central to all” I stayed here for 4 nights for a conference at the end of February. The rooms were nice as well as the bathroom (they had great bathroom ammenities!). The room service was good. Never saw the gym. Location was central to everything.

“Good Deal for the Price” I stayed here for a conference that I was attending at the Peabody Hotel (across the street). Given the feedback from fellow conference attendees, I got a better hotel at a much better price. My room was clean and relatively spacious. The bathroom was very small, but the shower rod was curved, which made it feel bigger than it was. On the down side, the windows were sealed, which meant that I had to rely on A/C at all times. In addition, the Hotel is half a block from Autozone Field (Home of the AAA Memphis Redbirds). After the game they have fireworks an concert, which can be very busy. The room had a very nice chair and ottoman, but since the TV did not move, it was hard to see from anywhere other than the bed. As with many hotels, they tell you that your USA Today is included in your room rate. What they do not tell you is that you can opt out for a savings of $0.75/day. Also, if you are a Priority Club member, a continental breakfast is included (since it is free to join, there is no reason not to join). They are supposed ot inform you of this at check-in, but they seem to be negligent in many cases. Overall, though, this is a good, centrally located hotel and I would stay here again

“Elegant, yet approachable” We chose to stay here last minute after a late night in the city. Check-in was super easy and our room was bigger than we anticipated. We had a great view looking out over the city. This hotel is definitely on our short list of places to come back to when in San Francisco.

“Cool hotel in a great location!” We stayed at this hotel over Memorial Day weekend while in town for a wedding. The rooms were large and fun and had cute quirky things that made it a great place to stay. Although we were only there for one night, we got a large room. The front desk staff were super friendly and I wouldn't hesitate to stay there again. However, I definitely wouldn't valet my car- the price is exorbitant (40$/day). There is a parking garage a block away with much more reasonable prices.

“Great hotel” This is a very sleek, modern hotel. Kimpton generally has quality properties, this is definitely in that mold. Good location in an area of town with many restaurants and night spots. Close to Michigan for shopping. Overall a great stay.

“Great Location, nice room, but very busy.” I stayed here with my partner over the Labor Day weekend. There were several events going on in the hotel and the lobby area was often very busy. Having said that, check in was a breeze (I am a Hyatt Gold Passport member, so separate line) and the room was very nice. The bed was extremely comfortable and it was obvious when they did the room renovations that sound was taken into consideration...I never heard a peep from the hallway, or the other doors slamming, which is often the case in other hotels. The bathroom was on the smaller side but clean and remodeled nicely. A true towel bar, rather than the hooks provided, would have been nice if the desire was really for us to reuse towels....they don't dry out on hooks! The location is excellent for the tourist things...Magnificent Mile, Millennium and Grant Parks, Art Institute, etc. It's a little walk from the Metro if you come in from either airport that way...but doable. The lobby has a great coffee kiosk which "proudly serves Starbucks coffee" that also sells bagels, donuts, microwave meals, etc, which never seemed to close. It was great being able to come down to the lobby for a morning cup! We did the breakfast buffet in the Bistro 151 only once. It was very good, though not cheap at $22 a person. I would definitely stay here again.

“Simply Amazing!!!” I booked this hotel becuase we were taking a trip to Sea World for spring break. We arrived on a Friday evening and the "kickback" service was already going on. Check in was a breeze, the staff was very friendly and helpful. We were given two drink tickets for myelf and my husband. Let me tell you the "kickback" was awsome, the food was really good. Everyday they offer something different on the menu, while we were there they had chili dogs, chips, salad and baked potatoes. For breakfast they offer all types of hot food. Everything was really good, it was nice not having to go out for dinner and my kids enjoyed it too. The drinks were wonderful, and so was the staff. The manager on duty there went above and beyond keeping everything running smoothly. I have never seen a manager at a hotel work as hard as she did. The room was very large and clean, the pool area was a nice touch with being inside. There are not enough things I can say about how nice this hotel was. We already have another trip planned in May. Can't wait to return!

“Excellent service” The staff at this hotel were exceptionally helpful when we had an unexpected stay due to flight problems. The room was comfortable, the free breakfast was great, and we were very relieved to have such a nice welcome from the receptionist. We definitely would stay here if we ever needed to be near the Denver airport.

“Sonesta Replaces Crowne Plaza” Four night stay for business at the Sonesta, which is the old Crowne Plaza. Location, location, location is the star here - in the heart of Center City, near all major businesses and a quick walk to most tourist attractions. Pool has nice lounge chairs and is popular in the summer. Hotel also has small workout facility and laundry room which are nice touches. Elephant & Castle restaurant/bar in lobby has stout drinks but so-so food. Bathrooms are very small - you need to be fully inside before you can close the door - with sink outside the bathroom. Beds are comfortable, hopeful that Sonesta will spruce up the rooms in due course. Would stay here again given the good value and excellent location

“Great water pressure!” We've stayed at the Helmsley Park Lane twice. None of the reviews I've read comment on the fact that, unlike many other fine hotels in New York (including Essex House, the Intercontinental Central Park South, and the Waldorf), the Park Lane has showers where the water's always hot and always plentiful. We've found everything else satisfactory as well. At $159-$179 per night for a basic room, it's the best deal in town

“Great Cool Hotel, A Few Limitations” The Clift is a very cool boutique hotel in a great location with a superb bar. For those looking for cutting edge design and/or a happening bar/restaurant, it is a fantastic choice. Pros: Exotic, dark lobby with funky decor leading off to a really excellent bar, the Redwood Room, which hosts a very happening scene in the late evening. Food was good too. Service is excellent throughout the hotel. Very comfortable beds. Really nice thick towels (way better than most hotels). My room (on a higher floor) was elegant, very clean and relatively quiet even though it faced the street. Great water pressure. Very close to Union Square, walk to BART. Cons: $15 for internet (the demographic for the Clift will not find this to be cool). Almost $60 daily to park a car? Some rooms are small (but still functional). Peeling paint and water stains on the bathtub can be overlooked if you get a deal on the room rate (there seem to be lots of discounts around) ... but the rack rate for the room is $315 for which I would expect perfection. Overall, would stay again if I got another good deal on the room rate.

“Posh elegance at the Wharf” My husband and I stayed here for a wedding in late Sept. this year and really enjoyed our spot at the Fairmont. We got a great rate because of the block of rooms was reserved for wedding guests, and felt it was well worth it! The rooms are beautiful, very comfortable, spacious and well equipped with modern ammenities. There is a very lovely and fancy espresso maker that was great in the mornings. One complaint I had was we could not get our DVD player to work and called the front desk several times and several times they said they would send someone up to assist us, however no one came, and this was irritating. Other than that the service was impeccable, from checkin when we were escorted to our room so we did not get lost, to the bellhop flagging a cab for us. The housekeeping did come rather late in the day (after 4pm), which was odd to me, but did a great job. It is located in a great spot, easy access to all parts of the city and right in the heart of LIttle Italy. We were able to walk almost everywhere and those parts we couldn't get to by foot we easily found a cab. I would definitely recommend this spot if it's in your price-range. Thanks for putting the cherry on the top of a lovely elegant weekend in Boston Fairmont!

“I stay at this place frequently while on business- a good sub for home” This location has become my home away from home over the last year due to an assignment in Jacksonville. The hotel is near The St. Johns Town Center where there are a variety of dining and shopping choices. The property is well-maintained with business services, pool and fitness center on premise. If arriving late, Seven Bridges Restaurant, literally a stones-throw away, is usually open for a decent late nite meal. I have stayed in other Hilton properties in JAX, but always opt to drive a little further to stay at this property.

“A very nice hotel that has gone a long way towards green.” I stayed here in the Fall for a conference. The hotel was chosen for its "green" practices, which are commendable and worth a mention. Like most places, they still have a ways to go in that direction, but they have many practices that go beyond just low flow toilets and not changing the sheets and towells every day unless asked. Aside from that, they were one of the nicer hotels I've stayed at in Seattle. I'm a government employee, and when we travel we almost always get the least desirable rooms as we pay the gov't rate. Mine was in the back of the building, close to both the elevator and the ice machine, overlooking the freeway and the city street, yet it was very quiet and very comfortable. The rooms are all set up suite style, and I must say the bed was as comfy as any I've slept in. Could I have found a way to get it in my suitcase, I might have been guilty of hotel theft. In addition, the hotel has a nice restaurant with a great view, and the food was very good and reasonably priced, with very nice wait staff. Staff at this hotel were outstanding, too, from the wait staff at the restaurant to the check-in staff to the doormen. Helpful, friendly, considerate, efficient, responsive. You can always tell a hotel that is good to work for; people seemed happy to be at their jobs and to really make an effort. Our conference facilities, too, were excellent. Even the food served at the conference was a cut above. I wasn't involved in setting it up, so I can't speak to how easy they were to work with, but if the flawless service and really delicious food (and I know we got the least expensive options, because that's a requirement) were any indications, if ever I need to set one of these things up in Seattle, they will be my first choice.

“Good Kimpton hotel” The location is excellent. The rooms are larger than I would have expected, and comfortable. The bathrooms are quite small, but that was ok with us. Didn't have much interaction with the staff, but when we asked for a broken iron to be replaced, it was brought up in less than 15 minutes. The attached Italian restaurant had a slightly impersonal, commercial feel to it, but we had a great experience with the quality of the food. I'd recommend it to anyone staying at the hotel. One tip - if you have a car and don't expect to be in and out much, it'll be much cheaper to park at one of the nearby public garages, instead of the very expensive hotel parking.

“Highly Recommended!” A colleague and I stayed here for six nights during a conference. Although it was further from the Convention Center, we chose the hotel over others on the list because of the reviews we read on this site. We were not disappointed. (And our friends who stayed elsewhere were!) The room and bathroom were very clean, beds and pillows, were very comfortable, and service was very polished and professional. We joined the Select Guest program and received complimentary wireless internet and breakfast beverages (coffee and/or juice delivered to the room every morning -- a classy touch). The concierge (Amy) provided outstanding and highly professional service (from restaurant reservations -- we just started calling her from anywhere in the city when we were ready for dinner and she would recommend a restaurant for our needs at the moment and make us a reservation -- to phoning us before our arrival to let us know that a package had arrived and was being held for us.) The complementary fruit water in public places, and the on-demand courtesy sedan service (a late model Cadillac driven by very polite bellmen) that will take you short distances for a tip just completed the experience for us. The staff was so nice that we could easily overlook as comical that no matter what newspaper we checked off on our door hanging request each night, we still got the USA Today; that despite our trying four times, they never could get the second guest name into the reservation record in a way that the next person could find it; that the front desk staff told us that the Convention Center was at least 3 miles away and that there was no way we could walk there (it's about a mile and a half and it takes 30 minutes to walk); and that although we were given the complementary breakfast beverage door hanging signs, colleagues in three other rooms who also joined the Select Guest program were not given them until they asked for them part-way into their stay. Also, we wished they had shown a little more eco-friendliness (things like the plastic cups for one-time use with the fruit water and replacing our towels even if we left them hanging in the bathroom, etc.) Tips: 1) The taxi drivers who line up in front of the hotel can be rather expressive in their displeasure at being asked to take you what they consider to be short distances -- i.e., 2 mile, $10 fares; use the hotel sedan if you're not going far and save yourself being publicly berated... I recognize this is not the hotel's fault; it's probably why they offer the sedan service, but if they could solve this problem which at least 5 colleagues experienced during our week in town, it would really improve the guest experience. 2) Grand Central Market is a block away and is not to be missed for cheap eats and a colorful experience!

“Clean, spacious room, convenient location” The staff was very helpful and nice. When I checked in I was given a room upgrade to what they called a "suite" (see pictures that I've posted). Paid $140/night including tax and free parking. Clean room, spacious, comfortable bed. My room had a view of the parking lot, but since you're in a city I'm guessing that none of the rooms had much of a view besides the buildings across the street. The room had a microwave & a refrigerator (and a safe, I think). The TV was not a flat screen, but had a decent selection of channels, ESPN, showtime, etc. I saw no sign of communal bathrooms mentioned in other reviews. My room had a private bath (#322) and I saw no communal bathrooms in the entire 3rd floor hall (at least on my side of the building).

“very good location for shopping” I went to Houston for the Black Friday and this hotel was a very good option to stay in. The Galleria, the finest mall of the city, is located a few steps from the hotel and as well the Westheimer Road and Richmond Ave where very good options for shopping are also available. The staff is exteemely helpful and I had no problem to receive merchandise bought at Amazon. The hotel has a parking lot which sometimes requires some skill, but the acces to it is not so convenient which for me is the weakest point of the hotel, mainly if you have many bags to carry. The room is not so spacious, but it's ok, is very quiet and clean. There's also a small kitchen in it. I definitely recomend and would stay there again.

“Great hotel and location” I was pleased with our recent stay at this hotel. I was a little concerned given the less than positive reviews. The hotel is decorated in a contemporary style. Very open and large lobby. Nice warm brown tones. The pool area looked nice. Glass elevators have a nice view of the pool and ponds. The hotel is next to several freeways but surprisingly very quiet. The hotel is very large and the front desk staff is a little reserved. The rooms are stylish, clean, and comfortable. We stayed in the executive floors 17+. The rooms facing the freeway are actually larger than the rooms across the hall because of the wedge shape. You have a small entry area with double closet and the bedroom part of the room is very wide with double windows. I don't think our bed was the Hilton Serenity Bed since it seemed firm. When we made our reservations we were told the Executive Lounge is open on weekends but when we arrived, we found it is not. Because of our Hilton Honors level we were given coupons for breaksfast but didn't learn that we could have ordered off the menu rather than being limited to the buffet. Internet access was sporatic during our stay but they had technicians onsite working on a resolution. I did agree with other postings about the awkward narrow door to toilet clearance.

“Perfect hotel in a perfect location...incredible!” There aren't enough good things I could say about the Courtyard Liberty Station! This is one of the nicest hotels I've ever stayed at with a great experience from check in to check out. Stayed here over Christmas 2010 and the hotel was so thoughtful that they hung stockings on everyone's door to wake up to on Christmas morning. How thoughtful is that??? Hotel is in a beautiful location on the water and has a jogging/walking trail in the back. There are restaurants within walking distance and a large park is also close by if you walk over the pedestrian bridge in the back and cross the road that takes you to the airport. The rooms are comfortable, clean, and ours came with a balcony with a view of downtown San Diego. Rooms feature large flatscreen tvs and all the other luxuries that a modern hotel should have. The only complaint is that the internet was rather slow. The lobby is clean and beautiful with fresh coffee, cranberry juice, water, and/or coconut water available to guests throughout the day. Outside is a fireplace on a nice patio that you can lounge around along with a fire pit that I never saw turned on. If you would rather stay inside, the other side of the fireplace faces a cozy indoor sitting area near the lobby. The zoo, Cabrillo Park, Old Town, and other San Diego attractions are a short drive away...and the parking is FREE! With a friendly staff, beautiful location, and comfortable accommodations, the Courtyard by Marriott Liberty Station is one of the nicest hotels I've ever stayed in.

“Overall a nice hotel” I stayed in this hotel this past weekend, and overall I was happy. The staff at the front desk were some of the friendliest and most helpful I have met on this long trip. For example, I got some horrible Chinese food down the street and they didn't give me any soy sauce. I went to the front desk to see if one of them happened to have any and the staff member actually ran across the street to a restaurant and brought me some back. They were also very helpful with directions and how to use public transit. The restaurant staff was not very friendly at all, but I didn't spend much time there. The room was HUGE. There are two large flatscreen tvs in the room. It was very comfortable, and I like having a fridge and microwave in the room. It seemed very clean.
