I did not hear anything from other rooms, and there was a party going on 2 doors down. The area around the hotel is very creepy. I am a female travelling alone, and I did walk around alone at night-very stupid, but it's cheap! I did not have any problems, but I was not comfortable. The entrance to the main lobby is in a dark scary tunnel, and there were a lot of loud homeless people outside. If you want to eat food that isn't chinese after 6pm, be prepared to walk a few blocks. The wawa across the street actually has cheap decent sandwiches if you don't feel like making the trek out of chinatown.

“Wonderful service!” Beautiful hotel, wonderful service, great location in Baltimore. My room was large, clean, and comfortable. The bar/restauant had delicious burgers and strong drinks. Can't ask for much more than that!

“excellent location - just ignore the hobos” Hotel Metropolis is a gem in the city. The close proximity to the BART and cable car/muni stops are wonderful. It is in the Loin but if you MYOB you will be fine. The rooms are sparsely furnished but it will do just fine for a place to lay your head. I liked that we had a refrig in the room too. The bed was uber comfy. Shower had good water pressure and plenty of hot water. We did not receive the baggy of samples/toiletries as some other guests had. You can hear Loin noise but it's pretty much par for the course living/staying in the city. Just bring earplugs if you are sensitive to noise. Join the Perks club too - it's worth it. Try the hotel restaurant, Farmer Brown. The mac n cheese is excellent! We will definitely be coming back to this hotel.

“Marriott Metro Center is one of Washington's better hotels” Conveniently located near the Metro Center metro station, the Marriott Metro Center is nicely situated near Ford's Theater, the White House and the National Mall. The hotel itself is well-appointed and maintained, with large, comfortable guest rooms. There is a Starbucks in the lobby, as well as a restaurant. The hotel has a pool, which is not stadard fare in DC. We found the service and housekeeping to be excellent and the overall hotel quality is among the very best that we've encountered in Washington. Internet service is excellent, but it is an extra charge through a third party vendor.

“Great Stay - even though the Brazil festival blazed outside” I surprised my husband with a day/night in NYC for his 65th bday - using my Intouch points (free night) as a lure. The streets were blocked off b/c of the Brazil festival, making it impossible to drive to the parking garage. But, once we figured it all out, the staff made our stay an absolute pleasure. They were friendly, positive, upbeat - and treated us like royalty. Our room was upgraded, a happy bday card & cheese/crackers/wine/water were waiting for us when we returned from dinner - AND - every single employee we encountered went out of his/her way to make sure our stay was enjoyable. We usually stay at INK48, which is away from the hustle bustle of Times Square - but The Muse was a perfect alternative and a gem of a retreat, once you step inside. Don't hesitate to stay here - it's outstanding.

“splendid Solamar” We spent a week here over Easter we have stayed in Kimptons before but this is the best so far many thanks to the wonderful Wendy and ever helpful Patrick on reception they were so nice. The staff in general are amazing, we askd for a non pet floor and we got top of the house floor 10 over looking the pool, the beds are brilliant they were in the process of replacing the matresses while we were there.The wine reception was a brilliant way of meeting some wonderful people, the only complaint we had was that the fitness gym would need upgraded as there was always a wait , there is a brilliant corner store -deli on 4th avenue and 4st does great breakfast bagels and lunch for a fraction of the [rice called Cine cafe. I would recommend this hotel to anyone planning a trip tp beautiful san diego

“Will Stay Longer Next Time” I stayed here about 6 years ago and didn't remember it had 3 floors. When I checked in this time and was made aware of this, I asked if there was any chance I could get a room on the 3rd floor. Connie, the front desk staffer, found a room on the 3rd floor for me and even called an hour later to check it was OK. The room was nice, had a balcony, even though it faced a parking lot. The temperature in the room was just right that I didn't have to turn on the aircon. I received a welcome gift which included a bottle of water and a snack. The room was very comfortable, especially the bed. I was only here for one night but do intend to stay here the next time I'm in San Jose.

“Odd layout” I arrived early and my room wasn't ready - this was expected. I was asked to pay $1/bag to leave my bags until my room was ready. That's not a nice way to start the trip, but it's not outrageous either. My room was ready around 1pm and I found it comfortable and nicely arranged. It was a bit difficult to keep the room warm enough and the HVAC system was somewhat loud, banging on and then blowing loudly, with frequent cycling. The bathroom was bright enough and included a smaller shaving/make-up mirror. One problem with the bathroom is the low water pressure, perhaps due to a water restrictor on the shower nozzle. This meant that it took 10 minutes to take a shower instead of 5 because there simply wasn't enough water. I must remember to carry a wrench with me when I travel to remove water restrictors when they're overly restrictive. Another problem with the bath is a permanent nightlight built into the light switch. This is a little bright and lit up the room at night a tad more than I'd have liked. Elevators, conference rooms, dining options, were all very good and above average. When I left, there was noone outside to call a cab. A police car had cut off access to the driveway and I wheeled my suitcase to the top of the drive. Still noone around, so I walked a few minutes to the subway instead of taking a cab. Not too inconvenient - about a five minute walk.

“Made Over Masterpiece” The newly renovated Dupont is a spectacular choice for any DC traveler, and it's in a perfect DC location. The rooms were elegant, large, and only outdone by the gorgeous bathroom! I had lots of windows overlooking a busy but not too noisy street below, and a comfortable sitting area. The restaurant downstairs was perfect for a celebratory lunch, the staff even making a stunning fruit plate for my 2 year old grandson to enjoy. We were able to take advantage of a secluded swimming pool at a sister hotel up the street. A perfect foil to the very scenic but hot Farmer's Market on the Circle. The beds were most comfortable, and the halls were quiet, despite a quite active bar scene downstairs. It proved a little hard to get a cab, but fortunately the Metro is nearby.

“finally a chic and comfortable hotel in nyc that won't break the bank!” I was a bit skeptical when my husband and I sat down to book our hotel in NYC for a wedding. Last trip, I was less than impressed by the overpriced, small hotel room that my husband had booked for us in trendy SoHo. However, after staying at Ink48 over the past weekend, I am happy to say that we've found a hotel in NYC that I would LOVE to stay in again. First of all, we arrived a bit early, but really needed to get into a room so that we could get ready for the wedding. The front desk was wonderful--professional and helpful, and actually upgraded us so that we could get into a room faster. The room itself was heaven---floor to ceiling windows overlooking the river, a bathroom which I swear was bigger than the last hotel room entirely that I stayed in in NYC, and a soft and comfortable king sized bed. I love the bathrobes in the room--animal print could be cheesy, but it was actually perfect for the chic vibe. We had a soaking tub and rainfall shower in the room, and I've never enjoyed getting ready for a wedding more. And the location--yes, a bit strange at first--you're surrounded by all of the car dealerships in NYC, but it's a comfortable walk to times square and the rest of NYC. My only minor complaints were that there was no turn down service--so late night we were struggling to pull the shades over those gorgeous huge windows, and the next day housekeeping woke us up at 9 AM after our late night of partying to clean the room, and proceeded to come back twice to see if we were out yet, despite it being our check out day. But that's really it--overall, we loved the place, and we'll definitely be back.

“A really great experience” Having worked in the hotel business for ten years in a previous career, I am pretty jaded by hotels and their marketing hype. The San Francisco Omni, however, exceeded the hyperbole and provided me with a very pleasant stay in a city not necessarily known for exemplary hotels. My room was large and handsomely appointed, with a nice selection of amenities. The staff was friendly, gracious and unobtrusive, and the bar and restaurant were elegant spaces with good food. What more can you ask for? All in all, this was one of the best hotel experiences I have had in San Francisco. Definitely worth a stay.

“Great location, great bed, great hotel” I was a little chary of booking a room here, what with some of the negative reviews, but ultimately the location decided me and I'm so glad it did. We really enjoyed our stay. You walk out of the lobby on the 2nd level right into the Galleria shopping mall--how great is that? Room was spotlessly clean, the bed was extremely comfortable, the room was very quiet (26th floor), the staff was very nice, esp. the young man who checked us in. Would absolutely stay here again. If there is one tiny suggestion, the valets out front weren't rude about us self-parking, far form it, but they weren't terribly helpful either. The self parking is very confusing--we wandered around looking for a way back into the hotel that didn't involve dragging our luggage down stairs (eventually found it-just walk out the way you drove in). A minor negative in a wonderful stay.

“Good experience.” Stayed at the Springhill pre cruise for a couple of nights,while not the idea location for a couple of seasoned adults we were able to walk to most attractions with a little effort. They do have a courtesy van that will drive you go certin locations but it seemed the drivers were put out when you requested a pick up and were not very friendly at all. The hotel desk were very accomadating and went out of their way to help,all in all the staff were top shelf. They do offer a comp breakfast which was actually edible which is saying alot if you've been through a few of these The room was standard Springhill,large with separate sitting area and a couple of tv's. I would recommend this property without hesitation for the budget minded tracker or for anyone who does not want to pay Ritz prices to stay on the water front. By the way the bowl of suckers at the front desk were a welcome treat. Thank you!

“beautiful hotel, great location” we checked in pretty late and were given a handicap room and didn't receive the amex upgrade (neither of which are complaints) but other than that the staff was very attentive and service-oriented. our room was pretty large and unlike other handicap-accessible rooms i've seen, it didn't seem like things were positioned lower and there weren't support bars on walls. there was a small foyer with the mini-bar that could be closed off with double doors and i love the bath/shower wet-room often seen in asian hotels. my main complaint with the rooms is we first had foam pillows which were squeaky, so we requested down. they were extremely firm. i asked for softer down pillows. i'm not sure if they were switched out because the pillows were still pretty firm. the fitness room has basic cardio machines, dumb-bells and some strength machines. it has a nice yoga studio room too. the spa has a great wet room with jacuzzi, steam, that mist shower thing. the spa menu is quite pricey. i enjoyed my facial but if i lived in boston, this wouldn't be my regular spot cuz of the prices ($195 for a facial). breakfast at asana was pleasant. they had birchermuesli on the menu which is my top vacation bfast food. and they make it well here. good service, food isn't amazing but it's very good and pretty presentation. definitely seemed like lots of business meetings conducted at the hotel restaurant. big plus is the location. above prudential mall, close to newbury, easy to get to the green T stops and red line areas are easy to reach via the Mass Ave bus just a few block walk away. (i can get my flour bakery sticky buns in just 10 min via the #1 bus to MIT!) overnight parking is $45 but on the central parking website (which is underneath the hotel), there is a printable coupon for $25 overnight. MO is a nice addition to downtown hotels since a lot of the hotels around are old and dusty. OH, and i do find it bothersome that many high-end hotels continue to charge for wi-fi.

“Great Hotel for the price” We stayed here for three nights before a cruise. We were on the tenth floor with a beautiful view of the Space needle. Rooms were very comfortable. Plenty of room for our family of four. We loved the location, since the hotel is situated centrally to everything we wanted to see. Staff was pleasant and helpful with any questions we had. If you don't mind walking, you can get to just about anywhere from this hotel. We will definitely stay here again when we come back to Seattle!!

“so unique !” the staff is simply great, as soon as you arrive you feel at home. Rooms are clean, quiet and modern. Breakfast is ok, good quality. The batroom is a bit small, but still ok. Good to have a small fitness room. I can only recommand this place. And a big thank you to the team!

“Great Stay, helpful staff, convenient location” The roads immediately around the Hyatt Regency are a little confusing, but the fact is that it's right off the highway and at the same time, right on the edge of downtown, walking distance to the West End eateries and right next to the light trail to venture to other parts, so though slightly remote for a downtown location, it still has some big wins. The front desk staff was very friendly and accommodating, As it was very hot when we arrived the water flavored with fresh fruit available by the front doors and front desk was a nice touch. The room was high and had a nice view of downtown including the JFK site. The room wasn't overly spacious and in good condition despite being a little dated, but otherwise comfortable. I'm not sure I understand the whining of other reviewers about getting nickel and dimed. Full service hotels typically charge for Internet and downtown hotel locations charge for parking and usually only have valet parking available, That's to be expected and the valet parking and bellman crew here were very nice and efficient and the vale parking price was less than in many other cities, including Austin and Pittsburgh.

“Very good hotel with helpful staff” Lobby was elegant, busy but orderly. Staff members were very friendly and helpful. Following their instruction I was able to find a really good late-night sushi place near there. The only draw back for this hotel was its bathroom. The size was a bit small, water pressure was on the low end, and I found lighting in the bathroom insuffient (maybe because I didn't find the right switch).

“very nice placeto stay.....make sure you have a car” this hotel was very nice, got it at a reasonable price and pick up at the airport & drop off at the cruise terminal was perfect...... no problems with the hotel at all - staff even helped us find a good medical walk-in clinic for a minor problem my only caveat is that there is not much in the area, you can walk to......and cabs are expensive, so if you want to see anything in san diego - make sure you have a car .... everything is close by, but like i said the cab rides added up

“New Very Comfortable Beds!” We stayed at this Best Western hotel Jan 6-8, a Friday and Saturday night. Our room was remodeled and very clean, with 2 extremely comfortable large beds. The bedspreads looked new. The room had a coffee maker, small fridge, microwave, ironing board and iron. We used them all. This hotel is very close to everything in Hollywood. I like to sleep with the sound of the airconditioner, we didn't need the cool air, but we used the fan only. If there was noise outside, we didn't hear it. The pool is small, but very cute in a Hollywood 1950's way, with trees surrounding it. The parking lot is small but we found parking both nights, getting in after midnight. Some of the SUV's parked along the side of the hotel rather than in the smallish parking spots. I think this is a great place to stay with a AAA internet discount. I'll be back!

“Terrific Choice” I usually prefer Hyatt and Hilton to Marriott, but this particular Marriott was great! Check-in was fast and friendly. Our room was in the south tower facing the marina. This was a free upgrade considering we paid for a city view and booked through Expedia. The room was spacious & clean with lots of pillows and hangers. Our large walk-in shower was a plus. The bed could have been better, as it was not as comfy as the typical Westin heavenly bed or pillow top provided by Hilton and Hyatt hotels. I expected more for a "marquis" property. Surprisingly, our mini bar wasn't stocked either. They would have made some money off us on drinks, but oh well, we drank tap water much to our disappointment. The next night I searched for a vending machine, since the shops were all closed. I asked the front desk where we could buy water and they just handed us two bottles for free. Nice touch but would have been better if it was just provided in the room. I still gave them five stars because everything else here is spot-on. As others have stated, the location can't be beat. You have the ferry to Coronado at your back door, Seaport Village and marina next door, and Gas Lamp across the street. What more can you ask for? The property is pleasant on the eyes and very clean. All of the staff including the guys at the front door are friendly. We didn't eat or drink here, but the pool bar & fire pits looked fun. I would definitely stay here again if in town. This hotel is great for either a convention or a romantic getaway.

“Ground Zero views, great location” As a former resident of Battery Park City and an urban designer, I like this hotel with outstanding views to the re-building of Ground Zero. The hotel is a single hall system so every room has a NYC Harbor, Ground Zero and NJ view! A pretty simple place, not a resort but great base camp for business or sightseeing. Nothing overly impressive about the lobby or public spaces, in fact don't expect much there at all! The rooms are spacious, nice big flat screen TV, desk, and floor to ceiling glass for great views!

“Quiet, comfortable” I have stayed at this hotel a few times. Both times, i had a very nice comfortable quiet room. Everything was immaculate, the hotel also has a beautiful lobby and nice seating area to have drinks. The hotel also has a nice bar as well that overlooks Central Park with full wall glass which is nice as you sit and enjoy your drink. Of course, like any high end hotel, the prices are very high. During one of my stays, i did have an issue with what i was charged for vs. what i was offered. I was told i would have a voucher for food and free parking, but they tried to charge me for parking, i had to dispute it with american express and it was a bit of a pain. Eventually it was resolved in my favor, so i do not think about it anymore and I do stay there when i am in the city. if i had to pay that parking, i would have been pretty angry and would not have stayed anymore, but since it all worked out well, its not a factor in my decision to book here. I love the location, its close to midtown in that you can easily walk here from times square, but its also situated in a nicer more residential area, where you have easy access to central park ( across the street). The Essex House is a very nice hotel where all of the times i stayed, i had a restful sleep, clean and comfortable accomodations.

“New favorite place in Seattle- Good location” Last time we were in Seattle we stayed at another Homewood Suites property in town but not this property. While there was nothing to complain about the other property this is where I will stay from now on. The hotel is pleasantly situated in downtown Seattle. It is about 8 blocks from the Pikes Street Market and perhaps 4 blocks away from the heart of downtown and the monorail to the Seattle Center. Its price based on location cannot be matched as your stay includes breakfast and happy hour during the week. The hotel is nice and clean, modern, and has all the extra amenities one would expect from a Hilton property and especially a Homewood Suites. My only mild complaint about the hotel was that parking is only valet and the price was a bit steep at $33 a night however parking in Seattle itself is a nightmare and the valet staff did wash our car. Overall as much as I travel to Seattle I will be back here again.

“Elegant Nob Hill Ritz Carlton” The hotel is perched up on Nob Hill in a building suitable for a Ritz Carlton. The location is actually really convenient bring a few minutes from Chinatown and the cable cars down to the Embarcadero area etc. The service was very excellent, room very large and sure clean. The gym was modern and well kept. The concierge was very god at arranging restaurants etc. i I'll come ck again.

“A Birds Eye View of 1600 Pennslyvania Ave.” Visited the city of my youth to stay in a hotel that always looked great from the street, turns out it is great thru and thru or is that through and through, how some ever it is spelled it is that. Historic as much of DC is, you couldn't be more centrally located to all the attractions that Washingtom has to offer. Lovely lobby, a great bar one flight down, Off The Record, rooms very comfortable and many of them afford a stunning view of the President's residence. I can't wait to return.

“Good business hotel but needs to be more consistent.” This is a good hotel, but it just lacks consistency. I've stayed here for 13 nights over 3 stays in the past month or so and usually, I leave thinking that it was a nice experience but that one or two things were a little off. Before that - the rooms are nice and spacious. The Heavenly bed is always comfortable to sleep in. The Internet connection (wired) is fast but I did not try out the wireless connection. Not a lot of high definition offerings on the tv - this is 2011, they really should improve in that area. Their workout room is pretty large and has a nice selection of machines and free-weights. This being Austin, they have live music in the hotel some nights. The hotel bar scene at night actually is pretty hopping some nights from what I can tell (I'm almost always working in my room, unfortunately). Overall, service at the hotel is pretty good. They usually have one or two greeters near the front door and people are quite friendly. But I've run into one or two people that have had a little "attitude." In one stay, my room didn't have a menu so when I called for room service, I asked for a listing of their menu items. The lady wasn't terribly pleasant about, but hey, it's not my fault you didn't put a menu in my room. Am I supposed to guess at what to order? Room service is fast (usually 10-15 minutes). Unfortunately, it's not very good. The margherita pizza is particularly terrible - I thought it was so horrible that I polled other people at the hotel that had ordered it and they agreed it was awful. Hopefully the attached restaurant is better - I've only had breakfast there and it was good. The hotel is also next to a mall with a bunch of dining options. For Starwood Platinum folks, I've not been upgraded to a suite once in my 3 stays here. 2 of my 3 times here, as a Platinum member they gave me these coupons that I could use for the breakfast buffet or pretty much all the food I want at the coffee bar in the morning. Of course, my first stay I didn't get anything, so I had no idea what I was missing. Again, consistency. I also once got a nice fruit/snack basket in my room when I had checked in. The other 2 times, nothing. Consistency. No club/lounge for Plats unlike some other Starwood hotels. There's always some niggling little thing out there that prevents a completely satisfied stay (either SPG-related or just general customer service-related). I should, however, give special recognition to the nice British barista who works there in the morning - she is awesome at her job and ridiculously nice. I plan to continue staying at that hotel whenever I'm in town for business, but I do hope they can turn their B+ game into an A game. It may seem like quibbling over trivial things, but I expect more from a Westin, particularly a Westin that often charges $250/night.

“I hesitate to let the secret out with this hotel...” I hesitate to review this hotel as I want to keep the secret to myself. I don't think I'll be staying at any other hotel when I visit New York again. It's a perfect location with two subway lines just out the door and in walking distance to all the LES has to offer. Are the rooms small? Yes, but you're in New York and honestly I've stayed in far smaller both in and out of NYC. Honestly, the bathroom was huge, probably took up a 1/3 of the room. The room was very modern with luxury toiletries and we had a sliver of a view of the Empire State building. The front desk staff was always friendly and allowed us an early check-in when we arrived. There's also a rooftop patio where you can enjoy great views and bring back food or drink to enjoy. AND its affordable, especially for NYC... If you're going to New York and plan to stay in the hotel room the entire time then maybe you want to find somewhere with larger rooms (good luck?) but I find this hotel to be perfect in every way. Love, love, love this place...

“Wonderful Suite” We booked a Sunset Suite and we were surprised to be upgrade in the Presidential Suite! Beautiful city view from the top floor, huge living room with kitchenette, dining table, sofa chairs and big screen TV, hi-fi for iPod, work desk. Very nice room aavec quality beds. Very nice bathroom with Jacuzzi tub and separate shower, 2 separate toilets. Service quality and considerate. Fabulous stay ...

“Very comfortable, great location, friendly service.” I stay at this hotel all of the time and said it is time to write a review as the service is always great. Jackie at the front desk is always has a mile and you can tell how pround she is to be working at this property. For the price of a hotel room you get a suite with very comfortable beds, a dining area, microwave and fridge, and a desk and a desk chair that does not hurt your back. You also get a free breakfest and an free evening cocktail hour. All of this while being in Center City. And if you are traveling with kids........the sofa bed in the living room is great. it is a no brainer. I guess that is why I have been coming to this hotel for over 10 years. Book a room with a view and ask for a 01 or 12 room on a high floor. The view is the best in Philadelphia. Oh did I mention each room has a balcony and there is a TGIF in the hotel for good cheap meals. Enjoy!

“Great location for if Going to Minute Maid Park.” My husband and I stayed here for two nights. We were in town to watch baseball and the hotel is only a few blocks from Minute Maid Park. The room although a little musty was very nice, until we got a leak in the bathroom. We ended up having to move to another room the next day (a suite with a full kitchen). The bar is on the second floor and it really has not character and they don't have a restaurant. I think it might be under construction?? The breakfast is free and it is pretty good for a buffet. Not a lot to do downtown on the weekend. Most of the shops and cafe close on Saturday and Sunday. We went to the Flying Saucer (one block for the hotel) and it was great. There are other restaurants around but we ate dinner at the game. Baseball, Beer, and Hot Dogs.

“Pretty Good Hotel” We stayed at the Hilton Polaris for 2 nights for a conference this weekend. The rooms and conference areas were great and had no complaints on the look of the exterior or interior (maybe it's newer?). There were a lot of kids using the pool area and I think this would be a great stop for any family traveling on I71. There is plenty to do around the hotel with numerous restaurants and stores. When we checked out and returned home we discovered we left clothes hanging in the closet. When we called the hotel they transfered us to Housekeeping where we got their voicemail. We called back again and they told us they would transfer us again. After some prying, the hotel took our name (customer service was lacking here), but the next day we called back and housekeeping had our items. Would we stay here again - absolutely!

“Nice rooms, very clean and good location” Stayed in a 1 bedroom suite. Room had a kitchen with full size frig, stove, microwave, dishwasher & dishes. We were only there for one night for a cheerleading competition for my daughters. The hotel is on the Riverwalk a bit off the beaten path, but still a decent location. Hotel was very clean and the staff was very courteous & helpful. Hotel has a rooftop pool. The rooftop setting is really cool, but the pool is super small. Probably not great for kids and swimming. Hotel offers a free breakfast, but the pickings were very slim, just OK. Overall liked the hotel and would stay there again.

“Best Hotel in Uptown Charlotte” The Hilton Charlotte City Center is the best hotel in the city and first-class all the way. This is my third stay (first in a few years) and both the room and the restaurant have gone through a great renovation. The entrance is a bit deceiving with just the check-in desk and bell station. However, just up the stairs is the main part of the hotel with access to the restaurant, elevators, store and opens up to the large Wachovia tower in the rear. The rooms are among the best I have seen at a Hilton or Marriott type hotel. Modern feel, especially the bathroom with a state-of-the-art sink (my kids were even impressed) and shower. New large HD TV (with HD channels) and comfortable beds made this a great experience. Very clean. The restaurant called Coastal Kitchen offered a great breakfast buffet (best in the Hilton chain that I have had) and a few weeks prior had a terrific lunch there while passing through. As a Hilton Gold member, my wife got complimentary access to the onsite YMCA. Self-parking was easy and the staff was great throughout. The Hilton is a few blocks from the main action of Tryon Street but is the best of the hotels I have stayed at including the Omni, Marriott, Westin and Dunhill.

“Great Hotel on the Riverwalk” Stayed here one night for a business trip. It is a wonderful hotel with a lot of charm with many of the original features from the bank (the hotel is a renovated bank). The lobby area is really beautiful, and the daily dinner and drinks provided free of charge were great. The hotel room itself was a little on the small side, but very cozy and very clean. The bathroom was beautiful and spacious. Free internet was a bonus, and the staff were very nice and helpful. The location is convenient to everything-you can park your car and just walk wherever you want to go-the hotel connects to the Riverwalk.

“Good for Business Travelers” I frequently stay at the East Side Marriott while in NYC for business. My most recent stay there was in June of 2006. This hotel is conveniently located on the east side of midtown, provided a great location when needing to get a cab to the airport and also within walking distance of most of my client meetings. The staff are friendly - they are always willing to call a cab with a smile or help with bags. I often arrive in the morning straight from LaGuardia, and if my room isn't ready, the bell captain happily checks my bags with a smile. The rooms aren't huge, but they are clean and functional. The rooms on the higher "club" level are larger than the regular rooms, but all rooms have marble bathroom and comfortable beds. I have not used the fitness center on site, but I have had no trouble with room service or the hotel restaurant. Overall, I think the East Side Marriott is convenient and provides good business services for travelers. I would also consider staying here for leisure, although I can't comment on the concierge service.

“I love this hotel!” Company business trip. I was upgraded to a "loft" room and this room was absolutely fantastic. Full bar, mini-bar, and loads of snacks. The loft room has a movie room which is a comfortable bed with an LCD projector and Bose stereo CD/DVD system and the hotel has a long list of movies to provide you with for watching or you can bring your own. Staff were great, always accommodating and my only complaint would be that the bar closed too early. Our bar maid staff were extremely busy taking care of all of us and did a great job though, and the drinks were always great too - thanks. Thanks again for such a great time in Chi Town at the James.

“Peaceful, relaxing luxury” We recently enjoyed an overnight stay at this hotel. I loved the location, as we could walk to Quincy Market and many shops and pubs in between. The room was beautiful. I especially loved the bathroom layout. It was spacious and had a TV speaker so I could listen to the Bruins game while I took a shower. The staff was welcoming although I must say, I saw them tripping over themselves for some of the other guests. It would have been nice to have 'that' type of service but we were more than happy. The concierge suggested a wonderful local brunch place that we loved! Overall friendly staff, nice bar for a beverage (but not the best bar layout), relaxing rooms that are quiet and comfortable, and of course, the Ritz experience. Worth every penny.

“Beautiful Remodel” Beautiful, newly remodeled rooms. Comfortable beds with clean, fresh linens. Lobby is being renovated so you check in to a conference room. Called housekeeping for towels and they were there in minutes!! The hotel had several events happening but was extremely quiet.The internet was $15.00 but that seems to be the standard, I would definately stay here any time.

“Great location” This hotel is located 1 block from the 16th street mall right in about the center of the mall. There is a free bus that takes you up and down the street to all of the shops and restaurants, which I recommend because if you walk the Planned Parenthood people will harrass you on the street. The hotel is recently remodeled, and they have a decent happy hour four times a week with complimentary wine and beer and a light dinner. Decent fitness center. Parking was kind of pricey, but if you are just going to be in the downtown area, you don't really need a car. The only negative thing I have to say about it is, even though it is only one block from the touristy area, the block in between has some shady characters hanging out on it, so I was kind of uncomfortable walking back by myself at night. I would recommend walking down 17th 1 block, then crossing over in front of the Westin to16th street. Free breakfast every morning, free internet, and lots of TV channels (about 70ish).

“Recommended” Booked this through my partners recommendation, really nice hotel. Friendly staff. Room is clean. The baths are a bonus for the USA - deep roll top tubs. The location is good although the adult theatre next door could be off putting for some. Parking is in the garage across the street at a reduced cost from the normal garage prices. If hiring a car through Alamo the office is right across the street. It is 5 minutes walk to Union Square- downhill although the walk up can be a struggle. The restaurant in the basement serves really good quality french food at a good price and is worth a visit.

“Wonderful experience!” Booking through Amex Platinum Concierge Service this was my first visit to a St. Regis (part of Starwood Luxury Collection so got my points too!). I usually stay at the Waldorf in NYC but wanted to try this historic property. The building itself is amazing and one of the best of its style in the city. The lobby is posh, albeit quite small and will not tolerate much of a crowd. Nevertheless the staff were very nice. I appreciated the personal touches of bringing the key around the desk to hand it to you in person, and the offer for assistance with not only luggage but unpacking as well. While I declined the unpacking I did end up calling the butler for assistance with touching up a shirt for a concert that night. Ok - I did feel a bit odd the first time, but the service was so professional and helpful (I was brought some tea while I waited for the shirts - impeccably finished I might add, with tissue in the sleeves and silk links on the french cuffs!). I quickly became used to calling for my coffee first thing in the morning. My room deal (if you can call it that at that price) included a continental breakfast in the main restaurant, a beautiful space off the lobby. It was great, although I thought $43 was a touch steep! I used room service once and it was prompt, good food and beautiful presentation. The room itself was beautiful and equipped as one would expect at this price point - bedding, bath amenities, etc. were superb. The turn down service was wonderful. No charge for small things like bottled water, coffee, etc. A small thing perhaps, but many expensive hotels still nickel and dime you on such things. I used the spa for a facial and massage which were great. The gym is in the same facility - it is nice, but rather small. Additionally, if you are there after hours for the spa you must call the desk to gain access - this is unacceptable and access should be gained by your room key. Overall I loved this property and hope I can stay there again!

“Had a very nice stay. Recommended.” I stayed here on business in June 2004 for 2 nights. I didn't read the reviews on this web site until after I returned. I did not experience any of the problems mentioned in the other reviews. Sure, the room was small (actually, I would say average). But that isn't unusual these days. I was by myself, so it didn't matter. The room was clean and comfortable. Great location next to the river/lake. No issues with the hotel staff. They were very pleasant. Nice lobby bar. The other reviews stated that the hotel was in need of a major renovation. To me, I thought the hotel was kept up quite nicely. I didn't use the pool or exercise facility, so I can't comment on them. I wouldn't hesitate to stay here again if in the area.

“Couldn't find a single fault..” Had a recent 5 night stay at this hotel and I have to say, I found every aspect of the stay flawless. My room was large, clean and well equipped. The bed comfortable, and the other furnishings were well chosen too. The bathroom was great, with nice toiletries and a powerful shower. Staff were unfailingly helpful and willing to go that extra mile, and the recent renovations made the place have that extra sparkle of "newness" that pushed the hotel up to the top of the league. The location isn't particularly friendly if you aren't able to walk hills - that must be said. All roads to this hotel are very steep, but there is little the hotel can do about the topography. However cabs are plentiful, and a town car service is offered on a first-come, first serve basis by the hotel in the morning which can leave you anywhere in town. The cable car lines also stop right outside - and the California/Van Ness cars are generally quieter and easy to get on, so head to the Embarcadero and take it all the way up the hills if you are heading back to the hotel! I'd recommend this hotel to anyone, and I hope that I get to go back there pretty soon!

“shy of perfection” I had always heard good things about the Royal Palms (and, obviously, judging from the comments here it has many loyal followers), so I was looking forward to a weekend stay with my wife -- at a nice offseason rate. As many satisfied guests have noted, the property is initimate, well-groomed, historic, romantic (part of its schtick is to promote romance), and an utterly refreshing change from the mega resorts like the Biltmore and Phoenician which are nearby on Camelback. These are high points, along with the good service and friendly staff. However, we thought it didn't quite live up to our expectations. And, frankly, I'm a bit surprised at the surfeit of "5s" in the tripadvisor ratings. The Royal Palms is good...but that good? We had a designer casita room which we thought was a bit dark and maybe a bit too in-your-face with a romantic furnishing (to be fair, this is the theme of the place). The bathtub in our room was mundane. Just a tub. But it had a huge walk in shower (with only one head). Far better, we thought, if the tub were a two-person jacuzzi tub and the shower more routine (to stick with the romance theme). The room had two patios, but the back patio was small, the walls were high, there was no planting or other vegetation. It was quite claustophobic. And the larger front patio -- where we did sit and eat breakfast one morning -- was not especially private. People could walk right by, within feet of our table (there were curtains we could pull across...but that just made it less scenic). Our room also was noisy. The AC was noisy, but most of all there was a constant running of water, like a toilet or shower was running next door. Maybe it was unique to this room -- Room 105 -- because we were at the end of a row of casitas and near the kitchen (could it have been kitchen plumbing?). Overall, the room seemed very nice and pretty but not luxurious by any means. Incidentally, these designer casitas are on the west side of the property and a bit isolated from the other rooms and casitas. You should ask to be on the east side -- you'll be closer to the pool and spa too. Finally, to our minds, one drawback was the lack of public rooms. Yes, I know, this is a boutique kind of establishment and I guess the expectation is that guests will walk the grounds or hole up in their rooms, but a couple of indoor public spaces would have been nice. The lobby here is not big -- just a check-in area. And when it's 110 outside, the outside sitting areas are not always comfortable. Call me a nitpicker, but it wasn't a perfect 5, at least if judged against other properties that try to reach the same customer base and at the same price range. But I have no problem recommending it as a sweet alternative to the big resorts -- especially if you are looking for a special romantic kind of getaway.

“One of the best in Chicago” Everything about this property is excellent. The staff at the front (bellmen and front desk) are very attentive and helpful. Property is located very conviniently between Michigan Avenue and Lake Shore. The hotel sits far enough off both roads so it seems a little more quiet. The decor is nice as the property balances their history and elegance of their property but not making the guestrooms to over the top and traditional. I would recommend this hotel to anyone.

“Had a nice stay.” Stayed at the Four Points by Sheraton San Diego for two days during a business trip to UCSD in San Diego. Arrived with car. Four Points by Sheraton San Diego have free parking. The staff in the reception was very friendly, and as a SPG Platinum member my room was updated from a standard room to a suite. The staff in the reception was also very helpful in recommending a good restaurant to have dinner in the area. As mentioned by other reviewers it's not walking distance to much, so you need a car to get around. The room itself was ok, after my opinion, things were starting to look a little dated. Everything was however clean, and the bed was comfortable. The hotel has free high-speed Internet in all rooms, which is not something common in Sheraton hotels. The breakfast was also good. Overall, the stay was very good. The staff at the hotel was friendly, and I have no problems recommending the Four Points by Sheraton San Diego to other business travelers!

“Great Location” Stayed at the Westin 2 Nights for a business meeting - but included alot of personal fun as well. Absolutely the best location - close to all the shows, Times Square chaos, shopping, etc. ! The Ambassador Meeting rooms were nice, very responsive staff, great food. The staff was extremely helpful and the rooms were quite nice - LOVE the bedding. I have never slept so well. Nice spacious bathrooms, flatscreen tv's. The bar was a great stop every night - extremely courteous staff, polite, helpful with recommendations. Always easy to get a cab from this location and always easy to find somewhere fun to go.

“You pay for what you get” This is by far and away one of my best upscale hotel choices. The cost makes regular visits prohibitive but if you can get a deal or want to splurge for an occasion this is where to stay in NYC. Great location on Park Ave. Not in center of thngs but close enough.

“Will Be Back” This is a very comfortable and very reasonably priced hotel. Great value. We stayed in a king suite. The layout is very nice, the decor is up to date, and the room is clean. The service is also accommodating and professional. I look forward to returning during my next visit to San Antonio. The only sub-par item I would mention is the use of those little square pillows so many hotels today are using. They are awful! You can't turn around on them without your head falling off. I certainly hope they will consider reinstituting standard sized pillows again. I did find one tucked away in the room, but it seemed to be rendered unusable (from overuse by people avoiding the little square pillows?). Anyhow, if this is an issue for you, and you are able, bring your own.

“Nice stay” Stayed here a few weeks ago for an overnight stay. The lobby was under construction but check-in was great due to an awesome unexpected early check-in and free upgrade to a corner room on the 21st floor. The rooms have been completely renovated and look FAB as do the hallways. My only complaint was that the doorman talked us into parking across the street - saving us $15 with in and out privileges. The only problem was that the service at the garage was EXTREMELY slow. You had to get aggressive with the guys in order for them to help you. The lines to get our car were long and one time it took nearly 20 minutes to get the car. To me it wasn't worth saving $15. We had a few drinks at the rooftop bar one of favorites hotel bars in the city. We were sad to find out that the bar was closing for good in a few days to make room for ballroom space. We had lots of good memories at that place - its the end of an era. But the completely revamped Grand Hyatt is a new beginning.

“A wonderful hotel and great value” I shouldn't even write a review on this hotel because in doing so more people will want to stay here and it will harder for me to get a room next time I am in NYC. This place is great for business traveler or even when traveling with the family. The rooms are big and very clean. I love the full kitchen. Roof top bar in the spring and summer are awesome with great views of the city. Staff couldn't be more helpful (be sure to say hello to Dennis at the door, he has info on everything) Super convenient location with just a short walk to the NY Public Library, Grand Central, Bryant Park and the list goes on. Do yourself a favor and stay at this hotel. You won't regret it . . . Joe Sloboda

“Nice Rooms, Good Service, Convenient Location & Shops” My girlfriend and I stayed at the Affinia Dumont from the last Saturday in October and departed on the first Saturday in November of 06'. The weather was a bit mild for this time of the year but did get a bit colder towards the end of the week. I was attending a week long workshop at Cornell University ILR Management centers - a few blocks downs on 34th. Since my girlfriend was with me...I wanted for her to stay in a nice place during the week while I was in class. Our taxi ride from NY LGA was about $24.00. We arrived early in the morning so our room was not ready. We walked to a nearby Guy & Gallard for early lunch and then walked to Macys. The Affinia doorman are attentitve and friendly. The front desk staff are not as friendly. They offer free fruit at the front desk as well as free NY Times & Wall Street Journal in the small lobby. USA today is delivered to your door every weekday morning. Our room was studio which featured comfortable bed, bright window view with the curtains open, a desk and Herman Miller Aeron chair and a lounge chair. The bathroom was small but clean. The featured tolietries - Avena products were so..so..so. The kitchenette was the best feature because we could keep beverages (Duane Reade down and accross street and grocery store on 3rd avenue) and leftovers as well as fruits and snacks refrigerated. The room was good size for New York city. The gym was nice but small and had a good view of 34th street. We used the facilities almost daily. There are many nearby restaurants and small grocery stores. In particular on 3rd Ave there are larger grocery stores and a Borders nearby for some recreational reading. The subway station on Madison is convenient for going both downtown and uptown. We took the subway to both Chinatown and then uptown to Rockfeller Center. We went to very good Malaysian restaurant in Chinatown called Jaya. You can purchase many knock off products in Chinatown such as Philipe Patek watches and Burberry scarfs. Since we like Asian food, we tried several neighborhood Asian restaurants, though I have to admit they are very Westernized and not as good as West Coast Asian restaurants which are more authentic. For cheap, good, and ample servings, we liked Spade's Chinese Resturant on 557 Third Ave & Corner of 37 Street. Also tried Saigon Taste - Vietnamese cooking which was average on 120 E. 34th street. Lemon Grass Thai Grill on 138 E. 34th Street is totally westernized and a bit overpriced. Koreatown is not too far away...on West 32nd Street. We went twice to Seoul Garden which is on 34 W. 32nd St. on the second floor. Many Korean American students go here because the prices are reasonable and the food is good. My Girlfriend ate in Macys for lunch which she was good. We ate the Chain Chiptole which is always good. We tried Italian placed called Libretto's Pizzera on 546 34rd Ave @ 36th St. We had takeout pasta and pizza. The food was good. But the service was Terrible and I probably won't go there again. Overall the Affinia is nice place to stay if you can get a good rate...I have a few more workshops to take at Cornell ILR so I will be back in NYC in both January and May of 07. I plan to stay at Affina's Murrary Hill Sheburne for two weeks in January, because some Cornell classmates recommended it, a bit old in decor and furnishings but otherwise very nice. The prices are very good. In May, I might try to save some money and stay at the Red Roof Inn on 32nd for a no frills but economic place to stay, it's true...you don't really spend too much time in NYC, so may not be necessary to spend $$$ to stay at better place, unless your partner is with you. In May, I might split a week at Red Roof Inn and at the Residence Inn Times Square. I'd stay at the Affinia again if I could get really good rate or if I'd want to spend a romantic trip to NYC.

“BEAUTIFUL and relaxing!” If you're staying in Dallas and want an out-of-the-ordinary hotel stay, check this place out. Our first fifteen minutes after check-in were so welcoming. Guests get one staff member who tends to your needs during your stay - they know your name and are super friendly! We were welcomed with a pear tart and pomegranate iced tea = FANTASTIC! The hotel restaurants are to die for. The room is beautiful and the bathroom is even better. This hotel has MY FAVORITE SOAPS THAT I'VE EVER USED IN A HOTEL. Must grab some to go. :) The spa and gym are great; eucalyptus oil in the steam sauna stays with you and even after your trip, you want to go back for more. Definitely coming back!

“Nice place- but wouldn't pay more than what we paid through Travelzoo” I spent two nighs here with my mom over MLK weekend. There were private events going on both nights, so we were not able to go into the Promenade area at night, and if you were staying on that side of the hotel you would have to walk around to the other set of elevators. Perhaps the special on Travelzoo was related to this ($139). It was pretty fun to ogle the beautiful people though! The room was clean and large. As others have stated, it is a bit worn, and has that grand old hotel feel. The bathroom was very spacious, but was freezing if you didn't leave the door open at night. Water pressure/hot water was fine. The beds were very comfortable, but the heating system kicked on and off. No noise in the hallways or outside. The only fridge was the minibar and there was not room for much else in there. The fitness center was really lovely. Some very top of the line equipment, and fresh apples to grab on the way out. It smelled good too. We did not eat in the restaurants. We asked for extra coffee packets and they were brought up immediately. The best thing about the hotel is its location. One block to Farragut North metro, and close to restaurants, Dupont Circle etc. It was not crowded at all when we stayed, I don't know what it would be like if filled with business travelers. We would definitely stay there again for a similar price, but not more than that. The affordable pricing and location push my overall review to a 4, but otherwise probably a 3.

“solid (if forgettable) convention hotel” Decent place that does a good job cranking through the massive amounts of traffic from the convention center right across the street. Front desk and concierge service were outstanding, though wait service in the bar/restaurant areas was slow and of the immediately bring you the check with the first drink variety. Rooms were large and just fine. I hadn't stayed at a Hyatt Regency in a while, but expected at least a notch up from the standard mid-range hotel. By that standard, this was a bit of a letdown. The positives: Beds were comfortable, TV was a respectably sized flat screen, simple coffeemaker (though arrrgghhh--one sugar and nasty non-dairy "creamer" per wastefully packaged packet). Big points for a laptop-friendly safe and iron/ironing board/hair dryer. Plenty of storage space. On the downside, the heavy down comforter might be great for the dead of winter, but combined with an underpowered A/C unit made sleeping a bit uncomfortable. Chairs were a bit dingy and stained, and shower/products felt a bit on the cheap side. Outside the room, the workout facilities are some of the best I've seen in any hotel--well stocked with aerobic equipment, at least a dozen upper and lower body machines, plus a few free weights and a large rack of dumbbells. I didn't use it, but I believe there was a small lap pool adjacent as well. Lobby was also nice, doing a good job of breaking up the usual cavernous convention hotel feeling with lots of separate seating areas and a slightly more upscale vibe. Decent (non-Starbucks for a change) coffee and great service at the small snack bar/gift shop. The bar bar was good, except for the previously mentioned pokey service. Overall more "Hyatt" than "Regency," but not a bad option if you're in town for a convention.

“Excellent location, large room by NYC standards” It seems like I am always staying in a different hotel in NYC, trying to get the best deal and save my company some money. This was my first time staying in a Courtyard in NYC and have to say that I will definitely return to this property on return business trips. First, there are a few things to know about NYC hotels. They are always going to be expensive and rooms are going to be small, that's just a given. So I thought the price was very fair and the room among the largest I've had in NYC. This is not the hotel for a romantic getaway with a spouse or a party of any kind as it does not have the amenities of a full service hotel, but for a business trip it was perfect. Walking distance to almost anything in midtown Manhattan, a drug store less than a block away and a number of good restaurants (I recommend Hillstone) in the nearby Citigroup plaza. I echo the thoughts of another reviewer, the 12th floor lounge was very comfortable. I did some work there while watching one of the many flat panel televisions. There is also a full service bar open in the evenings. My status as Gold elite was recognized, I was given an upgraded room (corner) on one of the highest floors. Sadly, silver elite is a dime a dozen for Marriott and I am not surprised by the reviewer who was not recognized nor given anything for that status. But that is the way airlines and hotels all work, it's normally only the premium elite that enjoy the perks.

“Large resort style hotel that's close to transportation into Seattle.” I chose the Hilton Doubletree Seatac Airport because it had a free shuttle to the airport. I had a 5am flight and the Doubletree had great free shuttle times to get me to the airport on time. This hotel was also close to the metro train to get into and out of Seattle. Check in was fast and my room was clean. This hotel had a nice on site Starbucks and a late night restaurant. The late night menu was very expensive and I could not bring myself to order because the prices were so outrageous. I'll pay good money for good food, but that was a simple late night menu. I'm glad I did not have a rental car because the prices they wanted to park were obscene and clearly taking advantage of the guest. The hotel had a nice outdoor heated pool and hot tub that was being used by a ton of children, so I didn't get a chance to use the spa area. There was a large band camp going on for high schoolers so the hotel was filled with kids. I note this because the hotel was very quiet considering. The hotel staff did a good job making sure the children were not a bother to the other guests. My room was clean and spacious. The shower area was nice and had a lot of counter space. My room also had a very large balcony. Over all I'd stay here again. I just wouldn't park a car or eat at the restaurant.

“Love the location” You can almost fall out of the Gallery Place Metro stop and end up in the hotel, which is definitely a plus. Walking distance to the Mall and several good restaurants. Rooms were nice... nothing too over-the-top, but definitely cozy, lots of power plugs and, if you're a Kimpton member, free wi-fi. My room had an amazing view of stacked up wooden palettes in the alley, so perhaps ask for an upper floor? Front desk was helpful when needed and the restaurant, Poste, is solid, if pricey. The layout of the place is a bit odd... the building used to be a post office and this gives you some very cool spaces, but the rooms are spread out. Overall, it's definitely on the better end of places I have stayed in the District.

“Wonderful Hotel...Great location!!!” Stayed here for a long weekend over Mother's Day. This was one of the best places we have stayed in the city. Extremely clean. Staff was more than helpful and friendly. Room was great size for myself, husband and 2 children. Had no problems with noise. We were on the 35th floor so I am sure that helps. Had room service one evening and it was fast and tasty. The location is what really put this hotel over the top. We were able to walk to everything we wanted to do. If we needed to take a cab there were always plenty out front. This will be our hotel of choice from now on.

“Fabulous location but as noisy as you'd expect.” This has got to be one of the finest locations for a tourist to stay. There is a fridge and a microwave so you can eat really cheaply if you want to. You literally fall put of the front door in to the middle of Times Square. But of course being in the thick of things means its noisy all day and all night, specially if you are on one of the lower floors. If you stay here then check out The View at the Marriott opposite. It's a revolving bar and restaurant right at the top of the hotel, with the most amazing views across the city. Pricey but literally the best view in town.

“Pretty good” Needed to try and different hotel from The Dylan where I have stayed before and I'm glad I did. T he Library is a nice small hotel, fairly unremarkable, not somewhere I'd take the Mrs for a romantic break but is plum in the middle of everything, has good staff, is clean, got a bit character and everything seems to work. Will stay again.

“Good location. Nice additions but implementation need to be ironed out” $140-150 standard double/night Pros - Location is good. Near the financial district, 4min walk to Pershing Square Metro station. The hotel is located between 2 streets (Olive St is the main entrance, but you can enter from Grand St or even California plaza). 7min walk to the financial district and very close to Central Markets (on Hill st). - Spacious and clean room. Sign up for Omni membership to get free wifi otherwise $10/day. Apparently you can also use the complementary sedan to get to places within 3miles of the hotel - I did not use this. -Nice decor Cons - Reception Staff not overly helpful or welcoming. - Apparently I should have received complementary morning beverage with my Omni membership but there was no form or anything to request this. Overall a very nice hotel in the middle of downtown. Omni membership was suppose to make the experience more special but it was just another hotel membership.

“Nice place to stay in Memphis” I was very comfortable and very happy with the location of this hotel. It was located by many restaurants and a LIfetime fitness. The room and bed was very clean, the food at the hotel was basic, but good. The staff was friendly and helpful. I would stay here again.

“Nice Location” The hotel is in a prime central location in central city which is essential given how dangerous Philadelphia can be. Walking around this area at night is fairly safe but stay away from the underground and smaller roads. My room was a really good size with good A/C and good views of the city. The bathroom was nice and clean. I would of preferred a mini bar but that's not really a big deal.

“Good value for NYC” Our family of 4 (kids aged 3 and 6) stayed for a week. It was good value for money and had everything you needed. It is a little tired but is very very clean. It's a perfect budget option for NYC. If I were to return to NYC, I would probably stay closer to Central park, we spent a lot of time traveling uptown to see museums, broadway shows, children's zoo etc but you might like the location of Nyma literally around the corner from the Empire State building.

“Really enjoyed my 6 nights at the Ace” I just returned from a 6 nights stay over Memorial Day long weekend and was quite happy with all the Ace Hotel delivered. I was lucky enough to have spied a $129/night + tax rate on a small king room back in Feb. through Travelzoo and as the rate could be cancelled up to 2 days prior to arrival I held a reservation thinking something as good or better might come along. Well, none did and the more reviews and online press articles I read the more I wanted to experience this hotel for myself so stuck with my reservation and checked in on 27th May. The room I was assigned was on the top floor, the 12th floor, in 1228 and it was more than adequate for a solo traveller. There are some quirks to the room like the closet right next to the bed consisting of a metal rack and half a dozen hangars, a darker colour sceme and "lived in" table. While it wasn't noted on the room info on the hotel's website there was a safe in the room, which came as a pleasant surprise. The Smeg fridge was big enough to store a few beverages bought off-site and hotel management didn't take them away for otherwise try to discourage. The pricing of the sodas & beer in the fridge is not quite as high as other chain hotels but $6-7 for a beer is at least twice what the little convenience store around the corner sells the same brand for so keep that in mind. Every review spoke of the hugely comfortable bed and it lived up to it's billing as it is super comfy and offerd a relaxing sleep. The two bedside table lamps are on a dimmer switch which is also a nice user-friendly touch and they along with the windows help brighten the room during the day. Also very much appreciated were the hooded robes provided for use during your stay, though you can puchase them for $150. The bathroom was small but everything worked well and the body wash, shampoo and conditioner dispensers were handy to use. The solid metal doors were also unique and while they were well built and offered good security they weren't too soundproof. Later one night a few guests standing outside their door directly across from mine saying goodnight at a casual conversational level almost sounded like they were in my room, though luckily during the whole stay this played a very small part and overall sleep quality was high for this fairly light sleeper. In short a very functional room with a slight twist to make it different and out of the typical chain hotel room mould. The lobby does attract a good size crowd most nights, though it seemed to thin out over the long holiday weekend which was the opposite of what I'd expected. I didn't have to deal with bouncer/doormen other reviewers mentioned but was given a very warm welcome when I checked in. I did spend some time in the lobby living room and one night ordered a beer and charged it back to my room but found the $7.50 beer became $8.88 when an 18% gratuity was tacked on so take note. It is a nice space and the staff don't demand you order anything from the bar so you could inhabit a comfy corner and unwind. I didn't try the restraurant, the Breslin, but the Stumptown coffee shop was good if also a little pricey. The location of the Ace has it's pros and cons; it isn't right in Midtown so isn't as convenient as other hotels but I liked being away from the hectic crossroads around Time Square. There is a subway stop a block away and getting anywhere within the city by subway is easy and convenient and I felt quite safe. The area directly around the hotel is changing and there are some less attractive stretches but there's enough foot traffic from the Empire State Building and nearby Korea Town that evern up to 11pm I also didn't feel unsafe walking from the subway or a nearby convenience store. I did walk one night from the Time Square area but at 15-20 blocks is too far to do it on a regular basis. The Flatiron Building and adjacent Madison Square Park is closer at 5 blocks. There is a wonderful cafe a block over on W. 28th Street called Cafe 28 and it serves cooked to order meals including a delicious breakfast I ate most days with two eggs with bacon, bagel and OJ for around $7, a very good value compared to other breakfast spots I tried elsewhere. Note this little cafe also sells stamps should you have forgotten to pick some up at the post office. I was referred to this little cafe by an Ace Hotel staff member and it was a good call as I enjoyed starting my day with a good breakfast and people watching from tables looking over the sidewalk. In closing I very much enoyed my stay at the Ace as I felt like a traveller, not a tourist, and wanted something different, more authentically New York for this my third visit to NYC. The staff was very welcoming and friendly and the accommodation was easy to like for me, though would expect its edgy aspects may not be as well liked by everyone. I could easily see myself checking availability & pricing here first if I was planning another escape to NYC but much would depend on price as to whether I ultimately would go back. At the Travelzoo rate I got including taxes of around $150/night I'd return without question but would hesitate at the normal non-discounted rate of approx. $300/night for the small king room I was in.

“GREAT LOCATION, DATED BUT OK” Rented a studio for a week but due to mixup on my arrival date, landlady put me up for one night in this hotel. Location is fantastic, right across from the Prudential, rooms are a bit dated but very clean, comfy, with large flatscreen tv, plenty of HD channels, kitchenette,shower with good water pressure. It is laid out as a motel (one floor only) but not noisy at all and definitely felt safe. If you get a good rate, I'd definitely recommend it!

“Great Airport Hotel” This Hyatt could hold its own in any downtown in a large city. Very nice lobby, great rooms, excellent food and truly outstanding service. The rates reflect it, too, so if all you need is a place to sleep when your flight is canceled, this may be more than you need. But, if it's in your budget, absolutely choose it. Only two criticisms: the rooms are not soundproof, so if you are a light sleeper, bring ear plugs for the air traffic, and the bathroom lighting is ridiculously dark. But, overall, very, very nice.

“Very happy with this establishment!” Stayed a Saturday night. Lady at the front desk with so friendly and helpful, she really started off the visit the right way. Lobby is nice and has a small convenience store area as well as a small bar and jukebox in the breakfast area. Breakfast was good with waffles, cereal, eggs, sausage, bisquits & gravy, toast, cinnamon rolls, bagels, coffee and juice. At this awesome price, I was shocked when I walked into the king bed suite...lots of room and immaculate. Had 2 spaces separated by 2 french style doors. Living room had fridge, microwave, sink for a wet bar, 2 chairs, footstool, sofa, desk and chair. The bedroom had large vanity and mirror, 2 wardrobes and a hanging closet, nightstand and tv with limited cable. Fresh paint, clean carpet, great heater and bathroom was in it's own little room and was very clean with an environmentally conscience toilet (2 different flushes). Only problems were minor: (1) tv was the only thing not updated, but worked fine and (2) shower water never got hot, but was warm enough to shower quickly. Overall, VERY pleased and look forward to staying again and again! Location is right off the highway and surrounded by empty land on one side and behind with 4 hotels lined down the street on the other side...very safe. Bus also stops right in front. Excellent choice!

“Very Pleasant” With the location and the price, my expectations of this hotel were pretty low. I was quite surprised to find how nice the hotel was. The staff could not have been more helpful or friendly. Upon check-in I requested a quiet room. I know, a quiet room in NYC, dream on! Again, shockingly surprised to get an interior room that was so quiet you couldn't have guessed you were even in a city. The beds were harder than I like and the bathroom had one of those annoying new square shallow sinks, but the wine and cheese reception was warm and friendly. Don't miss the chance to step out on the terrace from the hospitality suite, what a view!!! Overall, a most pleasant experience, one I will seek out again!

“Beautiful hotel, in convenient location” Was planning a trip for wife's "big" birthday so we decided on San Francisco and other parts of Northern California. Looked on TripAdvisor and other sites for good reviews and good value. Always like staying in in Omni's and price was reasonable (for San Francisco). Made reservations and was all set. Staff was very friendly and accommodating upon arrival and throughout the stay. When we got in delivered a cake plate other items in recognition of her birthday. Room was a little small but well appointed and very nice. Location turned out to be very good neutral site, in the heart of the financial district with easy walking access to Union Square, Chinatown, North Beach, Ferry Building and transportation around other parts of Bay Area. Fun time, nice place and highly recommend for nice luxury hotel.

“Quite happy with my stay” I came here for a conference and am basing my review on the rate I paid of about $120 per night. I travel quite a bit, with gold status with SPG and HHonors, as well as platinum with IHG. I stayed for 5 nights, including one leisure day. Basically, this hotel had just about everything I hope for in a hotel. No, the lobby ain't the most breathtakingly beautiful, and if I had to give one real negative, the pool is a bit of a joke. It's nestled between the parking lot and the parking lot entrance to the lobby and restaurant. Yuck. Who wants to have to walk through that. Other than that, it's just what I wanted (I wasn't planning to use the pool anyways). The room size is ample. Two flat-screen TV's, one with the bed, and the other with the couch. The sink area is separate from the bathroom--always nice if two people are trying to get ready in the morning (although I was alone for this trip). The desk was a comfortable work space, and the free internet actually worked quite well for a free hotel internet (I wish this were a case for a number of other Starwood properties). I'm a light sleeper and was able to sleep every night without earplugs. Such luxury! I once heard my neighbor who was talking loudly on the phone in the living room area, but couldn't hear him once I closed the door to the living room. They even have a turndown service--with chocolates and flowers on the pillows and towels. I wondered if I needed to tip them to get the flowers and chocolates, so I didn't tip housekeeping one day, and sure enough, no chocolates or flowers. Still, I felt like I was on a luxury cruise. Although this hotel is ranked only 3-diamonds by AAA, I really felt like I was staying at a 4-star facility. The only lack of luxury was the pool and the lack of a grand lobby, but I wasn't really worrying about that on this trip, since I came for business. The only other little glitch that I might mention is that on the Saturday night, due to a party, self-parking was full, but they did valet my car for no extra charge. The distance to the Galleria is walkable in good weather, but I'm sure I wouldn't want to be doing it on a hot, steamy Houston summer day.

“our favorite San Diego hotel” We like charm and unique (non-chain) hotels, so we've been staying at the Park Manor for the last 8 years whenever we're in San Diego. (If you require modern facilities, this is not for you.) With full kitchens and built-ins, I could imagine living at the Park Manor if I ever had to stay in San Diego for an extended visit. We've been bumped up to one- and two-bedroom suites a few times, and those are really nice if you can spend the extra $. But the studios are great, too - far more room than the chain hotels. The continental breakfast is adequate, but nothing special.

“great place to stay at LAX” I stayed at this hotel at the end of my trip, before an early flight out of LAX. The staff was great. The room was spacious and quiet, clean and everything worked. The WiFI (free) worked fine although a bit slow. The free airport shuttle ran on time. The hotel even has coffee and muffins in the lobby for guests who have to leave earlier than the breakfast opens- which is a nice plus that I have not seen before.

“Finally a place to stay in this part of town” I first found Ink48 when they offered special room rates for their soft open in 2009. I have been coming back ever since. It is my NYC hotel of choice, unless rates are through the roof - which can happen in NYC. The Hell's Kitchen neighborhood has so much to offer - especially great cafe's and dining spots along 9th. The hotel is a Kimpton, which always makes me happy - robes, free wi-fi, wine hour, and a very reasonable upgrade plan. The view from the city view rooms at dusk and dawn are worth it - especially if you can get a photo! The Hudson Suite - one of their premier suites on each floor offers a beautiful Hudson view. I think I have stayed in every size room this hotel offers and I am always comfortable. The bath products are either Aveda or Italian and when you have a soaking tub they leave you salts, The soaking tubs are so worth the room upgrade but all of the bathrooms are top-notch. I have not had an inside room which might be a bit claustrophobic but the lobby lounge is a comfortable hangout spot with a giant wooden table and comfy chairs. I have also dined at the in-house restaurant Print and the food is consistently delicious. The Press Lounge is a great place for a drink while you soak in the city views. The staff are attentive and respectful - I truly feel like Ink48 is my second home! The only draw back is there is not a subway stop close by but the walking feels great!

“Stylish and hip” I stayed 3 nights at the Valencia while attending a conference. It was a big change from my previous experiences with chain hotels in San Antonio. My room was large, with a balcony, and faced a lovely, quiet courtyard. I had read reviews that mentioned noise when people hung out in the courtyard but it was always empty during my stay. The bed linens (and the bed in general) were terrific but I was not a huge fan of the waffle-weave towels--cool and European in concept but just not all that fun to use. The overall look is sleek, modern, and very dark, with dark wood and strategic lighting (placed more for ambience than practicality). Free high-speed internet access and Aveda toiletries were a plus. The gym was small and only OK but not out of line for a small boutique hotel. The staff were all young, exceedingly earnest and friendly, and with time I think will develop into a polished group. All in all, it was a terrific experience and I expect to stay there again next year.

“Highly Recommended” I booked this hotel through Priceline and at check-in, the only mention of Priceline was that it was a prepaid reservation. The very friendly staff member asked what type of room we wanted and we asked if they had one with nice view. We were given an upgrade to a very nice room on a high floor with a view of the Empire State Building. The room was great, very clean and comfortable. The location was very convenient and a quick walk from GCT. I had a great experience at this hotel and woud happily stay there again.

“great for us” we needed a place to stay one night before a cruise....we wanted near the airport as we were travelling with 3 young children (3.5 yrs and below).....their van got us at the airport and all our bags (11 of us travelling together)....rooms were huge....everything was very nice....quiet for by the airport....we can't speak for the neighborhood as we didn't leave the property (van-ned the next a.m. to cruise pier)....my only criticism was restaurant was way expensive....if your travelling with kids like we were or on a budget, the restaurant was mucho bucks...not family friendly at all (seemed like good food, but....)

“Top hotel in top location!” After reading loads of reviews on this hotel (mostly good but some bad), we bit the bullet and booked it and thank god we did! We love the LES, so many great bars, restaurant's, cafes and shops within a stones throw of the hotel. Check Schillers for dinner and a drink 1 block away and grab an awesome crepe for breakfast on the opposite corner of the hotel.
