We have a room on the 14th floor looking uptown directly at the empire state and have had magnificent sunset's to watch from our room each night (i am looking at one as i write this). The staff have all been lovely and extremely helpful with everything we have needed, we have had complimentary freshly baked cookies dropped off to us in the evening, the room has been cleaned well and promptly every day and the tempur beds are wonderful - a little different at first but we love them. Great bathroom amenities, nice powerful shower, comfy bath robes and a well stocked minibar. For the money, this hotel is a winner if you want to be downtown. A 5 minute walk to soho and East village, rooms are a good size for nyc standards (we have a sitting area and 2 large suitcases and we can still move around easily) and free wifi. Love hotel on Rivington x

“Typical great Hilton Property Experience” I LOVE this place! Close to everything (Mich Ave, Oak St, Rush, Beach, Hancock Bldg, Water Tower, etc) & affordable. All Chicago Hilton properties are great but my stays in Chi are usually longer, so I enjoyed the the suites. City (Fantastic!) & lake Viiews from top floors are great. There is also a little grocery store in the bottom of the building right across the street.

“Great hotel” We had high expectations for our pre-cruise stay, and were looking forward to a couple of days of relaxation and shopping. Our room was spacious with a balcony overlooking the main pool and although not commanding the dramatic views of the higher floors, was very pleasant (given this hotel was obtained through an opaque booking option, sometimes choices are hit and miss). I am surprised at some reviews describing negative experiences with staff as we encountered nothing but friendly and very efficient service - the guest service agent who checked us in - Dinah - is a gem. The hotel location could be a somewhat negative aspect as the hotel is away from the downtown core of San Diego. However, I researched transport options and we had no trouble accessing public transit. Should you prefer a cab, it is only a 12 minute journey into the city. Given the hotel's proximity to the airport, there was little or no noise issues. We would stay here again any time.

“Great find in Phoenix” This was a perfect overnight in Phoenix. The fact that it was a gay, clothing-optional was icing on the cake. The Safari suite was very private, adorable and with a nicely appointed kitchenette.

“Very nice, but some things need attention” One really shouldn't complain about a free night (courtesy of our friend's SPG points) and we did overall have an excellent stay. So why the niggling? A 5* hotel shouldn't have cracked sinks (both our room & our friends, and a cracked shower tile & slightly dirty grout (it's a pet peeve of mine). The public areas & even the hallways are spectacular (very tall ornate ceilings), so why the inattention to the bathrooms?After a major remodel, we were also surprised that the walls were thin enough to hear our neighbors, and banging in the halls. Personally, the mattress felt hard to me, and I prefer a firm mattress. Another minus - no free wifi, and coffee only available up to 10 AM apparently in the lobby. The location is close enough to walk to ATT Park, the Ferry Plaza, Union Square & Market Street shopping. Slightly amusing note - Murdock was speaking at a conference, and there were pickets briefly in the morning at one of the entrances. The room was large for a hotel of this vintage & the interior rooms overlook the glass ceilinged Garden Court. Room also included a refrigerator (which was quiet), a safe (laptop sized), armchair & large work desk. No coffee maker. Good, quiet air conditioning. Check in was fast & efficient, and front desk was helpful with bus information.

“Nice property, convenient location” Large rooms, recently renovated ... Friendly, helpful, professional staff ... Convenient location ... Restaurant has breakfast and dinner buffet - nice, though a bit pricey.

“Good value with site seeing with young family” Good set up for our family of five (two queens in bedroom and 1 pullout couch in sitting area). For what we'd pay for a normal room, we were happy to get a suite. Nothing fancy about the hotel, but we came to see all the tourist sites, not to sit in a boring hotel room. Right across from Hancock Tower, one block from Magnificent Mile. Any taxi ride to stuff like the museum, aquarium, pier, etc. was never much more than $10. Only complaints: - couldn't use the pool (freezing cold - I think the heater must've been busted) - the pool area could use a good cleaning - $50/night valet parking - ouch!

“Well run hotel for an extremely busy weekend” I stayed here for the Florida-Georgia football game. The hotel was very busy and run well. Had a nice view of the river from my room. The walls were a little thin. I could hear conversation in the next room in the morning. I don't think they were being loud. No free wifi was a minus.

“Very convenient” We always stay here when we visit SF; very convenient to walk to many attractions/city transportation, plus the indoor free parking is great. However, leave your big pick-up or SUV at home because the parking is VERY cramped to say the least. Very nice, but small, rooms that are beginning to show a little age in the furnishings and fixtures. The last time we were there though the elevator had a terrible smell in it and the roof leaked at night in the hall and a light fixture crashed to the floor. Very quiet, in fact, one of the "quietest" places we've ever stayed in--you can't hear any noise from the halls, other bathrooms, etc. But if you stay on the Lombard Avenue side, you may hear traffic noise. A great little breakfast place up Lombard to the left, Lombardy Cafe. And a nice deli a block behind is the Fort Mason Deli. 70+ TV channels. Great rates during the week, and Bernard at the front desk is very helpful and personable. For the price/convenience/free parking in a VERY expensive city like SF, the Buena Vista can't be beat.

“Fun spot for everyone” We stayed at the Topaz Hotel for a long weekend with our 4yr old daughter and were very pleased with our stay. The location of the hotel was great for us as it is centrally located (cab fare to the White House, Georgetown, and Lincoln Memorial was $8). The rooms are spacious, well decorated, and clean. Noise was not a problem, though given my choice I would have selected a room off the street. The hotel staff was very accommodating. The hotel runs various promotions so you will most likely be best served using the online reservation system to take advantage of the one that suits you best. We did not eat at the hotel, but that is not a reflection of the perceived quality of the restaurant. There are many dining options within close proximity of the hotel that we wanted to at least check out.

“Interesting decor and good service” All in all a good stay. Positives: - Good location. While it's a bit away from the noising downtown area, it is good location for Rice University and the Museums along with a good public park. This is a hotel for relaxed travellers, not for the business people. - Shuttle service. The hotel does provide a first-come first-serve shuttle service within a 5 mile radius, which is convenient if you are looking for attractions around. - Unique decor. Updated decor in the rooms and common areas shows humor and quality. Liked it a lot. - Decent room service. The in-room dining menu was pretty good and pricing acceptable. The fruit plate should not be missed! - Great service. Impeccable hospitality from the bell man to the front desk to the room server. Negatives: - Room size. I had a queen petite and really, it was petite. No bathtub in the room, only a standing shower and spaces in the bathroom is quite limited. - Noise. I think there was a wedding reception or something going on in the hotel. I can hear music blasting around mid-night, although I didn't think it was too bad.

“great hotel, great location, great value” Stayed at the Salisbury for three nights at the end of a long road trip across the USA. I usually stay at the Milford Plaza, but booked with freinds into Salisbury. Same 'star' rating, but a better quality of stay here. The 'suite' was very large and clean. Stayed on the 12th floor, facing 57th. As has been previously stated, you can here traffic noise, but it's New York, you should expect that. I used the sofa bed which was very comfortable. Very large living area (for New York City) and flat screen large TV. Also kitchen area with microwave, fridge, coffee maker etc. Bedroom was large with two double beds. The bathroom (although clean) was slightly dated, and small. No problems with shower pressure and hot water. Ideal location, within minutes of Central Park and Times Square. Also walked down to Madison Square Garden for hockey and basketball. There is a subway within yards of front entrance. $45 taxi to JFK. Great stay, and maybe tempted to use this hotel in future on visits to NYC. Highly recommended.

“Comfortable with a great location and friendly service” Stayed here for the Game Developer Conference Online event which was next door at the Austin Convention Centre. The good thing about the hotel is that even though the convention centre had two events going on, it was nice and quiet in the hotel. Only the awesome lobby Starbucks was full in the mornings. The hotels' Champions sports restaurant is actually pretty good too even if the buffet breakfast is rather standard fare, it's okay for the price and has the usual stuff you'd expect. The restaurant is also spacious and has a small patio, so there's always space available. I have to say the hotel's service was really friendly and not intrusive. I'm European, I dont need to be asked how I'm doing every time I walk by! :) Both the staff at the reception desk and at the door, were friendly and very helpful. The room is your usual Courtyard room. Bed was comfy, bathroom big and definitely had enough space for one's toiletries and lots of towels.It was also really quiet and the free wifi was very fast for being free. The gym had lots of exercise bikes and felt like a real gym, not a small hotel crammed full of a few exercise machines. There's also a pool behind the gym. The hotel's location is superb. 6th street which has all the bars and restaraunt's is two blocks away and well, a block away to any direction, you had some great restaurants. I recommend the Downtown burger joint across the street from the hotel's main entrance. Would definitely stay here again. It's a franchise, but a high-quality one, feels comfortable and efficient and is not super-expensive, even if I find it strange I pay almost more in Austin, than in bigger US cities.

“Well located and nicely renovated” This hotel has been obviously renovated within the past year or two, as it isn't nearly as tired as most Four Points. The location is excellent for walking to downtown or parts of Queen Anne. Parking is $13 per night, but that beats driving around looking for nonexistent street parking and having the homeless break into your rental (Seattle is overrun with the homeless).

“Stylish hotel” Rooms are beautiful. We were staying with our 2 kids and felt we had lots of room in our King Suite with 1 kid on sofabed and the other in a cot. The King Bed was super comfortable. The rooftop pool is fantastic, very stylish. Fantastic location right on the Riverwalk and in the middle of downtown. Valet parking is expensive but there is a cheaper carpark opposite. Occasionally had to wait at front desk for staff but all in all excellent service.

“Great Location and price” We just visited Austin for the first time. This hotel is in a great place. It is on a major street that has lots of places to walk to within 6-10 blocks. It is right next to the river that is great for scenery, and to jog. The great thing about the location is that is the best hotel location to see the the famous bats that are under the Congress Street bridge. Sounds weird, but it is a sight you will not want to miss. Hundreds of people line up at dusk to see this amazing event, and the Radisson has the best location for this. The bats only are in Austin for certain months, so check on the timing with the hotel...I think it is May thru August. The Radisson has a Friday's restaurant that is hooked up as their eatery. The food was good, and predictable. All and all we really enjoyed our stay here and would definetly return to this hotel.

“Great Hotel” In a City of convention size hotels this boutique property has it all. The interior is done in good taste on a Ritz or Four Seasons level. Breakfast was very good and the Riverwalk seating makes it even better. The staff is friendly and dedicated to taking care of guests needs. You can have complimentary coffee delivered to your room at any time plus the is a Nepresso machine in the room.

“Once again, they did it!” There is no better deal in downtown Seattle. $86 for a decent, clean King Room in a Great Location!. Amy in the bar is a delight! Too bad it's gonna be knocked down. Amazon has purchased the property and is making room for 3 million feet of office space......

“Quirky but Comfortable” Superbly located opposite the harbour and within easy access to Downtown and other beach areas, the Dolphin Motel has a simple philosophy of "give us a chance and compare". This attracted me to it instantly - it was a no BS approach, and they didn't let themselves down. Having never been to San Diego before, I was unsure of the location, but once we were settled, we found it very easy to get anywhere we needed to go; and the added assistance of the front desk staff and particularly the owner who provided basic but effective hand drawn maps and easy to follow directions. However, I would suggest that if you wish to explore wider San Diego, then a car is a necessity. The rooms are quite small, but well appointed for the price, and the beds are extremely comfortable with crisp white linen. The bathrooms are tight, but the shower has the best water pressure of any hotel I have ever stayed at. The clientele of the hotel appear to be mainly people using the harbour for fishing or diving trips, and given they are up quite early in the morning, do not expect a sleep in, as the central courtyard area can get quite noisy. The complimentary continental breakfast provided consists of muffins & coffee, and is a welcome start to the day, however, those after a substantial breakfast will need to jump in the car and find a cafe or diner. Car parking is free as well, and there are plenty of spaces available. They are very clear about no-smoking in the rooms ($100 fine), yet they are happy for guests to smoke in the courtyard area, except for cigars, which we were told off for smoking. Go figure. Overall, this small but well maintained motel is a great place to stay if you are not too fussed about not having the little luxuries - ie, they only provide soap and no shampoo or conditioner, although they do offer these items for a nominal fee at the front desk. I would stay here again if I came to San Diego, but there are a couple of budget chain motels next door as options if the Dolphin is not for you.

“Doesn't disappoint” I have stayed here 6 times in the last couple of years - three times in the last 4 months. I always request early check-in and the room is always available when I arrive. Check-in is smooth although this time I had some difficulty understanding the accent of the clerk. I have always been welcomed back. Rooms are a nice size for NYC. I really like the desk and chair in the Garden Inns - very comfortable work area with free wireless. Ask for a high floor to get away from street noise. Breakfast is always nice - fresh food well prepared. There always appears to be a doorman on duty who never fails to welcome me back - small thing but an indication of a property committed to customer service. On this visit, I managed to leave an item behind. I called the next day. Housekeeping located the item, called me back, and arranged to have it sent to me. Following day the item arrived. Again, it is this attention to detail and customer service that keeps me coming back.

“I Would Go Back Anytime” This used to be a W, and I am not sure there has been many updates since, but nonetheless, I like it! I love the location, just a few blocks from Grand Central, and the staff are consistently nice, accommodating, and friendly. The rooms are typically larger than most NYC rooms and once in a while you get an upgrade to a mini-suite. The furniture is sort of dated, but i can overlook all that as the price can be good! On this last visit, my colleague checked in after me and he was given an upgrade to the executive suite, which was massive! Overall great location, staff, and value!

“Great but try not to get a connecting room!” The Palomar is a fantastic hotel, great atmosphere whenever you come into the reception, fabulous free drinks hour as at all other Kimpton hotels, lovely robes, socks and free umbrella (handy when we were there as it was horrible weather!). Location is good for the metro and for Dupont Circle/Georgetown but the main part of Washington is a metro trip or a 20-30 minute walk away so if you like being on top of things it's not that good for that. Rooms are fabulously large but unfortunately we were in a connecting room and our neighbour decided to get up at 6am and talk very very loudly with no concept of the time or that other people may want to sleep. We were also in a room at the front of the hotel so got noise from the road. If you are a particularly light sleeper I would recommend asking for a room at the back of the hotel and not a connecting room! I'd go back.

“Great Memorial Weekend stay” We had 4 teenagers and 2 rooms. Excellent stay. We requested 2 rooms next to each other. Arrived at 11am Saturday of Memorial Day weekend. One room was available and they said they would get our other room as close as possible. We ended up with the room next door which was great. Not so great pull out beds but you don't expect they would be that great. Excellent location to Navy Pier and the Watertower and Michigan Ave. shopping. Would stay again when we visit again.

“Great for group travel” We stayed here with our girl scout troop and enjoyed the great service. The front desk was quick at checking us in. The best was location, location, location! Close to fisherman's wharf, Pier 39, Ghiradelli, and the cable car turnaround. The muni stop was located at corner of hotel and the F-train stop was one block up, perfect for our needs. The hotel was recently renovated and it still had the new smell. Rooms were nicely furnished, we had a coffee maker & refrigerator. The girls enjoyed the pool which is heated and the fire pit area was cozy & inviting. This is a great hotel for a group to explore the area.

“Excellent Customer Service and Great Location” I spend a great deal of time in Chicago, and I've stayed at numerous hotels. What the Hilton Garden Inn lacks in glamour, it makes up for in terms of cleaniness, customer service, and location. I checked in hours early, but a room was ready for me -- and the clerk said, "I've given you a great city view," which she did (perfect night time view of the Hancock Tower). The room was spotless, and everything worked in the bathroom -- no slow drains or noisy fans. Room service was prompt -- not only in delivery, but in picking up the tray. The next morning, when I called to check out, the clerk asked me if I needed a taxi and had one waiting for me the minute I entered the lobby. The location is right near every possible amenity -- including a block from a Trader Joe's -- the room has a microwave and small fridge, so I could have easily bought something from TJs and had it in my room. I've spent much more to stay in supposedly 5 star hotels that were less well-managed and provided much less value. I truly enjoyed my stay.
“Fantastic!!” Absolutely huge hotel, big comfortable rooms and great location. The pool was great.

“Tremendous Hotel” I had the pleasure of spending 5 weeks at the Residence Inn Alamo Plaza in January and February. At that time the hotel was going through a complete remodel so there were a few disruptions but all in all the hotel is tremendous and the remodel a great change. I have stayed in the old rooms as well as the new and I must say that transformation was amazing. The staff at this hotel fom the top down is top notch and probably the friendliest staff at any Marriott property in which I have ever stayed. In terms of proximity to the highway system and getting around San Antonio the location cannot be beat. Additionally, for enjoying the Riverwalk, Alamo and downtown San Antonio this location is incredible. To look at your room and stare down at the Alamo is an awe inspiring experience. This is the perfect hotel to enjoy the Alamo City and all the San Antonio has to offer. I would not hesitate to ever recommend this hotel.

“Fun, funky, probably overpriced” When I visited, the hotel had been open just over a year, but was still experiencing some teething problems. There was no working A/C in our room, which was hot and stifling most of the time, and the staff advice was to 'crack a window' ... in March. Hot water usually took over 5 minutes to come through, morning or evening. Sound carries in this hotel - people talking and laughing in the corridor at stupid o'clock (and there were a number of them) disturbed us a few times, and while using one of the public computers in a corridor, I could hear every word of a conversation that was taking place in the adjacent room. On the plus side, it has fun, hip decor - many of the rooms have guitars in them (the theme throughout is rock'n'roll), and the minibar/fridge was housed in a black and silver gear case. The dark windowless lobby is full of trendy people hiding out with their laptops and lattes. Our room was very spacious by city standards, though my friend had a single room which was far smaller. The bed was the most comfortable I've ever encountered in a hotel. The staff were courteous and helpful. The location was great - a short walk from Macy's, and close to 2 subway stations. There were some great delis and cafes nearby which we used instead of the hotel's restaurant and coffee shop. I was lucky enough to get a special rate for my stay, which was good as I certainly don't think it was worth the full price!

“VERY surprised (and gratefully so)” I was not sure what to expect here because I had this hotel booked for me, and I almost exclusively stay at a Marriott property when traveling. Having said that, I was REALLY surprised with what I walked into here when I opened the door to my room. HUGE...that is the best way to describe it. Very much like what you would expect at a Homewood Suites (Hilton). The furnishings were very warm and welcoming (not like the military-issue stuff that you get at Residence Inn, and the kitchen looked more like a small apartment kitchen than a hotel kitchen. The bed...OMG...the BED! I_DO_NOT normally sleep well in hotels. This one...best sleep ever, without question. I really can't say that enough. In fact, let me say it again...BEST_SLEEP_EVER in a hotel. As far as the surrounding area, make darn sure you have a car. There really isn't any place close to get the things you might want without a car (unless you don't mind playing "Frogger" while crossing the highway.) The "BridgeMart" is lacking in some things I might want to have on hand, but all in all, it isn't bad. Breakfast...not fancy by any stretch of the imagination, but it is food, and the staff is very helpful and friendly. If you need a place to stay near the airport, I would highly recommend this property to you.

“Great Place to Stay” This was a very nice Hotel. I do not understand the few bad reviews. Hotel was clean and a nice location. Love the Adult shower for two :). We had a room on the 5th floor and the view was great of the city. Rooms were nice size. I would stay here once again without a doubt.

“Nice Staff & Location” Stayed for 2 nights in September. Friendly check-in and efficient valet parking. This is a stylish property that is clearly well maintained. The room had no wow factor and the bathroom was rather disappointing. The air conditioning was ineffective and the room much too hot during the night. Noise was not an issue.

“Very nice, restful spot” Stayed here for four days for a business trip. Like many CA buildings, the hotel is laid out with some outdoor walkways between buildings that house the guest rooms. The room was spacious and well appointed. The pool area is beautiful and a relaxing hangout in the evening. The exercise room was small - just four machines in a small room. Location was fine - just a few minutes' walk to bus stop or trolley stop and you can get most everywhere in the city. Breakfast buffet was included in the room cost, but the selection was limited and the same every day. All in all, though, for a mid range hotel, this was quite nice.

“Love the Renaissance” The Renaissance has changed its image from a standard hotel to what they now call an "urban sanctuary" -- and this label could not be more true. The renovations they have made include a fantastic and comprehensive fitness center, stretch room, and pool area. Additionally, their restaurant and lounge are excellent and the rooms are designed with everything that a guest seeking a "sanctuary" would desire. The best part of this hotel, however, remains the staff and the service. Everyone at the Renaissance goes above and beyond and truly has the enjoyment of the guest as the top priority. The only downsides to the Renaissance are that it is difficult to get a cup of coffee before 6 am and they have started spraying this very pungent scent throughout the lobby that caused some problems with my fiancee, who is very sensitive to various odors. Above all, however, the Renaissance is a fantastic hotel that I would recommend wholeheartedly.

“GREAT LOCATION” This is a very nice hotel in a great part of Chicago. I was here for business and stayed for the weekend with my husband. The hotel is so close to everything and anything. Would stay again.

“Nice and comfortable!” It is off season and the room was very fairly priced. The grounds are nice, the pool looked nice. We were there to visit a family member. The rooms at all the COurtyards are the same in my travels. SO you get what you expect. HDTV, Nice bed, Desk, clean room. Above average and perfectly fine. The hotel is near a nice shopping center that offers everything from Hair Salons, Dining, Markets-- very convenient.

“Decent stay in the Loop.” The hotel is a bit on the shabby side for a Renaissance property--it is an older site and the lobby is dark and on the small side. However, the rooms are quiet and larger than expected, the beds comfortable, and the staff was outgoing and sharp--I give it an extra star for solid concierge and housekeeping during the day. In short, what you expect from staff at Renaissance locations will be found here. The location can't be beat as the hotel is across the street from Grant Park and within a ten to fifteen minute walk from Millennium Park, the Art Institute, and the Museum Campus if you are traveling with the kids. It's also a quick cab ride to the Magnificent Mile and the River. Don't rule it out as an alternative if you are spending two or three days in Chicago.

“Convenient & Classy” Although it may no longer be the hippest place in town, the Palomar is still a good choice for travelers headed San Francisco for business or pleasure. It's convenient to either the convention center or Union Square and its environs. This hotel is a nice alternative to the nearby behmouths like the Marriott, Hilton, Westin and others. With its miniature lobby, it takes only a few steps from entering to the elevators. The rooms are mostly compact affairs but have all the comforts and amenities you expect from Kimpton. Bathrooms, however, are exceptionally small and can be somewhat challenging to navigate. There's morning coffee service on the 5th floor (why not throw in some nice baked goods and juices and call it a Continental Breakfast?) Service is fine. Although you can certainly pay less for a hotel room in San Francisco, you probably will not get the luxury touches and comfort that the Palomar offers.

“Always good value – But what’s up with calling this a B&B/Inn” No matter where I travel, the Hilton Garden Inns are reasonably priced and always exceed my expectations. This hotel is conveniently located on I-35, but it can be tricky pulling off the feeder (going downhill) into the hotel parking lot. I appreciate the fact that there is bar in the lobby that is open until 10pm. The room was clean, the glass enclosed shower was large and there was plenty of counter space. I did have a problem with the temperature control in the room – but other than that, it was a very nice stay.

“Clean, Stylish and Well-Located Gem” The Charlemark is an excellent choice for anyone looking to stay in a fantastic, centrally-located spot in Boston without breaking the bank. I just returned from a 2-night visit there -- my first and only time staying here. I would return in a heartbeat, and will be thoroughly disappointed if it is not available for my next visit. The room itself was on the small side, but they made the most out of the space with an oversized mirror and shelves. There was a large flat screen tv with DirecTV, a stereo and a DVD player. The room was clean and my window happened to look out onto Boylston so I had a fantastic view of the public library and the entire Copley Square area. The staff was extremely polite and helpful. They made us feel welcome and helped answer all our questions, going out of their way to do so. The location can't be beat. The hotel sits directly across from the public library and the Copley T station. It's in the heart of back bay, with Newbury, Boston Common, Fanuiel Hall, Downtown Crossing, Chinatown all within walking distance. With the green line T stop right out your door, you can get to any other part of the city (Boston College, Harvard, the airport) with ease. I would recommend this hotel to anyone who likes boutique hotels -- this is not a roomy, luxurious chain-hotel room. It's modern, minimalist, and stylish, with small rooms and a funky feel to it. There is a lobby bar which spills out onto the street....you can dine and drink outside on Boylston. There is also inside lounge with a projector tv and two computers for hotel guests (with a printer as well). The continental breakfast consists of Dunkin Donut bagels and muffins, juice and coffee. I really enjoyed my stay here, as a 30-year old married woman visting with girlfriends. If you're looking for a quiet roomy place away from the hub-bub of the city, it may not be the place for you. At night, I had no trouble sleeping as the bar downstairs and outside traffic did not seep into the room at all, even with a window facing the street.

“Close to shops and mountains!” I enjoyed my stay here as it is close to the mall, restaurants, movies and shops. Staff was friendly and the host (Don) in the restaurant was very welcoming. Their signature breakfast was excellent. Try the OJ. Very good.

“Enjoyed Our Stay” My husband and I spent four nights at this hotel in May 2012. We had a great experience - the staff was friendly, the hotel was convenient to the subway, our room was spacious and clean, the bed was super comfortable and it was very interesting to be so close to the WTC site. Having said that, I would not pay full price to stay here in the future. We got a great deal through Hotwire and definitely have no complaints for the price we paid however, we would have been disappointed had we paid full price. There were some very obvious construction errors/sloppiness, our bedside light was burnt out, the towel rack in the bathroom was coming off the wall and the very white walls are showing a lot of wear and tear even though the hotel is only a couple of years old. I don't want to sound like I'm full of complaints, because we really did have a great stay however the quality of the room unfortunately doesn't match up with other hotels of similar star rating/price.

“Perfect hotel for us” We are a family of three. Two retirees and our 25 year old son who was joining us for a wedding the following week on Martha's Vineyard. We wanted a hotel centrally located that was easy to get to by cab from the airport, to our rental car pick-up the next morning and one that could accommodate all three of us with some privacy. We also wanted to be in an area with restaurants with in walking distance. Hotel Commonwealth worked well in all categories. They also accomodated us with a small mini fridge that they brought up when requested. As with other reviewers, I don't know why they don't have a coffee and tea maker in the room. There is a Dunkin doughnuts near by, and room service, but I still like it in my room without having to order the night before and deal with a knock on the door while in pj's or having to get dressed to go downstairs. The rooms and bathrooms were lovely. Good bathroom ammenities. A newspaper of your choice delivered to your door in th AM. Wonderful door staff. I will say, that they solicited a review on TripAdvisor. No judgement here, just information.

“Great Location, Modern Room, and Excellent Concierge” Check-In was not impressive. What should have taken 5 minutes, turned into 20 because of the lack of training. I'd requested a quiet room, instead got the room outside of the loudest ice maker on earth. Called downstairs and was moved in under 10 minutes. The hotel room was nice, love the ability to hook up my laptop to the flat screen. The concierge had top shelf beverages and the food was excellent. I hope to stay here again on my next trip to NYC

“it's all good....” Chic, modern and comfortable. Good words for a hotel room in NYC. We had a corner room just below the top floor. We were told the mechanics of the building are up there and it might be noisy. Our corner faced MSG and Macy's. But we also had an unobstructed view of the Empire State Building. Our room was spacious with a micro/fridge. Sometimes with a new hotel, the kinks need to be worked out, but we experienced nothing to complain about. Ice machines are located on every other floor. This really is in a great location. Also, steps down from the hotel is another new Hilton property, A Hampton Inn. Just steps away from that is a hotel called Hotel Metro (Hotel Metro has stood the test of time--stop in to look at the lobby..you'll love it!) Parking was about $36/night, and the garage is directly across from the hotel.

“Solid option if traveling in/out of BWI” Stayed here one night after arriving in late on a flight into Baltimore. Had an early morning meeting to attend so was really only at the hotel about eight or nine hours. Besides the hallway corridors being abnormally warm, I have no real complaints. Shuttle was kind of slow coming to the airport, but I gathered there was some construction and it was after midnight, after all. The room was pretty standard if you've ever stayed at Sleep Inn before. Bed was comfy, it had a nice walk-in shower, the area seemed both safe and quiet, but everything else about it was pretty basic. Continental breakfast in the morning was okay, nothing too special. I wouldn't go out of my way to return here but it's a perfectly decent 2 1/2 star airport hotel.

“fine” I've been ther with my wife and my little boy (5 years old) for a one night stay in april 2007. It was fine.Very well located, prise as reasonnable as possible in this area, room very clean, and nice, bathroom as nice as the room. Service is fine. The breakfast restaurant is beautiful, but may be the break ast is too expensive, that's my only bad observation. A good address, definitly

“Great hotel, terrific location” The Mayflower Hotel is a lovely property in a great location in downtown Seattle. The service was great, especially at the concierge desk, which was extremely helpful. I was especially impressed with the subtle but appropriate concern for security that I noted at the front desk. The only small problem we encountered once or twice was in getting a taxi, which the doorman has to hail because there is no space on the street for taxis to wait in. There are LOTS of great restaurants, shopping, and even movies within walking distance, and the monorail station is just a block away. For relaxation, the chocolate martinis in the lobby bar (Oliver's) come highly recommended! The building is old, built in 1927, and truly has "classical elegance" and lots of personality. The rooms are lovely, but the bathrooms are old style, with only a minimum of shelf space for cosmetics and toiletries.

“Nice Hotel and Great Location” We stayed here for 1 night to go to a Red Sox game. We then moved down closer and stayed at the Doubletree. This is a nice clean hotel and had no issues whatsoever. A little pricey and you get a convention charge (tax). I would recommend especially if going to a ball game.

“Very comfortable stay” I was recently in San Antonio for a conference and spent 4 nights at the Mariott Rivercenter. It was a very comfortable stay. The room was nice sized with a view of the Riverwalk. The room was clean, with very comfortable bedding and a good shower. We had a daily newspaper delivered, and had the ability to do hot tea and coffee in the room. The convenience of this hotel's location couldn't be beat. Every night we went out on the Riverwalk for dinner and people-watching, and two of my colleagues walked along the Riverwalk each morning for exercise before conference meetings started. There was an abundance of restaurants and shopping close to us without needing transportation. I also found the staff to be helpful and quick to respond to any request. One day we requested extra towels, and we had them within 30 minutes, with a follow-up call later from the front desk to see if we had gotten them. The business center was also helpful in making copies of things we needed during the conference, and there was no charge for it. On the downside, there was a charge for internet service, which is aggravating when you are paying the higher rate for a nice hotel. With all the taxes, our room was about $190 a night, and the internet was an extra $10 a day. I realize that's common in most upscale hotels, but it still makes me cranky to pay for internet services, when it's often free in lower-cost hotels. Parking was also $19 a day, but we felt it was worth it to have the security of the underground garage parking and the convenience of our vehicle in the same building. Overall, it was a very pleasant stay for a business meeting, and we were able to combine pleasure with business due to the location of this hotel. If we ever come to San Antonio again, we would want to stay at the Mariott Rivercenter again.

“Excellent location, comfortable rooms” Thank you for a wonderful stay. Unfortunately, I was there for only 2 nights, wished I could have stayed longer!!! The location of the hotel is wonderful, just steps away from Union Square and quite close to different interesting areas. Being on a business trip the only thing that did not work for me was having to pay for the WI FI which most of the hotels these days include as part of their services, but other than that, it is definitely a hotel I would come back to...

“We loved it and will be back for another staycation!” We truly enjoyed our experience at this hotel. The entire holiday weekend was so relaxing, calm and the staff was a huge part of that. From the front desk, the bell desk, the in house driver Melkon, concierge to the room service and pool staff, we encountered nothing but friendly, helpful service. The hotel is really well done and peaceful. The new pool was amazing since it has a non-slip bottom and an infinity pool type feel. We were there attending a wedding but made a little staycation out of it. Our corner room was wonderful and plan on requesting it again next time. The bathroom needs a bit of updating but it was a nice size with a separate tub. Floor to ceiling windows and a balcony. WOW. Also, the room service food was so yummy! We stayed at another hotel for the last leg of our trip as it was closer to another event and let me tell you the room service was so yucky after having the food at the intercontinental hotel. The only negative thing and what I would make a note of is the "Valet Only: policy and the $36 per day/overnight parking rate. I know its the area and all but that is just an exorbitant amount of money. We dropped off our luggage, parked about 10 minutes away and never went to the car again. The hotel car take you anywhere at about 1.5 mile radius around. Anything farther will require a cab. Minus this, our stay was perfect and I don’t say that easily.

“A very good hotel” I stayed at the Marriott Marquis six days while attending a convention at the Moscone Convention Center just across the street. The location was excellent. Check in and checkout were fast and easy. The room was spacious, comfortable, and had all the necessary and optional amenities. Valet service was a little pricey, but was fast and reliable. As a minor note, I would note that the concierge lounge was a little cramped for the volume of guests that used it at breakfast time. Other than that, my only other complaint is more directed at the city than at the hotel itself in the sense that it was not easy to catch a taxi cab when you needed one, whether you did it at the hotel entrance or at a street corner.

“Good” This used to be called the Miyako, now it is Hotel Kabuki. We booked a 4 night winter special for $101/night, which was less than most full-service hotels in central S.F. Our room was really big in my opinion, plenty of room to walk around and store our stuff for 2 people. There was 1 queen bed, 2 bathrobes, free wifi, a sitting area, chaise lounge, coffee table, a desk, a mini fridge/bar, snacks and a balcony on 2 sides. Even with all this furniture, there still was plenty of room for us to stretch out. The bathroom set up was a little odd. There was the main sink room, the toilet room to the left, and a shower and tub room to the right. There were 2 shower heads, one in the tub and then one that was just in the shower room. The toilets are low flow, and sometimes took a few flushes to make it work. The house keeping staff kept our room very clean. The room itself is starting to age. The sliding glass doors on the two balcony access points were a bit sticky and old. The Japanese window shades were a little worn. The room paint was a little worn. Over all, I feel like the room was a good value for S.F. and being centrally located in the city. We forgot some toiletries, and the hotel front desk was very attentive and had them sent to our room right away. We needed instruction on how to use the in-room alarm and iPod Docking station, and they sent staff right away to help us. I think the people next door had a baby or small child, as I briefly heard a crying child in the hallway before I heard the next room door close. Once the family was in their room, I could not hear the baby anymore. The hotel is in the heart of Japantown. There is a nice breakfast in the restaurant I think it is about $16 buffet. The breakfast buffet staff was attentive, and kept coming with coffee for us. The bacon, fruit, yogurt and oatmeal were very good quality. There are coffee and a breakfast kiosks in the Japantown mall next door to the hotel. The hotel restaurant later in the evening becomes a bar. The bar personnel was great! We got a couple bottles of wine from Sonoma, and they gave us glasses and wine opening for a tip. The lobby has some nice sitting areas, and the lobby has free wifi. Parking when I was there, I believe valet parking is $39 per day with in and out privileges at no extra cost. There is a public parking garage access around the corner with a elevator into the hotel. The public parking is by the hour up to $16/day, but there is no in-out privileges, so you get a new ticket every time you enter. There is limited street parking nearby, and the residential neighborhood has permit street parking, so the best bet is to valet or public garage a car if you have a car. For convenience, there is a Safeway grocery store about a 2 1/2 block walk from the hotel, and there are Japantown mall groceries as well.

“Another short but great stay!” This was our second one-night Priceline stay over 10 years, but I have to say for such a short stay, a few things immediately stood out positively. Having used Priceline for many of my hotel stays over the years, I've noticed there is often some negative discrimination for Priceline guests whereby you don't get the same level of service from regular customers. I think they figure you're just a cheapskate who is not brand loyal and thus should not be given any benefit of the doubt or bother with the hotel's usual above-and-beyond level of customer service. Our main desk greeting at check-in was exceptional however. Marlot was very welcoming, courteous and fast, and offered my wife and I their evening welcome glass of champagne on arrival. As we were travelling with our two kids this time around, she accommodated our request to change from a single Queen to two doubles. The second floor double double room was very large (at least 50% larger than a standard hotel room) with plenty of towels and toiletries. Beds were comfortable and the location was quiet. We another great stay at the Mayflower Renaissance!

“Good Place to Stay in Manhattan” In my experience, this is the best place to stay in Midtown Manhattan. The room was clean and very comfortable. The location is one block off of the lights of Times Square and within walking distance of all of the shows and tourist attractions. The rooms at this hotel are much nicer than many of the other chain hotels in the area. (No, I don't work for this hotel or receive any compensation - it's just the plain truth.) Over the years, I've stayed at the Marriott East Side and Marquis, Doubletree Times Square, the Radisson on Lex and The Grand Hyatt - to name some. This Westin beats 'em all. On the other side of the coin, this hotel is pricey and the NYC hotel taxes that you'll pay are simply ridiculous. Yes, it's New York but still be sure to bring your checkbook.

“Still the perfect hotel address in D.C.” We've stayed at the JW Marriott three times over the course of 25 years and it has always been perfect. The rooms were clean, the beds comfortable, the amenities excellent. We stayed with our adult children on what might be our last family "unit" vacation for awhile (both are moving away for higher education) and all of us were very pleased with the comfort, price level, location, helpfulness of the staff and the overall experience of visiting our nation's capitol.

“Well recommended” RECOMMENDED. Just off Times Square, subway station 1 block, this hotel recently renovated. Check-in staff friendly and efficient. Troubled by being assigned 1st room as you left elevator and next to ice machine BUT room was quiet. Facing street, some but limited street noise (I was on 11th floor). Room is large by any standard. Elegant furniture, large LCD display. Bathroom was well appointed & illuminated. High level of standard. The BEST though was the bedding - this is bar none the best mattress I have ever slept on in all my travels, in fact I ordered one from the company today. Overall, best hotel I've found in NYC todate.

“Great El Paso hotel” Great hotel if in town for business; great lounge, excellent menu, outstanding service all around from entire staff. Super workout facilities. My first choice for accomandations when in El Paso for business. Clean, recently remodeled -- an overall great hotel for the professional travel. Quiet, distinctive, no kids running around lobby n bar!

“Beautiful property in Downtown Dallas” My family traveled to Dallas to attend the State Fair and wanted to stay in the downtown area. We do subscribe to the Omni loyalty program and have stayed at a number of Omni hotels in the past. This was a beautiful hotel inside and out. The lobby is very contemporary and had a fireplace wall that was very pretty and useful since there was a cold snap during our visit. We had a king room which was not huge, but the perfect size for us. We loved the artwork in the room highlighting Dallas landmarks. The TV in the bathroom mirror was a surprise and allowed us to keep up with football games even while getting ready. The staff were extremely nice, especially the concierge that helped us with Dart Rail maps and directions on how to take the rail to the fair. We were not there for a convention, but the hotel is attached to the convention center which seems like it would be great if you were there for that purpose. It is only 3 blocks to the red line Dart Rail at Union Station and only a little further to get on the green line and others at the West End Station. We were walking distance to the JFK landmarks and West End. We will definitely stay here again.

“Stylish New Kid on the Block.” The new Ritz-Carlton in Denver combines good service with a nice modern décor. Right from the start, the front desk staff was very friendly and welcoming. The attractive lobby of the hotel is pretty small with few areas for sitting. This helped create a nice quiet atmosphere and always made us feel that we were staying at a small boutique hotel that was not overrun by groups. Our room was very nice and seemed a little larger then most standard five star rooms. Features included an iPod docking station, flat screen TV, good lighting, and nice artwork, in addition to comfortable furniture and bedding. The bathroom was also large with white marble, two sinks, a big tub, very nice separate shower, and separate water closet. Our only complaint about the room was that the windows are tinted black and do not allow much sunlight to get in. If you like to workout then this is the hotel for you. A very large separately run gym with very good hours is connected to the hotel and available complimentary to hotel guests. In addition to workout and exercise class rooms, this gym has a basketball court, as well as a large indoor lap pool in the basement. The gym is not on par with the atmosphere at the Ritz, but it is still a very nice place. We did not use the spa that is a part of the hotel. It looks nice but currently costs $35 dollars to use if you are not getting a treatment. We had breakfast twice at the stylish Elways. The food was good, as was the service. The location of the hotel is on the fringe of downtown. It is a little quiet at night, but it only takes walking a couple of blocks to find some restaurants and night life. The Ritz seems to be a great new addition to downtown Denver and a stay here should be an enjoyable one for most visitors.

“nice hotel for jacksonville” We had a pleasant stay at the Omni, me and four friends went up for a football game. The staff was awesome, the rooms were spacious, comfortable, and clean, they be a little bit dated, but we didn't mind. The location is central, even though there's almost nothing to do in the city.

“lovely grand hotel in downtown Dallas” We loved stayiing at the Adolphus (one night only, while we went to the State Fair). The AAA rate was very reasonable, on a Friday night. Our room was elegant, very clean, and spacious. A comfortable king bed made for a good night's sleep after a long day at the Fair and dinner in the West End (walking distance from the hotel). The character and ambience of an historical hotel such as this tops the "chain" hotels any time. Look for the bellman with the "Elvis" haircut and great Southern charm. "Thank ya very much" for an overall charming stay at the Adolphus.

“Amazing staff, lovely wedding venue” One of my dearest friends just got married at the Four Seasons, and I stayed with him the night before the wedding at the Four Seasons. We had a lovely suite with an amazing view of the city. believe it was the hotel's first gay wedding so they took photos and video to feature the wedding in their newsletter and online. We were treating like royalty. And my friend had an elaborate and wild costume for the wedding and nobody looked at him funny or judged. The staff was so kind and attentive and just wanted to help on the special day. The food for the wedding was incredible. Everything cooked perfectly. We had a lovely lobster appetizer, and the lava cake for dessert was pure heaven. This hotel is really lovely. When you enter, you ascend these stairs up to the front desk. Very dramatic and striking. The room service was wonderful. We ordered breakfast before the wedding. As with any room service, it's pricey, but here I felt like it was worth every penny. Top quality, fresh, produce. I really enjoyed my night at the Four Seasons, and the wedding that followed.

“Loved this place!” My husband, 2 preteen sons, my husbands parents, brother-in-law, and his girlfriend all stayed here post Alaskan cruise for 4 nights starting June 25. We arrived very early and were impressed from the start. Everyone we came into contact with was extemely nice and welcoming. I did not expect any rooms to be ready (10 am), but wanted to check our bags. One of our 3 rooms (2 Queen beds) was ready, so we had all of our bags sent to this room so we could freshen up. Our 2 Queen room was much larger than I had expected and was also able to fit a rollaway bed, which they happily provided. This alone made our stay better since our boys would be less likely to fight over pillows, the spot next to the table, etc. Our window faced a side street but had a beautiful view of the water to the left. There was a table and 2 chairs in front of the window where I liked to sit with my laptop and look out over the water. We had a fridge/ minibar, microwave, and large closet with many shelves. The bathroom was beautiful, clean and huge. I liked the bath products very much. The hairdryer left a lot to be desired for my long hair. I have yet to find a decent one in a hotel, so I always bring my own. We dropped our bags and went off to checkout the rest of the hotel and Public Market. I have to say that even if the hotel hadn't been as nice as it was, I still would have paid what I did (250 King city view and 320 2 Queen ) for the rooftop deck and proximity to Public Market. The deck is large with several tables with chairs, a few lounge chairs and an outdoor living room set. It looks directly over the market and the water. I went up every morning with my coffee and whatever treat I picked up at the Market. We also spent each evening up there reviewing our day's adventures over a bottle of wine. It was perfect. The location of the hotel cannot be beat if you truly want to be in the heart of it all. It is actually a part of the Market, so you walk out the door of the hotel, through its little courtyard (which I love) and you are there. It was wonderful to be able to wander at my leisure during the off hours than suffer the rat race that the Market can become in the middle of the day. If you haven't been to Seattle, it is filled with steep hills. Even though we were in a great location, my husband's parents usually called a cab to go anywhere beyond the Market. The rest of us easily walked to our destintation or to the bus tunnel or monorail. We did walk to Safeco Field as well (about a mile), but opted to take a cab back since going back was all uphill and we were tired. The hotel staff, as expected, were very helpful with checkout. The loaned us a scale for our luggage (airline fees :( ) They also helped us to arrange a van to the airport. I was very sad to leave this hotel and hope I have the opportunity to return.

“pretty awesome” got an incredibly great deal on priceline last minute. was happy i got this hotel as i wanted to try it out. the lobby looks great in photos and even better in person. did not expect it to be as high as it actually is. might be the best lighting ive seen in a hotel. asked for double beds as was traveling with the sister, and they did give me stress over it, even if the two double room is a room category up as i saw in their website. the room itself is sparse and clean. all in all it was incredibly soothing. beds were comfortable. the bathroom worked. there was a large walk in closet. valet and concierge were helpful and accommodating. we had some fax issues and the front desk staff were very cool about it which i again appreciate. the location is a bit father north end of the busy area. the area is mainly fancy residential, but transportation is close by, and there are a lot of bars just a couple of blocks down. would definitely want to stay here again.

“Beautiful hotel with luxurious rooms” I stayed at this hotel for two nights in April 2011 for business. I was very pleased with this stay: check-in was seamless, and the front desk nicely upgraded me to a top-floor room with beautiful city views. I absolutely loved the spacious room: the king-sized bed was plush and extremely comfortable (providing great sleep), the furnishings were sleek and modern, and the large bathroom had luxurious Molton Brown toiletries, separate shower and bath, and a very modern sink. The sheer size/space of the bathroom and toiletries made it a pleasure getting ready in the morning and at night! The hotel staff were extremely friendly and helpful. I will be staying at this hotel again in July, and I wouldn't hesitate to recommend this hotel whether for business or for pleasure.

“Would stay here again” We stayed at this hotel on a business trip in Feb. 2012. The hotel is clean, in a great location, and has great water pressure. Room layout is convenient. Beds are reasonably comfortable. Best thing about staying here is the hot cookie you receive upon check-in. (They're really good cookies!) We'd definitely stay here again.

“Excellent service, great beds, free Internet, loved it” We stayed here for a conference and i have to say i was very surprised. Based pn the low price of the room I was not expecting the hotel to be very nice. To my surprise i could not have been more wrong. First, the hotel is "service inclusive" which means that nobody who works here will even accept a gratuity, and we tried real hard to tip the bartender and he refused (twice). And with this being said i would have thought that the service would be sub-par but it definitely was not. Everyone who works at this hotel understand the meaning of the word customer service. The rooms were very clean and the beds are very comfortable. Flat panel tv's and free wifi throughout the hotel is also a very nice change from many of the hotels we have stayed at. There are good restaurants and nitelife within a very short walk, and just a 10 min taxi ride to the airport. I highly reccomend this hotel. Joseph Sloboda

“Very comfortable and so convenient” The best feature was being literally across the street from Minute Maid Park. We were in town to see the Dodgers play the Astros for a weekend series, and this hotel was ideal for this purpose. Room was big and comfortable. The room service breakfast was quite good and not terribly overpriced. Only downside, and this is relatively minor, is that there was no "sleep" button on the remote control.

“Resort feel near the capitol!!!” What a great stay at the Liaison Capitol Hill!!!! My wife and I had a great long weekend here. The pool on the roof is the best! Just the right size and a "chill" feel. Love the bar right next to it!! Room was great. All staff always made you feel welcome.Will be back soon!!!

“comfortable” We just returned from a business trip to the hyatt this past weekend.Our room was very comfortable and very spacious.The food in the italian restaurant was very good as we went with the nightly special. The food at the revolving restaurant was excellent as was the service,although it was a little on the expensive side.The views are spectacular.The only thing that the hotel could improve on was seating in the main lobby--there is a couple of chairs and a couch and alot of empty space.

“Second time and still excellent” It has been five years since we were in Chicago. We stayed here before and we loved it so much last time we came back to the same place. I love the location and quality of this hotel. I will not hesitate to stay here again. It is in an excellent location, well maintained, good views, good sized room, good sized bathroom, comfortable, lots of restaurants nearby, theater, the loop, etc. A useful tip: it is an easy 5 minute walk from the blue line so don't take cab form the airport. For $2 per person, hop the subway to Clark/Lake. It's about 45 minutes and and $45 cheaper than a cab. I only gave it a "Very Good" last time. It is still consistently good in every way so I'm bumping it to Excellent.

“Great for business or a vacation” I stayed for almost a week at the Courtyard Marriott while in town on business and had a fairly spacious (for New York) room with two queen beds, looking out on Ninety-second Street. I needed to work while at the hotel and there was a reliable and fast Internet connection for my laptop. The bathroom was clean and pleasant, with a granite sink and mirrors galore. I had a moment of panic thinking there was no hair dryer, but it was hidden behind some towels. There were plenty of clean towels supplied daily, for once more than I needed. Beds were comfortable, and you are able to set your own temperature in the room, a definite plus. Really, the room was so up to date and functional you wouldn't believe you were in a New York hotel room. Free copies of the newspaper downstairs and a well-decorated lobby. The staff was fast, polite and efficient; I never had to wait at the front desk. Step out onto First Avenue and you'll find all kinds of restaurants. Down side? It is a hike to the subway, about 15 minutes on foot, and it can take awhile to hail a cab even on nearby First Avenue. There was no refrigerator in the room though it looked like there used to be, and for long stays you really, really want a refrigerator. The elevators tend to be slow and verrrrrrry crowded in the morning. Noise leaked through the windows from the street, and started early. All in all, though, I'd happily return, though I'd bring my comfortable shoes for walking to the subway.

“not as quirky as i thought it would be” We stayed here for 4 nights early last month, based solely on trip advisor reviews, i feel a little bit disgruntled. From the hotel website i thught our room was going to be really quirky but disappointingly it was just a bit old fashioned. Clean but old fashioned. We did have a seperate kitchen, bedroom and living room which was really handy when we put our son to sleep and then we could just chill out with a bottle of wine in the living room. The breakfast is nothing to write home about, and was a couple of pieces of fruit, some oj and some microwaved danish pastries ( never had hot danish before ) obviously brought straight out of the freezer and defrosted ?. Any way its a short walk to balboa park and the zoo about 5-10 mins. The staff were helpful but we didn't really see them much. The only main problem was that the tv didn't work throughout our stay, when we rang down they stated it was a problem with their cable service. i don't know if this was true or not. The pictures of the decking looks really nice but most of these flowers are plastic ?. All in all i can't really see why this is so high in trip advisors list.

“Great weekend rates” In this city of over-priced hotel rooms, the Hamilton Crowne Plaza is often a bargain (as it was for my recent stay). The service was great. They have a bathrobe in the room, free use of the nearby health club, the sleep amenity kit, and other stuff. Location is fairly handy. If your weekend travels take you to DC, be sure and consider this property.

“Refreshingly different.” I loved this hotel! I stayed for business and found the trendy decor and large plush rooms a pleasure to come back to after a long day. This is not your cookie cutter hotel . It offers cosy duvet's on the bed and W style decor but rooms that are double the size. High service touches included gourmet cookies provided with turndown and each morning providing an East Coast paper for this East Coast Resident (the New York Times). I was reluctant to stay at the hotel given some negative reviews but had no choice as other hotels were booked out. I'm so glad I stayed and shall definitely return.

“Hampton Inn Washington, DC: A superb property!” The Hampton Inn Washington, DC is simply a phenomenal hotel. Everything about it accounts for a memorable and pleasant stay. The hotel's location is decent. Union Station is a short walk away, and other locations can be conveniently reached. Chinatown is only a block away, providing varied and plentiful restaurants in arm's reach. The hotel's rooms are great! My room was the quietest in which I have stayed. The beds are superb, and the amenities and condiments are perfectly adequate. I particularly enjoyed my welcome card from Housekeeping, who kept my room spotless and homely. Although not the most luxurious, certainly the most notable room and stay I am yet to have. Every member of staff were simply incredible! Check in was quick, and very personable. The check in agent was very friendly, professional and above all, appeared human, having shared a laugh or two. Mayra, a staff member at breakfast, was extraordinarily polite, and ensured my table was kept clear. I was also farewelled and wished a pleasant day, which was a nice touch. Breakfast itself was perfectly adequate, and varied from cereals, toasts, pastries, coffee, juice, eggs, waffles, bacon, sausages, fruit and much more. It was varied each day also, which is very welcome if staying a few nights! The gym and pool are convenient and well maintained. I had no trouble finding an available treadmill, and the pool was never considerably busy during my stay. My one minor concern was the lift. You will find yourself waiting quite lengthy periods for a lift, particularly if the hotel is busy, and the hotel appears to be regularly filled with individuals staying for business, more so than the traveller or guest of leisure. Should you not wish to wait lengthy periods for a lift, I would suggest requesting a lower floor. I had no problem with the hotel. Overall, I have had one of my best stays here. I will certainly stay at Hampton Inn Washington, DC again, given the opportunity, particularly if I would like to ensure a remarkably pleasant stay.

“Fabulous Location-Some rooms are small” Having stayed here previously in a very small room, I was sure to ask for a larger room with 2 beds when I made the reservation although I was a solo traveler. I had room 1618 and it was very good. Their website/reservations are very clear about the square footage of each room - so pay attention when you book so you don't end up an unhappy traveler like other posters. Location: Excellent, excellent. In the middle of the Mag Mile. Can I say more? Rooms: No tub in mine - only a shower. Counter space was very limited - just a shelf below the mirror. Room had 2 flat screen Tvs, sofa, chair, coffee table and desk. Free internet. Mini bar, but no refrigerator or coffee maker that you can use in room. Full length mirror and in room safe. Lobby: Elevators are quite small, but there are 3 available. Check in on 2nd floor. One computer on 2nd floor you can use to print your boarding passes. Service: I had very limited contact with any staff - so I can't venture an opinion. Food: I was so close to dozens of restaurants that I did not eat at the hotel. I would definitely stay here again, BUT will surely ask for a big room again!

“Love This Hotel” I love the new look and feel of Springhill Suites. This hotel is modern, well equiped and centrally located. I could have played Hockey in my suite and I think the two bathroom concept in top notch. My room was well appointed and very comfortable and the lobby and lobby bar is extremely well done. If you have business in the downtown Columbus or OSU area, this hotel cannot be beat. I would stay here again with no hesitation.In fact, I am ready to book my next Columbus trip just to stay here again!

“New and clean, good value” The rooms are new and clean, and very small (as is the case with any NYC hotel). The decor is modern and comfortable. I chose to stay here because it was cheaper than any other mid-tier option I could find, and if it stays that way I'll continue to stay here when I visit New York because it's a great value. Also, the staff was super-friendly, enthusiastic, and helpful. A word about the location, as a former resident of NYC -- if you are familiar with downtown and/or the subway system, this hotel is good because it's easy walking distance to SoHo, Chinatown, and Tribeca, as well as many subway lines (the closest being the A-C-E). If you aren't familiar with the city, the location may feel a little bit like a no-man's land, especially at night. The immediate one-block radius goes dead quiet at night, and because of that and Holland Tunnel traffic, the cabs tend to avoid this area. But once you get familiar with the area, you realize you're really only a block or two from some of downtown's most bustling and fun neighborhoods.

“Great staff, location, and value” I would recommend this hotel. My family stayed for one night while passing through to LA, and it met our needs perfectly. Location is right downtown near convention center and ballpark. The young lady who checked us in was quite helpful and courteous. The room was clean. The public spaces were clean and well-decorated. Parking is free downtown from 8 p.m. to 8 a.m., and there are PLENTY of spaces available very close to hotel. We parked right outside the side door. This might be different if the baseball team is in town. The pool is kind of small, but not bad at all. Internet is NOT FREE. I find it hard to believe that anyone pays for internet. Hyatt should provide this as a free service. Overall, a great night.

“Nice Hotel/Good Location/Walk to Sites” Solid Sheraton Hotel in very good location downtown. Took just about 10 minutes to walk to teh white house... about the same if walked right down to the national mall... enough places to eat on K street close to hotel... some more high end nightlife a few blocks down on K but fore more serious bar hopping take a quick cab to Adams Morgan or Dupont... Parking $35 stinks, but downtown DC price is high pretty much everywhere... there is a public garage about a block down 12th which is another option, probably a bit less, but not sure.

“loved the room and hotel” we were there for a wedding and found this hotel clean, modern, well appointed and in a great area...try it! the tv and channel options were great, the balcony wonderful, the quiet option lovely...we would go back.

“Location, location, location!” Great location on Times Square (even though I would never stay right in Times Square again). Friendly staff, clean rooms, great room service and onsite restaurant. Absolutely no complaints

“New to Marriott so there is still updating but very good” No. 1, you cant beat the downtown location. The service was very good and the rooms were clean and comfortable. They do not yet have a concierge lounge which will be on the top floor when it is finished. That will be spectactular. (breakfast downstairs for Gold & Plat. Members) The Concierge gentleman downstairs is extremely nice and helpfull. Be sure to use him for local knowledge. The hotel sits in a mini-mall that has an ice skating rink (yes, that is correct) and a food court.. It is near the Pearl DART Station and only 4 stops to American Airlines Center.

“No doubts I will be back...” Before booking this hotel I had reserved other hotels in NYC and one day I saw good deal from quickbook. The price was the reason I chose hotel since I was having doubts on their design, location.... I cancelled earlier booked hotels and gave a try.After this stay, I know I will definately return to this hotel even if I have to pay more. People working at the hotel are so friendly, relaxed and laid back! Such a great welcome, no attitude or arrogancy as in many NYC's hotel of such level. They were always there to help us. The room is cute. Enough for two. Great bed and great bed linens from Frette. Huge flat tv, free internet. Bathroom is small but no problems with that. The only thing I did not like is old air condition machine, which does make quite a lot of noise. Luckily it was not too hot on NYC when we were there but in summer, you might need to leave airco on the whole night and I do not like that idea... No problems with location. Actually it was nice not to stay in up manhattan but in down town. Brooklyn is very close. Meat pack, Soho, Lower East a few stops with metro. Enough to discover and see. Thanks guys at Gild Hall for such a great service!

“Pretty good for what you pay” We got the room through Priceline so we only paid $80 per night. The hotel is Italian themed with nice attendants. Having valet parking was a big plus. The lobby and entrance of the hotel were kept clean at all times. Rooms were serviced everyday by polite employees. We definitely got what we paid for.

“Nice Place to Stay in NYC” My husband and I spent Labor Day weekend in NYC staying at the Radisson. It was our 4th stay in New York and this was one of the nicer hotels. It's out of the Time Square hustle and bustle (I don't care for Time Square), but still centrally located. It was a 3 block walk to the subway which we rode for the first time. We did a tour of Central Park and Rockefeller Center which we walked to. We also saw 2 Broadway plays within easy walking distance. We did take the subway down to our tour of the Brooklyn Bridge and the Chelsea High Line Tour. Our room was on the 22nd floor and was very quiet and clean. It was small, but had a nice size closet and the bathroom was adequate. After all, you're in New York. How much time will you spend in your room? The bed was really comfortable also. We came in early and they did store our luggage with a charge of $2.00. The bellhop walked us out to the curb and got our taxi for us on the way back to the airport. A word about the the establishments next door. Raffles is nice but you can get the same breakfast at a deli on Lexington and 52nd for half the price. There is a bar called Tienna (or something similar) which we thought was the hotel bar. We went in for a draft beer about 5:00 and they charged $11 each for the beer, plus tax and a $3.45 service charge. Two draft beers cost nearly $28.00. There are other places around where a happy hour beer is $4.00.

“Nice with Great Service, But Not For Me” This hotel is nice. The staff is pleasant and helpful and the service is excellent. The location is pretty good (although not as good as the Four Seasons Boston's location). However, the look and feel of the rooms was just not for me. I'd compare staying at XV Beacon to staying in an old but really nice, well-kept brownstone. The showers are weird/old fixtures, things generally look old, and the hotel doesn't have wireless internet access. To access the internet, I had to borrow an ethernet cord and even with that, I had trouble . . . in line with the excellent service, someone was there in 2 minutes to try (unsuccessfully) to fix it. The music system in the room is pretty cool - there are speakers in the ceilings all through the rooms, so you can really enjoy music while in your room.

“Great location; Great amenities” I spent the weekend at The James and really enjoyed my stay. The staff is attentive and plenty. I never opened a lobby door my entire stay. The room (we stayed in a Standard King) is large with everything you need including a very expansive mini-bar. The bathrooms are small, but efficient. And the "Intelligent Nutrient" toiletries are fabulous and regular sized for normal enjoyment and use. We used the room service for breakfast and a late night snack and found them to be on-time and delicious. Additionally, I stopped by the Spa on saturday morning for an hour massage. The spa was small, but tranquil. And the massage was just what I needed to get ready for a day of shopping at the Magnificent Mile. Cons: - The hotel lobby bar gets packed. If you want to sit there before dinner for a drink, you will most likely be snuggling up to another group on the couch. -Ask for a room above floor 10. Otherwise, you will definitely hear some street noise as apparently car horn honking is a pastime in Chicago. - Elevators are tight, but run quickly and there are two of them Pros: - One block off Magnificent Mile - Turnover service is great with brownies left on your bed -Fitness Center was packed with the right equipment and the spa is wonderful - Hotel Staff is knowledgable and friendly

“Great hotel and location” My family of 3 stayed here last weekend and were very happy with our choice. Just one block from the holiday hustle and bustle on Michigan Ave, and a short walk to the Navy Pier. The staff was courteous and professional and Neil (bell staff) was superb! Our room on the 20th floor was cozy, clean and quiet. The hotel was busy over the weekend but we didn't experience any issues at all, not even with the elevators. We would stay here again!

“Classic” When you arrive at the hotel by car, the valet parking is located around the corner almost behind the building. Valet parking was $35/night. The attendant was polite and asked if we would need the car again soon. We said we were going to the ballpark and he gave us both walking directions as well as trolley directions. Check in was quick. The lobby was tastefully decorated. We stayed on the 5th floor and found the elevators to be a bit small. Our room was located close to the elevator and there was noise from both the elevator and the street. Our bed was a bit small, seemed like slightly larger than a full size but nowhere near the size of a queen. The room initially seemed clean but we then noticed some trash in one of the cans and something stuck in between the cushion and arm of the chair. We were awakened early by maid service on our checkout day. The bathroom was roomy. Large towels were provided but they were not very soft. We were disappointed in the size of the gym. With only 6 people in there working out, we were kind of tripping over each other. Great location, close to many restaurants and shopping. Very classy hotel with outstanding staff.

“A great hotel and I stay here regularly” I come to Denver often on business and always stay here. I stay in the towers and always go for a club room on the club floor. The rooms are smart, modern and sometimes I luck out and get a very large suite. The club breakfast is excellent and the guy their super friendly and efficient. Location is great and there are lots of eating options around and about. It gets full quickly so book well in advance. The gym is huge and awesome. Sometimes I take a run down to the river.

“PHOTOS DO NOT DO THIS HOTEL JUSTICE” We pre-booked from the UK our first two nights in Texas at the Indigo. The info I viewed on the internet did not inspire me - it looked too garish - not my sort of decor. However, in reality it is lovely - yes, a bit different - but quirky and really nice!
