The rooms are all different - beautifully appointed - good TV channels - good coffee (in mugs, not disposable cups - deep joy!) The beds are quite high, so be aware of that! Free parking. Location next to the Galleria superb - not that we were in Houston for shopping but great to have a 'mooch' arround on arrival and some quick food in the Food Court (we were too tired to eat in a restaurant). Not good for getting Downtown which is some distance away - we drove and did find parking easy but it wasn't cheap. Well worth visiting the VISITORS' CENTER if you are going Downtown. Unfortunately, by the time we found it our parking was fast running out. They gave us loads of tips - free on/off bus around the city, many different places to visit. Due to the heat and the time difference (we were shattered), we didn't really make the most of our time in Houston - but we loved it. However, towards the end of the holiday we did manage to visit the other places she had suggested - the Port of Houston Ship Channel runs a free boat trip which was incredibly interesting. You need to pre-book (something which wasn't plain on the info given) as they need to do security checks. We turned up the first time - and although they had room, because we weren't on their list they wouldn't take us. So disappointing. We were told the next week was completely booked and as we were returning to the UK in 4 days time we had lost our chance; however, a lovely memeber of staff called us back and said they had managed to get us on the next day's trip. WEll worth it! We also managed to get to the San Jacinta National Park and Memorial. Leave loads of time if you can. You can travel to the top of the tower (lift) - stunning, breath taking views over esturary, the battlefield, towards Houston - amazing; there is a film about the history and battle and a very good museum. Also, just down from the Memorial is the Texas Battleship - again well worth a visit! We loved Houston and the surroundings.

“Great place for a business meeting, very attentive to detail.” This botique hotel is only a couple of blocks off the seafront/docks in downtown Seattle. Also it is only a few blocks south of Pike Street Market, as well as many restaurants. The staff is extremely friendly and will go out of their way to indulge whatever you need. The rooms are quite amazing, with bathtubs that fill from the ceiling, well appointed granite tile, and interesting lighting combinations. Each room is equipped with a French Press for making coffee. Truly light-blocking curtains that overlapped easily on the windows. Complimentary WiFi, which way too many upscale hotels charge for is a nice touch. I was there for a business meeting, which was held in the hotel. Excellent cocktail reception, moving through a curtained door to the dining area. The dining area had lots of glass, including the ceiling, with retractable panels that allow for those rare too-much-sun days in Seattle.

“Great Hotel but still needed earplugs” I've stayed at ths hotel before and thought it was great. Maybe it's just that it is a year older now or we just had back luck. Out suite was plagued with strange noises. Although these rooms have "central" airconditioning with a thermostat, the blower unit was in a utilily closet in the bedroom. It woke me everytime it cycled on and off. Fortunately it was not that hot while we were there and I simply turned it off at night. The worst offender was the refrigerator from hell. I've never experienced an appliance with such a variety of loud and annoying noises. I own four refrigerators and realize that all refrigerators make some noise but there was something wrong with this refrigerator. The manager offered us earplugs or to move us to another suite. I know she was trying but I think she should have taken our word that something was wrong with this refrigerator and either fixed it or moved it to another room as opposed to asking us to move all of our stuff. Aside from the refrigerator from hell, this is a nice hotel. The afternoon social hour is particularly nice. Kelly, the lady who runs it, is great. We were in a group of about 20 and this gave everybody a nice opportunity to meet their peers who are spread out over the country.

“Excellent for the Price” For the price I paid on Travelocity, the room was amazing. Actually it was a very large suite (Flat TV, Frig, dishwasher, microwave, dining table). The location is excellent , 8-9 blocks from Georgetown and four from Dupont Circle, basically walking distance to everywhere. The room was clean and room service fantastic. Of course like everywhere else in DC, the staff was NOT Friendly!!!! The view of the room was bad, but that's the price to pay in the City. But overall excellent hotel for the price and location.

“Top end in LA” Nicely appointed room and a friendly staff in a great location. Room service is quick but food in two meals was barely warm and of moderate quality. Good TV/entertainment system with easy connections. Internet works well. Location is great for LA Live, Staples Center, the Convention Center and Nokia Theater. Events at adjacent venues can generate noise but did not cause a problem.

“great after room change” Our first room, a studio, was way too small and the bathroom was impossibly small and not updated. They moved us after one night to a much better room. Our second room was huge and had two updated bathrooms. We loved it. The service was excellent the whole time. I would definitely return to this hotel.

“Wonderful stay and exceptional service” I live in Austin and like to experience the urban scene from time to time by staying in downtown hotels. This time, my husband and I brought our two sons, aged 10 and 12, with us because it was one of their birthdays. The day before our stay, I noticed on Facebook that the W was running an Easter special that included parking, brunch at Trace (their highly regarded restaurant) and Easter goodies. I emailed to ask whether we could switch to that package. They immediately contacted me and handled it, no problems at all, and even upgraded our room. When we arrived, the boys were delighted to learn there were Easter eggs hidden around the room for them...11 in all, each filled with very creative and thoughtful things. The hotel had asked in advance the gender of the kids, so they walked away with some very nice stuff: headphones, notepads, bags, drinking bottles, and candy...oh and spa samples and $20 of drink tickets for Mom and Dad! On top of this, they included a birthday card for my son...and at turndown, a whole plate of Easter treats. We were blown away by this. I mention this Easter promotion because it was very creatively executed and definitely demonstrated the level of care the W Austin takes with their guests. Besides all that, this is an awesome place to stay anyway. It's in a fantastic location for walking all over the city as well as proximity to the lake and to the running trail ( though the gym and yoga studio is sparkling clean with very new equipment ). The pool itself is smallish but the kids were able to splash around for a few hours without disturbing the adults in the pool, so it's not THAT small. Lots of seating all around the pool and to the side of the deck, by the outdoor bar. The whole place has a very community Austin vibe, with generous and comfortable shared spaces, indoors and out. I also got a pedicure at their spa, which is cozy but very relaxing with scented candles, nibbles and wine. Brunch at Trace was a highlight, sitting outside listening to music and watching the pedestrians go about their business. All in all, a fantastic time and we will definitely return.

“Convenient location and clean room” Stayed one evening in the Seattle airport LaQuinta. Was pleasantly surprised by my spacious room and the continental breakfast. Shuttle to airport runs on time and driver was very friendly. needed to wash some clothes and the dryer was the best working hotel dryer I've ever used. You're within walking distance to a handful of restaurants, fast food, a pub and some others. Wish the shuttle could run you to Southcenter for some shopping. Internet worked great. Met friends over at Southcenter where there are a lot of restaurants to choose from.

“Very pricey, but great room for Times Square” It's always a dilemma to stay in NYC during a popular week. We didn't want to take the chance with a last minute reservation so used Hilton Honors points "plus". The location is great - 1/2 way between the heart of times square and central park; easy walk to the upper west side or the upper east side. The room was updated very nicely. Appreciated having room to move around and 2 very comfortable queen beds. Staff members were responsive. Would stay here again, if the price seems right.

“Excellent Choice!” Stayed at the country Inn and Suites on 1/14 and 1/15 2007 during a layover in Denver. This place is very nice for the money. The rooms were spacious and clean. The breakfast was good (remember it's free). The public spaces were clean and attractive. Dining was right net door and across the street. Many options including Outback, unos, Applebees, Quizos, BarbBq place, sub and pasta shop, Mexican place. I had no car and it was 5 degrees but all of these places are within a 1 minute walk. The shuttle to the airport was great. The airport is 15 minutes away. This is one of the closest places to DIA. There was an Amerisuites accross the street along with a sleep Inn, a Hilton garden Inn, a Marriott, and something else. The hotel is fairly new and everything was in excellent working order. I will stay again next time I have a lyover in Denver. Excellent Choice!

“Nice Property” I was really disappointed when I found out that the JW was booked and I had to stay at this property. However, I was pleasantly surprised. The staff were extremely friendly and helpful. The rooms (though a little on the small side) were nicely appointed and very comfortable and cozy. The shower gel/shampoo/conditioner combination in the shower adds a nice touch as well as the bath and body works aromatherapy lotions. The food provided by the banquet staff and the Champion's restaurant in the hotel was very good. The only negative to this property is that in some spots it smells moldy. It is really strong on the second floor in the meeting room area, not sooo much in the sleeping rooms. Whenever I hit the second floor I would have a sneeze fit. It may be time to replace the carpet. All in all, I would recommend this property and will look forward to visiting again (but only if the JW is unavailable).

“Nice hotel, clean, great staff.” After staying here I was surprised that it was not listed higher on the trip advisor site. I stay in hotels all the time and this is a very nice hotel with front desk staff that welcome you every time you come in and wish you well as you leave. I recommend this hotel to all and have a great time in Austin!

“Wonderful Hotel” We stayed at the Hotel Lombardy over a weekend stay in DC. It was my wife and I plus her sister and husband. We each booked a deluxe room with a king sized bed. My wife and I loved our room and it even included a little kitchen area that contained a mini fridge and a small table with a couple of chairs. Her sister's room did not have the kitchen area. Their room felt a bit smaller overall. Our windows had wooden blinds plus drapery while their room only had the blinds. Overall, the room was very nice and the bed was very comfortable. After walking around DC all day long, I needed a comfortable bed. The bathroom is small but it was very clean. My wife loved the water pressure in the hotel along with the bath and body works soaps and lotions. Just about every light in the room was on a dimmer switch and the room had a ceiling fan. The TV in the room came with lots of channels but the signal was not the best. Many of the stations came in wavy or had lines running through it. Not a big deal for us as we had very little time to watch TV. The room was quiet although you could hear the person upstairs when they were walking around their room. It wasn't that big of a deal. Service in the hotel was excellent. We never waited more than a minute for the elevator. There was always someone at the front door to open it for us. Although street parking is free on the weekend, we couldn't find a spot near the hotel, so we would up using valet at $35/nt. I had no problem with the valet service and the service was quick. We liked the hotel location as there was a metro station within a 5 minute walk of the hotel plus lots of restaurants including TGIF, Au Bon Pain, Starbucks, Corner Bakery, Bertuccis, and many others. The White House was about a 20 minute walk away. We all felt very safe walking around the hotel area at night. We would definitely stay at this hotel again the next time we visit DC.

“Great location, lovely lobby, great club, satisfactory room” Stayed here for 3 nights recently as a result of a Hyatt promo. Used a Diamond suite upgrade and was given a balcony suite. First off, the location is great. The hotel is literally about 50 feet from the BART station, and is across the street from the Embarcadero. From there you can get on the F light rail line, which runs along the water to the pier, or get on at least 4 different bus lines in front of the hotel, running to a number of places including Golden Gate Park. The interior of the hotel lobby is very pretty, with its dangling strands of lights and large open atrium, as well as a neat rock filled structure with running water. Check in was easy enough and they offered me a Balcony Suite instead of the entry level suite if we could wait until 4pm for the room to be cleaned. The elevators are clear glass so you can see the lobby and atrium as you go up and down which is neat. Our room was nice, as it had a living room with TV, exiting out to the balcony, and a hallway to the bedroom. The bedroom had its own door, as well as its own bathroom, in addition to the bathroom in the hallway. The couch had cigarette burns and we found ashtrays in the drawer, which we were told were for the balcony. The room did not smell of smoke, although the linens did. The room itself was spacious, although poorly lit. The lighting in the bedroom was horrific, as there was only a little lamp on the nightstand, and one on the desk on the far side of the room. Even with all the lights on, the light was pretty poor. The bathroom was nice, although the shower was pretty small and caked with soap scum. Now, I know that soap scum accumulates, but if it is properly cleaned every day that housekeeping is cleaning it, you should be able to easily keep it clean. The bed was soft and comfortable, and the only issue was the smell of smoke which had permeated some of the linens, although not severely. The club lounge had a great view of the water, but is kind of a hassle to get to. You can only reach it from 2 of the 5 elevators, so unless you luck out and get one of those elevators when you call the elevator, you must go to the ground floor, call those specific elevators, and then go back up. The club itself is nice, although the hours are very short. Breakfast is 6-9 except weekends when it is 7-10 I believe. The club also closes at 9pm. Breakfast is your standard Hyatt cold continental breakfast fare, although the evening hors d'oeuvres are very good. We enjoyed meatballs, pizza, asparagus and a few other items one evening which were very good. The club also has 2 Ijoy massage chairs and 2 computer workstations with printers, which were great. Overall, the best Hyatt club I have been to thus far. The service was friendly and fairly efficient, and I had no complaints whatsoever. Overall a very nice hotel which I would definitely stay at again. The room was nice enough with a good bed and LCD TVs, although, aside from the size, it kind of lacked the impeccable "suite-ness" of that one would expect from a suite, if that makes sense.

“Wonderful staff, Very Nice Room and Great Location” I continue to be a Marriott fan and this hotel signifies the reason. Marriott has the greatest beds, the staff were exceptionally helpful and my room was spacious and spotless. This hotel is in a great location, right on the edge of Dupont, Foggy Bottom and close to Georgetown. My only request to Marriott, please get wireless in the rooms! Charging 12.95 for wired internet is such a negative characteristic!

“Met our needs - nice lady checked us in” We missed a connection at CLT. The lady that checked us in on Aprli 10 at 02:00 A. M. was very helpful and gave us a complimentary upgrade for my Platinum status. The grounds were well maintained. Room clean. Breakfast included sausage gravey, biscuits, pancakes, yogurt and boiled eggs. Would stay here again.

“This place was excellent and we will definitely stay again” We stayed here for 2 nights and it was a very good 2 nights. This place is close to the zoo, close to Cherry Creek shopping, restaurants, etc... Great location. Plenty of parking. Clean, large rooms to spend time in. Comfortable mattress and nice bedding. The hot breakfast that was included with our stay was fabulous with omlets, bacon, sausage, you name it. Free cookies in the lobby at night as refreshments during the day. The bar was also very nice. Great natural gas fire pit to sit around at night with plenty of comfortable outside seating. Restaurants on the front side of the building. This was a very nice stay. Hotel staff was extremely nice as well. Good free wireless internet was a plus.
“Great hotel!” It's nice clean and like brand new! Best hotel I've stayed at here in Indianapolis! I had no problems with my stay!

“All about the price” A double room in midtown Manhatten for $117 a night inclusive. If value is your thing then this is the hotel for you. It's got it's faults. The rooms are very small as are the ensuite bathrooms. The whole hotel is very worn looking and it does need brightening up and the rooms are only cleaned every second day, big deal. Any other hotel in midtown will cost you 3 times the price of this place. And outside of the price it also has very helpful and cheerful staff. If you're fussy and need little extras in your hotel then stay easewhere.

“Overnight getaway” We stayed at the Sheraton off of 290 for an evening. The room was quite large and the bed was comfortable. The bedding was soft, clean and very nice. I would recommend this for a getaway.

“Believe the positive reviews” I had read all the glowing reveiws before our visit. Yes, I was skeptical but I needn't have been because this place lived up to every postive. Our one-bedroom suite was cosy and comfortable. Even if we didn't use all the features of the kitchen, it was nice to know they were available. The value is excellent. A very nice breakfast; the week night dinner really exceeded expectations. We had expected to dine out every night but when we saw the quality of the dinner selections we stayed at Homewood instead. A small but fresh salad bar is provided along with one main dish that is chef- prepared. Not gourmet, but quality ingredients prepared with skill to create a simple but tasty meal. Plus the free beer, wine and other beverages was a big bonus. Several readers have mentioned the excellent staff. I must agree. Both Normas were lovely and helpful. And the rest of the staff was also top-notch. Much credit must go to the owner, Mr. Rauch and the manager, Ann Marie . We met both of them and much of the success of this property is due to their hands-on approach which creates the atmosphere of comfort, care and competence that is so highly valued in a hotel. Keep up the good work, everyone. When we return to the San Diego area, we'll be sure to come back.

“Nice hotel but eating options are WAY overpriced!” I have to stay at this hotel when in Boston for work, so I come here frequently. It is connected to the airport and if there is a shuttle provided from your terminal to the hotel I am not aware of it as we always walk through the airport or through the parking garage to get to the hotel. The hotel is a nice size and has a nice workout facility. But what I can't STAND is the overpriced eating options. I stay at a LOT of hotels, but this one doesn't provide a single meal (breakfast, lunch, or dinner) option for under $10. I had a burger in the bar during one stay, it was $16. That was with a 20% discount! Room service charges the 15% service fee as expected, but then there is an ADDITIONAL 3% administrative fee AND $3.50 room service charge. Continental breakfast will run you $20, that's for a muffin/pastry choice, juice option and coffee/tea option?!? What really bothered me on my stay here last night was 1) the toilet paper dispenser is in an inconvenient location and then, it didn't spin! You try to pull some, and it just tore because the roll stayed still. I had to wrestle the roll of the spinner and just spin it in my hands to use it. The facial tissue dispenser had 3 white tissues before they turned orange to let me know they were all gone. Great! Especially when you're coming down with a cold. Why they can't put a full one in during housekeeping cleaning time makes no sense, or keep a spare in the bathroom like some hotels do with the toilet paper rolls. I also couldn't fall asleep for 3 hours. If you're a side sleeper, you will not like the pillows at all! I also had to unplug that alarm clock, cause that orange glow wasn't making things any easier. This of course was after the 20 minutes we lost downstairs at the front desk checking in because they couldn't find my companies' reservation for our rooms. Unless your company covers your room AND meal charges at this hotel, I wouldn't stay here at all.

“Posh in the heart of Midtown” Took a suite on one of the top floors for a business meeting with about 10 colleagues. The suite was amazing, posh beyond belief - views of the NYC skyline, Times Square, etc. You felt like you were hanging in the clouds. The room was beautifully decorated and comfortable, the service was good and polite. The hotel is very pricey but since it was on business it didn't really play a role. I would think twice before shelling out this kind of money personally but it's definitely worth a look and deserves some consideration.

“Enjoyed the Sheraton” I spent a Saturday night in Baltimore due to family at John Hopkins. With no reservation, I walked up to the check-in desk and received a room for $89. I am a SPG member so that may have helped. The front desk personal was very friendly and efficient. I received a north tower room that looked like it was recently renovated. The beds were firm and comfortable. The room décor was pleasant and did not look worn. A new LCD flat screen TV was mounted on the wall. The room has Internet access but I never used it. The room and bathroom were very clean. Loved the heavenly shower hear with excellent water pressure. The only down side of staying here is the excessive parking fees. $22 for a guest is a very steep. Other than that, I enjoyed my night at the Sheraton.

“Very nice” I stayed here with my husband and children at the end of May for a weekend sightseeing trip. The location is pretty good, just a couple of blocks from the Mag Mile. We walked to the Sears Tower and Navy Pier and Millennium Park, but it was a pretty long walk. We had a Tranquil Suite which was very nice. Housekeeping was excellent and everything was very clean. Checking in was a breeze. The continental breakfast was very high quality and service was very good. Overall, I could find no faults with this hotel other than it may be a little farther walk to sightseeing destinations than others. It was a nice place and I would stay here again.

“For a last minute stay, this place exceeded our expectations!!” We decided last minute (7:30pm) to get a hotel room for the night. Checked hotels.com and there was a room for $99. Called the hotel directly to make and they quoted me $109, I mentioned a third person and the total changed to $129 (note to self: don't mention extra people). Upon arrival we were pleasantly surprised how nice the hotel was and how easy check in was. Our room was on the 12th floor, and we heard barely any street noise...but this hotel is not in Union Square- its in the Financial District, so expect it to be much quieter! Our double double room was spacious, the room was immaculate, the bathroom was big and had tons of space. We even had a partial view of the bay bridge. Unfortunately valet parking is really the only thing you can do and that is $49....That is the only downside though! Definitely would stay here again and would recommend this hotel to anyone! Oh yeah, and Starbucks is right across the street.

“Affinia Shelburne-We will be back:)” We recently had a 4 day stay at the Affinia Shelburne for my daughters 17th b-day. I mentioned this to them when booking my reservations. They were so kind in giving us a early morning check in (we came in on a red eye flight) we were also placed on the 15th floor and had a views of the Empire State Bldg and the Chrysler Bldg. The room was a 2 bed delux, with mini kitchenette. We asked for a coffee maker and they sent one up right away. I also loved the location of this hotel. Close to Grand Central, coffee shops, shopping, everything was central. The staff at the hotel was also incredibly kind and helpful. We will for sure return to the hotel on our next trip. We love NY and the Affinia Shelburne:)!!

“Awesome Union Square Boutique Hotel” We stayed at the Galleria Park Hotel for 5 nights over a Presidents Day Weekend getaway to San Francisco. We had a nice stay at the Dream Inn in Santa Cruz (another Joie de Vivre property) and the Galleria Park was offering a weekend special with free parking, so we decided to give it a shot. Man, what a great surprise! The hotel is in a great location on Sutter Street, just a block from Kearny and a few blocks from Market. Union Square is a short walk away, as is China Town, and there is incredible shopping and dining everywhere you turn. One night we ate at the very hip and trendy Farmerbrown Restaurant, and another night at the French seafood bistro Plouf. Public transit is steps away, so within minutes you can easily get all over the city. The hotel is beautifully decorated with a great chandelier hanging in entry, a huge decorative fireplace in the corner, great art throughout, a very cool terrace on the third floor and even a nice wine happy hour. The room was very comfortable with plenty of space. It was a typical old San Francisco building with steam heat, but lots of charm and all the new amenities you could ask for. The bed was comfortable and there was a desk w/chair and another chair in the corner. There was a nice note and a bottle of wine waiting in the room for us when we arrived. And since we arrived well after midnight, it was much appreciated!

“Solid 4 Star Hotel, with a great location” The entire downstairs staff is excellent. The doormen regularly did hold the door (rarely happens anymore), valet guy was courteous and allowed me to park for 10 minutes, concierge was helpful and available, and the front desk staff is first class- from Katherine who assisted me prior to arrival to Sasha who checked me in at 11am- into a high floor (as requested), but small room. The furniture was nice, bed comfortable, and there was a nice but small sitting area. It seems like each room has corner windows (due to the building's designs) and I thought that was cool. The curtains were perfect. The bathroom was small, there were too few toiletries (one soap), and the shower head was shooting some water into the ceiling, finally the toilet made a horrible sound when it was flushed. It still was clean but needed a little TLC. I was disappointed that my room didn't have a terrace (as I viewed right into the others around me), but I paid $85 on priceline and was treated like a valued customer. Finally, the location is excellent- walk to Union Square, Chinatown, Ferry Building, Fisherman's Wharf, North Beach... what more can you ask for? It's also close to Bart= airport train. Thanks to the entire staff for making me feel so welcome. I look forward to my next stay here.

“Excellent” Pricelined this hotel for $45. What a great room. Large, flat screen tvs, wetbar/fridge, nice bed. Really enjoyed this place. Unfortunately, I was only there to sleep. Would have been great for a couple "personal" days, but I was in and out of Columbus on business. Would recommend for either business or pleasure.

“Loved this hotel. Would want to return to it, definitely” Great hotel, right on the Riverwalk. Super nice room. I had a huge king sized bed, couch, desk, nice TV, big enough bathroom. The staff was great. The conceirge gave out vouchers for freebies at area restaurants. Everyone on staff I talked with from the front desk to cleaners to random people setting up the convention space was so helpful. The hotel is centrally located, right by the Alamo, the Riverwalk and the Convention Center. Guests are welcome to sit in the open bar seating in the lobby overlooking the riverwalk during the daytime. There are nice seats overlookign the river if you need to do work there. They have a riverfront restaurant too. The bus to Market Square runs right by the hotel. I don't write a lot of reviews but wanted to give this hotel a good review.

“The Drake is Great!” I have read through the reviews of this hotel before writing mine and want to clarify a few things based on my stay. First, this is a boutique historic hotel. When we arrived we heard another guest complaining about the size of her room, and I want to say "what did you expect?" If you want a big boxy standard room, go to the Sheraton. This is why you stay at a place like the Drake, because the quirlky small rooms are charming! We had a king bed (luxurious) in a smaller sized room right near the elevator on the 12th floor. Because this is an old building we couldn't hear a thing outside our door. Not a problem at all with noise. The bedding was very high quality, definitely Kimpton standard. The decor in the room was also great - mismatching striped wallpaper and headboard - also a great quirky feature of a boutique hotel. And yes, the bath was small. Over three days I think we probably spent a total of 30 minutes in the bathroom - does the size really matter? The best part of this hotel is its location in Union Square on the cable car line. You really feel like you in the middle of it all, and it is a great starting point for getting all over the CIty (right near the Bart, Muni, Cable Car, etc.) Also, the dining in this neighborhood is fabulous. Our best restaurant experience was at a Mexican place (Colibri) recommended by the Concierge! We booked on Expedia and got a great three day mid-week rate of $100 a night. The ONLY complaint I have about the Drake is the heating/cooling system (apparently new) in the room. Our thermostat was inoperable and the room hovered between 75 and 80 degrees the whole time we were there. We called to complain twice and either had no response or the fix didn't work (we were out when they came). Because we are from Seattle, I think we were pretty ok with a warm room in spring, but it was mildly annoying. I would definitely recommend this hotel for the value. Definitely above average.

“Good Location near Gayborhood!” Close to everything you may want to do in Center City. Nice view of Avenue of the Arts also, aka Broad St. The bar was comfortable & convenient. Not the friendliest bartender, but also not rude, just did his job. The restaurant staff was helpful also, & the food was quite good & extremely reasonable price-wise compared to other Hotels. Rooms are spacious & comfortable. We would have liked an in-room mini-fridge, but used ice machine instead. Enjoyable stay!

“What you would expect” Nice hotel with clean rooms. Near a lot restaurants and attractions in easy walking distance, including the Reading Terminal Market. Staff very friendly. As expected because of the distance, there isn't an airport shuttle. The cab ride for two with luggage to the airport was $38.

“Nice location, good play to stay” The location is excellent for easy walking to restaurants, around the corner is the Slippery Noodle, just blocks from convention center, Lucas Oil Stadium, downtown shopping, and a short drive to Eli Lilly, which is where I was visiting. I stayed in an executive room, it was very roomy, nice sized desk for working, large nice flat screen TV and a sofa. The bathroom decor is a bit dated but otherwise, it was functional. The continental breakfast is excellent. The staff were friendly and helpful. Finally, the hotel is a quick drive to/from the airport.

“Service with a Smile” The purpose of my stay was to attend a conference being held at the hotel. Warmly greeted at the front desk, we were able to check in a few hours early. My room was a spacious and pleasantly appointed double, with a small vanity area and seperate space for the commode and shower. There was a large desk with internet connection, no wireless, altho my laptop was picking up plenty of signals I paid for the secure connection. The only drawback to the room was the view - the parking lot. For the duration of my stay I was greeted with a smile and hello by every employee I interacted with or passed by. It was a very nice touch and I appreciated it. As meetings were scheduled closely together I ate most of my meals in the hotel and was happy with the quality. One morning I had the breakfast buffett and in addition to the coffee I had at the table, the server offered to prepare a to-go cup for me as well. It was most appreciated! The coffee, btw, was really good, not the typical hotel dishwater. The pool area was beautiful, large comfy places to sit along with a few hammocks for real relaxtion. The hot tub was nearby and looked inviting, tho I was not able to indulge. We had a cocktail reception and the passed hors d'ouerves were delicious. There are restaurants nearby which you can walk to, but the hotel is located in a very busy retail/office district and it is not exactly pedestrian-friendly. It was a great place to have a conference, and I would return.

“Fantastic Stay!” One of the best hotels I have stayed at in my years of traveling. I stayed the second weekend in July, and could not have been any more happy with this hotel. Upon arrival we were offered multiple times if we needed help with our luggage and we politely declined because we did not have that much to carry. The person checking us in (Kelsey I believe her name was) was very friendly explained everything we needed to know about the hotel, including the restaurants, fitness center and pool.After we checked in we went up to our room on the 11th floor, our room had 2 double beds, it was very clean, nice size for a hotel, and very well appointed. The hotel room was very business traveler friendly with plenty of outlets, a nice size desk and hook ups for your computer, on the bad side the wifi was slow. We chose to park our selfs at the paring garage right next door, the parking garage elevators were extremely cool and it was in out privileges for 13$ a day, not a bad deal! After settling in our room we decided to do he lunch buffet at one of the hotels restaurants, it was very average; the burger was very dry and luke warm, though the service was good.After that we decided to go and tour the stock yards, very cool considering this was our first time in Texas. After a long day at the stock yards and a nice dinner we decided to return to our hotel and to our surprise there was turn down service and milk and cookies, what a nice treat after a long day! . As previous reviewers said the pool was a little on the small side and the pool was a little to warm for my liking but it was a nice little refresher. Check out was extremely smooth and we did not have any problems. Over all a fantastic stay, if we are in the Fort Worth area again we would return in a heart beat!

“Business war horse in Union Square” I stayed here four nights on a business trip. The Grand Hyatt is an old war horse of a hotel -- it's been around for decades now. This was my first stay. The lobby is not much more than the reception desks and then turn the corner to the banks of elevators. It makes it efficient because you won't run into families or folks milling around in a typical tourist lobby area. But if you want the grand, welcoming lobby experience -- you won't find it here. The banks of elevators are a godsend because the wait is short. I stayed in a standard king bedroom. The room was modernized and had more than enough space at about 300 sq ft. The bed was comfortable with clean, soft linens. There's a large flat screen TV. The window shades are electronic which is wonderful when one is too lazy to get up off the bed to close them. The bathroom had enough space to manuveur around without feeling claustophobic. There were high quality toiletries in use -- a great touch was the small tube of toothpaste that lasted all week. One thing to note: I had one of those rooms that had a door which connected to the adjacent room. There wasn't much soundproofing on the connecting door because I could hear my neighbors when I stood in front of the mirror at the side of the connecting door.

“Great location, very basic gym” I stayed here for 8 nights whilst on holiday. The location is this hotels draw card and it is very good You are a couple of blocks from the heart of times square, which is good because 8th Ave is much quieter but you can be in the heat of the action within a few minutes. There are also a few subway stations close by. The neighbourhood feels very safe, even late at night. As for the hotel, checkin was quick and easy. The room was nice a clean, you get a coffee machine, a microwave and a fridge with no mini bar items (there is a vending machine in the corridor and a 24 hours convenience store in the lobby. The bathroom felt a little dated, and had a bath/shower but was fine overall. The bed was comfy, though the pillows were very soft. The room had very little street noise, but there was a little bit of hotel noise. In pariticular there wa an occasional thud, it sounded like some thing thudding against the room door (it wasn't though) and i heard it most nights, though it never woke me and I'm a light sleeper. My travel partner felt the aircon was loud. I think it was a bit loud, but it didn't bother me at all. Overall I had good sleep, so the noises didn't bother me. If noise gets too bad I sleep with ear plugs, but didn't need them here. The gym is basic, a few cardio machines and a very limited selection of dumbbells. But there is an excellent gym around the corner. The breakfast buffet is good, there is also an a la carte menu but our breakfast was included so we always hit the buffet. Had no problems with checkout, and the bellhop organised a car for us to go to the airport. Overall it was a good stay, a better gym would be nice but the close gym was excellent, and the hotel noise was disappointing but really didn't bother me. The location is excellent and definitely makes the hotel worthwhile.

“Great business value” This is my regular hotel when I travel to NY, which is probably 3 times per month. It is very close to our office on Water St, and that makes it really appealing. Additionally, we have great rates which helps keep costs down. The hotel is new and built in the past year. There is a decent restaurant downstairs and room service is good. The lobby is on the second floor so you have to take an elevator to get there. Check-in is always fast and they give you an excellent warm cookie! There are three elevators and they can be very slow. I have waited 2-3 minutes sometimes for one to come. The rooms are small but efficient. I am always alone, so it's not an issue. With two people and multiple bags, this could get very tight quickly. The bathrooms too are small with limited shelf space. The shower seems small too, but they have good water pressure and a large shower head. The air conditioner in the room is loud and not always easy to regulate. It can wake you up on occasion because it's so loud. Great TV and channel selection. There is a coffee pot in room and efficient room service. Internet is available for a fee, unless you have status and then it's free. As a business traveler, this is a good hotel and close to work. I would recommend it for this purpose. I would offer 3.5 stars if they let me.

“Loved It!!” This hotel was awesome! It's right next to the airport but you don't hear planes or anything it's a hidden gem and its a GREAT deal! It's right off one of the main highways so that is perfect, I would stay there again anytime

“Comfy, clean, and convenient for a lot” This hotel is very good for what it is worth. My party had no problems with check-in at all. They were very nice at the check-in counter, and were very helpful in sending toiletries up when I needed them. The room itself was comfortable. The beds were pretty good, the TV was good, the shower was good, and I liked the free internet. It's an awkward location for this hotel, with it in a corner right off the Sam Houston Tollway and the Westpark Tollway, but it works. It's very easy to get on BOTH Tollways to go wherever from the hotel (although for the Westpark Tollway, you'll need what they call an EZ Tag, and to go eastbound, you'll have to drive down Westpark Dr or Harwin Dr to South Gessner and get on there.) I also liked the fact that the hotel is very quiet. Considering it's flanked by two freeways, that's great. (I was in a room facing away from the freeways.) I didn't try the restaurant, but it did look busy. May be a good sign. So, this is a good, cheap hotel for Westchase, and very convenient for what we were doing.

“Exceedingly friendly service but paper thin walls” The stand-out here is the service. Everyone I encountered was friendly and helpful, particularly the guest services staff that arranged for an early check-in. The location is also convenient to multiple subway lines, River North and the West Loop area. What makes it less than 5 stars are the small rooms with paper thin walls. I could hear every word of my neighbor's conversations even with my ear plugs in. It's also a little less fresh and clean around the edges compared to the Palomar and Monaco in town.

“Location, lovely, and loved it” I enjoyed everything about the Beacon. Start with location, especially if you want to be on the Upper West Side. Close to subway, Central Park, shopping, restaurants, everything you could want. Very clean and well appointed rooms. Appreciate that each room as a refrig and microwave. Very helpful when you travel. Complimentary wifi (as it should be!). Helpful staff. Starbucks across the street, Viand Cafe next store--great place to eat. I only wish they had a loyalty or frequent traveler program or even an email list for deals because I would like to stay here as often as possible. (Fun fact: if you are a fan of 666 Park, the apartment building used in the show is across Broadway from the Beacon.)

“Nice Hotel at the top of Nob Hill” This hotel styles itself as boutique. It's really not that. In fact, it's a fairly typical Renaissance in terms of room size, style and amenities. That's more than good enough for me, and the views are spectacular. The hotel restaurant was less to my liking: crowded, trendy and overrated. However, the hotel was across the street from the Fairmont Hotel and the Tonga Room, which is a blast. If you like streetcars, they run right in front of the hotel, and it's an easy walk to most of the city (unless you are lugging suitcases, in which case the last two blocks back to the hotel are a pretty steep hike from almost any direction).

“Friendly Staff and Good Value” Stayed here for a convention. Very friendly and helpful staff. Free shuttle to/from airport. Free breakfast that is decent by inexpensive hotel standards - always had some form of eggs along with fruit, cereal, pastries, warm mini-cinnamon rolls (tasty), sausage or biscuits and gravy, juice, coffee, etc. Room was clean and well-equipped. Bathroom small as others have noted, but clean and fine with a nice showerhead and good, fluffy towels. Additional perks here are warm cookies at night, and a free happy hour with wine, beer, or soft drinks and snacks on weekdays. Free internet worked fine. Conference rate of $89/nt. made this a great value. Wish it had a fitness center. There is a small pool. Only other down side for those needing to go to the convention center area daily is that it is a bit of a hike. But the upside is that you are in San Diego and it is almost always a very nice walk.

“A little disappointed” With all the hype of this hotel I quite expected it to meet the standards that we are use to but we're disappointed with it. I booked" The Madison" one bedroom suite which was large but unfortunately was missing a beat to it. I had reserved it for several days as I was in for business with my husband. To begin with from the front doorman, except for one, we had to open the door even though they would be right there. Not that I have a problem with that but given we had to hail a cab with no offers from them for this service. Actually, they would just be talking to the other gentlemen outside the door of the bar. There was no door service from them at all not even welcome back or enjoy your day! The restaurant which we dined at for breakfast daily and lunch had a wonderful menu and was delicious but the wait staff was more in tuned with what was going on in the kitchen or talking about an inspector that was there for one of the days. We had a horrible strong smell of some kind of paint or something that was coming from a store the borders the hotel. After being seated there and asking to be moved to another location as the restaurant was empty at this time I wondered why the hostess would even seat anyone at this location. The waiter was more than gracious to relocate us inside closer to their bar, as the horrible odor wasn't present there. As I mentioned the food was delicious and we did have a fabulous waiter that day. Back to our suite, I found that the cleaning service wasn't up to our standards as the floors were a little dirty, dirty dishes left on our table in the living room for two days, as well as in the bathroom wasn't that cleaned well. The suite was very uninviting "cold" such as no magazines or books to offer it's guest to look at, which I find strange??? The bed wasn't that comfortable and we ended up leaving earlier than expected. I really wanted to like this hotel but probably wouldn't return. Rather go to The Surrey one block over as from the moment you enter it's lobby to every staff member and suite we have stayed in there we have never been disappointed. The bar is over the top compared to the bar they have here! Also, love the rooftop bar there. Sorry, The Mark we tried.

“Great stay adjacent to Downtown L.A.” Our stay at the Miyako was great, and we would definitely stay there again. The cheerful woman at the front desk (she looked like an older version of Lady Gaga) was completely accommodating in our request for one of the quieter rooms, even offering us the opportunity to pre-screen a few rooms before deciding for sure. That said, there's not much traffic in that area of L.A. on weekends, so I think any room would have likely been fine. The room was clean and spacious, with individual climate control. The window was able to be opened. The bed was a little soft for our taste (our only complaint). Parking next door in the Little Tokyo garage was very inexpensive on weekends, and at one exit time it was even free - no attendant was there when we left Sunday morning. The restaurants of the adjacent Little Tokyo shopping center were delicious, and wonderful for a mid-day snack or a full meal. We were in town for a show at the Ahmanson at Music Center, whjch was a short walk away - so no need for parking hassles at the theatre! We also walked to the gorgeous downtown YMCA for an excellent workout (the spa at the hotel was closed for renovations). Note that this particular YMCA charges guests a nominal fee, even if you have an AWAY sticker on your YMCA card. We were also able to get around the freeways easily from that location in L.A. (even though it was Carmageddon weekend), and took day or evening trips to Santa Monica, West Hollywood, Griffith Park, and Pasadena. We used the Burbank Airport instead of LAX, which was VERY convenient. All in all, a great stay!

“Great stay, staff improved” This was out 4th stay in a year. The front desk staff was by far the friendliest yet. First impressions do matter. The valet parking was fine, wish we could have avoided the fee, but no street parking available this time. They gave us the room we asked for and it was clean with a great view. We had a refrigerator, which I used. As an Hilton Honors guest we were able to have breakfast in the executive lounge. One of the best I have been in, the young man in charge was friendly and helpful. The food was great, especially the coffee. Best stay yet, will return when in Phili.

“Oh My Goodness, Great Value!” The New York Palace Hotel (formerly Helmsley) is a Grande Dame of the Upper East Side. Right on madison avenue across from Saks and St. Patrick's Cathedral it has a beautful courtyard out front. The restaurant Gilt for dinner is fantastic as well as the Madison Room for breakfast. The rooms are brand new and a decent size. Two big beds. View of the church and on a high floor. Great value for NY!!!! Definatly would go back! The staff and concierge were extremely helpful and friendly too!
“Nice hotel” This is a nice hotel with friendly helpful staff-you also get adecent enough breakfast. It's a little on the expensive side.

“Like a Fabulous trip back in time” I thoroughly enjoyed my stay at the Biltmore and am almost tempted to give 5 stars, except for a few little niggles. To begin with the good - the ground floors are absolutely gorgeous with a great deal of restored original architecture/decor from the 1920's. My room was only a standard but quite spacious with a very comfortable bed, desk, full closet and comfy chair. My room was on the inside of the building, overlooking a quiet courtyard and I heard virtually no outside noise thanks to the white noise generated by the heat/AC. And the water pressure in the shower was fantastic. The workout equipment in the health club facilities were a little squished and I think I used the oldest still-working elliptical machine in North America. But the treadmills are all pretty new and most machines have a personal flat screen. However, that was completely made up for by the rest of the facilities - the pool, jacuzzi, sauna and spa look original and made me feel like some robber baron in the gilded age. The location is excellent for business in or near downtown and is right in the heart of the financial district. It could also be a good choice for tourists because it is so close to the 101, 110, 5 and 10 freeways, so you can pretty much get anywhere. Now for the bad things - all of which are relatively minor and would not stop me from booking here again. First, like many hotels, they charge for internet access, which I find a highly offensive practice. Also, valet is $40/night. This is not unusual in LA, but should be factored into your budget. The tub/shower had a curtain, rather than a door, which kept sticking to me because it didn't have magnets in the bottom. This was particularly gross since the housekeeping seemed hit or miss - I had 3 great days and 2 "eh" days. The TV in my room was an old, small CRT type and many of the channels buzzed or otherwise had bad reception. Finally, when I ordered room service breakfast, my receipt had the wrong name and room number on it. When I asked, the staff person told me "You must have written the wrong number on your ticket, this is for you." That was completely unacceptable at this level hotel. Even if I actually had made the mistake, I should have received "the customer is always right" treatment. But, like I said, I would definitely stay here again, it's a great hotel.

“Great for the family” We just returned from a 4-night stay at the Alex and were very pleased. We had a 2 bedroom suite with a full kitchen for the four of us--mom, dad, and 2 young boys. The room was well-maintained and had nice amenities: comfortable beds, nice toiletries, good showers and very quiet rooms. We were on the 28th floor overlooking the Chrysler Building, which was incredible. The location is perfect as well; close to lots of great restaurants & Grand Central Station and a relatively quiet street at night. The Perfect Pint next door was great for an easy family meal and the Amish market down the street had a wonderful selection of treats--lots of fresh produce, cheese, flat bread pizzas, etc. The staff at the Alex was very helpful and accommodating. The rooms had lots of storage space which was extremely helpful as we were not tripping over our bags. The bathrooms were also quite nice; clean and well-sized. A few slightly negative things about the Alex: it has a tiny lobby and you will wait for the elevator if it's busy. While the linens were lovely and the bed comfy, the furniture looks a tiny bit worn. In another year or two it will not look good at all. The furniture is modern but inexpensive-looking. I am a bit surprised that it is part of the Leading Hotels of the World-- I usually think of those as being more luxurious. But this is a very nice hotel and was perfect for our holiday in NY. I've stayed in several hotels in NYC and this was, by far, the best place to bring children, that was reasonably priced.

“This hotel is a hidden gem!” Was very pleasantly surprised by this hotel. In the heart of downtown philly within walking distance to the business, shopping and little italy districts. This small boutique style hotel also offered free internet/computer use, free breakfast and free fruit and snacks all day. Was worried about staying at this "no name" hotel but they staff was very helpful and the clean rooms came through with shinning colours. Please note that this hotel is in the heart of the gay community, a detail I did not see in any advertising.

“Great stay!” The Hilton is super close to the airport with excellent airport shuttle service. Hotel has two courtyards (one with the pool and the other that's more a garden & sitting area). Workout facility was great -- new equipment, large and clean. Breakfast was great - I got a coupon at check in for complimentary breakfast which was GREAT! Parking -- is $20/day and the garage is a long walk from the lobby. BUT it's safe & clean. Room was nicely decorated, flat screen tv, great ac/heat. Bathroom small but functional. Overall, a great experience.
“Comfortable rooms close to airport” Its a fifity years building, however rooms are comfortable, clean and completely refurbished. KIndly staff. Good service of buses to airport.

“Nice - like the other reviews say” I've stayed here a couple of times for work. Basically I sleep in the room and then go to/from work. The atmosphere is very nice and I try to stay here when I'm in town - but it is often full I find. Staff are friendly and gracious. Rooms are crisp and refreshingly Euro in decor - not your standard hotel stuff. The suites have amazing baths; the regular rooms have just OK baths (you'll wonder why people go on about the baths if you stay in a regular room on your first stay). It is interesting sorting through the various furnishings to find things like sewing kit - it is all there, just look :) Anyway I find it refreshing and fun and is my first pick of hotel in the Distric.

“Modern and Convenient” We upgraded to a larger room, which was very contemporary and nicely decorated - with views of both the Lake and the River. Beds were comfortable and there was a separate tub and shower. Larger room comes with concierge level access - breakfast choices were very nice and I like having coffee, water, soft drinks and snacks available all day long. The location was good - in the past I always stayed on No.Michigan Ave, but this was nice, too - and it was about a 10 minute walk to the Miracle Mile. Also a short walk to the pier for the Architectural Boat tour - which was our favorite part of this trip. Housekeeping never replenished the shampoo, conditioner, etc. - but it didn't really matter since I didn't like them anyway. I would definitely stay here again.

“Great staff, nice hotel and the best location” I booked this hotel mostly because i wanted to live in that area and there are not so many hotels there, atleast not with good rewiews. I took a single normal room and it was good. A little bit small but who cares. It was clean with a nice bathroom and TV. Breakfast was great in the lovely restaurant and the staff was very welcoming. Next time i come to New york i will defenetly stay there again

“Better than the reviews!” I had heard unfortunate things about this hotel from a colleague and from other Trip Advisor reviews, so my expectations were pretty low. I was very pleasantly surprised by my stay as a result. The grounds are beautiful and I enjoyed eating breakfast and lunch outside. My room was older, but it was very spacious (probably because I got an accessible room for some reason). The architecture was unique, rather than being a hotel that could have been plunked down in any city. The staff were helpful and funny. The chintz-explosion decor was not to my tastes, the Internet was so slow I didn't even pay to use it for most of my trip, and the rooms could use more power outlets in better places, but overall, the hotel was comfortable and quiet, the staff was excellent, and I had a wonderful few days in San Diego as a result. Tip: Walk over to the mall via the footbridge. From there you can catch public transport, watch a movie, have a meal, or just walk around and windowshop.

“Very Cool JW at LA Live” This is a terrific business hotel. Very clean and new. The rooms have cool furnishings. Bathrooms are large and have big showers with great tiling--not bathtub, which is very nice. Executive lounge is nice and well-located. Lobby is very LA and inviting. The staff were very helpful and friendly. The restaurant is excellent for a hotel restaurant. Very healthy (but satisfying) menu and a great wine list. There a number of very good restaurants right outside the back door of the hotel in the LA Live complex as well, including a great sushi place. Not a great hotel to walk around, but cabs are easy to get.

“Great Hotel for the Price” I stayed at the Hotel Fusion for five days booking through Hotwire for only $69 a night. I got much more for the $69 than I expected. I found the Hotel had been newly refurbished and very modern. The rooms are small but nicely updated and all have high speed internet that worked great. They offer a "mini" breakfast in the morning that consists of toast or bagels and jucie and coffee. There is no air conditioning but in San Francisco that really isnt much of an issue. The rooms do get a lot of noise from the streetcars and traffic but was no more than I would expect in a busy city. The location is excellent, being in the heart of Union Square. Overall this was an excellent value in a City where rooms can easily cost three times what I paid. I would stay there again without hesitation.

“Great!” Simply great. Clean, large hotel rooms with flat screen TVs, free internet (sign up for the selectguest program), polite staff. With the selectguest program you also get a free room service drink in the AM. Charge $2 for incoming faxes - if you need a boarding pass, print it for $1.25 from the business center, or just check in at the airport. The breakfast buffet and dinner selection is great as well. They are relatively isolated, but provide a shuttle to destinations within 5 miles. Otherwise, count on taxis to go anywhere significant.

“Great hotel, even better service!” I really love this hotel. It was my second time to stay here for a business function and this time I stayed for 5 nights. I love the rooms and the decor, but the main reason I am writing this review is to brag on the impeccable service. The staff bent over backwards to make sure my colleagues and I had a wonderful stay. They charged my cell phone for me and brought it back to me the next morning...exactly at the time the night manager said they would. They brought a gift I left in my car to the reception I was attending. They also brought me toothpaste and then followed up to make sure housekeeping brought it to me! It was an excellent stay and I would highly recommend this hotel for business or pleasure.

“Argonaut - Don't stay anywhere else” This is my 4th stay at a Kimpton Hotel in 10 mos. Kimpton is now my favorite hotel chain. Pros - location (on Beach Street and within walking distance to the Wharf, Ghiradelli Square, next to the Powell-Hyde cable car turnaround, across from the National Park San Francisco Wharf and the list goes on), clean, clean, clean rooms, very friendly staff especially the door men (thanks for the recommendation of Mama's on Washington Square), wine happy hour, spacious "living room" with many seating options, beautifully decorated lobby and rooms. Cons - we couldn't stay longer. We were extremely happy that our room was ready for us when we arrived at Noon. We had travelled to California wine country to celebrate our 50th bdays (a few friends) and a couple of us decided to also visit San Francisco. We walked everywhere and the Argonaut is definitely within walking distance (if you like to walk) to many sites. Thank you Kimpton and thank you Argonaut.

“Great location and room” OK so once you realise this is New York where everything is huge except the hotel rooms you are good to go. Loverly room, great location, wonderful shows, lots of interesting restaurants especially on 46th st. Coffee maker in room but when we took stuff out of the fridge to put our own in they left a note to say if we did it again we would be charged the cost do restocking it. Very strange, when we called housekeeping they said we could hire a fridge for $25. We agreed to do this as we were staying for 5 days and it was hot. Last morning they slid the account under the door and we noticed they had charged us for all the stuff we took out of their fridge and then replaced. Apparently the sensor sends an automatic charge to your account. When we challenged it they removed it. Apart from that it was a great stay

“Amazing location!” My husband and I stayed here for one night on Labour Day weekend. Our one night was wonderful and would definitely recommend it. Excellent location - walking distance to Times Square and Central Park. Check-in was very efficient, and the rooms were bigger than expected and plush. Toiletries were by l'Occitaine. Big bathroom with a shower and a tub. My favorite part of the hotel was the lobby. Wonderfully done, and a nice oasis from the busy streets of New York. Other than the absent doorman/busboy service when we arrived (arond 11pm), our stay was wonderful. Happy travels!

“Ultra-sleek hotel in San Francisco's Union Square” Pros: -Great location - right in the middle of Union Square -Ultra-sleek, hip decor; lots of marble, water features, Japanese decor, orchids, stone, glass, etc. -Upscale bar with friendly bartenders, Japanese beer and sake -Tastefully-decorated rooms, glass-walled marble shower, plenty of counter space, wall-mounted blow-dryer, etc. -On-site valet parking available -Knowledgeable and friendly concierge - great suggestions for lunch, dinner, entertainment, etc. Cons: -NOT cheap! -depending on the room, some are very small for the price -lots of bums in Union Square; never-ending panhandling

“Nice, Funky Renovated Hotel Centrally Located” I really love this property. I like it's sort of funky 50's architecture yet I could tell that it's been totally redone. I travel a lot for work and have stayed almost everywhere in San Diego. This is really good value for the money I can tell you. No, it's not the W or the Westgate, or any number of 4 and 5 star properties, but it's not supposed to be. What it is, however, is among the best in class and a comfortable and well located property that is worth a (repeat) stay. As a walker who loves to just take off for a couple hours and detox from the office, this is a superb location. Any direction you go you'll hit something of interest. There is also a great little deli and sundries store across the street sort of hidden that is a great place for snacks, water, wine etc.

“My pick of the litter for a clean, comfortable midrange DC hotel” In the past year or so, I have had many trips to DC. The Doubletree provided a recently renovated, well furnished room in a reasonably convenient location. The quality was a cut below the JW Marriott and Westin Alrlington, a bit better than the Washington Plaza, Beacon, and Hyatt Arlington, much better than the Kalorama Guest House, and vastly superior to the Inns of Virginia in Arlington and the Hotel Harrington. Would definitely stay here again. Location: On Rhode Island Avenue near Massachusetts Avenue and 15th Street. This Scott Circle hotel is a 10 minute walk to the Metro stations at Dupont Circle and at Farragut West. Walk to Dupont Circle or take a taxi up to Adams Morgan for many interesting dining options. Or wander a block over to the Whole Foods on P Street. Room: Immaculate and recently refurbished medium sized room with a very comfortable bed, workable desk, large flat screen TV, sitting chair, coffee service. Bathroom was spotless if a bit small. Service: Friendly and efficient front desk staff at check in and check out. Staff were happy to offer advice on touring, transport and other local lore. I did not check out exercise and other commons or the on premises restaurant. The warm cookie on check in is a nice standard Doubletree touch. Cost: Superb value when booked via Priceline.

“really nice stay” We stayed in room 2805 this past wekend for my husband's birthday. It was nice the check in was friendly and quick. We swung around the block and by the time we got upstairs the luggage was in the in room. The view was ok Millenium Park and Lake south view. The room was modern clean and large. The Bathroom is nice large tub seperate shower and the WC is in it's own closet. The bed was comfortable enough and the sheets were nice the temp of the room was consistent. Housekeeping did a great job all of our requests were accomodated. They have several tv channels and that is nice while you are laying around relaxing. Only one thing that was not 100% was one of the mattresses had quite a dip in the middle. That was the only negative. Our bellman leaving was so nice very helpful. I really love this hotel, they even left a b-day cake in the room for my Husband's B-day. Room service is still reasonable, they are now 100% non smoking which is nice for some not for others...I do like it as a former smoker. I really enjoy this hotel it has a nice feel and I am sure I will be back.

“Very nice hotel - bed was hard as a rock...” We made an impromptu visit to El Paso and decided to stay here. The rooms were nice and clean. We asked for a crib for our son and it was quickly delivered and was very nice. The biggest complaint was a rock-hard bed. I noticed something at the front desk that stated the mattresses had some kind of adjustment devices but I could not find it and did not bother to look again or ask, so I maybe could have something about it. The breakfast was delightful and reasonably priced at about $11/person (our son is 2 and ate for free). I asked the chef for some hot sauce other than Tabasco, and he gave me some of his own green sauce and it was excellent!! We did get a USA Today delivered to our room. There were fresh baked cookies and complementary coffee at the front desk the night we arrived as well. Overall, an excellent stay.

“Wonderful Location” The hotel is in the perfect location if you want to be in Back Bay. It is connected to the Prudential Center and in the middle of Copley Square and Back Bay, with easy walking access to Newbury Street for shopping, Boylston for nightlife, and though a bit of a hike, walkable to Fenway, the theater district and Boston Commons. If you put your sneakers on, you can take a half hour walk to Faneiul Hall. The room itself was standard business class - clean, comfortable and spacious. The room lacks anything jawdropping or romantic. It is more for the business traveler with conservative, luxurious decor. The beds were comfortable and the view was poor, but if you want to feel comfortable in a clean, well maintained hotel, this is perfect for you. The bathrooms were mediocre, no granite or marble... I didnt have to wear shower shoes, but I didnt exactly feel like the shower was sparkling. The lobby was always super busy, and cans are lined out front all the time. Insider's tip - if you want to take the T, walk through the Prudential Center to Boylston and you wont have to go outside... Perfect tip in the rain. I would stay here again.

“Great service, old-world charm” My husband and I stayed at the Waldorf during the NYC marathon since we found a great rate ($275/night) by booking nearly a year in advance on the hotel's website. We loved the attentive service, and especially appreciated the free upgrade to a larger King room. The quality of the service and the history put this hotel in the 5-star category. However, we've stayed in hotels with nicer rooms in 4-star hotels. We recommend the Bear & the Bull bar for a nightcap. The bartenders were hilarious & very attentive. Be prepared to spend $30-40 for two drinks (unless you are drinking the $6 pints of beer). We would definitely stay at the Waldorf if we found another great rate, but there's no way we would pay the going rate of $700/night.

“Good value” My 2nd stay here for four nights in early November. If you are thinking of booking this hotel do so through Hotwire - it comes up as a 3.5* - that is the clue. I paid $66 (inclusive) per night and that was a real steal. Sure they get you back by charging $12 for car parking and $10 for the internet but its worth it. The hotel itself is fine. Its laid out round the pool and and another courtyard and is 'motel' type with open corridors to the courtyards. The pool looked a bit small for the size of hotel and the separate spa is inconvenient - but its minor. Overall its not quite up to the normal very high standard of the Crowne Plaza brand but its fine and, at the rate, a real steal. The internet worked well. The small gym is adequate with 2 x-trainers, two joggers and two bikes with a small weight machine. Its clean and the kit is in good condition. The hotel is slightly isolated so its eating on-site or driving. Nothing in walking distance as far as I can tell. The on-site sushi restaurant was fine if a bit pricey and my pasta dish in the main restaurant was surprisingly good. There is a good value coffee and bagels outlet in the morning for those who don't want the full buffet breakfast. To address some of the criticisms in the other reviewers. I personally didn't have the 'battlefield' noise experience of others but it certainly got noticeably noisier over the weekend (with slammed doors and kids running in the corridor) as it filled up - despite being in the quieter rear of the hotel. It worked well as a base for the San Diego area and for the conference downtown (15 mins on the freeway even at peak times) where the going room rate was circa $300 per night. I'd certainly recommend it the hotel and will have no hesitation in re-booking.

“Great location but....” Great location. Excellent restaurant. Had to call for housekeeping every day - and i was in a suite. One day, room had not been cleaned by 5 pm. Drives me nuts. Rooms near elevator are torture chambers as noise is awful. Zippo water pressure in showers. Front desk and valet staff are wonderful. Balcony on second floor is marvelous at any time of day. Club breakfast is excellent. With a few tweaks this could be a great hotel.

“The Best for a Girls Spa Getaway” 4 ladies in our mid thirties booked this for a spa getaway and we had the best time. The room was fabulous and the private spa area pool was the best - uncrowded and so relaxing. We booked a suite that was 2 rooms (with seperate entrances) adjoining a suite living area in the middle. We had sleeping for 8 even though we only had 4. There was an extra bed that folds out in the suite area. The suite area also had a full bath, so we had 3 bathrooms total. Full dining table and living area plus a kitchenette. We booked the spa package where the room rate each day includes a spa treatment and access to the spa area for the whole day. This is an area away from the main pool areas, no kids, complete relaxation. The spa treatments are top notch and the smoothies served at the pool are so yummy. We stayed 3 nights and only went to the main pool area one day. The main pool area is nice too, but just not as tranquil and relaxing. The hotel is away from everything so you will need a car if you want to venture out. Overall I love this Hotel and would go back tomorrow!

“Elegant on a human scale in NYC” I am always happy when I sleep well in the bustling city, and at French Quarters I could really relax. The rooms are elegant yet homey, with a great breakfast and excellent service.

“Wonderful Weekend in Memphis” My 2 younger sisters and I recently stayed at the Residence Inn to celebrate my sister's 28th birthday weekend. She's always wanted to go to Graceland so off to Memphis we went. The staff at the Residence Inn was beyond accomodating, they did every little thing to make our stay as wonderful as possible - arraging for our Graceland tour within minues of inquirying and offering off local spots to eat as opposed to the touristy locations. My favorite part about the Residence Inn was the comforts of home that are found in the room. We had a studio suite with more than enough room for 3 women to shower and get dressed without ever being in each other's way. The kitchen and dining room are things that you think you don't need on vacation but that totally amplify the comfort levels of your stay. We found ourselves on more than one occassion saying "lets go back home" because that's how it felt like - home. The free hot breakfast and all their selections were such a great way to start our morning and the free DVD rental was a nice way to end our evenings. We would head back to the hotel and unwind with a movie and popcorn just as if we were at home. Location was fab, a trolley stop directly out front on Main Street, ATM across the street, Walgreens a block away, 8 min walk to the Peabody Ducks and 15 min to Beale Street and 20 min cab ride to the airport. We couldn't of asked for better. Nothing but rave reviews for the Residence Inn Downtown Memphis!

“Very pleased” Stayed here one night for a meeting at the hotel, I arrived early afternoon on the day prior so had a fair amount of time in the hotel. Check in was very smooth. As a Platinum member , was given a nice room with view on high floor. Lobby was very nice, very open feeling yet had lounge and restaurant areas. There were plenty of seating areas and many had their own TV's. Sitting downstairs for a beer and chatting with friends was very comfortable. Room size was reasonably good and better than expected for a city hotel in DC. Bed was comfortable. Bathroom was ok size but for one it was plenty. Amenities were modern. It was obvious this was updated and still looked good. Had hotel food for meeting including breakfast and lunch, both meals were above average. Check out was the only glitch, there was a long wait to check out with only 2 people at desk. Either they were slow and had trouble keeping up or there was an onslaught of people all at once. However i had no problems related to stay so I used express check out which worked fine and was quick. Getting a cab was easy. Also this hotel is about 1-2 blocks (easy walk even with roller board) from Union train station. I flew in to BWI and getting to hotel via train was easy. I returned via Regan Airprort which was 20 minute cab ride including traffic. All in all, a very nice stay and would definitely come again. Seemed higher scale then a traditional Hyatt Regecy, perhaps bordering on Grand.

“Just wonderful” Couldnt agree more with what everyone else has already written here. A true gem in Boston, not least due to the great service, and wonderful rooms. Not a huge fan of the Mooo breakfast - unappetizingly large portions of average food at very high prices. But the hotel itself: Just Wonderful.

“Really Good Hotel” Stayed at Le Meridien this week on a business trip and I was very impressed. Check in was quick, room on the 17th floor was large, clean, modern with a wonderful view. The bathroom was quite large and the bed was a king. I'd stay there again in a heartbeat. Plenty of power outlets and internet connection was easy. Location was quite favorable as well. Found the staff to be very friendly and they served free, good coffee in the lobby!

“You won't regret booking a suite” We stayed here for 2 weeks and I have to say that the room was spacious, quiet and kept clean. The staff were really nice and solved a problem I had on the very first night. The staff are caring and would always give advice with a smile. Being on I-35 makes it easy to get to virtually anywhere in Austin or head South towards San Marcos and San Antonio. A lot of restaurants, a Wal-mart and Austin's Airport are all just a few minutes drive away. There is an indoor swimming pool which I never used. A bit far out of downtown, but 10 - 15 minutes drive will land you right in the middle of the busy night life. All in all, this is a great place to stay and would recommend it for any Austin visitor.

“good location for driving but not walking” this is a nice hotel, looks to be newly renovated. welcoming lobby area, nice cocktail lounge (not a bar, as it is more cozy and warm looking). Located just off I25 on Colorado Ave., which is a very busy street and not one you want to cross to get to the other side. Not much in the area to walk to anyway, but with a car, the places you can go are very accessible. The highway is just down the street, which can get you downtown quickly as long as you don't hit rush hour. Colorado takes you to the museum, zoo and taking a turn down 17th takes you to numerous good restaurants as well as downtown. Cherry Creek mall and the lovely shopping streets of Cherry Creek are just a ways down Colorado. Hotel rooms are nicely done, comfortable beds, nice breakfast buffet in the AM till 10. Would definitely stay again as it is very convenient to get to and from. Oh, and this is a big one, parking is free.

“Cosmo Scores Again” This is the fourth or fifth time I've stayed at the Cosmo, and it was once again a pleasure. Immaculately clean as always. Great friendly staff (though not too informed about the free wifi -- and now that they have the wifi, the place is even better than before). Great location. Only caveats: the elevator has gotten slower than ever -- one night it took more than two minutes to get to the sixth floor, and some street noise. Everything I want in a hotel when I go to NY.

“Excellent and Quirky” The George is a nice and fun boutique hotel. My room was quite nice: It was fairly large, had a nice and large bathroom, and had the usual Kimpton touchs(eg, leopard bathrobes). My room service meal was unusually good.
