The staff was attentive and friendly too. One tip: go online to join the Kimpton Loyalty Program prior to checking in. By doing so, you will revive free Internet plus $10 worth of minibar items.

“Great location terrible beds” Could not ask for a better location right on the water front with great pool and dining options in and around the hotel Balcony rooms overlooking bay are fantastic EXCEPT whoever purchased the beds needs to visit a Westin whilst the bathroom for such a large bedroom was terribly laid out

“Great service - facility still needs some work” I came close to giving this hotel an overall average rating - but the friendly service of the front-desk staff kicked it up to a very good rating for me. The hotel has some deficiencies - first, it is not really a "full service" hotel like other Hilton properties. There is no valet and if they have luggage service I did not see it. To me, this service level is no different than one of their Garden Inn properties. Second - The facility is older and needs some upgrades. They are working on remodeling the check-in area but the whole lobby area is disjointed and doesn't flow smoothly. There really is no lobby in the normal sense and the main entrance felt to me like a side entrance. Third - the business center is very unusually located in the bar area with no privacy and the the internet was not working the one time I used the system to print boarding passes. On the positive side, the front desk was very friendly and accomodating - one example, they printed my boarding pass when the business center computers were down. Also, the rooms have recently been remodeled and the housekeeping was really excellent each night. Everything in the room was very nice - with the exception of the main and bathroom doors which still have the early-80s fake wood look on the doors - which did not match the rooms at all. Also, the elevators need upgraded - they are very slow and you feel every little bump and motor noise as they seem to struggle to operate. The restaurant and meeting rooms seem like a long walk away from the front. The restuarant - though isolated - had a decent breakfast but that is the only meal I ate there. Overall, I got a discounted rate and therefore felt the value was pretty good but this hotel would be a disappointment if paying the normal $200+ rates Hilton charges for their full service properties. Finally, I have to disagree with some other reviewers about the great "location." Most of the shopping and dining are a good 10-15 minute drive east on Westheimer and all other things being equal - I would recommend staying at one of the many hotels just minutes from the Galleria and most of the restuarants also.

“Just Plain Cool - Not Your Father's Hotel” Everyone at the hotel is very friendly. The waitstaff at Dragonfly were exceptional - made my clients feel like they were the only ones there. Rooms are very big w/ funky furnishings....not a boring old hotel room with drab carpet and cookie-cutter furniture.... Bathroom great - shower is awesome. Fitness center is top notch....Shuttle service is great to Downtown - even the shuttle is cool with steer horns on the hood. Got an upgrade once to a "Magnificent Seven" room - too bad I was by myself on business because I could have thrown a party in the room it was so big! I travel very often - This is as good as an in-town hotel gets......

“Convenient for JHU, exorbitant parking rates” The location right next to the Johns Hopkins campus is convenient, if that's where you want to be. It's just a few blocks walk (to the south east) to a small college town neighborhood with some stores and basic eateries. The rooms are entirely fine, and the staff was helpful. Free wifi is always a plus. My only complaint was the exorbitant parking rates.

“I'd go back.” Note...if you are a member of Hotels.com, I've posted this review there, as well. We went to the Rafaello for Labor Day weekend. We were there a few years ago after their renovation, so we knew it was nice. We had a smaller (standard) room this time, but it was still well-appointed. The bed was very comfortable and I liked the little space between the bath and the bedroom for the mini-bar and dressing area. Other things I like: wonderful Gilchrest and Soames bath products! I liked that they didn't skimp and give you 2:1 shampoo:conditioner - I hate that. Towels were o.k., and we had plenty. For a four star hotel, we did not receive any additional amenities such as a shower cap or mending kit, however. The t.v. was great and we got an upgraded cable package with AMC and extra channels. Temperature was easy to control in the room and did not drift (which is sometimes a problem).

“Great service in a busy environment” For my Zero year birthday this year I treated myself to the spa suite at the Alexis. The room was very spacious with a nice view of Puget Sound. The staff was on top of everything, including getting me extra dog bowls for my three travel companions. When a mechanical failure happened to the AC in the room the front desk staff handled the problem quickly and always with a smile and honest information about what was going on. They took the time to explain what happened, how long it would take to get the problem resolved. I enjoyed working with the concierge to find local eating and entertainment. This hotel is just blocks from the warf and new Seattle Ferris Wheel. Lots to do within walking distance.

“Don’t judge a book by the cover” The Wharf Inn perfectly fit our needs for a two-night stay in the city. The location in the heart of Fisherman’s Wharf combined with free, on-site parking was the ultimate in convenience. Don’t judge a book by the cover: the classic motor lodge building exterior is dated and initially a bit worrying; however our room was recently renovated, clean and bright. Though it may be a no frills motel, it met all of our needs for a short stay. And perhaps we were fortunate with the location of our room, but did not experience the noise issues noted in other reviews (our room opened to the interior parking area and not the street-facing side of the building). If you need standard accommodations in Fisherman's Wharf at a reasonable price with on-site parking and a location convenient to restaurants, shopping and attractions, the Wharf Inn should definitely be considered.

“Old world traditional value but misses on the room” Growing up in NYC I always wanted to stay at the Waldorf, my parents always preferred St. Regis; now I know why. The Waldorf lobby is spot on old world tradition, dark wood, high ceilings, lots of staff to assist, seemless check in. Things change after you proceed to your room, unless you're staying in the towers you will be in a seemingly old room. Once you start down the hall from the elevator you'll notice that feeling of the lobby is stripped away and nothing stands out. The rooms are well appointed, flat screen, very comfortable bed, nice bathroom. But the everything else is old, I had to put a towel under the front door because of the large gap that allowed hallway noise; they need to replace the doors and get new wallpaper. The shower was narrow and took a bit of manuevering to not to have water hitting you in the face.

“Best Choice Near LAX” I've stayed at a number of the three and four star hotels near LAX and the Westin seems to be the best choice in the area. Room was quiet and clean, bed was comfortable, lobby and amenities were good as well. If you need to overnight near LAX this is a solid choice for an airport property.

“Great hotel, amazing location!” I've stayed at this hotel 5-6 times now, and every time is great. The location is perfect - right on the edge of Center Prak. It's a short walk to some of the big attractions in the city, and the subway is nearby if you want to travel further. The rooms are good size for NYC and clean. The beds are very comfortable as well. The only thing I wouldn't recommend is the breakfast, which is overpriced.

“Urban hotel in downtown Boston” The Onyx is one of the Kimpton hotels and while it was nice, it wasn't my favorite. Situated on a street lined with brick buildings and close to restaurants it was an urban stopover for our group. The lounge is a signature red but in the daytime its a little brash. The rooms were well appointed but very small. The staff had their smiles on but we didn't have a sense of any warmth from them. Overall, it was certainly an upscale hotel, but I wouldn't stay long at this one.

“Great stay for a couple of days on business” We stayed here for business at the Dallas Market Center, which is a short walk from the hotel. The rooms are comfortable and clean as all the reviews say, as well as large and well-appointed (love the Aveda products). The direct area is not really walkable to bars or restaurants, and taxis are quite expensive in Dallas so rent a car if you can ($20 fare to anywhere close and almost $60 to the airport). The staff are excellent, and check-in was fast and friendly. The bar and restaurant is also quite nice directly off the lobby, and we had lunch and drinks there each night. Overall a nice stay, I would give it a 4.5/5.

“Most Pet Friendly Hotel :)” I can't say enough wonderful things about this place! I stayed here last weekend as well as in December and each time was better than the last. This time in particular I brought my puppy. The staff was all so wonderful with him even offereing to walk him. The room had dog bowls and a dog bed upon arrival and they don't charge any extra for bringing him. I can't say enough great things about this place. They just opened the restaurant, I ordered room service from there and it was great. This hotel really does everything right to make your stay as wonderful as possible not to mention the views from your room are breathtaking. One bit of advice: The hotel charges $55 for valet, on 49th street half a block away there's a parking lot that's only $20 a day :) This is my new go to place while in NYC esp if I bring my dog :)

“Good location and functional rooms” I stayed at Club Quarters for about 2 nights in July 2011. The location was great - close to major subway, tourist sites, shops and restaurants. Rooms were pleasant and spacious - clean and comfortable. I like the fact that there is a water dispenser for guests to help themselves with water but there is no fridge in the room. Price of stay was reasonable.

“Perfect location, great room, bad view” My daughter and I had the rare chance to fly to Chicago for a night and chose the Conrad since we are Hilton Honors Silver members. The room was comfortable and clean with lovely robes, slippers, complimentary tea and coffee in the lobby, and cozy bedding. The location was wonderful and it was convenient to be situated on top of a shopping mall with a Nordstrom, cafes and nice shops. Our only complaint was the terrible view of nearby office windows and rooftops, with absolutely no glimpse of the city from our room. We could have been anywhere. The hotel did not seem to be crowded, so I'm surprised we were not assigned a room with a better view. I have found that when it comes to the Conrads, our Hilton status does not seem to matter and is never acknowledged (which is not true of our other hotel memberships--something I will remember in the future). To be fair, when I mentioned the poor view in a random follow-up survey, management responded instantly and kindly offered an upgrade in the future. But unfortunately, while that response was appreciated, I can't imagine I would ever be traveling to Chicago again, since this was my first visit in 25 years. Overall though, it was a beautiful hotel and we had a great stay--while keeping our shades tightly closed.

“Excellent value, excellent service” I just spent the weekend with high school friends at the Nine Zero. It was fantastic! The location allowed us to walk virtually everywhere. The staff was efficient and helpful. They offer wine and cheese in the lobby from 5-7, which is a nice touch. The queen room was comfortable for all 4 of us. Loved the zebra robes! The only very small complaint is that the bathroom fan didn't work.

“great price, location, staff...” I thoroughly enjoyed my mid week 3 night stay here...single female...felt safe...fun happy hour each evening, excellent 'real' breakfast...at the price, it's hard to be critical but if pressed, i'd say the room was a bit small and the shower perfect for a 5'5" person!

“Good Value for a Boutique Hotel in Downtown Chicago” I stayed at Hotel Allegro Chicago one night recently for business and pleasure. The lobby which is actually a floor up from the street is very warm and elegant. The front desk staff was friendly and courteous. The King Premiere room was actually large. The bathroom with the toilet, however, was one of the tiniest hotel bathrooms I had ever seen. The room strangely had another bathroom with a large tub and shower without a toilet on the other side of the room that was much larger. The bed easily fit my 6'2" frame and was comfortable. Not a bad view out the two large windows. There was a nice flat screen and an Ipod alarm clock. I would stay there again.

“Excellent Hotel” We stayed at the Westin St. Francis for three nights. The location on Union Square is perfect. The hotel is gorgeous. Our room was located in the newer Tower section. It was very large and the beds were so comfortable! The bathroom was large with luxurious shower products provided. We ordered room service for breakfast one morning, and it arrived quickly and was delicious. Our room had a coffee maker with Starbucks coffee. There was a large screen plasma TV, large closet with plenty of hangers, and plenty of drawer space. The concierge was as nice as can be, and he was very helpful. In the morning there was always a very long line for the concierge, but the excellent service made the wait worthwhile. All of the staff were friendly and efficient. There are many great restaurants in walking distance, as well as amazing shopping.

“Superb hotel in excellent location” Stayed here for one night and really enjoyed it - fantastic location on Madison and 31st, very nice room, and an excellent shower and bathroom. Highly recommended. If I'm being ultra-critical the room might have been a bit small for two people, but this is New York and that's kind of to be expected. Room was perhaps a touch too dark also, but I find that a lot in hotel rooms. The hotel is very nicely designed with a sleek lobby and I also appreciated that the staircase was very nice and accessible, meaning it wasn't always necessary to take the lift if you want a bit of exercise. Service was good too. And free wi-fi, which is always great.

“Sophisticated urban getaway with impeccable service” My husband & I are both originally from the Bay Area yet we have lived in Lake Tahoe for over 10 years. Now & again we make a weekend trip to SF to get some City life & escape the mountains. in any case, we booked a quick overnighter to the Intercontinental due to a great rate we found from Travel Zoo. We were celebrating my birthday & our first night away together since having our son, in June 2009. From the moment we checked in to the moment we departed our experience was excellent. The front desk gal was friendly, warm & conversational & upgraded our room to a junior suite when she found out about our 'dual celebrations'. This was very thoughtful of her. We were pleased with our corner room, enveloped in windows & views. The room was clean, contemporary & spacious, with great a/v & plush bedding. We grabbed a drink at the downstairs lounge & the bartender was also very friendly. My husband surprised me by arranging a massage and facial at the I Spa. My massage was nice and my facial (with Valerie) was outstanding-- the best I've ever had. She did an excellent job exfoliating my skin, talked to me about what I needed to do to get my skin healthier and recommended some products (which have worked very well!). She even gave me her card at the end of the facial and said to call any time with questions. We had a memorable celebration due largely to the Intercontinental Hotel having staff who are kind, courteous and knowledgeable in their respective roles. The only slight negative is the parking charge. I believe we paid $64, which seems a bit unreasonable. Other than that, lovely hotel.

“Lovely hotel - despite some problems” The Fairfax is a small European style hotel that competes with the Jefferson and the Hay Adams. It is enjoyable to stay at despite some draw backs. As the name implies, it is just off DuPont circle and surrounded by embassies. This makes it a fun neighborhood to walk around in. The hotel's lobby is quite small but there is a nice bar a few steps off the lobby that serves as a meeting place. The front desk staff is insanely good. They went above and beyond on every issue. Not the phony Ritz Carlton concern. I really felt they took ownership of my problems (both of which were of my own making). The same is true of the bellman, and this is the kind of hotel where you feel awkward if you don't use a bellman, plus there are a couple of staIrs to get to the elevator. I would recommend you try to avoid a queen sized bed, even if you are a single. The queen rooms are tiny and the bathroom is silly small. It is so small that there is no place to put a waste basket and, I suspect, anyone over six feet tall would be unable to comfortably sit on the toilet. There are three things that drive me nuts about hotels as a frequent business traveler, and all three are present at the Fairfax. First is the lack of electric sockets. The only socket is in the lamp on the tiny little desk. So if you use that for your laptop, you have no place else to plug in your phone (and in my case, a CPAP). To access another socket requires moving the bed and unplugging a lamp. Would it kill hotels to supply a power strip? The second is the tiny little print on identical looking bottles of shampoo, conditioner, lotion and body wash. Most people dont wear glasses into the shower. The third is paying for wifi (although the Fairfax's charge is cheap at $9.95 and the wifi is pretty fast). I had occasion to eat breakfast in the 2100 Prime restaurant (used to be The Jockey Club), lunch in the bar and dinner at 2100. All were excellent and not too expensive by Washington standards. But, all in, the quality of the people who work at the Fairfax exceeds any of the other problem, and I look forward to staying again

“Great location and nice hotel - Better for business than lesuire” We stayed at the hyatt for a week at the end of April / beginning of may. The rooms were nice and very spacious. It was really nice having a balcony and being able to sit out in the morning (Poolside rooms get sun in the aftenoon road side get sun in the morning). All the staff we came into contact with were very polite and helpful. There was a big conference on whilst we were there but it didnt affect us in any way. The shopping centre is only a 2 minute walk, lots of restaurants and shops and it is really nice having somewhere you can walk to (especially in LA). Only downside is the pool gets shaded in the afternoon (from about 3 onwards so sitting out in the sun is a monring only option. Valet parking was not cheap ($35 per day) but always efficient and not bad for beverly hills!!!!

“Perfect Location” My family of 4 stayed at this hotel for 4 days at the end of August and found it to be great. The positives 1)Great location at the heart of everything 2)Rooms were nice and view was stunning from the high floor we stayed on 3)Excellent dining choices, including the Palm Steakhouse. Also, for an inexpensive breakfast choice an Au Bon Pan is connected to the hotel. 4) Swiming pool and workout room were excellent 5) Staff was helpfull The Negative 1) Parking was $40/day at the hotel. We parked instead across the street at the 100 Claredon garage for $28 All in all a great city hotel where location, location, location is the most important thing. A few extras: Dining - Summer Shack for Seafood and the Palm for Steak Touring - Take the Fenway Park tour and walk Newbury Street Taxis - A taxi is sometimes about the same price as the subway for a short trip.

“Very convenient” This is your basic bargain hotel, The location is fantastic, with a streetcar stop right outside the hotel that will you get you to anywhere you would want to go downtown, for $1 a ride. The room rate was NOT a bargain, but I think that's because I was there for "Memphis in May", which is the local high season for tourism. The public areas of the hotel are clean and modern and pleasant, apparently very recently renovated. We chose a room in the "historic Kress building" because they're supposed to be bigger, but this wasn't really a plus. It was large with a high ceiling, but it's not really a suite - there's no door between the sleeping and living areas. There is an old standard (not flat screen) TV that swivels so it can be seen from either part of the "suite." The living area kind of dwarfed the furniture - a small loveseat and two chairs, and a simple desk. The "kitchen" area included a mini-fridge, a microwave, and a coffee maker, with no dishes and only enough coffee to make one cup. (It was dreadful.) The room was a little tired, with cracked bathroom floor tiles, some crud oozing from the shower safety bar, and so forth, but over all it was adequate and quiet with comfortable beds. The guy who checked us at the front desk managed to not say a SINGLE word to us until he handed us the keys and told us where the elevator was - so obviously we had to figure out for ourselves that breakfast was included in the rate. The breakfast itself was pretty good, with eggs, sausage, bacon, biscuits, bagels, cereal, sweet rolls, juice, and all that - other than the crumbly scrambled eggs and weak coffee, it was really quite good. Kevin at the front desk (NOT the guy who checked us in) was incredibly helpful and friendly, and called a ride for us to the airport that worked out great. All in all, there's no reason not to stay here, as long as you're not expecting the Ritz.

“Please with the hotel property and the location, not the internet or food” I stayed at the Courtyard Chicago Downtown/River North for nine nights while at a conference, with a couple of extra days for fun. For the most part I was very pleased and thought about giving it five stars. A few minor irritations prevented me. First, the good: The location was great for nightlife, restaurants, and getting around Chicago. I had no problem walking to various train stations to get around the city, and the hotel is a two minute walk from Michigan Avenue and only slightly further to the Loop. The hotel was immaculate and my room cleaned quite well every day. The front desk staff was helpful and friendly, as were the bellhops and housekeeping staff. Perhaps the best part was the room itself was super quiet; I could not near my neighbors at all, which is rare. I really appreciated that! The bed was also very comfortable! You should sleep very well here. The not so good: The internet is incredibly slow, as other reviewers have stated. There were times it was so slow it was unusable. When I needed to get some work done and answer some emails, I found this very aggravating. Another irritation was I had a daily credit at the State State Bread Company on site. The food there is very average, although there is also a Starbucks. When I checked out, at first the credit had not been applied to my room. It is a good thing I looked closely to make sure they applied it to my bill. None of the front desk clerks were very knowledgeable about the credit. I think they should be taught all the various special rates available online to help them answer questions and make checkout smoother. The people working at the State Street Bread Company all seemed unhappy to be there, and on the weekend they are very slow--don't waste your time there, get out and find something yummier and cheaper (or at least yummier!). The hotel was expensive but in line with other prices in Chicago. I would consider staying here again, but only for a pleasure trip when I do not need the internet very much.

“Great hotel” From the comfortable rooms, internet access, to the staff and the excellent breakfasts. Nothing bad to say about this place. Exceeded my expectations and a joy of a place to stay for business.

“Lovely Hotel with great staff” I really loved this hotel, the location was great - right slap bang in the middle of Fishermans Wharf, just across the road from Ghirardelli Square. We were warned away from staying in the wharf as it is so touristy so we were slightly worried before we got there but no need, the Wharf IS full of tourists but then so is most of SF! We felt like there was plenty to do in the area plus we felt safe there too. The Argonaut was beautiful, the room was spacious and cleaned to perfection everyday. We had everything we could possibly need, coffee maker, toiletries, iron, ironing board etc etc. The staff were super helpful & very well informed. The only problem is the restaurant attached to the hotel, which in my opinion is awful and really lets down the Argonaut. We had dinner & breakfast in the restaurant and both times had to send some of the food back, as did a lot of people we noticed. The are plenty of other places to eat though in the Wharf so there is not need to eat in the hotel restaurant anyway. I would really recommend the restaurant opposite to the Argonaut, also Ciopinos is great too.

“Elegant hotel” Stayed at this hotel for a wedding. While the hotel is older, that doesn't mean you lose out on any luxurys. The staff was helpful (though they charged us $20 for an "upgrade" because they did not have the room we ordered ready). The hotel is really elegant, albeit "old", but you will enjoy the throwback. the piano playing is a wonderful touch. probably would choose to stay in a "newer" hotel (like the Hyatt Regency) but really did enjoy our stay here.

“Service makes it # 1” We recently spent one night at the Lenox Hotel after a fall foliage trip through New England. I see now why everyone rates this hotel #1 in Boston! From the moment we stopped our car at the door, we were greeted as though we were special guests of this lovely establishment. The doorman, Peter, was extremely gracious and helpful and set the bar high for the service to follow. Well, the bar never dipped and everyone we encountered during our stay was extremely friendly, always helpful, and NEVER too busy to attend to our needs. We were upgraded to a junior suite which was a fabulous corner room with 2 beds that were absolutely some of the most comfortable I have every slept in. The room was very spacious and the cold bottled water waiting for us in the fridge was a nice welcome. Other hotels could learn a great deal from this establishment. I highly recommend spending a few extra dollars when in Boston and stay at the Lenox. You won't be sorry!!!!!!!!!!!

“Good deal if staying near airport” I thought the Doubletree was an above average airport hotel. My friend and I always judge a hotel by a number of factors and the Doubletree scored well for water pressure, room space, temp control (how well the AC works), beds & bonus points for a warm cookie on check in! The only issue I really had was that our room was sooooooo far away. We got in at midnight from our flight and then had to drag our luggage (well technically the bell hop did most of the dragging but still) the very last room in the very last building. That aside, everything else was more that sufficient. Oh yeah, we also didn't like the fact that for $1 the vending machine gave you a teeny tiny dasani! But for the price I paid on Priceline, I would absolutely stay here again if I needed to be near the airport.

“Great hotel in good location” This is a great hotel in an ideal location for exploring San Francisco being next to the Embarcadero opposite the ferry terminal. When I checked into the hotel I was given a free room upgrade to a room with a view of the bay bridge, the reason they gave for the upgrade was that I was stopping for 11 nights and so I deserved a better room than the one I booked which was a nice touch. The room itself was big and clean. Unlike other reviewers I found that there was ample space for my 11 night’s worth of clothes although I did have to ask for extra coat hangers. The room is turned down nightly when chocolates, water, ice and a weather forecast for the next day are provided. The room also has free internet access but if have left your laptop at home there is a business centre in the hotel which has PC's connected to the internet. The only problem I had with the room was the noise from the street which was noticeable until about one in the morning. The hotel is also convenient for public transport with the F line tram stopping outside the hotel, a number of buses also stop outside the hotel and the California line cable car is about 2 blocks from the hotel. For those visiting San Francisco for the first time here are a few tips. 1. The California line cable car stops in the middle of nowhere. 2. If you want to get the cable cars from Union Square then if you do not want to queue then get there before 9am or after 5pm 3. A visit to Sausalito is well worth it and it is cheaper on the ferry from the ferry building (which is opposite the hotel) than from Pier 41. 4. If you plan to use the cable cars or public transport then consider a Muni pass as this can prove to be a lot cheaper than paying for every trip. 5. On some maps the Pacific coast (Legion of Honor, Cliff house etc) looks quite close to the downtown area but some maps use a different scale for different parts of the map. From the hotel to the Legion of Honor took about 50 minutes on the bus.

“Would stay there again” Great re-done lobby and nice people at the front desk. The room was quiet and comfy, nice and clean. But my colleague had a problem with people partying in the courtyard below her room late at night, keeping her from sleeping. Myself, though; no complaints.

“Business Travel? Great Location” A very clean and quiet location. The hotel is new and the staff is friendly. Rooms are large, comfortable, have a mini fridge and microwave, and it's a non-smoking hotel. They have a great breakfast (free) and it's located between AMD and the airport. Book your room on their website.

“Good hotel, near to airport” stayed at the hotel as part of road trip from LA to NYC. very efficent checkin, very near airport, saw shuttle bus, although didn't use. very clean room. breakfast from 430am, so good if catching an early flight. ruby tuesday's is nearby for dinner. great shower, and tv.
“Amazing!” The Greenwich Hotel is, without a doubt, one of the most wonderful hotels we've ever stayed in. Everything was perfect.

“Very Nice Remodeled Hotel” We have stayed at this hotel 3 times in the last few months. The 3 rooms we stayed in varied in size from small to large but were all nicely appointed, clean and recently remodeled. The air quality in this hotel is great as it is smoke free and has no strong odors from cleaning products for those of you with asthma. This hotel does have some late night noise issues on the weekends especially if your room is on the street side of the hotel. If this is an issue for you get a room with no view facing the alley as that seemed to be our quietest room. As for parking if you arrive on a weekend you can park for free in a city parking garage 2 blocks away on second street. The hotel is in a terrific location with restaurants, theaters , nightclubs and museums all within walking distance. I don't think this hotel quite deserves a 4 star rating but if you get the $89 price they often advertise on their website it is the best value in downtown San Jose. Free Wi Fi is a nice bonus and works well. We have found the staff to be on the young side but mostly cheerful and helpful.

“Clean & friendly, not much of a pool” I don't like traveling to cities where you have to drive everywhere, but I had to go to Austin for work. Colleagues suggested the Springhill Suites, and it is a good hotel. Nothing fancy or inspiring, but clean, with the basics for a "suite" hotel. The daily cleaning service hasn't forgotten anything all week, which is unusual in my experience. The hotel is right next to several other hotels, and lots of chain restaraunts and stores. The views are of the freeway and parking lots. The swimming pool as a way to get any exercise is a joke. The front desk staff is friendly, parking works, and they have some "room service" menus from local restaraunts.

“very nice hotel” very nice staff. stayed here twice in 2 weeks was exec floor first time very nice nibbles in loungesecond time was normal floor went into room late afternoon and noise from tv next door wayyyy to loud so i rang down and was upgraded free of charge back to exec floor, pool lovely , bar food nice but pricey,

“Good quality hotel in convenient location (& great gym)” This was my second stay at the Westin Philadelphia. First time was nearly 5 years ago for business and this time was purely for a fun weekend visit. Got a pretty good deal via Priceline and was happy it picked Westin on my bid. Though I felt that the check-in staff wasn't as helpful - I had to proactively ask where the business ctr or the gym were. POsitives: Room was clean, bed is nice and comfortable. Nice flatscreen tv. They give you a free bottle of water - which was nice because most hotels usually charge you ridiculous prices on little things like water. Bathroom is all marble and well maintained. They have a pretty nice gym for a hotel - most hotel gyms are tiny with 3-4 equipments crammed in. This one was a decent size - with locker rooms and sauna! Location is great because you're right in the shopping area Chestnut/Walnut and near RIttenhouse Square. & on a nice day like when we went, it was good to walk off your meals by walking across town to Society Hill or South Street. Negatives: I noticed that the nice white bathrobe had a makeup/foundation like stain on the shoulder - which made me wonder if it was just hanging there from the last guest and they never washed it. A bummer but realized after using it (and I don't wear foundation make up!) and we were getting ready to leave so I didn't ask for a new one. Also they were supposed to have free shoeshine and I had 2 pairs of shoes but when I saw them the next morning, was not impressed - it almost seemed they didn't even put polish on them.. again, was in a rush so didn't ask if they had indeed polished them overnight. Parking is pricey so I parked nearby on 17th and Samson ($20). Not worth the valet ($42!) if you just want to stroll about town which is pretty easy to do on foot or even the buses. Overall a good stay, good quality hotel, easily recommendable - and definitely shop for the hotel prices! It's worth it.

“Best kept secret (3rd time staying; still a charm!)” It may not be a 5-star, but you can't beat it. Third time we've stayed and they've increased in our esteem again! This BW caters to the business crowd, but we've always stayed for leisure (usually on a weekend). For the rate, it's perfect. Clean, "green", and if you request & it's available: a drop-dead view of the Space Needle practically across the street. (Ask again at check-in to make sure.) A mere walk to Belltown (about 5 short blocks) where too many choices of restaurants, wine (and spirits) bars, younger folks clubs (live music, pubs, etc), jazz clubs --if weather permits, a nice hoof over to even Pike's! You don't get the usual BW complimentary continental breakfast buffet, but b/c rates are lower we splurge on breakfast via room service. Parking's free in lower locked parking, which has cameras so we felt cool leaving our many shopping finds from this great shopping city discretely tucked away in back of our SUV. Check them out, for the money they're not long for best kept secret status too much longer. Kudos to the staff and management of this property; well done!

“Nice hotel, but so much potential to be excellent!” I recently spent one evening at this property and I left satisfied but convinced this could be a top-tier property with an update. It is a very clean, modern convention hotel in a great location. The interior of the guest rooms is decidedly generic, lacking the style of some of Chicago's newer hotels (Sofitel, W, Kimpton boutiques). But the rooms are large and nicely equipped with all the essentials of a business hotel. Bathroom was nice if a little bit dated, but very, very clean. It seems most of the rooms here have great views and mine was no exception. The shades were push-button which I quite enjoyed, though I'm not sure if this was because I was in a handicap-accessible room or if it is standard. The sheets and duvet were great but I was not happy with the mattress. Most of the upscale and even mid-range chains are finally updating their mattresses so I hope this property will follow suit. The bar could use a bit of an update but it works if you just want to sit in the lobby and enjoy an expectedly overpriced drink. Staff was very accommodating and always smiling and ready to assist. For $109/night (see Travelzoo web site; this continues all summer!), the hotel was absolutely fine. It could be an excellent property if the rooms were updated with new mattresses, televisions and desks. But at this point, there are many better hotels to choose from in Chicago.

“Perfect for Nationals Park!” We stayed to go to the games at Nationals Park. There is not much retail in the area, outside of a CVS Drugstore, Subway, and Five Guys, but the lobby bar was fun and well-managed. The McDonald's a few blocks away is not one of their nicest or best-run franchises. The pubs on Eighth Street are a bit of a hike, but were also fun. The Metro station is very nearby, as well as the 'Circulator,' a bus line that runs to the Capital area. My brother made the hike from the hotel to the Mall, and it took 15 minutes of brisk walking. Neighborhood otherwise seems desolate, but not unsafe.

“Super friendly staff” I recently stayed at the Hilton Houston Southwest hotel for business. The minute I walked in, I was greeted by a number of staff. The check-in process was one of the quickest I’ve experienced. They had my key and breakfast coupons ready to go when I got there. Because I travel quite a bit for business, I am particular about the type of room. I asked if it was non-adjoining and the clerk said no. I had also assumed being Hilton Gold that my preferences were taken into account (away from elevator, ice machine etc). When I got to my room, it was 1) right by the elevator and 2) adjoining. Not fun to drag all of my things back downstairs to get a different room. However, in doing so, Gary (the manager) made sure I got a much better room and even escorted me up there. He offered me a free dinner or extra points and remembered my name throughout my stay. I told him extra points would be better. It took almost two weeks (and a reminder to the hotel) to credit me my points, but I have them. I just haven’t seen hotels where every one of the staff is waiting to help and very friendly. Each one of them seemed to really enjoy their jobs and were eager to please. It was a unique and comforting atmosphere. About the hotel, the rooms are spacious, it has plenty of free parking and a good location off the Southwest Fwy in Houston. The hotel is a bit older, but it’s clean and the staff are wonderful. I would definitely stay there again. Big thanks to Nina for helping me out!

“Delightful Denver!” The Embassy Suites in downtown Denver is a beautiful hotel with the friendliest staff I've come across in years. The location is great if you're in town for a convention or if you want to people-watch along the 16th Street Mall. The rooms are spacious and comfortable, and the cooked-to-order breakfast can't be beat. Kudos to Anthony, the short-order cook; his friendly greetings were a great start to our days. If I'm ever again in Denver, I'll be happy to stay at the Embassy Suites-Downtown.

“Not Your Typical Courtyard” My second stay here and I'd probably come back. It's a huge, downtown hotel with an ideal center-city location across from City Hall. The place is fancy, but has a very cold feel. The staff is OK, but hardly gracious and welcoming. Nice touch... a decent enough restaurant open for dinner as well as breakfast. Rooms are nice but windows are sealed shut, ie no fresh air. Leave your car at home: parking is $38 a day!

“Great location and customer service” Stayed recently for two nights on a business trip. Took the light rail train from Sea-Tac to Westlake (downtown). The Hyatt is in a great spot downtown and a few blocks from the station. Customer service was friendly and attentive (one night I asked where the nearest drugstore as I needed some ibuprofen) - the folks at the front desk gave me directions to the nearest one, but offered me Advil! Had a room on the 15th floor and it was clean, comfortable and quiet. Hotel internet worked well. Room service was quick and attentive. Had breakfast at the hotel restaurant and it was fine. If I find myself back in Seattle, I will definitely put the Hyatt Olive 8 high on my consideration list.

“The Sofitel hotel was amazing and it was in an amazing location.” The Sofitel hotel was amazing and it was in an amazing location. It was just a block from the White House and was walking distance to all the rest of the mall monuments. We went there for our wedding anniversary and the front desk upgraded our room at no extra change. They had champagne waiting for us along with a nice letter congratulating us on our wedding anniversary. It was very thoughtful and a nice touch to start our anniversary in D.C. The service was immaculate and the room was very nice. They always opened the front door for us and gave us complimentary water. The only thing that my wife didn't like was there was no lock on the French bathroom door. With our three year old in the room it didn't offer much privacy. We would definitely stay here again and recommend this hotel to anyway who is staying in D.C.

“We Love the Inn at the Market” We absolutely love the Inn at the Market. We've stayed here before, back when it was done in a somewhat French decor style. It's been modernized and is so comfortable and attractive. We booked city view room, but were upgraded to room on front of building with view of Puget Sound. It was delightful. You just can't beat this location. Wake up early and get to the market before it gets crowded. The restaurant Bacco serves a great breakfast and is located on ground floor. Service is terrific. This is just a great place to stay in Seattle.

“Comfortable hotel, but expensive and nothing amazing . . .” This hotel was comfortable, and the service was fine. It was fairly expensive (booked at the last minute for business travel at $249 for one night and $299 the next night). The lobby was funky, but not large. I had stayed at the 71, which is right around the corner on an earlier stay. The room I got at the 71 had a fabulous view, and I'd probably try the 71 on my next stay if I end up in the same section of town. One cool thing was the yoga channel on TV -- an endless loop of a yoga class. Unfortunately, the yoga gear that was promised (mat, accessories) was not in the room, and I didn't bother to request it.

“Sofitel sooths” Stayed here during peak Christmas season. There are many good writeups on here about this hotel. I agree with all the ones that define the hotel as an excellent one. Some pointers: Try to get upgraded to a king room. They are on the higher floor. We did so after one night in a standard room and were not disappointed. Had a nice view of the Chrysler building; close enough to see the gargoyles. As mentioned earlier, the higher you are in this hotel, the better. The staff here is very friendly and goes out of their way to make you happy. This statement does not apply to the inept servers at the hotel bar however. Go elsewhere for libations. Regarding the glowing writeups of the 'Red Flame Diner', I just don't get it. The place is o.k. for breakfast and they are certainly fast with delivery, but it is nothing special. A more interesting choice for breakfast and fast is 'Dishes'. Great quality food, even if the atmosphere is 'cafeteria-ish'; two blocks away. Ask the concierge. We ate at DB bistro (two doors down from hotel) and were sorely disappointed, especially after having eaten at the flagship Daniel two nights before. Of course it is much cheaper, but you can do much better for the money. For those from out of town, NYC water is terrific. It comes from upstate New York and does not have to be treated. Drink it from the taps, you are wasting money otherwise. Yes, it was expensive at $500 a night with tax, but my friends stayed at the Roosevelt for $300 and hated it. This hotel is so worth it. Planning to return in early summer; tres bon.

“Beautiful historic but modern hotel” I chose Ames on a recent vacation to Boston because I've stayed at 2 other Morgans Hotel Group properties and LOVED them. So, I had really high expectations. While the hotel is gorgeous (historic exterior, colorful modern interior with a really great bathroom and bed) like I've come to expect from these hotels, the customer service unfortunately did not meet my expectations. It wasn't bad necessarily, but it wasn't as great as the sister hotels I've stayed at. The front desk staff I talked to were a little snooty and not super helpful, and our bags were mixed up by the bell desk (after presenting our claim ticket, we had to describe what our bags looked like, after they tried to give us bags that weren't ours). I will give Ames another shot if I go to Boston again, as I am pretty obsessed with this hotel group, but I'm not sure it was worth the price I paid, given the less than perfect service. (And I am being super picky about this... Don't get me wrong, this is a nice hotel.)

“Great location, classice east side hotel” There are 2 Intercontinentals in NYC, a brand shiny new one on the west side @ Broadway and the grand old Barclay here on the east side. I love new hotels , but this classic hotel has an east sider charm that cant be beat. Check with Leslie at Guest Relations and she can help you with your needs. As an ambassador in the Priority club program, my upgrade as well as early check in and late check out is always confirmed. The location is close to grand central and cenral park and 5th avenue shopping. The breakfeast buffet, although, a bit pricey is great. Go hungry

“Nice Hotel with a great view” This was my first time staying at this Hotel. Not my first time staying at a Hyatt Regency. The Hotel is in a great location, right next to the river, so the views are fantastic (if you have a river view). The staff was very friendly and check in was pretty fast. I went to the bar downstairs and was very surprised how many people were there at almost 12 midnight. Good drinks I had there and very good bar food. The pizza was huge. The bartenders were also very friendly. The most I like about the room was the view. The room need some renovation, but the beds are comfortable. Just look at the pictures and you will know what I'm talking about. Also there were some chips on the side of the bathtub. The room was really clean, but there were some hairs still in the hairdryer. It is not the best Regency, but its pretty good. They are lucky to have that location. I Had a good stay. Just look at the pictures and make you own decision.

“Great location and all around great hotel” Upon my arrival I happen to see the manager who welcomed me back again, nice feeling to be remembered. This is a good hotel, my suite had a kitchen, spacious living area, bedroom, bathroom. one of Its best features is that it is located in the Hillcrest area of San Diego within walking to the best selection of bars and restaurants, close to Balboa Park, downtown and old town. The staff were very friendly and helpful. All of the above is why I would recommend this hotel.

“Nice hotel, just don't try to book a taxi from here!” We picked this hotel because of the ratings here on TA and as far the cleanliness etc goes, we were not in any way disappointed. The novelty Texas-shaped waffle iron at breakfast was indeed cute - even if we're not waffle aficionados! I would endorse what has been said elsewhere about the friendliness of the staff, though add a caveat to their 'helpfulness'. We were in Austin over a weekend (Saturday & Sunday night) during the Pecan Street Spring Festival - awesome fun, by the way. We asked at reception about getting a taxi into town for this and were supplied with a couple of numbers to call from our room - though warned it could be a while. Fair enough. After numerous attempts, we finally managed to get one booked and headed down prior to the alloted time for collection to wait.....and wait....and wait. At this point, the guy on reception told us all manner of nightmare tales about the difficulties of getting taxis on a Saturday night. My fiance asked if he could call to chase from reception, conscious it was a freephone local call, but was told he would have to go to our room to do so. Why? Especially given our room was a good distance from the main entrance. We were then further regaled with what sounded a lot like excuses to us, about how the hotel staff never got involved in helping guests arrange taxis because of the difficulties that were experienced....blah blah, blah. Well, maybe the local taxi firms are appallingly unprofessional/overworked. Yet surely if that is the case, the hotel should build a relationship with one so that it can (a) ensure that firm gets the work; and (b) improve service for its clients, instead of palming them off with flimsy 'good luck with that' asides? A small grumble in what was otherwise a really enjoyable stay - just be warned if you're not willing to drive everywhere (restaurants, downtown etc) that you are in a pickle!

“Glad I stayed” Stayed 4 nights. The location was close to all the major subway lines. Usually I do not stay above 14th street since my office is in SOHO. I also try not to stay in the Times Square area due to all the tourist but due to no rooms at other hotels and being that I am a memeber of the PREFERRED Guest Program, I chose Night. The staff was awesome and were there when I needed them but were never in your face. The room size was a large compared to other NYC hotels and small compared to the W chain. Linens and bed were great. The nightly turn down service with robe and chocolates were a nice touch. Did not encounter the shower flooding like some reviewers. The shower was like that of a lot of NYC and Miami hotels. Guess I am used to it. Would I stay here again - yes certainly and not as a last resort.

“Great budget hotel” We just returned from seven nights in NYC over the New Years holiday. We chose the Chelsea Lodge because the reviews were great and because they did not raise their rates at all for the holidays unlike many NYC hotels which raise them to astronomical levels. For the price I very much doubt you could beat the Chelsea Lodage anywhere in New YorK City. Yes the rooms are tiny, but they are very clean as are the bathroom facilities and the rest of the hotel. Chelsea is a wonderful neighbourhood from which to explore the rest of the city and a great part of town in its own right.

“Excellent hotel and service” Stayed at the hotel in late August. Took cab from DFW airport($50) and Carlos was waiting at the door with a smile to take our bags. We checked in around noon (2pm listed) and Carlos was waiting and took bags and showed us the room and amenities. Our room was a suite on a high floor and exceeded our expectations. 3 rooms.. Bedroom had closet with full ironing board with starch, flatscreen tv, and the best black out shades over blinds. batgoffered wonderful soaps and the hallway had a full size painting. The living area that a long couch, flatscreen, work area, coffee table. Oh, and all tge lights had plugIns.. I love that!!! Our kitchen was full size kitchen just like an apartment. Utensils, pots and pans, and even a single cup coffee maker. Breakfast was hot eggs, a meat and French toast or other treats. They also had breads, yogurts, and fresh fruit... The best and every morning complimentary! There is also a happy hour with two free drinks(they do need a snack- nuts or pretzels) hot cookies and milk from 8 to 10 and they were yummy.

“Modern, elegant rooms - great location!” Stayed here for a conference. Though my room felt like it is 10 minutes from the elevator (the hallways are lonnng), I had a corner room with windows on two sides with a view of the Washington Monument! The room looked days old. New furnishings, gorgeous bathroom with high-end finishes, nice flat screen and very comfy bed with extra pillows. Two tiny complaints: why do hotels that do not offer room wifi have the shortest internet cords known to man? I want to sit in bed people with my laptop! And the hotel lacks quick service food. It could use a Starbucks outlet that offers fresh bagels and sandwiches for those that are running between conference sessions. Others have said the rooms are small. Mine room with a King bed felt very spacious and featured a nice desk area and separate sitting area. Definitely would consider staying here in the future!

“A great deal” This hotel is a great deal for staying in LA: good price and good amenities, even if the surrounding area is not the greatest. The hotel doesn't look like anything spectacular from the outside, but it is clean and the rooms are spacious and comfortable, complete with a flat-screen TV and cable channels, a microwave and a small fridge which are very handy. My only complaint is the A/C, it's a bit close too close to one of the beds (we were sleeping in 4 people in the room, so we needed both beds). Included in the room rate are a very good breakfast (they had 3 or 4 different kinds of fruit, pastries, waffle machine, scrambled eggs and bacon, yougurt, etc), free parking and free wi-fi. Breakfast room is a bit small, but we never had problems finding a table (they only have 4 or 5 tables, but you can take the breakfast to your room). The surrounding area is not the best, but we didn't feel unsafe or anything like that, and since we had a rented car it wasn't a problem for us. Overall I recommend this hotel because you get quite a lot for the price (which is not expensive)!

“no problems” A huge convention hotel with some california touches (for instance cucumber flavored water in the lobby), by the personality challenged San Diego Marina (nevertheless by beautiful waters and with easy access to many restaurants and shope). The room was comfortable but small after a switch because first room was much too noisy (some vent problem). Internet access was without problem, room service excellent. Starbucks on the first floor is convenient and pastries are better than at usual starbucks actually. Hotel has several restaurants, all good if expensive.

“Center of Everything” Perfect location for experiencing NYC. Great views of Times Square. Close to shows, restaurants and subway. Center of everything. Spacious rooms. Not great for light sleepers. Would definitely return.

“High End and Strictly Business” The Fairmont is just exactly what are expecting if you are in the market for a high-end, business-traveler-oriented hotel. The common areas are mostly gleaming marble, the rooms feature large desks equipped for quick access to the internet and on the mezzanine the business center competes with the fitness center for space. Similar to other business-oriented hotels the DC Fairmont keeps its meeting rooms in the basement. Why people are made to fly to often distant cities only to meet with others in the basements of large hotels is a huge mystery to me. But I digress, in short this hotel is expensive (daily internet access is $14, the sprawling breakfast buffet is $25 and even with my firm’s substantial discount the room was $220) but you are unlikely to receive any serious complaints from conference invitees or colleagues to whom you recommend it.

“Quiet oasis with beautiful views.” I picked this hotel because it was in a part of New York I had not visited before--Battery Park--and I wanted a place with nice views to enjoy a quiet stay after a few days in mid-town. This was the perfect choice. The hotel itself was beautiful. Very large room with comfortable bed and chair and nice desk. The bathroom was large with a separate shower and (very large) bathtub. I had a room with a view of the Statue of Liberty--very nice. It came with a telescope; although I never quite figured out how to focus it properly, it was a nice touch. The staff was friendly and generally helpful, although there was no one around to help me lug my heavy suitcase up the dozen or so stairs from the curb where the taxi dropped me off to the hotel entry doors (which did not open automatically) (when I checked out I found the ramp to the right of the doors, but it was hidden by a little wall on the way in). The food served in the restaurant and room service was delicious but prepare to pay a lot for it--the charge for an American breakfast (2 eggs, toast, and bacon) was $34. (Walking along the waterfront to the right I eventually came to some shops and found a nice diner-like place for breakfast on day 2.) On the other hand, the room rate was very reasonable (much less than the Central Park Ritz-Carlton). This was a great hotel and although I planned this as a one-time experience I can't wait for an excuse to get back to New York and another stay at this hotel.

“A Last-Minute Success” I was sent to Dallas with little notice on a two-day business trip a few years ago. My colleague and I were literally driving into the city from DFW and scrolling through hotel options when we more or less blindly settled on the Warwick Melrose ecause it was fairly near where we needed to be the next day. As it turned out, it was a terrific decision. This was a grand, old hotel, and I appreciated its charming touches. If you're looking for slick, this isn't it. The staff was very friendly, and my room was large, old-fashioned and comfortable. We were in town on a Sunday, and we enjoyed an absolutely delightful brunch in the hotel restaurant. Not only was the food terrific, we soaked up the atmosphere. I distinctly remember a group of gracious women, dressed in their Sunday best after church, celebrating a birthday at the table next to us. They were delightful (their accents too) and we couldn't help but do some eavesdropping. The location was also a nice surprise. The hotel is located near the Oak Lawn and Turtle Creek neighborhoods, a few miles from downtown Dallas. The neighborhoods are affluent and pretty, with several good restaurant options. The first night, we simply walked down the block and found a good Mexican plan, the second, we drove to a fantastic old-school burger joint (alas, the name escapes me). We had a little downtime, and the hotel made a good base of operations to see some sights, including Dealey Plaza and the Book Depository museum, and the Ft. Worth stockyards. Lastly: while I can't promise this always holds true, we were pleasantly surprised to get a very reasonable rate. The hotel is worth checking out.

“Great location, really nice rooms, wifi connection is terrible!” We stayed in the Dylan for a night in October. Found the staff on check in really nice and the concierge was nice if not that helpful of where to go out to get a bite to eat! He didn't really know the area that well. The room was really nice, big king size bed which was super comfortable and impecably clean. Bathroom was big and spacious too! The only draw back was that the wifi connection was really weak and became very irritating to try and use! Would recommend the Dylan if the wifi wouldn't both you!

“Can't go wrong” I'll echo what others have said. Nice rooms, very comfy beds, stylish decor and helpful, friendly staff. Floor-to-ceiling windows offered a nice view of the bay and the TransAmerica Pyramid, even from only the 11th floor. Free business center was a nice touch. Location is a bit off the tourist path, but you're within 5-10 minutes of Chinatown, the Ferry Building, Coit Tower, North Beach (including City Lights) and the California St. cable car. The Powell line and Union Sq. is close by as well. We also walked to Fisherman's wharf in around 20 mins. Note that on weekends the immediate area shuts down. The Starbucks across the street is open, but not much else is. But it gets quiet, which is nice.

“Probably the best urban hotel I've stayed at on the last five years.” Service was great, the rooms were well appointed and clean, the restaurant was great. Not sure what worse you could ask for out of a hotel. I usually don't like staying at hotels this big, but the service quality was like that of a boutique hotel. The exterior light display is interesting as you pull up to the valet. Just like the high tech rooms, it's mesmerizing. The feature I liked the best in the rooms was the floor that lit up when you stepped out of your bed, guiding you to your destination when it's dark. The rooms were quite and comfortable and very large with a little seating area right by the window. Ask for a room with a view of downtown.

“A great location and a somewhat good and very friendly hotel” I have to say this place grew on me. Put it out of your head that you need a four seasons or a Ritz carlton class of service and room if thats what you are used to and you will not go too far wrong here. We were in a "wonderfull room" with a partial view out to union square.The room was fairly basic in my opinion and did not have a separate shower. For one of their better rooms,this was and always will be a major negative for me. When there is room for a walk in shower [rather than in the bath] then they should be put in. It makes the room so much nicer,I think. Servicing of theroom was good but there was no turn down. As we were there for a bit of partying and Xmas shopping , this was a disappointment but not a biggie. The hotel has a busy and very hip [for want of a better word] bar. The staff there are very friendly and theres always a buzz.It's a great people watching spot. The breakfasts in the restaurant beside the bar,I'd give a 10 out of 10 as they were delicious and the service there was great. We found the concierge service here to be excelent. The definitely went the extra mile to help us out! The other thing I'd say about this hotel is that everyone appeared so friendly,guests and staff alike. Maybe it was because it was the Xmas season but we liked it! Would I recommend it? Yes I would but hotel owner's...please install separate showers in rooms that can have them!

“Clean and renovated...across the street from the Convention ctr” I enjoyed the Westin Charlotte. My room was spotless. It has a great location. Food was average and restaurant was over run and couldnt keep up...food both in the restaurant and at room service was typical hotel fare....some challenges there...but all in all a very nice Hotel!

“Fun hotel, good value & central location” After reviewing the Yotel web site and other reviews I was apprehensive, but it turned out great and would totally stay there again. Be prepared for an ultra modern property catering to the solo traveler, tourists and younger/trendy people. Staff, restaurant, bar and night club all provided exceptional service and value. Areas that need improvement: No shampoo, conditioner or lotion provided. Motion sensors are slow to pick up movement. I don't like walking into a dark room when I left a light on... TV picture is too dark and not alterable. Lighting around bathroom mirror is not bright enouph. I would not recommend the Yotel for older couples, families with children or anyone sharing a basic room do to the bathroom configuration.

“Nice room, great service in a convenient location” Stayed here on a last minute family vacation to explore the Riverwalk & San Antonio's theme parks over the Memorial Day weekend. As we were going to be going to New Braunfels, we did not want a downtown location. However, hotel was only about 10-15 mins from Riverwalk. Hotel was 30 mins from Schlitterbahn. Room was super clean & house keeping did an excellent job keeping it that way. Front desk staff was friendly & accommodating. Looked at the $13.95 breakfast buffet & it was nothing special. Saw all the pilots & flight attendants with breakfast tacos from the cafe. The tacos were very good. This was a very nice hotel.

“An enjoyable stay near Union Square” The Westin St. Francis is well situated for most any activity in San Fransico. Located on Union Square you are at the hub of activity! The classic exterior hides a modern clean and accomidating hotel within. During my stay I misplaced my ebook reader while at the hotel gym. The staff was very helpful and recovered the item for me very quickly. The tower rooms are spacious and have all the features one would expect from Westin. The hotel is easy walking distance to the Moscone. An excellent choice in SFO.

“Everything I hoped” This place is in a great location, literally over the road from Pike Market and about a 5 minute walk to the centre of the city. We originally werent sure whether to stay in the city, but given the Inn turned out to be so close to the city and that the Pike Markets are so colorful, it was a great choice. We didnt feel unsafe at any stage and in fact the mafority of the stranger types appeared to mainly reside in the city itself. There are plenty of places to eat very close by, from quick snacks to nice restaurants, so again location was excellent. We had breakfast at a small French patiserie about 2 minutes away that served great coffee and fantastic pasteries at a reasonable price. We were also impressed with the hotel. Although it doesnt look much from the outside, its been decorated modern but refined and the room was great. We tend to try and get a room with a view and in this case stayed in a Parlour Suite. While expensive, the room didnt let us down with both the view and quality. We were very happy and comfortable. Didnt try the hotels restaurants, but they always seemed to show up on the "best in Seattle" lists. So overall we couldnt have been happier at the Inn at the Market and would recommend it to anyone.

“very nice stay” We were here for a conference and stayed for 2 nights. We had a great room with a airport view. The Grand might look nicer but nothing wrong with this hotel. Rooms are renovated and the Bar makes great pizzas.

“Great rate for a downtown hotel!” Pros: - Close to downtown Austin. - Great rates! - Clean rooms and facility. - Large pool and patio area. - Interior corridors w/ elevator. - Full breakfast in the morning. - Evening reception. - Right next to interstate and very quiet. - Cool A/C. - Completely smoke free. - Free parking. Cons: - Had an issue at check-in with our school group with the charge for exceeding 2+ non-related guests per room. The manager/owner conceded that the info is published on a limited basis, but be advised to contact management ahead of time to confirm arrangements if booking for large groups w/ multiple rooms. Thanks to the owner/management, the issue was resolved to our satisfaction and we look forward to staying at this hotel in the future. Notes: - If you are visiting Austin, this is definitely the place to stay! A great gem where you get so much for a great bargain! Be blessed!

“Great Location with Kids! Excellent Service as Always!” We selected this hotel based on its location, price, pool and the fact that we have always received excellent service from Hyatt employees. Even though it's located in a touristy area of the city, it worked so well for us. We could walk to the park, to the water, to so many things of interest to our seven year old son during our "down time". It's located near the end of the F line (the vintage streetcar line). The location gave us easy access to public transportation.One day we walked to the cable car, took that to Union Square, explored and continued on foot to Chinatown, more exploring, walked over to the Ferry Building where we ate all kinds of delicious food at the Farmers Market (4505 chicharrones, Blue Bottle coffee, Acme bread, etc.) and took the F line back to the hotel. One night we walked to a restaurant in North Beach and cabbed it back to the hotel, but we could have easily walked had we not been so tired from our day. We ended up never using the pool because we were so busy exploring but we saw lots of people who did. The hotel does show some wear, but our room was clean and large enough for a king bed and a rollaway. Even though our room was on the street side (with a view of Coit Tower), it was quiet. Service was great. Another plus for families - the hotel is near a grocery store, possibly two. If I remember correctly, our rate was very low $200s using a AAA rate. I would definitely stay here again unless I get a vacation rental instead.

“Best hotel I've stayed at in NYC” I stayed here for four nights in June 2011. Got a very good advanced deal through Expedia. The rooms were spacious, stylistic, clean, and quiet. Service was really friendly, breakfast was pleasant and there was free WiFi. I've stayed at about 10-15 hotels in New York and this one was by far the best. Would recommend it without any hesitations.

“Bring earplugs!” This was on our conference hotel list, but I have to wonder what they were thinking! The hotel is lovely--very hip, modern, and almost like a boutique hotel. My room was ready when I arrived and it was very comfortable. But at check-in, the host made a point of telling me that there was a nightclub and that music can be heard throughout the building. So I went out and bought earplugs, which did the trick. Thursday, Friday, and Saturday are nightclub nights. Sunday was blissfully quiet.

“I love this Hotel!!!” The staff is outstanding. They're very attentive, professional and friendly. Convenient location. There's a happy hour, breakfast and light dinner during the week. The rooms are very nice and spacious. It's like a mini apartment. I loved it!

“Very affordable, conveniently located hotel in Austin, TX” This hotel was clean as a whistle. The staff at the front desk were extremely helpful and friendly. Two computers available at all times, and the whole place is wireless! (WiFi--free) Small but adequate outdoor pool to combat the heat of Austin. Rooms are HUGE, with efficient AC units which work well! Very adequate continental breakfast is included. I'd definitely stay there again if I wanted to be in that part of Austin.

“Comfortable stay” We had enough Hilton Honors points for two free nights at the Hampton Inn Times Square North. The location was wonderful--close to the theatres,. Lincoln Center, subway, good restaurants. I requested a quiet room which we got. The bed was very comfortable with nice linens. However, there was a huge spot on the hassock and some on the carpets. The breakfast was great (Why is that the very expensive hotels never have breakfast?) but there were long lines given that this is larger than most Hampton Inns and a busy time of year. I would recommend this hotel.

“Trendy Little Gem” I stayed at the Back Bay hotel for 3 nights last month on a business trip. The staff was friendly and willing to help when I had questions and/or concerns. The bellman hauled cabs rather quickly and gave good advice on the best routes to go (via walking) and places to eat. The restaurant turns into a night club at night and can be rather loud when first walking into the hotel. Luckily I never heard a bit of noise from my 3rd floor room. My room was cozy with ample space to do work and sleep! The bathroom was nice along with the toiletry amenities each day (Avida and Kiehl's products) and the heated towel rack was a plus. Heated flooring would have been even nicer on a cold Boston morning! My only complaint in the room was that I had a hard time getting plug sockets to work. I ordered room service one morning since the restaurant didn't open in time for me to make my business meeting. The room service came promptly (food still piping hot); however, my order was incorrect. They quickly fixed it (within 5 minutes). Overall I would definitely recommend staying at the Back Bay. This trendy little gem is near the mall and convention center, and blocks away from the massive public library!

“Another excellent stay at a Kimpton hotel...” We stayed here for one night. We were in town for a concert so we were only in Chicago for about 24 hours. The hotel is boutique style. Our room was comfortable. On the small side and we had a view of a rooftop of the building next door, but we were hardly in the room. We also checked in early so that was the room that was ready for us. And the bed was comfortable and that's what matters most to me. The customer service was excellent as usual with Kimpton hotels. They let us check in early and greeted us with champagne and a personal note since they knew we were getting married at a Kimpton the following November. The bar was cool looking, it had a trendy feel to it. We had a late night drink there. We had room service for breakfast and that was delicious. Very comfortable boutique hotel and I would recommend.

“USC visit” This was our 3rd stay at the Radisson during visits to USC. The staff has always been great , very helpful and friendly. This is the best location for USC visits and its clean/modern.. I know of no other options that permits you to walk safely to USC. We usually have the standard rooms and they have been fine, just what we expect. There is a small gift shop in the lobby and the prices seem the same as the USC book store. Early in the morning the hotel lobby had complimentary coffee and some small items ( granola bars, apples). Car service to LAX was easily arranged at a flat $55. This was about the same flat rate I paid for the taxi going from LAX to Radisson.. Several fast food places a few blocks away from the Radisson. There are a few restaurants next to Radisson. This past stay I spent 2 nights in Junior suite Hotel was filled, so only the junior suite 104 ($199) was available, I would have opted for less expensive option if possible. Room was on the first floor, which I was informed was true for all Junior suites. I was a bit concerned about noise and safety on the first floor, but I had no other options.The room was very quiet, but I kept the shades closed as the view looked directly into the parking lot and public walkway. It was basically a fine room, but had minimal outlets to recharge cell phones/lap tops. Also very dark, since I opted for the closed shade experience. I do not remember if all the standard rooms were as dark?

“Great Weekend Getaway in Downtown LA” We stayed here over the weekend when we went to see Les Mis in LA. The hotel is very large with a big city feel. The rooms were comfortable, but we had to wait for our rooms to be available (after the 4pm check-in time). The hotel is in a good location and the breakfast was very nice. The rooms are very typical big city hotel rooms, very efficeint, but not much room. I think this is a better hotel for business, but if I needed to stay in downtown LA in the future, I would consider staying here again.

“A good option” We booked through Hotwire and got a rate of $58 which made the stay seem very reasonable. I would be hard pressed to pay the $129 a night found through their website. The location is central to the galleria and right off the tollway (you can avoid paying the toll by staying on the service road). We were able to park right out front and enter into what is an enormous lobby. The staff was friendly but I did think they were trying to upsale us. Upon check-in we were asked if we wanted to spend $15 to upgrade to a "remodeled" room. They just need to do all the rooms remodeled and up the price for all rooms. The facility and public spaces are very nice. The room itself that we got was big by normal hotel standards. The furniture and room itself was clean and not run down, but does look a bit tired. The best part of the room was the down top mattress, water pressure, and size of room. The amenities of coffee and toiletries were adequate as well. I would stay here again at the hotwire price but not over $100 a night.

“Made for your convention” I stayed here on business, had a room next to a hospitality suite. I went to the front desk and they moved me to a different room and threw in a free breakfast, although I got up too early to take advantage of it (the restaurant opens at 6:30am). The room was a little small, but comfortable and clean (and the new one quiet).

“Will be back.” Brand new hotel, just opened on April 19 (still has that 'new hotel smell'-ha!). Interestingly, though, does not have the usual HGI Garden Sleep System beds. They are still working out the punch list-painters tape still up around the pantry pavilion in the lobby &, as we discovered, the AC unit in my colleague's room was never connected to the duct, so we had to move our first night there. I ended up in a handicap room, which was huge w/equally huge bathroom, but at least this time there is amply counter space for 'stuff', something that is often missing in other handicap hotel bathrooms. Be warned, though, if you are w/o a car, you will be stuck at the hotel when it comes to dining options as the shuttle only goes to/from the hospitals.

“Much improved” Paid full rack rate for this hotel due to World Series. Was able to reserve a room through Hotels.com - hotel website was showing the property sold out. Room was ready for my early arrival, which was a nice surprise. I was put on the Starwood Preferred floor - not sure what the upgraded amenities were, although I did have one water bottle and a coffee maker. No soap for the shower, only bath gel (could have been an oversight). Room was clean and comfortable. Had drinks at their small bar, no table service. Had breakfast in their small restaurant - even though the room was redone in their make-over I don't particularly like it - a windowless affair. Had a bagel which I made myself from the buffet, which I thought was weird but OK. Valet expensive but fine. Only complaint was that before I left for the game I called and asked for turndown service - and was told fine, but didn't receive it. When I returned to the room after the game (3 am!) I called to voice my disappointment and they offered to send up fresh towels, but by then I was exhausted. Made due with the hand towels.

“Convenient location, new rooms and helpful staff” The Hilton in the Fashion District of Manhattan is a nice new hotel - very trendy lobby and rooms to match. We had a king room and it was spacious with a comfy bed, desk area, flat screen TV and beautiful bathroom. The rooms are presented beautifully and are impeccably clean. The service is outstanding. The majority of the desk staff are very easy to deal with and go out of their way to help you. Only downside of service was when we moved rooms (our choice), our bags were moved so roughly that a few items broke...which we weren't too happy with. Location is good - 2 blocks from a Metro station which is the only way to travel in NYC. Plenty of places to eat around and Macy's flagship store a short walk away. Times Square only 2 stations away. Good value hotel in the area.
