The rooms could be better insulated for sound as you hear a fair amount of noise no matter where your room is (from outside and from neighbouring rooms) but still got sleep. Would have been nice to have a couple of extra facilities like a guest laundry (though there is a laundromat across the street for holiday-ers who like to keep on top of their washing!). Gym is small but serviceable for what you'd need. All in all, very pleased with pretty much everything with this hotel! Would definitely stay here again when in NYC.

“Great location, great hotel.” Stayed here for a girls weekend. Right in the Galleria. Got lucky on Hotwire and got a $79 rate. (Narrowed the search to the Galleria area, and picked the 4 star plus hotels). Valet parking was $27, but worth it to avoid the hassel. Rooms were pretty, bed and pillows wonderful. I'd go back!
“Nice midtown hotel” I really liked this hotel for a quick trip. Small room but clean and comfortable. Got a great rate and great location. Staff friendly and professional.
“Great location in downtown Philadelphia.” This location was convenient to public transportation and most downtown tourist attractions. The quality of the room and of the breakfasts were very good.

“Nice stay after a Buckeyes basketball game” We have stayed at this Hampton Inn before and this vista was just as pleasant. We checked in late after attending a Ohio State basketball game on December 22nd. Check in was painless as usual with Hampton's. The only issue we had was trying to get the door to open. After getting some help for the front desk we were in our room. The room was updated nicely and comfortable. In the morning the free breakfast was welcome before heading out to do some last minute Christmas shopping. With all the other choices are the Polaris area the Hampton Inn is a good choice.

“Relaxing and friendly” Felt totally ripped off from taxi drivers. Charged $9 to get to hotel. Charged $10 to go back to Amtrak. My stay was quiet and peaceful. The harbor was beautiful. The Gallery had a huge sale on my fav Aerosoles shoes and boots. The staff was extremely friendly. Room service staff was terrific. The turkey burger was dry. I felt comfortable. Would return today if I could.

“Great place to have an event or just rest.” If you are planning a wedding, a reception, a birthday party, or any other function, you should check out thier facilities. They also do conferences. And the breakfast there are exceptional. Plus, if you are lucky enough to have the buffet, usually at Easter and Mother's Day. the food is abundant and very tasty. Prices for the buffet are somewhat less than the other places. Oh, this hotel is also very close the the Casino and the Mall. About 15 minutes from downtown and about 20 from the International Bridges.

“It's hard to beat a brand new hotel!” Enjoyed a two night stay there through Priceline. The hotel is brand new and extremely clean. If you are looking to visit Soho or Greenwich Village, the location is perfect. Otherwise, a 1 train stop is a few steps away. The staff was the most friendly I have ever experienced in NYC, and I travel there at least once a month. My only complaint was the lack of a view from my room, but as this in NY, I'm used to looking down an air shaft. Highly recommended.

“Very nice hotel; would stay there again.” Stayed here late August, 2011. No complaints. We checked in very late on a Thursday night and had no problems. We had great customer service. The room was spacious, comfortable. Bathroom shower has built-in shampoo, conditioner and soap dispenser. The bar has great drinks if you need a nightcap.

“Charming hotel” For this trip, this was the hotel that had the best price at my t. agent. My usual hotel asked for twice the usual sum for the night, so forget about it. I did not like the area much, it is a bit too south for me (I stay for business and prefer 40th to 46th area). But I did appreciate the room, very clean, lovely bed and pillows, nice bathroom. Of course it is not big, otherwise I'd go to a Sheraton or so, but I hate big hotels and this was just charming.

“Great location for a Broadway trip” Nicely appointed rooms, good location, good security, VERY resaonable Manhattan parking. Near food shopping and not far from kosher restaurants. I would stay there again without a doubt.

“Great Experience” We loved our stay at the Willard. This is certainly not a modern, sleek hotel but rather one that has a real sense of history and an elegance of a bygone era. Don't stay here if you like a modern hotel as you'll see too many faults. The Willard is a little tired in some areas, but those who appreciate 'age' will really value its beauty and style. We had a lovely room - large and comfortable, the staff were fabulous, the location was perfect and we really enjoyed breakfast in the cafe. I would love to stay here again if we ever returned to Washington.

“Great if you need to be near O'Hare” Stayed here in July for some business meetings, and had a most pleasant stay. Yes, it does cater (actually is setup) somewhat more for business travelers (2nd floor is meeting rooms), but it is still a very nice hotel, and would have no hesitation whatsoever to stay here with family or on any non-business itinerary. Check in is very quick, even though they were very busy at the time. They typically have enough front desk staff to handle the volume, and at one end of the registration desk is a separate place where Hilton HHonors members can check in. The hotel is in great shape, especially the rooms. They are clean, big enough (they have kind of a European look to them), have very comfortable beds, and are unbelievably quiet given the hotel is on the airport grounds. The restaurant and sports bar downstairs are nice enough; typical hotel fare and prices, but the food was good, and wait staff were attentive and timely. The atmosphere is nice and calm - good to get away from the hustle/bustle in the lobby. The hotel also has a great fitness center on the lower level, with plenty of treadmills, bikes, weights, etc. No wait at all. The pool is right there next to the fitness center as well. The location is convenient, especially if you have travel issues around getting into/out of O'Hare (e.g., early or late flights). You can walk to the hotel from any concourse without going outside, and as other reviewers have said, there are train and bus stops there in the lower tunnel level, so you can get downtown in about 45 minutes. There is obviously nothing to do outside of the hotel without some form of transportation, but if you are looking for a place to stay with the quickest access to O'Hare, this is it. You can check in for your flights, and print boarding passes from kiosks located in the hotel lobby - that is also nice if you want to save time from waiting in lines once you get back over to the airport. All in all, would stay here any time - the lone exception being pricing. It can be very expensive sometimes (not sure what drives the prices so much higher at times), but when the rates are comparable, wouldn't hesitate staying here again.

“Stylist, Modern, Different and Refreshing - a Wonderful Experience” Staying over 35 nights at various Hyatt the past couple months, I almost pasted up the opportunity of staying here and I am so glad I didnt and gave it a try. I wish I have given this hotel a try earlier so I could stay there more, but I stayed here the last night of my 5 months travel in San Diego.I will definitely stayed here again. Initially I didnt want to stay at this hotel because they didnt have a club lounge for platinum member. But dont let this fool you as it did for me. It makes up for it by offering all sort of complimentary drinks and snacks in the room. As a platinum member also I got free breakfast (excellent quality). This hotel is so pretty in the inside, the pictures on Tripadvisor doesnt do it justice (hence why I didnt stay here until my last night). Its so clean and so pretty. The staff are excellent. Their bamboo toiletry are one of the best, I will buy more because I like them so much. Definitely a unique Hyatt brand, this hotel is especially classy and a good fit for young and established professional who wants the best of both worlds. Their card keys are pretty cool - very hip.

“Residence Inn ROCKS!” Fantastic NYC hotel experience! Stayed here last year & was extremely pleased! This year was equally fabulous! The Positives: Splendid staff--they cater to the customer! Due to a redeye flight, we arrived at 8am to the hotel & there was one room available--they cordially accommodated us! Great buffet breakfasts each morning! Oh so spacious room w/all the treats: comfy bed, kitchen w/everything, a sofa, just perfect! Free Internet access! (This was partially a work trip--so nice to work in my room w/no technical difficulties)! The front desk was nice enough to give us a slightly later checkout time, too! Perfect! The Negatives: Not much closet space (but I can live with that). It also would be nice to have an extra hour of breakfast time on Saturdays & Sundays (Okay, I confess--Saturday was a wild night & I didn't wake up till 10am on Sunday--so no lovely buffet). Any chance you could extend the weekend buffet until 11am? Also, rates were pretty high for our stay--compared to Comfort Inn & a few other places I investigated (I still chose Residence Inn, because of the great treatment from last year.) It would be nice if you had a nice deal for people staying more than 2 days, or maybe some other little price break. Other than my mild complaints, the place really does ROCK!

“Great Conference Hotel” During a recent conference at the Marriott East in Indianapolis, I found a professional and flexible staff who made it easy to get the job done. Even with last minutes changes to the F&B and program, they accommodated our group successfully and always with a smile. I would recommend this property to any group looking for a site that offers adequate space, good food and a great staff.

“Nicely Appointed Hotel” We are a family of 4 that stayed at this hotel for 4 nights...we got a great rate of $125/night...This hotel is in a great location! It is a block away from the White House and a couple of blocks away from the Washington Monument...within walking distance to many other Washington landmarks as well as eateries. The lobby is enormous and generously decorated and the hotel comes complete w/a Starbucks and a restaurant and I believe a separate bar. The rooms are nicely appointed and well kept but very small-it was hard to juggle 4 people into the one room...nice large flat screen TV, and the flooring a combination of hard wood and carpet, and crown molding all around. The beds were only doubles so we asked for a cot which was available-very tight when the bed was down-when not in use you had to put it up on end in the corner....there was a stocked fridge and a small snack collection that we didnt use...I had read from a prior review that the snack collection was on a motion shelf so as soon as you picked something up it was charged to your room-so I made sure my kids didnt touch it...the bathroom was small as well-sink and mirror in the same room with the toilet and shower....Only used the restaurant on the last day for breakfast-food was good but the prices were very expensive...did use the Starbucks on a couple of occasions for a quick meal...Very nice hotel would definitely stay here again

“Large room with nice touches” I was able to book a room at this hotel through Priceline at an extremely reasonable rate, so I wasn't expecting much. I was amazed to find a very large, comfortable, attractive room with a huge sectional sofa, the largest TV I've ever had control over, a desk, and a great bed. The staff was friendly enough. It seemed like a nice enough place that it should have had a restaurant, which is too bad given El Paso's dismal dining options. We didn't quite understand if breakfast was free, so we opted out. But the public areas were nice, like a cozy cafe, and the free internet was icing on the cake. Color me very impressed for the price.

“not a top hotel, but better than most alternatives” This hotel bills itself as a top five star boutique hotel, which it is certainly not. The facilities are a bit dated and worn. The place feels like a chain hotel converted into something that was supposed to be hip, but this plan did not really come to fruition. There are telltale signs of the old chain hotel past everywhere, mixed with some southern style elements, mixed with some Mondrian hotels style elements, all of which does not quite go together. The tastefulness of the decor is also highly debatable. On the positive side, the Zaza does have very good facilities, solid food outlets, a nice pool, a spa, atmospheric lighting, and whatever else you may need. Service is efficient and on par with what you would expect in any upper midrange hotel. The generous breakfast policy and the courtesy bar cart in the lobby set a friendly tone. Services and facilities are solid and clean. To my knowledge there are also not really any alternatives in Houston in this category. So if you want to stay at a somewhat unique property instead of at a random chain hotel, the Zaza is probably the place to go.

“Consistently Good” I have stayed at Hyatt Place El Paso several times. The staff is consistently friendly and helpful. The breakfast bar is always well stocked and nicely presented. Rooms are large with HDTVs, refrigerators, nice amenities. Air conditioners can be a bit noisy. Location is fine next to I-10 but is not in a pedestrian-friendly area. I recommend this hotel for anyone on business in or passing thru El Paso.

“Fantastic , Historic, worth every dollar” This historic hotel is worth a visit. We stayed in the Arizona wing (valley bldg) which was recently renovated. We even had a terrace which is a nice plus. This Frank Lloyd Wright building design is historic and the entire resort stays in character. Some of the furniture was re-upholstered and rightfully so. The carpets, Flat Panel, and bathroom however are 21st century. The main pool is nice, so are the several smaller ones. The staff is very attentive, polite, and cater to every whim. I can't say enough good things. Had dinner in the main dinning room. The $35 pre-fix is the best bargain. Nothing is cheap here, but it's reasonable for a 5 star hotel. Mini-fridge will store some items, but this isn't the place to go to save money, this is a splurge. You may want to consider the 'concierge level' Aside from liquor, computer access, other amenities, they also provide all day snacks, lunch and breakfast. Desert at night. Worth the $85 a day if you plan on drinking several $20 martini's during your stay. Yes the $28 resort fee sucks, but it's better than being nickel and dimed to death at the Pointe Hiltons. As for the $15 a day self parking fee, don't tell them, they won't charge you. For the record, I got a sale price under 200 a day, the same price I paid at the Point Hilton Tappatio and Sqaw peak. Wish I stayed here all 3 days.

“Great stay, great location” This was fifth hotel I stayed at with my wife on our honeymoon-roadtrip and it was definitely a nice hotel, we had a great view of Philly and the room was large and luxurious. We were in Philly for Independence Day so it was an interesting stay. Only minor complaints. Presentation (4/5) Overall the room was excellent, very luxurious and clean. I wasn't a huge fan of the shower, but that is minor. One thing I found weird was while the lobby and rooms were air conditioned, the hallways of the hotel were not. This isn't a big deal, but a bit strange when exiting the hotel you go from cold, to hot, to cold, to hot again (outside). I understand that this is probably to save energy, so I guess it's OK. Service (4/5) The service was good at the Omni, none of the staff were overly friendly but they weren't necessarily rude either. Room Service/Dining (N/A) We didn't eat in the hotel, we only stayed one night and didn't really have the time. Location (5/5) The location of the Omni couldn't be better, right outside independence hall. We had a view of the park and the water, very nice. We also got to see fourth of July fireworks in our room, great location.

“So glad we stayed here!” We were visiting WIndsor, Canada, so we flew into Detroit. I have heard horror stories about Detroit, and had a little trepidation about staying there. Man, was I wrong. The Inn on Ferry Street is absolutely fantastic, and we walked around the area pretty extensively in the evenings, and never had any reason to fear. It's a great location, and the Inn itself is just fantastic! Beautifully cared for, and the staff was so kind and willing to go the extra mile. The shuttle was very convenient also. It was fantastic to see this carefully restored piece of history, and I'll stay again any time I am in Detroit.

“Great Hotel in a great location!!!” We drove down from northern NJ on Memorial Day Weekend and researched this hotel for about a month. This is a great hotel in a beautiful area of the inner harbor of Baltimore. The staff is well versed on working a hotel of the nature and from parking to check-in was a breeze. The price of this hotel isn’t cheep but it is well worth it. On previous recommendation we heard that the harbor view was the way to go and boy it was worth every penny of the extra money. The rooms are large enough for a family of four and very nice. It was true about the hall noise could be heard through the door but it stopped after 8 pm but the activity and noise from the street could be a problem if you are not accustomed to city life. The hotel is connected to a very nice mall and is in walking distance to everything to see in the inner harbor area. The restaurant and lounge in the hotel are first class and kids under eight eat free, with a child menu for kids under fifteen. This is great because the food isn’t cheep but the meals are worth it. The harbor restaurants in the area fill up fast so it is nice to have a nice place to eat with kids to avoid the wait near the water. Our family of four with young children found this hotel very kid friendly and accommodating to every adult need and more. We will be back for another two night in the near future as soon as our new addition arrives and try to fit five in a room ( if they let us ). Great place great location, give it a try!

“wonderful hotel with excellent gym” This is an amazing hotel. The staff makes it stand out. At one point, I realized that I was allergic to the toiletries, and to my suprise they went across the street to CVS and purchased full-sized Aveeno products. The fitness center is first-rate. I am very excited to go back.

“Perfect location and helpful staff” Dallas is the first stop on our road trip this year, we are staying in downtown close to the sixth floor JFK museum on Elm Street. There are a few unsavoury characters about but you expect that downtown. We have to pay $12 a day parking which is offset by the free wifi in the room. We were very impressed by the reception staff especially Melody who was super friendly and helpful. If we had any problems they were sorted out immediately. The room is spacious the the kingsize bed is very comfortable. We are on the corner of the building so we have a balcony overlooking much of downtown Dallas. There is a pool area on the ninth floor which is very welcome in this heat. If we want to visit central Dallas you won't go far wrong with Crowne Plaza and the price is affordable.

“lovely hotel” We arrived at our hotel after a late flight, a few problems to start with, all ironed out within an hour of arriving by the most helpful manager, who treated us extremely well and couldn't do enough for us. The hotel is completely wheelchair friendly, the room extremely spacious and clean, Town center about a 15 minute walk. The bar and restaurant very nice and reasonably priced. I cannot fault the staff or manager we saw at this hotel, I would recommend this hotel to anybody wanting to vacate in Philadelphia.

“The best of four Hiltons we tried in NYC” This week we stayed at the Waldorf, Doubletree Guest Suites Times Square, the Millenium Hilton and this one. This one was the best. Waldorf was poor, over priced and impersonal. Doubletree had a great location but tiny rooms. Millenium was friendly but noisy because of the building at Ground Zero. Hilton Times Square ticks all the boxes. Great location, warm welcome ( even though the current refurb works means you go in via a side entrance) good size rooms. This is the one we will go back to.

“Amazing location, lovely rooms” Recently stayed at The Melrose for business/pleasure in Uptown Dallas. Our room was fabulous--- spacious, well appointed, with super comfortable beds. The gym facilities were nice, on par with some larger, chain hotels. The hotel was incredibly quiet, which was great for work and relaxation. The location is excellent for walkability, as there are tons of shops, restaurants, and bars nearby. The only criticism we had was of the service in The Library (bar). The first night we were there, we were essentially ignored by the waitstaff. We thought it was a fluke and returned a few nights later, only to be ignored again. Our drinks were still enjoyable, we just were forced to hunt down our waiter for both our drinks and our tab. Regardless, we'll visit The Melrose again. Overall, a great stay.

“Fine if you can get a good rate” The rooms here were very comfortable, quiet and well-appointed (including irons). Bathroom very good too, and very clean. A good view from a high-rise window was pleasant too. In the nearby area there are plenty of interesting restaurants and bars. The big down-side to this hotel is it is a moderate distance (up a hill) to the nearest Subway station, on 3rd Avenue. Some attractions are within walking distance, such as the art museums around Central Park, but there aren't many other things so you'll really need to use the Subway. Unless, of course, you need to be in the Upper East Side, in which case this location is great. You don't really need all the features of this hotel given you're in NYC, so whilst it is comfortable and generally fine, you really need to find a good rate to justify staying at this hotel.

“A Real Find” For about $90 a night (including tax), I got a full kitchen, a big closet, secure free parking and a comfortable room right behind the Hollywood/Highland shopping center. There's even a little computerized safe you program yourself. The front desk people were very helpful as well. The place is on the old side, the pool isn't heated in December and the layout of my room was odd (the bath was well off from everything else), but who cares? I'd stay here again in a heartbeat.

“extremely quiet room” I stayed here for a one-night layover at LAX, based on online reviews. The room was one of the quietest I've ever stayed in, which is exactly what I needed. Staff was friendly, decor pleasing. My only complaint is that they use styrofoam cups instead of water glasses and coffee cups. Unfortunately I had to leave before the complimentary breakfast opened (at 6am). So did a lot of other guests--an earlier start time would be great.

“Great Stay!” My husband and I stayed here for our 15th wedding anniversary trip. I had booked a superior room, but when we arrived for check in they were all taken. So they upgraded us to a park-view suite! That totally made our whole week-end. The room was fantastic. The hotel is beautiful. The lobby is very intimate and inviting. All the staff were really warm and friendly. The location is the best in the city, right across the street from the park and Grace Cathedral on the very top of Nob Hill. I would absolutely stay here again. Even if I hadn't gotten such a fantastic room, the staff, the location, the warm decor make this a wonderful hotel.

“My usual place in Boston” The staff is consistently good at this location, including very friendly club lounge, though club is tight. When I returned to my room and found my laundry bag was never picked up, I was rather upset as it was Friday and I had no clean clothes. This was an important moment for me. At first I was told there was nothing they could do, but the bellman sent the bag out and I had everything laundered within a few hours. This was amazing service and I am very pleased that the hotel took such care of me after their error. Thanks!
“Great hotel and service” Ffor any hotel in this price category, $15 per night for WiFi, and $14 for a drink-is just sleazy. And AT&T is almost impossible to make calls from the room.

“Delayed at airport - welcome stay” I missed my flight and was given a $55 voucher for this property. It's about 15 min. from the airport and they had a shuttle that took us and brought us back in the AM. The guy that checked our van in was friendly and efficient, dealing with the stress well. My only fault with him was that he mentioned everyone's room number, loud enough for everyone to hear. I asked him not to announce mine and he respected my wishes. He signed me up for the 5:30AM shuttle and asked if I'd like a wake-up call. The room was surprisingly big and very comfortable. At 1AM (when I got in) the tv next door to me was quite loud but I made a quick call to the guest and he turned the volume down. I was on the first floor and heard a lot of folks going to the elevator but it wasn't too bad. Where I was super impressed was that the breakfast buffet didn't start until 6am but the same front desk guy knowing that a bunch of cranky passengers were on the 5:30 shuttle had breakfast ready around 5:15 for us. It was a well-appreciated touch.

“Solid Performer” I attended a business meeting at this hotel and found it to be great. My guestroom was very comfortable, great wireless internet speed, and the bed was very clean & comfortable. Also, the gym was very good. The staff was professional and friendly, and seemed to care about the guests of the hotel. The food at all breaks and meals was exceptional. All other elements of the meeting went very well too. I travel almost every week of the year on business, and I would highly recommend this hotel.

“Beautiful Blakely” I stayed at this hotel Nov. 28/29 with friends. Too bad we only had one night; we all loved the Blakely! Terrific West side location surrounded by lots of restaurants. Subway is right outside. Wish we had time to try the Italian restaurant in the hotel; menu looked impressive. Huge room; spotless; modern take on British decor; flat screen TV/CD players. Loved the marble bathrooms and the "computerized" shower (You punch in the temperature you want) Great water pressure. Hated to get out of the comfy bed. Hotel was very quiet; there are only a handful of rooms on each floor. Some street noise outside, but this is New York! In-room safes, plenty of storage space. The lifts are tiny, however, but fast and efficient. Will absolutely return. This is a sister hotel to the Elysee, another favorite.

“"Shagalicious, baby!"” I spent two nights at the James Hotel while attending a conference in Chicago. I received an upgraded room upon checking in, even without requesting one. The room was very nice--straight out of an Austin Powers movie, complete with a shag rug and corner bed/couch with a projection dvd player with surround sound. In fact, the room also included an additonal fairly large flat panel tv in the main area, a smaller one facing the bed (though I couldn't get this one to work) and a small stereo cd unit. Probably not everyone's style, but I thought it was pretty cool. While I was alone, I'd think it would be a great choice for a couple. Service staff (front desk, bellman) were very helpful and courteous. Location is quite good to the Chicago hot spots, but pretty far from McCormick Place, as most of the area's hotels are.

“elegant” This is a gorgeous property. I stayed here two nights on points and was upgraded to the executive floor. The staff (actually, every single member of the staff I encountered) was superb. Caring, informative, funny (in a lot of cases). The ambience is quietly elegant. Fresh flowers, really impressive public spaces. Beds, as usual for Hiltons, are incredibly comfortable, and linens and towels are top quality. The only thing I would change is the lobby music. The automated player Kawai in the Sierra lounge for breakfast is really just noise pollution, as are the uninspired renderings of the blonde cocktail pianist later in the day. But I'm a musician, so my ear is hyper-attuned to such things.

“Enjoyed our 5-night stay” We were a group of 4 staying in a queen queen room which was large enough and very comfortable. The rate we purchased included the continental breakfast. Upon check-in I was not given the certificates so I had to go back to the lobby to obtain them. It wasn't a big deal because they corrected the mistake without any hassle. The bathrooms are small but it is OK because they use that space in the actual room. It was nice that the shower had pumps that dispense the shower gel, shampoo and conditioner. The breakfast is pretty standard but arrive early so you can get some of the better pastries and cereal. On Sunday we waited too long to go downstairs so they stop stocking and we couldn't get exactly what we wanted but it was still OK. The room was cleaned daily and early in the day so when we arrived at the hotel after a long day of walking and sightseeing we arrived to a nice clean room. The first night we noticed that the room was hot so we called and the technician came up to fix the unit so we enjoyed the rest of our stay in a nice cool room. The staff was very nice. The best part of this hotel is the location. There is a Whole Foods a few blocks away and that came in really handy for a quick bite and water. There are a bunch of restaurants and its convenient to the major attractions within walking distance. The fitness center is a little crammed but you can always run outside like the locals. The internet connection is solid. We didn't do the wine hour but there were a lot of people there so it must have been nice. The bar also has a happy hours so Friday night it was packed with people but they were not disruptive for people that need to go in and out of the hotel lobby.

“Good Hotel For Business” I stayed here for two nights. I was VERY VERY THANKFUL the hotel allowed me to check-in early in the a.m. Some hotels just will not allow this even if space is available. They saved the day for me. The room was large clean and well appointed. VERY comfortable bed. No extra fee for internet, water, and use of facilities. The Molly Trolley stops right in front of the hotel to take you to the downtown eateries for free. All of these things make a difference to me in figuring out if I would return. The only con is that I found the front desk to be sort of lukewarm towards our business group. No smiles or emotions, just getting the job done. After they would get off the phone with a guest, they would roll eyes, make curt comments, shake head, etc . . . I would definitely stay here again for business if the price is right.

“Better Than Expected” I researched TripAdvisor to find a modestly priced hotel within walking distance of Riverwalk that we would only use for two nights. And the first night would come after a 9 hour drive from New Orleans to San Antonio. This hotel was way better than expected. Even with our limited stay, we didn't get full value. We briefly participated in their happy hour festivities the night we arrived, before going out to dinner. But we didn't partake of the events the second night or have the free breakfast either morning. How dumb are we!? In fairness we wanted to experience the city in the brief time we had there. But certainly if you are on a budget or with a family, these perks would be very valuable. For us the greatest advantage was a the hotel's back entrance being right on Riverwalk. We were quickly immersed in the beautiful night lights on our way to dinner both nights. And we used the exit to get to our tour of the Riverwalk itself. Not a premium price for the hotel but a premium entrance to the attraction. I had mixed feelings about the room which is why I gave this hotel 4 stars. This was a full suite including a separate living room with TV and pull-out sofa bed. So it was bedroom to living room to bathroom. That was nice. But the rooms seemed darker than they had to be. Even with two windows in the bedroom, the off-colored curtains made the room dark, not bright and sunny. Dare I say a bit dingy. But on the whole, much better than expected. And as I said, probably the best bargain on Riverwalk especially if you take advantage of the free happy hour and breakfast.

“Great, central, comfortable hotel” The Conrad is good, traditional elegance, with friendly, helpful staff. The lobby is bright and spacious with a popular-looking bar and nice outdoor area for summer. Our room was large and comfortable. Huge, cosy bed, armchair, desk, etc. Big windows. Both a bath (deep and nice) and a shower, and a separation door between toilet and the rest of the bathroom. Only disappointments were no in-room coffee/tea maker, and no swimming pool.

“A very nice hotel” I stayed here for one night on a business trip. The hotel is centrally located in Chicago on Rush Street. I was able to walk everywhere i needed to go which included Al's Italian Beef and Gino's East Pizza. The hotel is a $45 taxi ride from O'Hare Airport. Checkin is on the 5th floor lobby. The hotel is very nice and clean considering it is in an old building. My room was clean and a decent size. Bathroom was very roomy. The bed was very comfortable as were the pillows. I slept very well. Internet was free. Unfortunately I did not get to use the gym or Spa. We had catered meals in the meeting rooms which were quite good. If the quality of the food was an indication of the restaurants then I wouldnt mind eating there. The staff at the front desk was very helpful and courteous. Checkin took me literally 45 seconds. If you are here on business this is definitely a great hotel to stay at.

“Second time, great stay” Returning for second time. Big shout out to Abiy at the front desk for making me feel welcome and accommodating a couple of special requests. Not much to add over my previous review, this place is great. Quiet, clean, modern style. This is a difference from the Westin St Francis, which is more well known and has its own character. For me the westin market is more my style and the rooms are way bigger. Try La Boulange on Market street for French coffee and pastries, far more interesting then the Starbucks across the street from the hotel - though definitely convenient if you need it.

“Super Location for Excellent City Experience” We left the car with the valet parking and quickly checked in with out a problem. The room was immaculate, fresh and up to date. The Christmas throng was in good chjeer and the Gingerbread houses were a main hiliday feature. This is a Great Sheraton property. But the main attraction is the bustle of the Seattle stores that are in the immediate area. Further there are a number of excellenet resturants ready to meet your every need. We were most impressed by the reasonable price for this city get-away. We will return without a doubt.

“Great location - just a few little things keep this from a 5-star rating” Beautiful hotel! Service was impeccable - everyone was so friendly, starting with check-in experience, including all housekeeping staff... Just a few things that keep this hotel from getting 5 stars. 1. It's a bit worn. Yes, it's an old hotel and it's definitely charming, but a bit more attention to detail would bring this up a bit in the ratings. Blotches on the wallpaper, cracked tiles in the bathroom... 2. Missing towel hoop in the bathroom. Saw a chrome "blob" on the wall. Spied a chrome "hoop" under the sink. Put 2 and 2 together and realized the hoop should be fitted to the blob to make a towel hoop. 3. The iron had a scorched soleplate that exactly matched a scorched spot on the ironing board cover. Luckily, we had dark-colored clothes to iron, but would have been leery of ironing lights with that. I'm sure the scorched discoloration would have transferred. 4. Yeah, this is petty: We had no "do not disturb" door hanger for our room. That said, the property is in a great location. We slept VERY well, and the bed was comfy. The hotel is amazingly quiet - we rarely heard even hallway noise. The maze of hallways is intriguing! The elevators are nicely divided among floor groupings. Unfortunately, we arrived too early to get our preferred room, and were on the 12th floor; these elevators are shared with convention services, so we were quite often delayed by stopping for those attending meetings and traveling between floors 4 and 7. Spent our two nights trying desperately to rationalize a 5-star rating on Tripadvisor, but settled for four. It could honestly be better. And it could be a WHOLE lot worse!

“another solid stay” For $83 on Priceline we got a clean an comfortable room, with excellent service at the front desk. Hotel shuttle bus works well to and from airport, and the adjacent Daily Grill's happy hour (4 - 7 pm) is well worth attending if you want great food and drink at a reasonable price. There's a bit of plane noise outside, but nothing that kept me awake at night. We continue to be very happy when we get a four star bid accepted by the Westin Los Angeles Airport.

“What you expect from a top hotel” After spending a few nights at the Hudson Hotel, the Sofitel was a godsend! Simple, clean, elegant and large rooms. The service was good from the front desk, the concierge and the doormen. The next time I am in New York the Sofitel will be getting my business.

“loed the conrad” Beautiful, modern and well located. SERVICE IS EXCELLENT. Rooms are gorgeous and beds are very very comfortable. Hi definition TV in room and flat screen in generously sized bathroom. HIGHLY RECOMMENDED Attention to detail is obvious at this wonderful hotel.

“Comfort and class” Spent two nights here after reading other reviews and throughly enjoyed the time here. Hotel is small and immaculate. Staff is attentive to needs. One suggestion, book a room that does not face Park. Neighborhood still a little iffy, but close enough to downtown and Inner Harbor. Used their town car service coming in from BWI. Even with three changes in arrival time, thanks to airline chaos, the car was ready at the airport.

“Amazing service” I stayed on business for two evenings and from check-in to check-out came across the some of the most professional and helpful staff I've ever encountered. There were no rooms ready upon check-in and yet the front desk person made several calls, upgraded my room, and made sure I did not have much of a wait. Additionally, she apologized for the wait - a real rarity and very much appreciated. Everything I requested, including a fan (yes crazy, but helps me sleep through the evening), they were able to meet. The valet and room service were always prompt. I took two early morning classes in the gym and both instructors were wonderful - I believe their names were Josh and Nikki. They were very helpful, patient, and great in explaining everything. The gym was large, very clean, and modern. I didn't encounter the thin wall issue (whcih is often tough) but I was upgraded to one of the top floor rooms which was very large. This is a wonderful hotel which I highly recommend.

“Good hotel, central location!” I stayed here for a conference in 2003. Since I just recently joined Tripadvisor, I thought I should offer my two cents to members on this one! The Swissotel Chicago is a great property for business, leisure and individual travelers. It is centrally located, and their staff is knowledgeable and able to provide you with very good ideas on activities as well we good input on where to dine, etc. We had a very enjoyable conference and I still have a vivid memory of the entire stay, though it has been a while since I have visited. Taking Swissotel´s operating standards into consideration, I am pretty sure that the service, quality and value provided than is still the same, or even improved to date. I would definitely stay here again if happen to return to Chicago.

“Very Nice, but Not Quite Top Shelf” We used Starwood points to get a room here for two nights. We started out on the seventh floor, but as we were entering the room, it became apparent that our neighbors were a bit rowdy. We had no problem getting the hotel to move us to a different room on the fifth floor - one which was very quiet our entire stay. Staff at the entrance and in the lobby were friendly and helpful. The decor of the room we ended up in was unremarkable; I think maybe we expected a bit more for the money/points. We had a balcony large enough to sit on (with two chairs and a small table), but it overlooked the front parking lot and lots of traffic. Might be worth asking if they have the same type of room overlooking the golf course in the back. Our room had a king size bed, a comfortable armchair, a desk, and flat screen TV. I didn't like it that no in-room coffee maker was available, but that seems to be pretty typical of high-end hotels. Our bathroom was exceptional, with marble floors, a large tub, separate shower, monogrammed towels and bathrobes, and Remede amenities. My wife complained about the length of time it took to get hot water in the room - several minutes. We generally liked the hotel, but might have been a bit less happy if we had paid full price. I wouldn't be surprised if we came back here, but we also might try someplace different just to see what's out there.

“Fantastic Choice for Location and Overall Stay Comfort” It's experiences such as these that remind you why your loyal to a Hotel chain. I was participating in the Rock and Roll Half Marathon in San Jose and the obvious choice was this property, located near to the start line in downtown SJ. Locating the Hilton San Jose was easy, being close to the 101 and the 87, as I drove from San Francisco. The property was not only 3 blocks from the race start line, but within walking distance of many restaurants and convenience shops. I found many things to like and none to hate about the hotel location. As the hotel was attached to the Convention Center, the parking was underneath both, and convenient to walk from your car to the lobby. The Convention center was also the location of the Health and Sports Expo for the race. The convenience of walking from your hotel elevator to the sports expo in less than 5 minutes with a full "swag bag" cannot be understated! The hotel check in was painless, and I was upgraded as a Diamond member to the Executive floor. The room was very nicely sized, and had a superb comfy bed. A testament to how comfortable it was is that I didn't care for once that they did not have a king bed available and had to provide a room with 2 double beds. Alas, the bathroom was a tub/shower combo, not the shower stall as some upgraded Hilton's have. Overall tho, the bathroom was roomy enough and the sink fixtures modern. The shower head had good water pressure but tended to spray the water outside the tub around the edges of the curtain. The view from my 18th story window was also superb, with visuals of the valley and nearby mountains. The Executive Club was good but small. In the mornings and evenings at peak hours, they ran out of chairs :-( Another sad note is the "Honor Bar" where they charge for alcohol. Having traveled to many international Hilton destinations where they still do NOT try to rake in every penny, I continue to be disappointed with this US Hilton implementation. The stay convenience of location came together as I woke up at 5am for the 8am race start gun and only had to walk 3 blocks away...No cars, no travel pressure, and a convenient race breakfast as the Hilton restaurant opened also at 5am. It was interesting and curious to see that although the Hilton was a sponsor of the race, no special amenities were prepared for runners staying there or recognition of the event in any way. I have stayed at other Hilton properties that took these recognition steps and would highly recommend that the San Jose Hilton do the same. For an example of another Hilton property, they can contact the Hilton Bonnet Creek in Orlando, FL, where special packages are prepared for the Disney Marathon Weekend, or the Embassy Suites in Philadelphia, PA for the Philadelphia Marathon. It's a touch of class and sophistication that appeals beyond words As I signed up for the race next year, I will be back to this property without a hesitation and will be sure to reserve early!

“I recommend this hotel” I was very happy with this hotel. The room was huge, the lighting was very nice, the bathroom was fully equipped including a jetted tub. I ate lunch and then breakfast at the restaurant in the hotel and the food was amazing. I am a picky traveler and this met all of my expectations.

“Love the Club Lounge!” I stayed here for one night with my husband. This is a very nice hotel, great position within city, The staff was very nice and very accommodating. We didn't eat at the hotel, but we did have a couple of drinks at the bar. The Club Lounge is great! You can got there for some apps and drinks before you go out, breakfast and afternoon soup. Every hotel should have this option. Parking is very expensive ($50 a night!!), so we parked across the street.

“Great Location and Stay” We had three rooms; two rooms w/my wife and five children & another room w/friends, two adults and their two children. Upon check-in at the SPG counter, Chuck really helped us by getting a connecting room and a third room next door. We got a Platinum SPG upgrade to a deluxe room on floor 27 in the new tower overlooking Union Square. Great view! Our children love the glass elevator and its views. We love this hotel and its location. The service is very friendly and helpful. The Michael Mina restaurant and bar across from it are both worth the experience. It's near Market St so you have mass transit readily available; buses, Bart, cabs, trolleys, etc. Many nice nearby restaurants w/in walking distance. We like to walk down Post to Grant (lft) thru China Town to Columbus (lft) thru North Beach, to Coit Tower, down backside and stairs to Fisherman's Wharf. It's a great walk w/many cool sites. Our children loved the zoo; especially the lion house up close. More pricey, the Science Museum in Golden Gate Park (expensive but worth it). AAA discounts on both. SF is just a fun city to visit. If it was warmer, we'd have taken the ferry to Tiburon and eaten lunch at Sammy's, I believe it's called. Great outdoor deck on water w/good food and atmosphere.

“Loved this hotel, I will go back!¬” I really liked this hotel. Having seen the pictures of the outside online, I had expected the hotel to be somewhat ordinary, functional and fairly sterile. It turned out to be none of these. The hotel recently went through an 8O million dollar renovation which has turned it into a trendy, funky but stylish place - although the outside (other than the grand glass entrance) still looks plain and uninspiring. When you walk into the lobby you are warmly greeted and although it is a little gloomy you soon realise it has an interesting and unique style. There is, for example, a massive swirling steel sculpture in the centre and touches like a chair made of coins. The staff on reception are all chatty, tell you about the hotel and see you to the elevators. The hallways are bright and have a striking swirl designed carpet. The bedrooms are slightly quirky shape wise but this adds to the interest. The bathroom has no bathtub, only showers. The bathrooms are a good size and the basin is very modern, and the shower is fantastic. It has a large shower head above you so is kind of a "wet room" type of shower. As the bathroom has no window, there is a very clever solution as there is a large window in the shower that with a flick of a light switch makes it clear (so you can see into the bedroom and watch the TV while showering, the sound already plays in the bathroom which is something I always like). The bedrooms are not huge but have an enormous and very comfortable bed with amazingly soft pillows and high quality bed linen. There is a good sized desk to work at and internet access is about Ten Dollars. Another nice touch is the large flat screen High Definition TV. On the lobby level is an enormous bar which is trendy and attracts a hip crowd most evenings but is very busy on the weekend. The restaurant the other side is also great looking and the food pretty good. One stunning feature is the large fitness centre. This has loads of great equipment, is stylish and has nice touches like free bottles of water, fruit, internet access stations and even chocolate brownies as a treat for working out. The meeting facilities are good and team very helpful. I would love to stay here again. Not only for the hotel but a brilliant location with Beverly Mall opposite and seemingly zillions of very good places to eat around (every night we had some celebrity at a table next to us). I have poseted a video of my room (415) on tripadvisor or you can cut and paste this link to see the video: [--]

“First class Fort Worth property” My husband and I stayed at the Omni when we were in town for a wedding. Service is impeccable from check in to check out and everywhere in between. The rooms are flawless and stunning. I am a snob about beds (my husband and I hate leaving our TempurPedic) and I can not overstate how AMAZING the beds at the Omni are. Best hotel beds I've ever slept in. Room service is a vast selection and delicious (I highly recommend the venison chili). I did not like that the room we stayed in had only a shower, but I bet if I had asked for one before check in they would have accommodated. This hotel is first rate. The quality of the service and the property surpass and Loews, Waldorf Astoria or Ritz I've ever stayed in.

“Recently updated” Looked beat up from the outside but rooms are modern with flat screens, extra electrical outlets, MP3 compatible clocks, etc. Fitness center had a bunch of elipticals, free weitghts and some nautilus. Breakfast buffet is great if you get a free voucher or expensive if not. 1/2 mile walk to Stapleton Mall where you can shop but not necessarily eat higher end food.

“Great property in DC” I completed a two night stay at this property and was pleased. The staff is a real high point here, they are very friendly and attentive to SPG status and amenities. Rooms are large and feature spacious bathrooms with separate vanity and walk-in shower. This is a solid option in DC and I look forward to return.
“perfect location” the newly renovated rooms were modern and very comfortable.bathroom is huge.perfect location for shopping,newberry st,boston common.very good service and beautiful lobby.

“A great place......” I have been here about 5 times in the last five years...and have enjoyed it. The staff is a little pushy, but the rooms have been recently renovated and I will stay here again. Great location!!

“Nice Hampton Inn” We spent the winter in Austin but the house we rented was already rented out for the SXSW festival. Somehow we got our dates mixed up and came home to find the festival renters still in our house! Luckily it was the last day of the festival and we were able to get a room at this Hampton Inn, not far from the house. The room was clean and quiet. They were doing some maintenance in the front so the main door was inaccessible, but it was not a problem. We spent a very comfortable night there.

“Very Nice” Whenever we go to Chicago we stay here. I really enjoy the location and love the view. My boyfriend works during the day, and it's across the street from a movie theatre, which is a strange perk, but I like it. Also, a very cool bowling alley/bar is in the vicinity along with a great sushi place. The doormen are very helpful. If you need a good recommendation on Chicago Style pizza, hit them up. One day, my key became demagnetized while my boyfriend was at work. I went to the desk, but since my name wasn't on the room, they wouldn't make me a new one. Most people would see this as an inconvenience, but I see it as a sign that this hotel takes safety seriously. I like that. There are also these awesome interactive tabletops in the lobby. You can play chess, checkers, all sorts of things. Very trendy and cool. The rooms are nice, clean, and the beds are very comfy. Mini-bars are in the rooms. I've stayed in a suite, which is HUGE, also in a regular king which isn't as big but very nice. The room service is top notch the delivery people were always very friendly. This hotel is really good and come highly recommended.

“Lovely updated hotel” The Conrad was a very nice hotel. I stayed there one night on a business trip, and found the service and rooms to be outstanding - wished I could have stayed longer! It was convenient to my meetings in the financial district, but the area is still under heavy construction, so expect a limited selection of restaurants, and some challenges in getting around. Those issues, however, are temporary. I would recommend this hotel if you need to be near the financial district or WTC.

“We would stay here again” We stayed here with a park and fly rate and then returned here for a night after our trip. There was a sign in front that said newly renovated and that certainly appeared to be the case. Check in was efficient and cordial. The first night we had a standard king room. Vanity was inside the small bathroon and set at an angle. Not a lot of space on vanity top but the lighting was very good. The room appeared freshly painted and the light fixture in the bathroom was new. It was odd that after the old light fixture was removed, the new one was put up without painting where the old one had been. Left the area behind the light looking dirty and it would have been an easy fix. The coffee maker is on a small corner shelf inside the room. It was very easy to find room for our luggage in the decent sized room. Complimentary breakfast begins at 5:00 am which was great for early fliers. Cereal, sausage, scrambled eggs, waffles, etc. The shuttle, which we signed up for when we checked in, was right on time. We did have to stop at the nearby LaQuinta which had quite a number of passengers to load and we were full going to DIA. We only had a short wait to catch the shuttle to return to the Quality Inn.We checked in around 10:30 pm for our 2nd night and were upgraded to a king mini suite. There was a fridge, microwave and coffee maker on a counter in one corner as well as a couch and chairs sitting area. The vanity was outside the bathroom and had lots of room on top. It was in large enough area that our suitcases also fit in there. Although the vanity area had plenty of light, the bathroom light was very limited and dim. Due to the arrangement of the room, the flat screen TV was to the side of the bed and not the most convenient bedtime viewing.The air conditioner worked great and it was a comfortable bed and sleep.The fitness room needs to add an elliptical. One of the best things had to be the efficient shuttle system with the pleasant drivers. We would be fine with staying here again.

“Love Every Minute” The Willard is full of history and elegance. Everything from the service to the room was top notch. It is pricey but beautiful. There are many weddings and functions going on but the rooms are clean, spacious, and quiet. Would return.

“Highly recommend this hotel for a multi-day stay in NYC with family” Stayed for 3 nights in April (room 1214) and highly recommend it. Spring break with my teenage son and adjoining room with relatives. Adjoining rooms were located right off the elevator lobby and ice machine but it wasn't loud at all. Really heard nothing. Walls were very soundproof. This hotel is in a great location very close to Times Square (on 8th Ave between 48th and 49th). Lots of places very close by on 8th Avenue (Starbucks, Food Emporium, liquor store, bodega). Restaurant nextdoor, Pigalle, was very good. Breakfast for 4 (eggs, homefries, toast, juice, coffee) was $100. I went to Food Emporium the next morning for breakfast sandwiches. Great beds, pillows and down blanket. Fridge, microwave. Flat screen. Safe. Free wifi. Bathroom was small but spacious countertop (many hotels in NYC have little to no bathroom counter space). Good shower. Excellent service. The rooftop bar is not accessible from the hotel; have to go around the corner to a special door. Couldn't go due to a private party but pics looked nice. Would definitely return.

“Gorgeous” We stayed here over Christmas and New Year 2010/2011. This hotel is beautiful. The rooms are lush (if you are able to get a room that is not in-facing that is). The staff were great and nothing was too big or too small. We didnt find any attitude or snottiness from any staff member - it was all great! Don't miss out on the restaurant downstairs - especially for brunch!

“Great value for us, NO complaints.” Boston is a little expensive for us but this place fit our budget. Sometimes though thats the only thing thats right, but not this time. We're a family of four wanting to see a Red Sox game, take a Duck tour, and walk the Freedom Trail and tour Boston from the observatory of the Prudential building. We arrived early and found that our room was ready and we could settle in. The room was spacious, comfortable and clean. All we could ask for. Of the seven places we stayed on our 12 day trip, this was in the upper group. It was in walking distance of Fenway Park, the Prudential building, the Duck tour and easily accessable to the Green LIne. I'm sure there are other frills that someone might miss here but we rarely are in our room when vacationing and all we ask is that its clean and comfortable.

“Great Stay at LAX” Stayed at this property earlier this week. This hotel has recently been redone and it is a serious building, built in a way which is completely different from "newer" hotels. Room was very nice, quiet and very well outfitted/furnished. Bar was a nice place to relax and get a bite to eat. Bed was great for a good nights sleep which wasn't anywhere near long enough, damn you 4 am! When I got down stairs the team was buffing the marble floors, vacuuming the carpet and making sure everything was in it's place. I would definitely stay here again, solid, quiet and well appointed.

“A break from the madness” In selecting a budget-level hotel for a quick overnight visit on a weekend that seemed to command high hotel rates, I chose between staying near the train station and staying near the Broadway show we would see. I picked the latter. I knew it would not be as fun as staying in some neighborhoods, but we were looking for speed and value this time around. While this Comfort Inn is just a block off of Times Square, etc. and all that madness - the Naked Cowboy seems to never age - I had one of the best sleeps I've ever had after returning at midnight from said show. We were on the fourth floor with a "no view" window facing two brick walls and it was absolutely silent (and dark because of the walls). I guess room choice really does make a difference. Room is NYC small but I've stayed in smaller here, actually - there was space in this one for a chair and a desk. The bed was comfortable, HBO on the TV though we didn't watch it much, a clean and workable bathroom with hair dryer, tissues, shampoo, soap, We did use the safe to store our valuables. It's in a very large closet with light, which would be nice for stowing suitcases if you were staying for several days. The staff was kept busy as there were a number of senior citizens staying who seemed to need extensive help with directions, and foreign tourists. I do greatly appreciate we were able to get a room when we checked in early. Breakfast consisted of waffles, bagels, cereal, fried egg patties, hard boiled eggs, yogurt, raw fruit, coffee and juice - plenty of choice for me though I guess it would get old every day. Cramped and crowded in the breakfast room so we ate in our room. And yes, the elevator is verrrrrrrrry slow. Overall, this is a fine budget hotel, but keep the word budget in mind. If you want something a little nicer or in a more interesting neighborhood, scan the sales in advance.

“Nice stay at the W Washingotn” Stayed at the W Washington from June 18-21. When checking in, we were nicely greeted by Salome. She was very helpful in answering our questions, and when our room was not quite ready, she gave us tickets for a complimentary drink at the bar. On the next day, she also had water and fruit delivered to our room at no charge. As SPG members, we were also upgraded to a suite and given the options of either free internet in our room or SPG points. The location of the hotel was great. We were near the White House, and Metro Center, so we were able to easily get everywhere we needed to go. The suite was nice. Spacious and clean. The bathroom was good size so that more than one person could be in there at the same time. Only problem was that the water from the shower kept leaking out. I would definitely stay at this hotel again.

“Great hotel in Philadelphia” I stayed at the Westin for a conference for three days, and it was a great choice for a hotel. Close to Rittenhouse Square and many good restaurant, and the room provided the good quality the Westin properties are known for. The beds are awesome (heavenly beds)!! The staff was great and very helpful; concierge recommendations provided the basis for an awesome dinner at a nearby restaurant.

“visit to worthington, ohio” I wasn't sure about the place but decided to book anyways since it was short notice. The hotel though dated and in need of some repairs suited my needs accordingly. I requested a 2 bedroom handicap accesible room and was not disappointed. Sure the comments earlier by people about the train noise made me wonder what I may be geting into but.... The hotel staff and room were great. The noise from the train was tolerable to the extent that you get what you pay for. Overall, experience was good. Would come again.

“Very Good...but beware if you dont like noise” This hotel has a lot of pluses but I want to highlight one concern...this is a noisy property. The corridors on each level are extremely long. Noise travels easily along them at all times of the day and night. I was constantly disturbed during the day while working in my room - the maids were chattering and laughing - it was very distracting. The walls are very thin too and there is a surprisingly big gap under the doors - just more opportunities for noise to travel. I was woken at around 4.15 by the guy delivering newspapers - he through the newspaper under the door and it made a loud sound as it landed on the marble entry way. As a Diamond member I received access to the lounge but no room upgrade.

“Awesome hotel!!” I was assigned this hotel through priceline and I was a bit concerned after reading some the reviews, however, I am happy to report a great stay!! I arrived from the airport around 10:30am. The front desk clerk was friendly and put me in a room right away on the 14th floor. The hotel lobby was clean, neat and trendy. As previous reviewers have mentioned, the lobby is two levels and requires going up stairs or taking a elevator to reach the main bank of elevators. One of the downsides to this hotel is that you can find yourself waiting awhile for an elevator (to take you the your room). However, I have noticed this in several hotels in Manhattan The room itself was incredibly small. I've never seen anything like it. However, it was clean, modern and trendy. I expected a small room given it is in Manhattan. The bed was ultra comfortable with luxury linens. There was a nice ipod dock/clock radio and a LCD tv. This was the first time I actually received HDTV in a hotel room. It was pretty cool. The bathroom was quite spacious and very modern. Overall I thought the room met my needs. I would like to highlight the great service from the concierge (Meg I believe). She was extremely friendly and got me where I needed to go. She even gave me her contact information for when I was out and needed mobile assistance. The location of this hotel is IDEAL. It is in a very trendy part of Manhattan near the Four Seasons and luxury botiques. Really neat. One of the only downsides to this hotel was the outrageous internet price. I was charged over $30 dollars over 2 days for 2.5 hours of internet use. A little crazy if you ask me. All in all I would stay here again in a heart beat.

“Great location, great service. Rooms need upgrades for the price you pay here.” I would say that overall we were satisfied with our stay. The service was incredible. You can't beat the location. There is great shopping and tons of excellent restaurants within walking distance. As a matter of fact, the Crescent is in the same complex as the Capital Grille, Nobu and Stanley Korshak. The building is a beautiful one. Probably my favorite building in Dallas. The only drawback to this place, and it is kind of a big one, is that the rooms need updating and upgrading. The bed was pretty uncomfortable. There were several items that needed repair. The bathrooms needed an update badly. Everything else is great. But for the price, I'd stay somewhere else and then visit the beautiful Crescent complex. You can make a day out of it easily.

“Nice Hotel” Conveniently located in downtown Denver. $55 taxi to the airport. Beds were very comfortable and business travelers had plenty of room. Free coffee in the room was nice. Priced reasonably. I didn't try the restaurant or spa, so I can't comment. The customer service was fair, when checking out I asked for a receipt and she looked at me like I was crazy -- I know they emailed it to me but I wanted a receipt now -- no biggy.
“Wonderful staff, great location” Very large rooms, helpful congierge, easy to walk to Grand Central area,Rockerfeller Plaza, an even Times Square.

“Convenient” The hotel lobby was under renovation when we visited, so it was rather congested. The location is great. Many restaurants and museums nearby. The Mission Street Garage is 2-3 blocks away, so if you are driving but carrying limited number of carry-ons, the cost at the Garage is less expensive. You are next door to the MoMA, and within walking distance from the shopping area of town. The rooms are on the smaller side, but sufficient. The bathroom door is made out of almost-see-through frosted glass, so roommates beware. A good alternative from locations around Union Square.

“Great rate and a great stay” While we love to get out and have fun during the day, we enjoy a quiet place to lay our heads when it comes to down time. For this reason, Union Square and the waterfront areas wouldn't be a good choice for us, thus making this locale (and being on a high floor) much better for us. And while we.werent in the thick of the touristy stuff, we were close enough, with some walking & taxi's here and there, to get it all done while getting in some exercise to burn off all those Ghiradelli and Tony's pizza calories! Plus, love the Heavenly beds @Westin. All in all, yes the rooms are a bit on the generic, neutral side (I know a quick, easy fix for this if they want to contact me) but the staff was truly wonderful & it's a very nice hotel. In room breakfasts were quick, delish and reasonable and the rooms super clean plus when the dnd sign is on your door, they leave you alone. I like that!

“Very Suprised” Last minute trip to LA this summer, it was so late when we landed we elected to stay at the Embassy Suites North hotel next near our rental car agency. Not only were the rooms clean and spacious, the rate of $113 per night included free cocktails and breakfast the next morning. Every where I walked inside the hotel there were people cleaning and painting to keep the hotel in excellent condition. We were tired and the rate got us there, but I was truly suprised how nice the hotel was. Paid $300 plus many times at a beach hotel only to have a small room that is dirty. Congrats to this hotel, i will certainly stay there again.

“What Can I Say? Loved this Hotel.” I really loved this hotel. I think it should be a JW - much, much nicer than your typical Marriott hotel. The location is great, right on the Inner Harbor. The lobby is really stunning. When you walk in, there is a large "living room" area to your right. You can lounge here and take advantage of the free WiFi. I was upgraded to a Harbor View Room. I think the majority of the rooms have at least a partial view of the Inner Harbor. Very comfortable bed and nice amenities. My only complaint was the room temperature - I think the large windows absorb a lot of heat, making it hard to cool the room. That said, it was 100 plus degrees during my stay, so I really can't complain. I did not have much interaction with staff, but everyone I encountered was very, very pleasant. I would definitely return to this hotel if I wasn't moving to Baltimore very soon!

“Consistently a pleasant stay” I have stayed here many times over the last 2 years and it is always a very pleasant stay. From the warm cookies to the airport shuttle everything is delivered with great service and a smile. The rooms are average. Bedroom areas are nicely done and renovated, but the bathrooms are just average. This is a large spreadout hotel, so if you don't want to walk, make sure you tell them at checkin and try to get a room that is closer. I have not used the restaurant, but I have visited for several conferences and that food is always better than expected. The valet and shuttle service for stay and fly in great. It can be pricey, but I have snagged good deals a couple times (7 days parking and 1 night for $119!).

“Nice property, a little hard to find” Just returned from a night at this hotel and it is a nice property. Everything looks new and clean. Rooms are nicely decorated with a gold accent wall, flat screen TV, and a small kitchenette that has a fridge, cooktop, microwave and dishwasher. And there's a nice little swimming pool. As new and clean as it is, I will say it was difficult for us to find. Not impossible. But with Mapquest directions printed out, we still ended up doubling back and looking really hard for it. Once we spotted it, we almost passed the entrance, which is just past the hotel. It is located near the airport at the intersection of several highways, and is almost directly underneath one of the flyovers from one of the highways. That being said I would stay here again for certain things. We were visiting relatives so we weren't looking for a place to vacation. If that's what you're after, I wouldn't choose this hotel. The view out of our window was a wall from another part of the hotel. I didn't mind too much on this trip, but it's not what I want to see if I'm staying for several days. And at 5 a.m., the place is like Grand Central Station. I thought the entire hotel must have been leaving between 5 and 7 a.m. (Such is the plight of an airport hotel) But for our purposes it was fine. Last year we stayed at the Residence Inn Marriott/Stone Oak up on the 1604 Loop, which is a less congested, quieter, prettier area of San Antonio (albeit farther away from the Riverwalk and not in an area where there seems to be much to do). But that hotel wasn't as nice as this one, so I think we made the right choice in moving to the TownePlace Suites this time. The breakfast is also pretty good, with eggs, sausage, toast, yogurt, Oatmeal, and cereals.

“Gorgeous & Wonderful Location” We stayed one night at this hotel with our 2 children. It was very nice and clean. The beds were very comfy. The rooms are not huge but they are perfect for 2 people!!! Well decorated. The best part of this hotel is were it is located. You can walk anywhere you need to go. Valet is pricey just like every other hotel in SD. But they are very quick to get your car. The only problem we had was with the air conditioner unit, if we turned it on high it made a terrible noise. We never ate at the hotel because there are so many places around you can walk to. Also, shopping is right across the street.

“Brilliant location for sightseeing” I stayed here for a few night a few weeks ago. The hotel is a couple of hundred yards from Fisherman's Wharf and Pier 39. It couldn't be handier for restaurants and one of the sighseeing buses is based just around the corner. Because of its location it was a wee bit noisy at times but on balance the location trumps this. My room was a good size with a marvellous view over the Bay. The hotel staff couldn't have been more helpful. The hotel itself doesn't have a restaurant but there is a lovely wee 1950s type diner just out the backdoor of the hotel which serves the most delicious breakfasts.

“Wonderful hotel” This hotel is lovely and quiet and close to most everything we wanted to do in Philadelphia. The common rooms are very cozy, with the Continental breakfast (coffee, granola, fruit, pastries, toast, yogurt) served in the library. The staff are excellent. Our room on the second floor of the east side of the building was tastefully decorated with what looked like antique furniture. It was quiet at night. The curtains, however, did not block the light (I wore an eye mask). It was cold in Philadelphia when we were there, and they had a fire in the fireplace and homemade cookies for guests. We loved it here.

“Great business hotel” I stayed here for two nights for a business conference being held at the hotel. This is a very nice place. The lobby area is busy with people who congregate in the lounge...keep your eyes peeled, you might just spot a celebrity who is downtown for an event at the Staples Center (my colleague saw Patrick Dempsey right before the Clippers game). The room was very spacious and comfortable. It also had a gorgeous view - my room faced west, so I could see the sun set over the mountains every evening. All of the employees were very friendly and accommodating. It was very quiet at night, so I had no trouble sleeping. The meeting facilities where we had our conference were very nice. The hotel is part of LA Live, which features several restaurants, plus the Staples Center and Nokia Theater. The only downside to the location is that beyond the one block LA Live area, there isn't really anything interesting that you can walk to. That wasn't a problem for me since I was there for my conference though.

“Well Worth the Stay” So, I just had to see for myself: How can a nice hotel look like a prison? Well, with a little imagination, I could see the connection. However, that funny novelty aside, this is really a pleasant, refreshing place to stay with many nice attributes. The hotel itself is well maintained with a newer, bright, modern decor in a quiet parklike setting (even though it's next to a small airport, the plane noise was barely noticable). And that "prison" design actually helps give the place a bright, spacious feel (no long, dark corridors). To top it off the staff was great, the restaurant was solid (for hotel fare), the wireless internet was free (it worked most of the time), parking was free, the bed was comfy, it had a nice pool area, and the central location was great with about 10-20 minute drives to downtown, the zoo, Mission Bay, and La Jolla (plus you were out of the way of the hectic hotel corridors). A stay at the Four Points helped make for a great weekend getaway and I would definitely put it on my list for a return visit.

“Great hotel wonderful people” The JW is an outstanding hotel. I really enjoy staying there. The facilities are great. The gym is great (there are spots where the lighting could be better). I really enjoy grabbing a quick meal at the bar. The only poentially negative comment is that the restaurant is very noisy so it is difficult to have a dinner and discussion.

“excellent hotel one block from convention center” Stayed one night while attending meeting at the convention center. I had a conf rate so it was not outrageously expensive. Very nice room, regular hotel room. I asked for quiet room no feathers and I got no feathers. Room was across from elevator but I never heard it. There was a problem with whistling sound coming from under door (air pressure) during the first hour or so - which was fixed by placing a towel at the bottom of the door, but it was gone later that night. Hard Rock Hotel across the street can be a bit noisy at night as are the trains etc next to the conv center. This is not such a quiet area. I slept fine albeit with foam earplugs. No fault of hotel it's just the area is not quiet. Very modern guest room well appointed and with an operable window - very nice for air quality in the room. Window also seals well and is double pane so it is quiet. Valet parking at $32/day is expensive but if you want there is a public garage across the street. McCormick and Schmicks restaurant is in the hotel good for seafood. Cafe has good assortment of muffins and pastries do not have to order room service breakfast. Also good coffee. I would stay here again if I were attending a conference.

“Great Gem on Upper West Side” This is a great hotel and in my opinion gives you a great feel for what it might be like to live in NY. Three of us stayed in a 1 bedroom corner apartment which was massive. I've never know accommodation in NY to be so spacious. The hotel was originally apartments and there are some that are still homes which makes it all a little quirky. There is a great food market across the road which has everything and anything you might want and with a self catering apartment it is so convenient. There is a drugstore and a subway stop just abt 2mins walk away so you have easy access to the city. It might seem a bit inconvenient to stay away from the major tourist spots in the city but in fact I'd prefer to stay in this area in the future. You are also only a few blocks from Central Park which is great for a stroll to shake off the jetleg if flying longhaul like we did. We found some lovely bars and restaurants within a few blocks of the hotel and they seemed quite reasonably priced. The hotel staff are lovely, I could fault them in anyway. They are incredibley knowledgeable about the city and were able to answer any question we had. I was there first in Apr 2011 for work and am going back now on hols in Sep 2012 and am really looking forward to it

“Nice enough, but nothing special about it” It was hard to pick a star rating. I can't agree with any of the scathing reviews. But neither was this a faaaabulous hotel. We paid $200 each for 2 connecting rooms, and I would not be happy if we'd paid near rack rate ($300-400). We chose this because the other family we stayed with had a connection here. Otherwise, with our 3 kids (6-10), we'd have chosen someplace less pricey. Certainly the location is excellent. A quick walk by street or Riverwalk to everything we wanted to see in town. The bell and frontdesk staff were very nice. Room service quick and reliable (and super expensive as you'd imagine). Only poor service was from the concierges. They were fairly pleasant, but just not all that knowledgeable. I think I knew more just by having read TA reviews and forums. No turndown service, which surprised me and was kind of a bummer when we showered at nite and wanted fresh towels. Rooms were very nice and absolutely clean.
