There was no smell from pets, which had concerned me, since they are allowed. We were on the 10th floor, but our only view was into the parking lot : ) The shower seemed lovely with 2 showerheads, but was never hot and the temp fluctuated continuously, so couldnt really enjoy it. Low-end toiletries. Not sure what's meant by 'heavenly bath.' We had dinner at the restaurant (outside) one night, and that was quite good. There is one small terrace (the other is apparently a cigar terrace) on the main floor. We often played cards there after dinner. It would be nice if there were more space like that just to enjoy the outdoors. The pool is small but very nice. There is a bar/snackbar, but despite the pool area being totally full each day, it was not open. Don't know how they could possibly have enough space in the summer, but you dont choose a downtown hotel for the pool! I pick 4 stars as clean hotel and good service merit it. There was nothing actually wrong with it and it didn't stop us from having a great time in SA. But the hotel simply didn't add anything to our vacation. Only stay if you get a great price, or it's on your company tab!

“Good Hotel in mixed neighbourhood” The hotel is about 15 minutes drive from Downtown Houston and therefore a very reasonable priced option for people who have business in Downtown Houston but do not want to spent a lot at Hilton, Intercontinental etc.. The hotel is very clean and the staff friendly. Breakfast Buffet is above average. The rooms have had some upgrades. The location is adjacent to some mixed neighbourhoods. There is a security guard on duty during the night hours. The hotel has a business center with desktop PCs and a b/w laserprinter.
“Great hotel, very hospitable!” Great location. Great room with diamond membership - 42nd floor. room was very clean. view of the hudson river and chrysler building. front desk was very hospitable.

“Been Here Multiple times - Always Great” I have been to Memphis over 20 times for business and this is consistently my favorite place to stay. I think this was my fifth stay. Used to stay at the Peabody, but the service and hotel are no comparision. While Beale Street is close to the Peabody, take a taxi from here. Sit up on the porch in the afternoon and watch the Mississippi slip quietly by - people are always outgoing and friendly. Walk the neighborhood in the early AM or evening. Good local places to eat. Rooms are a bit pricey, but you get what you pay for and I have NE VER had a bad experience here. Try it out.
“Love this hotel” Great rooms, great service, great restaurant!!!

“Nice room in great location” My husband and I stayed here for four nights after booking through Hotwire. The location is excellent, between Union Square and Moscone Center, and one block from the subway. Someone complained about noise in a review, but if you're staying in the heart of a big city how can you possibly expect it to be quiet? We were on the 9th floor, so we didn't hear too much noise anyway. Our room was spacious, nicely furnished, and the mattress was very comfortable. The bed linens were of good quality and there was a down comforter. The room had the usual amenities (coffee maker, iron and ironing board, hair dryer) and the towels were thick. My only complaint is that the bathroom (the room that contains the toilet and bathtub--the sink was in an alcove outside the bathroom) was extremely tiny. I literally had to move my body sideways to get the door open from the inside or there would have been no room to open the door without smashing it in my face. We had a corner room, so perhaps the bathroom in those rooms is smaller. Also, there were no towel racks by the sink so we had to leave our hand towels on the counter. Otherwise we were happy with the room. When we received our bill under the door, we saw that we were charged $20 to receive two packages. These fees had not been disclosed, so we complained upon checkout and the front desk clerk removed the fee without an argument. Internet access is $15 per day from your room. The business center fees are steep, but you can print your airline boarding passes for free. Overall, the service was good. The concierge recommended an excellent (though expensive) seafood restaurant in the area called Farollan. (I don't think I'm spelling it correctly...), and the bell desk got us a taxi to take us to the airport (it's cheaper than taking the house car, which is a limo) in the morning. Our Hotwire rate for this property was $139 a night, which is very inexpensive for San Francisco. The regular rate is around $350 a night, which is way too expensive for us, but if I got this property again on Hotwire or Priceline I would be happy.

“Another Nice Stay” Stayed here recently for Nascar race weekend. Hotel was clean and there were no issues. Check-in and check-out was easy. Breakfast was good. Unfortunately I am never there during the late afternoon kickback hours for drinks and food. Not a fan of the extra small fridges without small freezer in top but all motels have gone to these now. Do wish this location had suite type rooms with beds and sleeper sofa for when I travel with family.

“Good postion” Stayed one night good postion close to Cheesecake factory . Walking distance to Market and waterfront. Room very pleasent beds so comfortable floor to celing windows with great view form 11th floor. Bathroon modern plenty of towels . Flat screen TV coffee machine. Bar very expensive as you would expect for city hotel Dont attempt to carry an 18 pack of beer from suppermarket through the lobby to the room to bring home to UK as you are not allowed to carry beer without it being covered with carrier bags!!!!!!! Had to take it back outside and wrap it up - How mad !!!!

“Public has great history and great present--neat hotel in wonderful Chicago neighborhood” From the days of Ambassador East and the Pump Room, to the new Public and very good restaurant, one thing is clear--it is a fine hotel in a great location. I had a beautiful suite, good looking and very comfortable. The bathrooms are updated but vintage size, not a Peninsula but ok. The lobby is wonderful, the lounge for coffee and meetings, the computer area, the bar, the excitement, they did it right. Room service is novel, and good. Bottom line: if I want absolute luxury and the price tag, I will go to another of Chicago's great hotels, and if I want to save a few hundred a night, enjoy a good neighborhood and have fun and get a good night's sleep, I will go back to the Public.

“It's a Ritz-Carlton, what else can you say” As always, you can expect a certain level of luxury and customer service for the Ritz-Carlton properies and this hotel is no exception. The only drawback is the location in WestEnd/Foggy Bottom section of DC.

“Shelter Island Getaway” A few words about me. I live in Arizona where it can be 110 degrees in the summer and so us "zonies" go over to San Diego most summers. I've been going since 1976. During that time, I've stayed in most of the tourist hotels available. Lately, I've been ending up at the Bay Club for about the last ten times. Why the Bay Club? It's on Shelter Island which is near Point Loma and on the Marina side. It sits across from the bay with views of both. It's a 2-story hotel with a small restaurant/bar downstairs that doubles as their breakfast area in the morning. It serves hot egg dishes as well as bages, cereal, etc. The room itself includes a small refrig and coffee-maker. The morning paper is delivered. The rooms are clean and decent-sized with a nice sitting table and chair set and adequate bathroom. Get the marina view (see photo) and enjoy the luxury boats. As a bonus, Humphrey's nightclub/restaurant is next door and you can listen to entertainment for free on your balcony on summer weekends. Some famous people sing there. There's covered, undeground parking and easy access to Mission Beach and the freeways. Downtown is fifteen minutes away along Harbor Drive. Would I recommend it? I'm going back in August, 2006, so, of course. Gotta beat the heat!

“Good size room for NYC” One of the better rooms I have stayed in in New York. Good size. Comfortable. Great location near Grand Central. Friendly service. No complaints. We had a lot of baggage and they were very helpful.

“It is the most beautiful hotel in SF” JDV did a beautiful job on this outstanding hotel! You could not ask for anything more in the hotel! The beds were better than a Westin heavenly bed. The amenities, well they were so good, I went on line and bought some. I was so lucky to be 1 of the first guests to stay at the Hotel Vitale, and let me say, they had all the bugs out before they even opened, you normally don't find this anywhere else. Can't wait for my next stay there

“Quiet Thanksgiving vacation” Drove by Hotel before turning around and finding entrance. Look for a low level dark green sign amid bushes on the east (left) side of the road just behind the Shopping center on Ray Road. Drive down a pretty but rather long drive back to the hotel. If you see the Alaska Airlines office park, you've gone to far. I got there early, got right in. The staff was less than exciting, but functional. the hallway carpets dirty, but the room fresh and clean. For a place next to the freeway it is really quiet. Bed in good condition, kitchen well stocked, my view not so great. I walked to meals. A large cineplex with dining across the street. A lot of shopping and other places nearby. A large park on 50th just north of Ray behind JCPenny gave me a place to walk my 5 miles each day. Great location, good place, ok staff. I'd stay here again. Especially at $29 a night.
“Beautiful building, great location” Liked the building, location, staff and room all very much. Check out the Tiptop bar/restaurant across the street!

“Great stay at beautiful, bay-view Grand Hyatt” Beautiful, if not over-the-top, hotel with awesome views in a prime San Diego location. Very quiet even though in the busy part of town -- we had a nice room towards the end of the hall on one of the top floors of the south tower with a magnificent, sweeping view of the bay. The room was amply sized and very comfortable. We got a great rate on the park and surf package which included self-parking and Internet -- and there was a room ready for us early in the day! Now that the hotel is owned and managed by Host Marriott, we would definitely recommend this hotel to anyone.

“Very grand hotel - great experience for a good price” I stayed here with business colleagues for a conference in November 2007 and had a good experience. The hotel is in a great location for both the convention center (but not as close as the Marriott) and the Seaport Village and Gaslamp District. The lobby is incredibly grand and the pool area is really nice - with views out over the water/marina. It is also a good location for running out into the marina and along the water. The rooms are of a decent size and comfortable. We also got a good recommendation of a restaurant for dinner one night from the concierge. Overall a great hotel, a good location, and we paid a reasonable rate for the rooms and so were very impressed!

“Very Good Location and Value” My wife and I stayed here for one night on Feb. 19 on a short visit to Boston. I booked the room on Price Line for $129.00 which was an excellent value. Parking underneath the hotel is convenient in the Prudential Center garage and an online coupon saves $14.00 off the 24 hr. rate. Our room in the north tower was recently refurbished, nicely appointed, and being on a Starwood Preferred high floor and a corner room, the views were great. Bed was very comfortable, room was quiet and we slept great. Good amenities, bathroom on the small side. With the connection from the hotel to the Prudential Center and Copley Sq. Mall, you can walk to loads of shops and restaurants without going outside - we dined at the Palm and Legal Seafoods. I would definitely stay here again for this rate.

“Nice Location!” This hotel is older, but clean and kept stylish in the typical Marriott way. There is a Starbucks downstairs, conference centers, indoor and outdoor pool with a an outdoor bar and cabanas. It's next to the park which can get quite busy on weekends with events, but we were still able to find parking on the street to avoid paying the parking fees the hotel charges. Beds are comfortable. We took our dog this time, and he had space on the covered balcony for his small kennel and food. We stayed 3 nights, but opted not to get maid service because of the presence of the dog. It was easy to pick up the towels, etc. that we needed. The weekend there, the hotel had a "costume college" going on and guests were wearing period costumes they'd made throughout the hotel, that was an unexpected site. There are four elevators and we never had to wait too long for one even though on the 14th floor. I would stay again. The mall and PF Changs is directly across the street.

“Wonderful service, fab location, just needs a little TLC from Marriott” From the minute I walked into the lobby, I was treated with special care and received great service. My corner room was lovely. BUT - holy street noise, Batman - the hotel was built at the beginning of the last century, and it is quite apparent that the windows have not been updated since then. After many years of traveling to NYC, one does expect a certain level of noise - sirens, horns, revelers - but this felt like we had left all of the doors and windows open. And, on the topic of windows, there was a window INSIDE the bath/shower combination, which was blocked by a large mini-blind, which is ok but - yikes - rust and - just yikes. Not a good idea. Having said that: we experienced wonderfully clean, well-kept, accommodations and a lovely bed with luxurious linens; super fluffy pillows; good lighting; easy to operate ac/heat; had breakfast at the nice restaurant in the building; and the Carlton is just two blocks away from one of the greatest restaurants in Manhattan, Hillstone, on Park Ave. Overall, I would recommend this hotel. (Marriott - please - just invest in some 21st century windows, and we would be ecstatic.) Love the Molton Brown amenities, too. Thanks for reading this review - hope that enjoy your stay!

“It's an intercontinental, how can you go wrong?” My girlfriend and I stayed here for 2 nights in August. The hotel is located in a pretty nice part of town, however you are in pretty close proximity to some setchy areas. It is easy to walk to the big famous square (name escapes me right now) and there is easy access to all the main amenities of San Fran. The hotel is apparently a very historic hotel, and you can tell by the architecture. The lobby is nothing special, but the rooms are large and elegant. Our room was not in the best location (2nd floor right above the main entrance) but everything worked out okay. Asked front desk about moving but they were fully booked. Oh well. Overall the Intercontinental lived up to its name. The staff were friendly/knowledgeable, and always recommended great restaurants. We got a nice room for $135/night, so it was superb value. I would say anything under $180 would be of good value for this place. *Please note: parking will cost you an arm and a leg and there is no restaurant in the hotel.

“wonderful stay; [almost] a 5” Stayed here five nights on business. The good: Very very clean room, just renovated; clean, modern decor with starched white high count linens. Neutral wood, tan/orange colors with just enough touches to make it not sterile, but not so much that it's overpowering. I had a corner room, which was quite spacious for SF for the price. On the 21st floor, I didn't have any noise problems, except the rare noise when my neighbors came in and out of their rooms -- I could definitely hear that. Otherwise, it was very quiet. I slept well every night. There are two power outlets built into the bedside tables in a convenient location on each side of the bed; extra airline-style positionable reading lights. Lots of new white good size towels. The refrigerator is a nice touch; no mini-bar, but you can bring home leftovers from dinner. There are bedside controls to raise and lower the black-out shades -- it was pitch-dark at night (except for the clock-radio/phone), and it was nice to raise the shades and see the city-scape in the morning before getting up. Service was polite without being cloying. Nice bath amenities -- I tip housekeeping well, but I got extras every day. The bathroom was spacious; the bathroom door was opaque glass, and it slides open/closed -- the effect creates extra space. The elevators were very fast; I never waited more than a minute, going up or down. One minor critique -- the sinks are shaped like a baby's bath, with a shallow end to the left away from the faucet; very attractive, but not practical. The ONLY thing that keeps me from giving this hotel a 5 is the following: the internet service is not free, and the WiFi is painfully slow and erratic. I've been using the wired connection instead all week. I truly object to high-end hotels charging for WiFi. Kimptons have always provided free wifi, and it's one of the reasons I'm loyal to them. Otherwise, great stay in a comfortable, clean, modern, upscale hotel.

“Good experience.” We booked the Allerton via Hotwire. We received a fantastic rate and the room was small, but probably very standard for Chicago. After two nights of sporadic sleep due to the elevator right outside our door, we asked to move to a different room. They were very accommodating and moved us to a room away from the elevator. And, it was even larger! The only "cons" to this hotel are the beds are just OK...for a 4 star hotel, they need pillow top mattresses. They have a feather mattress cover on top, but the feather poke you in the middle of the night. The elevators are horrendous!! You will wait for-ev-er for them. One employee told us a little trick---use the service elevator, even though it states you can't. Great location and excellent service.

“Great Stay in good location” Perfect location. Bed was delicious. TV large. Staff was friendly to fault. Quiet Great view. I loved the online check in and the notification when the room was ready via email! My only compliant is that internet charge is $14.00 per day. It is not as bad as some hotels but in todays world it should be free. I rented a car from Hertz for a day and it very convenient that they were located onsite. Definitely, take a cab to and from the hotel because parking is $50 per day!

“Very nice hotel with excellent staff” I was very pleasantly surprised by this giant chain hotel. They have added local flavor in their decor, such as the GORGEOUS light fixtures in all of the main areas and large ballrooms and the fantastic rock climber sculpture in the lobby. The lobby bar is open and bright and a natural gathering space. I never had a chance to go up to the Altitude bar/restaurant, but a local friend told me that the view is fantastic. The hotel gym was the best I have experienced, open 24 hours with lots of natural light, the person that designed the gym is clearly a pro. They had every free weight, band, kettle ball, and machine one could want, plus a pool and hot tub. I would stay here again any time for the gym alone! The staff in every part of the hotel is at your service and super helpful and polite. They really go out of their way to ensure you have a good stay. They also had recycling bins in the hotel room, which is a huge plus for me. Normally I am a boutique hotel traveler, so giving this hotel 5 stars is a great surprise!

“Hip and differant” Stayed one night in an upper floor. It was not high enough though as we had a view of a parking lot. The hotel has that modern flair and it was nicely set up. The rooms are somewhat on the small side and I do have to agree with the darkness. Although it is kind of sexy and romantic lighting, it would be noice to have an option for brighter if needed, especially in the bathroom when getting ready to go out. The bed was very comfortable and the set up of room was well laid out. The wardrobe cabinet was nice as well. We had good service and enjoyed the rooftop pool for just relaxing by. It is a small and shallow pool, but it does its job. For the area, you do have to pay more for hotels, so I guess it was average.

“Downtown dream in San Antonio” The Sheraton Gunther is a great hotel located in the heart of San Antonio. Rooms are very nice although the vanities in the bathrooms are a bit small. Self-park is unavailable and the hotel does not have arrangements w/ public parking. Only parking choice at Gunter is valet & it is expensive. Staff is extremely knowlegable and helful. Riverwalk, restaurants and bars are close. Nice hotel.

“Convenient and moderately priced” We stayed here for one night after a long flight from overseas before continuing on to our destination in the U.S.. It's close to the airport and the staff is very friendly and helpful. You can't beat the price of $72 plus change, including tax, for a clean and comfortable room with a kingsize bed. The place has a great continental breakfast consisting of bagles & cream cheese, granola & milk, yoghurt, juice, tea, and coffee. It has a restaurant which is open for dinner. There is another convenient restaurant, LAX Cafe', across the street. This place also has computers with internet access and is very moderate in its prices. The shuttle from La Quinta to Terminal 1 at LAX only takes 7 minutes.

“Fantastic Location if the Price is Right” My family, the 5 of us came over on Apr 23 to celebrate mum's 65th bday and parents 45th anniversary. We got a government rate of $201+tax and considering what you have to pay for this hotel I think we got a bargain. I couldn't really fault too much apart from some escalators being out of use and the quickness you have to get in the elevators before they started to close. The rooms were of a decent size and very clean with business like decor ie not modern like The Westin. They fit 3 adults quite comfortably. Housekeeping always done by the time we got back. Cannot fault this location as it is bang in the centre of Times Square. some of us had the breakfast which was great although pricey at $20+. Went to Sbarro across the street and got all you can eat for $7. The hop on off buses were great at $48 for 48 hours and went everywhere. Go on Statan Island Ferry and get just as good a view of Liberty for no cost. Went up Top of the Rock. Fantastic views of the city. Best meal was at Sardi's. Booked Pre Fixe before seeing Wicked and it was the best meal I have ever had and great value at $46+tax for 3 course + tea/coffee. Service was second to none. Wicked was fantastic. Whilst I enjoyed our stay a great deal at Crowne Plaza if we had to pay the going rate for a New York Times Square hotel I would probably opt for The Westin as it is more modern and the beds are "Heavenly". We realise we would be lucky to get a decent 3 star for the price we paid.
“One word: Awesome” The room was spacious and clean, the personnel was professional, and the restaurant Elway inside the hotel was great. I will definitely stay there again.

“Retro LA Vibe Near All the Hollywood Attractions” I recently stayed at this hotel for business and I was pleasantly surprised. It is in one of the best locations in LA for access to the Valley and Hollywood attractions. It is easy to get around without having to use the major (traffic clogged) freeways. This was a fine hotel for a business traveler. They have free WiFi, a small fee for parking and a Starbucks across the street. The only downside was the crappy off sight gym you can use...make sure to wash your hands after. There is also a bar in the lobby and some amazing sushi spots within walking distance. This would be a GREAT hotel for a family on a budget. The breakfasts were filling and inexpensive. I had a great breakfast sandwich for $6.00. They have a large enclosed pool and as I mentioned before, you are close to the Studio tours and Hollywood. There are also quite a few things within walking distance, including restaurantsand shopping. The vibe is definitely old Hollywood and it works. The rooms are a little out dated and the TV's are ancient but who is watching TV when you are in the heart of all the action? Just a little added bonus, they were filming CSI Miami in the back of the hotel during my stay. What could be a better way to see the LA scene in action?

“Great stay at a new hotel” I stayed for one night while on a business trip in Colcumbus. The hotel is spotless and the front staff was very friendly. The check in went smoothlessly and was a pleasant experience after a long day. The room was spotless and the bed was very comfortable. The bahroom had a large wlak in shower and was also clean and welll stocked. The room had a large flat screen TV with a decent selection of HD channels. There was an I-Pod docking station as well. The air conditoning worked well without being too noisy. I didnt use the pool so I can't say if it is good or bad. The breakfast was plentiful and well presneted. The hotel is in a good location close to shopping and restuarants. Overall this was a great stay It had what I consider to be important: clean rooms, friendly staff, good TV and internet reception. I will be returning.

“The Library Hotel - Sets the standard for customer service” I vacationed last week with my wife and three grown children in NYC. We were celebrating my wifes 50th birthday. We normally stay at the Hilton at 6th and 53rd, but they could not accommodate us during the Thanksgiving holidays. And I am glad they could not or I would not have discovered The Library Hotel. I found them via TripAdvisor. And never has TripAdvisor been more correct about a hotel than this one. The experience starts BEFORE you arrive. I spoke with Billy when making my room reservations. He was quick to point out that TripAdvisor was offering a good deal for their room rates. He also made some great recommendations for me as well as several reservations since we would be coming during a very busy week. He also set up our pickup at Newark airport which arrived like clockwork. When we arrived at the hotel, we were greeted by the doorman as well as one of the concierges. Since we arrived well before the check in time of 3:00 pm, they stored our luggage for us while we had lunch and checked out the area. When we came back, our two rooms were ready. We were on the 5th floor (the math and science floor). Our kids got a kick out ot the library theme. We learned alot about dinosaurs this week. And they had a special gift and personalized note on the table for my wife for her birthday! The rooms were of adequate size and the bathrooms were very roomy. We had a wonderful view of the NY Public Library and Madison Ave. The windows open completely, so you can open them for some fresh air if desired. Every night they turn down the bedsheets and leave fresh chocolate and bottled water as well as a handwritten note informing you of the following days weather forecast. The rooms have everything you need and we took them up on their offfer of free dvd's to watch late at night. Hotel slippers and bathrobes add to your comfort. They also offer a wonderful daily breakfast and evening wine and cheese gathering on the second floor. The breakfast is actually not an afterthought. It is excellent! Bagels, danish, lots of fruit and juice selections, cereal, yogurt, excellent coffee and even cappuccino! Outstanding! And the servers and hostesses are delightful. But the thing that sets The Library apart from any hotel/resort, etc. is their impeccable service. Everyone at their front desk is a knowledgeable concierge. I interacted mainly with Billy and Jessica. They were never too busy to help out with reservations, information, restaurant advice and tips for Broadway plays, etc. Jessica steered me to the best pizza joint I've ever been to (See review for John's Pizza!). But the ultimate came AFTER we had left and were about to board our plane for home. I received a call from Jessica letting me know that they had found several clothing items in one of our rooms that we had mistakenly left behind. She had already packaged the items and set up a Fedex pickup for the next day! She just needed to know where to send them. What incredible service! Two days later we received the package. There are so many things about The Library that make it my new favorite hotel in NYC. The great location, wonderful rooms, outstanding views, thoughtful amenities. But it's their genuine care for their guests that will bring us back.

“Decent motel” The property is an older motor court but the service was excellent. Some issues were the noise of I-35 right outside and the trucks. Also the TV was subpar and had. Horrid picture. The wifi was a bit weak but all in all it was a nice place to sleep!

“Highly recommend the Swissotel” My husband and I spent this past Thursday and Friday nights at the Swissotel. We were very pleased with the hotel and with the service. We had a standard room the first night. It was large and comfortable. The next day, we were out walking for hours and returned to our room at 3:40 p.m. hoping to relax. The room had not been serviced and we were not pleased. The front desk offered to have housekeeping come right up, but we were not interested in leaving the room again. They offered us a free upgrade to a corner room. The views on all sides were spectacular. We didn't use the fitness center or pool but they are beautiful. I've posted one picture of the view from the standard room, and the rest are pictures of the corner room. We will definitely stay at the Swiss again.

“One of the best in the chain” Whoever runs this hotel knows how to run a hotel. Professional staff, quality construction and comfortable furnishings/bedding make for a great stay. The hotel is one of the older models, but not ancient, so the rooms are larger and quieter than the new ES built nowadays with cheaper materials. HVAC works great and is not noisy, the water is hot and the beds are very comfortable. The free breakfast was excellent. Free parking is close by and convenient if you are in and out of a car all day. The health club looked very well furnished and had lots of eqpt. 2 minor complaints. Only 2 elevators to serve a large hotel, and the TV's are fairly old. This is the only 4 star hotel near Love Field so there are no other options. The closest is the Hilton Park Cities and there's no comparison from a value standpoint. This is by far the better choice.

“Overall very nice ambiance, terrific location, gracious service --but some uneven bits” We stayed at the FS/SF for a mini-vacation. Overall a great value with the extra night free and some preferred partner benefits (breakfasts plus one lunch). Everyone was very nice and gracious. The doormen were particularly welcoming and helpful --snagging cabs and providing useful dining advice. The concierge staff were very nice and helpful with directions but didn't really come up with anything i hadn't already found on on open table or interested in getting reservations to places i couldn't. The room was clean and spacious, lovely bathroom (pristine deep soaking tub-- but no bath salts) and great shampoo products. The room darkening drapes actually overlapped (most hotels seem to have an annoying gap)- big plus. And the window seat was just delightful. Cozy spot to read and look down at the kaleidoscope of Market Street traffic. As manager noted in response to another reviewer, coffee makers & teapots were available on request (but if you don't think to ask... ). Unfortunately the turn down people don't seem used to the idea-- they'd take away dirty mugs but didn't replace them (promptly remedied with a call to housekeeping, but i'd already made the coffee when i noticed...) Oh, another nice thing that could be better-- lovely new TV but many channels not HD. And the written channel listing provided was out of date-- the channel guide on the tv itself was more extensive. And charging for wifi is probably a big profit center but tacky. Less expensive chains provide it gratis. Restaurant was also a bit uneven. The smoked salmon benedict was absolutely perfect. In fact the breakfasts were all lovely, foodwise, and generally timing wise. But one day service was less attentive --maybe it was one particular server who was inattentive--the day she was serving it took forever to get breakfast. We also were disappointed with lunch -- (same day, same server)--- we ordered the soup, asked if it was vegetarian, were assured that it was. and it came served topped with distinctly unvegetarian bacon! We sent it back (i hate being put in the position of having to send food back!) but we could overhear the cook being upset that he hadn't been told to omit it. Waitress seemed indifferent to the error. the rest of the lunch was adequate but not up to the list prices on the menu. it may have just been a bad day or the A team on vacation. Overall a very nice property, comfortable public spaces and service orientation. And great location. But the handful of glitches were surprising.

“Clean, quiet, comfortable, and good value.” I stayed at the Drury Inn & Suites Houston Hobby over 1 night during the first weekend of spring break. We had a 1-bedroom suite and had 5 people staying in the suite. The only hitch was that I had called ahead to ask if we could possibly check in earlier than 3 pm due to my son normally taking a nap in the afternoon. The front desk person said yes, they could try to accomodate the request but made no promises. We arrived at 1:20 pm which I didn't think was all that early. We then were told we needed to wait while our room was prepared. I don't know how many suites they have, so perhaps that was a factor. The staff was very friendly as we waited in the comfortable lobby. However, it took until about 2:35 pm for our room to be made ready. I had a hard time believing it really took over an hour to clean one room and have it ready for us. Plus, the check out time is 11 am, so it didn't seem like it needed to have taken that long to get the room ready. But, the room was comfortable and very large and nice. The pool was rather crowded with noisy children but we still had a good time there. The next morning, we checked out the breakfast which is nice and a good value because it is included and has hot food (not just waffles). At the end of the stay, our toilet decided to quit working but other than that, everything worked fine in our room. We will be back if we are in the area again.

“Great Family Vacation Hotel” My family enjoyed the Drury Inn very much! They loved the Hot Breakfast and breakfast bar. My wife loved the free long distance and happy hour. The location was perfect for our short trips to Moody Gardens, NASA, Six Flags and Minute Maid Park. We all love this hotel!

“Great rooms!” This is a huge resort. It can be very confusing to find your room, as the corridors shoot off in all directions. There was renovations going on when we were there, but other than finding a dead end when we exited an elevator, you'd never know it. The rooms are beautiful, ours must have been recently remodeled. The beds were comfortable and the amenities in the room were nice. The pool area is a bit of a nightmare. There are a several smallish pools, one larger pool with no discernable water feature for kids. A fountain in the center of the large pool served as a perfect spot for kids to slip on slippery tile. There is a lazy river, somewhat small that has very limited seating surrounding it. Many people where camped out on the wet grass as they couldn't get a chair. Servers are plentiful and food/drinks are delivered quickly. Tried to get a reservation for dinner, earliest we could get was 8:30pm. There are several restaurants close by (desert ridge and city north).

“Truely deluxe!!” After having stayed at the various LA downtown hotels, surprisingly, I found myself at this hotel and can only say this place is incredible! Highend, expensive is one thing but if you are able to find govt or discounted rates, you'l be sure to find yourself in the laps of comfort and class all together! Their complimentary towncar service is great too if you wanted to swing around the downtown for work or pleasure. I am truely impressed. Wish I could have stayed here before rather than wasting my time at other closer places like the Westin and Marriott!!

“No problems here” This is, I believe, the third hotel I've stayed in which has been largely trashed on here but yielded no problems at all for me and my family. Check in and check out were smooth as silk, a lost room key was replaced with no grief and the staff couldn't have been more considerate. Yes, the rugs are due for some serious shampooing, but the beds were fine and the bathroom large and clean. Some people must set their standards so high that no hotel could reach them or perhaps they hit them at a bad time. Whatever the case, the Park Central did just fine by us.

“Wonderful location to convention center.” This hotel is on the river walk and is connected to the convention center so if you are attending a meeting there, it is most convenient. The river walk is pretty to walk around in the cool hours of the evening, and has a number of different cuisines feathered. There is a mall within a ten minute walk, and I would suggest taking the river boat ride around the river walk. This ride is 45 mins long and is interesting. On the whole an interesting place, but not a great deal to see in this area. The Hyatt had excellent staff, and the regency club room was one of the best I've been in. It was large and never too crowded, with very good snacks in the early evening and deserts after 8pm. The rooms were comfortable and fairly good sized, although it was more of a Hyatt rather than a Grand Hyatt.

“Great Hotel for Pleasure” Stayed one night at this hotel during a visit to the Riverwalk. Great hotel. I was in a high room facing the river walk, with a balcony. It appears that all rooms might have the same view and might all come with a balcony.....I assume this based upon the shape and configuration of the hotel. It is located between 2 other hotels. Either way, I highly suggest a balcony and River Walk view....it was excellent. Service was good. Check in was easy. Be aware that any hotel you choose directly on the River Walk will have parking "issues". I was able to get a good rate with valet included, otherwise, it is $25 and $15 to self park. Valet offers unlimited in and out and the valet staff was friendly, offered to help with luggage and was very efficient overall. The hotel has a nice coffee bar/cafe. It serves Starbucks beverages as well as a full (ish) bar. The menu was small, but seemed good. The bartender seemed a bit cold and service was slow, as he was the only person there with several people wanting something....but not "bad". The hotel offers maps of the area and you can walk, easily to anyplace in the area. We walked to the Towers of the Americas, had dinner, drinks, etc, all within walking distance. We felt very safe and comfortable in the area...police were seen often. The room was small. Definitely ok for a day or two, I could not see spending a business trip here...it is more for pleasure, in my opinion. The hotel common area/lobby was modern and staff helpful to tourists. The room and common areas were clean and seemed to offer anything you would need. I would stay here again.

“Great hotel” My wife and I stayed here for three nights in JUly 2005. It didn't hurt that the weather was the best I have ever seen in San Fran. We usually stay at the Drisco in Pac. Heights but needed to be closer to downtown and refuse to rent a car in any city. The check-in process was a bit sloppy but we were given a great room with a staggering view of the water. The outdoor spaces at the Vitale are wonderful and my time spent working on the fifth floor terrace (good wifi service included) was wonderful. The location is great as well. You can walk to the Ferry Building for breakfast and within a few blocks there are a bunch of nice places (including Boulevard, Chaya and Shanghai 1930). The spa was lovely as well although I tried three times to get a message lined up and never could get it worked out. The staff was helpful and the bar scene at the Americano downstairs was really, really hopping on Friday. I would stay here again in a hearbeat although I still prefer being in a quiet residential neighborhood.

“Nice convention hotel, some tweaking needed” This is a large hotel adjoining the convention center and their rates are surprisingly reasonable. The good - clean, large rooms, fairly soundproof. Front desk is efficient but not particularly friendly. Some bell staff made up for that lack. However, be aware the port side Coronado view rooms overlook a working container port and ships are loaded mostly on Sunday through Tuesday. They are supposed to stop at 10 PM but were going till 2 AM our first night. Bring your earplugs. Although the hotel works well, because of it's size, there can be lines for the elevators, and meal facilities.

“Hip Hop Summit!” I went to the Hip Hop Summit On April 13-15 2007. I chose this place because of the location! I was really glad to have this area. Detroit can be a little scarey if not in the right place. Everything is literally right around the corner! The Max Fisher music Hall was the location of the summit and with little driving distance it was ideal!!!!!! The Russell Simmons after party at The Envy club was in walking distance from the hotel on Larend St. The Greektown casino was only two blocks away. The Hotel all in all is well kept and convenient. There is a full service restaurant/bar right downstairs. A mini mart that actually sells spirits(alcohol,beer,& wine) right downstairs adjacent to the parking garage. Parking is $20 a day but the convenience is unbelievable! Now the room itself is spacious! I had a King size bed! A beautiful picturesque window overlooking the lake and Canada! The actual bed is heaven. I could hardly wake up. There was also a fold out bed/couch in the rrom. A mini fridge hidden in the bureau was a cute touch! Also you have your own coffee maker in the room. They have a Spa Jacuzzi and indoor swimming pool, A work out room on the 8th floor.......Nice! . This was a good look! I am happy to have stayed here. Oh yeah the Renassaince center was located across the street. Its like a mini mall and you could take the skywalk across if you don't want to be in the elements. Only problem is its only open on the weekday.

“Elegance and value in an older property” This building was the Ritz Carlton. Service and furnishings at the Taj are excellent, in some ways superior to what Ritz is doing with its newer properties. The bar is a great space, and the Cafe was quite good. The rooms are on the small side, and the bathrooms are very small, probably explaining why Ritz built a new building. But, the tradeoff is a great hotel experience at a much lower price than the Ritz or the Four Seasons.

“Concur: Middle of Nowhere” Now, with that said, the staff is on-task, on-message and bends over backwards to serve its guests (whom, at the time I was there, ranged from the University of North Texas Mean Green to DynCorp, to several overnight conventions). Exercise facility is above average. The one restaurant is marginal. The lounge is a friendly atmosphere. Rooms are above average and the housekeeping staff does a great, considerate job. Adjoining golf course is very nice, and if I get back there, I'll play it. Now, the fact of the matter is that this Marriott property is so far removed, that I doubt I would every stay there of my own volition. While the hotel provided shuttle service to Roanoke and the WalMart, there is ABSOLUTELY NOTHING. ZERO. ZILCH. NADA...within walking distance of this hotel (except the Speedway across the street).
“Great location” Room is spacious, the bar is great ( try the mission Beer) and location is great you can walk anywhere from here or from the santa fe depot, gaslamp, marina

“Great Service” We were originally disappointed in the size of the room, but the tile and marble bathroom made up for that letdown. The location of the hotel was great and if you needed to be anywhere within a 3 mile radius the shuttle was available; no more than a 10 minute wait. Although we did not use it, preferring to walk, the rail system is right in front of the hotel. Room service arrived in 15 minutes. The majority of the front desk staff, bar, and restaurant were excellent. I was disappointed that lunch was not served in the dining room, but there are a handful of decent restaurants nearby.

“Excellent Hotel” This is an excellent hotel. As other reviews point out, the lobby is nothing to write home about, it's fairly poky. But that really is the only criticism I have. While there I put the hotel through a number of tests. The first one was: I'm very noise sensitive, and although they gave me the kind of room I'd requested, very high up, with a wonderful view, it had a connecting door to the next door room, which was a potent and irritating noise source. I asked to be moved to a quieter room. At first they told me the only quieter room they had was on a smoking floor (I'm a non-smoker). When I said I didn't care, I just wanted a quieter room wherever, they found one on the same floor I was on, which was a non-smoking floor. It wasn't a better room, really, and was in some respects less good. But it was quieter, and served me well for the rest of my stay. Full marks on that. The move was executed within half an hour of my initial complaint. Secondly: I ordered a DVD from Amazon, and by mistake Amazon left my name off the package. In spite of that, the hotel staff ensured that it got to my room. The service in the Affinia was universally excellent. The concierge, bellhops and reception staff were extremely helpful at every turn. One word of advice: whatever you do, don't bother going to the Barking Dog, or whatever the hotel's adjoining restaurant/bar is called, for breakfast. For better value, and a more authentic experience, go to the Murray Hill Diner just round the corner on Lexington. The service and the food is much better.

“Exceptional and Comfortable” We stayed at the Staybridge Suites while on a college visit to University of North Florida with our son. The hotel is fairly new and is pefect for that home away from home feeling. The lobby is warm and inviting and the staff were friendly. The room itself was a 2br-2bath suite with a living area and full kitchen. The beds were very comfy. The breakfast was perfect and they offered several healthy options. The hotel is well located and is close to University of North Florida, Mayo Clinic, and the St Johns Town Center where there are MANY MANY restaurants and stores. You can't beat this place. We would definitely stay here again and recommend it highly.

“Top Notch Hotel - All the Way Around” We have stayed here several times in the past but not recently. It felt so good to return. The hotel is modern (unusual in SF), bright and clean. We had a standard room on the 24th floor which was came with welcome amenities as well as a great view. We opted for Club Lounge access (for an additional daily fee) as the complimentary breakfast is perfect for our needs. The food and beverages provided all day long, as well as the happy hour, cannot be beat. The lounge itself is large, beautifully decorated and so relaxing. The staff in the lounge provided exceptional service throughout our stay. Complimentary internet was provided in the lounge, as well. We felt as though this was our home away from home. Housekeeping did an exceptional job every day both with the morning cleaning and the evening turndown service. It was great to be able to electronically indicate that you wanted the room cleaned. We would indicate such as we were leaving in the morning and by the time we returned in the afternoon the room had been cleaned. Everyone in the hotel was professional, friendly and accommodating. We could not have asked for more.

“Good hotel in a great location” Spent a night on points to explore the city with my wife and daughter. Used a rollaway as we don't like the 2xdouble bed option, which often puts us in non-marriotts to get 2x Queen beds. Was a little tight with the rollaway, but perfectly usable. Know the two towers; in one all rooms have balconys, in the another (which has the concierge lounge) there are just large glass windows. Great views, easy walk to gaslamp diistrict, marina for harbor tours, ferry to Coronado, Midway carrier museum. My 11YO enjoyed the pool as well, though it was a bit chilly for me! Would stay again.

“The Jury has Reached a Verdict!!!” I was in town for a conference and the convention hotels were booked. I made a reservation at Jurys on Travelocity; the price was steep: it averaged $340 per night before taxes. For that price I expect something special.... Location: Excellent; within an easy walk of the Charles River, Back Bay, Copley Square, Newbury Street, and Hynes Convention Centre. Check-in: Fast, friendly, and accurate. Top notch in fact. Room: Small but nicely appointed. No view. Large modern bathroom with heated towel racks (nice touch) and high quality soaps and shampoo (but nothing exceptional). Beds were very comfortable. TV and stereo were excellent. FREE INTERNET SERVICE IN THE ROOM: YAHOO!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!! Only downside with the room: slightly stained carpeting. Concierge: knowledgeable and friendly. Business Centre: Excellent and responsive. Hotel Bar: hopping and busy. Check-out: Efficient, friendly and accurate. Overall impression: an excellent business hotel, well run, and friendly, but not a five star experience.

“Nice but some frustrations” I wanted to love the Hilton, and in some ways, I did, but in others, we were disappointed. My husband and I just came back from enjoying two days there relaxing over New Year's, and there were positives. Our room was clean and large by city standards, but I agree with earlier posts that size of room is completely luck of the draw based on what I saw on the floor diagram. The bed was very comfortable, and the location of the hotel was great for being out and about in the city for First Night -- close enough to get there fast but far enough away to avoid the worst of the noise. The staff was great -- helpful and courteous, though we were disappointed that our request for an upper-floor room was not duly noted until we pointed it out, and then we were only put on floor 9 (of a 15 floor hotel). Our room maid was wonderful, however. Breakfast in the hotel restaurant was fabulous -- a really good buffet though it was part of a package for us. Not cheap if you have to pay separately, but worth it. And that brings me to the negatives. The hotel nickels and dimes you with charges for things that in other hotels might be part of the high rate charged. Wireless internet is on a per-day charge, and if you instead decide that you'll just use the hotel's "Business Center," be prepared to pay a minimum of a $10 charge then $1 per minute after 10 minutes. This seemed ludicrous to us who just wanted to check our e-mail. The bottles of water in the room were available for a mere $4.50 each (we bought some of our own nearby for a lot less), and a $80 charge for dinner in the hotel bar when we only had a few drinks and two light entrees seemed really high, even by hotel restaurant standards. In general, it seemed that the four-star rating was not really warranted given how many of the little extras one expects at four-star locales involved extra charges here. In addition, there were some aging issues -- the sheet that had a hole along the edge where it was folded over on our bed; the scratchy towels that were too old to still be soft and fluffy; the slightly worn wood on the furniture like the arm chair and entertainment center. The room was also quite noisy, in part due to the expected city sounds, but also due to how easily we could here our loud neighbors across the hall as they came and went. It was not a bad experience -- in fact, we were quite happy when all was said and done. But with a little more inclusiveness in their rates and some upgrading of slightly aging fixtures, this hotel could more fully embody a four-star experience.

“Best Location in NYC!” My husband recently surprised me with a trip to NYC for my birthday. We have been to New York several times, but this was the best location we have ever stayed in. We like to stay in different areas to get a feel of the neighborhoods. We were literally steps from Macy's, the Empire State Building, Madison Square Garden, and so many other New York sites. All the staff that we met were so friendly and helpful. Our room on the 10th floor was clean, fresh, and had one of the most comfortable king beds we have ever slept on. Loved the in-room microwave, coffeemaker, and mini-fridge. A nice bonus was the amazing view we had of the Empire State Building. The marble bathroom was beautiful and quite roomy. The water pressure in the shower was awesome! We were a little concerned when we realized that our room was right across from the elevator. It turned out not to be a problem. The room was very quiet. The only minor complaint I had was that when I returned home, I realized I had left my mini umbrella in the room. It doesn't sound like a big deal, but it had sentimental value to me. I called the hotel as soon as I realized I had left it in the room and followed the instructions to contact housekeeping. I called twice and left messages, but no one returned my call. Other than this, our stay at your lovely hotel was wonderful!

“Would stay again” My sister and I spent 3 nights here. We were impressed when we arrived. It was an early arrival and our room wasn't ready, but that's to be expected. We loved the comfy beds, the location was excellent with the DC Circulator at the door. After touring Washington DC, we were glad we stayed here, as we had shops and cafes at our doorstep. The restaurant attached to the hotel was wonderful. The hotel was clean, one of our priorities, and spacious for us. Yes, we'd stay again without thinking twice and we'd recommend it. I can't understand how it can be so low down on the TA List.
“Good location, nice hotel” Good amenities, rooms are great, sleep number bed also is a huge plus. Lobby and restaurant are pleasing and food and drinks are well within walking distance

“Hidden gem, great hotel!” I travel to SF a lot for work and have never stayed at this hotel or even heard of it. I was recently in a wedding that was at the Marines Memorial Club Hotel so we stayed there with the rest of the wedding party. PROS: Location is perfect, right in Union Square. Quiet and cozy rooms. Amazing FREE brunch for all guests. Restaurant is on the top of the building with spectacular views and even better food. This was a nice surprise; we had brunch there every morning! CONS: It's just as expensive as the nicer hotels in SF. No bell man to help hail cabs, etc.

“Very good” We stayed here a few nights with a great rate from the hotel website. We arrived earlyish (11.30am) and were offered a room right away, or a top-floor room (like we'd requested) at the check-in time of 3pm, and we accepted the latter offer. They stored our luggage for free while until we returned to move into our room. The room was very spacious (see photos) with a large King bed, almost over-sized bathroom, bay window with a decent view, desk and seating area. I expected the hotel decor to be a little sterile judging from the website, but it looked much better in real life. Front desk staff were very friendly and seemed keen to help, as opposed to the "robotic" approach I've had in other hotels. They had a DVD library for (free) hire, though it's worth mentioning that our first 10 choices were all booked out each time we tried to borrow one! I used the free in-room wifi with no problems. There was a laptop at the front desk for hotel guests to use, but it wasn't at all private and I wouldn't have used this for anything other than basic direction-finding. The hotel's location is very good; it seemed very safe during the day and night, and was only a few minutes walk from Chinatown and transport links. There's a cable car stop right outside, though beyond the cable car itself being a tourist attraction I would suggest using the buses or trolley cars for any serious travelling you have to do within San Francisco! Orchard and its sister hotel have good eco-friendly credentials, but that really doesn't make any difference to your stay if you're not into that sort of thing. The rooms are huge, amenities are just the same as other equivalent hotels I've stayed in, and I suspect most of their eco-friendly qualifications relate to their back-office processes. Overall this was a very nice hotel in San Francisco, especially at the rate we got ($100USD / night or thereabouts) and at that price it would be hard to beat.

“Different but good” Half a block east of Times Square, a small hotel geared to the younger crowd but welcomed us anyway. The room was adequate in size, the black and white decor took some getting used to. We really could have used a flashlight to find our way around the closet and the elegant table against the wall would have better been served as a dresser so we wouldn't have suitcases all over the floor. The bed was great, nice linens, flat screen TV. Very good continental breakfast in the AM, New York Times and USA today complimentary. Noah was by far the most helpful desk person, all of the doormen were helpful. Late September appears to be a tough time to find a room in New York, this served our purpose well.

“Great Two Nights!” My family booked this hotel through William Shatner,s website for $95.00 per night for a Fri/Sat stay. Considering the hotel web site was booking at a minimum of $269.00 before tax, I went in with the expectation that I got a great deal....and we were not disappointed. The staff was very friendly (and didn't flinch that we'd obtained the room via P.line) The room was spacious and clean. The two double beds were very comfortable. Even at 10 floors up there is street noise, but once the window is closed, we weren't disturbed by anything. This hotel is attached to a pricey and state of the art health club which comes with a $12.00 fee. However, the pool is free and it's a full-sized (25 yard or meter) pool perfect for swimming laps. As mentioned above, self parking and valet are expensive. However, I found free parking on the street within 50 yards of the hotel one night and 1.4 mile of the hotel the other. If I had paid the full rate, I'd be upset by so many extra costs (health club, parking, etc) but when you start off over $170 below the rack rate, you feel a bit differently. Overall, I"d definitely bid for a 4 star north coast San Diego hotel again and be very happy if it came up with this hotel.

“We loved the rooms comfortable beds & overall a quiet hotel. Close proximity to lots of shopping!” We rented a car traffic was very busy they like to honk a lot!. There's not much time to make right turns due to all the pedestrians. We will definitely take taxis next time or ride the trolleys. Mass transist system is convenient to the hotel.

“Couldn't get much better.” We had a corner suite on 23rd floor with views of bay and space needle. With the floor to ceiling windows it was like being in a postcard, especially at night. Staff was outstanding. Hotel is within walking distance of all downtown. If you only have a carryon, take the light rail to and from the airport. It's $2.50 a person and you get off at Westlake, 2 blocks from hotel. Best deal is happy hour at Ruth's Chris Steakhouse in the lobby. In the lounge you can get prime rib sliders for $5.95, outstanding!! The reviewer who mentioned no carafe, the coffee maker in the room is designed to just have the cup put below the spout so it's brewed into your coffe cup. The only problem we had was solved without our even asking. I ordered room service breakfast for myself and a carafe of coffee for my wife, they we're a little late and my wife decided to go shopping instead of wait for her coffee. I asked them to take the coffee back when my breakfast arrived, then when I called to have them remove the room service table, they told me they'd comped the whole breakfast since it was a little late. Great service.

“Cute hotel with nice extras” This Kimpton hotel is located just a few blocks from the convention center. The decor is really cool with modern, but comfortable furniture and an awesome bathroom. The shower is hard to describe, but I don't think you'd see anything like it elsewhere. I had read complaints about the water pressure, but honestly, I didn't think it was bad at all. The bed is comfy! The one "inhouse" restaurant is very limited and somewhat expensive, but there are plenty of other places within walking distance. The front desk and restaurant staff are truly top quality!

“Really impressed and HUGE rooms” I read great reviews on tripadvisor for this hotel so decided to give it a try. Anyone that has stayed in New York before will know how difficult it is to find an affordable hotel in New York - rooms are usually very small and overpriced. Hence, I was unsure what to expect. When we arrived at the reception I was a little bit disappointed - it was very dated and in need of refurbishment. It was also very busy and we had to wait quite some time to check-in, however it was just after the New York Marathon so there were large groups staying at the hotel from all over Europe. Once checked-in we took an old and slow elevator to the appropriate floor. My goodness, what a transformation! The corridors had clearly been refurbished as well as the rooms. Most impressive of all was the size of the rooms - they were HUGE by New York standards. All were very well equipped, tastefully decorated and with really comfortable beds. I was really impressed and much better than some of the 5 star hotels I have stayed in New York. There is no restaurant (although an excellent buffet breakfast room) or bar, but who needs that in this city, just step outside the front door and you have more than you could ever need! The hotel is in a fantastic location and I highly recommend it.

“Great location, good staff, nice but small rooms, REVIEW your bill” I normally stay at either a Hilton family hotel in Times Square/Hells Kitchen or the HGI on 28th when I am in NYC and after reading some flyer talk reviews decided to give this property a shot when I found a rate similar to the HGI on 28th for a weekend trip this past weekend. Great staff, especially Lenny at the front desk and Raggo the bartender. I did an Online check in for room 811 and got there to find out I was not assigned that room (was an end room) and was told my room was 1810. Lenny was the clerk that checked me and told me that someone was in 811 and they didn't have any end rooms available but could try moving me Saturday and I just said I would stay in the same room both nights. The elevators require a keycard and will only work for your floor which I liked. The card got me up to 18 but didn't work for my room. I went back to the lobby and Lenny remembered my room number and my keycard got recoded and worked fine. I was also thanked for my loyality as a diamond member upon checkin and he remembered my name the next night when I entered the hotel which I always appreciate from a hotel employee. There was no exec lounge, but K-cup coffee brewers in the room and the free breakfast is the best I have had at a hilton in a while. If you wanted a hot breakfast instead of continental you could chose from a variety of hot entrees from a special menu along with a side and juice or coffee with the voucher with no upcharge. The rooms were very small but modern and the toiletries in the bathroom were great. The room I had was way too noisy. Even with the TV on I could hear people entering and leaving their rooms and people talking in the hallway. The Wifi worked great and there were two computers downstairs you could use for free which I utilized after checkout to print my boarding pass. Location is great. Only a couple blocks from the 28th street 1-line and I don't mind walking and it is a easy walk to the theater district. I ate at the restaurant on Friday night and the hamburger was very good but expensive. Total bill with tip was over $40 for just a cheesburger, fries and a drink. The bartender Raggo was very good and really friendly. I didn't go to the roof bar but it sounded fun. Couple problems with my stay: They only have three elevators and on Saturday they took the one out of service with a sign that said "reserved for a special event". They have an elevator dedicted to the roof bar and only 3 elevators for guests so I felt they shouldn't have taken an elevator out of service on a saturday for their guests. When reviewing my bill Sunday morning I noticed the total was very high. My room rate was to have been only $239 a night and I was charged $315 for one night and $350 for the other night. I went to the front desk to have them correct the problem and there was a long wait to talk to someone. On a sunday morning at 11 they only had 3 employees working at the front desk. After finally getting to speak with someone I showed them my email confirm on my IPAD, they said they would correct the bill. I was given a 2 p.m. check out and returned to the property around 1:15 after being out in the city to go to my room to pack and the keycard wouldn't work again and meant waiting in line again for the card to recoded again.

“Great Hotel in a Great City!” Second time staying at the Wolcott and was once again very impressed. The hotel is in a great location on W. 31st right near Herald Square (home of Macy's), numerous subway lines and about 9 blocks south of Times Square. You can walk right out of the hotels entrance and be in the hustle and bustle of Manhattan or hop on a subway or bus and be in SoHo, Chinatown, Battery Park, Central Park, or Museum Mile within minutes. The hotel is a very historic hotel that has been renovated but you must also take note that it is a very old hotel....this is not your cookie cutter Best Western. The architecture throughout the hotel (including in the guest rooms is truly amazing). When we there for example though one of the elevators in the lobby was not working but to make up for that the gentleman behind the front desk let us use one of the staff elevators. The room I had both times consisted of two huge rooms. One room had two twin beds with a TV, desk and closet, the other room had another twin bed with another TV and a safe as well as the bathroom. In my view this was a big room for Manhattan or any other big city for that matter. We didnt have a view either time...I dont know how you get rooms with a view but I didnt complain, I could walk right out and look at the city myself. The hotel has a concierge who can help make reservations to get to the airport or to go to the Statue of Liberty or something. The lobby also features a small convenience store. Also something very helpful for my family and I was the hotel has a parking agreement with a garage on W. 32nd St (right around the corner) where I was able to leave the car off for 3 days with no worries). Overall I would highly recommend this hotel to someone wanting to visit Manhattan, not pay to much and be in the middle of it all.

“Great Hilton property even though from the outside it doesn't look like much” This is a nice Hilton with a ton of ammenities. The staff was extremely nice and went out of their way to make you feel welcomed. From the outside the hotel doesn't look like much but it's a huge property. The room was very nice with a lot of space. The fitness room and pool were fair but adequate. The location is great if you're wanting to be near the Galleria but also near the convention center and many of the stadiums. I'd recommend this property to anyone.

“Overall, a Great Experience” Wooden hangers in the closet, an ironing board that didn't scream light fighting cats when it was opened and closed; a chair that fit under the desk wtihout adjustment (I'm 6'2 and need often have to raise a chair); two packs of coffee in the room (why is it hotels normally only put one in a King Size room?); short wait for elevator; great selections for breakfast in the club lounge (eggs, oatmeal, fresh fruit, etc.); super fast room service; close to the airport (you can actually walk). Overall, a great experience.

“Great Staff” The Hotel is located in the business district (river South) but not a bad walk or short cab ride to anything in town. I stayed at this hotel Oct 2011 for business and an extened weekend. I got a king room for $115.00 a nite thru Expedia. The Hotel was clean and comfy. No bussers or bells. The staff at the free breakfast bar were terrific. Extremely helpful and funny. It made the day get off to a great start. Parking is at the garage next door so it is convienent. However, like most lots in Chicago, it is pricey. IF you can find this Hotel on line for under $115.00 it not a bad deal tho there are other places a bit cheaper if you shop around. Obviouly ,the sooner u book, the better the price. AND, my favorite "DIVE BAR" Stocks and Blondes is just around the corner. Got to check it out.

“A great stay” My husband and I stayed here while he was on business. The service was wonderful and the rooms were quite clean and updated. The bed is amazing and I hardly wanted to get out of it. The location is very near Greektown with several tasty restaurants - Pegasus and we highly recommend a trip to the Pan Hellenic Bakery. I walked from the hotel all over the city, straight down Madison. It might be a bit of a walk for some, but the walk to Millennium Park is about 15-20 minutes. Despite the front desk staff who told us it would be too long of a walk, we walked to Little Italy but after a huge dinner, we took a taxi back. The area seemed very safe and staying at the Crowne Plaza Metro is a good opportunity to check out some of the neighborhoods.

“Pleasant surprise” This hotel is overall very good. Great location in the center of the touristic attractions of River North. Room was very clean with comfy beds, decent air conditioning. Staff was very nice and helpful. Very small lobby, valet parking service (that I did not use). Mini fridge in the room and Trader Joe's downstairs. Next door to the CTA's red line making it convenient to ride to Ohare or Midway. Would definitely comeback.

“Best Location and Great Hotel during Hurricane Sandy!” We were nervous about staying at the Standard since I know it's a hipster youngish hotel with the chic Boomboom Room on the 18th floor and supermodels (or wanna be super models!) all over the lobby. However, it was so much better than I could have imagined! The Standard was kind enough to offer a discounted rate during the miserable Hurricane Sandy. We had no heat, electric, power or internet for 12 days, so a hotel in NYC was the way to go. What we loved most was the location. The MPD is the best area in NYC, with great shops and great restaurants. The Standard Bar & Grill was excellent for dinner and we had breakfast in the restaurant every a.m., which was fabulous. You are a few blocks from the West Village, which is quieter and our favorite neighborhood. The Boom Boom Room on the 18th floor of the hotel has the best views, though drinks are pricey ($50. for 2 cocktails), but worth it. We found everyone who worked to be nice and pleasant. Though the rooms are small, the views are spectacular. Request a North side view w/ views of the Empire State Bldg. The mini bar is great, lots of high quality choices, though no espresso machine in the room. The negatives (and I am being picky, but honest): and the reason I didn't give the hotel 5 stars. The bathroom was not as clean as I would have liked. Lots of stains in the toilet room on the walls and tiles had dust, kind of bothered me. The bathtub is so high, like 3 feet, it was hard to step into and out of it, almost dangerous. And lastly, there is no real closet, so no where to hang a coat or jacket or dress. They need some more hooks in the foyer of the rooms to hang a coat........ Other than that, it wasn't as scary hip as I thought it would be (we are 47), and we would definitely stay here again, maybe in a better room upgrade........but we appreciated the nice rates during a difficult time for so many displaced New Yorkers and New Jerseyans.

“Nice property, good experience” Well maintained, including the pool. Someone has taken an interest. The owner must be on sight or close. Nicely decorated two and three story motel/hotel in borderline area. Just to the north are the big Market Center Hotels. Not far to the south are light industry/business and bail bondsmen. Across the street is a Dennys. Rooms well maintained, excellent bed. Everything in the room worked. Small elevator for the three story portion (luggage cart available). Breakfast of cold cereal, fruit, fruit juice, pastry, bagels with condiments. Breakfast is self serve, but is staffed by one individual, who keeps it stocked. Looks to be the best value in the area. Good staff.

“Great hotel” I was in Phoenix for a conference. I enjoyed the hotel: nice rooms, great outdoor hot tub and pool. I was in the hot tub before dawn every morning. Good fitness facilities as well. I wanted to make sure I got a chance to see the town while I was there. The hotel has great running maps that take you through the historic district. I recommend a walk or run to see the architecture. It is also in good proximity to local attractions and public transportation.

“Pretty good” Although this is a good hotel, I can't share the enthusiasm of the previous reviewers. It's fully functional and for a one night stay as I had, it works nicely. I would not want to base myself/family out of this hotel while on vacation. The room is somewhat sterile and the carpeting has definately seen better days. The immediate neighborhood is nothing to write home about. One huge plus is that the rooms are well- soundproofed, unlike the Hilton where I heard planes coming and going all night long.

“Amazing weekend at the Ritz, great value from the Club level lounge” We stayed at the Ritz a last weekend and I have to say this place is excellent. I stay in hotels 1-2 weeks a month for business, but this place is truly something else. Check in was a breeze, valet was $28 a day (dislike) but the valet staff was very friendly and more than willing to help out with directions and so forth. We stayed in a club level room which had ample space and great amenities. When we were dining, yes dining on horderves, the spread and selection was amazing. It is so worth the extra money to have access to the club level lounge. All around we received excellent service from the employees. One gentleman really stood out, providing exceptional service and making any guest feel right at home...in a good way. There was another younger female who sat at her computer and didn't really talk with any of the guests, maybe having a bad day, i don't know but she was pretty much clueless on how to provide any level of service. Don't let that dissuade you from staying at the Ritz though, it's truly a magnificent Hotel. The elevators are quick, the valet doesn't keep you waiting around and the bathrooms have everything one would need.

“Preferred Place to Stay” I travel to Indianapolis every month for business. I usually stay at the Conrad or the Hilton. Neither were available in my budget for my June trip so I opted to try the Homewood Suites. I am so happy that they were not available because I had the best experience at the Homewood Suites. The employees couldn't do enough for you. The valet was super helpful and even drove me to a meeting a few blocks away so I wouldn't have to carry a large box in a dress and heels. They all remembered my name! I've stayed at the Conrad at least a dozen times and they NEVER remember me. I have to use the valet quite a bit because I have meetings downtown and north so I'm always getting my car. Usually I have to wait 10-15 minutes at the Conrad. I never waited more than 5 at the Homewood Suites. I loved my room. It was large enough for me to practice yoga and had a great area for my laptop and work stuff. The bed was very comfortable. I enjoyed that I could also stretch out on the couch and read. The free breakfast was perfect for me. They could offer more fruit but I got enough to get my day going. Going forward I will always stay at the Homewood Suites. It will be my Indianapolis home away from home.

“Liked the tranquility and central location” We stayed at the Nikko for four nights last week in a 19th floor, corner room with King size bed and city view. A nice touch is the small stream that filters through one part of the downstairs lobby adding to the peacefulness of the hotel. The room was modern, decent size tho somewhat smaller than the Hyatt where we had stayed several years earlier, and furnished with a comfortable chair and hassock, desk and chair, 42 inchc hd tv, and good ac/heating. The bathroom was quite large and very modern with one of the best, hottest showers I have encountered anywhere. The room wa extremely quiet, with the only noticeable sounds being an ambulance or police siren in the distance-typical of any big city hotel. Hotel elevators are fast, efficient, and quiet. Concierge service was excellent with some exceptional recommendations for small reasonable priced sushi and italian restaurants nearby as well as innorth beach and off the main tourist path. We did not eat in the hotel but judging by the catering provided by the hotel during my seminar, which included sushi, I would not hesitant to eat in Anzu and the razz room has some well known jazz entertainers. There is a small pool with hot tub and a fitness center which have a one-time charge for use. During our stay, half price reduced tickets rom the U Sq ticket booth were available for one of the performances. All in all I very nice hotel if it is wsithin your price points. Try Sakanna restaurant on Post for very inexpensive and delicious sushi; sotto mare and Ideale in N Beach for excellent very reasonably priced Italian; and Stella's bakery for coffee and a cannoli made up at the the time of request. And if you have time, view the Maxwell Parrish painting in the bar of the Palace Hotel and its turn of the 19th century adjacent dining room as well as the diego rivera mural at the San Francisco Art Institute on Chestnut St, both free.

“Best travel deal in SF!” What a terrific find for a special rate of $79/night! If you want Four Seasons-type amenities and comfort, then I just suggest you pay $600/night and go stay at the Four Seasons on Market Street. If you want a clean, comfortable, charming hotel in a safe, central location then check out this hotel. Yes, it's old but so is most of SF. The room was a decent size. We had no problems with the hot water. Best of all, we filled up each morning with a nice included breakfast. $79 room + breakfast = score!

“Thank you Hotel Newton! Comfy, quick stay” What a neat little place-- on Labor Day weekend, a single room happened to pop open and I snagged it, and wasn't let down.
