The room was pretty spacious with a desk and the remodeling was really nice, although I am not a fan of hideous bedspreads, but the bathroom is indeed gorgeous. Nice front desk service, but paid wifi was a bummer (albeit cheap). Would definitely return.

“Excellent Stay at Hotel Chandler...” My experience at this hotel has been top-notch from start to finish. Check-in was a breeze - within several minutes, I was in my room. The staff is very courteous and friendly. The room is spacious, well-lit, well air-conditioned, and very quiet. The bed is very comfortable. The location is well-situated to the Empire State Building, Grand Central Station and the rest of midtown. Overall, a great experience, and I will definitely return!

“It feels like home” This latest stay at the Omni was probably my 15th! Our company stays there each year for our spring conference. So I know the layout and the restaurants, which is comforting. It's an older property and the rooms are spacious - truly making it feel like I'm "home" at the end of the day. Staff are friendly, beds are comfortable, rooms are fairly quiet if you get one closer to the end of the hallway. The location is fantastic -- close to public transportation, the zoo, many wonderful restaurants. The area has many trees making it beautiful and relaxing. Roberts Restaurant features a daily morning and noontime buffet with good choices. Dinner options are excellent, well prepared. My leadership dinner was a huge success - starting with cocktails on the terrace, ending with superb service by private dining. The Omni still has the special touches for me!

“Great stay when in NYC” The location of the Novotel makes it worth the stay. On Broadway, on 52nd Street nice walk to Time Square. There are many places to eat near by. The brunch in the dinning room off the lobby is a bit expensive but it is all you need until dinner plus it has a great view of Time Square. We stay here once a year and we are never dissapointed. The staff is always attentive and helpful.

“Great Place to Stay” I stayed at the Travel Inn Manhattan on December 4, 2004 and I was very pleasantly surprised. Given that it was a weekend during the very popular holiday season, I had a very difficult time finding a hotel. I has originally booked a room at the Super 8 Times Square ($329), but based on the reviews here about bed bugs, I looked for something else. I paid $190 per night at the Travel Inn and for this time of year, that was a good price. I've also stayed in much worse hotels in Manhattan and paid more. The other reviews here about the Travel Inn are very accurate. Positives: Hotel was clean, the lobby was attractive, the people at the front desk were friendly, the reservations process was smooth, the hotel was quiet, the room (double-double) was the size of an average hotel room which is large for a city hotel, the elevators were large (again, for an older city hotel) and fast., and the bathroom was large enough to have some counter space. The pool looked nice though no one was swimming since it was December. There was an area in the parking garage to check bags between checking out and leaving town. Negatives: the towels were quite thin...I thought that the hand towel was a wash cloth

“FANTASTIC HOTEL” I stayed at the W in SF for four nights in Nov 04, and I found the entire experience fabulous! My room had an awesome view of the Bay Bridge, everything in the room was super-comfy (esp. the bed and the bathtub), the hotel is quiet in the halls, I loved the Bliss bath products, the room service was DELICIOUS every time and always arrived within 15 minutes of ordering, and all of the service was wonderful, from the front desk to the room service to the maids. I have spent a lot of time South of Market, so I know the neighborhood well, and this is a great locale! I did not want my W experience to end, and I can't wait until I check into the W Seattle in January! I highly rec. this hotel--it's a wonderful sanctuary from the hectic SoMa world outside.

“Retro Glam” I was attending a conference across the street at the Biltmore, but decided to stay at the Hilton instead. It's walking distance to LA Live and is and easy cab ride to Hollywood. The gym there is small, but it has a great view of the city.

“nice remodel” this hotel is quite elegant as it has just undergone a huge renovation. club floor has a nice hors deurve spread as well as a bountiful continental breakfast. located on 9th foor with a view of airport runways. staff is accomodating Italian restaurant serves fresh cuisine...very good walls are thin so you will hear the guest next door if they talk loud

“Excellent hotel; clean, comfortable and fantastic location!!” I booked this room using a Travelzoo special and got a rate of $99 per night; however, I would have been equally pleased paying the full rate. The location of this property is exceptional...immediately south of the river on Michican Ave. Within great proximity to all major attractions by foot, or public transportation. There are several different el stops within blocks, and a bus stop one block north and one block south. This hotel could not have a better location! I had a one bedroom, king size bed on the 24th floor; AMAZING views!!! The room was the largest I have had in a big city; it was truly comparable to a one bedroom apartment. Full kitchen, seperate bedroom, living room, bath and office space. Also, two flat panel tvs. And the bed was exceptionally comfortable. Internet access is free, however there is no WI-FI. But, the front desk will gladly give you an ethernet cable to use. We used our computer daily with no problems at all. The free breakfast each morning was very nice--lots of variety. Juices, coffee, fruit, cereal, waffles, bacon, eggs, full size bagels, muffins and pastries...the works! Also, a very nice fitness center with the basics needed for a workout while traveling and a business space to print boarding passes. The staff was also very friendly and helpful; easy to talk to and knowledgeable. I spend very little time in a hotel room when I travel, so value, cleanliness and location are the most important factors to me. Ths hotel delivered wonderfully on all of them. If you have a similar mindset, you will LOVE this hotel. Howver, there is no bellman, fancy lobby or concierge...so if the 5 star amenities are important to you, book elsewhere. Last note: I always like to know what types of casual eateries are just next door to a hotel; there is a Subway, a Chipolte and a Starbucks on the same block. There is an "On the Corner" bakery around the corner, and a Walgreens on the block as well. Everything you could need is a step away. This property made my vacation great! I highly reccommend!!!!!

“Great Experience” The hotel is located right on the Wharf. We were on the concierge floor and the concierge lounge has huge picture windows that look onto the water. The views from both the lounge and our room were beautiful. The hotel is located next to the Boston Acquarium and the IMAX theatre, is a close walk to Boston North area and is near the Freedom Trail. Location is great. The check in for the hotel is located on the second level. Rooms had the typical great Marriott bedding with very comfortable beds. The rooms were very clean and well appointed. I always think Marriott could improve the quality of its toiletries, and this hotel was no exception. Serve was excellent. We were allowed both an early check in and a late check out, as we were at the hotel during Hurricane Irene. This accommodation was very beneficial in light of canceled fligths and inclement weather. The appetizers, drinks and desserts in the concierge lounge were plentiful and of good quality. One of the reasons I prefer Marriott's with a concierge lounge is I love being able to go in and obtain a diet coke, a bottle of water, a piece of fruit etc., throughout the day without spending $5 from a mini bar for a diet coke. Would definitely return if in Boston again.

“Just gets better” Logistics hadn't allowed me to stay at the Kennsington Park for several years. After a four night stay at the end of September I can say that the quality of the hotel has just gotten better. The bed is the most comfortable I've ever had and the service is impeccable. The location, a block from Union Sq, gives you a great location but a little less crazy than outside the St Francis. The lobby is lovely and a good place to hangout and socialize. The concierge is great and the front desk staff is very helpful. The rates were very reasonable. I recommend paying a little extra for a room on the 11 or 12 floor.

“Traditional New York Luxury” I took my sister-in-law and two of my nieces (aged 10 and 6)for their first trip to New York and the St. Regis made it quite a memorable experience. Yes, it is very expensive, but worth the price. We stayed in a Grand Deluxe room, which was lovely. Decorated in muted green and gold, with modern amenities such as flat panel tvs. The staff couldn't have been nicer, bringing cookies and hot chocolate after a long day of sightseeing. I tried to book the Four Seasons, but they wanted us to book two rooms at almost $800 per night because of "occupancy requirements", which was ridiculous. The St. Regis could not have been more accomodating. Luxury like this certainly does come with a hefty price tag, but they also gave us wonderful memories.

“Convenient, Comfortable, Price was right!” I booked this hotel on hotwire at a great discount! We were in Baltimore to attend a baseball game, and took the Bolt Bus from NYC. If you bring your car, there is a $10 nightly charge to park in the lot at the hotel. The shuttle runs every hour and has specific stops, however if you are going somewhere else and you speak with the shuttle driver, they may take you. That was the case for us, and we gave them a nice tip! The area, as others have stated, is very much a non residential, non commercial area. There are a few gas stations, but it is primarily warehouses, it seems like a lot are being demolished. It's super close to the football and baseball stadiums, but I would not recommend walking due to the traffic, and no pedestrian walkway on the bridge. There were 2 squeegee men who spent the days across the street from the hotel offering to wash windows of cars passing by. They were very considerate, and certainly not threatening. The room was clean and comfortable, just what we expected. The breakfast service was good, the cinnamon rolls are always a highlight, the eggs were a bit gritty. Stay here if you don't mind being about 10-15 minutes from the inner harbor. You save quite a bit of money, but you don't sacrifice comfort. The staff was very friendly and helpful.

“Great Stay” Stay there for a night. Got a great deal on Hotwire. Check in was fast and the front desk people were very professional and very helpful. The room was spacious, well lit and clean; it was decorated in a modern style, and it had a separate area with a desk, great for working in the room. Two very comfortable beds, I would have rather had a king size, but I did not even try to ask for a change, since I was just there for the night. Very large bathroom with lots of handle bars for people with disabilities. However to get to the elevators you have to claim a few steps and I did not see a ramp or a different elevator, but I am sure there is access for wheelchairs, etc. One strange thing, in the bathroom there is something like a closet and you will find there some hangers with night garments for sale (for males and females), which are animal print inspired, and some socks... I thought it was strange, but nothing wrong with that, just not what I expected to see in a hotel bathroom. Did not check out the restaurant, but it seem quite busy even after 11 pm. The hotel does not have big lobby. My room faced the inside (as in towards where the air conditioners units were located), which was fine with me, since I imagine you may get some street noise if your room faces the street. Dupont Circle Metro station is less than 5 minutes walk. So Location, Location, Location. There was a mini bar, for which I did not asked for the key. And when I came home at night after going out, there was a jar of cookies, Oreo like, in the lobby which I thought it was a nice touch. I guess my only disappointing comment would be the fact that I would have liked a little coffee maker in the room. I believe they do have coffee in the lobby, I just did not check it out, since I was in a rush to leave the next morning. I liked this place, I recommend it and I would come back if I have a chance.

“Good stay - ideal for convention center” Stayed 3 nights in Mid July whilst attending a conference in the convention center. Paid £99 per night (~$165) via hotels.com - this is a fully inclusive rate (i.e. incl all taxes, etc). Hotel staff very friendly and professional. Hotel fine. Good business class comfortable rooms, free internet is fast and works. The 'desk chair' lets down so many hotels but not this one. Had the continental breakfast buffet one morning (~$12.50 incl tax) which was standard fare. Basement gym pool area. Gym is larger than expected with a couple of X-trainers, three(?) joggers, some weight machines and (I recall) some free weights. It's right across from the convention center and 2 blocks from 16th Street Mall. I'd happily stay there again.

“Great hotel!” This is the hotel we choose to stay when we are in Austin, the location cannot be beaten! I like going out to 6th street and not taking long to get back to my room after going to the bars. The hotel is gorgeous! The front staff are nice and so are the servers in the bar/grill. The room was so gorgeous, we had a corner room so we had a double view. I liked the ambiance of the room when we walked in, lamps with a dim light on and soft music to greets us. I highly recommend the Driskill, worth every penny and cannot wait to return.

“Upscale La Quinta with Excellent Service” Our experience at this hotel was excellent. After a long day of travel, the hotel was close to the airport and easy to find. The staff were friendly and helpful and check-in took less than 2 minutes. Our room was spacious, immaculate, and quiet. We picked-up toiletries and snacks at the nearby Walmart & used the in-room microwave to heat them up. The in-room refrigerator was welcomed for our beverages. The bed was extremely comfortable and we had a great night's rest. The complimentary breakfast offered many selections of breads, pastries, cereals, boiled eggs, coffee & juices. Check-out was as quick as check-in - again with a smiling, helpful staff member. After getting to our car, I realized I had left my cell phone in the room. The staff member immediately re-issued me a room key and I retrieved my phone within 5 minutes. We thoroughly enjoyed our brief stay and will definitely stay there again when in the area.

“No toiletries in room, otherwise excellent” I stayed at the Hotel Wales for one night following a business appointment in that neighborhood (Upper East Side). I did not select the hotel, and I did not pay for the room, so I cannot comment on its value. The room was VERY small, but plenty comfortable, and normal for NYC, I'm sure. No view worth mentioning-- side of another building, but the view from the rooftop terrace was wonderful. I wish I had had more time to relax up there. The free round-the-clock coffee/espresso/cappuccino service was awesome, and the continental breakfast was plentiful and delicious. All the staff were extremely courteous and warm. At check-in, the family ahead of me in line were inconsiderately asking dozens of mindless questions and requests, and the clerk gave me a sympathetic look and flagged someone else to help me, seeing that he wouldn't be free soon. I appreciated that. My one complaint was that while showering, I discovered that the cleaning staff had apparently forgotten to restock my room with soap and shampoo, which was extremely annoying. I had just used their small gym (very nice equipment!) and was a bit gross. However, since I was wet, naked, and rushed, I didn't really want to call the front desk and have soap delivered-- would have been awkward. I mentioned this at check-out, and the clerk was extremely apologetic. I'm sure these minor mistakes can happen, and since I wasn't paying for the room, no big deal.

“Clean, Spacious, Convenient to LAX” I recently spent one night at the Sheraton Gateway, and I was quite impressed, especially considering this is an airport hotel! The shuttle is quick and prompt, but it was completely jam packed with passengers and one brusque driver. Check-in was quick and efficient, and the lobby area is spacious and attractive. The hallways leading to the rooms had me a bit concerned as they didn't quite appear to be as recently renovated as the lobby. But, once I got in the room, all fears were squashed - the room was spacious, spotlessly clean, and very comfortable. The blackout drapes did the job, and there was essentially no noise from outside or the hallway. The only odd thing - I didn't see a clock in the room! I did check out the lounge, and the Sauvignon Blanc was quite good, too!

“Good choice near Matthews, NC” This hotel is now called "Best Western Plus Charlotte/Matthews". Technically, it's in Charlotte, but just a short distance from the Matthews city boundary, on Independence Blvd., a very busy urban arterial. The hotel is fine (although you can't open the windows), with friendly staff and a reasonable breakfast bar. The rooms are fully equipped, including refrigerator, microwave and coffee maker. There's not much of interest in the surrounding area, however, other than other motels and chain restaurants. If you're looking for someplace to eat, I recommend Hops Brewery, about 1 mile down Independence in Matthews.

“Hip get away” This hotel is in an entertainment complex. There is tons of stuff to do and the food choices are amazing. The aloft concept is a cool one and it made this old man feel slightly hip. Perfect for business or couples but I wouldn't take kids here, more of an adult vibe. The rooms were decorated nicely and cozy. Connected by bridges to other hotels. The staff was friendly and helpful.

“Great hotel” Recently stayed at this hotel for 2 nights on business, and I was really impressed with the updated decor, great service, and incredibly comfy rooms. The bed was very comfortable, the shower was just right, and the buffet breakfast was good. If staying in this area, I would highly recommend this hotel.

“Experience The Drake Hotel, Chicago.” We did a 4 week tour of the USA over December/January 2007, with 3 older children (girl, 22, boy, 19 and boy, 18), going to San Francisco [Omni Hotel], Miami (South Beach) [Beacon Hotel], Orlando (Disneyworld, Pop Century Resort), Chicago [Drake Hotel], New York (for Christmas) [Beacon Hotel], Boston [Omni Hotel], New York (again) [Roosevelt Hotel] (including New Year’s Eve at the Renaissance Hotel overlooking Times Square), and a day trip to Niagara Falls. It was sometimes very cosy - sometimes downright stressful - with the kids. Anyway, here are my accommodation reviews. I’ll mention side trips and tours too. Sometimes the accommodation was arranged through a travel agent, but on a couple of occasions I organised it direct. I chose The Drake purely on its reputation, history, celeb status, etc. I did not expect this to be a cheap or budget stay (and was not disappointed!), but I did try some cost-saving measures which The Drake was happy to accommodate (see below). Put simply, I wanted to stay at the famous Drake Hotel in Chicago, regardless of cost. I couldn't seem to get a travel agent who could organise it, so I ended up contacting the hotel itself. I tried email from their website several times early in 2007 (for a December stay), but received no response. As I really wanted to try this hotel, I ended up phoning it from Brisbane, and made the booking that way. The girl I spoke to was very helpful with room options, but despite a promise that I would receive email confirmation, none came. It may have been my "Strein" accent. However, when I sought confirmation in November by email, I did get a favourable response promptly by email, and when we arrived at the hotel for our 3 nights, all was in order. One thing to note - we couldn't pre-arrange transfers from Chicago O'Hare airport to the city (the only place in many countries and cities that I haven't been able to), but it was simple enough to arrange a return transfer door-to-door from the transport desk near luggage collection at the airport, and phone in a booking for the return journey. The Drake is an old and impressive building, with views of Lake Michigan. Great foyer. It was all I'd hoped for in that regard. It is very well located - close to shops (including Macy's) and restaurants (some great and reasonably priced Irish pubs - we ate twice at the close-by Dublin Pub it was so good - and it is also close to a great pancake place - The Original Pancake House - where we had breakfast every morning). Some of our best meals were in Chicago. The Drake is also virtually next door to the enormous John Hancock Centre (you can view The Drake from the top). Very convenient location. We had a Junior Suite with two bathrooms, which would have been superb for less people. It had 2 comfortable queen sized beds, couch and chair, desk and chair, TV unit with drawers, closet, room safe, minibar, ethernet, and two enormous bathrooms (I'd say the best bathrooms on the trip). As there were 5 of us, we also took 2 trundle beds (my cost-cutting measure) at no cost (that I'm aware of). The staff were helpful in that regard. That meant everyone had a separate bed, but it was cosy, and the two extra beds (which stood upright during the day) took up a lot of floor space at night. We had windows but were too low down for a good view. The room was quite austere - very Hilton - but nothing to complain about. Reception/check-in was fine, as was check out, and the staff helpful with maps, etc. We did a city tour with an ex-Chicago cop as a bus driver/tour guide, which was very entertaining. We later changed buses to go to the John Hancock Centre (which was the last stop on our tour). Both drivers were happy to stop the bus and open the doors to let me take photos. Afterwards, when we were supposed to be returned to our hotel (remember - just around the corner from the John Hancock Centre), that bus driver was kind enough to take us all the way to the Sears Tower, even though he was under no obligation to do so. Just us 5 in the big coach - he earned his tip for that! At the Sears Tower, the bus driver (at his own suggestion) got out of the bus, lay on his back on the sidewalk and took photos of us 5 with the Sears Tower towering above us. Very friendly folk in Chicago. One girl passing in the street offered us help to find the Dublin Pub without being asked, simply because she'd heard us mention it . Lake Michigan was an awesome sight in winter. I recommend the free zoo at Lincoln Park. Chicago was great, and though expensive, I'm pleased that I stayed at The Drake.

“Good downtown location” Located across from the Boston Garden and walking distance to the subway and commuter rail. Lots of bars and restaurants in the area. We were upgraded to a suite which was nice. Only negatives about the room was that the toilet continued to run if you didn't wiggle the handle and the thermostat was falling off the wall and didn't always work. Room had a separate bedroom with a flat screen TV. Room included a refrigerator. Holiday Inn Express always has a nice breakfast buffet and this one was no different. Friendly front desk staff. Overall a very good hotel!
“Very nice hotel, great room for the $” I booked this hotel for an overnight stay in Houston. It had a shuttle, very good restaurant, clean room with all the amenities and super comfortable bedding.

“Comfy and nicer than I expected!” I would best describe this hotel and a cross between a Sheraton and an Aloft hotel mixed together. The decor and comfort of a Sheraton but the modern style of an Aloft! Issac at the front desk was extremely helpful and even gave us a complimentary upgrade to a suite for our 2nd night of a 2 night stay! Will def stay here again! The only negative was when we got back from a day at the zoo and Aquarium we changed into our bathing suits and were excited to go jump in the pool and then relax in the hot tub. The pool was not heated and the water was ice cold. There was not a hot tub at all! We had to turn right back and go back to our room. I'm sure the pool will be fine once it starts getting hotter though.

“Good Service in Columbus” We stayed for 3 nights while visiting family recently. The hotel is right downtown. It is close to German Village, the Brewery District and more. I found the valet service to be interesting. They would park your car and bring you your car, but they did not push you at all to take your luggage, etc. The valet attendants were all friendly. The lobby was nice and the staff friendly and helpful. We ate in the hotel restaurant each morning on the woman who waited on us was very nice. The room was nice and the view was ok. The only thing I didn't like was having to pay over $20 for valet parking every night with no self-parking option in a downtown that is not exactly buzzing during the day or night.

“Classy Contemporary Comfort at Madison Hotel” Terrific hotel in downtown Memphis. Very friendly staff, large and comfortable rooms with many nice amenities. Nice pool, small but serviceable gym, good food.

“Great place for a city stay” The location of this hotel is its greatest asset. My adult son and I stayed here for three nights and walked everywhere- to Pikes Market, the Space Needle and everywhere in between. The rooms are small, but clean. The bathroom has very limited shelf space for toiletries, but not a huge problem. The room was quite warm even with the heat off so we propped the window open which made it manageable. Seattle's Best coffee for the in room coffee maker was a nice touch. We parked at the parking garage next door which was $23/ day for guests.

“Tries a bit too hard but a fine place to stay” The Rittenhouse is in a great location and we had a fine view of the Square. The rooms were large and the layout a bit quirky. Plenty of room and a nice stall shower, complete with the usual upscale toiletries. I had a few complaints--an impossible to understand $100 free coupon which cost $50 and the usual champagne and chocolate covered strawberry welcome when you really just want a quick efficient check in--but oversll we were more than satisfied with our stay. The breakfast was great, the service fine and overall a sophisticated hotel, expecially for Philadelphia whihc is not known for this.

“Perfectly Adequate” The property is not in a great part of Austin but is convenient to the airport. That being said, I think it is good for a business traveller who is using the airport. If you are going to experience Austin, then I would recommend staying downtown or in the northern part of the city since the hotel is right on the highway in a not so great part of town. If you are looking for economy, numerous other properties are located in the immediate area which may be of better value. The property itself is clean and has an attractive interior. The bed was comfortable and the room was clean and small. There was nothing special about the hotel but also was not substandard in any way. I will say that I ordered breakfast room service and it was quite disappointing in quality. Since the property is on a highway, I would recommend the numerous surrounding options for breakfast as the Huevos Rancheros I ordered were typically pricey room service but more importantly disgusting. If you want nice accomodations close to the airport but not close to nightlife or the better parts of Austin, this hotel will be totally sufficient.

“Beautiful room, noisy neighbors” The room would have been perfect, only marred by cigarette burns here and there. The pillow top mattress would have provided a nice rest, if it weren't for the very loud and generally inconsiderate displaced New Orleanians.

“Perfect if you need to be close to LAX” We stayed one night at this hotel in anticipation of an early morning flight the next day. It was very clean, room was spacious, had a Starbucks in the lobby and a good gift shop - all of which made me happy. We used the shuttle to the airport without problems. My husband has also stayed at the Hilton next door and said that Marriott was definitely nicer. I would certainly stay here again if I need to be close to LAX.

“great location, nice hotel” The Westin Indianapolis is a nice (not great) hotel located in an ideal location attached to the convention center. The rooms ae comfortable and the heavenly beds are indeed heavenly. The hotel is large, but smallish compared to those located in big cities. Service is good.

“Can't Beat the Price” Chose this hotel because it was close to where we were going. Not the best place if you are coming for the Denver sites, but if the location fits your plans, you cannot beat this Doubletree for the price. We paid $89. Spacious and pleasant. Extremely helpful staff. We needed a 2nd room due to a miscommunication and they handled it with terrific customer service and a great compromise. Look forward to returning again soon.

“A good value adjacent to a ritzy area.” The Galleria section of Houston is a busy hub of corporate and high-end retail activity, and many of the local hotel options can be pretty pricey. This property is located just outside the Galleria district, which is reflected in the more reasonable rates. It’s still a very convenient location; it was less than a 15 minute drive from the hotel to my company’s Galleria office. It’s not in the best neighborhood I’ve ever seen, but it’s not all that bad, either. They do offer gated parking for guests for that extra piece of mind. Check-in and check-out were efficient and cordial. The complimentary breakfast area was well-maintained and featured a different hot egg and meat item each day. My room was certainly large enough, the plumbing, air conditioning and appliances were all in good working order, and the bed was very comfortable. The only downside was that my room’s entry door was not flush to the door frame, so I could hear whatever was going on in the corridor quite clearly. The hotel was undergoing renovations during my latest stay, so perhaps that will be corrected in the future. One nice touch (especially in hot, humid Houston) is that they offer ice water in the lobby throughout the day. In the afternoon they put out fresh-baked cookies. This is the second time I’ve stayed at this property, and both times I found it very suitable for my needs (and my company’s budget).

“Somethings Missing” Stayed at the Houstonian for two nights on business this week nd I have to say that this property lacks any real personality. The check-in was not personable, the room was bland but nice quality, the restaurant for breakfast was in-diffrent. The hotel does seem to be a big spot for corporate meetings and it seems that meeting are the focus more than the individual traveler. The facility is terrific- it just lacks any spirit or feeling of Texas hospitality

“You MUST read this if you are considering staying in Boston” We were at the Hay Adams (opposite the White House), followed by the Ritz Carlton in Central Park, NYC (both superb hotels) immediately prior to arriving at the Boston Harbour, which I really didn't expect would compare with our previous American hotels on this trip. I had done a late switch from the Boston W, as I wanted a sea view and a friend told me I'd hate the trendy bathrooms at the W. This hotel has been the surprise of our trip. If you are reading this, you are most likely wondering where to stay in Boston. Look no further. The Boston Harbour is way ahead of the curve and to such a degree that I'm seriously impressed. The clientele seems circa 70% relaxed businessmen and 30% tourists. As always, it's only when the staff at a hotel work as a superbly well co-ordinated team that something really special emerges. At the Boston Harbour the service, the efficiency, the care to detail and the total competence makes it a pleasure to be a guest. Examples: I told the hotel that one of my daughters is coeliac. Nobody on the property had to be told a second time....it was sorted.....and they deliver gluten free homemade miniature cakes every evening. We needed extra hangers....the fast-dial button for housekeeping didn't work on one of our three telephones and so I called the concierge with my request for hangers.....I later noticed that they replaced the telephone with a brand new one. Everyone is immaculately turned out, especially the housekeeping staff who are also spot-on with every request and quick. The Concierge Desk is firing on all cylinders. Ronnie Lamming, one of the concierges, is the best I've encountered anywhere in the world, since I stayed at The Setai in Miami two years ago where they also have a fantastic concierge service. It was a joy to discuss Boston with Ronnie, given it was our first visit to the city. I have a love/hate relationship with concierges.....e.g. I detest them at Trump and I'm appalled by the mafia-like activities at some other hotels. Few are perfect. Here, the Concierge desk is state of the art and will greatly enhance any visit. All their advice has been good. They also got us best seats for the opening of Riverdance at the Opera House and Red Sox tickets for the first game of the 100th season, both last minute. From the reception, to the door team, housekeeping, restaurant staff, concierge....it's impressively together. I tend to post on Tripadviser when somewhere is terrible or very good. The Boston Harbour is absolutely first class. Too many top hotels have beds that need replacing....not here. Pillows are also high quality. Rooms are very well fitted out. However what makes this hotel extra special are the huge windows overlooking the harbour. If in Boston on business, why stay down anywhere else when you can have a full-on harbour view and feel like you are on vacation. Similarly the view from breakfast restaurant makes a great start to the day....as do the breakfasts. From perfect freshly squeezed orange juice to the Pellegrino house water, it's very good. One day I wanted a bagel with lox (smoked salmon). Our waiter, a smiling lady called Susan asked me what type of bagel, they have them all. I then asked if they has Low Fat cream cheese. They did. I then wondered if by any chance they had low fat cream cheese with chives? Susan went off and brought it, having chopped up the chives and mixed them in herself. I'm not a VIP guest, they don't know me from Adam, this is the standard of treatment everyone receives here. The gym/pool is also first rate. As I'm travelling with two young daughters, I love the fact that they have times when children cannot use the pool. That way, adult guests can hardly complain when children make a little noise. The leisure facilities and staff are lovely. The shower works well. As does everything else in our accomodation. So it should, you may say. That is not the reality. At Sandy Lane, Barbados, one of the leading hotels in the world, room equipment has been a constant, ongoing irritation. After 8 stays over the past 4 years and after paying them a fortune for the privilege, I won't return. I will return to Boston and I will 100% certainly return to the Boston Harbour hotel. It is exceptional value for money, unlike Sandy Lane. Given how easy it is to get around Boston, why stay anywhere else? Finally the bell desk (as good as it gets) also double at driving guests about in the hotel sedan. One night I was embarrassed as I kept the car waiting 20 minutes beyond pick-up time following a superb dining experience at the plush 2nd floor restaurant in the Legal Sea Foods building....another terrific concierge recommendation. I would have been on time but for an exceptional experience there.....but that's for another review....but do also go dine there. We love Boston. It's so good when expectations are dwarfed by the reality. PS the free wi-fi is very fast and works everywhere

“Nice hotel in the Van Nuys Area” The room I had was very large and accommodating. Everything was clean except for the top of the toilet-- a hair. Internet worked great. Signal for TV was sketchy for about 2 hours one night. While carpets in hallway were showing a little wear, the carpet in the room was nice and fresh, The bed was very comfortable. The breakfast was super--not sure of the cost; it was free as a gold member, Everything you need or want with regard to shopping is within walking distance. Recommened in Van Nuys area.

“Another Fine Sofitel” Stayed here Apr 11 -14 and wasn't disappointed. Paid for an upgraded room and glad we did as it seemed to have the better views - the cheaper rooms appeared to look out over an alley. We had a view of a big church from our 5th floor window. All was as I've come to expect from Sofitel ... comfy beds, good service, etc, etc, though on one day the room wasn't made up until after 5.00pm. Breakfast buffet was a bit uninspiring, but there was plenty of it, and endless coffee. Would recommend it.

“What a view from the room !” This is third visit to San Francisco and this time, we actively took the decision to stay in a completely different areas and get off the beaten track a little bit and not stay near Union Square (2 years ago we stayed at The Clift). The views from the room was the reason we booked this hotel. Well we did splash out and get bay bridge room and it was worth it - it was a suite and the view from the room was fantastic. Would definitely recommend this hotel and if you can stretch to the bat bridge room, you wont regret it and it is well worth every penny !!!

“Another decent stay” This was my second stay at this hotel. Yes, it's a little noisy from various things such as the noisy plumbing and paper thin walls, but overall it's not a bad place. Room was clean, except for the requested fridge, which contained an old bowl of what appeared to be ice cream, and it had gone bad. Someone did come to clean out the fridge very promptly though. Also, of the best hotel showers I've ever come across. VERY powerful. Internet service was very fast compared to most hotels I've stayed in. Didn't eat at the restaurant. Shuttle service was very prompt whenever I needed it. Tip: Ask for a room on the ground floor, close to the lobby if you have heavy bags. On my previous stay, I had room 2407 which was very far away from the elevator and it involved a lot of walking. Very difficult with heavy bags! This time I had room 1208 and the location was great. Overall, I'd recommend this hotel.

“Great airport hotel stopover” Hotel is located directly across the street from the SeaTac Airport. Lobby is huge and spacious, check-in was friendly and quick. Room was very nice, two double beds, flat screen TV, in room safe which is a big plus, nice bathroom, very clean, with huge fluffy towels. Also offers complimetary shampoo, body lotion, and conditioner. The one big minus is no free wifi, at $12.95 for 24 hours or $4.99 for one hour is in my opinion a rip off. But find that most American chains charge so guess they are in line with others. There is a restaurant, did not eat there, but prices seemed quite high. Free shuttle from/to the airport is included in the rate and runs every 20 minutes. There are a couple of restaurants in the area, 13 Coins about one block away, and some fast food restaurants about 3/4 blocks south. If you arrive by the Sond Transit Link train from downtown Seattle you are but steps away from the hotel. You can walk from the hotel to the airport in less than 10 minutes.

“Lacking a bit for a Hilton” Our regular hotel was booked and this was closest Hilton property to use my points. You need to look carefully at it's location to find it easily. It's on a 'non traffic' part of Travis St., block west of Main. I found the signage a bit confusing and wound up trapped in the parking (front desk came and 'rescued' us). There was no bellman, but the desk clerk that rescued us, filled that job too. We were there on a Sa. and Su. night. The gift shop was never open and you couldn't get a paper. The breakfast buffet was not I expect of a Hilton and was overpriced. We had a two room suite which was really nice.

“Beautiful hotel!” My wife and I stayed overnight at the Book Cadillac for our anniversary. We got a great deal on the hotel's website for $109 non-refundable, which I thought was a great price. Parking is pretty reasonable at $10 per night at the attached garage. The hotel is a little far from other downtown attractions, but there is a people station very close to the hotel. We took the people mover to the Ren Cen and got there in about 10 minutes. The hotel features a really cool mix of classic architecture and modern decor. All of the old sculpture work and moldings have been kept intact and they are beautiful. Our room was very spacious, with a very comfortable king size bed, several lamps, 42 inch LCD television, and a compact but loud Boston Acoustics radio. The bathroom was large with nice granite vanity and shower with dual showerheads. Keep in mind this hotel was very recently renovated, so the rooms are in great shape and very modern. The only drawback were the prices at the Motor Bar downstairs. The place had a cool atmosphere, but my wife and I thought $9 a drink was too steep. Overall, we had a great time at the Book Cadillac and I would recommend this hotel to anyone who wants a comfortable stay in downtown Detroit.

“Confirming all of the Positive Comments” What everyone has said is all true - huge, clean rooms, comfortable beds, and the location on the East side is only a 10-15 minute walk to Rock Center and Times Square. Easy access to anywhere else in the city with a close subway and major throughfares for taxi's (2nd and 3rd Ave move quickly). Nice restaurants in the area, too. The Staff is extremely friendly. And you can often find a great rate under $200, if your timing is right. Downside? No free internet, that's about it

“Not your typical aloft” I really like aloft hotels. I think the concept is fantastic, the rooms comfortable, the food options more than adequate – and the value is tremendous. But I never considered writing a review as the consistency of the properties and the services is just that – really, really consistent. Essentially, why write a review when things are always the same and always very good. The aloft in Dallas is an exception. Walking in, the familiar décor is there, but the lobby is physically much larger than their other properties. I was upgraded to a suite – another first at aloft. And the room size was enormous and was very nice. I strongly recommend this hotel.

“Best in Class!” I had the pleasure of staying at the Hilton Bayfront for 9 days in early June. I was there on business as my company was holding a large event there. I had stayed there 3 times prior to this, while we were in the planning stages and each time I have enjoyed my stay tremendously. How do I begin? The rooms are excellent. The food is excellent and the cocktails are amazing. The Spa is also wonderful! Rooms: I love the beds, the view, the amenities. . .you name it. I've stayed in a regular room, one of their new "PUR" rooms and this last time I had a Suite. I can't fault any of them. Then there's the bar. . .Odysea is wonderful. They make classic cocktails, like the French 75 and a mean Manhattan. Plus specialty cocktails that change with the seasons. Knowledgable bartenders, friendly staff and the appetizers are great too. The food at Vela was outstanding, though the server we had on one occasion could have used a little caffeine to get him moving. The service was very slow. The breakfast buffet is very good, if a little pricey. . . but then again, it is San Diego and the location adds onto the price. The spa services were wonderful and the pool is a dream. Overall, Highly recommended. I'd stay there on my own dime anytime!

“Best Times Square view you can get, comfy spacious suite” This was my 10th visit to New York. I stayed here 30th May for 2 nights, and paid $250 per night (including tax) in advance to get the cheapest rate. I chose a King suite with a Times Square view. I really liked the room. The bedroom is separate so you can enjoy a quiet night without being disturbed by any noise from guests walking past the room. The sofa-bed was fairly comfortable, and the fridge was useful. The giant flat screen TV in the living room did not work properly. I am sure if I had reported it I could have got it fixed, but we did not spend much time in the room. Check in and out was very quick and easy, and the hotel stored our luggage on our last day. The bar in the lobby was small and always very quiet; but there are many bars around the hotel for a more lively experience. The best thing about the room was the view. We could see all of Times Square. I don’t think any other hotel in the area could give you as great a view – one that is now even more interesting since Broadway has been shut off to traffic and you can sit on chairs right in the middle of Times Square! I have stayed at the Marriott Marquis in a Times Square view room, and it was not as spectacular and cost a lot more. The area is obviously very busy all the time from the moment you step out of the hotel, but you only had to go round the side of the hotel and there was space to stand without being disturbed, or on the new light up red stairs above the TKTS booth outside the hotel . From my experience the rates at this hotel are usually pretty high; but if you can get a great rate like I did I really recommend the Doubletree Times Square. The following weekend I stayed at The Hilton on 6th Avenue, which was also very nice and I have reviewed this hotel too.

“The "New" Algonquin” We love staying at this hotel. It is our favorite hotel in the Times Square area. The staff is different here. They have a very professional way about them. We have stayed at the Algonquin at least 10 times and the service is always the same....Excellent!! The renovation seems to have gone very well. The newly decorated rooms have very nice bathrooms. They have managed to keep the charm of the Algonquin and update it at the same time.

“Brilliant hotel ! Love it.” Stayed here for two nights attending Otakon and preparing for a meeting before moving on to Washington DC for a few days of meeting. Love this hotel. Its modern with sleek lobby and rooms. The restaurant is stunning with a great view onto the inner harbour. It has its own mini shopping mall "Gallery" and for Starbuck addicts, it has a Starbuck in the mall. It has a good atmosphere, with non-stop jazz as background music in the lobby. Concierge is very helpful and very knowledgeable. Reception counter staff very patient and helpful. Location is great. It is on the inner harbour. which is very pretty, and "the place" to be. Among all the hotels in Baltimore, it has the best location. What makes a good hotel ? Good decor, good maintenance/upkeep (including everything in the room need to work), good location, convenience for shops/restaurants, friendly/knowledgeable staff, good atmosphere. This hotel tick all the boxes.

“Printers need ink, otherwise, very good value” This Courtyard is a great location near the 805 freeway. It is very quiet with very nicely kept grounds, a pool, and relaxation areas. Staff was very courteous and we had a very nice and fast check in. Nice lobby with plenty of comfortable seating. A car is a must if staying at this property. Free parking.

“Recommended - we would return” Stayed here 4 nights from Apr 10th, we arrived early for check-in and were pleasantly suprised to receive an upgrade to a king suite. Lovely spacious suite with 2 bedroom areas, small kitchen area with mini-bar fridge/coffee making facilities and decent sized bath/shower room. The staff were all very pleasant and helpful. The location is ideal for the North End and Quincy Market and a short walking distance from Downtown/Boston Common areas, plenty of restaurants in the nearby area. We had an enjoyable stay and I would recommend this hotel.

“Wonderful downtown location” My daughter and I stayed at the Courtyard Marriott during a visit I made in November. The location was great for all the area sightseeing we were doing on foot. The room was very comfortable and spacious for a downtown hotel. The lobby was spacious and accommodating for a brief break before heading to a new location. We always require a feather free environment and although I had failed to place that request at the beginning, a note to housekeeping and the feather pillows were removed. The staff at the desk were always friendly and I felt very safe with the doorman who kept watch on the coming and goings. The hotel was clean, and well kept. I would definitely consider it again. One note, as I was staying two nights then heading for New York and returning to Philly on Sunday. I did not stay at the Marriott for my return trip because of the huge increase in price. Definitely want to pay attention to the rate structure.

“Beautiful hotel” This beautiful hotel is close enough to downtown with easy access to all the major freeways throughout the metroplex. The new beds are incredible and the rooms are nice. The parking leaves a little to be desired, but it was adequate. The staff was very friendly and helpful. The rooftop pool was very warm and the terrace offered great views of the Dallas skyline. Altogether another wonderful Marriott experience.

“Wonderful location and great service” Stayed here during April break with my 13 year old daughter for two nights. Picked this hotel because of its location. It's in the heart of the theater district and we could walk to every place we wanted to see. The included breakfast saved us some money even though it wasn't the most exciting meal we've ever had. All the restaurants in the area made up for it though. Our room had two queen sized beds and was clean and comfortable. The bathroom looked a little ragged around the edges, but was also very clean. The hotel was filled with children (also on school break) but our room was surprising quiet. Didn't hear the traffic outside or the kids in the hallways. The service at the front desk was very pleasant as was the ability to check out bags in early. We arrived at the hotel during the latter part of the morning and were thrilled to be able to leave our luggage behind as we went wandering around. Would stay here again in a heartbeat.

“Great location, lovely room, nice meal” Stayed in a suite with riverfront views. Loved it. I have stayed there before; the thing I recalled best were the broiler-like heaters they have to keep people warm outside. Pleased that I am not taller or my hair would have sizzled! Check-in was efficient, lunch was quite good, room service good, wake up call on time and bed comfortable. Walking distance to almost everything downtown. Very convenient and would stay there again. Wonderful restaurants all around.

“Mixed feelings...good & not so good” We had 2 visits a few weeks apart, so we have combined the review. On our first visit, Ashley greeted us on our arrival...very friendly, competent. There is valet service, but we prefer to take our own luggage to our room. As platinum members, we received each a comped breakfast and self-parking for our vehicle in their parking garage. We received an upgrade to a large king suite with a fridge & microwave. We were even delighted as we walked into our room with a beautifully wrapped plate of fruit and edible goodies on the table.We had received a corner room with an awesome view of a fountain on one side & the river on other side. We had a very comfortable bed w foam mattress with lots of pillows. Our first visit, the breakfast buffet was fine, plentiful, but if we were paying the $13.49 we felt they should have had an egg station...w health issues I only ate oatmeal, fruit and milk. The next return to the hotel, during breakfast we were greeted by Heather, who said the breakfast did include "to order" eggs as well as other items....apparently a misunderstanding on our earlier visit. The breakfast staff was overall very friendly & seemed to really enjoy their jobs. As we had left the hotel on our first visit, we had requested the same room type on our return reservations. On our second visit, a few weeks later, the hotel was much busier with a few groups, so on our arrival we unfortunately did not receive our requested room type & instead got a much smaller room with 2 full beds (which were not the foam mattresses). We did get the comped breakfast & free self-parking. Our room did not have a refrigerator/microwave, nor a safe. A compliment to Pam, who was patient as I called her desk often to look for cancellations, so we could get a larger bed. Eventually the next day we got a queen bed room...still small, no fridge, no microwave or safe, but did have the comfortable foam mattress. I guess we get spoiled staying in so many Staybridges & Holiday Inn Expresses, which each have so many more amenities than the Crowne Plazas & for less of a price. Also we were so impressed with our King suite upgrade on the first visit, that we were disappointed on our second visit with the small room & bed.

“Nice hotel, great location, pricey” This was a 2 night weekend stay to see the heart of Boston. Hotels downtown in Boston are never cheap, and we actually went the Hotwire route in this case. The rates for this property are typically high, like $300 a night at the standard room level. Review... GOOD: --Great location, walking distance to a lot of the good stuff to see --Nice property, classy and elegant all around --Rooms are very nice, comfortable and well-appointed --Service is excellent --Sunday brunch was among the best I've had BAD: --Pricey, unless you get lucky --Rooms are a bit small --Sunday brunch was also far and away the most expensive I've had Overall, I'd say if the rate is within your budget, and particularly if you can get a good deal, this is a fantastic hotel to choose.

“Very nice hotel, bed and TV need an upgrade but price is right” Booked a one night stay via Kayak for $87. Fantastic price for a very nice hotel in a great location. $16 for parking is not out of line with hotels in this area. This hotel far exceeds the Sheraton Suites down the street. The rooms at the Royal Sonesta (formerly Intercontinental) are not huge. Even my corner room which is 30% bigger than a typical room isn't big by any standard. The hotel rooms are updated but the old TV with poor reception and the non-lux bed are the exception. (Bed linen is nice but the bed isn't anything to write home about) The hotel is going to have an update in the spring hopefully they will address these issues. The floor I was on had numerous teenagers but I couldn't hear them at all. For the price paid you cannot get a better deal in Houston.

“Clean rooms, fantastic location” I was in town for business, but the hotel's downtown location, with its proximity to nice places to eat, hang out (kind of college crowd-ish, but a good scene), and its convenience to the bank and to Starbuck's make it really nice for feeling comfortable for a visitor without a car. The service was pretty good, all were friendly and helpful. I met a hotel employee in the hall, asked where was the pool and the gym, and she took the elevator with me and showed me around a bit. The gym is nice, well-kept, with cardio machines and weights. The pool is kind of oddly small, but clean, and really only one person can do a lap in it. There's a nice hot tub, though. The decor of the room is an understated elegant style, but very pleasant and comfortable. The bed's very comfortable, though the pillows are overstuffed. Plenty of towels, and a very nice marble tile shower (no bath). A very nice stay with a comfortable seating area with a sofa, and a useful writing area for getting work done. Getting on to the Internet is easy, too. Downside: my colleagues thought parking was high ($25). Since we're consultants in business for ourselves, we purposefully looked for less expensive parking, and it was right around the corner for $10 instead. As you walk back to the hotel, there's a nice little cafe that has good coffee and breakfast sweets, and chocolate truffles made in-house, too. We had breakfast in the restaurant downstairs one day, too, it was fine, but there are plenty of good and less expensive places to get breakfast. All in all: A good stay at a well-run, very clean, well-kept hotel, at a great location.

“Great place to stay!” My husband and I had a weekend getaway Dec 17-18 and we stayed in room 606. Location: It's great. I usually prefer to stay in midtown, but this is a great option too! It's right across from the Lincoln Center, which looked especially gorgeous decorated for Christmas. The subway is also just across the street and Central Park is just a short walk. Lobby and hotel itself: It's swanky. The lobby is very impressive and fits the boutique label. The bar was hopping and looked fun, but since I'm pregnant, we didn't partake. Check-in was fine. I asked for a quiet room since I'm a light sleeper and preferably a king or queen bed. Room: We ended up on the 6th floor in a small room with a queen-sized bed. There really was not a view - just saw another building since we were in the back of the property. I understand why the guy who checked us in put us there though - it was quiet. We didn't hear cars honking or traffic sounds, and we were at the very end of the hall. Yes, it was small, but it was perfectly fine for us for 1 night. The bed was awesome, so comfortable! Be aware, if you are allergic to feathers/down, let them know. There was a feather bed, feather pillows, and a down comforter. Fortunately, we're not allergic and I love the softness of down bedding. Linens were high quality. The bathroom is tiny. The sink is poorly designed and placed. It was very challenging to wash my face and even washing my hands was difficult due to the strange design. It looks nice but the functionality is lacking. The bathroom amenities are very nice quality. We had plenty of hot water but the shower pressure was just ok due to the rain-style shower head. Again, it looks good, but not the most functional. Other thoughts: This is an old building. It gives it plenty of charm, but there are also quirks. When the people in the room next to us took a shower, dang, it was loud. It sounded like a loud sink was running right next to my head. Fortunately I was able to fall back alseep, but it was annoying. Overall, my husband and I really enjoyed our stay here and would definitely visit again (if the price is right).

“One Of The Best Airport Hotels - - anywhere!” The Westin at DTW is a good combination of location, service and comfort. Connected to the Delta terminal, it’s a perfect place to stay if you have a late/early connection or are traveling into Detroit for business. The rooms are very tasteful - decorated in muted earth tones. The bed is as advertised – heavenly and the bathroom / shower are above average. There is a reasonably good gym, pool and spa area – nice after long flights. The restaurant is also quite good (fire grilled pizza’s are better than most hotel food). I’d say the service is above average, but not perfect. At times the check in process can be very slow and irritating when I see only one person working at the desk and two others talking about schedules. Recently, they reduced the hours of operation for the club lounge to a schedule that makes no sense to me at all. Weighing the pro’s and con’s I’d say that the Westin is a very good hotel and is perhaps one of the best airport hotels in the country.

“Great Hotel” I really enjoyed my recent stay at the Hyatt Regency Baltimore. I am a loyal Marriott customer and I got a great deal for this hotel on Expedia so I gave it a shot. Lets just say I booked my next stay in DC with a Hyatt as well! I arrived late and check in was easy. The Front desk clerk, Valet and Doormen were very nice. I arrived in my room and it was clean and nice, the only issue I saw was a spot on the bench which of course I avoided like the plague. Otherwise the room was very nice. A beautiful view of the Harbor with floor to ceiling windows. There were extra pillows which I requested which was a nice attention to detail. I had to hurry and get to the bar/restaurant before it closed at midnight as I my flight into Baltimore was very late. Even though it was 15 minutes to close the wonderful bartender not only let me order food but stay and eat it while she was closing up. Thank you Debbie! Then I witnessed her serve another guest who showed up five minutes after closing. She even chatted with us both. This is great service at midnight! The housekeeper Chantay was very friendly and did a wonderful job refreshing my room while I was out at the Inner Harbor. She even wrote me a sweet note thanking me for the tip. The bed was very comfortable and the shower was nice. There were only two issues I dealt with while I was there... first one is a preference, I like a hotel hairdryer attached to the wall for convenience and cleanliness. The one they had was underneath the sink on a shelf and did not feel like it was cleaned very often. The other issue was that I put one of the large bottles of water in the fridge that was on the table and a flyer was left instructing me not to place things in the fridge. I called down to get a fridge so I could have my $5 bottle of water cold but they never brought me one even though they said they would. Neither issues were a big deal just little things that I would fix if I were the manager. There should be room left in the fridge for a guests bottle of water or an additional guest fridge. If I am willing to pay $5 for your bottle of water I should be able to keep it cold if I would like. I would definitely stay there again. Baltimore is a great place to visit with so many fun things to do and the Hyatt Regency Baltimore is in a perfect location to see them all!

“Central location, convenient for business meetings” Very central location, easily accessible, close to public transportation, and close to downtown corporate offices, shopping, sightseeing, with plenty restaurants nearby. Room is of decent size, nicely appointed, with electronic window covering, which is quite nice and less dusty comparing to cloth ones.

“Great location” We stayed here the last week of March for two nights. We were unexpectedly given a free upgrade when we checked in, so we had a suite. It was large enough to accommodate a full size crib (or almost full size), which the hotel provided free of charge. The bedroom had 2 double beds, tv, nightstand, and chair; the living area had a regular size couch, chair, coffee table, tv, and a desk. Everything was very clean, although there was a wet spot by the heater in the bedroom. The hotel has refrigerators available for $10 a night, although we did not use that option. Our view was beautiful--looking out over the planetarium and part of Central Park. There were plenty of restaurants and small stores close by, as was the subway. The location was perfect--it feels like you are just part of a neighborhood, but you are across the street from the Natural History museum, 1 block from Central Park, and a 5 minute walk to the Metropolitan Museum of Art (and just a few more minutes to many other hotels on 5th Avenue). It was so nice to be away from the crazy crowds down in Midtown. We felt very safe. One minor drawback was that when guests in adjoining rooms were using the water in the bathroom (shower/bath), the pipes were pretty loud. And you have to pay for the internet, which is pretty silly these days. But overall, it was a great hotel for our family and for our vacation and we would recommend to others, especially those traveling with children--and we would definitely reserve a suite next time so that we had plenty of room.

“Great Hotel.” This hotel may be a little hard to find, but it is a top recommendation for staying in Philadelphia. It is small and very quiet, but the service is good and friendly, and the rooms are sensational. It also offers a normal breakfast cafe in the basement. The location is ok, the street being much more like an alleyway, and is surrounded by much taller buildings, but is a block away from Rittenhouse Square.

“Friendly staff and comfortable room” Door staff and check in staff very friendly. Allowed us to check in a little early also. Room is small but very clean. Bathroom is modern and huge flatscreen TV. Would try again.

“Great location. Needs updating.” We booked this stay through a travel website offering a package on airfare and a hotel. I have stayed at several other Omni properties (including St. Louis and Chicago) and figured that it was a safe bet. The Omni Berkshire Place is in an older building right in the middle of midtown so space is at a premium and the hotel does a good job with what it has. The lobby is small but welcoming, the general areas are wearing well and don't feel as dated as the guest rooms feel. The view from the top of the hotel and the very nice health club are excellent. The king bed guest rooms do not leave much room for spreading out--but that isn't unusual for a hotel in NYC. The furnishings in the guest rooms we saw are showing their age (e.g. conventional tube television, bedspread rather than duvee cover, etc.). The bathroom is small but well done. Room-to-room noise needs to be addressed but thankfully we had good neighbors. The guest rooms we saw on one side of the hotel had terrible views of construction but what can you expect? The restaurant and bar are excellent. Last but not least the staff was excellent. Front desk and concierge were polite and accommodating. Housekeeping staff encountered in the common areas also excellent and helpful. As for location, it would be difficult to find a better centrally located hotel in the city, and if you can get a good rate, all the better.

“Top Notch” Terrific Ritz and consistent with others around the US. All of the amenities and service you would expect. Location is great. Standard roooms are roomy and well appointed. Meeting facilities are great.

“Second time was better” Our first stay at the St. Greg was fine except for the funny business from the Dir. of Operations. Our second stay was the epitome of customer service because of the effort of Dir. of Operations. He regarded us personally to make sure that our stay was as pleasant and care free as we expected it to be. He did all he reasonably could to insure that he understood our previous complaint and he succeeded in reestablishing a connection with this guest/customer. From check in to check there was great attentive and pleasant service. He has me sold. I'll surely make every effort to stay at the St. Gregory or recommend it whenever possible.

“Nice stay except......” Stayed at the Drury Inn for several nights. The hotel is located right off the interstate 70 and is very easy to get to. If you have business in downtown Denver (about 15 minutes by freeway) or in the Aurora area, it's a pretty convenient location. The Good- The hotel staff is quite friendly and helpful. The maid service was great and consistent during our stay. They offer a free breakfast from 7:00 to 9:30am They offer snacks (chili dogs, nachos, pizza, drinks, etc.) in the evening. Lots of free parking. Friendly neighbors. (See photo) The only area of concern: The main room door has the auto close mechanism on the top which is suppose to close the door automatically. One the 2nd to the last day at the hotel when we got back, we found our room closed but not enough to lock. Evidently if the door is not at least half way open when you let the door close, it will not "click" shut. Can only assume when the maid finished cleaning the room, they let the door close without checking. This was brought to the hotels attention and they assured us that it would be taken care of as soon as possible. Based on our experience with the hotel in other areas I have no doubt this would be taken care of- but if you stay here, check the door to make sure it closes properly.

“Excellent Hotel” I love the Intercontinental Hotel and its chain. They have always treated me with great respect and taken wonderful care of me. I am a Royal Platinum Ambassador so they upgrade me to a suite when i stay with them. The Century City Intercontinental Hotel is fantastic. Great staff and great service. I stayed with them for a few weeks after I did a San Francisco to Los Angeles bike ride in June of last year and love the experience so much I went back. The hotel is convenient to get to Beverly Hills and all the shops in that area. There is also a great mall a short walk from the hotel. I highly recommend this hotel!

“It's WAY more than just the ducks.” There are grand hotels. And there are also great hotels. The Peabody is both. The total package is so beguiling as to be almost seductive. Of course the ducks are the centerpiece, literally, in the marble fountain, in the magnificently carved lobby. The "duckmaster" schtick at 11:00 a.m. and 4:00 p.m. has become not-to-be-missed viral youtube theater. And the ducks are everywhere: on the floor mat in the bathroom, on the stationery, on the marble floors in the elevators... Even the bathroom soap and dinner table butter are molded in the shape of a duck. It's all so broadly kitschy that it's utterly charming. But then there's the rest of it; the countless little touches: a huge new flower display atop the lobby fountain every day, glittering Versailles-style public function rooms, wake-up calls from a live person who asks if you'd like that day's weather, scratch pads, stationery and pens (emblazoned with ducks, of course) replaced each day, laundry returned in wicker baskets, extra staff at the front desk at check-out time in order to deal with exiting conventioneers. And speaking of staff, one certainly gets the impression that the staff really IS delighted to know that you're pleased with the experience. There's something to be said for the old saw about the Mississippi Delta starting in the lobby of The Peabody. It's a constantly busy place, with people from around the world coming and going, flowing out to the elegant horse-drawn carriages on Union Ave., or down the alley to the Rendezvous for ribs, or walking a few blocks to Beall St. and the Civil Rights Museum (i.e. the Lorraine Motel). The place is quintessentially Memphis. But it's also quintessentially the South: elegant, but also casual, proper and sophisticated, but earthy and whimsical at the same time. I've stayed at the Peabody three times, and each time seems better. Some places just do it all right.

“A peaceful stay.” After a horrible stay at the Holiday Inn in NYC, we were delighted when we arrived at Savoy Suites to see smiling faces at the front desk and a clean, comfortable room. The hotel has a free shuttle that will drop you off at the Metro which goes to downtown DC. The hotel is down the street from Whole Foods, Starbucks, a bagel shop and more. It is close to the National Cathedral. We thoroughly enjoyed our stay and would stay there again!

“Great hotel in great location” My wife and I stayed at the Courtyard for a week in February and it was perfect for what it is: a conveniently located hotel that provides a nice, clean and safe place to sleep in between the hustle and bustle of NYC. The concierge and all the staff were helpful. The location was great with a subway stop literally on the corner and the room was clean and large. Not a lot of amenities but if you're visiting NYC, you need to get out of the hotel and explore anyway! Would definitely come back.

“Lovely little hotel on the river” Wonderful stay! Nice room, loved that each room in the suite had its own bathroom. Also, the website said the beds were a queen and a twin/full, and really they were a king and a queen. The water dispenser was a little slow, and the elevator needing the key to get between floors was annoying, but the hotel was safe, so I guess that's a necessary trade off in convenience. The bed was a little hard for my taste, but I slept well. And I would have liked it if the room had more than one window - the layout was long and narrow. Still, it was a great stay, lovely spot on the river. Easy walk to the Hyatt where our conference was, and the Corner Bakery and Cafe was excellent for breakfast each day. Very good service, always with a smile and a "how are you today". I ate in the restaurant one night and while it wasn't anything special, it was perfectly fine and good.

“Yummy” Stayed for two nights on a business trip - on the meeting convener's dime. Truly lovely hotel, spacious room, extensive workout area that included private women and men's whirlpool and steam rooms. Staff members were helpful and good natured - the turn down service warmed the room each evening in ways I'd not experienced before. This was the most resort-like hotel I've had the pleasure to stay in. Two things to note: there is no commerical district nearby, so dining option are very limited. If you're willing to walk a mile or two, you can get to areas with more choice. While menus from the hotel's restaurants / room service offered a broad array of choices, the prices were very high - I paid $46 for a house salad and appetizer. Would gladly stay again if seeking a respite from the mad rush of D.C.

“Pleasantly Surprised” Staying in a hotel connected to a major airport, I had very low expectations. But I was very pleasantly surprised by the quality of the Hilton and have no reservations recommending it to anyone. The hotel is attached to the airport. The quickest way to access the hotel is by walking outside. However, the airport signs direct you through an interior route that makes you think you've walked a mile to get there. NOT the hotel's fault -- try asking someone for the shortest route. Check-in was quick. I asked for a "quiet" room and was given one where I never heard an airplane, despite being next to the airport. The room was of adequate size, with a large desk and comfortable recliner. There is a large TV (not flat screen) and a well-stocked mini-bar. Bed was very comfortable and wake-up call was timely. The bathroom was modern. The only negative was the shower curtain looked dated. Not a huge bathroom, but adequate and well appointed. Room service was prompt and the food was decent (if not exceptional). Many choices on the menu and the server was very pleasant. Empty tray was cleared very quickly. This hotel is obviously geared toward travelers who need to overnight in Chicago. However, having stayed at a number of "airport hotels," this one was much better than most. And, you can't beat the location -- a 3 minute walk to the United terminal. If you find yourself needing to overnight in Chicago and want a nice hotel with great convenience, the Hilton is it. Not having to wait for a shuttle and having a modern, comfortable room are major extras.

“Ridiculously outstanding!” Was stuck in Chicago for a few days due to a huge storm in Denver - booked my room through Starwood Preferred Guest and from the moment I entered the lobby, I knew I was in for an experience. Exceptional customer service by all staff. The small touches are what I noticed at the W ... a real person instead of a recording for the wake up call ... staff noting their names and indicating that I could call them personally for any needs ... an attentive concierge with great suggestions ... turndown service on request .... Just wonderful. Hip, trendy lobby scene - rooftop bar is a little crowded and small, but the views from 33rd floor were likely stunning. Since I was traveling alone, I far preferred the "Living Room" lobby bar. Less clubby. Better people watching. My 23rd floor lakeview room featured a luxurious shower - a deluge from above! A perfect weekend that could have been spent at a regular, boring, chain turned into an adventure to remember. Absolutely, stay at the W Lakeshore.

“Excellent value!” We - family of 3- stayed here a week and were very impressed. Complimentary breakfast and dinner. Free WIFI. Very close to Seattle Centre- no more than a 10mins walk; and, a 20mins walk to Pier 66 & 70. This is not a downtown hotel but makes up for far away location with great services. Staff is courteous and helpful and will book packages for you at hotel discount. The suites are incredibly spacious and very clean. Our room was quiet but faced 2nd Ave. and not Western Ave. which is a major road. We booked online and got a very good rate. Zipcars are just around the corner also. Parking is availabe if you drive. Grocery store is a 5mins walk away. Laundry room onsite.

“Excellent location, value, experience in unique neighborhood” If you are looking to experience New York City without the bustle and chaos of Times Square (and the more expensive hotels), you should consider the Sohotel. The location is great! It is a one-minute walk to all the great restaurants in Little Italy (and Lombardi's Pizza!), and just around the corner from Canal Street. You feel like you are in a neighborhood rather than a crowded major city. The decor of the hotel is trendy, warm, and inviting (think exposed brick and zebra-striped couches in the lobby). While the rooms and bathrooms are not very big, the beds are extremely comfortable and there are nice TVs on the walls. Internet is available in some rooms and in the lobby, where you can also watch TV on a on a huge screen while you check your email. Even though there are no elevators, the staff is extremely helpful and carries your bags up to your room. I have stayed at many hotels in Times Square before, and staying at the Sohotel was one of the most relaxing experiences I have had in the city.

“Great Place to Stay” Excellent location in Union Square, conveniently within walking distance to many places of interest. Cable car to and from Fisherman's Wharf is right outside of the hotel. Nice respectful staff, clean hotel. NO free internet.

“Clean and upscale at a reasonable price” This is the first time I've stayed there since Wyndham took over. It has the modern feel of a Westin at a lower price. The rooms are in great condition. The fitness center is large with a variety of cardio machines and a smaller number of strength machines. Fruit and towels, but only a slow water fountain to drink from. Registration is on the second floor, but the main entrance is on the first. It becomes quite deserted at night down there and did not feel as safe in that part of San Francisco as I would like, especially considering Wyndham's reputation for caring about such things. All in all, I'd definitely stay here again.

“Great Service On Such Short Notice” I was not suppose to have stayed in Houston on the night of February 19th. I was suppose to have been onboard the Carnival Ecstasy departing from Galveston, however, due to fog the Port of Galveston was closed. The ship was stuck out in the Gulf and we were stuck without a place to go. Carnival handed out a paper with 3 Hotel names on it, The Hilton was the 2nd one on the list and since all hotels in Galveston were booked we had no choice but to go to Houston.
