I am so glad I chose the Hilton. I don’t think anyone else could have been as nice as they were! Carnival had put the private cell phone number of the GM on the paper they gave us but she took it very well and just directed us to call the property directly where I was able to get a King size room. The room was very nice and was clean and my granddaughter loved playing in the big tub! I love Hilton properties anyway and will always stay at a Hilton property over any other brand but this was just a bonus for me. The Hotel is very lovely. There is a huge aquarium in the lobby that kept my 4 year old grandchild occupied while I was checking in along with about 50 others from my bus that had brought us to Houston. Our room overlooked the front parking lot and we could see the planes take off the next morning. There was a very nice restaurant onsite that was very gracious about allowing us to go ahead and be seated and order even though they were closing in 5 minutes. I felt so bad to do it but since we were without a car and it was late at night and I had a child to feed, I had to. But I do want to thank the hostess, waitress and cook for allowing this. The next morning the front desk clerk ( a young man) was so nice and sweet. He put up with all us panicky cruise passengers and was awesome about it. I think I owe him a great big thank you as well! There is a very nice business center on site that we could use (allot) to check the various websites to see when our Ship was coming in. I loved it there and if I ever have a cause to stay with the Hilton Hobby Airport location again I will! Thanks again to the poor manager who put up with about 500 cruise passengers calling her cell phone and for giving us a very good rate for such a wonderful property!

“Very nice!” I stayed at the DoubleTree for 5 nights and I think it is a pretty good hotel. The staff is friendly and want to help, but have their mistakes from time to time. The rooms are spacious and clean but have some details that betray the fact is a renovated hotel (old TV, noisy AC, no safe in the rooms) but everything else (carpets, bathrooms, desk, beds) is new and very clean. The bed is super comfortable. The hotel’s location is very good for shopping and eating, if you are more into museums it is better to find something in the Loop. Other reviews said the elevators were very slow, I didn’t have any problems there. What I didn’t like is that they charge the use of computers in the business center.

“Enjoyed my stay at The Prescott” The Price: I went on priceline to look for a hotel deal in San Francisco. I paid only $500 for 5 nights (normally goes for $200-300 per night). It was worth every penny. The Room: The Prescott has a very upscale feel. The rooms are clean, quiet, and beautiful. The bed linens are soft and mattress is very comfortable. The room itself is small, but they make good use of the space. My only complaint about the room is that the water pressure in the shower isn't great. The Staff: The hotel staff was very helpful. They had great tips... where to dine, what to see, how to get around, etc. Also, there is a private club on the 4th floor of the hotel that offers a complimentary breakfast and happy hour (full bar & appetizers). We didn't pay for the club membership, but the front desk slipped us a key pass anyhow. Location: If you want to be in Union Sq, this hotel is perfect. There is lots of shopping, restaurants, and other things to do. The Prescott is one block from the heart of Union Square. There are some homeless in the area, and a suspicious massage parlor around the corner, but overall, the neighborhood feels safe. It's close the to BART and the Powell St Trolley. It's a $7 cab ride to Fisherman's Wharf, The Ferry Building, and AT&T Park. $35 cab ride (plus tip) to the airport.

“Heaven in San Francisco” We have been staying at the SF St Regis since it opened. We have stayed at several other hotels in SF and always return to the St Regis. The staff is cordial and professional without being stuffy. Rooms are roomy and well lit, with good work areas. The location is excellent and within easy walking to shopping, dining, and the financial district. The rooms are starting to see a bit of wear, but not nealy as much as most other business hotels. I highly recommend this hotel.

“Clean, comfortable” Recently stayed at this property for 1 evening. All in all a good stay. Area is safe and ok, just off the Metro line as well as the 101 in the Silver Lake area. Have to say, not really all that close to Universal, but as both are off the 101, guess the title fits...Room was refurbished and huge. Although it fronted Vermont, was not affected by street noise. Good shower iwth plenty of hot water and water pressure. In room safe is nice as wella s the flat screen tv with cale channek options. Checkin and check out easy enough as prepaid. Did have to pay a parking fee however, these added charges bug me. Should be included in the room rate. Left before breakfast was open, so cannot comment. All in all, a good clean, basic stay worth the rate.

“Excellent value” I really enjoyed The Monticello and would have no hesitation of staying there again. I had one of the Jefferson suites and found it to be very comfortable and homey. Ask for a view of the interior courtyard as there was absoultely no noise. Best things about this hotel: the service, the beds and the location. Worst things about this hotel: could not find anything. Enjoy this great value hotel.

“Cute, cute, cute...........” We were in-town for a friend's wedding and stayed at The Franklin for 3 nights in 2/09 before heading down to stay 3 more nights on the lower east side. The hotel is located in a great spot on the upper east side very near the 86th/Lex subway stop. The hotel is walking distance to the park, the met, and places to eat/drink on 2nd ave..... It feels quieter and more residential up there than other more "touristy" areas of NYC which is so welcomed in such a crazy city. We flew in on the red-eye and got to the hotel around 9am. HUGE points for letting us check-in so early. The staff were sweet and friendly throughout our stay. The place has a bed and breakfast/home-like feel to it. We saw very few guests during our stay and felt like we lived here by the time we left. Very private and relaxing. The rooms are tiny, but very charming with soft colors, nice lighting, and great beds. Our room had a small desk, large TV, queen sized bed, and decent closet space. Expensive mini-bar (but aren't they always?)....do wish they had offered free water though. Wireless internet service was great as was daily newspaper delivery. We were on the 7th floor and maid service came late (around 2pm), but we are not "morning" people so this didn't bother us a bit. The bathroom is really small and the water pressure on the rain shower a little weak, but other than that, they did a great job with the space. The breakfast area is small, but cozy. Don't expect a full on American breakfast, but the rolls, cereal, coffees, and tea are a great addition to the place. I loved the textured wall paper...might have to add some to my dining area back home. We also enjoyed the free evening wine and cheese further adding to the romantic, charming feel of the hotel. The coffee machine runs 24/7 so you can always pop in and get yourself a latte and tea.....which is so nice on the chilly winter Manhattan nights. Really a great boutique hotel worth checking out.

“Impeccable service: Three cheers for the staff here” I've stayed here many times -- it's a great property no question about it -- even if you don't have a room with a view. This time I have to say that everyone I spoke with/met -- from bellmen to housekeeping to front desk and beyond...truly one of the nicest, most accomodating teams I've encountered in a long time. It makes the stay even more enjoyable. Thanks!

“Nice hotel, perfect location. Nice and quiet!!!” This hotel is five blocks fron the Pike Place Market on Pike St. In the middle of everything. Macy's is one block away. Can't get a better location. I am a light sleeper and truly appreciate a quiet hotel. This place is really quiet and well built. (stayed on St. Pat's day) Get a high floor for a great view. Has underground parking ($32 overnight) and a Elephant & Castle Restaurant. Decent pub fare without leaving the building. I will be back here.

“Recent business meeting stay” Based on my recent stay during a business meeting, I highly recommend this hotel. From the moment of arriving to my departure, overall the hotel stay was excellent. The receptionist was very helpful and was able to allow me to check in early without any difficulties. I also requested a later check out than normal and i was pleasantly surprised how easy it was to accomplish this. The room and facilities were extremely clean and comfortable. The bed was amazingly comfortable with the pillow top mattress. The only food i experienced was the service provided during out meeting which included a lunch and breakfast buffet which were both very good. I highly recommend this hotel.

“A little different...” We had a nice room with a balcony overlooking the open area near the pool. We were there on a weekend and it was a little loud at night but we had no difficulty sleeping. The room was clean and had a nice set up. The bed was quite comfortable. Other than the person taking up our luggage, who was quite nice and helpful, the rest of the service was average. Great location for the hotel. I would not recommend it as an ideal place for familes with kids but not terrible for them either. If we go back to San Diego we would certainly consider staying here again but it would probably not be at the top of my list.

“Great location and awesome staff!!!” I really liked the location of this hotel. There were so many great restaurants near by! Everything was convenient. The staff was very friendly and helpful. My TV was broken and that was a hassle, every time I turned it on, I had to call the desk for service. On day 2, the maintenance staff replaced the TV and everything was fine. The engineer who helped me was great! I also had something gross on my shower curtain and they quickly brought a new one. Otherwise the room was kept very clean. The downfalls would be street noise, lots of sirens waking me up all night and the thermostat was hard to control. Otherwise everything was good, even with all the construction going on.

“Travelodge - Close to everything.” Enjoyed my stay here in San Siego. Checkin time is 4pm, arrived at 130 and was able to check in early with no hassle, greatly appreciated. Location right off the 8 freeway, 5 min from Hillcrest, 5 min to Downtown, 6 min to San Diego Zoo and 11 min from Airport. 2 restaurants next door, old style feel with awesome food. Adams serves a great breakfast and Albie's serves up Old Style Ambiance with Hearty food. Full bar at both. My room was clean and roomy, didn't feel crowded. I asked for extra towels and housekeeping was more then helpful. I will stay here again, loved it!

“Great small hotel” The Villa Florence is a small boutique type hotel that is right on the streetcar line and a half of block from union Square. The hotel is clean, newly refurbished and has a nice dinning area. Very European feel and excellent service. Some of the queen rooms are quite small and some are just right so be sure to ask for the largest size or get a king room. a little more money but worth it. I'm confident you will love this intiimate hotel and it's dining room ---as well as its location --many neat stores and dining places nearby.

“Great location and friendly” Chose to stay here when visiting New York after good experience at Palomar in Los Angeles. Very friendly hotel with nice welcome and very helpful front of house staff. Super location for my business visits and also just a couple of blocks from the bus to JFK and to Grand Central Station. Free wine hour in the evening, and fresh fruit always available, plus plenty of morning papers. Nice if compact room, beautifully clean and well air conditioned and soundproofed, and good sized TV and fast Wifi as in other Kimptons. Also great minibar and snack offering. I had a great view across Park Avenue. If you arrive on a Sunday beware that the restaurant can be closed on a Sunday evening, although there are plenty of nearby places to eat. I had room service as I had arrived after a long flight and was not that impressed with a turkey breast sandwich, although the ingredients all seemed fresh. Later in the week I had an excellent dinner at the bar at the Silverleaf Tavern - the hotel's restaurant and bar - including wild mushroom risotto which was yummy - and had friendly company there too. Breakfast was OK - a bit expensive and not a very exciting range of things to chose from in the buffet - It was interesting to observe that it is clearly a destination for working breakfast meetings for nearby business people. However the staff were attentive and plenty of nice fresh coffee available, regularly refilled.

“"The Shining"” Great location and Service, the hallways were very long and reminded me of the movie. The parking was a little steep at 50 us dollars! The Bed was comfortable, but the carpets were a little worn. The property is over 100 years old. The room was larger than most. I would stay here again

“Exquisite Stay” I just returned from an absolutely wonderful stay at the Gansevoort - Meatpacking District property. The service, ambiance, and location were just superb. And, my room (Deluxe Room) was just wonderful, with a very comfortable bed, and great bathroom. I enjoyed a quiet night's rest in this very active neigborhood. While I was in NYC this time for business, I will return here for both business and pleasure. I highly recommend you enjoy a stay at his fantastic property, in a fun neighborhood.

“Great visit” Been travelling a ton for business and we were booked in the Cliffs for a two night stay. I was put in an end suite that was tremendous, beautiful living room, bar, 2 bathrooms and a beautiful bedroom w/ small porch overlooking the valley. Had room service the first night and food was great. pools were beautiful and clean, check in was flawless and service wa terrific w/ them driving me to my room in a van. wish the wife and kids were w/ me.

“Nice and Affordable Surprise” I stayed at this hotel in June for $160/night, which was significantly cheaper than other Manhattan hotels. The hotel is new, clean, and very comfortable. Before you book this hotel, you need to understand that you are reserving a "POD" hotel room. The room is essentially 150 square feet, which includes the bathroom. The bed doubles as a couch, and is similar to an electronic Futon (Bed wasn't comfortable by the way). The bathroom and bedroom are separated by a semi-transparent curtain. The hotel rooms would be too small for families or more than 2 people. Furthermore, if you are staying in the room with a friend or someone you are not close with, expect to lose bathroom privacy. If you are a couple or single person, this room is more than adequate as a hotel room. There are a few positives to this hotel that I'd like to point out. -The hotel is right next to the Lincoln Tunnel, which makes it convenient for anyone driving into the City from Jersey. However, it is a good 10 minute walk to the heart of Times Square and the subway. -I loved the rooftop lounge, which had beautiful views! Make sure you go there. -Free internet in all the rooms

“Even our Labrador fell in love.” Pet friendly. Family friendly. Yet still sophisticated. Lived our stay. Staff was wonderful from the front door to the front desk. Room very clean and contemporary. Lobby super chic with wine tasting. Dog park on the 3rd floor. This is a GREAT hotel. Will be back next time we're in SF. Will recommend to others too. Thank you Galleria Park hotel!

“Nice Hotel” The Westin Market Street is a very nice 'upmarket' hotel in an excellent location in San Francisco - a quick walk to Union Square and public transport on Mraket Street to just about anywhere We ( family of 2 adults + 2 kids, 5 and 13) had a large, bright and very clean room - on the 7th floor I think - and the beds were wonderfully comfortable. Bathroom was a little dark, but spotless and we had a bath , which was nice for the little one. Check-in was smooth and the girl at the desk who dealt with us was extremely pleasant, as were all of the staff we met there, including in the restaurant. This was a pleasant surprise given some of the remarks made on this site. We didn't have breakfast at the hotel - Starbucks is just up the street if all you want is a coffee and pastry- but we did have a very good , if rather expensive, meal at "Ducca". My only complaint would be that our room was right next to the service elevators that rumbled noisily up and down late at night and early in the morning. I presume that our room allocation was due to the fact that we had got an absolutely fantastic rate on Expedia, which I imagine gives the hotel some scope to allocate better -placed rooms to those paying the full whack. All in all our stay was very pleasant, and if we're ever back in SF ( it's a long way from France!) and get a similar deal, then I'd stay there again.

“Would stay again...” The hotel is in a great location and was a wondeful respite after a long day. Very close to excellent restaurants and of course the Polaris Mall. The gentleman who checked us in had the right balance of friendliness, helpfulness, and professionalism. We loved our room. Very clean, spacious and comfortable beds. If I had to make one suggestion, it would to be to put a curtain between the sink area and the bedroom. We saw this feature in Europe and in Disney and it really helped to block out the light if another person(s) remained sleeping while another was getting ready. Will stay here again when we go back.

“Relaxing getaway” Just returned from a week's stay in a 2 bedrm villa and had a lovely time. We were accommodated on the 2nd floor in building 2600 overlooking a quiet courtyard and just 1 building away from the main pool area. This is out 2nd time at the CV's after trading in through II. The unit was spacious, very clean and comfortable. We had the usual 'mid-week tidy', which was sufficient since there were plenty of towels and trash and re-cycle bins conveniently located right by the elevators. Every morning we took a nice walk over to the JW Marriott, a pleasant, circular route of about 1/2 hr round trip. As CV guests, we took advantage of using the JW's facilities, including the pool which was much less crowded (and more quiet!) than the one at the Villas. We ate at 'Sage' Restaurant as well as 'Roys'. There is a cozy small patio seating area at Roys by the firepit, nice for drinks and appetizers if a full dinner is not wanted. Both of the golf courses are in great shape and challenging. The staff both at the JW and CV are very pleasant and nice, always ready to help and answer any questions. The spa facilities are wonderful, with a relaxing pool and light fare bistro. We drove to Kierland Commons (about 15min southeast off Scottsdale Rd) a couple of times and had dinner at the Greenhouse Rest as well as Tommy Bahamas. Both were excellent. In Old Town Scottsdale, we had dinner at the Mission Restaurant www.themissionaz.com at 3815 N Brown Av, which serves small plates (tapas) in an old converted Iron works building. Wonderful food and service. The Villas are located a bit north of the downtown part of Scottsdale, but with easy on and off freeway access, everything in that area is within 15-30min. The Marketplace down the road has an Albertson's, gas station, stores and restaurants, the Marriott shuttle runs between the hotel, villas and marketplace approx every 1/2 hr. Highly recommend this property.

“Fabulous Location and Views” We chose this hotel because of its location and it did not disappoint. There were many great restaurantss and shops nearby. The service was excellent. Despite the fact that it seemed busy, we never had to wait for an elevator. Our room was indeed quite small but doable for a weekend. The view from our room, however, was very nice. We would return.

“Good location” A solid hotel with a good bar serving the best cappuccino I've had in ages. Friendly welcome. The room was clean, the bathroom spacious. The beds were comfortable - we both slept well. The downstairs restaurant was ok but nothing special. Location wise it is near the lake and at the top of the Magnificent Mile. A 15/20 minute walk to the river.

“Better Every Year” I've had the opportunity to visit the Grand Del Mar each August for the last three years as part of a small conference that includes serious half day meetings and fun interactive afternoon events. Every year that I return, the hotel gets better. The customer service is unequaled. One morning I needed copies of an outline I had prepared for a presentation. I went to the concierge to ask where I could find the business center. Instead, the concierge volunteered to print out my documents on the spot. She did so quickly, with a smile, and free of charge. One more example, upon checking out of the hotel early one morning, the person at the check out desk encouraged me to review my bill. I noticed that there was a charge for one of the hotel restaurants on my bill and I had not visited it during my stay. I mentioned the $60 charge and without hesitation the check out assistant waived the charge. No "I will need to speak with a manager" or even a follow up question or two. It was prompt and decisive. Impressive. Similarly the help by the valets and attendants at the golf course were stellar. When I noticed that my golf bag did not include my wedge (grandchild strikes again), the attendant went and got me a brand new quality wedge at no charge. Speaking of the golf course, it is one of the best that I have played. It's fair and fascinating, with each hole offering a unique challenge. Greens are fast, the conditions are outstanding, and the caddies are energetic and knowledgeable. It's pricey, but worth the experience. Lastly, I have to add that the hotel itself is gorgeous. The grounds are immaculate. Forget the fussy comments elsewhere, this is a first class hotel with great, plush rooms, expansive bathrooms, very comfortable king beds, and nice furniture. The common areas are attractive, nicely decorated, and rarely too crowded. Next year, despite the business meetings, I'll want to ensure that my wife joins me. This is too nice a place to experience alone.

“Eastgate - Thumbs Up!” My wife and I recently spent 5 nights at the Eastgate Tower Hotel (March 1-6) and thoroughly enjoyed our stay. We booked a Junior Suite and it felt like we had our own 1-bedroom apartment (kitchenette, spacious sofa area and dining table) - and, above all, at an affordable rate. Important to add that the room was impeccably clean. We were checked in within minutes and given a key to a safety deposit box (upon request). Hotel staff was courteous and efficient. The walk to the the Times Square area is about 15 minutes. We liked being several blocks east of 5th ave. - a noticeable difference in the level of traffic noise at night. Upon our return, we received an e-mail from the hotel inquiring about our stay. A first class operation all the way for budget-minded travellers.

“A good place for a long stay” I recently spent 4 nights here -my first at an Embassy Suites. The staff was terrific. Every single employee I encountered was friendly and helpful. The rooms were very clean and comfortable. It was great having the extra room to spread out and relax, especially for a longer stay. I liked the atrium and the fish ponds. The waterfall could get a little loud, but didn't bother my sleep. The morning breakfast was very plentiful and varied. It was kept well stocked with fresh fruit, yogurt, coffee, and breads - plus the cooked to order omelets and sides of potatoes and breakfast meats. A great way to start the day. The manager's reception was a nice surprise - complementary cocktails and trays of fresh veggies, hummus and the best pita chips I have had. I only got to use the pool once, but it is bigger then the photos and the landscaping is pleasant. There is also a good Jacuzzi. As others have noted, the plumbing is a little weird – my shower ran hot then cold. The toilet would randomly start running – usually in the middle of the night. I did call and someone came up to work on it right away, and it got better, but was not completely resolved. I would certainly stay here again!

“Very clean. Nice stay.” If you need to be in this part of Houston, this is a good choice. It's clean and quiet (make sure you request a room not facing the highway). It didnt look all that full, so try and get a good rate.

“wow. better that i thought it would be.” i was not expecting the service to be so good. I have stayed at Marriotts for years but never have i had such a Ritz experience at a Marriott. Great hotel and great stay. Thriving nighlife scene in the bar and rooms were comfortable.

“Best sleep ever” We stayed at the Ballantyne Resort for two nights recently and we had a great time. From the moment we pulled up everything was great. The valet was awesome. Check-in was a breeze. I assume since I am a Starwood preferred member we were upgraded to a room with a balcony that was very nice. The room was spacious and perfectly appointed. The bed was so comfortable I literally slept for 9 hours (which is unheard of for me). We ordered room service several times and every time it was prepared perfectly. We also used the indoor pool and hot tub and found them both to be well maintained. A couple of minor complaints: This is an expensive resort, I felt a little "nickel and dimed" by being charged for internet. However, I have this complaint often...why is internet at the Four Points Sheraton or Hampton Inn complimentary but at a Sheraton or Hilton it is not...annoying! The balcony could have been a little cleaner of dead bugs. I understand that this is the south but a few too many dead bugs for my liking. At night for turn-down service they swapped our robes out and my friend left her cell phone in the pocket of the robe. It took a couple calls to the front desk that night when we noticed and also in the morning, but we were pleasantly surprised when we heard a knock at the door at 9 am to deliver the cell phone...very happy! Overall, a beautiful and relaxing stay. Not close to downtown Charlotte, there was plenty of shopping and restaurants in the area. I would recommend people to stay here.

“High quality Westin Stay” I stayed for 5 nights towards the end of May for a work conference. Positives: -My executive club roomon floor 18 felt very spacious with a nice river view -Big bathroom and super comfortable bed -Nice amenities - free bottle of water, iPad in the room, free breakfast and wine hour, free printing at club level -The conference staff (AV, catering, room set up, etc.) were all excellent. Especially Linda and Jonathan. -Room service was very quick -Location was very close to metro station, restaurants, etc. It's also a very easy walk to many tourist attractions. Negatives: -Had to wait quite a while at both check-in and check-out. They should probably add a second employee there more often -The lobby was beautiful, but not very "cozy" for chatting with others. We didn't use this as a meeting place like we have in other hotels because it didn't feel very comfortable.

“Excellent service” Arriving at noon, the front desk staff checked us in without any problems and even gave us a water view room. The included continental breakfast at the hotel restaurant Ruth Chris Steakhouse was delicious. When the front desk staff found out ,upon check out, that we were unable to check in at their online kiosk, they quickly forwarded us to the concierge who took care of this with a smile! The room was in excellent condition, spacious bathroom with a large shower. The hotel is located next to the Pacific Mall with Pike Market only a few blocks away. This is my number 1 hotel in Seattle!

“Slice of HEAVEN” Wow, aaaaaahhhhh, WOW. What a marvelous surprise. Where do I begin? Elegant, yet rustic and sophisticated. INCREDIBLE views. I am talking breathtaking views. There is a calm and serenity that permeates this oasis in TEXAS! All the trees breathe calm and peace all around you on this magical property. Do you get what I mean? Lovely trails/walkways between the casitas where the rooms are located with stupendous views of the Hill Country and Lake Travis in the distance. Lush linens, large size well-appointed baths and super wi-fi throughout the property- almost where ever you want to stop and enjoy the views and nature. The staff was also lovely throughout the property and committed to making your stay not only pleasant but an adventure. Some of the must do activities are the Equine Experience- DO IT- even if you are a city slicker like us- and run by Zen-like Rodeo masters (we had Jodie and Betsy)- AMAZING. Couples connection and Life-coaching also fun and run by a wise beyond his young years genuine shaman who is entertaining at the same time (Josh). What might not be obvious from all of this is that the property is large- yet only has about 60 or so rooms- so you are not over crowded- this adds to the luxury. The yoga classes and meditation and breath-work classes were run by an absolute sage/guru named Jennifer- thank you for your wonderful skill and insight. The spa is large as you would expect excellent and has diverse types of treatments in a beautiful setting. My favorite place is a zen-like almost mystical building and garden (Solidago –[Latin meaning to strengthen and make whole] Gardens) that is part Texan Hill Country and medieval gothic yet full of light. Some of the meditation classes were held here, peaceful, centering. Finally, the food- in a word- superb! Interesting menus, quality fresh ingredients, delicious and filling. We will be back soon, already planning a family/friends celebration and perhaps even a conference.

“Affordable Luxury, Comfort and Charm in the heart of Philly” On Christmas morning (before our trip) we opened presents to see what we got. The very next day, we arrived at Hyatt near City Hall in Philly for our next surprise - - did we get our requested half-price upgrade to a corner suite? I think you can guess the answer. It made all the difference. Hyatt got a little extra $ but we got a space larger than my son's apartment. Service? What can I say? The staff seems to compete with each other to see who can fulfill your requests faster. Rollaway, extra towels, room service, maintenance ... all arrived before we expected. Notable - - biggest bath towels we've ever seen (wrap yourself in comfort). Is it perfect? Of course not, the place is over 100 years old. But the staff is genuinely welcoming and the views from the restaurants on the top floor are so great you'll quickly forget any blemishes (which are few and far between anyway.)

“Lovely!” I travel to Washington, DC on business about twice a year. I've stayed in quite a few hotels in DC (Sofitel, Mayflower, Hilton, Hotel Rouge, Melrose Hotel, and Washington Terrace), but none was as lovely and as comfortable and as reasonably priced as the River Inn in November 2004. The River Inn is a converted 1960's apartment building that is snack dab in the middle of a charming and safe historic Foggy Bottom rowhouse street. The River Inn is decorated in lovely browns and beiges and muted pumpkins and golds. The corporate suite is spacious and even has a pull out sleeper sofa . The corporate suite has a very nice kitchen with two burner stove, full size refrigerator, sink, place settings, cabinets and microwave. The kitchen even has marble floors (to demonstrate that this is a nicely decorated room). The suite's kitchen is conveniently set out of the way, though, ...in case you never need or want to look at a kitchen during your stay. There is a grocery at the Watergate Hotel which is only a short 2 blocks, if that, from the hotel. The hotel generously offers Aveda shampoos and moisterizers in the bathroom. The River Inn is just a few blocks from the Kennedy Center and a short walk from the Georgetown Harbour. Really, the White House is within walking distance to the River Inn if you don't mind a 20-30 minute walk. The only fault I could find with the suite is that the faucets in the bathroom are a bit old and plain...but only when compared with how nicely decorated the room is. (You can tell that I'm really reaching for something negative here.) There is a very nice and trendy, though a bit expensive, restaurant in the hotel lobby. I highly recommend this hotel and would return again to stay here!

“A bit away from the city” Booked this hotel on hotwire trying to get the Omni. Same Hotwire price, and same star-level... ended up with the Airport Hilton so was curious to see how it was. First of all, if you're planning on spending time in the "city," I would think the commute would be somewhat painful. But the hotel is VERY convenient to the airport. Driving aside, I would say that the hotel is nice, has a great lobby and center rotunda bar. There is a musty smell in the rooms... maybe it is a carry-over from my Air Force days, it gave me the chills, sorta like the building once housed labs where they ran illicit experiments or something. But that could just be my agent orange acting up again. Other deals that stand out about my experience: parking was $11/day, internet was $10/day, local calls are charged by the minute. Another nickel and dime experience from a "luxury-style" hotel. How is it that lower quality hotels offer these things free of charge? (that was rhetorical). Basically, I enjoyed the stay, didn't have bad dreams, and if I don't need to travel to the city to work, would stay here again.

“Spacious for the price” I've stayed at several properties near the Metro Center and this is at the top of the list. As a Hitlon Honors member I was looking for a property in the area and they had an attractive <$100 rate. There were some critical reveiws though it appears that this property is under new management. I experienced friendly service from the front desk staff and housekeeping. The property while by no means is perfect, is well maintained. The room as an extended stay is very spacious. Full king bed and bath in the bedroom suite, and a large comfortable sitting area with a small kitchen with full fridge. Entire room was clean and orderly. Lighting was adequate although not always where you need it. Free internet that worked great. Bed was comfortable with fresh linens. Bath was a tub/shower with good pressure and plenty of hot water. Towels were larger and softer than those you'll find at a Hampton Inn. Each room has a TV, ceiling fan in the bedroom. There were a couple of points deducted. Sleep can be interuptted as my room faced the I-17 and I was awakend by vehicle noise a couple of times during my stay. It usually quieted down around midnight. I found it easier to sleep when the HVAC was on, but it was louder than I like but helped. Slight issue with the drain in the shower running slow but nothing but minor things. Property also features a nightly small buffet which I didn't enjoy but seemed well attended. Breakfast is available a no charge also. Really enjoyed my stay and it was a great value comparted to some of the other properties nearby..

“Huge Rooms by NYC Standards” I stayed at this Courtyard for two nights on business travel and was amazed by the size of the rooms. Not only are the rooms large by New York City standards, but also by Courtyard standards in general. The corner room I was assigned was larger than the rooms I've stayed in at comparable Courtyards across the country. Aside from that, you can't go wrong with this hotel. Standard Courtyard all the way. Quiet room, good bed, hot water, and adequate internet. I didn't stop by the pool or eat breakfast in the restaurant, but why bother when the city beckons?! This hotel has a pretty good location in Midtown. Close to the train, and a short 15 minute cross-town hike to Times Square. I wouldn't expect a quintessential New York experience if you're on leisure travel, but if you're heading to the city on business, book away!

“Great Stay ” Just got back from New York - stayed at the Affinia Dumont in a king suite. There were three of us - my sister, myself and my adult son. We arrived for check-in early, around 1:00 p.m. and our room was ready. The guy checking us in told us "You are going to love your room." He was right! We were in room 3305, a corner unit. We had views of the Chrysler Building and the East River, it was totally awesome. We were treated like royalty the entire time. The staff is so nice and helpful. We booked through Expedia, and never requested anything special - I was hoping for a room on a high floor - but never asked for it - Normally when I book through a discount booking service, the rooms are not always the best - but you compromise because you get a good price. We were really surprised that we got such a great room at a discounted price. The bed was great, we took advantage of the "pillow" menu and ordered some down feather pillows, which were delivered immediately. My son used the sofa bed and he slept really good on it. The kitchen was great, the bathroom was big too - the bathtub was enormous, great for soaking in the tub. I cannot think of one negative - it was all positive. We loved the Murray Hill section, used the subways and buses mostly to get around - sometimes got a cab - but tried to rely on public transportation. The doorman was great, always helped us and always welcomed us back after a long day of sightseeing. If you go to New York - treat yourself to the Affinia Dumont, it really is a great place.

“Great place to spend time-lovely amenities” We stayed here for 3 nights while visiting colleges nearby. It was a great location for stanford and ucla berkely. We spent the afternoons here relaxing. The pool is beautiful with a hot tub. Lots of palm trees and lovely vegetation. The breakfast was fantastic. There was a business area with a compter with free internet. It was upstairs above the lobby. Kind of hard to find. No one was hardly using it. They had cookies and bottled water all afternoon in the lobby. The room was modern and comfortable. We had a fridge and microwave and two sinks. Great for getting ready in the morning. There were great restauraunts right across the street and a starbucks. The bus stopped right across the street to go downtown. Even though we were near an airport, it was quiet. The shuttle bus was quick and on time.

“High Class Hotel but a little bit to formal” This is the former Ritz Carlton Hotel. It is a high class premium hotel and the service is from A to Z absolutely perfect. The TAJ Chain wants to promote the fact of this kind of premium, palast like service and I am sure they have customers that go for that. personally, I think it is a little bit to formal, but again, expectations are different. if you are looking for a high class location in Boston, then you definitively are going to be happy if you select this hotel. If you want to go for business or if you want just to have a great location for visiting Boston, then I think another location would be more appropriate. The Restaurant is fantastic, the Bar.... ok... there are more fun places to have a beer then in that Bar. But again, tasts are different.

“Great place, conveniently located” Having visited San Francisco over a dozen times in the last year (my sister lives in the city), I have been keeping watch for any hotels that may be acceptable for my next visit. I had dined at Anzu in Hotel Nikko and noticed the impressive decor and cleanliness but had figured the prices were no match for my usual go-to accomidations at a 3 star Fisherman's Wharf. When I discovered I had Easter weekend to visit my sister, I did some minor price checking. I found that Hotel Nikko was not only competitive with my usual hotel, but cheaper for a deluxe. I especially its close proximity to the BART as the "other" hotel was in the Wharf. The room was a touch small but the bed so wonderfully comfortable with nice sheets and lots of pillows. The giagantic big screen tv was great and I love that the shower had a detachable head...way more important than nifty upgrades. The only complaint is that the frige had no room for any items I may wish to cool and was so hyper sensitive (as I read in the reviews) that I chose to just leave it be. Overall, I was very happy with my stay and will stay again, especially if arriving via the BART.

“A Sure Bet” As usual, the Embassy Suites is a sure bet--I'm always confident that I will get a nice room and a good deal. The room was clean and well-appointed, the beds were comfortable, and the location was convenient to all the places we wanted to go on this particular trip. That said, we were given a room on the second floor above the pool and could hear noise all night long. Would have liked to sleep longer, but the breakfast setup was very noisy. If I go back, I'll certainly request a room on the third floor or above.

“Great value for money” We stayed here because of an early flight out. With 2 kids we took a suite with a king and a twin rooms. The kitchen area did not get used but would be great for those who need it. There is a small lounge that separates the 2 bedrooms. Comfortable and very clean throughout. The breakfast area was very clean and the food was great. We took advantage of the self service laundry on site and this was excellent. Can't speak highly enough of this place, great.

“Good value, good location, almost perfect” Stayed from 8 to 12 July. Selected this property based on price, location, and Hyatt Gold status. Good location for meetings, shopping, and other events. It is a 40 minute drive from DFW Airport off of Interstate 635 E. Good location, if you know the Dallas area well. Might be tricky if Dallas is brand new to you. A few fast food restaurants in the immediate area. The Galleria Mall and Valley View Mall are a minutes away. With a few exceptions, recent renovations of lobby and my room on 6th floor were obvious. Room layout was very good. The bathtub and its fixtures had not been renovated. The linens and towels were nice. There were few issues about the cleanliness of my room's walls and doors. Only one of two elevators seemed to work at a time. The elevators were slow which was odd since there were only 6 or 7 floors. Staff made it a point to greet guests as they entered and exited lobby. Free WiFi in room. Very fast and stable. Free parking. No parking structure. It is just a simple uncovered lot surrounding hotel.

“Better than you'd expect from Doubletree” I've had some so-so Doubletree experiences lately, but the Doubletree in downtown Houston was top notch. Only strange thing was that the hallway reeked of cigarette smoke even though I was on a non-smoking floor: is the hotel not really all non-smoking? Fortunately, the room's air was clear, so it was more a bepuzzlement than a problem. Nice hotel, nice location, I will stay there again when in downtown Houston.

“Still Wonderful After 20 Years” Had the opportunity to spend an overnight at this beautiful hotel It had been some 20 years or so since last booking a stay for my parent 30th anniversary party. The Swan Lounge and Fountain Restaurant continue to make the mark with their amazing cocktails and food. Ivan at the Fountain Restaurant was a stellar server. The rooms could use a little refreshing. Bathrooms are a bit dated and there is no separate shower and commode area like many of the other Four Seasons. Carpet in our room was a bit dirty and worn as well We had a wonderful rate however through travelzoo and for $199 I have no complaints The spa and firness facility are top notch and the pool indoors is an added bonus the other 5 star property (Ritz Carlton) can not boast about. Would stay again if in town overnight and definitely will be back for a great meal nect time I am in Philadelphia.

“Liked it” Stayed at the Alexander Inn for a weekend in November. As I frequently do, I used TripAdvisor reviews to find a property that met my criteria of good location in the city (to me that means you can get around easily either on foot or by public transportation) and reasonable price. The Alexander met both of those requirements perfectly. I came in from the airport on the train and it was a short walk (maybe half a mile) from the train station to the Hotel. It was a even shorter little walk to the Kimmel Center where we went 2 nights, once to see the Philadelphia Orchestra, once to see PhilaDanco dance company. The breakfasts we above average for a continental breakfast bar and there was a very nice man who staffed the breakfast area and he was a great source of local entertainment info and options. We had the smaller of the queen rooms and it was rather small for 2 people but we were there to see the city, not the hotel room, so that was fine. I would definitely stay here again.

“Great for one night get away” We are locals who spent a night away from the kids and the Doubletree was perfect for us. Yes the elevators are slow. The rooms are smaller but clean and new. We had no issues with the front desk or the cleaning people disturbing us. The beds were comfy and everyone we encountered was really friendly. Keep in mind we didn't spend much time there. Not sure if I would choose this for a week long stay but for the most part it was clean and comfortable for us. Plus its hard to find anything under $200 that halfway decent in Manhattan!

“Loved the hotel- hated the location” The hotel itself was very cute. Our room was clean, clean comfortable bed, clean bathroom, great shower, staff very friendly and accommodating. We had dinner at the restaurant one night- really enjoyed the food. My only problem was that the hotel is close to fisherman's wharf which I felt to be kind of a dirty part of town. Lots of panhandlers out at night- I didn't feel safe walking around. I would stay more downtown next time.

“location, location, location” We stayed here for 5 nights. Overall I was impressed enough to reccomend this hotel in terms of location and value for money. It is a simple, no frills property located in an older style building. Check in staff were efficent, room was quite small but again, met our needs. The real selling point is location. Turn left at the hotel entrance and It is steps away from Chinatown gate which if you walk through will lead you through this area, down Columbus (Italian Quarter) and eventually down to Fisherman's Wharf. (approx 30min walk) Turn right instead and you are 5 min walk from Cable Car turnaround, 10 min walk to Market street, Union Square and the BART station (cheap and easy way of getting to and from the airport) The hotel is for the budget aware among us. If price of accomodation is not an issue then choose somewhere else but in a similar location. However, if like me you treat your room as little more than a crash pad and somewhere to freshen up between siteseeing and dinner then this hotel will suit your needs well. San Francisco is a very walkable city and the public transport links are pretty decent. In this respect, I would highly reccomend staying in this area as opposed to down at the Wharf where, it is more touristy. It is truely a beautiful city. Some highlights include: cable car to lombard st... hop off... walk down and up to Coit Tower... beautiful views bike the bridge but continue on into Sausalito... explore this lovely bayside community with art gallaries and cafe culture before you and your bike catch the ferry back to the Wharf.... beats cycling back!.. P.S. biking the bridge is a tougher ride than they let on. Go do Napa for the day... Take the nighttime Alcatraz tour instead of the daytime... far superior and atmospheric as dusk and then dark settles while you are out on 'the rock' You will love SF and if you are ok with no frills accomodation then you will love the Baldwin

“Best service ever! Incredible hotel in Hollywood” I only stayed one night at the Magic Castle Hotel but I completely understand why they are #1 on TripAdvisor in Los Angeles. What an amazing hotel. When I arrived, I received the best service I've ever experienced at a hotel from the gentleman at the reception (I believe his name was Zeeshawn) and felt very welcomed immediately. VIP treatment! I even got a welcome drink which I've never experienced before, even at the fancy spots in Las Vegas. The room - or apartment rather - was huge and very clean and pleasant. You get a large living room type area, a kitchen with full amenities, even a dining room area, a large bathroom and a tucked away bedroom. You could live in this room for weeks. The hotel offers free (yes, free!) snacks and beverages, delivered to your room if you wish, and I got a free newspaper in the morning as well. There's also complimentary breakfast included, which was a wide selection of quality products, and many in-room amenities such as multiple TVs, microwave, DVD player and so on. Nothing was missing. With a nice pool in the middle, the hotel layout is very nice, and it is adjacent to the Magic Castle Club which you can get access to as a hotel guest (I didn't try it but I hear it's a very cool experience). From the hotel, you're a 2-minute walk from the busiest part of Hollywood Blvd, with the Chinese Theatre, Hollywood & Highland, Kodak Theatre etc. The location is perfect if you want to see the sights in Hollywood. There is not much of a view from the room, but you'll be hard-pressed to find that anywhere in Hollywood. One small thing - the Wi-Fi was a bit unrealiable and seemed to work better in the living room than in the bedroom for some reason. Could have been a temporary thing. I have nothing but praise for this amazing hotel and can't wait to return!

“Wonderful, wonderful, wonderful” This is a super hotel!!! We had such a great stay here from start to finish and will definately be back. The location is great and the staff were exceptionally helpful and gracious. Can't wait for our next trip!

“Quite enjoyed my stay” I stayed here for business and quite enjoyed the stay. The hotel is modern and clean. The front desk was kind and helpful. The parking is in a secure garage where you just put a code in, so you can come and go as you please. The hotel is a little on the outskirts, there is still plenty within walking distance. I made it to the White House once on accident by walking around. There are some good restaurants within a half mile of the hotel. My room was good sized and quiet, even though it faced the street. It was in a safe neighborhood as well. I walked around on Halloween evening and felt safe. I'll be back in January!

“Great stay awesome price!” Close to activities, clean, great value, friendly staff, and easy in/out. I highly recommend this hotel...this was our first stay at a Drury..pleasant surprise! We would normally stay at a Holiday Inn but took the word of reviews here and friends who stayed here a few weeks back. Glad we took a trip out of our norm!

“Great choice” Found a discount rate on their web site for a king room on a higher floor, breakfast included. Was much, much cheaper than other hotels in the area. Requested room facing inward, not much to see but very quiet for NY. With the air cleaner in the room turned to low, was very quiet and comfortable, and no bedbugs! Breakfast was OK, not many choices and almost impossible to get a glass of water from the waitstaff (had to ask 4 times), but was included in price for room. If bought separately may be too expensive. Subway stop very close to hotel. Gave me later checkout than usual to wait for status of my flight out of LGA during the storm, desk staff were very accommodating.

“Nothing Short of Spectacular” Whenever we check in at the Grand, we take a deep breath because we know we are "home." The resort grounds and rooms are utterly amazingly out of this world. It's hard to fathom that a resort of this size has less than 300 rooms, suites, and villas because the Grand emphasizes detail, impeccable customer service, and nothing short of making one's stay a perfect 10. We love the idea that the hotel remembers our favorite room so every time we come down, they immediately put us in that room. We come to San Diego now just to stay at the Grand Del Mar! From the time we arrive and the time we depart, there isn't a minute that we don't feel pampered or treated like royalty. So many staff members recognize us and address us personally which is hard to find these days at many large impersonal hotels. But then, the Grand Del Mar doesn't fall under that category because it is in a truly 5 star category of its own. This 390 million resort is one of a kind -- over 30 types of different rocks and over 30 types of different wood. Once you have stayed here, I guarantee you that you will not want to leave. At least, that is how we feel each time we are here because we have found our "paradise on earth."

“The 2 1/2* hotel it claims to be” These reviews made me worry that I had landed a one star hotel for two and a half star prices. The hotel isn't as fancy as the three star DoubleTree across the highway, but it is fine. Room 510 was by the ice machine and the maids' room. Neither was a problem. There was some road noise, as to be expected in a hotel by a highway. So what if the parking garage turns are narrow? It's a parking garage. Room was clean and attractive, with coffee machine, balcony, two beds and sleeper couch, and all the usual amenities. The hotel has a fitness room and restaurant. Entree to the running/hiking trails on the hillside behind Hotel Circle South is from the road to Hillcrest beside the Holiday Inn. My travel companion liked the room a lot, and that was after a night at the Omni. The coffeemaker is Sunbeam instead of Cuisinart. Not a major problem.

“Great Character and Location” I did not expect to like this hotel based on other comments on Trip Advisor but I really, really enjoyed it. The service was excellent, the food in the restuarant was great (and Starbucks was in the lobby) and the rooms were clean and comfortable, with SleepNumber beds, which was a great touch. The hotel is a historic hotel so it has a lot of charm and character and during the daylight hours, you can walk to the inner harbor in about 3 minutes. Overall, great hotel and I will stay again.

“Over the top resort” I'm not a golfer, but stayed at the Grand Del mar this past weekend. The intent was to have a place to "crash" after a romantic multi-course birthday dinner for my dining companion at Addison. Quite the place to crash. I've traveled around the world and been on many high end cruises and five star hotels. The Grand is definitely one of the very best I've had the privilege to stay at. We started with a hike / run around the property. The concierge has maps of the trail(s) which ( I believe) connects to the Los Pensaquitos trail system. It's a great 3.5 mile off road run with some hills to get your heart racing. They do horse rides there too so watch out as there are droppings to dodge. The last mile is the main drive (paved) but still a great workout. The hotel is sprawling, elegant and lush - only a few stories high and service is impeccable. Decor is high end mediterranean - kind of what you would find in a brand new Ritz Carlton. A good way to think of it is kind of a "toned" down (and much, much higher quality) version of the Venetian in Las Vegas. Pros: - Room quality was excellent. The property IS a few years old but the room felt BRAND new. It was like we were the first ones ever staying in it. Towels were large and soft and linens crisp and comfortable. My only gripe would be the pillows were too big (overstuffed) but I'm sure had I called I could have gotten a different set. (This is the type of place that you get whatever it is you ask for.) We had a "basic" room and it was absolutely everything you could need. The master bath was the best I've seen in a resort and the closet area well thought out. - Dining - we ate at the Hotel restaurant Addison which was one of the best dining experiences of my life. Room service was also excellent. - Resort - We don't golf but loved the fact the resort had it's own hiking trail. The pool(s) looked nice and there is a separate spa pool that is for adults only. There is also horseback riding. Cons: - Maybe the crowd - they are how do I put it delicately, conservative and not exactly the most diverse? Not that folks weren't dressed casually or friendly, but they are very much the "country club set". That said, the staff was great and made everyone feel welcome. - Price. Again I shouldn't really complain - this place is worth the going rate of $500+ night and dining isn't inexpensive either (expect $500+ on dinner for two at Addison.) Hotel bar cocktails around $15-20 each, etc. Again, you get what you pay for. Worth a splurge - and perfect place for a special occasion. Highly recommended.

“Nice choice in good location” My husband and I stayed for five nights at the Grand Hyatt in Seattle. Upon arrival, we were met immediately by a bell captain and valet for parking. There didn't appear to be better choices for parking in the immediate vicinity, so we had to pay the parking fees. We arrived at check-in time so there was no problem getting our room right away. We were on the 24th floor with a beautiful view of the city down to the sound. The room was good size with a king bed, flat screen TV, desk, chair and ottoman. Floor to ceiling windows made the room seem larger. They had automatic window treatments for either letting in or blocking out light as needed. To me what really made the room was the enormous bathroom with separate soaking tub and shower plus a large vanity for putting out our belongings. They also provided robes and nice toiletries (including toothpaste which was a nice touch). There is a mini-fridge, but it's filled with items for purchase, so it's hard to use. They offer to bring up a small refrigerator for a $5 fee. I don't know where we would have put it. It would've been nice to have another chair in the room for lounging and reading. Otheriwse, one of us was always relegated to the bed for reading, which I found uncomfortable after awhile. We used the concierge and found his information to be a bit wanting. He directed us to a local laundry, which proved to be a long walk for nothing. We used the map they gave us after that to find out where things were, as well as the Internet. I did get free Internet as I'm a Platinum member, but I agree with others that it should probably be provided given the cost of the rooms. On a bit of a sour note, we were held up for quite some time when we went to check out. We had prepaid for the room, but were charged again. It took them some time to figure out how to back the charges off our credit card. The Pike St Market is a must-see, but try to go during the week. The weekends are crazy with masses of people moving through the market. The Music museum and Musem of Flight were really worthwhile; I recommend both. Vonn's restaurant (next door to the Hyatt) was a big disappointment....try something else. There's a great crepe place around the corner under the arch for both sweet and savory crepes made right in front of you. A few bumps at the Hyatt, but still a fun trip....loved Seattle!

“Pretty property, disinterested staff” I stayed at the Westin a week on business. Overall, the property is in a nice location, near the Green and Orange Lines of the "T" (public transportation), across the street from the beautiful library and near many shops and restaurants. The area is pretty high end so if you're looking for decent food at a low price, you can take the "T" two stops down on the Green Line to the Symphony station where you'll find a Whole Foods Market. The room was fine. It had a beautiful view from the 28th floor. It was hard to get the room as cool as I'd like it but otherwise, everything in the room worked well. The only thing that I would ding this hotel on is the staff. For example: one morning, the elevators stopped working. Announcements were made but they neglected to provide an approximation on how long it would take for the single working elevator to arrive. I waited 35 minutes and ended up walking down 28 flights of stairs in suit and heels, one day after walking up and down the 294 stairs in the Bunker Hill Monument! I felt badly for the elderly couple who were waiting for the elevator as they had a significant amount of luggage and were trying to catch a flight. The second example is when I spoke to the front desk about the elevator snafu. The Westin credited my colleague's account when she inquired. The front desk offered me SPG points. When I requested a credit, the receptionist was clearly unhappy and at no point did she apologize for the inconvenience of the elevator mishap. None of the staff looked particulately engaged or interested. If you'll be in Boston for a few days, it's worthwhile to purchase the 7-day "T" ticket for convenience and to save money. The ticket also gets you on the ferry from the Aquarium station to the USS Constitution, which is a beautiful ride. The Westin is a fine place to stay if you're not looking for warm and engaging staff.

“Great Location” We stayed at this hotel the night of a Red Sox game. It is absolutely the best place if you are going to a game. Definitely within walking distance of Fenway. The hotel lobby was nice and service was very friendly. The rooms were average. Nothing fancy and the beds weren't the best that I have had at a Hilton. However, we had everything we needed and had no complaints other than the high priced parking. However, that's just the price you pay for staying in this area. The best thing overall about this hotel is the location. You can't go wrong.
“Right downtown and very nice.” The hotel is very clean and well run. Super quiet and close to downtown.

“A lovely hotel, with maybe some service issues” Just stayed 3 nights at the Hotel 1000. Thanks to Amex FHR I was upgraded to a suite, which whilst it had no view, was very nice. The room has some nice features, such as an audio cable to plug your mp3 player into the TV. A lot of hotels now provide you the ability to connect your music or laptop to the TV, but never give you the cables, and who carries one with them? There was also an ipod cable so you could connect that or charge it if needed. It's about the only hotel I've stayed in where the HD TV displays everything in the right format. There is some style over substance. The bath that fills from the ceiling may look nice, but in reality it splashes water everywhere, and the water had to be on full to get it hot. It's then almost impossible to top up the bath later on. The hotel is in a great location, a few blocks from the University Street station if you come in via the Light Rail, just head for the 2nd Ave exit. Ordered a continental breakfast on my first day, and all I got was a yoghurt muesli thing. The tray came with jams and butter, but a bit pointless with no pastries or croissants to have them with. Wasn't sure if I'd made a mistake on the card or not, but didn't seem much of a continental breakfast. The breakfast card also wasn't replaced so hard to re-order the next day. I decided on breakfast in the restaurant after that, and one time was seated then ignored, a coffee came with no spoon or sugar, but no issues the other times. All the staff I did interact with, seemed to be genuinely happy and interested. Overall, the hotel has a very good hard product, and except for a few issues with the soft product, I had a very enjoyable stay. I would stay again if I go back to Seattle

“Worth the stay!” Loved staying here. Really nice hotel. Staff was excellent. Gave us breakfast vouchers for their restaurant. Nice breakfast. Beds really comfy and the room was roomy. Enjoyed my stay very much.

“Both Hyatts are nice” Not really much to say. I stayed at the Grand Hyatt last month -- it was one of the best hotels I've ever been in. This time I wanted to save a little, so I moved around the corner to this place. It's only slightly less luxurious, a bit less on the common areas. I like the room's style (cool glasses!). Check out the wine bar's happy hour. Dinner around up the street at the Dragonfish is also highly recommended!

“Airport hotel but not walking distance” Good hotel and not far from the airport building but not close. Bit hard to get to the hotel by walk, especially for those carrying big suitcases and passge is complicated through the parking area and no good sign board for direction which is not fault by the hotel but hotel should better discuss it with the airport authority. Room is OK and comfortable. Some kind and unkind reception staff.

“Great no-frills hotel in convenient Manhattan location” My boyfriend and I stayed here on our first trip to New York. We were on a budget and this was the cheapest place we could find (Quikbook.com had a good deal) and our friend recommended it to us. It did not disappoint. Our room had a large King size bed and a view of the city. The room was very small but we were sightseeing all day and didn't need anything larger. The room and bathroom were clean and it was nice and quiet at night. The location couldn't be beat - it's in a side neighborhood that you were far away enough from the main streets and didn't have to deal with noise but close enough that it's only a few short blocks from Times Square. Our room came with free breakfast every morning which was unexpected but very good, with cold cereal, oatmeal, yogurt, eggs, fruits, cheese, meats, bread/bagels and pastries. You were seated and waiters would bring out espresso as you ordered it, which was very nice. There were a couple times we had to wait to be seated but not long. Because this is an Italian hotel there were a lot of Italians staying here that didn't speak our language and the front desk people had accents but were helpful nonetheless. The beds weren't super-comfortable but we were so tired from sightseeing all day that it didn't matter to us. For a great, no-frills hotel in a superb Manhattan location, I would definitely recommend this hotel and hope to come back again soon!

“Hipster Heaven” The location of this hotel, a few blocks off the Magnificent Mile and near the lake is great for a getaway or business. It seems obvious what they are going for at this property is to draw a hip crowd as you basically walk into a nightclub/bar. Actually, it is an assault on the senses if what you want is a retreat from noise. The lobby on the Saturday night I checked in was loud and crowded. Front desk staff were helpful as were the valet staff at check-in. Once on the guest floors you find it dark (though apparently by design) and but for the color scheme, utilitarian and not fancy space. The room we were assigned was small but, like the overall theme given a funky decor. The room with two beds was tight, not cruise ship style but more than a couple people in this room would have felt really cramped. I didn't eat at this hotel so cannot comment on it. There are other hotels in Chicago I would rather stay at for the same money. I just couldn't get a better deal that weekend. All-in-all, just ok.

“No Views...But Great Service and Location” I stayed at the Hampton Inn Baltimore Inner Harbour for one night while attending-working a few Orioles games in early June. I arrived after midnight, checked in with no problems with a very courteous staff member, and received the king room I had requested. Also, during check in, since I was a member of the Hilton Honors program I was told to grab a few waters out of the cooler, and 2 snacks from the wide selection they had onsite. The room was very well equipped, nicely decorated and very clean. There was ample workspace, and free internet service. The TV channel selection was very good as well as the reception. The bed was very very comfortable, soft sheets and great pillows, I could have stayed in bed all day but I had some sightseeing to do. The bathroom was very big….lots of room to move around, great soaps and stuff provided, large shower, rounder shower curtain rod for extra room, great water pressure and plenty of hot water. I had the complimentary breakfast buffet located on the lobby level, it had a wide selection of cereal, fruit, breads, hot cinnamon rolls, biscuits and gravy (on that day), coffee, juices and assorted beverages…it was a bit hard to navigate as things seemed kind of out of order and place…but items were replenished well, and there was plenty of room to eat, and lots of tables, along with a wide screen TV to catch up on the news… This hotel is located about town and a half blocks from the Inner Harbour area, and was very safe to walk around during the day time, and when I arrived late at night via taxi, there did not seem to be any bad activity in the area. Lots of places to eat and see in the Inner Harbour area. I took advantage of the luggage storage service from the bellmen desk, and they secured my items in a locked room ( free of charge + tip ) while I saw the sights that day. Keep in mind that there are basically no views from this hotel, your window either looks down to an alley or a street out side, I was on the alley side of things and there was virtually no noise issues whatsoever….but the rooms and service are great ! I would have stayed here the other nights but was staying on an award night, and wanted to be closer to the ballpark, 6 or 7 blocks away….enjoy this property…I did !

“Nice weekend visit - but packed with conventioneers!” Stayed here for the weekend to go to a Cubs game and visit family and friends. We were very pleased on arrival - front desk staff couldn’t have been nicer, noting we were SPG members and thanking us for our stay even though we booked a low rate through Hotwire and weren’t in the SPG system for this stay. Our room was ready when we arrived on a Friday morning at 10am, so we were happy to be able to drop our things, do a little work, and freshen up before the game. The room overlooked the city with a sliver of Navy Pier visible in the distance, though the weather was so foggy we hardly saw it all weekend. Rooms with two double beds were comfortable enough, though a hotel of this quality should really have two-queen rooms instead. Bathroom was old with standard fixtures – didn’t feel like a four-star hotel bathroom, honestly – but was clean. Room overall was fine but there seemed to be a layer of dust on everything – housekeeping could definitely be more thorough. “Sweet Sleeper” beds were as comfortable as advertised and we all slept very well. Big-screen flat screen TV was great, but the clock-radio was old-style with no iPod dock. There was a party going on in the room next door to us on one of the nights and we heard some noise but it definitely could have been worse. There were several conventions in the hotel while we were there, so the huge lobby was always hopping. There are a couple of ‘game tables’ with built-in video games – including old school games like checkers – that were declared the highlight of the place by the youngest member of the party. We didn’t even notice the internet café on the bottom floor until our last day when we were permitted to print our boarding passes there for free – looked like a good place if you needed to jump online for a few minutes but I don’t know what the fee is. In-room internet was $12.95/day, I think, so we used the hotspot in our smartphone instead. Overall, totally fine for a weekend stay, and would probably be great for a convention. We’ve stayed at other hotels in the neighborhood that are more suited for families but had problems finding a good rate for this weekend, so the Sheraton did just fine. We didn't rent a car until the last day when we left to visit people in the suburbs and go to the airport because at $49/night, parking was much too much. It's just a few blocks from public transportation which was just fine. The hotel is just a few blocks from our favorite breakfast spot West Egg Cafe, and we visited Sue the Dinosaur at the Field Museum while we were there, too.

“True 5 star service on par with Peninsula and Four Seasons, exceeds Ritz-Carlton” I have been here for several business meetings and have not been disappointed yet. The service is truly 5 star. Of course, at these prices, it should be. The gym is extremely well equipped and has sufficient machines that all are accomodated. The restaurants are excellent; but the prices for food and drink are exorbitant

“Cool, but very very busy” If you are looking for a quiet hide away....this isnt it. However, if you are looking for a loud, hip crowd then this is a good spot. I thought staff was very friendly and helpful. out door bar was great for drinks and snacks. The place is packed and crazy at all times, but hey....its Hollywood.

“Could not have stayed at a better hotel!” We stayed in Baltimore for the Memorial Day weekend. We could only get the Hotel Monaco for Friday night. The location is great, the staff is very friendly in the hotel, and the amenities are good. The turn down service was a welcomed surprise and so was the $10 credit for being a kimpton member. We did not use the valet service. We went up on street past the hotel to Fayette street and parked in a self-park underground lot that was roughly $13. The Happy Hour in the lobby from 5-6 was great. It was a nice way to unwind after a long day of travel. I will suggest if you book early, check your rate before arriving. I was able to find a lower rate the day before we checked in and changed it online to the lower price. The restaurant that is attached is great for drinks in the evening, but the morning staff was very disorganized and we ended up leaving before having breakfast. As with most Kimpton hotels- truly worth the money for the little amenities that they provide.

“Probably the best concierge club ever” Spent two nights here while working in the area. Checked in the Sunday of Thanksgiving weekend to find it overflowing w/Irish Step Dancers attending a competition @ the nearby convention center. Thankfully they left that night, but not until very late that night-lots of running up & down the halls until they were gone. We were given one of the executive suites w/another room connected to it which worked out very nicely for us, especially since the suite had a mini-fridge. Concierge club is one of the best I have seen-full hot breakfast & very substantial evening appetizers and desserts. Several restaurants right across the street along w/the hotel restaurant for other dining options. Would definitely stay again.

“Excellent Drury” We've stayed here numerous times and always enjoyed our stay. As mentioned by others, the staff is excellent which I've found typical in the Drury chain across the US. They seem to make a point of selection and training good folks. The hotel has been recently remodeled, so everything seems fresh and new. The grounds are especially nice with a well landscaped pool with separate sitting area with chairs, picnic tables, etc. Very nice on a cool spring day in San Antonio. Rooms are well equipped with micro, fridge, wide screens (suites have two TVs), good bedding and pillows. Breakfast is way above average and well presented, snacks in the evening are worth a look as well. Location is great for the airport, and there are main arteries nearby for quick access to downtown and other areas of the city. Ask for the eSaver rate or managers special to save a few dollars.

“Mostly awesome stay, with some quirks” Overall, my three-night stay at The Avenue Hotel Crowne Plaza was quite good, with no major complaints about the things that were most important to me. There were numerous quirky things though. I might call it the good, the bad and the weird. THE GOOD The location, just barely off North Michigan Avenue is in the real heart of things, especially for anyone visiting on leisure. Tons of great restaurants and shopping is all in walking distance. Other attractions and destinations are a longer but nice walk in pleasant weather, a short inexpensive cab ride way or accessibly by subway, the nearest station being just five short blocks away from the hotel. I wouldn't call the room spacious, but it's not cramped either. There's adequate room for two. The firm beds with pillow-top mattresses and very comfy linens provide a great night's sleep. Having a window that opens enough to allow a decent amount of fresh air in is also a great feature of the room. Giant kudos to this hotel for having free wireless Internet. Not only that, but the quality and connection is solid and doesn't even require having to continually sign on an agree to terms each day. I didn't have a single hiccup with it during my entire stay, which is a rarity for free or pay Internet access. The minibar is not only appropriately stocked with useful/common/popular items (instead of some of the strange things that some hotels offer), but the pricing on it is very fair. Housekeeping was prompt, thorough and very courteous. The staff was generally very helpful with requests and directions. THE BAD My one major complaint was the heating/air-conditioning unit, which was controlled by an electronic thermostat, but curiously located on a side interior wall, though it looked like a wall unit that would typically face outside. (Note that it was set at 65 when I arrived and it quickly became too cold, and I'm not a person who usually minds cooler air). Regardless of the setting, it seemed that the fan wanted to run nonstop. The temperatures during my September stay were moderate with cool nights and I felt like Goldilocks, because it seemed that it would either make the room too cold or too hot, but never just right. Turning the thermostat setting up just one degree, to 69 or 70 would cause it to start firing heat, which was completely unnecessary. Before the first night, I quickly learned that turning it off completely and opening the window for a while during the daytime made it perfect, not to mention quieter. I If this were brought to management's attention, they would probably say they would address it, but really, I think it's just a matter of the way the system is and not that it's malfunctioning. 'd be willing to bet that in hotter or colder months, the unit would do it's job better. Speaking of air-conditioning, even on chilly nights, the central air in the hallway was blasting cold air at full throttle from the vents in front of the elevators. Speaking of elevators, as others have pointed out, there's only three servicing 28 floors of rooms plus the lobby and two other floors. For the most part, it wasn't a big problem, but if you happen to catch an elevator rush hour when several people are checking in or a lot of people attending a convention are returning to their rooms at about the same time, it can get rather interesting with long waits from the room floors and a line in the lobby. THE SORT-OF BAD Soundproofing wasn't a strong point. Thankfully, I couldn't hear anything from my neighbors' rooms sans one toilet that flushed at least once every half hour all day and all night, but even on the high floors with the windows closed, the windows don't keep out the sounds of frequent sirens, horns and some other street noise.
