It didn't bother me in the least, but some light sleepers may be annoyed, While there was a newer desk lamp, newer duvets and and a newer flat screen television, most of the furniture was older including two lamps and the desk. I don't mind the mix of eras, but the desk, which was nice and large to work on, creaked when it got a little push. A new desk with some desk level electrical outlets would be a welcome addition. The bellman was plenty polite, but I have no idea why he offered to get me a cab every time I came down. Even when I asked for DIRECTIONS to a restaurant that was barely a 10 minute walk away (on a beautiful night, I might add), his response was "It's about a $5 cab ride. I'll get you a cab." I had to ask again, specifying and stressing that I was walking. Do the bellmen get a kickback from cabdrivers or what? THE WEIRD The cab-happy bellman could certainly fit into this category too. All of the front desk/guest services staff (it seems to be all one in lobby) were plenty nice and professional. Some were quick and confident in giving fairly simple directions and others had to pull out maps and/or ask someone (which sometimes led to asking someone else). They weren't beyond suggesting cabs either. When it came to accommodating a special request there were some inconsistencies -- one attendant gave an apologetic "no" without any checking while another was pleasant and more than happy to accommodate. The indoor pool and (outdoor) sundeck on the top floor seems like one of the hotel's treasures, and a secret treasure at that. The front desk staff never brought it up at check-in. On day 2 of my stay, I noticed it conservatively listed next to the 40th floor button on the elevator and checked it out. Another secret treasure is the breakfast (additional charge) available on the top floor, with a great view. Again, the front desk staff never mentioned it, but I noticed a very small sign for it somewhere in the hotel. The biggest unanswered question: Why are all glasses and cups stored at the furthest possible point from the sink? Seriously, both glasses and coffee cups were on a little table by the window at the far corner. They're almost hidden. Something should be rethought here. I've heard of water-saving shower-heads, but the fancy one in this room must hold the record -- at least for the minimal amount of water it puts out. I'm not sure that having to shower for twice as long ultimately saves anything. Personally, I'm of the opinion that they should save a little on energy with the nonstop AC and spend a little more on water. The fancy rod for the shower curtain, which curves out beyond the bathtub, requires users to really be sure to create good seal with the inner curtain. Amazingly, that meager amount of water can still flood the bathroom floor with the way the curtain is set up. I would have never guessed that I would ever notice that a room has too much artwork, but this one does. The room is still quite pleasant, but five wall-hangings in the modest size room is a bit much. Three of them are stunning black-and-white nicely framed large photos of the Chicago skyline and various Chicago landmarks. One of the three is partially masked by an old lamp that sits in front of it (photo provided). The two that seem out of place are panoramic color photos of the Chicago skyline that hang at a high level above each of two beds, above the already high good-looking headboards of the beds. Even more odd is that the two pictures are exactly identical. Someone astonishing is that in my room one of them was not centered with the bed -- and it was off by a sizable amount (picture provided).

“Parc 55 Visited 20 months later...last minute deal” My original review was for January 2008... I had wanted to go up to SF for a couple days but was tentative of commiting to the purchase a hotel room due to the threat of a BART STRIKE...Getting into the city would of been VERY problematic. (see parking tip) Now, since my trip was Last minute (No Strike, but I was told many Bay Area people took that monday off because they expected horrible traffic issues) I was having issues making a SF purchase on Priceline with the usual hotels I like. Usually I try to pay between 80-100 = taxes.. I tried the PARC 55 site which has a room for 125ish a night without taxes. I kept clicking around for specials on their site. I found a NON-REFUNDABLE special for the same room for 102 a night (two nights with taxes was 235...PERFECT!!). The hotel is close to the POWELL STATION...I knew it was SAFE, CLEAN and though VERY large doesn't feel so which is why I liked it the last time I visited. My biggest issue my last visit was the lack of consistent Internet...I actually called PARC 55 to ask them if it was more stable. They said they thought so. They also mentioned that the Internet cafe around the corner I mentioned in my last review is closed for 6 months of remodeling ( FYI) The hotel has done a remodel since I visited last. Check in is now in a much more modern area on the second floor. They let me check in early at 12pm which was pleasant since I had been driving from LA and on thr BART for 40 min . The lobby was full of people but not a long wait. Originally they were going to put me in a 13th floor room but I asked my receptionist if they had anything with a view..She upgraded me to the 23th floor which was VERY appreciated by me.Sometimes being pleasant, asking with a smile makes a difference...AlsoTheir new lobby/close by bar area welcomed the NEW York Mets...I heard this is a hotel for a lot of the teams... My room was as I remembered, big bathroom with a cimfy bed, I did like that they no longer used LATHER for products which I though were sucky on my last stay. THE INTERNET was $12.95 a day but WORKED perfectly. they had both wireless and plug in. I was VERY HAPPY! AREA COMPARISION: Since I know the city better this time around I can confidently tell you that this location is WAY better then the Union Hilton and Hotel Nikko. Though they are only a block away sometimes you can feel it in a city such as SF. Plus both those hotels looked SOOO BUSY. **PARKING TIP: Go to the BART SITE, buy an extended parking permit ($5 a day,not 24 hours) Then take the BART into the city. Parking in SF can be 35-50 a day depending on the area. 3 days of parking (15) + a roundtrip from pleasanton (10.55) was = $26 bucks... Also If it is a three day weekend, that Monday parking is free! ***Dining. Hotel is super close to a SUBWAY, WALGREENS (buy water), COLDSTONE, PIZZA PLACE within a block. There is a nearby Chinese Resturant. My fave is PUCCINI & PINETTI off Ellis and Cyril Magnin..GREAT happy hour ($3 champagene but not boozy.

“Great Location and Quiet Rooms” This is the first hotel in a large city that was absolutely quiet. Even the hallway noise was barely perceptable. It must be the solid 1926 construction that prevents hearing a snore fest in the room next door. We were on the 14th floor and did not have a view of City Hall. The fellow who checked us in was willing to let us have the view room for one night however we didn't want to change rooms for nights 2 and 3. The front desk staff could not have been nicer or more helpful. Great location for seeing the sights but be prepared for the many homeless/street folk who will approach you for money. (There are some social service offices nearby.) Parking at the Convention Center is less than the Marriott lot.

“2 nights in Houston” My husband and I stayed at this hotel for two nights while visiting some family nearby. The hotel was a good location for us. Our room was great, spacious and clean. The bed was quite comfortable. The only unfortunate thing about our stay was that our original booking was for three days and we had to change it to two on arrival due to change in plans. This change is length of stay ended up increasing our room rate by $80 for the first night! I am still happy with the property, but if I had known this rate would have jumped this much, I may have looked around for a better deal elsewhere.

“A fine hotel overall” We stayed at the Rex for 4 nights over Christmas. Rooms were pleasantly decorated and adequate size. One couple had a standard room off the street (609) and we had a larger King room at the rear of the hotel(604). Only problem in both rooms was low light..lamps did not illuminate the rooms well and light from the window was low. Staff members were all great. The lounge was cozy and wine reception was well attended.Hotel is in art gallery neighborhood...lots of activities. 1 block from Union square. We heard the cable car bells when the window was open. Rooms had that old building smell...open window took care of it. Room was very clean. Water pressure in the shower was great. Mini bar refrigerator had room for our extra food. Cafe Andre breakfast was pretty good but not up to the excellent reviews we read.

“Great location, good value” Stayed with a group of friends for a long weekend in September. The location is great. Near the L and one block from Millennium Park and all the shopping up Michigan Avenue. Coffee shops and restaurants all within walking distance. Somehow ended up with a one bedroom suite. Full living room with separate bedroom and huge bathroom. Rooms were very clean. Furniture could be updated but functional and clean. Hotel staff very polite and helpful. You can't beat the price. I'd stay here again. Take the blue line subway from direct from O'Hare and get dropped off two blocks away for $2.50 (better than sitting in traffic in a cab and paying $40).

“Tiny rooms, but good rates” The MAve is well-located and well-priced--these are its main recommendations. The place has some style, the free wi-fi, flat-screen tv and iPod dock are nice touches, and the staff is friendly and helpful--but in the end, the selling point is a clean room in a prime Manhattan location. We are former New Yorkers coming back for a visit, and we just needed a place to sleep and leave our stuff in an area convenient to everything we wanted to do--and this fit the bill. We had the most basic room category, which has a full bed--not a queen, as another reviewer said--and is about the size of a decent walk-in closet. But that was fine--we knew what we were getting into. The room was very clean, with crisp white bedding and a modern bathroom. A couple downsides: the humidity in the room was never quite right, so the sheets often felt damp, and the blinds let in a lot of light come morning. We got a lot of use out of the free wi-fi and certainly appreciated that amenity. One suggestion I would make is not to have such sharp corners on the beds in such a tight room, which invites people like me to smash open a toe on them. But whatever, I am clumsy. The part that concerned me was when I asked for extra pillows to elevate my foot and a staff member (who had come very quickly with band-aids and antiseptic wipes) told me there were no extra pillows in the entire hotel. Seriously? In a hotel? To be fair, he managed to produce some fairly quickly after that. Despite any such issues, overall it was decent value in the amazingly overpriced world of Manhattan hotels. The location was really the selling point--right in the very central Gramercy area, easy walking distance to Union Square, close to the subway.

“Opulent, HIgh Class and Worth It!” The Arizona Grand Resort is a luxury resort that has a very opulent feel. It has lots of extras you don't find in other hotels. It is in a convenient location just a few minutes drive south of the Airport on I-10, so its easy to jet to. All the rooms open to the ouside (no interior halls....hey in Phoenix, who needs them?) and have outdoor balconies. There is a massive pool complex. So when you talk about the hotel 'pool' you have to specify which of the six or seven you are talking about. They have lots of hottubs and even a very large waterpark attached on the south side of the property. They are true suites. So they have a living room with a sofa that converts to a pull out bed AND a separate bedroom. The rooms have a bit of a Southwest feel to them but its not overpowering. The rooms are well appointed and have very nice soft beds. There are kids activities and even a special kids room where during the high season you can drop off the kids for an adventure of their own without their parents while the parents can take a little time off to be with each other. There are lots of lobbies, seating areas and gathering spaces all over the resort so there is plenty of room to stretch out and not feel cramped. The resort is tucked at the foothills of South Mountain Park, so with a quick 10 minute drive south and west you can be driving up to a 2300 foot peak and take great pictures of the Phoenix valley below. Plus the mountains make a nice backdrop for sunset. Just a few downers. The resort is so outdoor oriented with tons of walkways, stairways, and nooks and crannys that at night if you get turned around it can be tough to find your way back. And in some of the spots its a bit dark and creepy especially late at night. They don't have free internet. Instead you pay a $25 'resort fee' that is not well disclosed until you get there. This pays for internet, health club access and other amenities that they then don't nickle and dime you for. But I was there on business and the only thing I used for my $25 daily fee was the internet, which is steep. Also, I was only given one bar of soap, rather than like other places that give you two...one for the sink and one for the bath. But otherwise, a great location for a business conference. They have excellent meeting facilities.

“Very convenient location. Typically Hyatt in other regards.” Best thing about this hotel is it is walking distance to a great deal. A few blocks to the capital and National Mall, 15 minutes to the restaurants around 7th, 20 minute walk to convention center (about 1.25 miles). There is a large homeless center behind the hotel with many people milling about at all hours, but did not seem unsafe. Hotel is typically Hyatt, who does do a better job of making their lobbies functional instead of just places to sit and wait for people. TVs, tables for impromptu meetings, open to bar and restaurant area. The hotel does get dinged for a dated decor. Actually, this is the result of three hallway issues. First, the lights are dim and have shades that cast a dull yellow hue, the doors are 1970-era flat laminated fake wood, and the wallpaper is that beigey-almond color that looks it is from an old Denny's restaurant. The overall effect is old and depressing. The rooms and public areas are fine. Internet service has two fee options...really slow and kinda slow but overpriced. $17 for internet, really?

“Nice choice for an airport hotel.” First time I've stayed in this part of Chicago, (Usually it's out at ORD or Downtown) and the hotel is very new & very nicely furnished. It's in a center with all of the major business hotels represented, and this appears to be the best choice of the group. The rooms were very quiet & well insulated (Heater hardly came on all night) and had plenty of space. I did use the gym, and it is nicely equipped and a good size (not just a converted hotel room) and they had a very nice indoor pool as well. About the only drawback to the place was is it's great if you need something near Midway, but otherwise it's in kind of a rough area and not that close to Downtown. Outside of a few chain resturants, not many choices for resturants nearby past fast food. Still, If I have to be on the west side of Chicago, I'll be back here again.

“decent hotel, provides shuttle....” we stayed here a couple of nights to tour rice university for my son going to college. the hotel is clean, comfortable mattresses. the main reason why i booked this hotel is because they have shuttle service. it is really very convenient to take their shuttle. it brings you wherever you want to go within 2-3 miles radius. the driver is very conversant as well and even brought us to rice village and picked us up from there. all you have to do is call the front desk. it takes only 15-20 minutes wait. check in/out was a breeze. my only complaint was that their housekeeping takes forever to clean the room. we went out in the morning for our business in town, came back early afternoon, the room was not service yet. we called front desk since i wanted to freshen up a little bit (needs towel), before we go out again to visit some friends who lives outside houston. the front desk woman said, "ok". i guess, in that part of town, they are slow in cleaning rooms and it's normal. we ended up leaving anyway. we saw the housekeeper when we were leaving, she's on her phone talking non-stop. maybe they take it easy and do their job whenever. also, the bar is closed by around 9pm? we drove down to cvs to buy some wine which by the way close to the hotel. we also had to buy wine opener since the hotel doesn't have one (most of the chain hotels do have one, but not this one). other than that, it is close to area hospitals and businesses.

“Great location and service!” I stayed at the Residence Inn Downtown in Memphis recently with a group of girlfriends, and we had a great time! We booked a 2 bedrooom, 2 bath suite and found it to be a comfortable stay for a group. Things we liked about it: Excellent service from the beginning to end of our stay - the receptionist, valets, and other hotel staff were friendly and extremely helpful. They went out of their way to help us have a good time, such as calling a restaurant we were interested in to find the best driving directions or letting our car stay past our check-out while we explored downtown. Location - you can't beat the location of accessibility to everything downtown. The trolley stop is right around the corner, and the trolley runs along the river and through the downtown area, including a stop at Beale St. We were able to easily get to any downtown attraction we were interested in. If we had known that ahead of time, we probably wouldn't have paid the extra to valet our car with in/out privileges, but would've just left it parked the whole stay. Room size - the rooms were large and comfortable for our group. One of our bathrooms was handicapped accessible (not something we requested), but that made it especially roomy. The living room area was great for visiting and watching TV together and the kitchen was equipped with what we needed (although we wished for a blender to mix drinks!) We had a corner room with large windows that looked out two directions onto downtown and the river, and we watched a horse and carriage with a wedding party go down the street from our window the first day we were there. Even though we were only on the second floor, we didn't have any problems with street noise. Amenities - the roof has a great view of the river that we visited at sunset, and there is a hot tub on the roof that looked like a perfect way to view the sunset. It was pretty cold when we were there, so we didn't try it, especially after someone in the elevator told us the water wasn't very hot, so I can't speak to whether it's a good hot tub, but it sure looked inviting. The complimentary breakfast was also nice with waffles, fruit, muffins, eggs, biscuits (no meat though). It was definitely more than we needed. Checkout time was noon, rather than 11, which gave us an extra hour to sleep in and enjoy a lazy breakfast downstairs. Here are the downsides we found to the hotel: We had trouble with showers in the morning, all getting hot water consistently. While we were all able to shower, it took a lot of fiddling with the faucets to make it happen. There is no ice machine because the rooms come with a refrigerator with an icemaker. However, the icemaker was turned off when we got there, with no ice in the tray, and by the time we realized it, there really wasn't time to get any ice made. The ice maker only seemed to make a few cubes at a time. I don't know if we could've gotten ice downstairs from the front desk, because we weren't really in the room that much, but it was aggravating to not have ice when we wanted it. However, I'd say that positives definitely outweighed the negatives, and I would highly recommend this hotel for a group who wanted a larger area than a standard hotel room. While it was somewhat pricey ($279 a night plus $15 valet parking), it wasn't bad when we split it among ourselves. The hotel helped us have a memorable getaway in Memphis.

“2nd time staying here and it was equally as good, would go back” This was our second time staying at the Hampton Inn and it was as good as I remembered it. The rooms are very clean, beds very comfortable. The free airport shuttle is reliable, as is the shuttle to the general area. The T stop is about a mile away- my son walked it with no problem, and living in a city felt safe walking both during the day and at night. The bus stop is just outside the hotel if you don't want to walk to the T. This just might be our go to hotel in Boston! The price is extremely reasonable for a city hotel.

“Nice hotel, Lovely, clean rooms.” I stayed for 8 nights in a King Deluxe. It was very roomy, especially for NY. A coworker had a queen room, very small, but they also had a balcony. Not much help when it's freezing out, but in the summer, I'm sure it's awesome. My room nice and clean and comfortable. Bathroom, very modern, big "open" shower, no tub in my room. Towels could have been a little larger, I like big towels. The robe was a nice touch and the Kiehl's amenities. Housekeeping was excellent. At times it was a little loud from street noise, my room was on the 7th floor on the Chambers st. side. But nothing some ear plugs resolved. Never heard another guest in surrounding rooms the entire week I was there. Front Desk and Bell ppl very nice. Can't comment on the limited room service menu b/c I never ordered from it. Bar prices kind of steep. Starbucks right next door and Le Pain Quotidien for a nice breakfast next door as well. Also, the common areas in the lobby, tres chic, and comfortable. Nice touch, the French Macaroons a gift from "Perfect Escapes". The subway, 1,2,3 right outside the door and many more located a block or 2 away. A former NY'er, it was really easy for me to get around. Great time, great area, walking distance to Soho, even when it's cold outside! Bundle up and be off.

“Great location, walking distance to Chinatown and Fisherman's Wharf” We didn't spend a lot of time in the hotel because we were out sightseeing a lot, but the fact that it had a fridge and small kitchen area was impressive. We didn't need to use our car to get to all the places we wanted to go. Overall, a great value.

“Clean, Easy, Roomy, Good Value!” I needed to leave the Denver airport early so headed up the day before from Colorado Springs via shuttle and was picked up at the airport by the Hyatt shuttle. Check in on line was easy. I'd asked for a quiet room away from ice machines and elevators and the room they gave me had no shared wall on the bedroom side! I got to the hotel which is located in a fairly open, barren plain about a mile from the airport. There is no restaurant or room service but they have a nice little store where you can buy food one can heat up in the room's microwave OR oven, plus beer, wine, and travel supplies...great selection of ALL. I had an excellent Italian dinner about two blocks away. In the morning, they do provide a FULL breakfast buffet for free...very tasty and starts at 6am. The room was very big with a foyer/FULL-sized kitchen, LARGE couch, ottoman and flatscreen TV area, a desk and biz chair with free internet, and nice big comfy bed, large tiled shower, bath with full size closet. This is a room one could certainly live in as an extended stay option. The room was $109 with AAA discount. Next morning, I took their free shuttle to the airport. All in all, more expensive than some nearby airport hotels, but still a great hotel room value. I highly recommend it!

“Fantastic Value!” I stayed in Denver for a few days for a conference and chose this hotel partly due to reviews on Tripadvisor. I was not disappointed! The hotel is close to the convention center, and also convenient to the pedestrian mall for shopping. The amenities were great --full kitchen, with little extras like microwave popcorn, and high-speed internet, exactly as the hotel website advertises. Cutlery, dishes, everything was fine. The morning breakfast was quite comprehensive. The evening snack/happy hour is really just a snack and, for vegetarians, just salad. Even without the complimentary meals the hotel would have been a good deal, though, and with the meals included it's even better. Apparently the concierge will shop for you, but I didn't use that service. The staff were polite and friendly. The gym is small but adequate and looks out onto the "rooftop deck" Some reviews mention the great view -- it's not! On 3 sides, hotel rooms look down (my room had a view of the pool deck) and on the other side, tall office buildings. There's a peekaboo view of country past the office buildings, but not of the Rockies. So, be warned, people can look down onto you. Still, it's nice having an outside Jacuzzi. It's well maintained -- the guy checked chemicals several times and kept adding until the combination was perfect. I was upgraded to a 1-br suite which was more than I needed but for 2 people travelling it would be useful to have an extra room. There are some pleasant walks nearby, if you go through downtown to a residential district. This hotel exceeded my expectations, and I would definitely return.

“Trouble-Free Business Visit” First, you should know that I paid a discounted conference rate (including parking) for my stay at this property. I would have considered staying somewhere else, if I had been visiting for a vacation and if I was asked to pay full-price for a room. Hotel is in a good location relative to the airport, train and nightlife (not too close or too far). DIY parking was easy and convenient. Check-in was fast and friendly. Elevators were responsive and fast. The only restaurant/bar in the hotel is small, but I thought that the food and drinks were good and reasonably priced. Someone told me that room-service meals were good, but I did not like the sound of the mandatory three-dollar service charge, plus an additional 21% gratuity. My room with a king-size bed on the 11th floor was sufficiently roomy and had a nice view of downtown San Jose. The bed was comfortable but would benefit from being turned/flipped. Free WIFI in the room would have been a nice service (ten dollars per day was charged for in-room Internet). The clearning crew were consistently nice. The gym was small but nice. The pool was very small (but clean), and one jacuzzi was available. These facilities easily became crowded and required waiting to use them. The business center was easy to use and free (at least for the things I used it for). Free WIFI in the lobby was appreciated, but seating in the lobby was very limited. The meeting facilities that we used were acceptable. There were climate-control problems that apparently haven't been solved since we used the same space two years ago. Staff that supported the meeting (water, food, tables, chairs, etc.) were polite and effective. Given the rate that I paid and the purpose of my visit, this property provided a very good, trouble-free experience.

“Will be back; Clean, affordable & great location!” I stayed here for one night during a very warm week in July. The aircon shuts down if you are out of the room for a while (motion sensors) but since they are brand new it cools the room down very quickly. The shower and bathroom were spotless and laid out nicely. The complimentary internet and bottled water are nice amenities; they also had an ipod docking radio which had decent sound. My king bed room on the 30th floor had a nice view of the Empire State building and city in general. It was very quiet and well decorated. Elevators were slow during peak use times, but never more than a 5 minute wait for me. The only ice / vending machines are in the basement which is slightly inconvenient. There was also a fitness center down there but I did not try it, nor did I try room service or the lobby lounge. I arrived at 12:30 and as others have stated no rooms were available and the small lobby was full of bags, which looked a little shabby. Had lunch on 9th Ave and then came back around 1:30 and was given my room, which was nice since check in is technically at 3. As for the area, it is fine- not Park Avenue, but certainly not dangerous in any way. It is close to multiple subway lines and cabs are plentiful. The airport express bus departs from the north side of PA bus terminal on 42nd, a cheap way to get to nyc airports. All in all it was a clean, affordable hotel in a great location for a quick visit to New York, no major complaints at all.

“Management turnover, but no break in service” This is a top award winner within the Hyatt brand, largely due to the manager, Andrew Davidson. He has moved up to manage the Park Hyatt Washington DC; look for that property to improve. The current manager, Lance Martin, is still settling in. There are minor lapses, but overall the hotel has maintained its excellent service.

“Awesome hotel” We got this hotel for $120 on Priceline on July 4, which is a great deal. The hotel opened only 3 months ago, so everything is brand new. The employees are all very friendly and helpful and the room was great. The bed was very comfortable. The shower was great and separate from the tub area. There was a sliding window by the bed to look into the bathroom area. Flat screen tv with many channels. The fitness area was great for a hotel, but the pool area was very limited and there were only a couple of chairs to sit on. Also, it is a lap pool, but it is only 3 ft deep, hardly deep enough to do laps and there were unsupervised kids all over the pool, preventing anyone trying to actually do laps from swimming. Valet parking is a bit pricey, $39 for 24 hrs, but that's to be expected in a city. If you do go, check out Fajitas & Ritas Mexican restaurant near Boston Commons. There is also a restaurant you can walk to that's two blocks away, the Barking Crab, which is awesome. Overall, a very nice hotel.

“Great for a business traveler” My stay at the Courtyard was quite nice. The location right in downtown Austin was just right for my business trip. Lots of dining choices nearby. Hotel service was great. There is a good amount of construction in downtown Austin right now, but you could still get around on-foot easily. This is a standard Courtyard except for the fact it adjoins a Residence Inn. The fitness center is located on the Residence Inn side and the Residence Inn side provides complimentary afternoon cookies for their guests. The Courtyard just has flavored water or coffee in for their guests. The Courtyard had some evening music in the lobby, a guitarist one night. That was fine, but it would be nice if they provided a manager's reception. (I was there two nights mid-week.)

“Great Hotel for One” I often travel to New York on business and tend to stay at Morgans, this time I thought I would give the Hudson a go. Yes, the rooms are small, but you don't come to New York to stay in your room. The room's are a good size for a single traveller - plenty of wardrobe space and amenities. The bar always has a great atmosphere and the roof terraces are beautiful. The only downside was that room service was non-existent and no mini-bar. I was informed that the hotel was re-doing the system and therefore not available, however if I had know this before I probably would not have stayed at the Hudson. Still, good location and great for a business trip /long weekend.

“Didn't actually stay here but excellent customer service” We had reserved this hotel but due to unforeseen circumstances, we didn't end up keeping our reservation. However, I wanted to write this review to single out the exceptional customer service from the manager, Paul Masai. My emails were always answered promptly and when we had a problem, he resolved it immediately. So...no comment on the actual hotel not having stayed there, but the management was certainly worth a mention.

“Nice size room” We just returned from a night in NYC. My husband had business in the city and I played tag-a-long wife to shop and see a show. Park Central offered convenience and proximity to everywhere I wanted to walk. Our room was clean and larger than average by NYC standards. I got a deal on eliesureline.com for 165 including tax which again by NYC standards was pretty good. The gym was well equiped. Only problem was the check in line (long) and elevators (crowded and slow).

“Houston Marriott West Loop” Hello fellow Marriott Premium members, Overall, this is a great property with fantastic customer service (especially at the front desk). The rooms are very clean, spacious and well-laid out. My only issue with this particular hotel was the lack of service in the Concierge Lounge. Often times in the evenings, the food items were either all gone (or cold and stale) and the staff was not particularly attentive to its upkeep. Breakfast in the lounge wasn't really any better, although the staff did seem to care more about its patrons. Enjoy your stay!

“Nice Hotel and location” Just returned from a few days away with my son. My son enjoyed the pools but I was surprised that there wasn't a lifeguard on duty. The pool closest to the slides wasn't heated while the one closest to the jacuzzi was. The rooms wee spacious and the beds comfy. Within walking distance of Belmont Park and the hotel offers valet service to this destination until 7pm. The kids also enjoyed watching the fireworks from SeaWorld. We took the Amtrak down and the hotel was close to the bus stop which was convenient to the use of the trolley. If the price was right, I would definitely stay here again. My main complaint was they didn't offer shuttle pickup from the Amtrak station but Best Western did.

“Best Choice” I stayed in Hilton Garden for 4 days. The staff is friendly and you get answer for any question. The hotel is close to 16th Mall Street which full of shops & restaurants. I would stay there again.

“Nice new hotel but less than optimal location” I generally like Starwood properties and was pleased with this Westin overall. It is relatively new, the room was nicely appointed and I found the service to be good. The concierge with helpful with directions and dinner suggestions. Not too keen on the location because there is little to do within walking distance. We were told there was a shuttle that would take us to the train station but after waiting a long time, we gave up and walked to the station and took the subway to Copley Square. Oddly, we ended up having dinner at the Westin there. One advantage of the location was the proximity to Logan airport. I took the Silver Line from the airport and was at the hotel in about 20 minutes. I was surprised that the hotel website did not mention this option. I only knew of it because I called the hotel and specifically asked if there were public transportation options from the airport. Big convention hotel so lots of traffic and noise. Hotel is not on/near the water and the view from my window was not “Harborview” but “abandoned empty lot view.” I know it is not fair to compare prices of hotels in different cities but I could not help thinking back to my stay two weeks earlier at the W Midtown Atlanta where I had a much larger nicer room for half the price of the Westin Harborview. I was at this hotel for business but given the price/location would probably not choose to stay there if I were traveling for pleasure.

“Location = Wonderful Convenience” O'Hare Hilton, Chicago. First visit, and we love this place. Rooms are clean and nicely furnished. Comfortable recliner conducive to relaxation. Public spaces are exactly as depicted on their website. Indoor pool- suitable for a dip, laps, as well as jacuzzi. Large gym on premises- subject to daily fee. WALK to hotel from any terminal through the underground walkway or take the terminal connector shuttle to Terminal 2. WALK to CTA BLUE LINE subway. 40 minutes to the Loop. Breakfast buffet is nothing short of spectacular. We enjoyed the hospitality of the GASLIGHT CLUB, on lobby level. Great steaks, food, and ATMOSPHERE. Talented piano player - welcomes sing alongs. Restaurant is richly decorated with red velvet wallpaper- dramatic chandeliers- in a turn of the century San Francisco Barbary Coast motif. At the conclusion of our stay, wewalked from the room to our gate! NO SHUTTLES- AND WE DID NOT EVEN HAVE TO GO OUTSIDE. There is only one hotel in our future for Chicago- the O'Hare Hiltom.

“Friendly Service” I usually stay at this property when I have an early flight the next morning. I always find the staff extremely friendly and professional. They always say hello and ask if I need anything. The rooms are clean and comfortable. You cannot hear the planes that fly near the property. I would reccomend this property in conjunction with the airport. It probably would not be suitable for a vacation hotel.

“Sublimely Above Par!” The hotel is beautifully restored in every way. Service from Charlotte, Jaime and Marissa to name a few make you feel at home. Rooms are spacious and inviting. Complimentary wi-fi and wine hour make you wonder why you go anywhere but a Kimpton. The Monaco confirms the Kimpton record of excellence, don't miss the Grand Cafe!

“Perfect setting!” We stayed four nights at Humphrey's for the San Diego Rock & Roll marathon. We did not care for the first junior suite they gave us (too close to the restaurant dumpster and overlooking the parking lot), but they graciously upgraded us to a full suite at no additional charge. We had a beautiful room overlooking the marina. The bed and pillows were comfy and, of course, the grounds are beautiful, although it was a bit cold when we were there to really enjoy the pool. They even gave us late check out. And since I am such a slow runner that it took me past the noon check out time to even finish the race, it was a bonus to be able to come back and shower before our flight home. The only complaints I have are that, like others, I found the carpet to be very dirty. I didn't really see the dirt until I looked at the white slipper socks I had been wearing and they were almost black on the bottoms. I had to throw them away. The only other thing was that the walls were VERY thin. We could hear coughing and snoring. etc. from the room next door. This wouldn't have been as much of an issue if I didn't have to get up at 4:00 AM on Sunday. But I would absolutely recommend Humphrey's if you want a place to relax and get away from it all.

“Great Position” The Phoenix Park Hotel is very well located for your exploring of Washingon. Very close to the Union Station and Capitol Hill it is very easy to be seeing the sights virtually from the time you leave the front door of the hotel. Reasonably priced, the rooms were on the small side but kept clean and tidy. Staff very helpful on arrival and nothing was too much trouble.

“Great location, easy to get to and comfy!” Visited Chicago for a meeting... Stayed here for the location and proximity to Wow Bao! Room was nice, clean and well designed. Employees were friendly and service was fast! Reasonable rates are the norm, it appears. Took the L to the station closest to State and Lake and popped in Wow Bao to grab some grub. Took it to he hotel, ate, watched TV' took a bath and got a great nights sleep. For someone on the road all the time, that's about as good as it gets! I will stay there again, for sure!

“Clean, well appointed rooms and very friendly staff” The Hilton Garden Inn is located on the very busy Colorado Blvd. Traffic is a bit of a pain in the neck but road noise is non-existent in the rooms, which is nice. The hotel is located within walking distance of the Cherry Creek Shopping Center and there are a number of restaurants and other amenities nearby. The hotel is very new and in excellent shape. The staff is friendly and helpful. Rooms are well appointed and comfortable. The only criticism is that the cleaning crews go pretty heavy on the deodorizer they use in the rooms. Once it airs out it is fine... I would definitely stay here again.

“Nice stay at a nice hotel” We stayed here for four nights in April 2012. This was our second stay at the Wyndham. We had the same pleasant stay we had last time--big bed with lots of pillows, clean room, nice TV with a good selection of channels, and my wife ordered a burger from room service and was happy with the quality and the price. We got the room at a very attractive price on Priceline. Last time I reported that the carpets needed replacing because we could hear a lot of noise from the hall. The hall carpeting was replaced, and it's much thicker and prettier than the old hall carpets. Because of the thickness, it blocked the space on the bottom of our room door better, so it really helped in keeping the noise down compared to last time. Since we had as nice a stay as last time and the hotel did respond to my previous comment about the hall carpets, I'm bumping up my score one level. Thanks for listening, Wyndham Folk!

“Top Notch Hotel” I stayed at the Trump Tower in Chicago for business for 2 nights. I had the option of upgrading to a 1 bedroom suite for an extra $75 a night, which I took. The suite was amazing. Absolutely gorgeous, great detail has gone into all the furnishings of this suite. 2 flat screen tv's, plus a tv in the bathroom mirror. This hotel is relatively new and I did see another reviewer comment on the shower and the backup with the water. I also experienced this, along with a request for a new hairdryer and it was taken care of immediately. There are a lot of lightswitches and dimmer buttons, but to simplify they do have an "all on" and "all off" switch next to the bed which is helpful. The views are amazing and the location is ideal. The suites have a complete kitchen with marble counter tops and modern cabinets. The meeting rooms were really nice on the 16th and 17th floor. Its great to have an actual view during a meeting instead of some hotel basement. We also spent some time in their onsite "Re-bar", good scene. The staff were incredibly helpful and very nice and remembered me by name. I would highly recommend this hotel to both business and leisure travelers.

“Small but perfectly formed” Right where you need to be in NYC. Rooms are small but clean and comfortable. No frills NYC hotel perfect for your weekend sight seeing. We were on the 10th floor with only one lift it could be a little slow getting up and down sometimes. Would still recommend.

“Nice hotel and close to everything” The Westin Memphis hotel is one block away from Beale street, near all of the bars and shops in Memphis. It is also walking distance to the Civil Rights Museum at the Lorraine hotel (about 10 minutes). The accomodations were fine and staff was friendly. This hotel is up to par to the expectations for a Westin Hotel.

“A very solid hotel” My wife and I stayed a night at The Orchard, to have a night in San Francisco. I wouldn't say there was anything outstanding about The Orchard, but everything was very good. The room was large by San Francisco standards, clean, well-lit, but dark at night, with a huge king bed and a desk with two chairs (an important issue to my wife). The bathroom was comfortable but not oversize, with a bathtub long enough to stretch out in (at least for someone not too tall). The decor was pleasant, though not strongly of any style. We didn't have any noise problems on our Sunday night/Monday morning--we were on the Bush Street side. Since the play we saw was two blocks away, no complaints about the location. It's very close to the Union Square shopping district and the Financial District, as well as Chinatown. The hotel is well up a hill. It's in a neighborhood that mixes hotels and apartment buildings rather than in the core of the downtown--we find these neighborhoods generally more pleasant. I thought the breakfast was well above average--it included fruit, meat, cheese, all sorts of cold food. I'd rather have good quality cold food than steam table hot food. I also appreciated the way they asked if we wanted a minibar key, that allowed us to say no and not have to worry about it. I'd certainly reccomend this hotel to people coming to San Francisco.

“best airport option” Stayed here twice on recent trip.This property sits just outside the airport but is very quiet.The shuttle driver gave us the spiel about the hotels benefits on the short ride in.....Free shuttle within 3 miles,free cocktails,free custom breakfast,internet,sleep number beds,free movies,etc.... .The first time there was a dust storm and it was cold and they gave us a ground floor courtyard pool room.There was debris that had accumulated and hadn't been picked up.The pool and patio with fireplace and little waterfall was very nice.The room was large and nice decorated and CLEAN.The beds were very luxe.They took us to a local restaurant for dinner and the the store...We did have to wait a bit as it was the weekend and lots of guests.We tried to get a movie but most of the good ones were checked out and the other titles were not so great (they need to improve this) On the way back we arrived to very warm weather and the pool was mobbed.We didn't want to be on the courtyard ,or facing the airport but were only offered a room on the hidden upgraded back courtyard for 30 extra dollars.So we settled for a room facing the airport but it was very quiet. The breakfast were good..but I would have liked fruit.Now for the downside.I don't drink so we ordered one margarita and one coke at the happy hour..yes you guessed it they charged us for the coke....I think they should have warned us about the charge..

“Nice basic hotel, with updated bathroom!” After a full day in LA, we found ourselves too exhausted to drive home, with nowhere to stay. The Ramada Wilshire Center had no vacancies, but we drove a little bit and stumbled upon Dunes Inn. The location was great for us, relatively close to the Wiltern Theater (not walking distance though), and the mostly residential neighborhood--Hancock Park--was quiet and safe. (By safe, I mean, the only entrance is manned by a watchful clerk; there are no vagrants around; nearby are expensive condos, houses, and a few churches; and I would feel comfortable walking around the block, though the streets are quite dark.) The bed was comfortable, but not luxurious. The tv worked fine. Best of all, the bathroom must have been recently renovated, because it was impeccably clean with a nice granite countertop and new tilework. There was a refrigerator, a pool in the atrium, wifi, and a few rooms with a small kitchen, but we didn't use these and can't comment. Since we didn't pay full price, the room was a really great deal. Parking was free and greatly appreciated; since the neighborhood is not within walking distance of restaurants, night life, etc., you'd want to visit with a car. As a side note, some nearby places to visit by car: charming Larchmont Village, Koreatown, Griffith Park & Observatory, Downtown/Japantown, and LACMA. To summarize, Dunes Inn Wilshire is like a Travelodge but with a fancier, cleaner bathroom, and we'd definitely stay here again.

“You'll enjoy it” Have now stayed at the Hotel Monaco twice for a total of 5 nights. Overally, I've been very pleased. Checkin and checkout are easy and I've never had to wait in line. I've stayed in both a suite and the basic king room. The suite is essentially a very large room separated by a curtain. The sitting room has a couch and additional flat screen TV. Unless you're traveling with more than 2 people or want to spend a lot of time in your room, the standard room is more than adequate. Suite bath is pretty much the same as a regular room (they do have suites with jacuzzis that might be more elaborate). Hotel is only 11 floors so don't expect panoramic views. Furnishings are "funky" but tasteful. Rooms appear to be in good repair. Robes (with animal print) are standard. Large flat screen TVs with many, many channels are standard. Bathroom amenities (Aveda) are replenished daily. Bathrooms are modern with tile floors and granite counters. I've had mixed room service experiences. Twice, it was fast and food (pizza) was excellent. One morning breakfast was late and cold. The soft-boiled eggs were hard, which is good because they didn't provide a spoon. The attached restaurant is okay, but the one time we tried it service was very slow. Have heard that it's good for lunch/dinner but the menu wasn't that appealing to me so didn't try it. The concierge was helpful but was rarely seen before 9 or after 5. However, the front desk personnel were great. Wake up calls came promptly. There is free wireless and wired interet access as well as a computer in the lobby for those who didn't bring their own. There are some additional nice touches. First, they host a "wine hour" from 5-6 each evening. Wine is decent (and free) and they do refill your glass. It's a nice way to unwind and mingle with colleagues or even strangers. They are also very pet friendly -- actually seem to enjoy pets rather than merely "accepting" them. For example, this huge dog joined the wine hour and started to wander off into the restaurant. The staff didn't panic -- merely quietly alerted the owner who rectified the situation. The location is good -- walking distance to a lot of things. However, the hotel is on a San-Francisco type hill, so if you walk down to Pike Market, it's a VERY steep walk back up. The one nice thing about this hotel is that it caters to a variety of traveler types. We saw Packers' fans (in town for the NFL game), business people, tourists, etc. A nice mix with nice staff. It is a pleasant change from the traditional loud, impersonal hotels you find in so many large cities. Would definitely recommend it and stay there again.

“Great place to stay!” Staff cannot do enough to help you. Serivice is top notch from top management to housekeeping. This is our hotel of choice if we are to do LA again. Walking distance to the Cathedral. Parking is steep but you can find a lot across the hotel for much less.

“Good value and very clean hotel. Pleasant surprise.” This is a Fairfield Inn but compared to others in that category this is a notch above. Great value since downtown Indianapolis hotels are surprisingly pricey. Hotel provides free breakfast, good choices. Breakfast area does get crowded, I was staying there when a big conference was going on so I had to take my food to my hotel room. Very nice and clean rooms, not your typical Fairfield Inn.

“This hotel was perfect for our stay” We stayed at The Chancellor for 3 nights in April. We had a fanastic stay. We had twin beds. The rooms, staff and location were all excellent. We stayed on the 11th floor, the street noise wasn't bad at all, It added charm to our stay - I loved hearing the Cable Cars go by. The strength of the free wifi was always excellent. Occasionally heard the footsteps from the room above but only ever for a few seconds. Showers were really good and the wardrobe was very spacious but we never used it. We had both our suitcases out in the room and there were will plenty of space left. The beds were awesome, great nights sleep after long days sightseeing around the city. We had originally planned to return to the airport using the BART but our bags were quite heavy and there was no problem booking the Shuttle bus with Lorries with short notice. The tea and cookies in the lobby were a great way to start the morning. We will definately be returning in the future.

“I booked the hotel at a half off rate of...” I booked the hotel at a half off rate of $95. We arrived at the hotel and found there is valet only parking at $20 per day. Check in was nice, but they have this weird quasi-techno music playing in the lobby all the time. Our room was ready as promised. What they didn't tell us was the $100 hold on our credit card for incidentals. Although I guess it is expected, that seems a little steep. The room was fairly standard; comfy bed, chair, desk, LCD tv, minibar (avoid the minibar....$5 for peanut M&M's!). The bathroom was very nice. I would discover later the water pressure could have been better in the shower...but the amenities were nice. The hotel bar and restaraunt are interesting. The restaraunt is featured on an Oxygen Network show and the prices are no kidding. Entrees were about $30-40. Not to mention the clientele appeared to be a little snooty. We chose to eat across the street at a great Irish pub. Overnight, the room noise was quiet. Housekeeping did get an early start in the morning and that was a little loud but not too bad. All in all, it was a great hotel. However, I would definately shop around and/or call the hotel directly to find the absolute best rate.

“Large, centrally located hotel” I stayed at the Mariott Marquis recently for a business trip. However, I think this hotel is a good choice for all travelers, be they business or leisure, couples or families. The best thing about it is the location. While it's technically in the SOMA neighborhood, it's right on the edge of it and within easy walking distance to Powell Street and Union Square shopping, Chinatown, and the waterfront. If you plan to spend most of your time in Fisherman's Wharf or Pacific Heights, however, it's a bit far to walk on foot. The rooms are comfortable and spacious. If you want a large bathroom, request a handicapped-accessible room. The bar is a great place to relax on a business trip. Lots of space to spread out with laptops. Also, head up to Floor 39 for some great views of the city.

“Great Hotel !!! Hyatt Mission Bay is the way to go!” Wow another great hotel. The pool was fantastic! Love the tower rooms and the view was fantastic ! This is the first time and it was great. Staff was very nice and friendly, the spa was fantastic and the food was good in the Red Marlin? I would highly recommend this hotel!

“Not just nice, but the Best” Affinia Dumont is a delightful hotel in a great location. We chose this hotel to celebrate Hanuka, our Silver anniversary and Christmas. Pros- Great Location, friendly staff, AMAZING pan⋅cakes Barking Dog Cafe adjacent to the hotel, breath taking view from high floor rooms. Pillow choices, fitness pack, pet set to use during your stay - awesome. Cons- Pricey. No blender in the kitchen. I think since so many today drink protein shakes for breakfast and this is a fitness hotel, Having a blender in the kitchen would make a great additions to these magnificent accommodations. I would stay at this hotel again BUT only if I got the same room and rate I did on Hotel's web site. Take advantage of the 25% coupon in the spa, I recommend Reflexology.

“Stayed here almost two weeks in November - very restful.” The Hotel Max has taken an older property and provided a fun flair. The doormen and front desk are very friendly and willing to help. The rooms are a tad small, but for business travel that is alright. The biggest drawback I saw was the manual thermostat on the heating/cooling unit. I would have preferred a wall-mount thermostat. The Internet quality was average. VPN was sometimes difficult due to latency from their Internet provider.

“Typical upscale W but New York sized” I realize a lot of people add reviews complaining about the room size, unfortunately this is New York for you, and honestly other boutique hotels in the area and especially times square are A LOT smaller. I really enjoyed my stay at The W, the room was perfect and has just enough space for my boyfriend and I for a 5 night stay. The room had ample space for all of our stuff and a decent sized bathroom and closet. The hotel is well located for midtown east (across from the rear entrance of the Waldorf) and is close to everything without being directly in the action. I love that they have Bliss products and they replenish them generously. Also, the beds are super soft and comfortable! I have nothing to really stay for the staff and service, it definitely didnt stay out to me at all, but the house maids were very friendly and helpful. The only thing I would have to complain about this hotel is the loud music they play at night. It is good for the atmosphere but far to loud to really enjoy, especially because the main lobby is more chill than lively. I would recommend this hotel for couples, friends and family with older children.

“Great location” I agree with what many of the other posters have said. Great location, comfy beds, and close to many hot spots in the Gas Lamp district. The only disappointment came from my 9yr old who was sad that the pool was only 3 1/2 feet deep and didn't quite meet his standards. I would definitely stay here again especially if attending a Padre's game. Tip: Try eating breakfast/dinner at the Broken Yolk which is only a 10 min walk.

“Great Wedding Anniversary Getaway!” The Royal Palms is my new favorite place and probably the best well kept secret in Phoenix. I read all of the reviews on TripAdvisor when planning my anniversary getaway and can honestly affirm the positives. It is worth the money for rest and relaxation. When traveling from Sky Harbor Airport, you will want to get clear driving directions. We missed 2 turns, but once I finally broke down and had my wife ask for directions, we found it. Now that we have been there, it is easy to find on Camelback Road (but you will not find any signs along the way). Once on the property, we found ourselves in a different world. The reception staff welcomed my wife and me with a smile and accommodated us with an early check-in. We enjoyed an awesome Sunday Brunch at T. Cook’s (make reservations well in advance). Our Estate Room was a little dark for reading, even with all the lights on, but very comfortable and quiet which more than made up for it. The grounds are beautiful with orange and grapefruit trees and fountains and fireplaces and seating areas around almost every turn. What really differentiates Royal Palms is the intimacy of being in a smaller resort. Guest services were A+. Dinner at T. Cook’s was delicious (sit outside under the stars near the fireplace if you can). The Lounge was cozy. The Pool service was superb! Try the fish tacos – so good! Fruit and cold water was a nice touch in the fitness room. The hot tub was relaxing. The main pool was heated. The Alvadora spa rejuvenated my wife (try the “Tempting Trio”). Take a morning drive/walk around Camelback Mountain, which is a short distance away and the background setting at the Royal Palms. This place is a photographer’s paradise. Check out was a nice experience, with no surprises on the bill. This is not your kids’ kind of place. Take the entire family to one of the big resorts with multiple pools and structured programs if you’re into that type of experience. But for a special occasion for you and your spouse, you cannot go wrong in choosing the Royal Palms. It is first class. People are great. Prices are fair for the value. I highly recommend it and long to return again!

“Great location and comfortable hotel rooms” On Union Square so right in the location for any tourist visiting San Francisco. The staff are very friendly and do try hard to make your stay pleasurable. The rooms are compact (common for San Fran) but all you need for a few nights. The bed was comfortable and the room nicely appointed with a nice chair and desk. I had breakfast in the restaurant which was very nice and not overly expensive. The one thing I didn't like was that you couldn't control the heating in the room. This was controlled by reception and couldn't be turned off even when the room became an oven. Fortunately the room had opening windows. I was in a top level room so didn't have any issues with street noise. The free wifi worked really well and a nice added benefit. Overall, I would recommend this hotel as good value for money in prime location. Easy to carry your bargains back to your room after shopping at Macys!

“Great location; Hotel will be great Business Hotel after renovations” Stayed at the Westin this week, on 10/3 ... just two days after the change over from Helmsley to Westin. I am very excited to have a new Starwood property in this neighborhood, as it is very convenient to my office, to Grand Central and to many of the major mid-town business restaurants. It will be very convenient. The hotel is still under a lot of work, so be prepared for noise. The rooms have been updated and were very nice, although a bit small even by New York standards: perfect for business where you won't spend a lot of time in the room, but not really something I would book for a vacation or weekend get-away. I was a little disappointed to hear so much noise from the hallways at night, assuiming that updated noise control would have been a part of the renovation. It was not bad enough that I would not stay here again, but generally have me the feeling that I was not really in a very private location. (I found myself wispering on the phone as I had concern that people in the hallway and the rooms next door could hear every word of my conversation.) Overall, as a business hotel in this neighborhood, it's a great choice. Much newer than the tired Grand Hyatt and with so much construction, I can only assume that great things are planned for this property. I only hope the build out a nice rooftop bar like the Grand Hyatt has, as their location makes for a perfect place for such a bar. (If they don't however, and you still choose to stay here, be sure to go to the Grand Hyatt rfooftaop bar, it's spectacular.)

“Excellent Hotel, as Described on Web Site” I do not have to write too much about the Sheraton Seattle because all that is pictured and described on its web site is absolutely accurate. It is an excellent hotel with congenial service in a terrific location. Additionally, I can say that it has one of the best fitness centers I’ve ever encountered in a hotel, with plenty of single purpose weight machines, a stepping board and sufficient floor space, in addition to the usual cardio, etc.

“Favorite Hilton outside of downtown San Antonio” I've stayed at most of the Hilton branded properties on the north side, and this is by far my favorite. The staff is very friendly, and even put me into one of the 2 bedroom suites on a couple of occasions (This is a little bit of a waste as I was by myself, but I still appreciate an upgrade for no reason!). The rooms are clean, cozy, and I can feel at home. The dinner isn't amazing, but does the job when I am working late at the hotel. The cookies are delicious! My only complaint is that if you are on a bottom floor room, you can hear people being loud at the pool.
